I always had Gramercy Tavern bookmarked as a "special occasion" spot, but my burger tour brought me here on business..... BURGER BUSINESS!  And business was good tonight my friends.  

The burger was amazing; easily in the top 3-4 burgers in NYC.  Every component was great, from the perfect blend of meat (nice flavor, ratio, grill, and no gristle), to the clothbound cheddar, and the thinly sliced house-bacon.  I could've used a few more chips, but it was all very satisfying. Then on top of all of that, the staff went above & beyond from the time I walked in, until I left (most likely the rest of the night as well).

Where to start! The entry way is so inviting. The hostess was super sweet.

We were sat in the bar area for lunchtime and were given waters with lemon and bread/butter. 

Our waiter Paul was so great. Attention to detail is so well executed here. You're not just here for the food, but the entire experience.

Started off with a glass of rose- light and refreshing.

App- Lamb flatbread with eggplant, pickled green tomato and mint Holy cow, my senses.

My husband and I shared the cold soup to start- It was a watermelon veggie soup. This cannot be explained in this review. It was to die for.

Entree we shared the lobster broth. I'm not usually a fan of soup for lunch but this may have changed my mind. Lobster, grilled calamari, fennel and muscles in a light sauce. It was seriously so well executed. Perfect seafood cook, the veggies and potatoes were on point.

We did not finish with dessert but it all looked so tempting. 

Service and food both a solid 5. Go. GO NOW!

Danny Meyer is a genius.

Being from Houston where great food is abundant, I was completely disappointed by Gramercy Tavern.  Our foodie friend recommended it, and she is usually spot on.

The atmosphere was nice, but nothing over the top.  The waitstaff was attentive, but not overly friendly.  The food, however, was BORING, and over-priced.  All four of us agreed.  We're on our 4th day in NYC this trip, and by far this has been the least impressive meal we've had.

The heirloom tomato salad and the clam spaghetti appetizer were both excellent.  From there, no one at our table of 4 was enjoyed their meals, except for maybe the lamb.  I was told that it had a nice flavor and was cooked well, but the portion size was so tiny that he couldn't spare sharing one bite with anyone for fear of leaving hungry.  The sea bass was dry, extremely salty, and left virtually untouched.  The spinach ravioli was also salty and bland.  Think pasta in chicken stock.  Like I said, boring.

Overall, the staff and the name are what earn Gramercy their high ratings, but this city is loaded with restaurants that actually deserve 5 stars when it comes to the food, and atmosphere.  Mark this one off of your list and try something else.  It's not worth the money or the experience.

For our anniversary, we opted for Gramercy.  We've been wanting to try this place for a long time.   It was nice to dress up a little for this special occasion.  You definitely get that fine dining experience here.  The service was attentive and friendly.  The dining room had a warm and comfortable feel.   It's also nice to not be crammed like sardines.   We went with  three course meal.  The highlights were the clam spaghettini (first course) and smoked sea trout (second course), which was done to medium.  These dishes were stellar and so refined. I also enjoyed the corn and grain salad.   The dressing was full of flavor.  I think anything with sauce or dressing is going to be amazing here.  The other entree was the sea bass. Unfortunately it was overly salted and the salt overpowered the delicate fish. Now for the dessert...oh boy.   I was so disappointed with the old fashioned strawberry doughnut.   It looked kind of scary to me.  It was dipped in some kind of a pink monstrosity of icing.   It was so sweet and the doughnut seemed to be soaked in syrup or something.   I was expecting freshly made, warm doughnut but I couldn't distinguish this from a boxed kind.  Perhaps because I'm not a big fan of extreme sweets, I didn't appreciate this much.   However this execution of this dessert didn't seem to fit with the refined dishes in the earlier courses.  In fact, I probably could get a better doughnut at a street fair.   Other things on the dish were good though such as the yogurt and berries.  The other dessert, the cream cheese tart with huckleberry was a bit better but I also found it to be overwhelmingly sweet.   So, if you're like me, stick with sorbet or ice cream.  Although not every course was a winner, I had a lovely dining experience at the Gramercy Tavern.

Could not be happier with this place. Fantastic service, beautiful decor, and delicious food. We came here to celebrate our anniversary and Tavern did not disappoint. From he moment we walked in every single request we had was immediately addressed. We picked the seasonal tasting menu and every single thing on it was delicious and beautifully done.

Went here for lunch and had the lobster broth (recommended by the waiter) and cookie & milk, the food & service was very mediocre but food itself was decently priced. 

Drinks are okay, not the best but I've had worse, We had orange blossoms cocktails. 

Overall experience was very average.

Although not our first choice, after some research we decided to try it! Friendly and inviting hostess, great service staff and even better food! We got the $120 seasonal tasting menu and it was perfect! It had the yellowfin tuna tartare, lobster salad, poached halibut, farfalle, beef ribeye and peach for dessert! Everything tasted great! I definitely recommend this place!

I had the pleasure of dining here for lunch today and both the food and service were fantastic.  The atmosphere is very rustic and I loved all the greenery as I walked in.  I started with the lobster salad as my first course and finished with the artic char as my second.  Have to mention the amazing rolls they out on the table, they were soft and warm with a salty sweet flavor. I cannot wait to return!

After reading my review, I was contacted by the restaurant.  They were really concerned, wanted to learn from my experience and they even invited me to come back.  Which I will. I believe my experience was the result of an untypically off day and I look forward to a great dining experience again at the Gramercy Tavern Soon

We did the regular evening tasting menu. This restaurant did so many things right that it's almost easier to say where the hiccups were, so I'll focus on those. To be clear, EVERYTHING else was amazing- loved the ambiance, outstanding service, presentation, etc. Also, the staff learned we were celebrating something due to dietary restrictions, and they brought us a "congratulatory" dessert. Really sweet and unique.

Only minor cons were:
1. I started to see the same ingredients were being used over and over again in the tasting menu. I didn't feel like each dish was a totally new adventure. There wasn't a dish where I wished there had been more on the plate-- and that's my gauge for 5 stars for food.

2. We told them we had a show to get to at 8, so we had the first seating of the night. Our waitress repeatedly acknowledged we needed to get to the show, but the experience slowed dramatically at around 7:15. We didn't end up getting out the door until almost 7:40 and found ourselves literally running into the theater to make curtain. I think as the restaurant got busier, our courses got slower and server got busier. I was really afraid we wouldn't make our show.

Apparently difficult to get a reservation if you aren't dining in the dining room.  Went with a handful of people and sat in the dining room to only find out that if we weren't ordering the pre  arranged menu that we wouldn't be able to sit there.  Not a huge deal, I understand.

Ordered a bottle of wine, only to have the waitress question why we ordered the wine, and to suggest we order a more expensive bottle.  Very strange.  Have never experienced that before.  I am glad that that my wife was able to back up why we ordered the bottle we did since she had ordered a glass of it before.  Not the least expensive bottle on the menu either.  Seemed very unprofessional of the the waitress.

The entrees where delicious, albeit overpriced, which is what salvaged the extra star.  Really wished there was better service so I could give this place a better rating since the food was that was good.  I suppose if you look like old money you will have a great time.  The waitress apologized for her poor service at the end, but I couldn't tell if it was sincere or sarcastic.  

This was planned to be an all out dinner for an anniversary in the future, but based on the service tonight, I think we'll find someplace else that will feel a little more special.

The decor of this place is so beautiful. Fresh flowers everywhere. The food was excellent but the entrees are fairly small since its a very fancy place. This is definitely the place to impress. I had the seabass and I ate every last bite. My friends opted for the chicken and it was excellent as well.
First time and what a wonderful experience to be recommend as the place to go in NY on your travels or if you are local make it your second home

Came here to accompany someone to do research on an assignment on the hospitality business. It is what it is. You are paying through the roof for good service. Yes, the floor manager and the waiter were professional and pleasant. Yes, food is good (friend had the 3-course menu; I had the Seasonal Tasting menu), but, it is equal to, if not just ok than a casual less expensive restaurant around. 

The hospitality is forced and rehearsed; it is not natural or sincere. For example, hostess was more than joyful to see us arrive and when seating us down, However, much like that sports gastropub where the wait staff is "nice", as soon as the check drops, you are a nobody; hostess ignored us as if we did not exist when we were leaving. It may seem like that they are your friends, welcoming and accommodating and someone you can rely on -- mindful and compassionate, but that's only lasts up you paid the check, because that's what they are conditioned and paid to do. They are not your friends; they are there to bank. 

Also, we told the wait staff and manager that a student is doing this for an assignment. Least they could've done was comped us for a dessert or a glass of wine, since a student --*hint* *hint*, broke and struggling, is dining here, but instead they upsold the most expensive glass of wine they have. Going here is like going to Vegas. You go there to feel good, and yes you will fell good, but you leave broke, disoriented, and with the newfound knowledge that you have an STD. 

I do commend them for their professionalism. I felt that we we were not rushed and condescended upon. People come more for GT's hospitality and ambiance here than the food. And they do provide great hospitality here, but you have to pay A...LOT. Nothing wrong with that. Restaurant is a service industry after all, and food is secondary. At least I can cross this out of my bucket list and say that I've been and eaten here. Can't be a New Yorker without having to have eaten here.
Delicious! and great service. our waiter was great too, he didn't mess up our order (and yes that is a big deal). everything was cooked the way we asked for it.

Food was reasonably priced considering its reputation. Food was excellent, staff were very knowledgeable and even the back of the house took time answering questions about food. Excellent food of course but the experience was 5 star. Will definitely go back again.

Great service, great atmosphere, great food. As it should be at Danny Meyer's restaurants. Can I get the names of the bartenders next time? I would like to personalize the review a little bit more in the future.

Happy Birthday to me. My girlfriend had the benevolence of taking me here for my birthday. The food was amazing. We both got the tasting menu that was well thought out and artfully balanced. However, the service stole the show. Our server was just as excited as we were. She was knowledgeable and attentive to all our needs and more. The sommelier gave us a visit and paired tastings with each course that complemented the meal and wines. I feel that other places of such caliber can be snobby at times, but I felt both front and back of house had gone out of their way to create a truly incredible experience for us. To top it off we got invited to see the kitchen in action and the goody bags of petit-fours and muffins for breakfast the next day.

This has to be one of my absolutely favorite restaurants in NYC. They put so many Michelin star restaurants to shame with their superb service, wine selection, presentation, food quality and taste. Gramercy Tavern is always on my "must list" while in NYC. And they always deliver and make every visit equally special.

We got stuck in traffic due to a wreck...should have taken the subway...and were 20 minutes late for our reservation.  I went up to the hostess, apologized for our tardiness and asked if it still might be possible to get a table in the dining area.  He just smiled and said, "Not a problem!". We were seated within 5 minutes.  Karen was our server and she was friendly and very knowledgeable about the wine and the menu.  We decided to do a tasting menu with food pairing and started on our journey through the five courses.  It was one of my best dining experiences in NY and that is saying a lot.  The food was exquisite and the progression from scallops to halibut followed by a mussel, calamari, and chorizo pasta to then the most amazing piece of duck that I have ever tasted was a fabulous experience.  I think they have an amazing deal to have such a cheap lunch tasting menu and definitely plan on checking it out again once the season changes.

We came here for NY Restaurant Week and because it was full, we were seated in the bar. It wasn't ideal for talking since there were 3 of us so we just ate our meal and left. We didn't really mind because the bartender was very attentive so it made up for the less ideal seating arrangement. Everything we had was good.

This is a review of the dining room. 

SERVICE: The waitstaff was phenomenal. They were attentive and had no problem taking on the challenge of getting my parents to the theatre in a timely manner. The waiter we had was knowledgeable about the menu, without being pushy. He set up a game plan and a timeline that made the experience move quickly enough to get my parents to midtown, without having it feel rushed whatsoever. The birthday cake they brought out for me went above and beyond any expectation I could have had for a restaurant's "birthday" treat. This item wasn't on the menu, so you've gotta have a celebration in order to try it. UNREAL.

FOOD: we did the $92 prix fixe menu. I had the most divine steak tartare (Wagyu Beef Tartare, Tomatoes, Peppers and Lima Beans) I could have imagined--if I could eat that every day, I would. The tastings that came between the dishes were also well-timed and delicious. For my main I ordered the Smoked Arctic Char with Corn, Shishito Peppers and Peaches. This was just absurd. The fish was light (but somehow tasted like bacon?!), and was topped with bits of miniature popcorn. The bed of corn and peaches was also a delight. The strangest thing we had was the pallet cleanser between dinner and desert--a like cucumber granita with a creamy component you mix together, topped with little white minty tubes.  The desserts were a delight. I ordered the Selection of Sorbets, (which they've already changed the flavors of since last weekend), I had the Peach, Blueberry and Melon Tomato--but would love to try the Pear Pink Peppercorn that's now on the menu. I made my dessert selection based on the Melon Tomato, and it was so unique (even by my Salt & Straw standards). The mini birthday cake they sent came on a miniature pedestal atop a plate with the cliche, "Happy Birthday Callie" written in chocolate. The cake was an incredible angel food cake with coconut, iced in a meringue. Everyone at the table was pleased with their meal and service, and I cannot wait for another opportunity to dine here.

Yes it's pricey but I don't celebrate special occasions at Burger King.  The attentive and buttery smooth service is what you're shelling out for.  The food plays second fiddle but is impressive as well. Ambiance is classy but not stuffy.

Don't be scared. Go ahead and treat yo self!

I returned to Gramercy Tavern after a 10-year absence, not sure what to expect from what had been a longtime favorite. It was a birthday lunch with a friend in the tavern room, the first time I ate there. Our lunch was excellent, the service divine. My martini still the best in town.Unlike other upscale restaurants, G. M. is a warm, friendly place, and the food remains superb. You can go home again...

Highly recommend the seasonal tasting menu for lunch. $58 for a five-course meal isn't too bad for the quality and service you get, if you have two hours to spare at lunch. Every course was a symphony in your mouth. The atmosphere was pleasant too. Not too stuffy. Service is 5star standard too.

A quintessentially NY lunch experience. Had lunch in the Tavern along with business folks taking their lunch break and an older crowd of ladies who lunch. Loved the fresh flower stand display in the Tavern as well as in the ladies restroom. 

Started with the delicious heirloom tomato and peach salad. Sweet crunchy baby tomatoes and ripe peaches with cream. 

Had a summer squash rotolo for my entree. Too heavy and rich. Was imagining something different when I ordered it, like actual pasta made out of summer squash instead of it being stuffed in traditional pasta. So much sauce and cream. 

For dessert I had the chocolate cake with raspberry sauce and actual chunks of raspberry inside of it. Salted caramel and a scoop of frozen yogurt on the plate as well. Such a delicious combination of flavors.

Gone on both birthday lunch and dinner in 'dining' room and it's a pure treat.  Fine dining service takes entire experience to a new level. Reservationist asked my friend who called to book my birthday lunch if it was a "special occasion". On that note, they brought an assortment of desserts at the end of our meal, a happy surprise! For a dinner, I had the seafood tasting menu -- a must. Always memorable and worth it!

Finally made it to the dinng room for lunch with a reservation through opentable. There was a line forming outside even before they opened and many people opted for the Tavern with no reservations - will def. try in the future! But for that day, we had the seasonal tasting menu $62. 
1. Marinated Scallops with fluke, almonds, and plums - so delicious! I was really impressed with this starter! So light and amazing.
2. Poached Halibut with tomatos, shell beans, and olives  - the fish was cooked perfectly and the my friend was raving about this dish after lunch was over.
3. Farfalle with calamari, chorizo, and mussels - this was probably the dish that we felt was fine, but just compared to the others the weakest of them all. The seafood was fresh and tasty, but just a comparably 'normal' dish.
4. Duck breast and thigh with araflex cabbage, blueberries, and lemon verbena - the sauce, the meat, the dish, pretty much perfect!
5. Peach with vanilla rice pudding, pistachios, and basil - this dish really WOW'ed me! I'm not usually a big rice pudding fan, just a big dessert fan, but I gave it try. This was SO GOOD. I'm pretty much out of words because you just have to try it to understand how good it was. This left us with smiles on our faces and cannot wait to come back here in the near future!
Overall the service was attentive, on par with the quality of the restaurant I've been dying to dine in. Will definitely come back for tavern, or dining room experience, or both!
I wasn't too fond of my app (lamb pizza I think) and fish entrée was average.  service was great but nothing memorable about the food. Actually I didn't finish the fish because I didn't like it.

Love it. Celebrated a friends birthday party here. The dishes prepared here are delicious and makes you want more. So many entrees, deliciously prepared to satisfy your hunger. Also if you're coming not for a multiple course dinner and only for something small to eat, try the French press coffee its a must! Also the different cheeses with a glass of wine.

AMAZING food, incredible service!

Came here after a horrible experience at another nearby restaurant while visiting from California, and I could not have been happier with the experience! We were able to get a last-minute reservation and salvage the evening that was very nearly ruined by the rude staff at the other upscale eatery. The entire staff at Gramercy was polite and attentive, the food was unbelievably good, and the atmosphere was inviting. Our waiter provided expert wine recommendations to accompany the chef's tasting menu we ordered, which was delicious. We had dessert, espresso, and then after-dinner drinks at the bar. 

I have no trouble saying this was the best meal I have ever had!

(If you're wondering what restaurant we had such a horrible experience with, I'll give a hint: "Aaron Burr").

I was brought here (as a surprise) by my boyfriend for my birthday. From the time we got there the service was impeccable. We were sent to the bar while we waited for them to set up our table. 

Once our table was ready, our waitress, Angela, explained the menu perfectly and we decided on the 6 course seasonal tasting. My boyfriend also did the wine pairing. Each course was better than the next and when it came time for dessert, I was surprised with a complimentary birthday cake (so nice!). 

They also gave us a bunch of complimentary tastings, such as a bean salad before our first course, a selection of tiny desserts and some delicious muffins to go. 

The bill was, as expected, a little over the top but you can't put a price on the perfection! 

This place was outstanding and I would definitely go back during a different season to see how the menu changes, because I'm sure it will be perfection!

My friend and I had a girls weekend in NYC in April.  I can't believe it's taken me this long to post!  We made late night reservations at Gramercy Tavern and had a delicious meal.  We both had the house special burger (not your typical burger) and shared a bottle of wine.  But the highlight of our evening was the service!  Our waiter was a charming southern gentleman named Leslie.  He helped us order the best items, chose a fabulous bottle of wine (within our budget) and allowed us to have a leisurely meal.  Our conversation with him was delightful...we wanted to have him join us for dessert!  What an absolute pleasure to sit at his table!  With so many restaurants, it seems unadventurous to repeat visits.  However, next time I'm in New York, I will return to Gramercy Tavern and will request to sit at Leslie's table!

My wife and I always look forward to dining here every year during our annual trip to NYC, after making our reservation 28 days in advance.  We had dinner there recently.  I must say my meal was awful. The first course was a pasta dish.  I appreciate al dente pasta, but this was just plain undercooked.  Next I had a plate of assorted lamb bits.  The tenderloin was delicious, but the piece of lamb shoulder was so tough I couldn't chew it or bring myself to swallow it.  Finally, the dessert was Pavlova.  The pastry was so hard I could not cut through it with a fork.

However, the service was excellent.

In a city as fantastic and diverse as New York, there are few things that one can classify as a "must do", I must state here that Gramercy Tavern is an experience that everyone should place on their bucket list, and make every effort to cross it off as soon as possible.

The experience was fantastic. I was lucky enough to score a place at the bar, which did nothing to lessen my experience. While waiting for my friend to show, I was able to enjoy one of the best cocktails I have had in a long time. My bartender was gracious, professional, and fantastic! The only thing that matched my bartender was that I would soon learn that the rest of the staff were equally impressive and excellent!

After enjoying the cocktail, I would soon enjoy a culinary experience that was truly heaven on Earth... The roasted and raw oysters were fantastic, and the lobster salad with brioche delectable. When my friend arrived, we ordered the pork shoulder (which I'll get to in a second), while waiting we were given a sample of their swordfish and seabass. The fish was so light and flavorful, with a crust that did not overwhelm the flavor of the fish, I was surprised it did not float off the plate!

When our pork shoulder arrived, nestled in a wild rice and vegetables, I truly thought that I had died and gone to heaven. The meat was so tender and flavorful, the rice both spicy and sweet and all around delicious. The after dinner aperitif rounded out a wonderful experience.

Yes, an evening at Gramercy Tavern will be somewhat expensive, but it is an experience that should be had by all - special occasion, birthday, anniversary, proposal - save up and truly experience dining at its best!
Attentive staff. Delicious food. Good beer selection. Sat at the bar for a while and didn't feel rushed.
The food was absolutely amazing and the service was great too. Worth the money for a special occasion :)

Worth the money!!! I went there for lunch tasting menu. 5 courses for $ 62. Delicious in every single dish. Service was so great and ambience so home and beautiful. Great spot for dating and ceremonies.
GT can do no wrong in my book.  I'm a particularly big fan of the front Tavern -- the food, service and ambiance are fantastic and it's a good value for a wonderful dining experience.

Had a wonderful experience at Gramercy Tavern!  The food was spot on...the seasonal tasting menu was "tasty" but the vegetable tasting menu was a bit lacking in flavor and creativity.  Our lead waitress was amazing and the service was attentive but not overwhelming.  Looking forward to going back again soon!!

A little underwhelmed. Based on the reviews I had high hopes for this dinner but unfortunately it fell short.

What I liked: the service was impeccable, I never went without water, bread or a glass of wine. The servers and other wait staff were super polite and attentive. 
I enjoyedmy appetizer: the tuna tartar, it was very refreshing and tasty.
The atmosphere and overall decor was really nice, they had just decorated for fall and the whole environment was very harvesty.
The prices were very reasonable for this caliber of restaurant. Especially in this area of the city. 

What fell short:
I ordered the kielbasa and was very excited for the entree however it tasted like a glorified hotdog and the potato accompaniment tasted like vegetable oil. Very disappointing.

Anna Pickler, our server, was fantastic. Charming and knowledgable, Anna was as lovely as the food. She made the night. 

Encouraging everyone to double down on the most pungent of cheeses in lieu of a sweet dessert. Corn salad also amazing.

Certainly with All the hype.  David ordered all the cheeses and I ordered the veg tasting menu.  Excellent cheeses!  Any place that has my all time and obscure favorite Harbison (by Jasper Hill farms) is impressive.  The veg tasting menu was a gorgeous preparation though not all to my liking. The first course was a cherry tomato gazpacho which would be great if I liked raw cherry tomatoes.  The second a fantastic beet salad!  The third was this sweet onion on a bed of corn affair.  The only issue here was that the onions were so raw it made them difficult to cut.  And the forth was spinach fettuccine in a vinegar sauce that David loved.  Of course I had my half or more of the cheeses!  The only interesting thing missing was a fruit selection that most people pair with the cheese.  I've never been to a place that didn't have honey, fruit, nuts... They served some crackers and bread.  I list this only as a curiosity as we don't actually need all that stuff - just the cheese please.  =p.  We were done and skipping dessert and they brought a little petite four selection as a parting gift.  All were great.  We would certainly return if in the area.  It's not a wonder dinner is booked three months out!!!

Our friend recommend this resto, they said we have to try Gramercy Tavern because Gramercy is one of the best resto in NY (and very popular)
and yeaaaaaah we're really enjoyed time there and the food super super delicious!!

A lot has been written about this restaurant, its owner, and chefs. What I noted about Gramercy Tavern, beyond the taste and execution of the meal, is the warmth and graciousness of the staff. This was evident from the start, in how the staff responded to my reservation request and in the cordial and professional service throughout the meal. Service was well-orchestrated, from the timely delivery of warm bread during the meal, to the graceful presentation of each course, to the deft removal of crumbs. I was thoroughly impressed by the genuine, smiling staff, as was my sister, who commented extensively about the experience.

The meal itself was exquisite. We went with the 3-course prix fixe menu; a separate 6-course tasting menu is also available. I started with the clam spaghetti, with impossibly fresh and tender pasta, plump clams and sweet corn.

Next was the thinly-sliced pork loin served in an earthy sauce with charred broccoli. Along with the pork was nicely smoked deckle, reminding me of a cross between beef and bacon.

Lastly, I enjoyed a highly inventive cherry cheesecake, one made of goat cheese, with a brûlée topping and chunky fresh cherries. The sweet, poppyseed cookie crust was incredible, as was the sorbet made with cherry steeped in port liquor.  

We also had complimentary cucumber and mint ice palate cleanser with mint meringue and separately, mignardises of apricot shortcakes and lemon chocolate bombes.

The fantastic experience continued the following morning with a delicious coffee cake with a tasty topping, a take-home treat from the restaurant.

I was taken the as a birthday surprise by my other half and it was wonderful. 
We had the seasonal trading menu and it was lovely. For two people who are fish fans and dislike seafood we managed the whole thing without an issue. Unlike other restaurants of singular quality they don't make a big sing and dance about that aspect of the menu which worked for us. 
As it was my birthday they surprised me with a coconut ice cream cashew which was delicious. 
The atmosphere was very intimate and the staff were excellent, very subtle when clearing dishes. 
The only negative I have is that I asked for fresh mint tea at the end which wasn't on the menu and I'm pretty sure I was given regular mint tea due to the colour and strong taste which is not quite what I wanted. Otherwise the restaurant was amazing.
Overall, food was ok but some dishes were a little too salty for me. It wasn't a bad meal, but I wish I could remember what I had in this restaurant without looking at my pictures.

We visited Gramercy Tavern to celebrate our anniversary. This places lives up to the hype. Everything about our visit was outstanding. The service was top notch. We never waited for anything, our wine and water glasses were always full, and our server was friendly, knowledgable, and pleasant to talk to. The wine and cocktail list was superb. Every course was absolutely fabulous. Some added bonuses were an anniversary dessert (see photo) and take-home coffee cakes for the following morning. We even got a message via Yelp thanking us for our visit. It certainly is a cumulation of the little things that make a big difference. Highly recommend!

Had lunch here this afternoon. Food was good but it was way, way late. It was annoying but without us having to complain the manager got us a round of drinks and when it was further delayed comped our entrees. That works.

I came here with my husband for our first wedding anniversary and everything was perfect. We had three courses and let the waitress choose us a matching wine for each one - everything tasted fabulous and all the wines were on point. She picked a sparkling red to go with my beef tartar starter which worked so well.

Every course was a hit and we were actually pleasantly  surprised by the price, under $300 before tip.

I had cheese for dessert and they picked me three fantastic choices based on my terrible description of what I did/didn't like.

They also brought us the most incredible tasting complimentary coconut cake (my husband doesn't like coconut and still wolfed it down!).

Overall the service, atmosphere and food were all excellent. A very relaxed and friendly, but still up market, posh dinner option. We would come back.

If you need to have a sure bet dining experience for any reason, whether it be a special occasion, a client to impress, this is your place.  And - the prices were far better than expected, similar to any fine dining establishment (I was expecting to pay $20-30 more than what I did for what I had).  This was a bucket list restaurant that I can now happily say I've been to.

If you want to get in without a reservation - get to the tavern before 6.  After dropping in one night at 8:30 and being told over an hour wait, I came back the next day at 5:45 and was seated at the bar right away.  They will do a waiting list at the bar if they are busy, a plus.

The staff was amazing - service was perfectly timed and flawless, the bartenders made every drink as though their reputation depended on it, and every detail was thought of...even using a spoon to taste the drink before serving it.

The food was spectacular American fare - creative but approachable.  Cavatelli with Lamb, holy crap.  Broiled pork shoulder, yum.  

I would for sure go back next time I'm in the city.  I'd almost recommend eating in the tavern over the restaurant (separated in the back with a thick curtain) as it is a bit more lively...but maybe there is something behind that curtain that is even more special.  Hmmm.....

We came to have lunch at the Tavern. We wanted more of a casual option at one of well celebrated restaurants, and the Tavern fitted the bill perfectly! 

I had the duck meatloaf and my husband had the lobster broth with seafood. We finished our lunch off with their apple pie and butterscotch pudding, which is just out of the world! 

Perfect lunch to kickoff our night in the city.

I've been wantingwantingwanting to dine at Gramercy Tavern for 5 years and one of my dearest friends made my foodie dreams come true last Monday. We dined in the tavern area and I ADORED it. There are no faults. 

What does a NY restaurant look like in your head? Because in mine, it looks and tastes like Gramercy Tavern. Dark wood. A gorgeous bar. Waiters in suits. Women in cocktail dresses. Mirrors. Dried flowers. New American cuisine. 

My friend and I decided to create our own tasting menu and it.was.magical. 

I can't recommend the raw & roasted vegetables enough. It was served with 3 dipping sauces: grenada pepper, cauliflower caper, and walnut miso. I'm not one to order raw vegetables (are you?) but I was just so curious about this plate. It. Was. Amazing. First of all, it was a feast for your eyes. The colors just popped. But most of all, it was just sooo fun meticulously sampling the vegetables, comparing raw to roasted, and trying all the sauces. 

Then we shared the sea bass with pole beans, cucumber, and lobster and the grilled pork shoulder, fingerling potatoes, cabbage, and scallions. Everything was cooked and seasoned perfectly and did you know that pole beans + cucumber + lobster go together? I think it was the dill that tied the three together. It tasted like a lobster salad. Everything was impeccably fresh. Gramercy Tavern is a fine example of farm-to-table. 

I'm not quite how sure we managed it, but we didn't say no to dessert. My friend knows I can't say no to pumpkin anything so we got the pumpkin spice sundae with walnuts, specullos cookie butter, and cinnamon MASHMALLOW FLUFF. Honestly, I would've ordered the whole dessert menu if given the chance. 

Oh, and finally, the cocktails. If I hadn't been so sleepy from taking the red-eye from CA to NY, I would've ordered something stronger than the Orange Blossom (sparkling wine, elderflower, orange bitters), but it was a lovely, light drink. I stole sips from my friend's Concord Crush (Tito's vodka, concord grapes, and lime) and it was one of the best cocktails I've ever had. It's a dangerous, thick, grape juice.

This may be one of my favorite restaurants in the world.

My husband and I chose this for our 10 year anniversary dinner and are so happy we did.  The evening started with a champagne toast.  I ordered the Cauliflower Cappelletti and and Flounder; my husband ordered the Wagyu Beef Tartare and Sea Bass.  One of the best meals ever!  Service was great; the staff work tirelessly to make sure you have an incredible experience. Dinner ended with the cashew and chocolate desserts.  They also brought out a complimentary coconut cake for our anniversary, and you also get muffins for the next morning.  Amazing meal; exactly how you want to spend a wedding anniversary!
Just go and try the seasonal menu, great creations and excellent service. If you are a food porn lover this is the spot. Also great drinks. There is some special gin creations you should give a try

A major and expensive disappointment for what should have been a memorable one month same sex marriage anniversary.

We are both food and hospitality professionals and our reservation reflected such.

No chef visit to table, no one inquired how dinner or about main course. When offered amuse that had allergen, alternates discussed but never delivered. Took a while to see bread and menus.

We needed an additional glass of wine that when poured  was barely even covering bottom of glass.

Expresso came sandwiched between cheese course and dessert. All other tables around had a cider course and a mini celebratory cake and petits fours except oUrs.

Restaurant not full, and no other gay couples or same sex couples in sight.

Would it have been too much to expect a free dessert wine or petit four like our neighbors? 

Now about the food that didn't work. Desserts did not meet the bar of high expectations either. The mango confection was too sweet and too green. The chocolate bar lacked layers of flavor, and I finished it just to keep myself occupied however unsatisfying it was. Temperature for the lamb main course was offered yet not delivered as requested.

We were dressed in casual business attire which translates as more appropriate than some of the gym wear otherwise adorning some of our table neighbors.

With the bill came take away muffins to bring the experience home for breakfast. Which definitely did when we found a hair in the muffin.

If this is an example of fine American dining, I will stay far away from this kind of Restaurant group. It is a pity that in a city like new York we cannot get the respect nor service which we happily would pay for.

One of the best restaurants I've been to in terms of both food and service. Bread basket selection is really good. I might have gotten full off of them. Tip, don't eat more than 3. I got the tasting menu. Oh, and you get a generous size coconut cake if it's your birthday. So good. 

So, you start off with a tiny puff filled with cheese. Probably the size of a quarter. Although it was small, it's packed with flavor. Wished I had more. The courses in between are all flavorful and delicate so nothing is too overwhelming. The seafood here is great. The ceviche, shrimp, and fish are presented beautifully and the sauces paired with each of them are perfectly balanced. I had a meat dish too but that wasn't too memorable. Desserts are light as well. Nothing heavy (except for that free birthday cake). This place is awesome. I definitely will be back.

Had business lunch there yesterday; service was excellent and food not so much. Ambiance is spectacular and food not so much. Drinks were awesome and you guessed it... Food not so much. Not worth the visit!

This restaurant is great, but definitely not my favorite in New York.  The customer service and food is good, as you can expect from any Danny Meyer restaurant.  The food was 4/5 stars - good, but nothing to write home about.  The customer service was friendly, 4/5 stars.  The ambiance was 5/5 stars, unique, charming, & just the right amount of fancy.  Maybe I came away with a 4 because I had such high expectations, considering it is a restaurant in the Union Square Hospitality Group and I felt underwhelmed.

If you're in the neighborhood & want a high quality, comfortable upscale dinner, &/or want to dine at one of the Union Square Hospitality Group restaurants this place is a good choice.  

*Disclaimer: my review and photos are based on my dining experience there years ago.  There may have been improvements/changes made since my last time there.

I was visiting New York from Atlanta and have dreaming of eating at this restaurant for 3 years. I work as an executive chef in Atlanta and took a sort of food vacation... All I did was eat and drink and I regret nothing. I was worried that I had set expectations that might be unobtainable. However, I was quickly proven this was what I had been waiting for. I sat at the bar for dinner and was immediately impressed. I chatted with the bartender about a half bottle of wine and she quickly recommended a bottle she thought I would enjoy. It was fantastic. Everything I had described I liked in wine was in this bottle. 

Then I saw the menu. They were offering a four course goat tasting menu. I couldn't resist and decided on that. Then the food started to arrive. 

First a lobster amuse that blew me away. Everything an amuse should be. Simple, elegant, with enough flavor to make me want to eat the rest of the food. 

Then a kale and brussel salad with goat prosciutto(made and cured in house). I would have never expected a salad course to have so much flavor. Truly remarkable. 

Next came a goat sausage with stewed peppers and yogurt. Also fantastic and full of flavor. 

The main course was an Agnolotti with celery root, beans, and braised goat. Fresh pasta is one of my favorite things to eat and make. This dish was full of complexity and richness. A little on the salty side, but nothing crazy and overpowering. 

Now time for dessert. The dessert offered was a banana cake with goats milk ice cream. The asked to look at the dessert menu anyway and saw another option I couldn't leave without. The Butterscotch pudding with a pear granita. I requested to switch it out for the tasting menu even though the one offered looked amazing. Instead of simply switching it out, the bartender delivered both, one compliments of the restaurant. Talk about amazing service. Both desserts were wonderful, but the butterscotch pudding will truly change your life. 

In summary, I can only hope that one day my food and service will be comparable to this restaurant. You can see the care and refinement in every step of service and every plate of food. The best meal I have every had.

Great food! ceviche was amazing, as was the clam pasta- probably one of the best i've had. service on par, water glasses were never empty. the bread in the complementary bread basket was still warm. only thing is the menu is bit pricey...but it's great for a special night out splurge and probably a lot cheaper than many of the other restaurants with the same great quality of food!

Didn't have an opportunity to eat in the dining room, but this is easily one of the best meals in the city served at the bar. On my shortlist going forward. Sea Bass w/ Pole Beans, Cucumber & Lobster along with the Goat Cheese Agnolotti off the Goat-Ober menu were the highlights. I'd absolutely come back.

Food and service spot on. We had cocktails, sea bass, monkfish, apple pie (bit dry but tasty), caramel pudding and bottle of wine. We were happy and prices reasonable (ate on tavern side).  Worth a stop if you're in the area.

One con is when we first arrived and thought we might sit at bar we were told to stay in reception area until seats available. However, when we got a table and dinner hour approached there were 3 deep at bar and people holding onto back of chair and eyeing/commenting on our food. Distracting. Should not be allowed to happen. Thank goodness we were nearly finished.
My waiter was very nice and pleasant and the food came out so quickly. I will definitely be coming back again. Don't be deceived by the slightly unwelcoming decor.

Excellent restaurant with a memorable ambience.

Disclaimer: this review is for the dining room and spring tasting menu.

It was time for another date night with the lady. I've been to the restaurant's tavern several times for cocktails and thought it was time to experience the dining room. I followed the advice of others by placing a reservation 28 days in advance via telephone at 10:00 AM, which allowed for maximum flexibility when choosing what time I wanted to eat.

We arrived on time for our reservation but had to wait approximately 10 minutes to be seated, which was understandable given the popularity of both sections of the restaurant. The dining room was aesthetically pleasing, and our service was great. I appreciated the attentiveness of the staff throughout our meal.

As mentioned, we ate from the seasonal tasting menu. The quantity and quality of food was very good. I remember the lobster and duck breast being especially tasteful, which was impressive considering I order these items often at other restaurants.

I definitely recommend eating in the dining room. Hopefully, you will enjoy it as much as we did!
Phenomenal experience.  This place is a well oiled machine of perfect service.  Food was great.  Toni, Isabella,  and Karen made our night.  Told you we would write this.  Thank you!
One of the best meals I've ever had.  This is true gem in NYC and I highly recommend enjoying a meal here.
not a lot that I can add to what likely has been said.  however if you go here, just get the tasting menu and wine pairing and call it a day.  you won't be disappointed.

I went back to Gramercy Tavern due to my first experience being so wonderful. I had to say this time around was good, but not as good as my first time around. They were doing a 3 course menu which was a bit pricey for what you received in return. I started with the smoked fish which was just OK and not really filling. The Pork was excellent and complimented nicely with my Cabernet Sauvignon. I highly recommend the cheese plate instead of the dessert. They have a great cheese cart. Almost comparable to Gary Danko in San Francisco which is pretty hard to beat. This one cheese just blew me and my friend away, and if they still have it on the menu it is called Coupole Bloomy Rind Goat from Vermont Butter & Cheese Creamery. It was truly amazing, and you don't even need to eat it with bread. It just melts in your mouth. Our server Marcelo was great, but seemed a bit busy and not surprised to see us again considering how attentive he was during my first visit. The wine list is a bit pricey, and they need to take it down a notch in price. At least 10 to 20% less. If a bottle of Shafer sells for $75 at the store or winery, then no more than double that at the restaurant. Overall, Gramercy was great, and I will be back.

Gramercy Tavern update. I wanted to get a good nights rest & gather my thoughts to reflect on last nights turn of events. As I posted earlier we stopped at Gramercy for a nightcap after a 2 star dinner experience at an establishment just down the street. We have been enjoying our trip to NYC tremendously up to this point and wanted to end the evening on a high note. So based on the crowd at this establishment at this late hour we felt it would be a great experience. And to be truthful it started out to be a fabulous end to our evening. The bartender was courteous and attentive. He even put the effort to remember our names after one attempt. This was exceptional especially since it was standing room only at the at bar. He made us some great Belveder Martinis shaken perfectly and pure in flavor. Even though we were full from our dinner we saw the customer beside us thoroughly enjoy his sautéed vegetable platter, so we ordered it. It was fresh nicely charred with great dipping sauces on the side. We decided at that moment that we would make a point to comeback for lunch to enjoy a complete meal on this trip. Unfortunately, this is when it started to take a turn for the worse. My girlfriend ordered a third Martini to share and after taking a sip she noticed a slightly odd flavor and asked me to have a sip to confirm her taste. I could taste a slight hint of another kind of alcohol and agreed with her. she decided to ask the bartender to remake the drink, especially since we were paying $20 for each drink. Instead of just remaking the drink he proceeded to insinuate that there must be something wrong with our palate by stating that he washed the shaker and gave us a new glass and then grudgingly offered to make her a new drink. After that he didn't make eye contact or ask us if the drink was ok, but very unprofessionally talked to his co worker while looking back at us and not coming to our side of the bar. At this point my girlfriend decided to talk with the manager and explained the situation to him. The manager apologized and offered to cover a round for us. We were fine with that until the bartenders associate came over to us to see if we were ok and to see if there was anything he could do to make things better. He offered us a drink and my girlfriend asked if it was on the house? He stated maybe and then came back and gave her a half full martini and said here is a shortie on the house. It was obliviously a slap in the face. I told my girlfriend to not drink it and I asked for the manager. After explaining the situation he apologized and asked how he could make things right. We said we didn't expect to pay anything & he agreed. He even asked if we would come back again to give them another chance. We stated that we would not, but he gave us his card anyway and asked if we changed our minds to contact him. My friends know that I am a pretty tolerant & easy going person. I know we all make mistakes and a simple apology or courteous behavior would have gone a long way. I usually show my appreciation to an establishment by repeated patronage or a positive recommendation. This is the 1st time that I have publicly made a negative comment due to the blatant retaliatory behavior of the staff.  I believe the excellence of a great establishment is it's willingness to acknowledge it customers concerns and strive to make things right. With my so many other options in NYC we  definitely  will not be back to Gramercy Tavern and if our friends ask we will not hesitate to warn them to go at their own risk if they decide to sit at the bar.
Great food, nice selection of Italian wines.  Attentive service.  Super popular place, reservations are a must.

The a la carte menu is very good and I would highly recommend that. However, the prix fixe menu was disappointing and I would skip it. It was overpriced without being terribly memorable. 

FINAL RATING:
4.25 (a la carte menu)

We did the tasting menu in the dining room, which was very tasty and typical of an upscale tasting menu (small portions, many courses, premium ingredients).

Because it's taken me a long time to write this review, I unfortunately can't remember everything we ate. However, the most memorable and delicious were the lobster appetizer and the halibut entree - both were outstanding and beautifully cooked.

A place like this is renowned for its food, experience and service, and we were absolutely not disappointed. Perfect for a fancy date night or a celebration.

The perfect date spot. The pre fixe menu is really special. Each course is unique and bursting with flavor. The wine menu is fabulous and a lot of great options at reasonable prices. The staff is impeccable. Kind. Warm. No pretense and needless stuffiness. Genuinely there to provide exceptions service. This is a great place to celebrate special occasions. Would go back again. And again.

A somewhat pricy place but much much more affordable if you come here for lunch. I came here for lunch around noon with a friend around 11am on a weekday morning (I was between jobs) and we were seated immediately. All the sommeliers here are incredibly nice and helpful, so do ask them what a good pairing with your dish would be. The menu changes frequently but I had the lamb chop and he had a cod dish, and both were great individually and with their wine pairings. New York City might have the greatest fine dining scene in the world, so if you want a small taste of that, come here. You won't regret it.

After reading so many wonderful things about this place it is with great regret that I'm writing this review.
I made a reservation for my husband and I wedding anniversary which I noted in our reservation when book. We we greeted promptly and sat pretty quickly.
Our server was wonderful and very kind. The food left a little to be desired. We started with the celery soup which was pretty tasty. For our entree I ordered the sea bass and the hubby ordered the duck confit. Both of us were disappointed but he did say my seas bass was better than his confit. 
As we ordered our expresso I eagerly awaited the complimentary coconut cake I read so much about and saw coming and going out of the kitchen. And to my disappointment it never came :( 
My husband was going to ask about it but I was so disappointed over all I told him to forget it. But whats the point of letting them know your celebrating something special if they're not going to do anything.

Favorite restaurant in the city.  My husband and I eat in the "tavern" quite often for lunch on the weekends, and in the main dining room ~4 times per year for special occasions.  
For both dining experiences, the food is not only excellently prepared but you can tell the ingredients are top notch, seasonal and fresh.  The "tavern" has amazing food at pretty reasonable prices - the sandwich special and burger are amazing.  They usually cure their own meats in house.  Pastas are always freshly made.  The main dining room is always a great experience and a great meal.  Service always impeccable.

The front of the house doesn't take reservations, but is a phenomenal deal. Prefix for less than 100$ - and the food is stellar. 

Less enthusiastic about the dinning room, but the tavern is likely the best value for money in the city.

A real once in a lifetime dining experience everyone should try at least once. Impeccable food and service in a wonderful setting. Very expensive but well worth it. The chefs tasting menu is a must. Just go for it.

The food at Gramercy Tavern is undoubtedly delicious.

However, factoring the dollar signs, I'd say that the pre fixe menu doesn't quite live up to its price. It's certainly good, but that money can be well spent on the a la carte menu, with more options and the ability to have more buying power. The dessert menu is also quite underwhelming.

Nevertheless, the food options are indisputably good, the service is impeccable, the complimentary bread is probably one of the best I've had, and the a la cart is the way to go.

It could be because I am part of the industry or it could be because I used to be a member of USHG but I was very underwhelmed by my experience in the Tavern. The food was alright but nothing that would make me return. The service was good but all in all my favorite part of the meal was a dessert; rice pudding. Time to turn it up a notch, Gramercy.
Great food and decor! Had the oysters and sea bass which were excellent. Took off one star because the service wasn't up to par with the prices. Would return.

My god that burger is good.  I want to do a side by side comparison with Spruce, but alas, different coasts.

We ate at the bar, and the service was super slow as the bar was understaffed.  But the bartender was nice.  The drinks were so-so.

But damn, the burger.

Went there for our anniversary and couldn't be happier with that decision. They made it so romantic & special in a modern, trendy atmosphere. Very attentive and knowledgeable of menu. Great food of course. Probably will go there every year for our anniversary now :).

The best dining experience ever!  Fabulous food at a very fair price. Top off the great food with the wonderful staff and this is what a restaurant must be when you dine in heaven! !!  Can't wait to go back.

Finally I've tried this Danny Meyer restaurant in NY! Where I have been all this while...

I was in NY for work and dined solo at the bar. The decor was very classic. Not trendy and hipster type of cool though still has the "a place to be seen at" type of vibe. It's the Gramercy Tavern after all. The atmosphere was great and not stuffy. 

They have Old Overholt in their list of rye whiskey which means extra brownie points from me. I ordered an old fashioned with Old Overholt and watched the bartender make it in front of me. Chris was his name, and upon learning that I was visiting from Chicago, he told me that he helped open The Dawson in Chicago and also worked a summer stint at The Aviary. Wow, amazing coincidence. We bonded a little over what we both had in common: Chicago.

Mind blown by the arctic char tartare. SO good, really. It was topped with cod roe and shredded radish. It wasn't overly dressed which is important to me, so I could taste the freshness of the fish. I transitioned to the pork shoulder as my main which was a good choice. Oh my, the dessert. I had the puff pastry with warm pear and oat ice-cream. Kinda felt like a glutton but whatever right? I was at the Gramercy Tavern. Gotta do what I gotta do and eat right ;)

Me (to the Wait-Person): "It's our 25th Anniversary... so I would like a {Name Brand} vodka martini. Straight up, please."

Wait-Person (WP): "Congratulations on your 25th! How nice for you. Coincidentally, your martini will cost $25.25."

Me (tight grin): "$25.25? That's not so nice. Are you charging me for each year of marriage?"

WP: "Seems like it, but our policy now adds my gratuity into the price and, of course, we can't leave out New York sales tax, can we? And that brings it all to $25.25."

Me: "Well, maybe you have a two-fer deal? If we order two martinis and skip olives can we save S-O-M-E-T-H-I-N-G? ANYTHING?"

WP: "Nope. Two martinis costs $50.50."

Me: "Humm. I'll be back in 25 years for those. Or maybe I won't."

But you know what? There was no conversation with the WP. Wish there was cause that charge appeared on our bill (less gratuity) and that sucked. Big. Time. To me, $25 for a couple of ounces of vodka is worse than sneaky. 

It happened, though, at Gramercy Tavern, in fact on our 25th Anniversary. Wanted to be nice (I'm superstitious) so I gave the Wait-Person a normal tip. 

By the way I'd venture that vodka costs Gramercy Tavern $20 for a bottle (25.4 oz.). I'd also venture there's about 10 martinis in it... $200 worth. I say, "Piggy, piggy, piggy, piggy." 

Future news is grim: Grammercy Tavern owner Danny Meyer, we hear, like it or not, plans to include the gratuity automatically. We fear the price of a martini will creep close to $30. Humm, two martinis for $60.00. Just like Uber. Now there is Martini Surge Pricing!

My boyfriend took me here for my birthday, and what a wonderful experience it was!

We both got the 6-course tasting menu ($120 pp), which actually comes with a couple freebies, so it's a pretty reasonable deal). Unfortunately, I do not remember what the dishes were but some of the memorable ones that I do remember was the sea urchin, striped sea bass, and the wagyu steak - as it is a tasting menu, the portions were small and had me wishing for more! As for dessert, there were quite a few that we had, including the rice pudding (divine!). I was even given a cute little coconut meringue cake for my birthday, candles and all!

The service was impeccable - our waitress was on point with everything and made sure we were taken care of the entire night we were there (and we were there for almost 3 hours!)

A solid 5 stars. This is the kind of restaurant where you don't just go for the food, but you go for the overall experience as well. It is definitely a high-end restaurant so it's perfect for a special occassion (unless you got that $$$$ and can afford to go here on a regular day, then you do you!)

Great service. I came with a couple of friends for lunch. This was not going to be one of those huge special occasion deals. We didn't have a reservation. I found the menu creative and quite good. Everyone was super nice and accommodating. Definitely not cheap but worth it

Follow up:  
I decided to give Gramercy Tavern another try, and I did so (early) on New Year's Eve, of all nights.  Clearly an occasion that frequently proves challenging for many restaurants  -- but not this one!  I must be honest, this time Gramercy Tavern exceeded expectations and absolutely earned their two stars back!  Service was fantastic (and very friendly). Food stupendous.  Ambience great.  And their Christmas decorations were uniquely wonderful.

Terrific atmosphere, good food.  My only complaint is the bartender was rude and overly aggressive in securing seats at the bar for those on the waiting list.  Yes, there is a waiting list for a seat at the bar!! Admittedly it was not my turn on the waiting list (for a bar seat), HOWEVER a kind gentleman, who did have an assigned seat at the bar, and was sitting in it, got up and gave me his seat, while he stood behind me.  The bartender came over to me, raised her voice, and literally kicked me out of the seat (given to me by the man it was assigned to, who was now standing behind me): "You have to get up -- right now -- right now -- that seat goes to the next person on the list."  This experience with the bartender knocks two stars off my rating.

My wife had been expressing a strong interest in having dinner at Gramercy Tavern, so I brought her here for her birthday a couple of weeks ago. The original reservation I had was for 10pm (the only available time), but the folks at the restaurant were really nice and called me when an earlier time slot opened up. Of course, I grabbed it with both hands!

We arrived a few minutes before our reservation, but were seated fairly promptly anyway. We chose the 3-course pre-fix option. The selection of beers and wines is also quite good. Our waiter was very knowledgeable and helpful, and was able to give us a good idea of all the options we had.

We made sure to order different things for each of our courses, so we could try each other's food (i.e. so I could try my wife's food). Each course was excellent - the pasta appetizer particularly stood out in my opinion. The dessert options were also very tasty. The extra dessert (coconut meringue cake) on the occasion of my wife's birthday was a very nice gesture, that we will always remember.

Overall, we had a great experience, and if you're looking for a fine dining experience, this is a pretty solid option.

Great dining experience, from the service to the food in an elegant, but non-stuffy atmosphere.  We tried the seasonal tasting menu with the wine pairings.  My fiance really enjoyed the shrimp and flounder, and I particularly liked the duck.  Everything was exceptional though.  The wine pairings were delicious.  We also received a yummy handmade granola bar to take home!

Fine New American cuisine at a high price point.

We arrived 10 minutes before opening on a Sunday and there was already a small line, but the queue was fast and we were seated promptly.

Bread had unremarkable crumb but an excellent, chewy, smoky crust. Duck liver mousse ($14) contained a real depth of flavor on fine toast, almost like panini, and some pickled vegetables with a salty, savory punch to offset the richness. The wagyu burger ($26) had a rich patty with loose-packed, ultra-tender beef, but was let down by a surfeit of tasteless cheese on top. The potato chips served with it were completely extraneous too, but the patty's quality was such that, along with the optional other toppings to balance the richness (house made ketchup, for example, and good red onion) it was still a successful burger.

Of course this is Manhattan so it's never going to be cheap but with one starter, two entrees, just water and service (professional and fast, but surprisingly reserved given the tavern format) a check of over $80 is a little much for the quality. A very enjoyable meal but one for special occasions as opposed to an everyday tavern experience.

It's mostly my fault that Gramercy Tavern was such a colossal disappointment. 

Reason #1: I walked in expecting to dine at the tavern. Due to circumstances beyond my control, we were only able to dine at the restaurant--which we agreed to. So I wound up spending three times what I had expected to spend. 

Reason #2: I thought Gramercy Tavern was more of a New American place, along the lines of French Laundry or Le Bernardin. You know, a spot that combines familiar American ingredients with a few random non-American ingredients. No, I was mistaken. This place is classic American. As in, you can pronounce and recognize every single item on the tasting menu. I like exoticism. I like words I can't say and have to Wikipedia. I was let down.

Reason #3: I generally assume most high-dollar-sign, Michelin-starred places emphasize gorgeous presentation and elaborate dish* announcements. We got neither here. On the first: I don't mean molecular gastronomy. I just mean nice plating. Nope. On the second: Most of our dishes were presented with little flare and only a general statement of, "And here is your shrimp dish". I must have missed the memo on when they changed that policy.

I appreciate that this restaurant has been around since the dawn of time, and it's a perennial favorite among the upscale NY dining circuit, but I just can't recommend it. Kudos to the hard-working staff who deliver quality service and upscale Americana, but Gramercy Tavern just wasn't for me. 

------------------------------
*The dishes of our seasonal tasting menu were as follows:

Scallop & Cucumber Salad - Fluke, mussels and American caviar
Ruby Red Shrimp - Zucchini, almonds and mint
Poached Halibut - Artichokes, green olives and lobster sauce
Clam Spaghetti - Garlic, herbed breadcrumbs and pickled chiles
Duck Breast & Smoked Thigh - Summer squash, pistachios and cherries
Raspberry - Vanilla rice pudding, pistachios, rose, and basil

Second visit to Gramercy, and I'd say it falls into the "great to visit, not a MUST visit" category. DO make a reservation if you know you are headed here! 

TIP: Lunch tasting menu is 5 courses for $65 seasonal meat or $55 vegetarian! A cheaper way to do a fancy pants meal while on a pseudo-vacation budget! 

Order a la carte or a la tasting menu at lunch or dinner. The food is large-and-by excellent. We had the current seasonal tasting menu, and everything was excellent except the duck agnolotti, which was "un-dunte" instead of al dente, and it was salty as hell. Everything else was tasty.

Service is excellent here with lots of stuff to keep your glass full. Pretty great news- I'm NOT a fan of what their current dessert on the tasting menu is (rice pudding), and our server graciously told me I could sub it for anything else. I had the chocolate custard pie with bourbon, and it was very good.

We came to the conclusion that this meal is best when coupled with lots of boozing; when it got busy, it took a long time between some of the courses, and our meal ended up at a tiring 2.5 hours. 

There are places I would definitely rank ahead of Gramercy Tavern if you are on a strict schedule with limited meals here, but if not, surely worth a try especially at lunch.

This place is wonderful. It's got a Michelin star and its earned it. I mean even the ice cubes are perfect. I went for lunch. I started with the oysters which were excellent. I also ordered the pork shoulder which had an incredible sauce and was the perfect consistency. I took a bite of the special that day a wagyu beef burger. It was unreal. For dessert we shared the butterscotch pudding and cookie platter. What a way to eat lunch!

Top notch. We decided to get at the seasonal tasting menu. Absolutely perfect. The staff was spot on, service was impeccable. Wait staff had wonderful personality with a great understanding of the wine list.

Lunch in the Dining Room - Oh Yeah!!

We decided to hit up this reliable old friend for lunch and were not disappointed. 

The restaurant is as beautiful as ever. Filled with beautiful, seasonal flowers. Nothing old or tired about this place. It has been well maintained over the years. 

We decided to indulge in the Lunch Tasting Menu. We had:

Rolls - I don't normally mention bread, but the rolls were great and the butter was terrific
Lobster with celery root - delicious. The Lobster was perfectly prepared.
Flounder - very soft and tender 
Duck Agnolotti - not something I would normally order, but it was super good
Lamb Loin - cooked perfectly
Selection of Ice Creams - delicious

The service was terrific and our cocktails were amazing.

On the laundry list of places to eat in NYC, Gramercy Tavern was near the top for me. The restaurant is split in two: The Tavern, which is a la carte walk-in only, and The Dining Room, which is a la carte and tasting menu. My table ate in The Dining Room and opted for the tasting menu.

Fun fact, Gramercy now does lunch tasting menus on the weekend! I advise you actually to do a tasting during dinner instead, but more on that in a second.

The décor is akin to grandma's cottage - not exactly a fine dining atmosphere. Fortunately, the service more than makes up for it. The food does as well, of course.

Everything is cooked and prepared extraordinarily. Of note was a cold lobster salad (imagine a lighter version of a lobster roll without the roll) and lamb loin that was like slicing through butter.

My biggest issue with Gramercy, while technically perfect food, is that tasting menus should be enjoyed over a lengthy period of time. I wholeheartedly concur with that sentiment, but my lunch reservation was at 12:30; we left at 3.

2.5 hours. For lunch!

I don't mind if dinner spans a longer period of time, but I ate on a Saturday in one of the coolest cities in the world! I've got stuff to do! Things to see! More food to eat!

So really, it's a lack of foresight on my part. I simply assumed that lunch tasting would be an "express" (I think 1.5 hours is reasonable) version of dinner, but I was sorely mistaken. I wanted to fall asleep in between courses at times.

Still, though, the food really is amazing (and crazy filling) with top-notch service. Definitely worth a try, but make sure you have the patience for a long meal!

Wonderful experience. Stood at bar until they could seat us. Our group ordered Fall Cocktail, Dirty Martini and Moscow Mule. All delish! Once seats were available at the bar, we were seated.  Service was impeccable! All the bartenders were so friendly and helpful. They made us feel like locals! Had the cheese platter and apple pie w/ Brie ice cream .. Yum! Will definately return next time in NY!

Ate in tavern dec 11th. The menu was very very ltd. I ended up with a flat bread
that I could, and would not eat. My friend had the sea bass which was a 4 on a scale of 1 to 10. This place was recommended by 2 of my city friends who now owe me dinner.
The waiter was polite in a way that said i really don't give a damn.
Regarding this restaurant the King has no clothes.

Came here with some friends a couple weeks ago and the restaurant was beautifully decorated for the holiday season. The restaurant was super busy when we arrived for our 7:30pm dinner reservations and had to wait a good 20 minutes or so before we were seated. We felt like the youngest group there (late 20s) while everyone else around us were a lot older, maybe late 30s/40s and up? 

We all decided to do the three course dinner. They started us off with some really good complimentary bread! So good that we actually asked for a second plate of bread while we were waiting for our appetizers. I wish they gave you normal butter along with their special butter which I think had blue cheese in it because since I'm not a fan of blue cheese I couldn't use any butter. But the bread was still amazing on it's own! For my first course I ordered the special, the lobster salad and for my entree I picked the sea bass since my friend said that's one of the dishes they are known for. The lobster salad was really good and they gave us a pretty big portion of lobster as well. The sea bass was also good and big portions but I think the bread and appetizer filled me up pretty good because I could barely eat half of my entree. 

For dessert I picked the pear shortcake which was very delicious and still light enough for me to eat half of it even though I was really full. After the bill came they also gave us some complimentary sweet dessert bites and a homemade granola bar to take home! 

All in all the food was really good and the restaurant was definitely up to par with decor and the quality and quantity of food. The only thing that would have made our experience better is the service. Our waiter was really nice and friendly but we waited a while for our food to come and when I ordered a drink after the first round of drink orders were taken, my drink took forever to come. It came when our second course came out even though i ordered it when we were still eating our bread waiting for our first course.

Damn. This place lives up to its reputation I'm every possible way. 

I walk by Gramercy Tavern every day on my way to work. Finally had a chance to dine there. And let me say it was sensational. 

We started with some great bottles of wine at the suggestion of the sommelier. A fantastic cab that we got two bottles of. Perfectly decanted and poured.
First we got some great bread with sumac butter. Followed by an amuse bouche of pimento ricotta cream puffs, which were great.

My girlfriend went with the squash and grain salad to start, which was essentially two types of squash with quinoa and mushrooms. It was good. Didn't think it was fantastic bit im also not a huge squash fan. I on the other hand had the beef tartare, which was superb. Very high quality filet chopped perfectly with citrus and herbs. Very good. I also tried the lobster salad and smoked trout that others ordered. Both were very good. The lobster was well cooked and tender. The smoked trout was warm from being smoked and was nice and rare in the center.

Next my girlfriend got the arctic char. Which was good. I thought it could have been a little better seasoned but it was amazingly tender and well cooked. I got the duck. A nice piece of breast, and a slice of confit as well. It was hands down the best duck I've ever had. And I've eaten duck at at least 5 michelin star restaurants. 4 out of the 5 of us at the table got the duck and we were all in agreeance that it was the best duck any of us had had the pleasure of consuming.

We finished off with some after dinner drinks, as well as the apple and carob cake, pears and shortbread, chocolate custard pie, a cheese plate, and the birthday coconut cake. All were very good.

Our waiter was very nice and had a great sense of humor. He gave us all kinds of recommendations. The sommelier was also very nice and actually recommended a wine that was slightly under what we told him our preferred price point was. A truly respectable move on his part. The service by all parties was excellent and we were very satisfied after the fantastic experience. We will definitely be returning asap.

I recently spent some time in NYC for the holidays and for my 28th Birthday.  We headed to Gramercy for lunch after Blue Hill was full.  There was a short line down the street at about 11:40 AM, but once the doors opened, we still managed to get a table without a wait.  

When people work in hospitality as their profession rather than as a side job, there's a marked difference in the overall ambiance and feel of a a restaurant.  Such was the case a Gramercy.  We were made to feel welcomed and special - not as a ploy for a good tip - but because the people sincerely love the art of hospitality.  Real sincerity emanates from this place!

The food was absolutely stunning - beautifully presented and nuanced, detailed flavors.  I have a gluten allergy, and was accommodated without any eye-rolls or attitude.  This meant a lot to me!  And the waiter was so helpful in listing my options; he even brought a gluten free mini cornbread with toasted pepitas - absolutely amazing.  No gumminess or crumbly texture - it was rich and buttery, salted perfectly.  

For my lunch, I had the sea bass with broccolini, quince and pecans.  Wonderful.

And then, unbeknownst to me - they brought out a mini gluten free coconut cake for my birthday.  It was on a little stand with a candle, surrounded by toasted meringue.  It was the best gluten free dessert I've ever eaten: creamy layers of coconut cream between a rich coconutty cake; not too sweet, paired with the caramelized meringue...almost too much to handle.  And completely on the house!  

Again, the food at a restaurant can be stunning, but to me, the hospitality has to be sincere in order for the experience to be truly meaningful.  Food is about helping people feel cared for and nourished, and the staff at Gramercy was truly attentive and kind, not because it's their job and they're supposed to be, but because they genuinely delight in what they do. I felt so special on my Birthday!

No joke this was one of the best meals I've had in a few months. I ate the duck meatloaf which was an unusual order for me and it was simply divine. 

I wish I could afford to eat here all the time. The host was extremely accommodating. We came on a Monday night without a reservation and we were seated in 30 minutes in the tavern area. 

My waitress was such a gem too. She had great suggestions on the food and wine and was clearly very knowledgable.

winter tasting menu in dining room $125 12/29/15

one bite cheese puff- underwhelming, why bother?
sullivan st raisin bread and homemade crackers-crackers were ok, bread was good, goat butter was just that and nothing more
lobster appetizer-lobster was tender and overall dish was refreshing but could have used more acidity, again nothing special. 
shrimp-sous vide shrimp lacked flavor, and bed of rice was simply blah. crispy texture from roe was a pleasant and needed surprise
flounder-fish could have been fresher but it was well cooked. i enjoyed the puree however others at my table did not. dish lacked inspirstion and brightness
duck agnolotti-pasta undercooked. could have been filled with anything thus did not do justice to the duck. rethink this dish GT!
lamb- STUNNING. perfectly cooked, flavor was balanced and memorable. clear winner and a favorite by all. 
apple shooter- sparking apple juice refresher. alright?
