deserts- 1)cheese platter- nice selection. would recommend this 2)flan-amazing, excellent acidity and fruitness balanced well with rich smooth texture of flan. yum 3)quince-eh, not memorable and i loveee rice pudding. 

GT simply did not live up to my expectation. Atmostphere was fine, service was OK(served table while one guest was in bathroom a No No!). Overall, while it was a decent meal I would not go back nor would I recommend it to.

Gramercy Tavern is one of my favorite restaurants.  I especially love sitting in the casual area in the front.  I had never had a bad meal.  I love the way they change the menu to reflect the seasons.  Outstanding service as well.  The Dining Room is lovely for a special event or dinner and if you are prepared to dine for a long tasting menu - you won't be disappointed.
We had our first lunch of 2016 in this awesome place. Great service, beautiful decoration, and delicious food. Will definitely go back for other items on the menu.
Top of the line meal! Had the wagyu beef tartare and the lamb squash pasta. Amazing! Drinks are pretty good also and service too.

THE GOOD
Atmosphere: cozy, warm and inviting (First star)
Wine selection: thorough and exciting-you can definitely find a good value on the extensive menu. Wine captain knows her stuff. We were looking for a super Tuscan and she knew a comparable one that was actually less expensive than the one we had picked out. (Second star)
THE BAD
Service: wasn't as attentive as I would have liked. We did the tasting menu and the time between some courses took a long time. Waiting for bill took an unusually long time as well. They forgot our sparkling water yet charged us on the final bill (they removed it)
Food: my husband ordered the regular tasting menu and he said "I didn't leave the meal feeling satisfied". Not to mention the table next to us had a larger serving of the 4th course.
They accommodated (or attempted to) serve me the vegan tasting. One dish came out with cheese and had to be sent back. Another dish came out VERY salty and had to be sent back. I gave them ample warning about my diet and the kitchen didn't seem to care or even have it in their notes.
Final bill: $400 without gratuity.
Oddly enough, it's like they know people will leave hungry so they give out granola bars at the end of the meal. I didn't understand the connection.

I won't go back and sad I parted with $400+ for such a lackluster experience.

I feel like I'm going against the grain saying Gramercy Tavern (not the Dining Room) is just ok. The appetizers were completely different sizes, and so were the mains. I wish there was a better way to delineate which were meant for single eating and which were meant for sharing. Either way we were both stuffed so there was no way dessert was happening. After NYE, I decided to go dry and get an Apple Crisp, and it's definitely the drink to go with if you're trying to look like you're drinking without having any actual alcohol. The service was on point, but the food just didn't blow me away like all the hype around it made me expect.

Last year after dining at Gramercy Tavern I experienced severe food poisoning.  After speaking with the management we were invited back and told that they would "take care of us and make it right".  This past December we went back and they did not make good on their word.  It was very humiliating.

One of our favourite NYC meals and that's saying a lot since we basically ate our way through the city! We didn't have a reservation and went in on a busy Friday night, arriving at 7pm. We expected to wait a while for a table in the Tavern as we were a party of 6, but to our surprise, we waited maybe 15 minutes before the friendly hostess came to grab us as they had a table ready! 

The table ended up being a bit squishy once the 6th person arrived so they relocated us to another table which worked out really well and much more spacious.

Everything we ate really hit the spot. For entrees, the Kielbasa was great as were the other mains, but the Duck Meatloaf was the best! We tried a selection of the appetizers as well and although all were very good, unfortunately I can't remember them all! Cocktails are on the pricier side at $16 each but were strong and good. 

Overall we had a really nice dining experience, great service and nice atmosphere! I highly recommend The Tavern!

This is my husband and my favorite restaurant in NYC. We hosted a dinner party in the private room a few years ago and our guests were all very impressed with the food and service. As a host of the party, the staff made it incredibly easy for us - in fact, I felt like a guest at my own party (which is often not the case if one has to worry about the restaurant "delivering").  Our most recent dining experience was on 1/3/15. The winter tasting menu was delicious. My favorite was the shrimp on black rice risotto. Very very creative use of SE Asian black rice (I confirmed with the chef the it was indeed southeast Asian black rice often used in desserts). I am not a big fan of lobster, but I thoroughly enjoyed the lobster preparation. Bravo once again, Gramercy Tavern.
Our dinner at Gramercy Tavern was memorable. We opted for the tasting menu and the entire experience was spectacular!

GT has been a bucket list restaurant for years!  I really had/have no interest in the prixe fixe dining room, but really wanted to eat at the Tavern.  We went on a Saturday night...got there at 9:00pm and there was still a 90 minute wait!  Normally I would have bailed, but this was the night to eat there...so we put down our name, gave them the cell number and went off for drinks.

A little over an hour later we got a text that our table was ready and so it began...

...GT has a stellar reputation for a reason and it lives up to it.  It reminds me a lot of Blue Hill in the simplicity of the dishes, yet amazing flavors they pull out of such simplicity.  Some favorites are below:

Raw and Roasted Vegetables--I think it's crazy that I'm about to type out that this was my favorite dishes of the evening!  More perfect, flavorful, raw and roasted vegetables I have never experienced.  The contrast of raw and roasted and depth of flavors and textures is incredible.  It changed the way I want to cook and eat vegetables!

Sunchoke Ravioli, Leeks and Reading Raclette--Simple ingredients = Flavor explosion here!  Sunchokes are one of my new favorite foods, and incorporated into the pasta with leeks and cheese really takes the idea of the sum of the "parts" couldn't possibly make a "whole" this good!

Ricotta Cavatelli, Braised Lamb, Kabocha Squash and Almonds--Another head shaker...perfectly cooked pasta, deeply flavored lamb ragu, sweet squash and the nuttiness from the almonds...truthfully altogether bordering on too rich for me...having said that; it was as impressive as everything else in it's execution.  

The service is typical Danny Meyer.  The room was bustling and busy even at 11:45 when we left.

So...yes I do recommend you try GT at least once in your life...for me, it will have to be an off-time, when I don't have to play the waiting game.  I'm truly not sure I need to go back, but I'm glad I can say I've been there.
Best dining experience I've had in NYC. The food and the service were absolutely perfect. Can't wait to go back one day.

This food is simply outstanding!! Our table (2 couples) went there on Saturday for dinner, the staff, food and ambiance was out of this world.  We had, SeaBass, Flounder as well as the duck and everything was outstanding!

If you can't go on holiday this week, go to Gramercy Tavern for lunch. Time stands still in this warm and well run restaurant. There is just the right mix of activity and privacy. The food is excellent, the service is perfect, and the sommelier suggestions for wine pairings is brilliant.

I thought the service here was superb. I came here for an early dinner with an girlfriend and the wait staff really go the extra mile to make the guests feel special. We each got a glass of complimentary bubbly to start our dinner, which was great. We ordered the seasonal tasting menu and the vegetarian tasting menu, just so we can try more than one dish per course. 

The first few courses were the start of the show. The flavors were bright and the combination of sour, sweet and savory went so well together. However, the entree courses really fell flat. Both my friend and I thought the dinner started to fall off around the 4th and 5th courses. The dishes were uninventive and not well executed. 

The dessert was great and brought the meal back on course. We even got a complimentary small cake and also some chocolates and granola bars to take home. 

All in all, I thought the atmosphere at the restaurant was amazing. They have great service and paid attention to every detail. On the food front, I thought the food was uneven, with great appetizer and subpar entrees. I think this is a pretty common issue at many restaurants where the meal just takes a dive after a few courses. You pay more for the server and atmosphere than food.
4.5.  So nice. Went on a Sunday evening.  No wait.  They don't take a res, so call before arrival to find out what the wait time is.  The prix fixe is a great deal...Just go.  You can't go wrong.

I came here with my boyfriend for our anniversary dinner on Sunday January 10th. We had dinner in the Main dinning room, which was not as glamorous as i've immagined. We both had the three course dinner option instead of the tasting menu. We had the Potato  and leek , Celery root, salsa verde & croutons soup- very boring(This soup sounds interesting, but it was not. We were both disappointed), Sea Bass, Parsnip, wild rice and Lobster sauce- Lots of great combined flavors- really enjoyed. BF had the  Warm Lobster, sun chokes, tatsoi and Ponzu salad( VERY GOOD), Duck Breast & Confit, Brussels Sprouts, Hazelnuts & Quince which he loved and thought was memorable.  For dessert, we had the Pear, shortcake, caramel sauce, goat cheese mousse and Pecans- I really liked the combination of different things, but I did not think that it was the best thing i've ever tasted.  We also had the Butternut Squash, cheesecake, walnut, maple milk foam and cranberry sorbet- We both DID NOT like at all. The presentation was very nice, but the taste was just off. We were  very disappointed that the Potato and Leek soup , and that the Butternut Squash dessert was not good. We also received a free plate of chocolate and homemade granola bars which we thought were just okay.

In the end, we did not think that the food was exceptional, but the service definitely was!

What is there to say about this New York classic spot that hasn't already been said? Top notch service, beautiful space, spectacular food...

You can make a reservation in the main dining room but you are locked into a prix-fixe menu. With the dietary restrictions of the person I went with, the Tavern Room was the way to go. While they are great in accommodating, we felt we just had more flexibility in the Tavern Room. No reservations needed for this beautiful, warm, inviting space.

If you enjoy vintage beers, their list does not disappoint. It's one of the only places that offer that kind of selection. Forget the wine, although they do have an impressive wine list, the uniqueness of the vintage beers are the way to do. I spotted a 1999 Rodenbach Alexandre which is a sour Flemish style offering that I have not seen in the states before. Prices are more than reasonable for these bottles.

We started with a delicious calamari flatbread with meyer lemon and purple potatoes. This dish packs a punch and the flavors work so well together. The calamari was tender and added a different texture contrasting the crunch of the flatbread, and tender soft creaminess of the potatoes. The Arctic Char Tartare, was well dressed with bacon, apple, and parsnips but it wasn't as exciting as the flatbread being that the fish was very mild tasting.

For the main dish, my date had the Guinea Hen roasted with chestnut puree and brussels sprouts. The Guinea Hen was tender and worked really well with all the unique ingredients. I have to get it myself next time if they still have it. I got the Sea Bass with Broccoli Rabe, slices of pear, and toasted pecans in a Mustard Sauce. This was done in a classic way and is a great dish. Everything is made with the freshest seasonal ingredients.

We finished off with some Intelligensia Black Cat espressos to end the evening.

It was a beautiful night and a great restaurant to share a few bites. I love that it is a classic spot, but with an inviting casual Tavern Room, and even have vintage beers. Gramercy Tavern hasn't changed much in years and I hope it stays this charming spot that I always love to go to.

I have come here multiple times now to eat in the Tavern - both for dinner and for lunch - always a great experience. Having read Danny Meyer's book, Setting the Table", I have a deep appreciation for his concept of dining, and Gramercy Tavern really delivers exceptionally on that concept.

The atmosphere is comfortable, not stuffy. The staff friendly, inviting and helpful. The food...delicious. The cocktails, works of art.

Highly recommended for any occasion.

Okay, let's start out by establishing that Yelping about Gramercy Tavern is ridiculous.  But last night was so incredible that I really wanted to add just a few things to the pantheon of comments:

- classic without being stuffy at all.  it's not always easy to get a michelin-starred meal for those of us who usually sit at the bar.

- everyone around you is thrilled to be there.  coming here is an event for most people.  that's a very, very good thing.

- this ain't alenia.  you are not having food you've never had before, particularly with the seasonal menu.  you are having amazing classic food.

- get the wine paring.  it's pretty reasonable in the scheme of things, and you'll try things you wouldn't have been able to try otherwise.

Two final thoughts:

- the one quasi-negative of the evening is that the current vegetable tasting is *heavy*.  they are so great with vegetables, but right now the menu falls into the trap of good veggie dishes=heavy.  our party of three went 2 veggie tastings and 1 meat tasting, but in retrospect, i'd have reversed it solely due to portion size.

- the staff knows that you are there for a special night, and they really make sure you feel it.  in many ways, it's a better experiance than the few places up michelin-star chain for this reason alone.*


* digression.  i hate clubs.  never understood why until i was b.s.ing with a bar-tender, and he pointed out to me that clubs reverse the usual customer-business dynamic.  at clubs, the customer is supposed to genuflect and feel grateful that the club finds them cool enough/hot enough to admit--i feel the same way about certain 3-star restaurants.  gramercy tavern is the opposite of that:  they go out of their way to make you feel that they are lucky you chose them.  i really appreciate that.

One of my favorite places to dine on this side of the pond! I ususally dine here once a month and it's still does not get old. Ask for the sommelier Alvaro! he's the best, he always ushers us into a amazing diining experiece by pairing some of the best wines with our course.

Underwhelming. We got the lunch tasting menu both the seasonal and the vegetarian. My favorite was the smoked Arctic char - cooked perfectly with great flavor. My friends loved the first course - the lobster. Everything else was really salty and very average. Good wine selection, but took forever to get it. Service is very slow so make sure you have more than a couple of hours for lunch.

Fantastic. This place is very well-organized and the food is exquisite. The bartenders really know how to make a drink and the rest of the wait staff is top-notch. Pricey but 100% worth it - definitely recommend.

Where to begin??? 

I think the BIG problem with Gramercy Tavern might actually be me! My wife and I were meeting two sets of friends from college for a "reunion" weekend of sorts and to celebrate a 25 wedding anniversary. One couple came all the way from California, another trained in from Connecticut, and we made the trek up from DC. We were all excited about having that Holy Grail foodie experience in NYC and reviewed several options, but were limited in our choices due to a Sunday night reservation. 

We gathered at the restaurant a little early - about 30 minutes before our anointed time - and the hostess staff could not have been more accommodating or pleasant. We hung out at the bar while waiting for the CT couple to show up, and had a fun time. The hosteses, Meghan and Livia were stars - they kept coming over to the bar and checking in on us. They were aware that I brought some special wines to serve with dinner and reviewed their corkage policy with me. When we did finally sit down at the table in the formal dining room, our server was polite and enthusiastic about helping us decide on course selection based on the wines I had in tow. She was very knowledgeable about wine pairings. We selected the three-course tasting menu.

But the food, all of it, was just, well, meh. I mean it was good... but it wasn't OMG Great! I guess our expectation outpaced our experience, and that's why I think it might be my (our) fault. It was classic food done well, not great.

I had the special snow crab pasta as a starter and the duck two-ways as an entrée. The pasta dish was very good, with shredded pieces of crab. The portion size was decent. And the duck was fine - but I mean, just fine. Nothing wrong with it - the confit portion had a crispy skin and tender meat and the breast portion was four small slices cooked to a nice medium-rare, but it was slightly under-seasoned and lacked any kind of gaminess to remind you that you are eating Duck - it was closer to chicken than it was to duck.

Dessert was fine. A decent selection, but nothing out of the park. The cheese selection was excellent, but we never got a description of the cheeses!

My only two negative observations were that we went out of our way to share our wine with the wait staff AND the kitchen and were still charged full corkage for all three bottles. Now, I know that corkage is a privilege and NOT a right, but it was still a first for me... my normal experience has been that when you order wine off of the menu (which we did) AND you share your wine with the staff, the corkage - for at least one bottle, and usually all bottles - gets comped. Well, not here... at least, not for us. Which is too bad, because we are very generous tippers when that happens.The other observation - it is A LOT of money to spend on just-good food. All in, it was about $250/person. While it may not be a lot by NYC standards, it is by mine - and I was expecting to be blown away (like the night before at Betony).

So - bottom line; Great service, friendly staff, nice atmosphere. Just too expensive for the food you get and the corkage fee left a sour grapes (pun intended) taste in our mouths.

I have been dying to try this place for so long. So when I finally got the chance to try just how good Gramercy Tavern is, I had such a high expectation. Thankfully, I was beyond satisfied. We had our dinner at the dining room. It's a pity I did not try the tasting menu, but the ones I ordered were excellent. Will definitely have to go back to try the Tavern and the tasting menu. One last thing, the duck was indeed the best!

Everyone should have that one perfect dinning alone experience. One that you can keep going back for and it not only stays the same, it just might get better every time - you solitary enjoy every moment: a dream perhaps. 
My solo* dream: Gramercy Tavern. 

With their wonderful, always perfectly complementing the menu selection of wines I tend to start my solo cozy journey with a red (although I've strayed to their wonderful selection of seasonal cocktails and Champagnes - There is always an excuse to drink Champagne!)  
On this my dream of "I couldn't possibility keep count"  it was a glass (or two) of the St. Aubin, Prudhon, Cuvée Les Rouges Gorges, Burgundy, which at $19.50 a glass you swear you're stealing it.

On these solo dreams I am almost always predictable. The prediction is simple: Beef Tartare.  I'm not dreaming yet fully awake when I say the following " The Gramercy Tavern has the BEST Beef Tartare in all of NYC!"  

That's right, the very best. I could eat it for days and months and years. And I have been! Gamercy Tavern prides it's self on being ' fiercely seasonal' and that it is as many of the dishes here stay the same as the magical jewels that surrounded them and elevate them to new levels change as our seasons and local farms do.  Today I'm riding on a tartare cloud surrounded by Asian pear, rye and pine nuts. One time there were fresh flava beans, last time I was here Brussels sprouts.  

Each bite is perfect, each scoop on the perfectly toasted bread points has me never wanting to wake up.

And then as I walk out the door I do awake, only to have nightmares that this place never did exists...but of course it does and of course I'll be back. Just a girl, some wine, a book, and some tartare. 

* I prefer solo dream dinning to happen on midweek extended lunch hours.

Honestly, I didn't think I was going to love this place, even though I chose it. It's old fashioned, been around for a while, mainstream/a lot of people know about it... and I usually prefer the hidden gems. Boy, was I wrong!

Friend and I came here for a business anniversary day after New Year's, and it was one of the best meal experiences I've had. I don't use that phrase lightly!

Our waiter made the experience for us. His friendliness and attention to detail was incredible. I wish I knew his name so I could give him props, but one of the best waiters of all time. My dining partner was a vegetarian which was part of reason we chose this place - they have a vegetarian tasting menu. I got the regular tasting menu, she got the veggie tasting menu, and we both got the respective wine pairings. They're very accommodating about asking if you have food allergies, or if you straight up don't like any food. Though I appreciate no substitution policies and that dishes need to be executed in the chef's vision in order to convey the message blah blah blah... I loved that I could tell our waiter that I can't stand the taste of olives, and that he would make sure there were no olives :)

Would take me all day to go into each of the dishes, so just trust that they were all delicious. Couldn't pick a favorite, which is a good sign for the meal. I don't know if it was actually the wine or our waiter's description or presentation of the wine, but this was the first time where I really tasted the connection between the wine and the food. Our waiter went into what was complementary about each and why they were chosen, which really helped us taste the pairing's intention. I looked up some of the wines after and they aren't your run of the mill crowd pleasing restaurant wine - these are some obscure wines! And each was fantastic.

Example of our waiter's attention to detail - my friend went to the bathroom, waiter came out to pour our next wine pairings, and I saw him recognize the fact that she was not at the table, and he turned around and came back when she was there, so that she could hear about the wine. I know that sounds like a small thing, but I've experienced tasting menus where the wine is an afterthought and poured if someone is in the bathroom, and it just showed how on point this guy was with orchestrating our experience. 

Don't let the tons of reviews and storied history make you think this place is popular because all the old timers like it - No! It's a spot I will remember fondly and would love to go back to.

Had lunch here and had high hopes based on reviews, reputation and initial service we received. From there it went downhill. 

In not too many words I'd say the food was insultingly small in terms of serving size. Furthermore, the food was so seasoned you could not taste the ingredients. All we got was hot salt burn followed by insatiable thirst!

For the price of the meals and the reputation I expected so much more. I won't return. There are so many far superior places nearby.

Review is based on our experience at Gramercy Tavern on December 29, 2015. 
We never got beyond a clueless unprofessional hostess. Upon arrival we inquire about seating protocol and was told 'first come first served' in the bar/tavern area and a wait list for dining area. So it's mid afternoon and we are there only for a drink, so we opt to monitor bar area for an open table. As one became available, we moved to table, only to have same hostess come over and state that although this is a first come.... area, there is a waiting list!? Somewhat embarrassed by the experience and since hostess now declared wait was an hour, we left and not likely to return. Feedback; Change your website that indicates no reservation required in bar, and provide some additional training to your hostess staff, which are the first face of your establishment. I'm only out the cab fare!
My absolute fav restaurant in NYC. The beautiful souls and ambiance warm and fuzzy & the seasonal menu vibrates at a high frequency. All together a magnificent experience!
Even tho it was restaurant week and we had to wait over an hour at the bar... Food and service were top notch!! Duck meatloaf? Epic!!!
Swanky. Went for lunch. Great menu and service. Solid drinks. Here were you go to have a bit more space to chat to clients I'd say. Ideal for secrets.

I go back again and again.... Service atmosphere food all of it rolled together is what sets Gramercy Tavern apart and why I will continue to come. 
From the Sommelier to the wait staff and management you feel comfortable and at home. 
The food....FANTASTIC 
Wine ... Selection .... Unbeatable....
What I can say has already been said over its 20 years as one of the top restaurants in the World. 
A must for any foodie...

Sat in the front - had a fun waitress.  Lots of after-work types - food was okay but nothing exceptional.  I would honestly say it's about as "average" as it can get in terms of this place.  I don't think the four $'s is accurate - it's not THAT expensive compared to other similar spots but as said, nothing that makes me say "I need to come back here again."  It's blah to me - find out for yourself, if you must.
Excellent dinner, I had a food allergy and they were very accommodating.  Great place for date night.

I'll keep this short and sweet, the food here is fantastic. We had the tasting menu and every course was delicious. But, as good as the food was, the service was even better. Attentive without being overbearing. If you're lucky enough to get Siobhan as your waitress you'll definitely be treated well. Awesome experience all around

I went with my husband and we did the seasonal tasting and pairing which was fantastic. The cauliflower tortellini was unreal and the lobster starter was so different than how We had ever had lobster served. I had told the hostess we were celebrating and they sweetly sent out a glass of champagne for us both to start the meal and then during the pairing I realized that I really didn't care for one of the wines and without hesitation our server offered to grab another to make sure I was happy- and I definitely was. The food was awesome, service was impeccable and I want to go back!

I'm definitely the type of girl that loves her food - everywhere as long as the flavors, textures, and service is all there. Then again, I do love my fancy foods too. 

The Gramercy Tavern was one of my many choices when I was in New York. I partly wanted to try the dining room, but my friend and I decided on the tavern half since it was easier to get seating there.  We ended up sitting close to the edge of the dining room which isn't separated by too much. 

I ended up ordering the Jalisco pear as a drink - definitely delicious, but slightly small for the price. Alcohol versus price value was okay. The chicken liver mousse I ended up ordering for my appetizer (since I do love mousse), but it was a LARGE plate to food. I do wish there was more of delineation of what items are definitely sharing and which appetizers are small enough for a hungry person. I then ordered the burger that's supposed to be secret or at least not on the menu because it is apparently really delicious. It was good, but definitely not the best burger I've ever had. 

Guess I'll just have to try the dining room someday to really make my final decision on this place. 

Protip: reservations for the dining room. Tavern is a little less full, but still busy at times.

Reading through reviews I noticed a lot of people raved about the cookie and milk tray. Going to such a nice restaurant I didn't get the appeal of something as basic as cookies. Let me tell you - I was so wrong! These cookies were amazing. Bite after bite each cookie was better than the previous. Chocolate chip, snicker doodle, coconut macaroon , walnut bar, pb square .

A beautiful experience.  My company came here for a group dinner and I had heard from a friend who trailed in the kitchen how great the staff is in addition to the food.

Service: The waiters are unpretentious and attentive on both the wine and the meal.

Environment: Very festive during the holidays (Dec 2015), and 

Food: We had the regular prix fixe dinner menu except one person who was vegetarian and expected to be disappointed because she generally doesn't like anything too crazy.  Every dish was meticulously made and very flavorful, although small (but I guess that's how it is with fancy places).  The vegetarian coworker LOVED her food.  In fact she said it was the best meal she's ever had at a restaurant, and she's eaten in some fancy places.

If I have the opportunity to come back, I will.

My kind of spot. A very accessible spot, no need to dress up for this place, casual works well. Ordered a cavelli ( really good) monkfish (good) and Nebbiolo wine. Spent less then $100. Worth a visit.

This was an amazing, amazing lunch. The service was spectacular, and the food was to die for. We ordered duck liver mousse (the best I've ever had), cauliflower soup, ham and raclette sandwich, the burger, and the kielbasa. 

The hot chocolate is a MUST-ORDER. So delicious and the homemade marshmallows made it.

Have now also tried the steak sandwich (yummy), a beet/strawberry appetizer which we loved, and a seafood soup which I liked but wouldn't necessary order again.

The food was delicious but I wanted to mention the service.  Our waitress (Captain Liz), knew every answer to any questions I had about the food and wine list. She was totally delightful with a warm, charming and fun personality. 
I had to use the restroom so I asked another waiter where it was. He didn't point, he walked me right to it! 
Everyone from the coat check lady, host, bartender, and (waiters that weren't for our table) were so cheerful and polite. They all seemed to like their jobs. 
This restaurant was run like a well oiled machine! They even brought extra 'goodies' to try and a morning breakfast bar to take home. 
Everyone needs to experience this extra fine dining experience. 
5 STARS!!

Great food, excellent service and ambience. I love the shrimp risotto (the shrimp tasted absolutely amazing) and the final course lamb loin ( cooked & garnished perfectly ). The bread is soft and warm (or hot), my second favorite bread behind EMP.

In my opinion, Gramercy Tarven  offers beyond standard delicious food, I enjoy everything courses;  flavor and texture are impeccable. However, the only downside is that I didn't find it too inspiring or I would give it 5 stars. Nevertheless, it is still one of my favorite place to go when I am in crave of consistent high-quality food.

Came here for the first time to celebrate my wife birthdate, both of us had the 3 course menu a la carte, the best dishes: garganelli with pork ragout, sea bas with sweet potatoes and a very good chocolate crust tart! Everything perfect, only our waiter very nice guy but disappeared several times during the dinner. Very nice restaurant.

One of the most pleasant and delicious lunches I have had in NYC. My partner and I enjoyed the tasting menu with pairings. The service was professional, on point, and generous. The experience rivaled Jean Georges.
Amazing restaurant. Amazing service and menu. A great place to bring a date for a 1st class night out in Manhattan.

Perfection. That burger. That lobster starter (paired with wild rice to make it GF). They even have a gluten free bread option. A sweet potato and crispy onion muffin. Hands down the best GF bread substitute I've ever eaten. Service was impressive. It's nice to know lots of people still pay attention to detail and really care about providing their customers with not only great food but also provide them with a pleasurable experience. I think our server's name was Rick. If so I want to publicly thank him for a wonderful experience.
Reminds me of the hottest girl from High School that peaked 10 years ago. This place will steadily satisfy you if money is no object but lost its wow factor.

My boyfriend and I frequent Gramercy Tavern a few times a month. It NEVER disappoints. The food is always outstanding and service great. I seriously have dreams about the desserts! The chocolate pudding cake is the best thing I've ever had in my life. I also love the apple pie & brie ice cream, 

I absolutely love sitting in the bar area and ordering the tasting menu -- one of the best deals in the city!

Well, at the time I'm writing this, Gramercy Tavern has a solid 4.5 stars over almost 1,900 reviews.  Look around...that is not an easy thing to do!  So, rest assured, this place is in no need of my opinion or commendations, but that won't stop me from giving them.

To start, the service you'll find here is absolutely top-notch, from the coat check to the hostess to the waitstaff and all, these people are at the top of their game. The term "professional" is probably the best descriptor I can think of; there is nothing unnecessary or artificial in their delivery.  They are polite, direct, and very knowledgeable on the things they serve. In a restaurant, this can be a difficult thing to achieve, but those who work here have pretty much nailed it.  

For the food, what more can I say...it was delicious. The menu shows that experienced and creative minds are at work here, and I can't imagine anything served would be less than praiseworthy.  The banana cream pie dessert just about made my day...it's "for two" as advertised, but can easily become "for one" after you realize just how good it is. Combine this with a bar serving perfectly-made $19-dollar Sidecars, and, even in the town of 10,000 restaurants, this is a place I will gladly and anxiously return to.

Amazing service and delicious food. I went with a few colleagues for lunch. We had the lobster salad for our 1st course. Delicious, tender, lobster. For my 2nd course I had the red snapper, tender, and seasoned perfectly. All around great food and atmosphere. I'd love to go back and try even more.

Came here with my gf for a pre-valentine's dinner at the dining room since booking at prime time is very difficult. We both got the seasonal tasting menu. My gf also got the orange blossom cocktail. They started us off with complimentary bread and a cheese puff. The bread was very soft and warm. So let's start rating the 6 course menu:
1-Lobster salad: 3/5, good to start off to open up your appetite but nothing extraordinary 
*My gf happened to find a lobster cartilage/shell inside the salad, we didn't make a big deal out of it, we were just staring at it at first wondering what it might be and talking amongst  ourselves . Our waitress then comes over telling us her colleague noticed my gf found some inside. She insisted in taking it back to show the chef and asked my gf if she would like another one but my gf declined. 
2-Ruby red shrimp: 4/5, black rice was interesting and the roe+shrimp makes for a good taste
3-Smoked arctic char: 5/5, very moist and flavorful with the crushed pistachios
3.5-Lobster with stuffing/potato on the side: 5/5, this was a complimentary dish for my gf due to the lobster salad incident, we enjoyed this dish more than the lobster salad
4-Cauliflower tortellini: 3.5/5, not sure if the tortellini was made from cauliflower or there was cauliflower inside but the sauce makes a good dip for our bread
5-Duck breast and confio: 5/5, I've had duck at asian places before but this dish took it to a whole new level, very soft and tender. WIN!
6-Caramel Flan/Warm Chocolate Cake: 4/5, nothing can go wrong with warm chocolate cake and (ginger) ice cream, the flan was on the sweeter side
They also gave us some pieces of fruity chocolates post-dessert, granola bars for tomorrow's breakfast, and took off the cocktail from our bill because of the lobster salad.
Overall,
-Decorations 4/5, the bathroom (men) seems small. There were only 2 urinals and 2-3 stalls for a restaurant of this size. 
-Food 4.5/5, full in flavor and variety
-Service 6/5, my water was always filled, ensures everything is going well with our meal, it's the little things that count

The same menu is served in the Tavern and the dining room but the prices in the latter were a little more for better service and roomier seating. The freshly warmed bread puffs were light and airy as was the whipped butter. The apps were small but good - lobster salad was poached and beets were tender. The sea bass was served in a light coconut milk broth with mushrooms and parsnips $28. It's clear why this place is loved by locals and visitors.
You can't beat the service, professional staff, knowledge, and friendliness. The lunches are outstanding and the drink selection is full spectrum.

It wasn't a bad experience but it wasn't that impressive either. Bread wasn't warm when served to us. Calamari Flat bread was just ok. And among the main courses, I would say that the Sunchoke Ravioli beats the Lamb T bone and the Monkfish. The intervals of wait from sitting you, to taking the orders and serving appetizers to the main course, were so long to their own detriment since there were parties of three, or two that could have been seated if food came in faster than half an hour. Service was very polite and even friendly. Wait staff is very well trained. The ambience is worth coming for though. We were at the Tavern and it was definitely livelier than the Dining Room which seemed austere. I would definitely go back if the meals were more memorable, but the only thing memorable was the chocolate pudding cake with coconut ice cream.

Came here for Valentines Day and dinner was superb. The service was top notch and catered to our every need. I have a shellfish allergy and they were able to accommodate with great dishes.

We started with a small clam appetizer and a squash salad which was nice and fresh. We then had hamachi tartare with golden beets, blood orange and black rice. My girlfriend is not too fond of tartare but we both loved he freshness and savor of the dish. The next course was sea scallop with caramelized cauliflower, fennel, and kumquat for my girlfriend and a carrot soup for me. Both tasted very good. Next course was saffron taglierini with snow crab, Swiss chard and caviar and I had a cauliflower risotto. My girlfriend was in love with the taste of the taglierini while I enjoyed the polenta. Both dishes were top notch and made the dinner worth it. Next was smoked sturgeon with red cabbage, pistachios and horse radish. We have never tried sturgeon but it was very good. Texture of the fish was exceptional and the cabbage and horse radish complimented the dish. The main dish was roasted duck with squash, apples and foie gras. The duck was cooked very well and the apples and squash had a nice sweet taste. I was never a fan of foie gras, but I did try it and it was ok. The dessert plate did not let us down with an assortment of chocolate and marshmallow ice cream. It was the icing on the cake for a wonderful Valentine's Day dinner.

I would recommend going there if you can get a reservation in the main dining room. Just be aware that it is pricey but worth every penny.

The seasonal tasting menu for lunch is one of the best deals in the city ($55 to $65). Service is better than any fine dining restaurant I've been to (including Eleven Madison) - I think it was the best service I've ever had at any restaurant in the city. No music in the dining room - may be a good thing depending on preference. Expansive drinks menu. Food's great. I've had better vegetarian meals elsewhere but combined with the service, it's hard to find a better overall dining experience in NYC. Four and a half stars is a good assessment.

Came for lunch about 2pm with no res, they got us a great table back in the main dining room and treated us like a king and queen.
We both had the tasting menu, great food, great cocktails and wines, great service.
It couldn't have been better. I've dined at the front bar before, but never back in the main dining room. It's set up like a real dining room, with space between tables like dining rooms used to be.
Lunch was $200 for 2 with a $45 tip - and worth every penny.
Gramercy never disappoints, and their service is so gracious and professional, its really special.
Cant wait to go back for another cocktail and wine oriented tasting menu lunch.
Are you kidding me?  The waiter touched the wine bottle to the glass and didn't rotate.  The 7 course was enough to feed a bird.  Never go here unless you are an old man with a mail order.

Came here for lunch on a Saturday and tried the seasonal tasting menu. Overall a great experience: food  was good and service was awesome. The smoked Arctic char was probably the best among all the dishes we had. Will probably come back to check out other dishes.
incredible incredible restaurant. beautiful and cozy interior, friendly staff, and amazing food. highly recommend the lobster salad (appetizer) and the duck (entree).

I dined here recently with a friend to celebrate her birthday. It was a memorable experience. We each had (if memory serves) a glass of chenin blanc. Delicious! We also each chose for our appetizer the warm lobster salad. Wonderful. We were treated to complimentary tiny clams. Delicious. (I know I'm repeating myself.) My companion had sea bass for a main course; I had red snapper. Her dish was very good; mine was excellent. We had sorbets and ice cream for dessert. But when the waiter (and the service was excellent all around) heard that it was my friend's birthday, he brought out additional sorbets and other treats. In short, we both had a great time. The entire staff was extremely friendly, professional and totally unpretentious. Dining at the Gramercy Tavern was an absolute pleasure.

I am speaking of the dining room, not the tavern, although I imagine that the tavern side of the restaurant is also excellent.

My boyfriend and I went for our anniversary at around 2 PM. The space is elegant but not intimidating, and they welcomed us with a glass of complimentary prosecco before we ordered anything. We opted for the lunch tasting menu with wine pairings, since at five courses, it seemed quite reasonable compared to other Michelin-starred restaurants at $65 for the food and $48 for wine. The courses included: 

Lobster
Celery Root, Apple and Horseradish
Rosé Brut, Mas de Daumas Gassac, NV, Languedoc, France

Arctic Char
Sunchoke, Pistachios and Preserved Lemon
Muskateller, Loimer, 2013, Kamptal, Austria

Cauliflower Tortellini
Salsify, Parmesan and Black Trumpet Mushrooms
Pinot Noir, Belle Pente, Murto Vineyard, 2011, Willamette Valley, Oregon

Duck Breast & Confit
Brussels Sprouts, Hazelnuts and Quince
Gigondas, Goubert, 2011, Southern Rhone, France

For dessert, however, we were allowed to select our own preferences, where I chose a chocolate custard pie and my boyfriend the cheese plate. I am not a dessert person, but the chocolate--and my macchiato--were just sublime.

It is difficult to choose my favorite course, since all of the dishes played with texture and flavor expertly, the courses followed each other seamlessly, and we were simply delighted with the wine pairings. Our server was extremely knowledgeable, happy to accommodate a dietary restriction, and cordial without being over-attentive. When we selected our dessert, for example, he proposed to change our wine pairing from the standard one on the tasting menu so that the flavors would shine better. He gave my partner half pours of two wines, given the diversity of cheese flavors. His choices were excellent and I felt not only sated but as if I had learned more about food and wine. 

Having eaten at several Michelin restaurants in NYC, this was one of the best dining experiences I have had. Highly recommended.

Gramercy Tavern is a great place for special occasions. The season menu is delicious.  The restaurant is larger than it seems from the outside.  It is a serious restaurant with excellent service.  From the moment I walked in, I was treated wonderfully.  The staff was extremely professional, yet friendly and down to earth.  The next time I go, I would like to try the regular menu because I'm not too into the duck on the seasonal menu not because it wasn't good, but because it's just not my taste.  The seafood dishes are excellent.  It's difficult to get a reservation so you have to call early in advance.  Their processco was uncommonly good, along with the selection on their wine tasting menu.

I've been a customer for lunch and dinner for years--always in the tavern--and there is nothing else like it.  It's not just the excellence of preparation, inventiveness of cuisine and warmth of service, but G.T. is a training ground for new chefs who go everywhere and do everything.  G.T. is a unique resource that Gotham can't afford to lose.

I went here on a date and needless to say the food was amazingly good. The service was wonderful, the decor simple and nice. There were flowers everywhere. If you happen to be served by Amy, youre in good hands! I will surely be returning.

The dining room was excellent and overall, this was one of the most memorable dining experiences I've ever had. The seasonal menu is exceptionally well prepared and literally delectable. Can't wait to try summer menu.

Had lunch with coworkers this past Thursday.  We shared 4 appetizers. My favorite was the spinach fettuccine we ordered as an app.  The beet salad, beef tartar, and bollonaise were also good.  I had the pork shoulder which was cooked perfectly with vegetables which matched very well.  Service was attentive and friendly.  Great dining experience.
Came here for my birthday last year and it was one of my most favorite meals in the city! If you are looking to splurge, look no further!

This review is for the dining room and not the tavern. I found the service and food exceptional. The waiter took a good amount of time to explain the menu and drinks.  
I had the beef tartare for appetizer, lamb for main course, and chocolate cake for dessert.  My favorite of all three was the lamb. As you chew the lamb, the flavor keeps on opening up. After you swallow the lamb, the flavor never leaves your mouth.  The lamb was delicious. 

At the end, the restaurant gave us chocolate truffles that were out of this world. I've asked if I can buy some to take home, but they don't offer the truffle for sale.  I also learned they make the truffle in house. 

The restaurant also gave us a granola bar to eat the following day for breakfast. I thought that was kind of them. 

Overall, I highly recommend this place! Great service, great food, and great experience.

It was our first time visiting the Tavern and it was one of the best dining experiences of my life.  Having celiac I get nervous about eating out but the staff took such care that it wasn't an issue (I was even given a tiny but delicious gf pumpkin bread).  We went with all of our waitress Siobhan's recommendations for apps and wine pairings and she nailed it every time.  Not only are we planning our next visit for this Friday but we will definitely request to have Siobhan be our waitress.  She, along with the amazing food, made for an amazing night!

Love this beautiful location & of course their delicious food!  There's so much about this place you can enjoy..  good food, nice staff and the bar!  They offer regular menu as well as tasting menu and it is a must try!

Our trip to Gramercy Tavern is in thanks to my boss, who suggested we try it out on a recent trip to NYC. While we normally wouldn't have stopped somewhere of this caliber (usually we prefer a little more low-key), we highly enjoyed our experience. We had to wait for about an hour for a table on a Monday night, but ended up eating at the bar when a seat opened up. We ordered a delicious bottle of Riesling, which was suggested by the wine steward. She was extremely nice, understood exactly what we were asking for (we aren't wine aficionados, and weren't looking to spend a fortune, just wanted a decent bottle at a good price). She didn't try to upsell us, and she didn't look down on us for not wanting to spend a fortune.

We ordered the raw/cooked vegetable appetizer, and the calmari/clam flatbread pizza to start. They both were very good, although I'd skip the vegetables next time. For dinner, I had the fish mushroom fried rice which was DELISH! When I saw mushroom fried rice as an entree, I wasn't expecting too much. When our server told us that it was one of the most popular dishes, I had to try it.  I'm so glad I did. My husband had the duck meatloaf, and said it was fantastic. We left feeling very full and satisfied.

The restaurant is very trendy inside, and it's definitely worth a stop, if you can get a table!

Prepare to dress up, feel fabulous and fine dine to your heart's content. Do make a reservation well in advance and start the countdown to a great night out. 
Attentive, professional service, (complimentary chocolates with tea), beautiful surroundings and a delicious menu make a lovely night out.
Very classy and ritzy place! Great service and awesome drinks. The food was very good as well as the service with beautiful ambiance.

I am writing this review probably 4 months after dining in. 

I went to Gramercy tavern around Thanksgiving time, 2015. Our family ordered the seasonal tasting. We loved all the dishes. What I still remember from many months ago is their lamb dish. 

I come from Asia culture where not many people are raised with eating lambs. In fact, I have not met much people who eats lambs in our country. That being said, sometimes the smell of lamb's particular flavor can be hard for me to eat. However, gramercy's lamb was perfectly cooked. I loved different textures of their lambs and how juicy they were. 

What I also liked among the tastings was of course, their desserts. We tried 3 different kinds and ended up loving them all. Chocolate ganache cake was so rich and smooth that really culminated our culinary experience.

Any time you have the opportunity to eat at a New York institution such as Gramercy Tavern, you must savor the experience.  Besides the food, the atmosphere and decor is lovely and the service is 5 star.

I started my meal with the duck ragu with gargenelli.  I think this was actually the highlight of the meal - the ragu was very flavorful and the pasta was delicious.  I went with the lamb loin for my main course.  It was cooked perfectly and had good texture, but the meat did not blow me away the way it did at Quality Italian or Minetta Tavern.

If I had to return to one of the five star restaurants, Gramercy Tavern would not be at the top of the list.  However, the food was still superb and the ambiance excellent.

I've been to the dining room once, but where this restaurant really shines is its tavern room. A regular lunch spot for me and my fiancee, we have tried almost all of their dishes and it has always been a perfect combination of tasty, fresh and fairly priced. I finally tried their "worst kept secret" burger (after constantly observing everyone around us eating it), and it was DELICIOUS. Juicy and flavorful - perhaps one of the best that I've had in the city. I would highly recommend stopping in here for lunch. Its more casual than you would imagine, and always a fun dining experience. I would just advise getting there by noon if you dont want to wait (on our most recent visit we arrived at 1230 and just about managed to snag a couple of seats together at the bar).

I had wanted to eat at Gramercy Tavern forever but never had the opportunity. Well, this past Friday was my birthday and my amazing boyfriend took me there for dinner.
First let me say that everyone working there was very friendly, front of house, wait staff, everyone we encountered. The service was excellent and attentive. No complaints there.
I had very high expectations for the food. I had been hearing about and reading reviews of this place for years. Don't get me wrong, the meal was good, but it wasn't amazing. 
We had the seasonal tasting menu with the wine pairings. Hats off to the sommelier. The pairings were very good. 
As for the food, there was really only one dish that knocked our socks off, the tortellini was excellent, but the rest was honestly nothing to write home about. The flavors just didn't wow like I expected them to. Plus my duck course looked like the very end of the breast and was more fat than meat.
Doesn't mean I didn't have a good meal. Like I said the service was beautiful and they brought me a sweet little cake for my birthday. All very nice. $500 nice? Not really.
Worthy of 5 stars. We had the 3 course fixed dinner option plus some additional components of the kitchen dishes and everything was top notch. A good place to take someone you're looking to impress!

Ambiance is great. Ate in the tavern and ordered Jerk Chicken which came out looking great but was totally raw below the charred look. Returned, they brought it back, apologized, and it was not good. My wife had the shrimp stew served with 2 shrimp 2 mussels and totally inadequate. The broth was good but what a disappointment. They took the chicken off the bill (nice) but I won't be back.

Heaven on earth!

This place is amazing. I highly recommend trying it at least once in your life - and after that you want to eat there every day and night.

My husband and I went on a spontaneous trip to NYC and he mentioned Gramercy Tavern to me and that he would really like to try this place at some point, but you need to make reservations months in advance. Out of curiosity I checked open table, and lucky me: 5:30pm table ope that same day.

I had no expectation of GT: I hadn't heard about it before, I didn't check reviews, but I just glanced at the menu before we walked in. 

Imagine my surprise when we walk into this beautiful restaurant, and everyone is just wonderful. Everyone on their team was just really pleasant, warm and just made us feel like home. 

We started with 2 drinks (Orange Blossom and Cider) and both were simply delightful. We then had an hors d'oeuvre (pickled salad), which was really good - and I do not usually like pickled vegetables.

Once I had my first bite of their bread roll with goat cheese butter I knew this dinner would be epic. Goat cheese butter. Sooooo good! I'm still dreaming about it.

For our first course we had the warm lobster salad (as the name implies: amazing), and the duck ragu with garganelli. I usually avoid ordering pasta, because more often than not I am disappointed, but this changed my life. If I could have this meal every single night for the rest of my life: I'd say yes, hands down.

Second course: Sea bass and the daily special - wagyu steak. Both were cooked to perfection, the flavors were exceptional. I don't know what else to say.

Now at this point we are both stuffed. We had a great dinner, we are full, but I really want dessert, no I need dessert. If the food until now has been outstanding we simply must get dessert! We ordered the chocolate fudge cake and the carrot cake, and surprise: it was fantastic. I really couldn't eat another bite, but I also could not leave a single piece behind. We ate it all. 

And to top it off: we received petite fours, which we obviously had to eat as well. And they were delightful!

But that wasn't it - after we paid our check the waiter brought us 2 granola bars to enjoy the next day for breakfast. Now I'm not a huge granola bar fan, but this granola bar: heaven! It was Christmas in a granola bar, and I sure would pay a lot of money if I could buy this in a shop. 

Gramercy Tavern: Thanks for an amazing night!

Went today with the wife from an open table reservation and had a great time. We had the 2 lunch tasting menus and enjoyed almost the entire meal. I found the grapefruit meringue was too bitter and the chocolate cake too dry. We also didn't expect to be charged for sparkling water. We wrote this down on the comments card they gave us, thinking it was anonymous. Within half an hour they called us and told us they were going to refund the desserts and the sparkling water. I was very impressed with their customer service. 

As for the meal: really enjoyed the duck breast and the artic char. From the vegetarian tasting menu, the carrot soup and spinach fettucine stood out. We've been to Per Se, Jean Georges, and Eleven Madison Park and believe the food here is as good or better than the more famous places. The ambience and service were great too, the food came out fairly quickly for a busy day before Easter.

The restaurant is beautiful!  Fresh flowers, inviting decor.  The food is good...explosion of flavors in your mouth.   The service was not good.  The waiter was condensing, entitled and not pleasant.   If I am going to spend $400 on a lunch it should be amazing on every one of my senses.   Last night, I spent $400 on Buddakon and I have no regrets... Today I should have gone elsewhere.

Gramercy Tavern is a famous Danny Meyer restaurant has been around since 1994. It was on my to-try list for 8 years.
The service is extremely professional.
The company was wonderful.
The food was acceptable but average. 

For those of you new to Gramercy Tavern, the restaurant is split into two parts. The more casual a-la-carte dining experience is the Tavern, in the front. The back is The Dining Room. The Dining Room is more formal with reservations recommended and fixed price tasting menus. 
We dined in at the Tavern because the Gramercy burger is only served at the Tavern. 
We ordered: the lamb, parsnip ravioli, the burger, cider, espresso, cold brew coffee. 
Dessert: Kumquat upside down cake, pistachios and green curry ice cream.

The sunchoke ravioli was crisped in butter and had tender sweet morsels of roasted sunchokes. This was the best dish.
The lamb was tender but was served medium well instead of medium rare.
The burger was soft, slightly dry and served medium well instead of medium rare.
The kumquat cake was sweet, sour, and sticky. I really liked this flavor! (I grew up eating kumquats as a kid). The cake was average, not dry, not moist.
The green curry ice cream tasted like green curry. Not the best ice cream flavor but I appreciated that the chef wanted to try a new flavor. 

Two of the men in our party were wearing t-shirts and sneakers. Sometimes at a formal restaurant, if you show up as if you are going to a baseball game, the staff would give subpar service, but not in this case. 
The staff was so nice.  Checking in to make sure we liked our food. Refilling our waters five, six times. I must have drank my full serving of fluids in those 3 hours.

For the prices and the quality of food, I would rather frequent another restaurant.

We opted for the more relaxed setting in the Tavern at the front of restaurant.  It was our first time there, I found the food to be satisfying , we enjoyed our food.  The personnel there where very pleasant.  All-in-all it was a good experience.  Really can't complain about anything.  Would probably go back.  Would like to experience the Dinning room setting and food.

OMG! still a nyc classic.  i real must-go-to!  the service is impeccable as is the meal selections.  the wine list is OUTSTANDING!  the servers are polite, knowledgeable and just plain FABULOUS! eat, drink and be merry t the tavern!

Restaurant side review

Great food and superb service.  Wife's lobster salad was really fresh and with great flavors and her striped bass entree was really flaky. My duck entree was good but def would get seafood next time (this is coming from someone who prefers red meat over seafood). 

Desserts were good esp the comp coconut cake as we were celebrating our belated anniversary. The lemon dessert (forgot name) was too floral and tangy for my wife and def a hate it or love it dish. Michelin star well deserved...great job Gramercy Tavern team!
I had an opportunity to learn what restaurant service should be today. Excellent service from the host to the server. Food was absolutely excellent and the wine was served at the right temperature.

We had dinner on the Tavern side of the restaurant--the food and service were excellent! Special shot out to "Ivan" the bartender who did an awesome job of managing an extremely busy bar!  The atmosphere of the Tavern is cool and local.  Not being from NYC, I felt connected to the locals scene.  It was the right combination of food, excellent service, and local environment -- I highly recommend this restaurant!

One of Danny Meyer's coveted restaurants. It definitely lives up to the hype.

I've tried both the tavern and the dining room, while both differ in their offering and vibe, they bring more similarities than differences - quality food and service. 

I highly recommend the full dinner tasting in the back for a special occasion. They really do make you feel welcomed without overdoing the whole hospitality thing. Food is delicious as well - their ruby shrimp dish stood out the most for me.

Will come back to try the bar-only burger
The service was impeccable. The staff and managers created a dining experience that you don't see very often anymore. The menu was thoughtful and the presentations were gorgeous. Loved it!!
I ve been here 2 times and will come back 100%. Food is very nice and I like that a portions are very small but at the end you feel like you are full. Big choice of vine. Nice atmosphere for dinner.

We came here and ate at the Tavern and it was a great experience with fast service!  We told the wait staff we needed to get out before 7 to make our flight and the wait staff was receptive and made sure we still got the still Tavern experience with three full courses!

For appetizers, we started with fish croquettes with a carrot and grilled cilantro salad and a yogurt dipping sauce.  The veggies were crispy and fresh and were a bright side to the croquettes, which had a melt-in-your-mouth filling.  For entrees, I got the mushroom fried rice with arctic char and sunchokes, which was delicious.  The fish was flaky and the mushrooms were fresh.  My only slight complaint was that the proportion seemed a little off because there were a lot of toppings for not that much rice, but that's likely my own personal preference.  My boyfriend got the grilled lamb with sweet potato and broccoli rabe.  Again, the lamb was cooked perfectly! 

Finally for desserts, we were feeling ambitious before our flight and got the chocolate peanut butter pie for two AND the chocolate pudding cake.  The chocolate peanut butter pie came with crunchy chocolate covered rice cereal on top and slices of fresh bananas.  There was a delicious passionfruit caramel sauce that we poured on top that added a delicious fruitiness to the super chocolatey peanutbuttery-ness of the tart.  The chocolate pudding cake was definitely a surprise.  It was encased in mascarpone and topped with coconut ice cream.  The cake was a little small for all the topping, but every bite was still delicious!  

Overall, great upscale meal with a relaxed and fun vibe!

This review is for the bar only. Prompt service and good drinks. They don't skimp on the alcohol. Restaurant vibe is lively. It's a slightly older crowd, which I appreciate at my age. I didn't have to yell to be heard. Seems like a very classic and classy establishment. Good for happy hours, drinks with friends, even a date. Would love to come back and try the food.

What else can you say except that this place is an institution and well worth the reputation! Fantastic food, beautiful upscale atmosphere without being overly stuffy and great service!
The seafood chowder at lunch was absolutely delicious!!

We went there on Sunday with friends, it was a great experience for us. We sat at the tavern not the main dining room. We walked in and we sat right away. Food was great, we ordered a stream white rice which I believe they don't serve white rice. I just want it for my 7 year old daughter. They actually cooked it for her, I knew it because it took long to hit the table. Really appreciated!! Atmosphere was great, dessert part was ok. Overall we are happy diner.

Not much left to be said that hasn't already been said in other reviews. Impeccable service and the attention to detail paid to each course is second to none.

Highlights of the meal were the off the menu lobster appetizer and the seafood chowder entree. I normally wouldn't get a soup as a second course but the chowder was hearty and contained a fair amount of seafood, bacon and potatoes. Absolutely delicious.
We tried the seasonal tasting menu and it was GREAT!!! Service was willing and welcome was genuine. Very busy, but well run.

Fantastic food, service,  atmosphere. Really the best place we have ever eaten.  I would recommend this restaurant highly to anyone that enjoys good fresh food everything from the first course to the third course was fantastic. They made my husband's birthday a very special occasion thank you Gramercy Tavern for all your impeccable service
This is for the dining room. Delicious fine dining! Beautiful building, delicious and creative offerings, excellent service. Come here for a special evening! It was a real treat dining here.

Our first restaurant we went to on our vacation from San Francisco. What a great experience! The food was superb, the service was fantastic, the ambiance was perfect. Do yourself a favor and get the tasting menu, you will not be disappointed!!!!

We sat in the dining area and enjoyed it. The service was amazing and the ambiance is good as well. I did the three course menu with the beef tartar and I loved it. For my main course I had the lamb shoulder and it was cooked just perfectly. The dessert was probably the best part. I went with the chocolate and It was one of the best desserts I have ever had. The wine list is extensive and I would definitely go back to this restaurant

Great steakhouse. We had a large group and a room. We had a sampler menu for a birthday. Hosts were incredible. Excellent service combined with great food and wine. Thoroughly impressed. My new favorite restaurant in New York

Great food, great drinks, amazing ambiance, but I want to make special mention of the greeter. You wouldn't think this would make a huge impression, but Zach really made us feel welcomed. He really cares about doing a superb job. Also, his food and drink recommendations were spot on. This guy is going places. Also, you should go places....Gramercy Tavern perhaps?

Went last night with my husband for our anniversary 
Fantastic!!!! I had the vegan tasting menu , he had the other tasting menu.
We didn't make a reservation early enough in the month so ended up with a 10 pm. Worth the wait. 
It was top notch. The wait staff was super! Funny, personable and quite knowledgeable. My favorite was the cabbage sprout fritter. Will go again!
Great burgers and steaks.  Love the draft beer they have.  Just get up and go right now.  Great people and great fun.  Go now.  Enjoy!

Saddened Burger Lover
 What happened to the burger that blew me away? Went Thursday for lunch so my burger loving friend could be blown away....... My first trip to GT was in February, I was so impressed with the burger, yesterday's 4/14/2016 trip made me want to pull a " Teresa Guidice" and flip the table !!!! Burger was half the size, different cheese, icky bacon that I could make at home, and all around BIG POOP !!!  They cannot keep up with the big boy's anymore !!! Very surprised at a Danny Meyer restaurant, Shake Schack is better !!!!

I had oysters for appetizing, they were fresh and delicious. I also tried grilled lamb, it was cooked just right, soft and juicy. The place is beautiful, I was happy with food, they use high quality products, but the cocktails were a little bit weak for me, I'm going to order wine next time;)

This place is stunning and it has been happening for the past 20+ years. They have pre-fixe dinner starting at $98 and a la carte as well. The place is split into two separate areas. You can have the dinner in the Dining Room and a la carte near the entrance/bar area. The service here is nothing short of impeccable.

They have a beautiful setting of fresh cut giant blooms at the entrance, by the bar and an area next to the busy kitchen. It was a tablescape of different types of blooms, fresh ranunculus, roses, tulips. It was beautiful. It was a little dim so we weren't able to capture the entire setting. And right next to this beautiful tablescape lies the variety of cheese selection. I believe there are about 20 different kind and regretfully we never made it to cheese. 

We did the pre-fix 3 course dinner. Everything was exceptionally delicious and not even my pictures are worthy. The only disappointment was that the coffee/tea isn't complimentary. I wouldn't have mind it tasted decent, but it was awfully bitter. I took two sip and costs me $5.00 yikes! Since the dinner was so perfectly delicious, I decided to not hold that coffee accountable for the lackluster of after dinner drinks.

I highly recommend visiting this place at least once...
One of my favorite places whenever I'm near flatiron / gold coast.

Loved my lunch here! Booked a last min lunch in between work and enjoyed both the food and hospitality. Def worth paying for for both.

I think I had a lobster salad as an appetizer which was super yummy with decent portion of lobster. And then the seafood gumbo as main- fish was perfectly cooked, and the sauce wasn't too oily. 
Also loved the small tease- something with yogurt, totally worth putting it in the menu, I would order that for my appetizer for lunch.

The environment was def cozy but upscale at the same time. With enough space in between the tables, you can hear yourself talking to others or thinking without yelling.

Five star for sure!

she looked with excitement at the menu while my stare bounced between her beautiful  cheekbones, +, chin, -, and the menu prices that turned the whole thing into a complex exercise in game theory. my point being first dates at expensive restaurants, even the tavern part of those, should be bolded underlined big no-no-s in any dating for cheap dummies book.
she was indeed the kind of gal looking for a prince on a white horse or a black porsche, one that her slender body, wavy hair, blue eyes were worthy of. please don't take this as an admonition of her kind, the opposite, if at all i'm completely berating my kind, a kind that thinks with its groin directly playing into the hands of these gorgeous devilish creatures instead of choosing someone like, for example, the middle age lady sitting alone at the bar across from us. because even though she might be extremely smart and intellectually challenging she will never overcome her greatest affliction to my kind, being a 5.
and so the ordeal continued, the waitress hurried to take our wine order, a hurry that would endure the evening even when the place became empty, my princess expecting champagne while i gravitated toward one of the first wines of the wine list, a wine list i've quickly recognized to be ordered by price, from pricey to very pricey. to compensate her disappointment i was quick to say -i'm crazy about this sauvignon blanc. giving my cheap wine a flare of sophistication by skipping the n and c in my otherwise american pronunciation of everything. she smiled back, i wasn't sure if it was out of politeness or she was as excited as i was feigning to be.
when the time to look at the menu came, to my dismay i realized that my preparation for the evening was met with its first obstacle. i've looked at the wrong menu! the meat, fish and pasta i was raving about on our way to a place i lied about frequenting were from a different restaurant, that happens to be the gramercy tavern dining room. apparently a common mistake, both taking place in the same geography and only separated by a change of decor but separated enough to make our menu a completely different thing. more humble and less appetizing with only few things to offer and giving my date affair a cheaper vibe, one i was trying to avoid at all costs, except for financial ones that is.
to add a layer of complication to all this i couldn't but keep staring into the dining room both to look at the dishes dispensed there and because the lawyer dude from weeds, what's his name, was sitting there. andy milder. i just looked him up.

to be continue, maybe.

The tavern at Gramercy tavern is easily my favorite meal in the city. Consistently excellent on multiple repeat visits. There seems to be some menu staples that change slightly as the seasons change, but it's always incredible. I strongly recommend dining in the tavern section of the restaurant, at the bar, and ordering multiple appetizers to share, though the mains are just as good but a bit more filling.

Some of my favorite dishes here include the duck liver mousse with pickled veggies, raw and roasted veggies, kielbasa, any fresh fish on the menu, and any fresh pasta. It's really hard to go wrong here, but I love how the vegetables are treated with an expert hand here and can be a satisfying meal on their own. 

The pastry chef makes some amazing desserts, and I always find myself ordering the selection of unique ice creams and sorbets. 

Service, as with all USHG restaurants, it's perfect.

Umm - most amazing meal EVER. They were so accommodating and paid attention to everything! I LOVE this restaurant and would love to come back
For 380 dollars we spent close to 4 hrs eating drinking etc. Time spent vs cost = totally worth it

Five Stars - hands down one of the best meals I've ever had. We took a trip to NY for our Anniversary and decided to head downtown and away from the commotion of Midtown. Gramercy was on our radar and we almost couldn't contain ourselves until lunch. 

We arrived at 12:20 and got the last table in the tavern (which is first come first served). They have a dining room as well but that requires reservations and they have shorter lunch hours. We sat down and immediately ordered cocktails - hubs got an aged Aventinus and I had the Amarita which was basically a grapefruit maragarita and it was SO delicious I had to have a second. An order of fresh, raw oysters went in next as we sat back and enjoyed the atmosphere. The Oysters are served with lemon, cocktail sauce and a red wine sauce with chives and shallots. AHH!! 

Lunch consisted of the Tavern Burger (not on the menu but always a staple) and the Sea Bass. I would say 75% of the resaurant ordered the juicy, wagu beef burger served with a smokey thousand island, pickled hot peppers and lettuce with house made potato chips. The Sea Bass was over a bed of barley and cauliflower, topped with a balsamic reduction - this was easily the best meal I have ever had. Our lunch was complete after the cookies and milk dessert and special anniversary cake of meringue. 

The tavern is small and cozy, they have fresh flowers (trees) throughout the restaurant with an open kitchen and wood grill. The bathroom is cozy, gorgeous and covered in more fresh flowers and washcloths to dry your hands with. 

Definitely recommend this to everyone - make the trip down to 20th and you won't be disappointed.

My husband introduced me to Gramercy Tavern to celebrate my birthday last night.
I would say that the food on the tasting menu ranks among the best 3 meals i have ever enjoyed.
The flavors were perfectly executed and the variety of textures in each dish was exciting.
The dessert was ok.

Booked a large group about a month in advance for a birthday celebration.  We all did the chef's tasting menu (one vegetarian).  We were greeted with a complimentary bottle of champagne.  The menu consisted of a good variety of exciting flavors and textures.  My favorite was the lobster dish.  The wait staff was almost choreographed they were so swift with serving and clearing dishes.  The decor was breathtaking with fresh cherry blossoms spread throughout.  Finally we finished with some unforgettable desserts.  One of my most memorable meals in NYC!!

Yes! Fabulous! Don't miss this place. 

Service was excellent. I love it when I come to a highly rated restaurant and the service is still stellar. Too often there are places in NYC that are considered coveted spots and the service is just snotty and awful. So Ye! Cheers to the hostess / hosts and the servers here. 

We didn't have a reservation on a Saturday night. We arrived at 10:15 and were seated in the casual area. The menu is small so I would recommend checking before you come. Just know, every dish will be amazing! I mean even the mixed veggies plate was delicious!

Gramercy Tavern is the best restaurant I've ever patronized. Great food, EXCELLENT service. Have eaten here on several occasions and am never disappointed (whether at the bar or in the dining area). Fish, red meat, wine, desserts... always measure up and totally worth the price. Make reservations weeks ahead bc they are usually booked up.

A class act that is suitable for any special occasion or just an evening enjoying great food and drinks.  Service is polished and relaxed and everyone in the dining room is clearly having a great time.

It's good for what it is...but in my opinion it was a bit expensive.

We came for and early lunch and the burger and the burger, while good, was not amazing.  So...there ya go.

Exquisite, hardworking, and imaginative would describe my experience. We had the 6 course plated meals with wine pairing. The dishes included beets, carrot soup, cauliflower which sounds boring but we're prepared with an attention to detail that I would expect from a restaurant like this. Wait staff was attentive and friendly. Only issue I had was I thought the hospitality policy existed based on the freaknomics pod cast but guess it hasn't made it here yet.

I have been wanting to eat here for a few years, since I saw the restaurant featured on a "CBS Sunday Morning" segment. I also found the cookbook under my Christmas tree as well and had prepared a few recipes (the chocolate bread pudding and the sweet corn ice cream have been huge hits at gatherings with friends).
Living in Charleston SC, I am so lucky to have access to so many amazing restaurants. So much, when I have traveled and dined at restaurants with sterling reputations, I have sometimes gotten up from the table at the end of the meal thinking "Meh".
