I feared that this would be the case with "Gramercy Tavern" and I was so thrilled that proved untrue. It was the best meal I had on my trip to NYC and the best one that I have had anywhere, period.
I feel that my review would be redundant (there are 1k plus posts for "Gramercy" on Yelp!), so let me say this: You will be impressed. You will leave feeling special. You will leave feeling euphoric. You will leave wishing that you could repeat the sublime experience over.

This place is amazing !! Without a doubt a must in NY!! I just had dinner last night with my family and it was superb! I've been here before and I never get disappointed, everything was perfect! The food, the space and the service are marvelous. Last night we started with a sparkling rosé (wonderful wine service) we waited for a while for the waiter to take our food order, and we started getting little impatient but they compensated all that with the perfect food (plus an extra appetizer) and perfect service! The "raw and roasted vegetables" are a must and the "smoked ham flatbread with blue cheese and endive" is perfect for sharing, on the entrées the grilled lamb is very good, the mushroom fried rice with grilled artic char is amazing and the jerk chicken, butter beans, spring onion and yogurt is just unbelievable! My favorite! About the desserts the kumquat upside down cake with curry ice cream is super delicious and the Chocolate Pudding Cake, Mascarpone, Buttered Pecans and Coconut Ice Cream is WOW!! It blew my mind! The selection of wines is very good, cocktails amazing, cheeses and coffee unbelievable too! Can't ask for anything else! Perfect evening, lots of wine and food, and being taken care of very well.

One of the best, if not the best meal I have had in my life. Food was beyond delicious. Interesting menu with unique flavor combinations but everything pulls together quite nicely. Drinks are fabulous and staff is top notch. I had one of the friendliest bartenders as my server at the bar. She knew the menu inside and out and helped with any questions I had (made awesome drinks too!) I will be back to this highly recommended spot! No question a 5-star joint reasonably priced for the quality delivered!
The experience was amazing all the way around. The food was great and the service was even better! Calling out Karen for her ridiculous attentiveness and warmth. Great job! We would highly recommend!

One of the most delicious food I've ever had. This place taught me what foodgasm is. It cost us about $150 per person for a 3-course meal but I didn't think it was overpriced. The interior was beautiful and the service was excellent. Also remember to dress nicely!

I cannot say enough good things about our experience at Gramercy Tavern. My husband and I went in on Friday and each got the tasting menu, which was phenomenal. I enjoyed every dish, and the wine pairings were excellent as well. I don't know much about wine and was particularly grateful for the explanations that our server provided for each pairing-- I felt like I was learning over the course of the meal but not at all being talked down to when I asked questions about the pairings. The service was out of this world as well. Our server, Alan, and the sommelier prepared a beer tasting to accompany our meal upon my husband's request, and it was clear that they put a ton of thought into complementing each dish. They were even kind enough to give us an extra dessert to share after I changed my mind about my order. Overall, the food was amazing, the service was incredible, and we left full and totally happy. Even though the prices are high, I felt like the experience was completely worth it. Big thanks to the whole team-- everyone there clearly put a lot of thought into making out evening special. Also loved the granola bar!

This dining experience was single-handedly the best I've had in years. From start to finish, I can only describe the entire experience as smooth. 
My party had the seasonal tasting menu. I did the wine pairings with the tasting menu. Both were PHENOMENAL. There wasn't a single dish from the 7 courses that I didn't think was wonderful. The wine pairings with each dish was perfect. 
Add to that - the service was impeccable. From the server that handled us, so the runners and the bus boys. Each dish was laid down together for the entire party. The dishes were cleared away at the same time. It was seamless. 
They gave you just enough attention but not so much that you felt smothered. 
There are so many choices in New York, but I would come here again and again. 

Highly Recommended. You must go here!!

Whenever someone asks me what my favorite restaurant in New York is, I always point them to Gramercy Tavern. Their tasting menus have been consistently delicious, and I can confidently say that I've had some of my most memorable meals here.

I ordered the 5-course Lunch Tasting Menu this time, which at $65, is honestly a steal. Including the extra courses, I had:

- Bread: House-made Biscuit with Goat Cheese
- Amuse Bouche of Carrot Custard with Grapefruit and Fennel
- Clam & Scallop Salad, Sea Island Peas, Shiitake Mushrooms and Basil
- Smoked Arctic Char with Asparagus, Rye and Black Rice
- Mushroom Tortellini with Nettles, Pecorino and Pickled Burdock
- Roasted Duck Breast with Duck Sausage, Rutabaga, Black Radish and Mandarin
- Palate Cleanser: Sweet Pea Panna Cotta with Almonds and Mint
- Strawberries & Cream with Whipped Cheesecake, Candied Pistachios, Meringue and Nettle Ice
- Mignardises: Passion Fruit Chocolate and Rice Puff with Black Sesame Chocolate

Every course was perfectly executed, but the Carrot Custard, Arctic Char, Roasted Duck Breast, and Sweet Pea Panna Cotta were by far my favorites. If the carrot custard or panna cotta were offered on the ala carte menu, I would order them without hesitation. The custard was full of carrot flavor and was the perfect way to start off the meal. The panna cotta was extremely refreshing and smooth, and was a good way to transition from the savory courses to dessert. The duck was perfectly cooked to a medium-rare and paired greatly with the mandarin and rutabaga - I could probably have eaten an entire plate of this. 

The highlight of my meal had to be the dessert though. The Strawberries and Cream dessert now ranks as one of my favorite desserts of all time and is alone worth making a trip to New York city for. I didn't see the Strawberries and Cream dessert offered on the ala carte menu, so it may be exclusively part of the tasting menu, in which case I would suggest getting the tasting menu just so you have the opportunity to try this delicious dessert. I treasured every bite of this.

Some non-food related notes: The interior of this restaurant is one of the most beautiful I have ever seen - the inside is always decorated with beautiful bouquets and flora, and I'm sure the restaurant spends a fortune purchasing all these flowers. Even the bathroom is beautifully decorated with huge bouquets. Service is usually fine, though a bit slow at times. The quality of the food makes up for this though, so don't mind waiting a bit between courses. All in all, Gramercy Tavern is the quintessential New York restaurant and is worth dining at at least one in your life.

Our first dinner in NYC and oh my goodness .. I can't even begin to describe how fabulous it was.  Everything from start to finish was top notch - one of the best dining experiences my husband and I have ever had.  If we lived in NYC, we'd be here every weekend, I'm sure of it.

First of all, our server was excellent.  She was friendly, engaging and really made us feel comfortable.  We never lacked for anything.  She definitely added to our awesome experience.

But the food - OMG, THE FOOD! - was stellar.  We both opted for the tasting menu, which if one does it the whole table does it. However, they have two options for the tasting menu: Seasonal and Vegetable.  We were allowed to each do one - so technically we had 12 different dishes to try!  Aside from that, it's a really nice option for vegetarians to have their own tasting menu.  Here's what went down:

1ST COURSE - Clam & Scallop Salad (hubby) and Beet Salad (me) .. I didn't try any of my husbands salad, but I know he liked it.  My salad - while I am not a fan of beets, I figured if I'm going to have them the very best way possible, Gramercy Tavern held up their end.  Aside from that "beet taste" I thought the salad was very well done and I was able to eat the whole thing without issue.  People who love beets would devour this.

2ND COURSE - Warm Lobster Salad (hubby) and Carrot Soup (me) .. Again, my husband loved his, but I swear my carrot soup won the prize.  It was the perfect balance of sweet and savory.  Nice and creamy and full of downhome goodness.  The best way to eat a carrot, that's for sure.

3RD COURSE - Smoked Arctic Char (hubby) and Chestnut Custard (me) .. I did have a bite of my husband's dish because I was curious as I'd never had arctic char before.  It was very good.  Paired with pistachios and crème fraiche - yum!  My chestnut custard was heaven on a plate, for real.  Served with mushrooms, pears and pecans, it did have a sweet/savory thing going on.  But it was incredibly light and packed good flavor.  Pears went surprisingly well with mushrooms.

4TH COURSE - Mushroom Tortellini (hubby) and Buckwheat & Cabbage Fritter (me) .. I only took a tiny bite of the tortellini because they don't give you a plateful but they were very good.  It's hard to not love pasta.  However, my fritter blew me away.  Tasted like a potato cake but soooo much better!  It was hearty and filling - I was sad not to eat it all, but I honestly couldn't.  Two more courses were coming!

5TH COURSE - Duck Breast & Sausage (hubby) and Cauliflower & Barley Risotto (me) .. At this point my husband has stopped talking.  His food left him in a stupor of ecstasy.  As for me, risotto is perhaps one of my most favorite things in the world.  Barley made risotto style was a new thing for me, but every bit as creamy and delicious as the traditional.  Served with a savory mix or mushrooms and brown butter.  Ugh.  So good.

6TH COURSE - Grapefruit Meringue (hubby) and Warm Chocolate Cake (me) .. This time, hubby and I actually switched.  He's a chocolate lover and I like to experiment more with the desserts, so I ended up with the grapefruit meringue.  Such a light, refreshing dessert!  Perfect ending to the meal.

All six courses were delivered over a 2.5 hour period.  Service moved very smoothly and for once in my life I was able to eat without getting miserably full.  Portions were the perfect size for a tasting.  Presentation was excellent. If you are considering a trip to NYC and wondering where you should have a very nice dinner, look no further than Gramercy Tavern.  We will recommend it to everyone we know.

Wow. After five nights and four days eating and drinking our way through New York, I have to say that the meal I look back on most fondly is the dinner we had here. 

We didn't plan ahead, so we didn't have reservations...and the place was packed. At 8 pm on a Friday. Craziness! Still, we added our names to the wait list, then walked next door for light apps and drinks while we waited for a table. 

The process to get our names on the list wasn't exactly what I'd call "efficient"; there were three girls working the stand that night, but apparently only one of them could add names to the list. 

We were texted when our table was almost ready, which gave us time to close out next door and walk over. The place was still super packed, so we headed to the bar to grab another glass of wine while we waited. 

The bartender made a great show of the fact that we didn't have reservations, and that we were still waiting for our table. We simply wanted to buy three glasses of wine and close out the tab before sitting down, but he wasn't having it. 

At any rate, we were given a cute little corner table for our party of three, and sipped on our wine while going over the menu. 

Our waitress was Whitney, and she was a doll. She answered the food allergy-related questions, gave us recommendations on both food and drink, and then answered our additional questions about dessert. 

I ordered the sea bass entree (because me), and it was phenomenal. It was just the right amount of food on the plate, and it was expertly cooked. It was also delicious, with a good flavor that enhanced the fish, instead of overpowering it. I couldn't place the actual flavoring at the time (four glasses of wine tend to numb my taste buds), but it was distinct, yet subtle. I know I sound crazy. 

Side note: while we were waiting for the food to come out, someone came by and dropped bread rolls on our plates. Of course, one of our group has a gluten allergy, so she couldn't touch the bread. We're used to that, so didn't think twice about it, but not two minutes later, another guy came by with another roll that he said was gluten free. Whitney came out right afterwards and  confirmed that it was gluten free (the one with celiac didn't believe that it could be). It was such a nice thing for Whitney to do, sending that to the table so that we could all enjoy a bit of bread. 

The night ended with us ordering desserts to share. And to be honest, it was the dessert that drew us to this place to begin with. Well, specifically the different ice cream offerings. 

So, we got the chocolate un-cake and a scoop each of the bourbon and brie ice creams. 

The chocolate un-cake was a winner. The ice creams were a bit of a letdown, after all the anticipation. Still, two small scoops of novelty ice cream does not a dinner make, so I don't even count them in my rating. 

Definitely go for the food, the wine, and the service. You won't regret it!

We had the seasonal tasting menu with wine pairing, May 2016.

I ordered a dark and stormy, which took about 10 minutes to arrive. The server said they were having trouble finding the proper glass? I don't believe they had ginger beer and tried to make one out of simple syrup and club soda. terrible. No ginger flavor at all.

The servers forgot the first wine pairing for my wife's order. We let that slide.

The servers duplicated a wine pairing one right after the other. I asked what the difference between the previous wine and current wine were - as a nice way to let them know we were offering the exact same bottle and the answer was "this one is a little bolder". Indeed.

That said, the food was tasty overall and the servers were friendly. Normally, these defects with the meal wouldn't be a big deal - but when you are paying the prices they ask, I expect perfection. I'd probably try this place again, I guess, but wouldn't recommend it to friends.

My wife and I visited Gramercy Tavern and we absolutely loved it. The food, atmosphere, and service were fantastic. We had been here once before in the Tavern but this was our first time eating in the Dining Room. We both ordered the seasonal tasting menu and were very happy with our choice. We tried foods that we wouldn't have tried before and we were served food that we normally don't enjoy. Each dish was better than the next. Our favorite was the duck breast and the tortellini - both were perfect. Everyone should experience this wonderful restaurant.

I love Gramercy Tavern, from the neo-Colonial decor to how, just when you think you're finished with your meal, the waiter pops by with some blood orange truffles. I even love the ladies who lunch and the rotating groups of summer associates from all the nearby law firms. 

But most of all, I love their cookie platter with milk. Hear me out. The platter comes with oatmeal cookie, rugelach, pecan bar, lemon cookie, whoopie pie, brownie, and poppy seed cookie. If I wasn't with other people, I would have dived in. The oatmeal cookie did the impossible - it convinced me that its oatmeal raisin brethren weren't the devil's spawn. Hands down, my favorite thing that we ordered. 

The beet salad and striped bass were excellent enough, but, seeing as how neither is loaded with sugar, don't quite merit my effusive adoration. Keep in mind that the portion sizes are on the small to reasonable side, so, unless you eat three quarters of a cookie platter, you'll walk out of here feeling quite pleasantly satiated. If, however, you do choose to order the cookie platter AND two separate desserts, you may need to skip dinner. 

NEXT TIME: I've only ever eaten in the Dining Room, but I hear amazing things about the Tavern's off-menu burger.

Came for Brunch a while back, was not disappointed.

Outstanding service, delicious food, pleasant and lively unpretentious environment. Definitely will return.

Frequently when I dine at restaurants with a lot of preceding accolades and hype there always seems be a little bit of a "is that all there is" let down to my experience. I am thrilled to report that Gramercy Tavern lives up to the hype and then some. I would also like to add that they have a superb wine list and specialty cocktail menu as well. Rob, my impeccable waiter deftly straddled being professional yet friendly with charm and grace. I decided to change my reservation from the evening to having lunch before about 2 hours or so before my arrival and they were able to accommodate me without any issues or problems. My meal was superb. I began with a delicious Carrot Soup that was only on the pre fixe menu. I then had a Pasta Bolognese that was one of the tastiest Bolognese that I have had. I had the Lamb entree and it was perfectly cooked and melted in my mouth. For dessert I decided to keep it light and had a trio of sorbets. Please do yourself a favor and dine here when you are in NYC. You only live once and this restaurant is splurge worthy.

The tavern is quite the place to go. the decor is warm and inviting, the dining hall exquisitely detailed and designed.

The food in the tavern, pairs perfectly with the setting, is light and tasteful. It goes down smoothly with no problem or loss of flavor. I had the lamb, which did not have the same lingering special aftertaste that plagues many smaller lamb dishes.

It is important to know that reservations cannot be taken at the bar, wait list only. Also, there are two different menus separating the dining/tasting room, and the tavern hall.

One of the best restaurants I've eaten at in NYC. From the first course to the dessert, it was a 10! We did the tasting menu which was amazing, the lobster app was unreal, the duck to die for and the Strawberries and cream dessert was unheard of. Can't wait to go back!

Gramercy Tavern was my first michelin dining upon arriving to NYC. I heard really good things about it and happily wasn't disappointed. I went with the tasting menu for $125, which I think it actually a pretty good deal for a restaurant of this caliber.

The "journey" so to speak of the food was well thought out. We started off with lighter flavor seafood courses like smoked arctic char (my favorite dish), scallop & clams, & lobster salad. Each dish was executed perfectly and the flavors were fantastic! They also served freshly baked dinner rolls that were fluffy and warm. 

Next our meal started moving into heavier flavors. This started with a home made mushroom tortellini, which I actually thought was a bit too strong. It was good, but the cheese and mushroom flavors were overpowering and I had to make an adjustment to my tasting palette. Next came the duck course, which I substituted with chicken instead. Major regret. I usually don't like duck and had not been a fan of the duck dish I tried at Lazy Bear (another Michelin restaurant in SF), but this duck was so good! It was definitely better than my chicken, which was pretty average for me.

Finally, dessert. They knocked this one out of the park and I think it was some of the best desserts I've had for fine dining. First, we got a "pre-dessert", which was dessert before dessert. What an awesome concept. It was a sweet pea puree flan with some sort of cream. Wow, who knew vegetables could make such good desserts. Our entire table loved it. Next, they presented the actual dessert, which was a strawberry cream. This came with fresh strawberries, cream, and a green colored snow ice. Presentation was beautiful and it tasted amazing!

As if that wasn't enough they also came out with two types of chocolates per person after. One was passion fruit flavored and the other was blood orange. Both tasted so good and I stuffed them down even though I was already too full. Finally to wrap things up, they brought out homemade chocolate granola bars to take home. These tasted really good - we ate them the following days.

Overall, it was a solid fine dining experience. I think I should have subbed out my main course for either the duck or a seafood dish as they seem to be REALLY good at doing seafood. Service was friendly and attentive as well.
i had an amazing experience.. now on this is defiantly one of my favorite place in NYC food was great..and service was fantastic.. good job guys coming back anytime soon for sure....

Some Things never get old, now for me i would have to say my favorite restaurant on this continent is possibly the tavern, I have been privileged to dine here on some occasions, but this it was very unique. Besides the Great Food Service, whole deal, BLAH BLAH, i had a opportunity to meet a remarkable waitress here, she was gracious, direct, and pretty much you everything you could ask for... Thank you Aiesha, i was also given a opportunity to see how their operations is conducted from the back of house, being in the hospitality industry i couldn't help but ask all sorts of questions. I met the Sous Chef, And other Chef which i forgot his positing.. sorry, but they not only inspired me, they also reminded me how great of a responsibility they have, and their possibilities are endless with the direct commitment they receive from all their team members, besides being given all the extra bells and whistles, as i heading out our waitress handed me a crafted snack bar made by GT. She reminded us to come back when we visit, which we always do anyways :) I can tell a lot by some1's smile, and hers is 1 i won't forget thank you.

Seems like a nice place
I didn't eat, but a nice selection of wines by the glass and good service.

My wife and I had lunch reservations at 1pm for our 25th Anniversary celebration. I saw on line the tasting menu along with the wine pairing menu that had me intrigued. Gramercy Tavern has been on my "foodie" list for years.  From the moment we stepped into this place, we felt special. An opening celebratory drink ended with a closing Anniversary dessert. The perfect service only complimented these extraordinary dishes. An admitted wine rookie, I saw how each wine exemplified each course. Keep in mind, I was totally looped walking out but this only made a park bench in Washington Square Park more relaxing. I felt like each ingredient in each course was not used by chance. Every dish was memorable. My wife had the vegetarian tasting and I had the other one. That was fun, because we shared. We spent 2 1/2 hours eating and drinking and I can honestly say that this dining experience was a bargain at $150 a person. We're not waiting another 25 years, we 'll be back next year!

What an amazing meal. I could not decide what I wanted from the menu so the staff sent over a second opinion. Decided to go with the duck mousse and sea bass. These were amazing dishes!! The service was a little slow but the staff made up for it in spades. First they served me an oyster on the half shell, again amazing food. Next when dinner was slow to arrive they offered a complementary glass of wine. I could not be happier will be back for sure!!

Possibly the best meal I have had in the city is outside of the 3-stars. I am very glad to get a reservation for my trip back to NY 2 years after I lived here and failed to get one. 

The food, service, atmosphere were all top notch. While a typical white tablecloth establishment, the staff is very friendly and down to earth, nothing stuffy about them at all. Food-wise, I just chose the prix fixe and let the waiter dictate what to get. Everything came out perfectly.
I absolutely love this place.  One of the best restaurants in New York City.  Great for client dinners with a wonderful wine list.

I'm sure enough has been written about this place. None of the dishes stood out except the dessert. The dessert (strawberries with some type of shaved ice) was absolutely delicious and innovative. Just thinking about it makes my mouth water, even 2 weeks after dining here. Overall this is a great place for a fancy dinner.

Top notch, amazing service, quality food. Very memorable. 
Had the squid ink tagliatelle to start followed by the lamb! Ended up having to take the desert home. It's a $$$$ night but they treat you right! We will definitely be back.

We love Gramercy Tavern!  It is everything we want in a restaurant: high quality and well executed food, elegant yet unpretentious and cozy atmosphere, superb service. You can go there for a casual drink and light bites in the tavern; you can go for an extensive, multi-course, fine dining experience. Danny Meyer is a culinary genius!

Grammercy Tavern has to be one of the best restaurants in NYC. It is versatile on all fronts and the service is top notch. You are never left with an empty table and you can expect the atmosphere to be very welcoming. I found it to be pricey at first (since I'm a very cheap guy) but it was worth every dollar. Look at the selections in the tasting menu!

Two words:  cheese kielbasa 

Two more words:  everything else

Amazing food, drink and atmosphere all at reasonable prices (in the bar/lounge) for a high end restaurant.  Highly recommend sitting at the bar for dinner (or in the lounge) area.

I haven't been in years so thought the tavern would be fun for a Sunday lunch. I grabbed a seat by the bar. That's bartender was very nice. I had the raw and roasted vegetables which was very good. A large portion of a variety of vegetables. The oysters were good too. I had the duck meatloaf for a main and was not disappointed. It was delicious.
I've been here twice. Once in the dining room and once in the lounge. Both were fantastic. The food and service are both top quality. The atmosphere is nice and relaxed and you never feel rushed.

Such a great culinary treat. I came here on Sunday evening for brunch and enjoyed some great beer and equally amazing food. I don't recall what I ordered but I remember how great the service was and how amazing the desert was. I'll definitely be coming back here for dinner and drinks in the near future

We went during the day on one of the nicer days of the year (so far). The place is absolutely beautiful. Even before a single drink or food item is dropped off you begin to enjoy the experience. We were seated in what was literally the 'back corner' of the restaurant, however it was just as pleasant of a spot as anywhere else.

The menu is obviously an array of different and unique dishes. They offer 'a la carte' options as well as two tasting menus, one of which is vegtables-only. All said there's a ton of options and really something for everyone. 

One note about the menu - the tasting menu has some items you can get as a main course (slightly larger). I believe it depends on the item and the chef. And thank god you can do that because the duck was spectacular. Probably the best I've ever had. With duck I always have it done how the chef recommends. Sometimes it's medium, other times medium rare. It was about medium rare here, and it was great. I'm trying to rack my brain to remember what it was served with, but I can't recall - it was great though. Another member of our party got the chicken which was very good (according to her). I also tried some of the sausage that came with the chicken and really enjoyed it. 

For starters, I had the steak tartare. This was very, very good. Others had the asparagus soup and lobster salad. All of which got incredible reviews. Didn't try the lobster salad, but found the quantity of lobster to be quite generous. The soup was not my thing, but everyone else seemed to love it.

Deserts were good, however the cookie platter was a little different. Everything was great, but I am a bit more of a traditionalist when it comes to cookies. 

Overall, an excellent experience. I do have to say I was hungry when I left, but that's to be expected. Absolutely plan on going back.

I've been here a few times and really enjoyed all my experiences here. While their main dishes were delicious, their desserts are to die for. Make sure to try the chocolate macaroon with peanut butter as well as the other desserts!

Lived up to its reputation for classic, fine dining. The asparagus soup was excellent with a rich texture and crunchy vegetables concealed within. The striped bass was perfectly cooked and the luncheon as a whole was reviving even with a good pour of Riesling at lunch. Reminded me of bygone days at the Harvard Faculty Club without the tweed jackets.

I wish there were more stars to give.

We've been dining here for years and as soon as you walk into the main dining room, it's like being transported to a beautiful lodge in Maine.

The food is always perfect, the service flawless and the florals are so impressive.  

A little secret but they offer BYOB.  Don't bother unless you are bringing something extra impressive and be kind enough to save some for your server.

It gets no better.
Went to Gramercy Tavern last night for dinner. It was fabulous. We expected great food from all of the reviews we read. We were not disappointed

Went here for dinner last night.  Nice ambiance and layout. Arrived 10 minutes early for reservation and we were seated immediately.  They do a 3 course price fixe menu which was a pretty good deal.  

Food:

Pork bolognese: fresh pasta,  perfectly al dente,  rich hearty sauce.  Finely chopped carrots gave it a great crunch. A-

Seafood stew: decent,  but somewhat bland and lacking significant substance.  My least favorite entree. C

Pork loin and belly: loin perfectly cooked and belly tasted like candy. B+

Striped bass: great portion,  seasoned perfectly,  seared for a great crust,  yet perfectly delicate middle.  My favorite entree.  A

Strawberry dessert: fresh strawberries,  whipped cheesecake,  and flavored ice. Flavors were all fresh and bright.  Whipped cheesecake was light and delicious.  

Overall, decent dinner,  great service. Not sure that I would go back.  Reservations are advised,  it was very crowded.

This place is 5 stars.  We had the dinner tasting menu with the wine pairing.  I recommend you do that because the sommelier really pairs excellent choices.  You know at this place the menu will not disappoint, so I'll focus on the small touches.  

First the service was amazing.  The servers were very nice and helpful without being overly eager or sounding fake.  Also, the bread and butter here is delicious.  You probably think, oh its just bread and butter, but actually its more than that.  The bread is warm and crusty and the butter melts perfectly over it.  This is just one of those NY institutions you must try.

I've had Gramercy Tavern on my wish list for a long time.  I was pretty underwhelmed though when I finally got to go.  Thankfully I went for the lunch service, so I didn't blow all my hard earned cash on a fancy dinner.  I think I've finally learned at this point that one star rated places in NYC are usually a let down.

Service is friendly, but not exceptional and not up to par with other fine dining establishments in the area.  I did the five course vegetable tasting ($55) while my husband did the five course seasonal menu ($65).  Nothing was bad, but only one out of five courses had a wow factor.  Here's a run down of both courses since I tasted both:

The meal began with some fresh bread, little square rolls with a crisp crust outside served warm.  The texture was great.  Flavor was okay, but I did really enjoy the goat cheese butter.  It was creamy and tart.

1st Course:

VEGETABLE:  Chilled Lettuce Soup (Turnips, Croutons, and Pickled Shrimp) - *Good* They pour the soup over the dry ingredients table side.  Yes, this was the vegetable tasting, but there were shrimp.  They did ask me if it was okay before hand.  I like seafood, so it was fine, but I can't imagine this dish without it if you're a vegetarian.  That's where the acid in the dish was coming from and without it, it would be lacking something.  The soup was green and full of fresh flavors, but a little over-salted.

SEASONAL:    Marinated Scallop (Fluke, Rhubard, Cucumber) - *Okay* Very acidic.  Not memorable though. 

2nd Course:

VEGETABLE:  Beet Salad (Pistachios, Mint, Ricotta) - *Bland*  Honestly not much going on here in terms of flavor. It tasted like beets with those things on it.  I've had far better beet dishes at casual restaurants.  

SEASONAL:  Smoked Artic Char (Asparagus, Rye, and Red Rice - *Good* This was the best dish of the seasonal course.  Smokey fish with great texture from the rice.  The best part was the asparagus which just tasted very fresh and had a lot of flavor.

3rd Course:

VEGETABLE:  Roasted Asparagus (Radish, Picked Ramps, Tarragon Custard) *Excellent* This was the only wow factor, and strangely enough, it was the dish I was least looking forward to. I'm not a fan of custards in general.  However, this one was light and creamy and more similar to a mousse in texture although not as airy.  It was savory and full of tarragon flavor.  The texture contrast of the crisp veggies was amazing.  The acid from the pickled ramps really brought out the sweetness in the custard.  Dishes like this is what I expect from a Michelin rated establishment.

SEASONAL:  Mushroom Tortellini (Nettles, Pecorino, Pickled Burdock) *Bad* Sodium overload.  The pasta also was a little tough in spots.  

4th Course: 

VEGETABLE:  Leeks and Broccoli Rabe (Semolina, Almonds, Yogurt) *Okay*  It tasted like something I'd quickly whip up at home and the presentation was a bit sloppy.  Some fried semolina cakes with some greens on top and yogurt on the bottom.  Also, a bit under seasoned.

SEASONAL:  Roasted Duck Breast (Summer Squash, Fennel, Morel Mushrooms) I don't like duck, but my husband thought it was good.

5th Course - 

DESSERT - You could choose between two desserts or a cheese plate.  We both got the same dessert, the Lemon Meringue Tart (Cherries, Wild Chervil, and Frozen Yogurt).  *Good*  The tart itself was just okay. It was your typical lemon meringue.  So was the frozen yogurt.  However, the cherry sauce was amazing, but the fresh cherries were a little under ripe.  We were also brought some chocolates that were pretty, but too sweet for my taste.

Also, I noticed there was no amuse bouche or little gift from the kitchen.  That's the first time I've been to a Michelin rated place that leaves this out. It was a little strange considering the price point.

If you're torn between the vegetable and seasonal tastings, I'd say do the vegetable.  The things that actually stood out were the quality of the fresh vegetables used.  Besides, you can get a regular tasting that isn't veggies at plenty of other places in the area, many of which are far more impressive.

Lunch isn't a bad deal, but I don't get the hype of this place. There are far more tastier and inventive places in the city.  I wouldn't turn down a free lunch here, but I don't think I'll go out of my way to go back.  If you're craving a high end vegetarian/vegan dining experience, I would recommend going to Philadelphia to dine at Vedge instead.  Definitely a different atmosphere, but more creative, tasty food.

I tried tasting menu during lunch. It was just AMAZING! I dined several michelin restaurants in New York (including JG, Daniel, Per se, EMP...) and other areas, I love gramercy tavern in terms of food and price. I did have a diner at EMP 2 days ago before I dined at gramercy tavern and disappointed a bit.. It was fun experience and every dishes was creative. However, I did not enjoy the dish. (Mainly due to overly salted dishes..) Although the price was much lower than other michelin restaurant, I was really enjoyed every dishes here! I was surprised that all dishes were sooo great since I usually disappoint one or two dishes in tasting menu. All staffs were attentative and friendly. Also, I was really surprised that the sous chef visited my table and glad that I had a conversation with him for a moment. It was a memorial meal in New York and higly recommend Gramercy Tavern!! I could know why many people love here.

all hail, the cult of Danny Meyer.
delicious and great value.

Went here for my graduation lunch. Had the chefs tasting menu with wine pairings and it was amazing. The service was impeccable and our main waiter was incredibly knowledgeable and answered all the numerous questions my family had not only about the food but NYC as they were visiting from Canada for the event. As it was my  graduation they brought out an adorable coconut cake at the end along with chocolates and the desserts we had ordered. The wine pairings were also spot on. One of the wines we tasted before we recieved the corresponding course and none of us were super big fans, but when we paired it with the food it was amazing. They clearly know what they are doing. 

I've eaten at many other Michelin star restaurants including places like le Bernadin and this experience was most definitely my favourite.
Had the lunch tasting menu. Called the morning of to make my reservation for when they opened and got in with no problem. The vegetarian tasting menu was fresh and adventurous.

I have been here few times and its finally fair to say I owe it to Tavern to write a review.  The service is top of the line and the taste of the food is something which drives me and my brother to this place all the time.  I love the orange truffles and literally everything else and one of my brother's favorites is Smoked Arctic Char with Asparagus. Its a great place for office gathering as well as I was first introduced to Tavern by my law firm event. 
Prices are high but I guess you have to pay for great quality and great service. Enjoy.

Great location, wonderful place and fun environment!!
Well-recommended despite being a bit pricey.
The food and service is subtle, understated, and remarkable. Everything is exceptional...everything.
This place has now become a ritual sunday brunch spot. The staff is SO lovely and attentive and the food is exceptional. Be prepared to leave later than expected but beyond happy!

My husband took me here for my graduation lunch a little while back and I have to say it was probably one of the best meals I've had this year. The tasting menu was great and the chef even sent out an extra course and a complementary dessert! Definitely would recommend this to everyone of my friends!

My friends ranked this place as their favorite one star michelin restaurant, so I had high hopes for it. 

I opted for the seasonal tasting menu for $125 since it had the most courses and they all looked delicious.

The meal started off with clam & scallop salad. The clams and scallops were very very fresh and tasted great. 
The warm lobster salad was also quite good. Lots of flavor and lobster not too tough or chewy.
Artic Char was definitely the highlight of the meal for me. I've never had a salmon so soft and taste so good before. There wasn't much of a distinct salmon taste, which made it tastes even better.
Mushroom tortellini was a huge miss for me. I didn't like the mushroom cheese flavor on the inside cause it tasted too heavy. 
Roasted duck breast and sausage tasted good. I had the duck breast and the sausage individually and they were great. I mixed the two into one bite and it still tasted great albeit a bit different. 
Strawberries & cream dessert was a very unique dish that I've never had before. The green ice had a vegetable taste that I couldn't quite put my finger on.  

The light to heavy food transition was great and was really well thought out. Service here is top notch and they also happily accommodated our vegan friend.

Came here for a new experience not quite sure what to expect. My date and I arrived 20 minutes early for our 8:30 pm reservation in the Dining Room on a Saturday night. The hostess let us sit at the bar to order a drink while we waited for our table. Before we could order a drink we were seated.

A woman stepped forward introduced herself (i forgot her name) and explained the two dining styles to us. She was very warm and courteous. 

SIDE NOTE: There were basically two people serving us the entire night but this woman seemed to be the lead server

We asked her to order us 2 drinks off the menu at random as a surprise. When our drinks arrived, we were not disappointed. Our drinks fit our personalities & palates perfectly. They tasted wonderful and looked beautiful. We were also brought a cheese puff and some of the best bread we've ever had to start.

We ordered from the 3 course dinner menu. My first course was the Squid Ink Campanelle, Lobster without the Chorizo (Not a fan of pork). The pasta was al dente and had a beautiful color, the lobster was perfectly cooked, the tomato based broth had a touch of heat and the sweet peas brought the flavors together.  It was my favorite dish of the night. My date had the chilled cucumber soup and said it tasted fresh and delicious.

Our 2nd course, I ordered the Lamb Shoulder. This dish was a bit disappointing. I love lamb and after the first course I was looking forward to this dish. Although beautifully plated, I couldn't get past the licorice flavor that seemed to be in every component of the meal. The server detected that something was off and asked if my lamb was cooked ok. She went on to say if I wanted it cooked more it wouldn't be a problem and she wanted to make sure I had exactly what I wanted. After some prodding I told her I wasn't crazy about the dish.  She offered to take the dish away and brought me another menu to see what else I wanted to order. She also offered to take my date's meal away and bring him better version of what he was eating so we could eat at the same time. We both agreed.

I ordered the chicken and it was perfectly cooked but underwhelming and bland. The crispy mushrooms were a nice addition. 

For dessert we had the strawberry and the carrot. My date enjoyed the strawberry (like a deconstructed cheesecake) and the carrot (like a carrot cake with carrot ginger sorbet) was ok. 

Overall it was a great experience and I would definitely return.   I would come back just for the Squid Ink Campanelle, Lobster without the Chorizo, the cocktails and the bread. The service was certainly 5 star. Maybe next time we will try the Tavern.

Went today and ordered the chicken dish. It was really good but $26 for chicken the size of two chicken nuggets is a joke. I don't subscribe to the NYC small dish high price crap. 

I suggest you fill up on the bread which was amazing

I took my boyfriend here as a treat for his birthday and it was definitely a treat! We sat in the tavern area so we could order a la carte. The service was phenomenal - everyone was super friendly, respectful, and pleasant to talk to. 

Literally everything we ate was great. The Raw & Roasted Vegetables, Mushroom, Sweet Pea and Kimchi came with amazing dips. I had the Ricotta Cavatelli which was amazing and my boyfriend had the Kale & Cabbage Salad, Einkorn, Mint and Duck Confit which he said was incredibly delicious and filling. They even brought out a coconut cake for my boyfriend's birthday. I'll definitely be going back again!
Beautiful restaurant and really good food. Classy, elegant and great service. No complaints, just something to definitely try when dining in NY

Perfect on every level. Perfect ambiance, service and food
The way the chef combines textures and flavors is unparalleled. We opted for the prix fixe menu. 
Wagyu steak tartare was the best and most original presentation I have experienced
Smoked trout with pickled ramps and trout roe. Beautiful.
Striped bass. Best I have ever tasted.
Desserts were delicious as were the after-dessert-dessert.
Love this restaurant. My favorite restaurant in the U.S.

Disappointed!  Sat at the bar and the service was perfection, wine was good with excellent recommendations. I was in the tavern not nation dining and ordered oysters natural,(fresh and delicious) and the Calamari work snow peas that was salted within an inch of being palatable. Couldn't eat much of it and my tongue is still zinging from the salt

My favorite restaurant in Earth, and the best in NY on several occasions I've been here. We've done both the dining room, and bar and both were incredible. This time we say at the bar and had the chicken and the lamb. The chicken was incredible. The lamb could have been a little bigger and was served on a bread crostini but was excellent tasting.

We made reservations at the dining room for our third anniversary dinner. This restaurant had been on my list of places to try for quite some time and I'm so glad we finally did! All of their desserts were amazing, especially the complimentary chocolates and coconut cake. My favorite parts of our tasting were the smoked Arctic char and mushroom tortellini, both executed perfectly. Our waitress was extremely sweet as well and did a wonderful job at addressing our dietary restrictions and offering alternative options. I will definitely be returning and have heard great things about their more casual counterpart, the tavern, as well.
I believe this courses is mediocre, beef is good but dessert is not tasty, famous but not deserves that

We are long time fans. Live right around the corned. 
Still being locals a reservation is a must. Go for the fixed tasting menu and splurge on the wine.  Relax and save room for dessert

Gramercy Tavern encompasses two restaurants in one: A more casual, a la carte space, and a more formal dining room. My boyfriend and I came here for my 30th birthday dinner, so we opted for the chef's tasting menu in the dining room.

Remember that episode of House where one of the characters has Abulia, or the inability to make decisions? Well, the chef's tasting menu is perfect for the Abulia sufferer, as you basically just sit there and the waitstaff brings you dishes galore. We did have to pick a wine, though, a task we took on with some help from our server (the wine list is obviously extensive). She was exceedingly pleasant, by the way, all full of cheer and good nature throughout the entire course of the dinner. 

We settled on a bottle of 2012 St. Aubin, a light-bodied red burgundy that went nicely with everything.

The meal began with some fresh bread served with the best butter I have ever had: Goat Cheese butter. It was the kind of butter that was actually a little upsetting to eat, because most of us are just going to have to go back to regular butter after this. What is wrong with the world that we cannot be having goat cheese butter all the time?

Whatever, I'm over it. The courses consisted of the following:

Marinated Scallops (Fluke, Rhubarb and Cucumber)- One of the best dishes of the evening served straight away. Every ingredient was perfect in this dish, but I think I most enjoyed its bed of light sauce, which was sweet and tangy.

Warm Lobster Salad (Fregola, Sweet Peas and Basil)- Another excellent sauce, this one creamy and lemony. The fregola (I'll admit, I would've confused this for Israeli couscous if not for the menu) was also delicious.

Smoked Arctic Char (Summer Beans, Rye and Black Rice)- SO GOOD! Delicious, perfectly cooked fish topped with some sort of a crispy crust. Served with greens topped with a very light dressing with a nearly imperceptible hint of smokiness. 

Mushroom Tortellini (Nettles and Pecorino)- Not my absolute favorite of the evening, but I did enjoy it. The nettles were served pureed and the tortellini concoction was topped with a culinary foam. The flavors in this dish were bright and intense. 

Kinderhook Beef (Young Garlic, Blackberries and Blue Cheese)- I should preface this by mentioning that I almost never eat beef because I generally don't like it, but I occasionally forego this self-imposed dietary restriction and I chose to do so here. That said: Both of us thought this dish was a big miss, albeit the only miss of the night. The beef, cooked medium rare, was not flavorful and had too much gristle, and I had to swallow big bites because I just couldn't chew it. In addition, the blackberries and blue cheese just didn't do much to enhance the flavor. At least it was beautifully plated.

Lemon Meringue Tart (Cherries, Wild Chervil and Frozen Yogurt), and
Chocolate cake (Apricot Jam, Wild Rose, Fudge Sauce and Stracciatella Ice Cream), and
Coconut cream meringue birthday cake (complimentary)

All three of the desserts came out together and I was actually emotionally overwhelmed by the beauty of it all. I seriously cried (a very small amount, like 2 tears max). This was most likely due to the wine + cocktail I had before dinner, and possibly a slight, unconscious response to the emotional toll that comes with aging, or perhaps just other people commenting on one's aging, because it's really kind of a morbid joke when you think about it because the implicit punchline is really just our mortality, but anyway, seriously, I cried, and I think some of it had to do with the desserts. 

All of the desserts were wonderful- especially the lemon meringue tart, which was SUPER duper tangy with the lemon and cherries (yum). Of course, this was a LOT of dessert to have at the end of a meal so we only got through about half of the birthday cake and I took the chocolate cake home. 

The treats seriously just kept on coming, as we were presented with four complimentary after-dinner chocolates and a granola bar for the road, which I have not yet tried. Finally, to sober up as the check was coming, we ordered coffees, which were just perfect. I am a big coffee fan so that doesn't mean much coming from me, but even my boyfriend, who doesn't drink much of the stuff, raved about its quality.

In short, everything is pretty much impeccable at the Gramercy Tavern. It's unlikely that you will go wrong here.

Came in for a dinner at the tavern with my husband. We were told an hour wait. As we stood there 4 couples walk off the street and told that they would be seated within minutes. They didn't have reservations. I'm sure the food would of been amazing however their service was horrific.

Gramercy Tavern has all of the makings of what makes a restaurant memorable, mind blowing, delicious, incredible and a true joy. Not only is the restaurant beautiful, but they back it up with amazing service, delectable food and an amazing ambiance. I dined alone, the staff was friendly, accommodating and delightful. The food was flavorful, decent portions for the price and works of art. I enjoyed the dining experience from start to finish and loved dining at the bar. Would absolutely return for another memorable meal.

Came here for my 21st birthday a couple weeks ago and it was the single.best.dining.experience OF MY LIFE. My boyfriend and I have recently started trying to do a mini tour of Michelin stars whenever possible, and we were blown away here. 
We had a late reservation (9:00 I think) and showed up maybe 15 minutes or so early. They weren't quite ready for us but I wasn't expecting them to be, we had every intention of grabbing a drink at the bar before we ate. The ONE and ONLY downside of the entire evening was that the bar was packed and the bartenders weren't as customer-oriented as I was expecting. They seemed very stressed and flustered. I would have been too, in their defense, but they shouldn't have been so conspicuous about it. I ordered the Roger Fitz Spritz (Strawberry Liqueur, Vanilla, Aperol, Proscecco) which was delicious and garnished with a flower which I thought was awesome. I can't remember what my boyfriend had but he really enjoyed his too. After sipping on our drinks, we were sat at our table (the host took our drinks for us to the table, which was unnecessary but awesome service). 

[The Food]: I opted for the 3 course menu, and my boyfriend had the seasonal tasting menu. 

My first dish was the Squid Ink Campanelle with Lobster, Chorizo and Fava Beans which was TO DIE FOR. It was so rich, the flavors were balanced perfectly, the campanelle was perfectly al dente, the spice in the chorizo was complemented by the creamy sauce, and the portion size was much larger than I expected.

My second was the Duck Breast & Sausage with Cabbage, Pumpkin Seeds and Blueberries which was also amazing. If I had to pick a last meal I probably would choose the campenelle but GOD i wouldn't complain about having the duck breast either. It was so amazingly tender and juicy and I wasn't expecting the blueberries to be so awesome with it either but they were. 

For my last dish I had the cookie plate which I had been dreaming about for months. SO SO GOOD. And adorable presentation with a tiny jar of milk. The waitress also brought out a coconut cake for my birthday, which was delicious and beautiful. 

I can't remember all of my boyfriend's dishes, but standouts were the scallops (his first course), the smoked arctic char (which was some of the most amazing fish I have ever eaten), and the mushroom tortellini (which he hated but he's a picky eater- i can objectively say it was great though). 

Little complimentary treats included AMAZING bread with goat cheese butter (I could live off of that butter), homemade granola bars to take home and eat the next morning, mignardises, my cake (as previously mentioned), and a champagne toast for my birthday. I was absolutely stuffed with goodies, all of which were phenomenal. 

[Other]:

Our server gave us the most perfect service we've ever had and was a huge part in making my day incredibly special. I wish I remembered her name because I absolutely would like to give her credit personally. When we ate at Bouley a few months ago I found the service there very cold and mechanical and I docked it one star accordingly, and this could not have been any different. She was so nice to both us and the other front-of-house employees (thanked the food runners), recommended a fantastic bottle of wine, and orchestrated the champagne toast and complimentary cake and everything. I'm aware service is a huge component of her job, but she absolutely made me feel like a princess on my birthday and I'm so grateful for that. 

Also, cool bathrooms- the towels are a nice touch (LOL). 

[TL;DR]:

Can't recommend this place enough. Best dining experience of my life.

Amazing. A tastebud delight. 

Came here for lunch on a weekday and ordered the seasonal tasting menu (the entire table must participate -- vegetarian options available). I had been hearing amazing reviews about this place all summer so the hype was real ... but nothing disappointed. The tasting menu is a 5-course meal that varies per season. When I went, we started with (1) marinated scallops, which were perfectly tender and so, so fresh (2) the halibut, which was served with tomatoes  (3) mushroom tortellini, a small bite for truffle fans to swoon over (4) pork shoulder, which was melt-in-your-mouth good, and (5) chocolate cake so decadent I couldn't eat more than a bite. 

I had to refrain from licking the bowl of each dish. Everything was so good -- even the sweet pea palette cleanser they served before the dessert. Definitely a dining experience worth indulging in! 

Tips: Make a reservation 2 weeks in advance, business attire required for the formal dining room area, carve out time for a 2-3 hour meal (granted, service was a bit slow the day I went). Have heard great things about the duck, so will try next time I'm back (AND I WILL BE BACK).

With a party of 7 for an early Sunday dinner, we were given a window seat moments after arrival. Our waitress was friendly, helpful and attentive to every need. Each of us were served at the same time as several staff came with our meals. Price points were reasonable for the portions. Shrimp and wonton in a miso broth was very tasty and fresh! And the sea bass was phenomenal! We shared with our waitress my son had just come from a performance and she made sure the guest of honor received desert "on her". It was the only desert but each of us were given a plate and spoons "to share" cake with warm brownie, creme fresh and coconut ice cream. As more and more people came for dinner, I did not feel rushed and their was no appreciable change in noise level. Dress is casual to a bit formal. Highly recommend!

I played hooky on a Monday to come here for lunch and it was FANTASTIC. Totally worth taking a vacation day for, totally worth traveling into the city on a sweltering day for, totally worth dressing up a tiny bit for.

Service was great, although a little stiff at first, but the guys warmed up when they saw how much we enjoyed our food. We went with the five course seasonal tasting menu, and the absolute highlight was the mushroom tortellini. (If you know me... you won't believe that I just praised a dish that isn't a slab of meat.)

I'm going to let the pictures speak for themselves. :)

Delicious!  Ivan at the bar is great. 
Food was fantastic. Get the lamb flatbread. Cannot go wrong!!!

I could give you a long-winded review about how much I loved Gramercy Tavern at first sight, starting with stepping foot into the restaurant, our most attentive waitress, the soft, buttery and biscuit-like bread, the out-of-this-world squid ink campanelle, or the disassembled strawberry cheesecake that appears in my dreams at night.

But I won't because a picture is worth a thousand words, and I took plenty. This is a spot that's not to be missed!

The best restaurant I have ever eaten at. The food, service, and atmosphere are incredible (as a New Yorker, I realize how rare it is to find all three characteristics in one place). Our table did the seasonal tasting menu, and the flavors were nothing short of delicious. The dishes are unique but not outlandish. Gold star for Gramercy Tavern.

Walked in with wife in early July.  All the 1%'s were off to the Hamptons. Ate at the bar.  Nice and simple food, well prepared,  great vibe, service was spot on.  Not an arm and leg considering the high ratings.  Try the bar, you won't be disappointed.

I love gramercy tavern! Came for Saturday brunch for my birthday, and loved every second of it.  Amazing service by Carolyn and Juan - really made my mom and I feel special.  Had the tasting menu.  Favorite course was definitely the mushroom tortellini, and treat chocolate cake!  Best chocolate cake I've ever had - so moist and delicious.  Can't wait to come back!

Gazpacho was basically summer in a first course. Perfect.  Scallop and ruby red shrimp seasoned incredibly well and worked great.  Asian influence but not overpowering.  One of the best lunches I have had in NyC.  Capped off the experience with chocolate, black currant jam brittle.  Unique and memorable.

Have you ever sat in a restaurant, staring with longing at other people's food, wishing you had ordered differently?  That was my experience at GT.  Don't get me wrong, the food was all pretty decent.  The service and the graciousness of the staff was bar none.  I wonder though, if instead of the tasting menu in the dining room, what if we had stayed in the tavern?  What if we had instead ordered the three course menu that looked so appealing?

Should one ever feel this way after dining at a restaurant of this caliber and at this price point?  I think not.

We started in the Tavern with two excellent glasses of red wine.  The 2012 Priorat, the better of the two and the '12 Sinsky Cab which was also pretty good.  Both a little young but tasty nonetheless.

From there, we moved into the dining room and started our adventure.  First up was a tasty little amuse bouche which was decent but wasn't enough of a departure in flavors from the excellent bread with goat cheese butter, on which we doubled down.  It's amazing.  All the good food in these great restaurants and we fixate on the bread.

Next came a small and unimpressive looking chilled scallop and watermelon dish that, well, was tasty but not that interesting really.  Following that was the Warm Lobster Salad.  Now, honestly, there was lobster and it was delicious and this dish overall was a treat, but I think calling it a lobster salad is a bit of a stretch.  I would have called it a chowder salad with lobster.  The flavors of this were on the money with the sweet corn and sauce complementing the delicate lobster perfectly.  The Riesling paired with this dish wasn't impressive by itself but the pairing made the wine.

Overall, the wines were somewhat forgettable for me except for the few that paired ideally with the food.

After a decent amount of time, out comes a white plate with a white object smothered in white sauce.  Ah, not frosted dessert, but poached halibut.  Phew.  I thought we had somehow made it through the savory dishes already.  Now look, the halibut was cooked very well.  But the presentation was bland as was the overall flavor of the dish.  If it wasn't for the acidity of the sparse tomatoes, the dish would have been even less exciting.  https://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/gramercy-tavern-new-york?select=ZcW8v_r5E5q-zuxuuhwuUw

The Lumache came next.  A dish of white beans, pasta shells, parmesan and truffles.  I liked this dish.  The texture of the pasta went well with the flavor and consistency of the beans and the sauce was a rich, buttery base for the cheese.  That said, I felt like it could have been more.  You've had fresh shaved truffles before?  You know that aromatic, intoxicating quality that is why truffles are so sought after?  That just wasn't here.  Despite the generous brown topping, the effect was surprisingly minimal.  I'm not sure why but I'm sad about it.

The Willamette Pinot that came with it was also disappointing.  To be fair, earlier in the night, we opened a bottle of '04 Shea Estate which is one of the best Pinot's of the region in my humble opinion and maybe the J.K. Carriere they served didn't stand a chance.  To me, it was more like a Russian River Valley Pinot than the earthy wines I've come to expect from Oregon.

I barely remember the Pork Loin.  I can't believe I'm even writing this.  I'm reading the description of the dish now and thinking HOW CAN THIS BE?  Two preparations of Pork, Hazelnuts, Blackberries, Blue Cheese... OMG.  Sounds like the cornerstone of the meal of the year, doesn't it?  And yet, it was good.  It was good.  What it should have been was unforgettable.  It should have been monumental.  I should still have memories of its flavors on my palette.  Yet I don't.

Finally there was a nice, light palette cleanser and a stupendous chocolate cake.  And also the Vin Santo del Chianti pairing was easily smile inducing; not too sweet and a perfect pairing.  The cake.  This I remember.  The depth of the rich chocolate and the moist delicious cake was out of this world.

Was the meal awful?  No.  I do keep thinking about how much happier I could have been paying a third as much and staying in the tavern section.  As I look through the pictures on this site, almost all of them look better than many of our dishes.  What did I do wrong?

Final note, the staff and service, to reiterate, were top notch.

I went just myself noon and got a table in Tavern.(rather than dinning room after I checked the menu) Ordered duck mousse and calamari fried rice. The portion is really big . Actually it's the biggest one among the Mechlin restaurants I have tried both in London and NY.  Cant say how it gets Michelin star and also 4 and half on Yelp. The service is rfriendly and I give one star for that. But the food maybe is not just my type. Asian people might have higher standard on rice. Calamari fried rice is very salty for me and oily also. Besides I don't really like the bread of duck mousse. The plate display is just Okay.

Summary
This is a wonderful single Michelin star restaurant in the flatiron 'hood.  While I'm not sure why this place has a Michelin star and Sushi Nakazawa doesn't, I did enjoy the ambience, food, and drink selection.  Solid 4 stars.  Great place for dinner!

Atmosphere
There are several areas: a loungey front bar area, a rustic dinner area, and a more formal dining area toward the back.  Overall, it's very inviting, warm, and pleasant.

Food
My friend and I both got the lamb which was cooked to perfection with an arugula salad, perfectly seasoned.  We were pleased.

Drinks
A very commendable selection of wines.  We opted for a bottle of pinot from Willamette.  Still not overplayed.

Service
This is an area that could use half a star's worth of improvement.  Although it was busy around the 6 o'clock hour, service could have been slightly more attentive.  Once it got us going, it improved.

I was very disappointed with the food we had at the tavern last night. After having eaten in the dining room six months ago, I had high hopes for the tavern but the food fell flat. All the mains and appetizers we tried -- the cavatelli, testa, sea bass and lamb -- were incredibly salty; in fact, all we could taste was salt for most of these dishes. Eat at the dining room but skip the tavern.

I work around the corner and had chance to dine couple times, i never had bad meal here and let me tell you my office talks about it all the time . My favorite strawberry cheesecake i have to say i dont like desserts but this is something you cant resist. Pretty sure we will see you soon.

Was amazing! As always!  This is a treasure. The food is ridiculously good and the staff is fantastic!  My favorite!  I live for the desserts...seriously their pastry chef should be famous!  Super welcoming and always enjoyable! Love love love!

We ate here after a spontaneous morning of flywheel....... And we wanted to treat ourselves after  almost dying on those bikes......(don't worry we showered)

This review is for the casual section of the restaurant. We got their burger which was cooked decently but I feel like the bun could have been better? I'm not sure if the price could justify it as I've had better burgers a few dollars cheaper. We also got a nice simple salad so we would feel better about ourselves. And then the ice cream with peach  pie? It was super sweet so I couldn't finish it but that's why I bring MM around.  Service was great and everyone wore summer dresses or casual sweaters that you would find at country clubs. Great vibes but will come back for dinner.

Amazing restaurant and experience! My wife and I sat at the bar and had a fun time with the staff. We had our bartender/server choose for us some little appetizer/small plates that she liked and they were all outstanding. I'll definitely go back!

Seating & Service
We came early, our reservation was at 7:30, but we were seated at 6:45, so nice. The service is impeccable, just super friendly and really attentive. My husband and I came with our 2 kids to have dinner with a friend we were visiting. The number of utensils and napkins that were dropped and picked up by the servers merits an award. 

Food
The chef made the kids a pasta and chicken dish that my kids gobbled up (and the adults snuck in a few bites too because it was that good). We all had the seasonal tasting menu. I'd say that the food was good, nothing really stands out, but the strawberry "cheesecake" was outrageous. The strawberries I think were heirloom, small and packed with flavor. And the cheesecake filling was to die for and had bits of crunchy almost freeze-dried texture cake.

Perfect place for the full white tablecloth experience. The service, decor, and food are all amazing. NYC dining is often a cramped and hectic experience. This is the opposite: relaxed and enjoyable. Every course was delicious, and they even sent us home with an amazing muffin that was accompanied by a tiny jar of pb&j topping. I loved it. Highly recommend!
This is one of the best tavern for draft beers . Pretty nice place to be out with your friends . Classy ambience .

Been coming here on special occasions for years.  It has been impeccable every time.  Whether you're in the pub side which is more casual or the dining room, service, food, cocktails all perfect.  Dining doesn't get any better.  thank you for years of consistently wonderful food and service!

I will start off by saying that I am a huge fan of Danny Meyer and have been to pretty much all of his jaunts.  Gramercy Tavern is clearly the classic, my Flatiron fav that never fails to "wow."  The ambiance is beautiful and flower-filled; service is superlative. I typically will only consider the main room for major celebrations, given the expense.  But the front tavern also offers fabulous a la carte offerings at a somewhat more affordable price -- making Gramercy Tavern a realistic option not just for birthdays and anniversaries.

Amazing. Simply amazing. The seasonal tasting menu was paired so expertly with wine and each course better than the last. The service was also outstanding. This is easily in the top 20 dining experiences of my life and at the end I sincerely felt we had underpaid. We will be back for an encore!

We did the tasting menu, and it was phenomenal. Service is pristine. Cocktails are great. Lobster salad course was one of my favorites along with the bean pasta and pork done two ways (belly and loin). Overall pretty unique offerings on the tasting menu, not really dishes I'd order on my own, but all were surprisingly great. 

We said the occasion was for me just having moved to New York (not a traditional occasion to celebrate) but they still brought out a free yummy dessert with "welcome to NY" written on the plate. Great and appreciated gesture. We were able to replace the sweet dessert on the tasting menu with a cheese course instead. We were able to choose 3 cheeses, and the waitress was very knowledgeable in helping us choose based on our preferences. She had recommended the water buffalo, but I haven't loved buffalo cheese in the past, so I told her this and she allowed me to choose 3 others but still wanted to bring out the buffalo for me to try (also comped). This was great, and I actually ended up really enjoying all the cheeses I had including the water buffalo. 

Overall not my absolute favorite tasting menu I've ever had, but definitely a great and memorable experience. It is pricey, but that is expected with a tasting menu, and the service was just fantastic. Bread is also very tasty and comes with goat cheese butter spread :)

Great French country update vibe, bar area filled with beautiful flowers dining area a little more formal. They had our favorite oysters, a great fish entree for lunch and of course their home made sausage is always outstanding. Favorite and consistent go to place

Extremely friendly service, excellent food, and an amazing selection of non-alcoholic drinks (the gewurztraminer juice was particularly good).
Although we just ate lunch at the somewhat more casual "Tavern" section, there was an impressive selection of innovative appetizers, entrees, and desserts. The blueberry pie with corn ice cream (!), especially, was a remarkably unusual, and delicious, combination.
The jazzy music and interesting decor create a wonderful ambiance, and along with the food and the incredibly friendly staff make for a really great experience.

This place never fail to delight me. We ordered the seasonal tasting menu and, of course, loved them all. But first of all, THE BREAD!!! Ahhhh the beautifully fluffy bread with goat cheese butter, is the best thing ever. 

Okay, here's what we had: 
- Marinated Scallop: refreshing, amazing summer starter. 
- Halibut: FAVORITE of all! The tomato and kombu sauce sooo perfectly complemented this extremely soft and rich halibut. 
- Lumache: savory and chewy shell pasta with mushrooms and Parmesan 
- Duck Breast & Sausage: the duck was perfectly cooked medium rare- flavors elevated by the cabbage and sweet blueberries. I didn't really understand the addition of the sausage, which was good but not really needed to complete this dish. 
- Panna Cotta with frozen melon: palette cleanser: very light, on point
- Latte: they use intelligentsia coffee: light and sweet, makes my heart so happy
- Peach Rice Pudding: creamy consistency, simple and soothing flavors 
- Chocolates: such beautifully made chocolates (I can just look at them all day haha): one topped with crushed chips and includes caramel. The other containing jam and (I think) lemongrass or verbena cream
Absolutely loved it! Impeccable service, delicious tasting menus, both seasonal and vegetable. Special thanks to Anna who made the night extra special! Will definitely be back.
Went for lunch on sunday. Food was bland and very salty. No flavours. Service was very good.

This evening we tried the seasonal tasting fixed price menu in the dining room. From the moment we entered the restaurant, the service and attention we received was outstanding. All staff members were very personable, and made us feel right at home. Our dinner was delicious and lovely to look at, and after the dessert course was served there were still more treats to follow. This was an expensive meal, but it was a fine dining experience I recommend.
Absolute perfection. Waited for over an hour to sit down without a reservation but it was WELL worth it. Do not miss the beet salad. Everything was exquisite.
Great location, the park is just near by, food is really good but limited menu in my opinion. (For lunch) love this place anyway !

A wonderful experience from the greeting at the door to the goodie bag offered when you leave. Lots of excellent choices for both meat eaters and vegetarians. I've eaten in the casual Tavern area and the formal dining room. Both included great service, knowledgeable staff and impressive menu offerings. Great place to celebrate a special occasion.
New York is always a good choice and so is The Gramercy Tavern. I have a lot of favorites in the Big Apple. - This place, The SOHO Grand Hotel, Gansevoort, and The Four Seasons are a few of them!

Ridiculous!  That's the only word I can think of right now. Ridiculous awesome service-Emmanuel was wonderful. The food was amazing. We had a small issue that one of our dishes was cold (probably because one of the other dishes was fish). Emmanuel took it back right away and even got us some more wine complimentary for our trouble. Furthermore, we had trouble choosing between their amazing desserts, the so they brought one of their favorites in addition to what we picked. What a wonderful pleasant surprise. This is now one of my all time favorite restaurants in NYC. Can't wait to come back!

Bf made reservations for my birthday last year after hearing so much about this place. Unfortunately, the food did not meet our expectation whatsoever - especially for the price point. The service was amazing but the dishes weren't palatable - a bit bland. We felt like something was missing.

Just had an absolutely superb meal. Food was delicious and drinks were perfect. We were treated like Royals and we also received a special surprise as we told the staff we are on our honeymoon. Staff was very friendly, we are gutted we didn't get to say goodbye to Allen who looked after us as he was absolutely spot-on and made our evening a special one. Definitely reccommend!! Eli

Bland. I have no other words to say. I've heard word of mouth and read the reviews all stating the same thing, no season is used in this establishment. Now I dont know if this is only the tasting side because the other food definitely looked better. I wouldn't return to try but if you're thinking of going definitely do the normal sit down not the tasting.

One of my favorite restaurants in the city, eaten here more times than I can count, many times a year at the bar and generally once a year in the main dining room. The bar room is one of the great deals in the city, where you can go upscale with duck liver mousse and a nice piece or fish, or casual with a flatbread and the fantastic house made kielbasa (best when they put cheese in it!).  Great cocktails, wines by the glass and one of the most interesting beer lists in the city, including a whole section of vintage bottles. Service is great, as is the case at all of Danny Meyer's restaurants.

holy s**t! I know everyone raves about this place, but I was still caught off-guard. Attended a business dinner there the other night, and ate things that never knew would go together. Warm lobster salad? Amazing. Seabass? Good God. Even the butter they provide with the bread had me amazed. I need to come back...soon. It now makes sense. They deserve the reputation. A stunning experience.

Didn't expect anything less than a five star review for this Michelin star restaurant. I came here for my wedding anniversary dinner and they did not disappoint! We both ordered the tasting menu and it was delicious! Dinner started with the most amazing fluffy bread! We had two orders of that! My favorite two dishes were the halibut and duck breast. The halibut was cooked to perfection and the dish was light and delicious! The duck breast was cooked perfectly and very flavorful. Since we were dining there for our anniversary, we received a complimentary dessert which was a coconut cake. The cake was very fluffy and not too sweet. Overall, I had an amazing experience and would recommend this restaurant!

Welcoming and warm from the time I set foot inside the doors.  Opentable reservation for 530 PM to celebrate a wedding anniversary.  For what looked like first seating each party was brought to table by a personal host. 

We were seated in the back of the dining room and being early it was quiet until "regular" dinner time. 

The best thing about the evening was that everyone and everything was so accommodating with us having dietary restrictions (no pork or lobster) and me being pregnant.  We chose the seasonal tasting menu but got to pick 1-2 dishes from ala carte or vegetarian tasting menu to substitute. 

Here's the layout I had:
Get the sweet corn agnolotti if you can at all cost!  It was the most memorable dish of the night for me being fluffy-filled and flavors married perfectly!  Hubby got marinated scallops (served raw), "very refreshing" to him.

Halibut was good and I don't usually eat fish.  Lamb strozapetti was delish with a tiny spicy kick!  Lumache was even better.  All pasta was perfectly al dente and I was drinking the sauces with a spoon. 

Duck breast (perfectly seasoned and cooked) and sausage (strong fennel flavor) was good way to end entrees. Hubby got smoked cobia which he said paired well with eggplant. 

The next best part was being able to choose dessert (bc I loathe rice pudding which comes with seasonal tasting menu).  I went with the strawberry which is a deconstructed dessert of whipped cream that tastes like cheesecake, angel good cake crisps (amazing!), sorrel (herb) ice and tons of those delish mini strawberries! 

As it was our anniversary they gave us a mini coconut cake which was of course also tasty!  The meal is finished off with chocolates and house made granola bars to take home. 

The service was excellent: attentive, water always full, super diner-centered/accommodating. Hubby choose a wine but actually didn't like it so waitress rec an awesome one which he enjoyed. 

Overall, our experience was warm, welcoming, and delicious!
