Love the beautiful front room even if you can't make reservations. The food was delicious and reasonable, the service excellent  but exorbitant price of $20.00 was over the top.  My friend had a non alcoholic cosmanot that she loved and was $8.50 and delicious. I'm not sure why the martinis were so expensive. I know there is gin but can it add so much   Really love the restaurant other than that

This place was amazing!

I came here for a lunch reservation with a friend and was seated promptly. Sometimes when I step into places like this with a stiffer dining room feel, I sometimes feel like I've done something wrong already just by walking in. However, the wait staff  here is very warm and welcoming and make you feel right at home.

My friend opted for the tasting menu and I chose the beef tartare for my first dish and for my second dish I had the pork loin and deckle. After we ordered the waiter informed  me that there might be courses where I don't have food and my friend did (due to the tasting menu). However this was totally not the case throughout lunch! they were nice enough to send out two amuse bouches, which I thought was a really nice touch. They sent out gazpacho and another dish which was like a melon shaved ice on top of a cherry tomato panna cotta.

Onto the food!
Beef tartare - this was my first time eating beef tartare but it was soooo delicious! None of the flavors overpowered each other and the texture was perfect.

Pork loin and deckle - The pork loin was a little salty but the cut of meat was on point and cooked to perfection. This was the first time I had even heard of deckle which I actually thought was pork belly at first but is actually a cut of fattier brisket (please correct me if I'm getting this wrong). Normally I am not a fan of the texture of fat and gristlier foods but the deckle was definitely a gamechanger.

I had a bite of my friend's halibut (so tender) and his duck breast (so juicy). His favorite he said though, was the escargot. Then for dessert he kinda split off from the tasting menu (which they allowed) and we ordered the cookie plate and the raspberry coconut milk cake with the apricot sorbet. The coconut milk cake was very unique and the apricot sorbet was suuuper delicious. The cookie plate was very fun as well. They also gave us chocolates, I don't know whats in the one with the red dot on top but it's certainly magical.

5 stars for the service and food, for sure.
Cold drinks, friendly staff.. Nice woodlawn (Bronx) feel in lower Manhattan.  Fantastic burger, no frills, no frozen patty.. definitely recommend a visit for a few cold ones and a beer

Wow.  I've never had such attentive service.  Crab & corn salad was just a wee bit salty, but other than that, everything was hit out of the park.  The poached chicken was exquisite.  The ice cream - strawberry ricotta, black pepper, and corn - was unbelievable.  Then they plied us with petit fours and a granola bar to take home.  I was pretty much spoiled for anything back home in Vermont.  Worth it.

This is Gramercy Tavern. Everybody wants to say wonderful things about Gramercy Tavern, and I am one of them! However, while it is a beautiful place, with impeccable service and an innovative menu, the truth is that I have simply had better. I have had better dinners derived from better tasting menus; therefore, I simply wasn't impressed with the food. I just wasn't. 1789 in Washington DC, The French Laundry in Yountville, Tommy Toys in San Francisco (before they so sadly closed)...those were all memorable meals. This one just wasn't. It's not snobbery, it's just my honest experience. 

If I could give a half-star rating, I would. 3 stars is just too low, but 4 stars is too high...3.5 would have been just right. We'll come back again to give it another try...because it's Gramercy Tavern!

It's good dawg. This s*** hit the spot like Robin Hood slays archery targets and princesses. But yo... Dat smoked tomato soup tho... Even betta than mah Gma's, but don't tell her cuz she don't have much time left... Nah mean. Seriously tho, check dis joint out

We did the tasting menu with the wine - Everything about it was fabulous.  
Can't wait to go again!

After countless tosses and turns, I finally made up my mind to make the reservation a month ago just to make sure I get to try the famous Gramercy Tavern on the anniversary day with my beloved.

Since we have 2 friends attending with us, we were able to try almost each item on the 3 course menu. Overall, I don't find their dishes particularly outstanding. They didn't really give us the "WAO!" factor that we are expecting from a Michelin star restaurant. To be quite honest, I have had better experience at few other restaurants that would make me go back more than once. One thing that all their dishes are lacking is the taste of dedication and focus from the chef, and That's why it tasted like too many things are going on with your dish but none harmonized with each other.

However, I have to give them a big complement on the dessert! Special shout out to the lavender cream with chocolate cake. It is certainly a taste that you would not find at other places. If it wasn't for the dessert, I would have given them 3 stars instead.

Last but not least, the staffs are very friendly and customer services is excellent. Our waiter is very patient to answer all of our questions professionally. I would recommend to try at least one time to see if you like it.

Nice- expectedly nice tho. 

To Eat: anything Lamb; Lamb Flatbread and Lamb Entree, plus great items like Roasted Tomatoes Mac & Cheese, and Kobucha Squash

To Drink: cute mixology but not extremely different from any other bar, wine (POV), and an IPA 

Service is one of Meyers platforms; and tho it was good, it wasn't exceptional like I had anticipated.  For New York tho, I guess this place is better than most...nobody cares at all in this city, everyone treats you like you are lucky to land on their establishment...everyone.

I had lunch at this restaurant. The food was fantastic! I ordered Warm Lobster Salad, Corn, Romano Beans, and Spiced Almonds as 1st course, Black Bass, Mussels, Peppers and Potatoes as 2nd course, and Gramercy Tavern Cookie Plate with Milk as dessert. Warm lobster salad had nice mild taste, but was pretty unmemorable. The lobster meat tasted fresh and was enough big for my satisfaction. Black bass was amazing. A waiter entertained to pure beautiful pink lobster sauce around the black bass. The sauce was outstanding and I dug in bass,veggies, and sauce together with a spoon lol It was sooooo yummy! Finally, I had famous cookies and milk. The chocolate cookie was the best I have ever had. It was perfectly soft and moist inside and slightly crispy outside, and fresh! It was just heaven and great match with the milk. I had cappuccino on the side and it was average. I also had 2 glasses of white wine, Tokaji Sec and Scheurebe Spatlese with food. Both were nice. Service was a little slower and nobody cared my wine glass was empty so long. Two waitresses kept gossiping behind and it was annoying. I felt this restaurant was a little more for tourists not high-end.

Food is absolutely amazing!!! Pork Loin and Squid ink dish--highly recommend. Dessert was wonderful too. We had the cookies. Generous portions. And they gave us homemade granola bars to take home. 
The service is not as good as you expect. They are super polite but it seems they are not as attentive as they should be considering type of restaurant. Maybe they were short staffed when we went. Although the kitchen did a wonderful job with substitutes due to allergies.
Outstanding! We had the tasting menu plus the wine tasting menu and loved every moment of it. Worth the splurge!

Excellent service, prompt and polite. Had the tasting menu with wine pairing. The squid ink pasta with lobster was delicious and impressive. They gave out free chocolates and a coconut cake for my daughter as well coz it was her birthday. A very good fine fine experience! Definitely recommend!

I went with my girlfriend on a Sunday evening and we had a flawless dining experience.

The dining room is beautifully presented and one thing I noticed was the music - there was none of it!  Too many bars and restaurants in NYC these days have loud music assaulting your ears but the dining room was filled with the pleasant hum of conversation instead.

Our server was extremely helpful and friendly.   We both did a testing menu (the veg one and the meat one), and all the dishes were original and delicious; the food was beautifully presented and filling.

By the end of the evening, when the two beautiful small chocolates arrived just after the check, I felt like Mr Creosote, and could not have managed another crumb.

The Gramercy Tavern dining room is expensive but worth every penny; the perfect place to treat yourself to a wonderful dining experience.

"amazing experience"

had dinner there on 10/8/16 in group of 7. some ordered protein tasting with wine pairing; some ordered vegetable tasting. all items were delicious and service was very attentive without being intrusive. main server was anna, who was very knowledgeable about food and wines. she was also very entertaining. complimented the manager, luciana, on the food and personnel. she was gracious. would DEFINITELY go to here again.

Finally able to dine at this very popular, Michelin star New American restaurant under Executive Chef Michael Anthony.
The lunch tasting menu reasonably priced at $65 pp.

Highlight dishes:  Warm lobster salad, Artic char, & the perfectly prepared duck breast/sausage course. 

Extensive dessert list (they allow you to substitute the dessert on the tasting menu for something on the dessert menu): Tried the Strawberry/whipped cheesecake & Mango/frozen yogurt, and enjoyed both.

Service - Very good.

Unlike other Danny Meyer's establishments, gratuity not included here.

Highly recommend.

: 9 calendars

IN SHORT: Whether you're choosing from the a la carte menu at the front tavern, or the fixed menu in back dining room, Gramercy Tavern's high-end, yet informally New American food is sure to win over both your tastebuds and your heart.

THE STORY: If there is one anecdote to summarize the experience of Gramercy Tavern, it is this: at a meeting the day after a recent dinner, I mentioned offhand to a group of colleagues that I had eaten at Gramercy Tavern the previous night. For the next 10 minutes, nearly every person in the room shared a story about the last meal they enjoyed there, be it for a special occasion or a lovely meal with close friends.

Gramercy Tavern is a restaurant where memories are made, where everyone in the dining room has something in common. It is a restaurant that nearly every New Yorker seems to look upon with fondness, relishing perhaps not the best meal ever had, but the most enjoyable one. Yes, in New York, Gramercy Tavern may not be the most fiery, groundbreaking, adventurous restaurant, but it is indubitably the most loved.

This year, Gramercy Tavern celebrated its 22nd birthday, and it's clear that the classic, accessible dishes coming out of the kitchen haven't lost any of their luster, or appeal. In the Dining Room, Chef Michael Anthony's straightforward, exquisitely cooked food can be experienced with a $98 3-course prix fixe, or a $125 6-course tasting at dinner. Anthony works best with ensembles of vegetables, all reflective of the season and sharply complementary, so the $110 vegetable tasting is not to be overlooked either. Carrots, fennel, green olives, and orange are thrust together in one dish, while cucumber, melon, and dill balance with light-handed finesse in another, true testaments to Anthony's classically light, New American style of cooking.

Though the food at Gramercy Tavern is often more soft and low-key than it is vivid and passionate, it is anything but tame. At a recent dinner, wagyu beef tartare was served with mushrooms, pine nuts, and turnips, a subtle, nutty, yet somehow rich elevation of the meat. Anthony doesn't rely on much salt, and in another pasta dish, creamy, garlicky flavors played off of crunchier, more vegetal ones for an elegant, approachable bite.

True to his gentle style, Chef Anthony also excels in poaching and braising meats, particularly naturally light flavors like pork and chicken. A pork loin and belly dish sat in a delicate, Asian broth, its vinegar and kimchi flavors brightening the entire plate. A braised lamb loin and shoulder with squash, sunflower seeds, and lots of herbs was also excellent, full of hearty, but still clean flavor.

Desserts are slightly less strong and sometimes a little formulaic, but a quenelle of carrot ice cream atop a slice of carrot cake was some of the best I've ever had. Every ingredient seems to be treated with a wholesome respect, a sentiment that the staff applies to service as well. Of course, this is a Danny Meyer restaurant, and graciousness and unpretentiousness reign supreme, despite the fine dining surroundings. In this sense, this unlabored sophistication is the essence of Gramercy Tavern, a vibrant, blended, quintessentially American classic. It's no surprise its appeal is so broad, and so deep.
I tried their lunch tasting menu and i enjoyed my time there. They deserve their Michelin star.

Always my favorite place to come for every special occasion!  Have spent many birthdays here and always love to bring family and friends as a special meal for them.   The beautiful flora arrangements and open kitchen add so much character.  I have dined in the main dinning room and the tavern.  Such a beautiful space we come from Brooklyn to dine here!

My wife and I went for the lunch tasting menu during August 2016. Simply put, Gramercy Tavern would be THE BEST restaurant in virtually any other American city. The lunch tasting menu was an absolute bargain at $65 per person. We told our waitress that we were celebrating our anniversary, and she returned with complementary champagne. My wife does not drink, so our waitress quickly returned with sparkling cider. That is just one example of the fabulous service we had here during our 3-hour lunch.

And the food - wow. Everything was perfect. Most dishes were quite light and simple, letting the ingredients shine. We added the warm lobster salad to share as an additional course - that was probably the highlight. Oh, and a beautiful lumanche pasta with mushrooms and herbs... holy cow I am drooling just recalling our meal here.

We don't live in New York and don't visit often, and with so many amazing restaurants there it's hard to repeat things. But I can say with 100% certainty that we will have lunch at Gramercy Tavern on our next trip!

This remains one of the top restaurants in NYC with one huge caveat -- the a la carte available upfront is 5-starts and the tasting experience is 2-3 stars. The front doesn't take reservations so go early and do it right, skip tasting in the back. Order the off-menu burger if that's what in the mood for and if they haven't run out.

Another great meal at the Tavern We had a late dinner at the pub area and as always it did not fail 
The service was great and the food was fantastic
Had the clam pizza which was crisp and lite and so tasty The cauliflower and kale salad was crunchy and perfect My favorite were the baked oysters the sauce a bit spicy but left me wanting to eat more just delicious Our sea bass entree was also very lite and well prepared For dessert we had the pudding that had so many different flavors textures and temperatures that awakened all your taste buds 
We have come here many times over many years and commend the staff for their devotion and consistency Will be back
It was very good, The service is great. I wouldn't choose to do the 6 course menu if I were a larger person or a man since the portions are extremely small.

One of the best restaurants in Manhattan.  Wanted to go for so long and just kept putting it off.  Sorry  we did.   Absolutely fantastic.   I will give it one and ONLY one negative.   They are doing construction right in front and since my husband has a leg problem.  Not good.   But lets forget that because construction or not we will be back.   Food.  Clean, fresh , delicious.    Waiters and staff.   Couldn't be more helpful.    Enjoyed our anniversary
It's super amazing! You should definitely have a try!And the service is perfect! The food, the wine, the atmosphere... Love it!

We went to Gramercy Tavern a few months ago.I just made a Yelp account,but it is this meal, from months ago during a weekend trip, that deserves my first review.

My first contact with the restaurant was by phone, weeks prior to my trip, in order to make a reservation. Although they were pretty booked up, the staff on the line was very helpful by finding a seating that worked with my plans. I asked that they follow up with me in a few days to see if anything opened up...and they actually did. First impressions matter.

The bread and butter were amazing. At a restaurant of this level, bread and butter should of course be an easy win, but it was worth mentioning. My wife and I were a little buzzed by the time we got to the restaurant, and the bread was a welcome carbohydrate. In all seriousness, if you were to visit just for bread, butter, and wine, you would have to give this place at least three stars.

My wife and I both had the three course. The menu changes frequently; while Yelp reviewers often go into lengthy explanations course by course, suffice to say that every single dish we had hit the mark. 

The wine list is extensive and there are great options at all price points. We ordered an 07' Bordeaux. The Somm first brought out a Bordeaux, but certainly not the one we ordered, and at a price point I could not fathom spending. Thankfully, in my stupor, I actually paid attention to the label before he opened and poured.

The wine mix up was minor, the staff were deeply apologetic, and certainly not a big deal. That being said, if we would've drank up the whole thing and seen the check, it would've turned a great night a bit awkward. Servers and somms might want to be more proactive in getting this right. 

Otherwise, my experience here with my lovely wife was second only to dinner at August in New Orleans.

Went there for lunch. Had the dumpling soup, Mac and cheese and Sea Bass. All were amazing. We were there for brunch on a Sunday and sat in the bar. This place is definitely a win and you should add to your list.

Excellent service and well mannered staff
Well portioned food and delicious
Not salty and desserts are perfectly not too sweet
Clean place and vary nice ambiance
Had a great time and will come back

Coming from San Francisco, I had great expectations regarding Gramercy Tavern as I wanted to taste one of the best table that Big Apple can offer. I was highly disappointed by my experience.

We came for dinner on Saturday evening. We had the $100 prix fixe menu.

The starters were both delicious, definitely what you can expect from a one start michelin restaurant.

My main course was good. However the main course of my girlfriend was not satisfying at all as the lamb sausage was undercook. We had to send it back. No one is checking the quality of the plates before serving them to the customers?

The dessert of my girlfriend was a pavlova. It was ok not great, definitely not as good as the quality of pavlova we can eat at Frances in SF - for half the price! I had the cookie plate and was very disappointed. What's the point of bringing a dessert that has more than half the calories of the whole dinner? It it not balanced at all. Furthermore the quality was really bad compared to for example to the cookies you can get at Bi-rite Market in SF.

Regarding the service it was professional. However it was too slow after the main course.

We won't recommend this place. When you pay this price, you should get a great experience.

Dining at Gramercy Tavern last night was a real treat and incredible experience. We were advised by our server Stafford, who was relaxed, fun, and generous with his time, to try two of the seasonal menus, so we could explore more of the menu. The food was delicious, intriguing, and easily the best meal I have ever had. We learned a lot about cheese and wine and more from Stafford and found our experience to be educational. At the end of the evening, Luciana Autilio stopped by to check in our experience. She was warm and friendly and made us both feel right at home. I told her that the restaurant and staff gave off the warm feel so often described in setting the table. I hope this restaurant is around for another 20 years. We will be back!

I first heard of Gramercy Tavern while reading a Yelp review for Noma in Copenhagen where someone praised Gramercy over Noma. I went to their Yelp page and saw with well over 2,000 reviews they had a 4.5 star average. I then saw a couple of my Yelp friends who have excellent taste raved about it too. It sounded like a sure thing and I definitely thought I'd be in for a treat. Unfortunately, I did not have one of those amazing experiences many have wrote about.

I made lunch reservations a few weeks in advance, arrived on the dot, and was seated right away. They sat me in the dining area which felt a bit cold when compared with the front bar/"tavern" area. The bar/tavern felt more lively and festive and if I were to come back, I would much prefer to sit there in the future, especially for lunch.

I had the option of going with their a la carte menu or doing their seasonal tasting menu. Considering it was a special occasion I figured I'd go all out and go the tasting menu route, plus my server recommended it over a la carte. In retrospect, I definitely would have gone the a la carte route instead. While I've seen pricier tasting menus, I would have much rather spent half as much on the a la carte if the result in the flavors would have been the same. In fact, some of the a la carte options being served around me, looked better and more substantial than what I received with the tasting menu.

So many of the reviews here speak to the spectacular service. With 5 courses plus an amuse bouche and a pre-dessert bite, not a single person came up to me during my meal to ask how things were. Not even once. Look, I'm the last person who comes to a restaurant expecting them to bend over backwards for you, but simply checking in on a table during a meal to see how it's going is restaurant 101, especially at somewhere like this. The only time someone checked in on me was right after the meal when I had left the dessert half eaten. I think he was the manager and he asked if I did not like it to which I said parts of it I did and other parts I did not. He offered another dessert to which I declined. He was great and on the level of exceptional service other reviewers have written about, unfortunately it came too little too late. The rest of the servers seemed like robots, reciting lines and going through the motions. I can believe that this may not be their normal mode of operation, but this was what I experienced.

As for the food. Most of it you could tell was crafted with a great degree of skill and expertise. Perhaps my expectations were too high coming in, but there was zero wow factor with any of the dishes in terms of flavor. My carrot salad amuse bouche pretty good as was the arctic char. The rest was easily forgettable, except for the duck sausage that tasted like Johnsonville brand frozen sausage (this is not meant as a compliment) and one of the truffles which I found to be disgusting. I love chocolate, but one of the two truffles they gave was just awful in my opinion. I can't think of a time at a restaurant where I actually wanted to spit something out that I was eating, but I really wanted to with that truffle. I got through it, but man oh man I did not like it at all.

No one is perfect, and there are enough positive reviews here where my experience here could easily have been an anomaly. Unfortunately, it was an anomaly I had to experience and pay for and as a result, it is unlikely I'll return.

We had a reception for our intimate City Hall Wedding in the private room, and could not have been happier! 

The room itself is beautiful, of course- but also generously sized- perfect to set up a small bench for the nieces and nephews to occupy themselves quietly with coloring books while the adults mingled. The table was set for our party of 13 and was comfortable and the perfect size to allow for conversation among our new family.

The food was spectacular; everyone was happy with their meals, from the 'foodies' to the meat-and-potatoes father-in-law! We are all still talking about how delicious this meal was!
The service was impeccable; specifically the dedicated wait staff who took care of us were so friendly and attentive. They were so sweet to the children in our party who wanted to try the 'fancy' appetizers! The presentation was impressive and perfectly timed, and we did not have to ask for anything- the whole event was perfectly orchestrated without us having to lift a finger!

The planning process was smooth overall; through a series of emails & meetings, we were able to define exactly what we wanted, and Marci on the event team filled in all the rest with the perfect details. We gave the team a cake topper and no direction other than flavor, and were presented with a simple and gorgeous cake that was as delicious as it was beautiful. We asked if a few special family photos and objects could be displayed in the room, and on the day of I was brought to tears at how perfectly my late father's wood carvings looked peeking out among the plants in the centerpiece, and how lovely our guestbook and photos looked flanking the cake. 

Overall, we loved every moment of this experience, and can't wait to come back again!

Fantastic experience! I sat at the bar, asked for a drink recommendation, and had lunch. The amuse bouche of shredded carrot salad was grounding- so few ingredients, so flavorful. Following this- I had what was very likely the best fluke crudo of my life. The entire experience from start to finish was accommodating, anticipatory, and smooth. I will look forward to my next visit.
Food is superb but the service was below standard from what were used to. Very slow and inattentive which is not typical.

The food is perfection. Delicious down to the last morsel. The staff is very professional and service is great. However it's very loud and you're seated very close to other patrons especially if your table is by the bar. Other than that it is definitely worth trying for the food. I look forward to going back.

Went for lunch back in July 2016. I ordered the beef carpaccio with peach, lamb, and split dessert with two friends. 

Pros:
- Easy reservations, relaxed but sophisticated atmosphere, generous portions, and reasonably priced menu. 
- Beef carpaccio was scrumptious. Thinly sliced and well marinated, complemented perfectly by the tangy peach. The croutons were slightly crunchy and offered a bite to an otherwise soft-textured dish. The presentation was gorgeous as well.
- My friends both ordered the duck as their entree and loved it! 

In-Between:
- The dessert was quite average, delicious but nothing novel; wasn't impressionable enough for me to remember what it was. 
- Fresh, warm bread! Unfortunately, they serve it with goat cheese butter, which is too pungent for me.

Cons:
- I'm actually not that much of a fan of lamb but it was recommended by the server, so I figured why not. It was too gamey for my taste, but I usually don't eat much lamb to begin with. There was a chunk that was way too overcooked and hard to chew, but everything else was tender. The citrusy couscous balanced the heavy flavors out well though.

We were late for our lunch reservation but we were seated promptly. Service was excellent and attentive. As we were having lunch at 1pm and our dinner reservation was at 6pm, we did not want to get stuffed. However, we didn't regret for our decision to have the lunch tasting menu. It was well worth to put extra work on our digestion system. Our waitress was very nice to us to allow us to share the wine pairing as we didn't want to get bombed with the alcohol for the rest of afternoon. We will come back again for sure.

Excellent meal. Every dish was superbly executed. Kale salad and roasted chicken show stoppers. The black bass too. Customized wine pairings available. The vibe is unique -- distinctly rustic while maintaining modern finesse.

It was once excellent, The provider is quality. I would not prefer to do the 6 direction menu if I had been a greater character or a person seeing that the parts are particularly small. The location is break up into two separate areas. You could have the dinner in the dining Room and a la carte near the entrance/bar area. The carrier here is nothing short of impeccable.I extremely recommend visiting this situation at the least as soon as...

Amazing meal! 
We went in a group of 8 for a work dinner and decided on the tasting menu. One of our colleagues has several allergies and was prepared to not be able to eat a meal here but they were excellent about accommodating her requirements. My favorites were the salmon and squid ink pasta. We also did wine pairing and it was excellent. 

Highly recommend and would definitely go back!

My fall trip to NYC included many good restaurants. This meal was S U B L I M E. 
We spent a leisurely Sunday there, imbibing wonderful champagne and eating the finest tasty choices. 
It's a wonderful experience, the staff is very excellent, and friendly, treating customers like regulars, or family.  They bent over backwards for us on a few points and couldn't be more gracious about my special requests. The space is gorgeous in a simple, rustic way. The fall floral designs of pumpkins, mums, orange roses and delicate posies and the fall bounty on the antique wooden sideboard created a picturesque mood. The ingredients are the freshest, and the cooking style brings out the best flavor in each item. Each course was more surprising than the next and each plate is plated on beautiful, and some unusual dishes, in such a creative array. It was art for the eyes, and a joy for the palette. 
Many warm feelings as we shared in our delight of each morsel. It's truly still one of the greatest offerings of this magnificent city. Don't miss it.
Gramercy Tavern is one of the best restaurants in New York City. The service was excellent and the food was delicious. Great for a romantic dinner. It is expensive but completely worth it.

I went to gramercy last Thursday for a class project. During my entire service, all the waiters were attentive to any questions i had and the food did not take long to arrive. The price for lunch was very understandable (I had a 3 course meal that was priced around $60). Overall, I would go back just for the experience once more.

I had the opportunity to dine here for my birthday. We were only able to secure a 12PM reservation on Saturday (this place is too popular!) so we opted for the Lunch Tasting Menu for $65.

Lunch Tasting Menu:
1) Marinated Scallops, heirloom beans, grapes and kohlrabi
2) Arctic char, cauliflower, apples, and chiles
3) Squid ink lumache, lobster, chorizo, and peppers
4) Duck breast and sausage, lentils, celery root, and cabbage
5) Concord Grape Palova, goat cheese, mousse, sesame halva, and mint

My thoughts:
1) Delicious and refreshing since it's served cold. The amount of scallops we had was also very surprising! I was expected a 3-4 chunks, but this was enough to fill the bowl! The grapes were a bit icy too, so super refreshing.
2) The Arctic char is smoked to perfection and was the softest fish I have ever had. If i didn't know it was fish, i would have thought this was tofu. 
3) This was probably my favorite dish. Overall composition of the flavors went together so well and had a little bit of a kick. The pasta was al dente and the sauce was perfect with the bread that they serve.
4) This was probably my least favorite dish only because I'm not a fan of duck. It didn't taste too strongly of duck and was super well cooked and very moist. The sausage on the plate helped fill you up just in case you weren't full.
5) This has a distinct goat cheese taste. My boyfriend, who isn't a fan of goat cheese, even liked this! It wasn't a strong goat cheese taste, but you can definitely tell it's goat cheese. It was paired with a merigue-like cookie and grape sorbet. Yum!! All different flavors and textures in your mouth.

Besides the amazing food, the BREAD WAS DELICIOUS. Don't forget to ask for seconds and thirds! The warm, buttery bread with the goat cheese butter...mmm!!!

Before course #5, they served a walnut ice cream and lime sorbet as a palate cleanser.

This place has an extensive wine/beer selection and my boyfriend was very happy to sample their beers. They offer half glasses for $4.50 and full glasses for $9. So no loss if you wanted to order two half glasses to try two different beers.

Lastly, my boyfriend made me go to the restroom between the palate cleanser and the dessert so he could order me a birthday dessert. So they bought out the cutest coconut layered cake with a candle and "HAPPY BIRTHDAY JASMINE" written on it, which made me feel super special. The best part was that they comped it too!

Service was flawless--our waitress was very attentive and made us feel so welcomed. She even kept wishing me happy birthday.

Total bill was about $180, including drinks and tip. Well worth a special occasion and I will definitely love to come back!

Timeless Perfection...I am never disappointed by the food or the service here.  When I travel to NYC and have time to sneak in a personal dinner, I head to the Tavern and pray for the good fortune to snag a seat.  My foodie karma is is good so I have lucked out many times!  This place is on my Top 10 restaurants list for good reason

This place was absolutely incredible: the location is great, the service is amazing and the food surpassed all my expectations. They had a selection of vegetarian options as well and were flexible with food restrictions. We tried the seasonal dinner tasting menu. Each dish had a unique taste and was absolutely delicious! It's a MUST try. And it was just the right amount of food. 

It's one of the  best dinners I've had in NYC. If you're in NY, you must try it!

we had the seasonal tasting menu which has about four courses for $125/person and it was very good. The dishes were a nice play on textures and contrasts. Service was great and room noise was not too loud. It was a nice place to have dinner.

Edward norton was sitting across from us in the main dining room. The food was 10/10. What an experience!

This place is still on another level - the food, service, and ambience is unparalleled anywhere. We went for our anniversary and every waiter knew the occasion and graciously mentioned congrats on the way out. If it wasn't a pretty penny and a challenge to get a table I would eat here every night  out.

Gramercy Tavern:

Zagat: F 4.8 D 4.6 S 4.7
NYT: ***
Michelin: One Star

Lunch Seasonal Tasting Menu (http://www.gramercytavern.com/menu/#the-tavern):

* Marinated Scallops
Horseradish, Meyer Lemon and Trout Roe
- The scallops were served warm combined with trout roe and lemon sauce; the dish presentation harmonized well and the garnish was very pleasant to the eyes. Scallops were tender but at the same time chewy (on the positive side); in general the dish was light, hearty with a touch of lemon-sour.

* Arctic Char
Cauliflower, Apples and Chiles
- Arctic char served on grilled cauliflower and apple slices; the char was prepared perfectly - juicy and succulent, and it well (maybe a little too well) absorbed the sweet and tart flavor of the apple.

* Squid Ink Lumache
Lobster, Chorizo and Peppers
- Squid ink lumache with shredded chorizo sausage and peppers. The lumache was completely dark and had an implicit flavor of the squid ink, but somehow it was too chewy. The chorizo sausage added some meaty flavor to complement the dish that could otherwise be pretty plain.

* Duck Breast & Sausage (RECOMMEND)
Lentils, Celery Root and Cabbage
- This dish was highlight of the day; the two otherwise unrelated meats were cooked to perfection and paired so well with each other to let the dish shine. The duck breast was slightly peppery and the sausage was smokey, both enhanced by the flavorful sauce underneath. 

* Concord Grape Pavlova
Goat Cheese Mousse, Sesame Halva and Mint

Restaurants like Gramercy Tavern - dishes were themselves a delight but it was the beautiful decor and welcoming service which made the dining experience as memorable as the one we had.

Overall: 4.5/5

Very good. even it's expensive, quite. But it's worth it. 

The marinated scallop is a pleasant surprise, very fresh!

This is one place where the food and service definitely live up to the cost and the hype. Came here for a business lunch recently and I could not have been more impressed with both the food and the service. My chicken was cooked perfectly and tasted delicious, and arrived with a small sausage on the side which was also delicious. The food was delivered by a man wearing a suit probably nicer than the one I had on at the time. All in all a fantastic experience. I will surely return soon.

This place is 5 stars.  We had the dinner tasting menu with the wine pairing.  I recommend you do that because the sommelier really pairs excellent choices.  You know at this place the menu will not disappoint, so I'll focus on the small touches.  

First the service was amazing.  The servers were very nice and helpful without being overly eager or sounding fake.  Also, the bread and butter here is delicious.  You probably think, oh its just bread and butter, but actually its more than that.  The bread is warm and crusty and the butter melts perfectly over it.  This is just one of those NY institutions you must try.
One of my favorite restaurants in the city! This is a MUST for everyone during the holiday season!
Service was terrible they kept picking up the plates before we finished. The only amazing thing here is the beef tartare. Everything else is ok.
Hands down best service I have ever received! Loved the ambiance, food... everything. Amazing!
This is the best meal I've ever had in NYC.  The next time I have something to celebrate, or someone visiting from out of town, I'm coming here.  For sure.

One of the BEST dining experiences I've had in the city of New York. It's not just the fancy setting or the fining dining. Service was so attentive, and it almost certainly made me decide to come back next year on the spot.

Oh yeah. Finally a 5 star.   Took me my lifetime to make it here and it sure didn't disappoint.  Our lunches were delicious and so was the bread.  Even got a nice little coconut cake dessert from the manager for some strange reason-- maybe because I was a big 9 1/2 months prego- but wow did we appreciate it.   The service from the waiters and host was all class.  Not like so many other uppity restaurants in town.  The service was not only friendly and respectful but very efficient.  The decor with the sunflowers everywhere - gorgeous.
It is not only the food but the excellent service that makes me want to go back.

We ended up in the hospital. We educated our waiter and told him we can have a deathly allergic reaction to all nuts and forms of sesame and he served us a dish cooked in sesame oil. Scariest night of my life.

I have heard great things about Gramercy Tavern and with it making so many lists, I had high hopes. 

My husband and I arrived around 1:50pm and got seated around 2:15 on the tavern side. We ended up staying for a little over two hours. Our servers (we had two, as they ended up swapping at the end of our first server's shift) were kind and helpful but not always the most attentive. They were great and well versed but we often found it difficult to spot them as they seemed "too busy" to drop by out table. 

We took a while to order because I am often undecided but definitely made some great decisions. As it was a gifted birthday dinner, we went all out. We got three cheeses, the raddichio with bacon, the brussel sprouts fried rice and the duck andouille. Although everything was truly delicious, the brussel sprouts fried rice was probably one of the best things I've had. As a meat lover, I often only order meat dishes but I love brussel sprouts and wanted to give it a try and it did not disappoint. The roger spitz(?) Was also splendid. 

We went with the baby pancake for dessert and although it was good, the pear brandy was wayyyyy to strong on the side that i started eating on. It almost felt as if I was inhaling straight up rubbing alcohol which was slightly disappointing. 

Although there were a few hiccups throughout the meal overall it was a good experience and we did enjoy our time there. 

Oh, also, the bottled sparkling water is 10 dollars a bottle and they don't keep it at your table.
Always impeccable.  Great hospitality, great beverage list, great food.

Great food and superb service. lobster salad was really fresh and with great flavors and her striped bass entree was really flaky. My duck entree was good but def would get seafood next time. Desserts were good esp the comp coconut cake as we were celebrating our belated anniversary. The lemon dessert was too floral and tangy. great job Gramercy Tavern team!

One of my favorite restaurants in NYC! Every single dish tasted amazing. I came here with no expectations but had heard nothing but raving reviews from friends. Came here on a weekday and put my name down - wait was about ~2hours but they will text you so you can grab drinks elsewhere then come. They also have a private room for special events. 

They have a tavern and living room area. The living room area is pre fix I believe and reservations are booked out for months. I got seated in the tavern and it was still really charming! I love love the ambiance, service, and FOOD.

Okay now onto the best part- FOOD
Ordered the clam flatbread- AMAZING, seriously every single bite I was getting sad that it was disappearing. So crisp and flavorful but not like too salty or anything. Best app for sure!! The Radicchio & Grilled Bacon Salad, Apples and Red Eye Gravy was really fresh and delicious as well. You CANNOT go wrong with any dish honestly. Next time I would def try the cheese.

For my entree I got the meatballs. Juicy and great sauce. The sea bass is also REALLY GOOD. I would recommend trying the sea bass. It doesn't look as tasty but once you bite into it- OMG! I really did not think the food could get better after eating the apps but then the entrees blew my mind. 

The service is excellent- they also keep your water full and ask if you want any drinks. 

For dessert I got the Cookies & Cream Sundae, Chocolate Cookie Crumble and Sherry Sauce - BEST ICE CREAM IVE EVER HAD IN MY LIFE. SERIOUSLY! If they sold their own cookie and cream ice cream 10/10 I would buy. 

For drinks I recommend- JALISCO PEAR- pear alcohol drink- really tasty! 

The place is worth the $$$$. I'm coming back asap. Top 5 fav in NYC!

Ever since I was little, mom told me I was special. So when I got the surprise dessert from the chef on my anniversary dinner, I was elated...... but I now see the pics of others and the dessert is the chef's one-trick pony and I'm crushed! It feels sooooo good to be one among 1000s. Another diner left behind. First world problems.

Alright, jokes aside, this is my wife's favourite restaurant. We had our honeymoon dinner at the tavern the year of our marriage and my wife's made it a point to visit the tavern every year since. This is the second anniversary and GT never disappoints.

I just love being here. I see they have relaxed dress code a bit, which is kind of a sob story as it steals the fine dining experience. I saw a dude with a polo shirt. But other gentlemen had formal jackets so it saved the day.

As for the food, we get the same thing every year. Well, I changed up a little this time and I was pleased with the lamb pasta dish in the first course and I had pasta again for the main course.... some of their menu items comtain words which you need a foodie thesaurus a la Roget's and I had to google them with an arm under the table and that's okay. Because.... wife's orders - "don't ask the waiter and embarrass me".

They served biscuits and goat milk butter in between and it was so good that I made a beeline for whole foods when we returned home in Connecticut to recreate the goat butter experience at home.

They generally serve a palate cleanser in between courses and it was missing this time - wonder if it has any connection with the dress code relaxation. Either way, I hope dress code and palate cleansers come back in style.

The waiters were fantastic. Of course, I'm going to be knocking on the door next year.

I went in for lunch at the bar. I ordered a simple sandwich and salad. Everything was good and the service was attentive. The atmosphere was nice, if a bit stuffy. I could judge the place better if I went back for dinner.

Gramercy Tavern was my first choice for fine dining and it didn't disappoint! Every single entree we order was delicious along with wine of course! To top it off, the server was friendly and attentive. Delicious food and great service! Highly recommended!

Went on a recommendation from a friend.  First attempt , three hour wait!   Nope.  The next night we went earlier and were seated in 45 minutes.  Worth the wait?  Yes, we had a great meal. I had sea bass that was creative and flavorful, but not too spicy.  Perfect.  She had veggie stir fried rice.  Great chili pepper sauce, but don't expect miracles, it is fried rice after all.  Wait staff incredibly courteous.  Wine was overpriced, but overall meal was reasonable. I would certainly go again, provided the wait time is not  ridiculous.

My family had a wonderful, fantastic experience here at the Tavern last night as we celebrated my sister's (super early) birthday. It is incredibly spacious, with more casual space in the front and more dressy tables in the back. I highly recommend OpenTable or phone reservations to secure a spot. 

Courses were all delicious. The lamb dishes are worth every penny, and their fishes were cooked extremely well. The sauces were flavorful with a good consistency, and paired nicely with their respective dishes. 

The bread is ADDICTING. I swear I couldn't finish my meals because the bread was just so good and fresh out of the oven. Honestly, if I had a meal of their bread alone, I'd be okay with that, haha. Thanks to dad, my meals didn't go to waste as I let him finish my food. We ended the night with filling desserts, and my sister received an adorable coconut cake as well. 

Throughout the night, small details made a big difference with their service. It always remained friendly yet professional. When my sister asked where the restroom was located, a waiter said, "Follow me" and led her. When my mom was being THAT person taking photographs of every single square inch of their decorations, they were actually pretty cool about it, haha. Granted, their stuff really was cute, especially with holiday decorations.  I found the clientele were celebrating birthdays or holiday-related events, which was nice. 

I personally found the wine list a tad bit overpriced, even for a restaurant that builds their tip system into the pricing. That said, it was an impressive collection and I did notice many patrons ordering them. But no matter--their cocktails are on point. If you like prosecco and sweet drinks, get the Roger Fitz Spritz. If you like more aromatic and bitter drinks, get the European Union. If you like negronis and the like, get the Moneypenny. 

Two things:
1. Gratuity is built into their prices, including coat check. 
2. As of this time, the area is under construction, so their entrance is a bit hidden, but it's worth it. 

Verdict: Thank you, Gramercy Tavern, for making my sister's birthday a superb one! I will be back-- just not anytime soon so the charm and novelty isn't lost on me :)

All around one of the best meals I've experienced. The prix-fixe lunch menu, at $85 plus the wine pairing at$58 is definitely worth it, as "hospitality is included". There is no line to add a tip which would be "respectfully declined".

On to the food:
- Marinated Scallops with Riesling - excellent preparation, super fresh, even my wife who doesn't like raw food gobbled it down.
-  Arctic Char with Fumin Blanc. The BOMB! Incredibly subtle in taste and perfectly poached (?), for me it was the best course. I never imagined it tasting like this. The texture was heaven.
- Squid Ink Pasta with lobster and Chorizo, Nero d'Avola. Very hearty, satisfying savory dish. It has everything one could ask for.
- Duck Breast with Tempranillo - very good, I wished the skin was crispy but still it was an excellent dish, wine pairing was spot on.
- Frozen Chocolate Pudding with Porto - I'm not much of a dessert person but it certainly ended the feast well.

Service was very professional, the wine pairings were superb and the setting was very nice, lots of beautiful space, bathroom was clean and modern.

They went out of the way to accommodate my son, who is allergic to nuts by creating a dessert for him that was actually better than the rest of the table. 

No tip accepted at the coat check - all service is included. I like that, hopefully it means the staff is being paid a decent, living wage.

Chatted with one of the managers about the menu, when it changes and he stated they are flexible, the kitchen can make smaller portions of the a la carte entries to substitute for the standard tasting menu. He was very gracious.
 
We will be back.

Actually 3.5 stars.  Decor was lovely and service was courteous.  For the price, the food, although refined, was not especially memorable.  Seasoning was an issue as the scallop dish which was first on the tasting menu needed salt whereas the squid ink pasta w/ lobster was quite salty, (and had very little lobster).  Drinks were also very expensive.  The frozen pudding dessert was delish.  Can't say it was bad, but can't say it was all that great.

BURGER REVIEW ONLY

I knew I was gonna have a burger when I woke up that morning. Five Guys, Fast food or some pub burger, it was going to happen. I saw Gramercy on my bookmarks and I remembered reading about this off-menu burger.. 

THE DILEMMA
Every morning, Gramercy inspects their wagyu and decides to make a burger or a philly. Today, they did a philly.. A bit disappointed, I said ok; however, my feeble mind was clearly not expecting this avalanche of flavor

WAGYU PHILLY
My God. I looked, perplexed, at little strips of beef nestling an amusing cheese foam. This is going to let me down, I thought. Grabbed the tomato lettuce parts and did a Ford assembly line crafting this giant, sliced, took a bite. And screamed on the inside.

HOLD ME BACK..
I can't tell you HOW MUCH FLAVOR is in this. I could only taste it. The marbling and fat in the wagyu had such a real depth, umami, delicious, jaw-dropping, crazy good, someone give me a thesaurus, mind blowing FLAVOR. It was SO SATISFYING and I felt so content. A must for anyone who appreciates burgers ($26)

In my top 10 burgers, Cannot WAIT to go back and try the regular Wagyu. Gramercy Tavern is also known for amazing vegetable dishes and top-notch service! Defn a NYC Flatiron treasure!

Came here with some friends and got the 6 course tasting menu but not the wine pairing.  We had quite a late reservation for the 6 course and we were the last or 2nd to last table to leave the restaurant.  firstly, the cocktails here are really freaking good.  I'm not a huge drink snob or anything but its something that everyone should try.  The free bread was also something we kept asking for because its so good. 

On the 6 course menu, I enjoyed all the dishes except the 2nd dish with the crab.  I didn't think the presentation was very appealing nor was the dish anything special.  The lobster and steak courses were the best.  They also gave us 2 types of desserts and people were split on how much they liked it.

There is no tipping here but the service is really really good.

What an iconic Tavern! We did not eat here but had a drink at the bar to toast the holiday!! Very expensive. $20 for a martini, but no tipping needed. It's all included. One of those places you have to go to at least once!!!

My husband and I dined at Gramercy Tavern while on vacation at NYC. Our trip was booked around food and this was our first dinner in the city. It set the bar high!

Reservations are a must (30 days in advance) if you want to secure a seat for a multi-course meal in the dining room, and I promise it's worth it. I don't want to share too many of the food items so that you may also be surprised on your visit. And, because I am sure the tasting menu changes often. 

We were particularly impressed with the level of service and detail. Even though we did the tasting I LIVE for dessert and knew we needed to order a few things from the regular menu. best decision ever as our cookies and milk platter, chocolate cake  AND mini coconut cake...yes, we ate almost all of it. 

Our waitress was super friendly and never let our wine run low and our booth felt private in the otherwise crowded room. 

Will be back as we'd love to dine in the tavern area and have a few cocktails.

This review is for the tavern section of the restaurant (by the entrance). There's a casual but sophisticated vibe that's great for date nights. Shows that you're trying but not trying too hard ;) Pricing is also reasonable for the quality of food. 
Food is seasonal, so always fresh and excellet. Pick something interesting and give it a try! If you're craving a burger, they offer one of the best in they city. It's available year round but in limited qualities.
The place is always packed, so come early or be prepared to wait (no reservations).

I went Gramercy Tavern on New Year's Day evening at 5:30 with my son and Boyfriend with high expectations. I chose the 3-course menu, my son and BF chose the tasting menu. The maître d' induced us to get the truffle tortellini special., neglecting to advise us of the surcharge. After we decided on 2 orders of truffle tortellini, she advised us that there was $40 surcharge for each dish. She apologized for not mentioning earlier. VERY UNPROFESSIONAL!! And the truffle was not of high quality!
      Overall the food was decent, but not memorable. The dessert was a bit disappointing. As the room became crowed, the level of the service became inferior. Our maître d' lacked warmth and was somewhat robotic.
     My son loved the bread. I asked for 3 pieces(twice) to take home.... Sadly, there was only one piece in the bag!
     We've been to some of the fine dining restaurants in Manhattan, for example EMP, Le Bernardin. Jean-Georges... I must say Gramercy Tavern is not in their league.

This dining experience was probably one of the best I've ever had. Unfortunately, I wasn't able to order from the tasting menu, since my group decided they didn't want to partake, but the 3 course entrees still blew me away.

To start, I ordered the corn and crab salad. The crab was cooked perfectly and the corn was roasted to perfection. It had the perfect crunch and it was the perfect combination of flavors. Next, I ordered the sea bass with the red pepper sauce. The sauce was more of a soup-like consistency, but nevertheless, absolutely amazing. The shishito peppers as a garnish were the cherry on top. Lastly, I ended with the pavlova with mango sorbet. This was pretty good. I personally prefer a merengue that is crunchy on the outside, but a little softer on the inside, but this was a little hard all around, but the softness of the mango sorbet was able to balance out the textures. Overall, the dessert had great flavor components.

This was on my list for too long. I finally got to try it. 

There are two places you can dine at here: the tavern and the dining room. The tavern is smaller but you wont need a res to get a seat here. We waited about 20 minutes on a friday night :) You will need a res for the dining room and they were booked for the month when i called. The tavern and the dining room will have different menus. 

We got

Duck Liver Mousse, Pickled Vegetables and Grilled Bread 20-- I "mousse" say, this was delicious. This was a good start. So rich and creamy-- will make your mouth water. 

Duck Andouille, Caraflex Cabbage, Apples and Hot Sauce 29-- My tastebuds "apple-y" enjoyed this dish.  This dish was actually my favorite dish. It was soo good. GET THIS. 

Grilled Lamb, Green Garlic Butter and Market Greens 35-- Oh my "Lamb-ta!" this was amazing. You need to get this. So tender and flavored perfectly. 

Sea Bass, Smoked Potatoes, Fennel Gremolata and Shell Beans 30-- this was one of the "bass" ive ever had. So flakey. Perfectly cooked. 

This place is so good. You need to come here. You wont regret it. Everyone here is so nice too. I was getting a little chilly and they offered to bring me blankets and to see if they can turn up the heater.

i went here with a chef
i guess it was good haha
fancy place!
lovely food
Excellent birthday meal. Great service. Liked chatting with our sever Toni. We did the Tasting Menu which was fantastic. Great atmosphere.
Amazing Food! You can't got wrong with anything on the menu. The best thing is that they hangs the menu all the time.

Been here twice both to the tavern and the dinner hall. Nothing can go wrong in Gramercy Tavern. Excellent selection of non-alcoholic drinks, innovative food combinations and delightful blueberry pie with corn ice cream. 
This is the kind of perfection a NYC dinning experience can offer. Highly recommended.

Fine establishment.  High-end feel..but not pompous.  Prices are on the aggressive side, but gratuity is included.   The duck mousse was great.  The salad with bacon was decent..a little too much dressing.  The Wagyu cheesesteak was overcooked.  Very accommodating for GF clientele....amazing GF bread and crackers for pate'.  Nice scene too..

Really Great service. 
I expect high prices but still a bit high for the quality of the food. They were extremely helpful and even brought a complimentary appetizer. -1 star because either the prices should be just a littleee bit lower or the food should have just a littleee more flavor.

I've been dining out in New York City for something like 60 years, and Gramercy Tavern is in my top five alltime great places to eat (and drink wine) (others? the long gone Lutece, Le Bernardin, Peter Luger [Williamsburg] and Queen [downtown Brooklyn])...the service is terrific, every detail is extremely well thought out (Example: the steak knives are Laguiole) and the bar area is wonderfully welcoming if you're alone...do not miss!

Gramercy Tavern has "The Dining Room" section where making a reservation at least 3 weeks in advance is recommended if selecting a popular dining time. I have dined here multiple times for dinner, and easily this is one of my favorite restaurants in Manhattan. I bring my out-of-town guests + in-town friends/family here. Highly recommend their dinner tasting menu which changes seasonally. Creativity and taste are exceptional here. Consistently excellent. Terrific service. I did try the "The Tavern" section just once, which does not require reservation, but the dishes are not quite the same level as their dining room's -- hence, their term "The Tavern." Very highly recommend "The Dining Room."

We had dinner here last night (in the main dining room) after getting engaged and it was really perfect. The food was excellent and the service was above and beyond. Our server, Michael, was attentive, helpful and just plain nice. The whole place has a down-to-earth vibe which is a breath of fresh air compared to other fine dining restaurants. And the ambience is perfect -- not too stuffy but you can actually hear people speak. Highly recommended.

I finally made it to Gramercy Tavern.  It was my first stop for lunch when arriving in town.  I half expected it to be like a movie that you've heard so many good things about that there's no way it lives up to the expectations.  Gramercy Tavern exceeded my expectations.  The wait staff is everything I would expect after reading Danny Meyer's book years ago.  Our wait between courses was a bit long, but the payoff in flavor was worth it.  The Cheddar & Pilsner Soup, Parsnips and Apples was a great light starter.  Not at all heavy as I was expecting.  The Chicken Breast & Thigh, Parsnip, Tatsoi and Trumpet Mushrooms are outstanding.  Great diversity in this dish.   But...I have to say my favorite thing was the butter served with the angel bread.  40 percent goat cheese, 60 percent butter.  It's not often I'm impressed with the simple bread and butter they bring to your table with drinks.  All in all great experience in a great atmosphere.

Holiday weekend, Monday lunch. Looking for a casual, decently-priced, Michelin-starred restaurant where we don't need a reservation! Head to Gramercy Tavern!

Doors open at Noon, so the plan was to arrive a bit early in case there was a line. Arrived around 11:55am, and there's construction going on outside, so you enter from a side service door. The main entrance seems so much more pleasant and welcoming though. Open side entrance door and there's already a line of ~15 people waiting. However, the bar area is pretty large so we sat immediately at the bar. Bar area gets cozy and the girl next to me was right up on my side so I had to nudge her to give me some space. C'mon girl - go cozy up next to your friend, not me. The Tavern filled up pretty quickly for lunch but the tables/seats turnover fast too.

Foods: 
-Complimentary cheddar bread - tasty though I wish it was warmed.
-Duck liver mousse: Really good and a HUGE portion. This is enough to feed 4-6 people. We ate so much as we didn't want to waste it, and we still barely ate half the portion. The bartender is so attentive in that he noticed we'd almost eaten all of our toasted bread with half the mousse still there and he ordered additional bread for us without us even asking - excellent. The toasted bread is the bomb, btw. 
-Duck Andouille Sausage: Good sausage but I think I've had similar-tasting sausage recently and this one didn't stand out unfortunately. However, the accompanying pickled veggies and slaw are delicious and memorable. 
-Special Burger with bacon and fancy cheese: BFs order - it was good but too salty for me.

I got so full off the bread and appetizer that I barely ate my main course so they packed up all my leftovers, including the mousse, and I had a wonderful dinner later. The mousse tasted fantastic the second time around. 

Bill came out to ~$120 and tip is included, so no need for more math. Very reasonably priced, IMO, as we easily spent the same amount for a casual dinner the night before, and here I had leftovers. 

Overall, a lovely time at the Tavern of Gramercy Tavern. Not sure I'd come back right away, though I would easily recommend it to friends. The mousse was the bomb, and our main dishes were good, just not exceptional. The decor of the Tavern is beautiful. Service is excellent.

Mostly, I appreciate how accommodating everyone was - I asked our host if we could order from the Dining Hall menu which I learned they do not usually do, but he offered to ask the chef if it was possible, if there was something I wanted. It depends on whether they have enough food, it seems. Ultimately, I ended up ordering from the Tavern menu but I greatly appreciate the effort. Also, our bartender-server was so nice and attentive. He's super busy, but takes care of his guests. 

I chose the Tavern over the Dining Hall for lunch because we only had casual clothes but in seeing how the place is laid out and the lunch vibe, we would've been fine sitting in the Dining Hall too and prices are about the same. If you don't want to worry about getting a table or waiting, I'd get a lunch reservation for the Dining Hall.

Great food, very expensive.  Two of us for a birthday dinner and the bill was over $400.  Found similar food for a better price in NYC, but the fantastic atmosphere was worth the price. I had the Tartar and lamb trio which did not disappoint.  My wife had the striped bass, which was a bit uninspiring.  However she also had the Octopus which was the highlight of the  night.  Decent service for the price we paid.  Tip is included which was reflected in the rather robotic wait staff IMO.

Yet another home run for Danny Meyer. Gramercy Tavern definitely lives up to the hype. 

Behind an amazing three course menu (and a vegetarian tasting menu option, if you're into that) is a staff that is warm, welcoming and ready to please. Our server was cute, fun and high energy; she got really excited about summer when I ordered a Pimms Cup on a cold and rainy January night. She reminded me of Phoebe from Friends... except smarter! She was great. 

They brought us a small carrot, sunflower and sesame salad to welcome us. Honestly I would have been satisfied just eating a huge bowl of that for my meal. It was g.d. AMAZING. The wheat biscuits were also wonderfully light and airy. Could have eaten 20 of them. #carbs 

For dinner, I had:
Cheddar and Pilsner soup- light and brothy, not heavy and creamy, but still had a good cheddar flavor. Honestly so good. 

Flounder- this might seem weird but it was my first time trying flounder ever. Anyway, it definitely did not disappoint. It was served on top of some warm barley/farro/misc. warm grain salad and it was . Happy taste buds. 

Chocolate- tbh by the time dessert came I could barely eat anything else. I was so full. But like a true champion I powered through because that's what you do when a plate of deliciously moist chocolate cake is in front of you. 

The menu changes seasonally. I'm coming back in the summer to see what kind of magic they do with some fresh local produce.

Got the Brussels sprouts and meatballs. Both were great. Cocktails and bread were also really good. Gratuity is included in the price of the food. Despite not having tipping, which some would say removes an incentive for good service, the service was phenomenal.

Worth for what you paying $$$$ ! food , wine and dessert and plus great service from the front door when you walked into restaurant. I have tried both front room and back dining room. They both was great experiences. Service very professional and friendly

I love this place.  I've been coming here for years and have eaten both in the front part of the restaurant (walk in traffic, no ressies) and the back part of the restaurant (reservation only).  Excellent food, excellent service.... always.  They pay great attention to detail without being fussy.

Definitely one of the best places in New York for family and business dinners. The staff is polite, available, and ultimately wants you to enjoy your time there. It's an expensive restaurant, but it has become my little treasure in the labyrinth of NYC.

Came here during lunch for my mother's birthday. The service and food were both phenomenal. Love the fact that tip is included. We got a small almond cake for free due to the birthday celebration and it was super scrumptious. We also got two other desserts. Highly recommend the quince.

We  had lunch reservations for the dining room.  Had the tasting menu at $85 (tip included). We had a meeting at 3 pm and asked if the 5-course tasting menu could be done by 2 pm. The waitress assured us it could be, and we were out comfortably by 1:45 pm. My partner wore dark jeans with a collared shirt and nice dress shoes; we were let in and the wait staff didn't say anything about his outfit. 

The staff also called and pro-actively asked if it was a special occasion. They threw in an extra mini coconut cake which was appreciated and unexpected.

Overall, a great menu

First we started off with warm soft biscuits with goat cheese butter.  So yummy.
First course: scallops that were lemony and really woke your palate up
Second course: arctic char fish with cauliflower puree. I could eat just the cauliflower puree for dinner, who knew vegetables could be so delicious.
Third course: black squid pasta with chorizo and lobster. This was the only bad dish of the meal. The sauce had been over-reduced and so it was too salty.
Fourth course; duck breast with duck sausage. Came with a delicious crispy skin. Spectacular!
A sorbet as a cleanser with some nutella cream and crunch.  It was novel to have a sorbet with 'extras'
Fifth course: Profiterole with lemon sorbet

Overall, the lunch was relatively light and we didn't feel too stuffed afterwards which is always a worry with the tasting menus. You can always ask for more biscuits if you really want to fill up, but we didn't think that was necessary.

Service was great, and we liked that hospitality was already included.

I wish I lived in New York and could eat here everyday! It was amazing! Service was great, food was from first bite to last incredible! Super delicious ! Definitely recommend coming here and I will definitely be back :)

Sat in the bar room for early dinner and cocktails since we thought the prix fixe would be too much food. So beautiful and elegant. Everything was delicious and all the wines by the glass were outstanding. First class all the way.

My boyfriend & I came here for his birthday back in October. Overall, the food and waitstaff were excellent.

 However, I confirmed twice that we were celebrating his birthday and was disappointed when there was no special birthday dessert brought out for him despite it being brought out for others.  After writing a yelp review, Luciana from GT called me and was so sweet and apologetic and thanked me for my feedback.  I really appreciate the call and on top of that she sent us a gift card to come back for dessert. Thank you Luciana for the excellent customer service!

I've been to Gramercy Tavern twice now, once for my mother-in-law's birthday / parents-in-law anniversary celebration, as well as for a deal closing dinner.  This is an excellent, fancy and celebratory location to have events.  The food is just excellent.  However, I would have to admit, the restaurant has gotten a bit dated over the years.  From the first time I went, Gramery Tavern was the "it" expensive, fancy restaurant.  It's lost a bit of its cache over the years to newer restaurants.  This has nothing to do with the quality of food or the experience of dining at the restaurant, but just want to give a friendly heads up that it's hard to keep a restaurant exciting when so many newer and nicer places keep opening up.  If I were to organize a closing dinner nowadays, Gramercy Tavern would likely be lower on the list of places to consider.

I always appreciate their beautiful decor but it's their service that's top notch. One of my favorite places for a consistently excellent experience. I dined here with a friend in the restaurant industry for the tasting menu and loved it but also came on a separate more casual occasion early evening-around 5 and had a wonderful time at the bar with a few wines and small plates. All the food has always been great as long as you're prepared for the prices, prepare to enjoy wonderfully well orchestrated service. Get there early if you're trying to get a seat at the bar as it gets crowded quickly.

Gramercy Tavern received such wonderful reviews that I thought I had found the best restaurant to go to lunch on my birthday, but it was an awful experience.  The service was not as good as it should have been and the quality of the food was lacking from the bread to the main course.  We waited an uncomfortable amount of time after our salad for our main entree (it took over an hour).  We each ordered the striped bass, one was fine, but my fish was slimy and tasted so foul that it was inedible and I had to send it back. The experience was the worst I have had while dining out in New York, so I would suggest choosing another place.

There is a reason this place has its reputation. It was outstanding. 

Really wanted to sit at the bar, gave my name to the bartender due to a wait and took my glass of wine by the hostess. Internally, they have a convenient system that allows the bartenders to let the maître d' know when your seat is available. 

No matter where you are sitting, or what you are ordering the staff is exceptional. They cater to what you need; and anticipate everything. 

Food was impeccable. You must order the Apple Pie for 2! I could have eaten that myself! 

I returned shortly after my first visit to Gramercy Tavern to try the elusive burger. Arrived at 11:45 AM to secure 1 of the daily 30. With so many other wonderful things on the menu, the burger could not compare.

What else to say that has not been said already? this place rocks.  It is a staple for american fusion cuisine.  I try to come on weekdays when it's not so crowded, regardless service is on point on any day of the week.  Last time I had the calamari saffron rice with mussels and peppers, which just had the right spices and was quite perfect.  My friend had the red snapper with the sherry sauce, she mentioned it was delicious, alongside the crunchy fresh vegetables.  The complimentary bread and the mignardise, which come with the dark chocolate raspberry bowls were quite the delight of the night.  Water and drinks were always taken care of in a great timely matter. 
Will definitely come again.

Came to Gramercy Tavern during my first year as a NYC resident and it was totally worth the hype. From the interior decor and impeccable service to the perfectly portioned plates of the most fresh and seasonal ingredients, there's probably no other lunch that I can have in my life that will ever compare. I got the seared salmon over a bed of legumes, and my husband got what he quotes is still "the best burger I've ever had." Really simple sounding dishes, but with serious flavor power and skillful plate settings.
Always a pleasure to unwind  and relax at the tavern. Great service always with a smile. Never a bad moment!

I had a birthday lunch at Gramercy Tavern. The whole experience was amazing. The waiting service was great and the foods were all excellent. I highly recommend the lunch prefix.
Ambiance for the restaurant was beautiful and calm. The noise level was perfect for a business dining and for a romantic dates.

About 1hr 45min wait at the tavern during prime time on a Wednesday night. Easily manageable and exactly as quoted!

The service was fantastic. The bar area was crowded and the waitress made sure our table was comfortable. Super easy going and fun to dine with.

The food was solid. Some very memorable dishes but nothing wowed me as new and different. Price point was reasonable for the experience. The oyster were some of the best of my life! The chef came out to discuss them and gave some impactful advice on how to shoot them - straight up with a drop lemon! Clean refreshing bright briny flavor - similar to some ultra fresh SB uni!

The tavern was a great choice for an accessible meal. Amazing service wth great food (just not quite magical).
Words cannot describe the incredible experience while dining at Gramercy.  Incredible service, incredible and exciting food and incredible atmosphere.

i havent eaten here in 20 years. the last meal was fabulous and ahead of the curve in those days .new digs and hefty $$$$ does not make up for preciously silly presented food. $125 for 3 courses should have been beyond wow. lamb was tender but carved from a large mouse sized body.pork loin served alongside a token piece of" bacon"seemed traif.
how can one mess up cookies and milk?by using the same  bland dough and adding different toppings. sorbets of quince pear and blood orange was refreshing.
the best thing was the fresh warm yeasty rolls but spoiled by (wha?...)goat cheese mixed with butter). i asked for plain butter which came graciously.
service was sweet and accommodating .
the bar seemed liked the real scene. different menu and people really were having a good time

My favorite place for lunch and a boozy afternoon in The City. 

Pro-move sit at the bar. The service is always insane. 

I've been there a ton and have always had great experiences. Great food and great service in the dining room, tavern and at the bar. But there's something special at the bar. Super attentive. Drinks as soon as your done - before you have to ask. The bar and bartenders rock!

My wife and I have ordered many of the entree's prefix courses and individually. My wife loves the food that has too many steps / unique ingredients to make at home. 

I love the hamburger. Period. Explanation point. It's often a special at the bar. If they have it GET IT!

I can't recommend this place enough!!!

Disappointing. The restaurant has a nice ambiance and great service staff. But the food is really bland and not really creative. 

I had the buratta citrus salad which was ok. And the Arctic char ceviche. The flavors of the ceviche were off and it lacked proper seasoning. 

For dinner, I ordered the Brussels sprouts fried rice. It was plain. No real flavor to it at all and nothing that brought the dish together. It was just the sprouts and rice with some fingerling potatoes which really didn't seem to fit well with the dish. 

It was nothing special and rather disappointing. 

Finally, for desert, I had the deep dish apple pie. Took a few bites but had to send it back as the apples were mushy, the crust was dry and excessive, and - you guessed it - no real seasoning or flavor. Think apple sauce on dry wheat toast. 

Not worth the price of entry. Will definitely not be coming back to gramercy tavern.
Gramercy Tavern is a favorite and I've dined there at least a dozen times over the years.  It's classy but not stuffy, the menu and service are always impressive.  It won't let you down.
So glad I got to spend my last night in New York having dinner here. Amazing place, my favorite restaurant around. I will miss it! I wouldn't have traded it for the world

Worth the wait and every penny. Exceptional service, amazing food, no detail spared. Everything they say about just showing up without a reservation is true. They really do hold tables for walk-ins, and you might have to wait a bit, but they make it so pleasant with lovely and imaginative cocktails and the gorgeous decor that you don't mind at all. We walked in on a Saturday night, gave our name for the dining room, and then got a drink and gave our name for seats at the bar. Within 30 minutes we were cozily seated at the bar with our second cocktail in hand and our savvy bartender's advice on which appetizers to share. The arctic char tartare was light with citrus and fennel, and the chicken liver pate was creamy and flavorful. Sea bass and lamb entrees were perfect and the staff's wine suggestions were on point. We were actually too full for dessert, and while we were made to feel welcome to linger until we were ready to try one of the many creations we had seen delivered to other patrons, we had a show to get to. Seems like a good reason to go back...

Had chefs tasting. Service was close to perfect. Food was amazing. Atmosphere was a bit more stuffy in the back dining area than in the bar area/outside area. I prefer the outside/bar area unless I were on a date.
