Went to Gramercy Tavern with friends and sat at the bar.  We heard such great things and I have to say everything we were told was true!  Delicious burger, great drinks and stellar service!  I will definitely be back!

I've had this restaurant on my list to go to for a long time. Finally, the opportunity came when I was trying to find a place for a family member's birthday. We made reservations for a weekday dinner. We were seated at a corner, round table, away from the bar. It was cozy and more intimate, but we could still have fun people watching the after-work patrons at the bar. 

We ordered:
1) Fluke (appetizer)
2) egg & pea flatbread (appetizer)
3) sea bass (entrée)
4) jerk chicken (entrée)
5) lamb (entrée)
6) sorbet (dessert)

Everyone really enjoyed their entrees - not one dish was bad! They staff was friendly and attentive - our water glasses were always full and we could always find someone when we needed another round of drinks.
Yes this as good as it gets. It never disappoints!  We always love their seasonal menu, but this one topped itself!  Great wine pairing and the service is always sublime.

It was simply perfect. Our waiter, Greg, was excellent. He was eloquent and very polite and attentive. Our food was delicious. When they realized that my guest and I were simplifying an appetizer, they brought it in two separate plates. Because I couldn't finish my cocktail, they didn't even include it in the check. I got the lamb for entree and it was very yummy. The desserts were spectacular. I cannot wait to go again!

I've been here a few times but never wrote a review.  Decided to dine here a few weeks ago with some friends and had the best time. Had the tasting menu, which I get every time. I had the octopus and the pork loin, which was delicious.  Love that it is no tipping restaurant and the service is outstanding.  A top of the line NY favorite for me.

Went there for my birthday. We sat in the dinning room and I must say it was one of the better experiences I have had. The food was impeccable but beyond the food the service was some of the best I've ever had. Too bad you can't tip. Would go again

Love the atmosphere in the tavern. Few places so effortlessly strike a balance between casual and fine dining. The service was exemplary and the food was both creative and well executed. New favorite!

No reservations, no problem!

One of the best Restaurants in NYC. 

Service: The Hostess kept my group updated with the waiting times and made sure to seat us as soon as possible. The place was crowded as any other night and we were able to get a table with no reservations in 20 minutes.

I ordered the Quiona Salad, followed by Smoked Artic Char, and finished with peach sorbet to try a multitude of flavors. One word... Savory!

I am not sure how often the menu changes, it maybe seasonal or annually.

This place is good. 

My relative always comes from Boston and we always go to these fancy spots. I was a bit underdressed in shorts and a polo, compared to the suits that were there for the after work crowd. 

The atmosphere and staff etc.. was expectedly good. The food was good, but maybe it was what I ordered. I had this cheese infused kielbasa. But I'm not sure what all the fuss is about this place. I suppose I would go back sometime, in the event of a special date or occasion. 

Funny thing was I had never heard of this place, so when she suggested it, I'm thinking "great a tavern that sounds perfect, I'll get some beers and some bar food type thing", only to find out its like a really posh place, so I was ironically a little disappointed.

Disappointing and rather limited menu for a Sunday brunch.  We could only choose either the tasting menu or the a la carte - no mixing!   We weren't offered off menu options - would have loved the burger.  My leak and potato soup with horse radish and smoked trout roe was quite bland - couldn't taste the roe at all.  Lamb loin was tender but seem to taste of bacon sprinkles - non of the deserts appealed.  Recommended wine was very nice but had sold out when I wanted a second glass!   My son-in-law's starter of crab and lobster spaghetti was the best dish  of our party's choices.  Service excellent!  Won't rush back for the food.   Rosheen T.
I came here for the dinner with friends I really like this place our sever was very friendly and the food was good i really want to recommend this place.

Heard great things about this restaurant, and loved it! Went here on a Monday night without a reservation and got a table in the tavern without a wait. The service was excellent, and the ambience cozy. We started with the stuffed clams (a special that night) and strozzapreti with pastrami both of which were delicious and not too filling. I got the sea bass with potatoes, which was really good and had leftovers for the next day. Will definitely return and save room for dessert next time.

Big fan! The bread with the goat cheese butter was incredible. We also loved the octopus dish.

Tried the black bass as my main course & loved it. The puree that came with the fish was incredible.

We had the matcha cheesecake for dessert and it was definitely interesting. The consistency took some getting used to but we enjoyed it. The cookie plate was also great-- definitely worth it for the snickerdoodle alone.

Will definitely be back!

Possibly my favorite place in the city. It can be both CASUAL or FORMAL depending on how you feel like that day.
So this place has two restaurants: 

The Tavern: (walk in only)
Casual, a great place to bring your date to. They have great selections of wine and beer, most of them are available in half glass, so you can really taste a lot of different kinds of drinks without breaking your bank. They have some great burger that is not on the menu, and I especially like the apple tart dessert

The Dining Room: (Michelin one star)
I've tried their dinner tasting menu. Just WOW! I am not sure if it's the wine (we ordered 4 bottles for the 6 of us), but everything tasted amazing. I have been to almost half of the Michelin one star restaurants in NYC and I will put Gramercy Tavern as #1. The service was amazing and the staffs are knowledgeable about the dishes. I will definitely come back again when the new tasting menu is up!

Tips:
+ the Tavern has some amazing desserts, good for people who just want to have an afternoon tea
+ order half glasses (they are generous on their pour), try different things
+ they have roasted oysters at the Tavern, amazing!

What a beautiful restaurant!!!

One of the most beautiful restaurant I have ever been to! 

The best of the best is their dinning room! So warm and friendly! 

I love good food, having been coming with my son to this restaurant for few times, so I can say this is my to go restaurant ! Great job! 

But, food is getting a little saltier after Michael Anthony left the team. Maybe is just me? Anyway, awesome ingredient does not need much salt. Hope those young chef would see that

After all, great place for the price!
Came here for Valentines Day,  everything was delicious until the bad oyster... spent the night praying to the toilet.  Wouldn't come back... bad conditioning.

I don't usually write reviews but Gramercy deserved one! For those debating between the pre fix or tasting menu, splurge and do the tasting; it was AMAZING. For a tasting menu I thought the portions were sized perfectly and we were stuffed by the end. The restaurant is so cozy, get there early and have a drink at the bar before you sit down. Truly a great NYC restaurant!

I dined at the Tavern (as opposed to the Dining Room) in February 2016. Went on a federal holiday around 5 pm without a reservation and there was no wait. The service is excellent. My first time I had a duck liver mousse (awesome) and arctic char fried rice (amazing!). Would definitely go back.

2nd time here. I don't live in NY but if I did I would be a regular here. 

Got the prix fixe menu with the wine pairing, which I'd recommend. Everything was very good. Service was also stellar. The entire ambiance of the restaurant from the time you enter until the time you leave is very enjoyable. 

The one small negative was that the meal didn't make me full-- but I have a big appetite and in some ways that's probably a good thing. If I had to do it again I might supplement with an additional appetizer or 2. 

Note that they build the tip/service charge into the check. The coat check girl wouldn't even take my tip. Not sure what percentage the automatic service charge was. In retrospect, making that clearer could be helpful, but I may have missed.

This review is long overdue. I REALLY wanted to like Gramercy Tavern but unfortunately was very disappointed. My fiance and I came here for a special night out and were really excited to try it due to rave reviews from friends and the Michelin star. 

Since it was a special occasion we decided to do the wine pairing and the tasting menu. First I'll start with the food. The tasting menu had about 8 courses of small plates. Unfortunately none were particularly memorable. Maybe it was just a bad night, but the dishes lacked flavor and the "wow" factor I was expecting. I specifically didn't like the beef, which you would expect to be full of flavor but instead was just fatty and nothing special. The absolute worst part of the meal was the wine pairing. For $90 per person, they brought you a small glass of wine with each course. I have to say the wine choices were pretty awful and we didn't end up drinking half of it. For $180 we could have clearly gotten a great bottle of wine that we would have enjoyed much more. We probably should have known this and opted to get a bottle of wine instead of doing the pairing as we don't really like port wine, so I definitely take some of the blame. 

Overall, for the price we paid, this was really disappointing. Maybe we just had bad luck but we definitely won't be back to the main dining room but will maybe check out the Tavern at some point.

Booked a private room here for a corporate dinner and aside from the food, the service was exceptional. Never thought I'd like the taste of beets, but the chef really out did himself. Got this girl to eat her vegetables without the desire to shove it to the side of her plate. Also, giving five stars because the chef's skin was flawless like a baby's butt and the wine expert's eyebrows were on fleek.

This place is WAY over-rated people! Don't get me wrong the food is decent but for being a 1 star Michelin you would expect he waiter to more about that they are serving and food to be outstanding.

Beeing from Italy I can tell you that the dishes they serve paste and duck are not worthy of the price. There is better food out there for the price.

Ambience was excellent.

Amazing food and atmosphere. 
The meatballs dinner was like no other meatballs that I've ever had. We ate at the bar. It was a great dining experience.

We experienced the tasting menu with a few friends and it was really a wonderful meal. Didn't love the rock shrimp serving. Very meh on that one but everything else was delicious. The service was wonderful as well. Our server was knowledgeable about the ingredients and how each dish was prepared.
We stopped in here for dinner after a show while visiting New York. Our water answered any questions we had and made recommendations . The food was very good as well.

Our first time in NYC.  I wanted to treat my wife and Gramercy did not disappointed. We both had the seasonal menu and it was 5 courses.  Needless to say we cleaned our plates. Be warned, they serve it on big plates but small bite offerings.  The experience from entry to leaving was top notch.  We don't do this often but this was an opportunity we couldn't miss.  Thank you Gramercy Tavern for a beautiful dinner and  unforgettable trip.

So first thing is first, my boyfriend was running late, as usual, and they graciously held our table for about 30 minutes past our reservation time, which is really not a thing many restaurants would do. I am a vegetarian, which we made known when we made the reservation and they were very accommodating. Beware, the vegetable tasting menu is NOT vegetarian, which is strange because what nonvegetarian would willingly order only vegetables? 

To me the dishes really were not memorable, and honestly I don't even remember what I had. Backtracking onto service: It took probably 5 minutes to get menus, and if you're paying up for a meal, I would expect to get the menus sooner than that. The service was a little spotty all together, and at some points it was hard to even find our waiter, who I will add was friendly. At one point, when one of the people was bringing food to our table he even forgot what it was and had to go to the kitchen and ask. Again, this is not the type of service I expect when you're paying for a high-end meal but I wouldn't care if it were some casual place.

I always see people complaining about wine pairings so I was wondering when people will realize it's a total rip off?! It's much better to just get a bottle. My boyfriend and I wanted to get a bottle and we asked the waiter, and usually at this point they would send the sommelier over, but that never happened. Maybe they don't have one? Seems a little odd. We ended up going with the Wind Gap Syrah, which was not fantastic but way better than the Pinot Noir on their BTG list. 

I really wasn't a fan of the dessert because I found it all to be too sweet, but we ordered a cheese plate and it was deeeelicious! I'd actually say it was the best part of the meal, and they didn't even make the cheese! 

All in all it's not a super romantic restaurant based on the sheer size. I would probably return one day to try it out again, but it's definitely not on the top of my list.
As fabulous as everyone says. Perfectly seasoned, fresh, inventive food with spot on portions and excellent, caring service. Would go every night if I could!

Executive Chef Michael Anthony's passion for good food and service were on full display this evening.  The oysters were the best we've had in years and the service was outstanding.  We are in town to celebrate daughter's 21st birthday and choosing this restaurant has been the hit of our celebration.  The attention to flavor, presentation, and preparation far exceeded our expectations.  Finally a dining experience worth remembering!!!

This place lives up to the hype!!!

On Saturday around 2:30pm the four of us were lucky enough to snag a table at the tavern (which only accepts walk ins and is more casual than the formal dining room in the back).

Like all Danny Myer restaurants, service is a key component to dining and you don't tip since hospitality is included in the price.

To start.
---Clam flatbread, celery root & salsa verde ($24)
Shared between the 4 of us this was by far everyone's favorite dish. 6 small slices were plenty to start the meal. The flatbread was super thin with a thick, decadent and creamy sauce. The clams were a nice touch, not fishy or overpowering at all.

Entrees 
---Tavern Burger (I believe $30)
This is actually not on the menu, is exclusively served at the tavern at lunch and if you look around it's a very popular dish. The burger comes with a thick layer of cheese which I believe is cheddar/gruyere mix and on the side: aioli, onion, lettuce and finely slices spicy pepper.

---Brussels sprouts fried rice, Poached farm egg and sunchockes -$29
Was able to try a bite of this as well and it was certainly interesting, a medley of flavors and very complex.

We were ogling at the desserts around us (cookie plate & beignets) but just couldn't think of eating more. 

Well done Gramercy Tavern. Well done!!!
Wow, what an amazing experience. The meal was perfect. One of the best restaurants in nyc for sure! Service was so engaging and tasting menu was so balanced and flavorful.
Had a reservation but we still had to wait 10 minutes. We didn't mind as we were quickly seated at the bar - with prosecco on the house. Food and service were excellent.

Worth the wait. Had the kale salad and the sea bass at the Tavern - both dishes were amazing for the price. Complimentary cheddar bread was also really good. 

The service was friendly and I appreciate that gratuity is included in the pricing. Overall a great dining experience.

The food was delicious.  Tasting menu was filled with exciting twists.  Loved the beets with curry and pine nuts.  Duck was the favorite all around.  Gluten allergy was easily accommodated by them.  Even provided the most amazing sweet potato, curry, toasted pumpkin seed GF bread for me.  Halibut was so tender.  I found the earthy dessert with the cheese, lemon sorbet and custard like icing to be very creative combination of flavors.  Had a 15 mo old with us and they were very patient and whipped her up a special pasta dish.

Start to finish - from the greeting at the door to our goodbye to our waiter the night was perfect.  Food was spot on, cocktails superb and wine recommendations hit the mark.  Sort of fell into this spot on our weekend visit to NY but will be singing the praises of the Gramercy Tavern to all of our friends.
Best cheeseburger and roasted oysters we've ever had. Ate at the bar during busy lunch. Bar staff super attentive.

Maybe the most relaxed "fine dining" ever.

As soon as I walked in, the warm & easy vibe was immediate & engulfing.  The bar was particularly inviting; it was almost too bad my table was ready early.  

The prix fixe menu has a few options in each course so that there's little chance of not finding something that appeals to you.  

From the amuse bouche to the complimentary chocolates at the end of the meal, this dinner was delicious & impressive.  The house rolls were hard to resist.  The crab spaghetti was surprisingly unique & light.  Both the black bass & the flounder were artfully prepared, but the flounder was the star.  Moist, flaky, tender, silky...this fish practically melted in my mouth.  Exquisite. 

And then, GT surprisingly succeeded in topping off a perfect meal, w an unforgettable dessert.

Matcha "cheesecake."

They use the term "cheesecake" loosely here.  Just as the waiter explained beforehand, it is more like a mousse.  The lightest, silkiest, & creamiest mousse you've ever had in your life!  The first spoonful stopped my thoughts.  It's a showstopper...visually & gastronomically.

This is one of the best desserts I have ever had.  A highlight of my NYC trip.

I understand why everyone loves it here.

A perfect meal.

5 stars.

There wasn't a meal at Gramercy Tavern which didn't knock it out of the park completely and severely. I'm talking to you especially, lamb loin. 

If the food wasn't so good though, they'd've gotten four stars for the acoustics. The place is loud and the Dining Room has acoustics which seem to fill the room a few times over. More than a fine dining restaurant calling itself a tavern ought.

 This means that among four people at a table everyone can hear each other; but with the table of 6, there have to be two or three conversations going for everyone to be involved. Again, though, the food was amazing and if I had the opportunity I'd've exhaust that menu's options.

Unimpeachable service as well. Who knew a living wage made people nice & friendly.

Gramercy is the penultimate NYC restaurant. Always an awesome experience. The tasting menus and wine pairings near perfection. The atmosphere couldn't be more cordial, elegant and comfortable, in a subdued and relaxed environment. The service is impeccable, knowledgeable, pristine, thoughtful and anticipatory. Always a favorite for a good meal on the town or when guests visit the city. Come back to try the various rooms.

The atmosphere is phenomenal. The sweet potato lasagna is delicious and savory, especially with a glass of red wine. I tried a new cabernet from Washington (Gramercy something). If you are looking for dessert, that coconut cream pie and a cup of coffee is the way to go.

Came here for dinner.  We had to wait 15 minutes even with a reservation.   The dining area is beautifully decorated.  

The menu is simple, for dinner, it has a 3-course menu for about $125.  The dishes change seasonally.  

We had the beef carpaccio and squid ink campanelle (squid ink pasta) as the first course.  The squid ink pasta was very tasty, it had bits of lobster, chorizo mixed in the sauce.  The beef carpaccio went well with the garnishes - peach and arugula leaves.  The appetizers were the best part of the meal. 

For entree, we both ordered the duck breast with sausage, the portion size was very small and honestly, the sausage didn't go well with the duck breast.  The combination was very strange.  The duck tasted okay but the meat was not tender.  I had better duck elsewhere. 

One thing to note, their rolls are very good. They are flaky and buttery, I believe they are called Angel biscuits/rolls. 

For desserts, we had the raspberry and chocolate desserts.  The raspberry dessert is a coconut milk cake, topped with apricot sorbet and raspberry.  The chocolate dessert has milk crisps, lavender and hazelnut brittles.  The ingredients, etc. are listed on the menu which would help the selection process.  

For special occasions, they would present your table with a small cake on the house.  There was a couple sitting next to us, celebrating their wedding anniversary.  They were given glasses of champagne and a cake.  Great personal touches there.  

At the conclusion of your visit, your server would give you some goodies from their bakery to take home, we were given 2 homemade granola bars.  

Overall, I think the food at Gramercy Tavern is average.  Their menu also seems to carry very basic American dishes.  The taste of the food is not very tantalizing.   Their dining room is also very loud.  The restaurant does seem to be very popular as customers kept coming in during my visit.  However, I believe you can get better quality food in NYC with that price.

This is an incredibly beautiful restaurant.  Layer on exceptional food, drink and service and it becomes an absolute must when in NYC.  While all the food was great (with the exception of dessert which I found lacking - an apple funnel cake concoction), the lobster spaghetti was my favourite.

Amazing! 

Definitely lives up to the reviews. The staff was attentive to detail. Extremely courteous.

Although rated in yelp with $$$$. Keep in mind that everything is included in the price (including tax, tip, coat check). So although the standard menu is $125 and the tasting menu is $165. It's all encompassing! Somewhat reasonable for a business casual sit down restaurant. 

All-in-all my significant other and I spent 2.5hrs of un-rushed, top notch service at this establishment. 

Gramercy Tavern sets the standard high to fine dining.

My girlfriend and I celebrated our anniversary here yesterday evening, and we're glad we did! The food was amazing and the service was impeccable -- our waiters and waitresses really did a fantastic job making us feel comfortable. I must've had my glass refilled, like, eight times throughout the evening, and only once did my glass fall below the 25% mark. Exceptional service!

We each had the dinner tasting menu ($165 per person before tax). I'm not going to go into detail for each course because that would make this review the length of a term paper, but I will say that the chefs made phenomenal meals with ingredients which I normally wouldn't eat. The marinated scallops with blood orange, fennel, and pumpkin seeds, for example, was surprisingly delicious -- I usually don't like pumpkin and would never eat the seeds, but I really enjoyed it! I also very much liked the squash tortellini with bone marrow (super rich!), and the wagyu beef was just a grand slam.

Literally everything about the evening was perfect, from the ambiance to the decoration to the service to the food. I didn't feel at all rushed over the course of 2.5 hours, and we both left with full stomachs! (I note this because I'm always a tad nervous having tasting menus for dinner -- the portions are pretty small per meal, but we certainly left satisfied!) The experience was absolutely phenomenal, and I can't wait to eat at more Michelin-rated restaurants!

Really nice place. Profesional stuff. 
I like this place and i recomend a lot to come here.

Drinks great but what a shit show trying to get a seat. Food can't possibly be worth the wait and they tease you at the bar. We were three and waited an hour and then they said "oh we have two". We needed three. Probably more hype than quality anyway. 

As an update to this review. The manager reached out to me to find out what happened and was very gracious in following up. I appreciate the extra step he took to try and make it right.

Yeah, so this happened! Happy 21st Birthday to me! The wife treated me here for my birthday and this was bucket list worthy. Our waiter was just kind of OK and a bit awkward, I'd say he was new. The other server we had was outstanding. It is 4.5 stars for that all the way.

I am still speechless. Absolutely speechless. This was one of the best meals that I have ever had in my life. Gramercy Tavern is one of the top restaurants in NYC and completely lives up to the hype that surrounds it.

Everything we tried on the menu was delicious. It was a home run. I highly recommend trying the tasting menu so you get a sense of what the chef is made of but visiting GT bar-side is still worth it. Overall, the cocktails may not be the most creative but they are made with quality alcohol that make them worth ordering.

For me, the highlight was dessert. That chocolate pudding was easily the best dessert I've had in my life this far. It's a must if it's an option and you're visiting GT.

The price tag may be high but I've found that GT is able to deliver on if you should pay for it. If you're in NYC, living or visiting, you need to try it at least once.

Walked in for an anniversary lunch on a Saturday around 1:30 pm.  We were surprised to learn there were seats available in the main dining room, but decided to sit in the bar room anyway in order to order a la carte.  It was pretty full but there were a couple of empty tables.  Very good lighting (little spot on each table creates intimacy), nice non-hipster, mostly over-40 crowd, a couple of babies/small children in evidence, good noise level, and nice table design -- an oval where you sit on the long sides facing each other, so you are close enough to talk and touch, but there is space on the table for everything.

Solid but not necessarily great service.  I love the fact there is no tipping, and I think it changes the relationship with the waiter -- I found our waiter a little reserved, even remote, though the table service was well-timed and beautifully executed.  Anyway, no complaints: I'd much rather have a reserved waiter than a fawning one.

Food was the highlight.  We started with oysters (can't remember the type, they were GREAT, though, sweet and complex), then the duck liver pate and the arctic char tartare, which were both excellent -- the tartare particularly good, paired with apple and daikon (we thought), hardly any salt, a super clear taste.  After that, we had the monkfish (served with lobster, ha ha), and the pork belly fried rice.  The monkfish and lobster dish (with hen-of-the-woods mushrooms and strong fennel notes in the puree/sauce, plus fresh terragon leaves) was especially awesome, mainly because the monkfish itself was cooked so so well -- an amazingly meaty texture.  The sauce had a kind of smoky barbecue layer to it that was a bit too strong and a bit too salty, IMHO, but otherwise this food was all superb.  Bit too much salt in the pork belly also.  I don't have a lot of recent high-end dining under my belt but the dishes struck me as innovative, and also generously proportioned.

We were totally full at this point so just shared the ice cream dessert, which was shockingly good and served in an appropriately small portion (since we were full, otherwise I might have been a bit annoyed): coconut, coffee+cardamom, and sour cream, each of them excellent.  The texture of the coconut ice cream is especially great.

I would come back here again and again... hope to afford it!

If you are looking to celebrate a special occasion in NYC, look no further!  

Came here on a special occasion the other day and Gramercy Tavern did not disappoint! :)

Upon being seated, we were greeted with glasses of champagne, which was a very nice touch.  As for the dinner menu, Gramercy Tavern's offers a few options for dinner: (1) a seasonal tasting menu, (2) a vegetarian tasting menu and (3) a three-course pre-fix.  We opted for the seasonal dinner tasting menu.

Seasonal Dinner Tasting Menu (Spring '17):
** Marinated Sea Scallops
** Lobster Salad
** Hake
** Squash Tortellini
** Duck Breast & Sausage
** Strawberries & Cream

The tasting menu was absolutely delicious.  The textures, presentation of the dishes and flavors were stellar.  I would have never imagined pairing sea scallops with pumpkin seeds, but it worked!  My only one gripe is that the timing of service from course to course could be a bit more consistent.  Other than that, service was superb--our wine and water glasses were continually refilled throughout the night.  Waiters were friendly and made us feel relaxed and comfortable with our dining experience.

Towards the end of dinner, we were also surprised with a mini coconut cake and homemade granola bars.  These small touches made the entire experience a fantastic one to remember!

P.S. The Angel Biscuits with the goat cheese butter that they serve are BOMB.  Warm, light, buttery, and dreamy...

The first time we dined at Gramercy Tavern, I ordered a bottle of some slightly obscure Poniatowski Vouvray, and our singularly lovely server looked at me earnestly and replied, "What an intelligent choice!"  (This left my wife muttering, "oh, brother..." quietly under her breath, her tacit acknowledgment that flattery will get you far with me.)  I was hooked (and she quickly followed).  There is a peculiarity to the Union Square Hospitality Group's welcome, and that is that they perceptively size you up very quickly, and then do whatever it takes to make you leave on cloud nine.  I am either vain (as in, my wine choice _was_ so intelligent, another eye roll from my beloved), or just easily susceptible to their considerable charms, or they just really are that good at what they do.

I'm going to vote for the last one (though, let's be honest, definitely two of the three are true).  We've been to the restaurant a few times over the years, most recently, this past fall, and we're never less than completely delighted by the experience. You enter a pretty vestibule, make a quick left, and there before you is a mammoth floral arrangement, a whimsically charming tavern, anchored by Robert Kushner's iconic Cornucopia mural.  You will immediately notice the buttery smell of woodsmoke from their grill, and you will be greeted with great and sincere cheer.  

There will be excellent seasonal cocktails, delicious ales on tap, or a fantastic assembly of wine by the glass.  If you're dining in the tavern, the menu will be à la carte, full of Michael Anthony's excellent farm-to-table fare.  The provenance of their wares will be acknowledged, and that's good to know, but what will strike you, even more, is the power and subtlety of the food.  In a dining world full of bells and whistles and the latest in modernistic cuisine, it's all the more refreshing to dine on food that is cognizant of all of the innovations, but, nevertheless, remains cheerfully accessible and somewhat analog.  This is not a backhanded compliment:  there are restaurants where you can geek out on all that stuff.  What I love is that, at Gramercy, the experience will be no less engaging to the senses, no less creative, but, rather, instantly comfortable, akin to the excellent service.  The last time we visited, it was an early Sunday supper in the tavern.  We had a lamb flatbread with green tomatoes that was impossibly savory.  Grilled vegetables prepared simply, but also lavished with care (with some amazing accompanying sauces).  A late summer salad of roasted beets with berries (including fraises des bois, three times as intense as the average strawberry) and bleu cheese, was so nuanced, but also exploding with flavor.  A salad of tomatoes and nectarines at their peak was an inspired combination of flavors.  Cavatelli with eggplant and summer squash were little bombs of happiness, particularly when shrouded with lashings of pecorino.  

Then, Miro Uskokovic's wild blueberry pie for two with corn ice cream.  Good Lord.  Pure happiness in pastry form.  I think that's the point of Gramercy Tavern:  in addition to the occasional (and welcome and necessary) didacticism of Michael Anthony's advocacy, what has always struck me is how genuine and sincere everyone we've been in contact with there has been about making us happy, through kind interactions, through polished and unimpeachably professional service, and through flawlessly-executed food that clearly comes from the heart.  Incredible and very rare.

Great food, atmosphere and service.  

I was alone in New York on business and lucky enough to get a walk in seat at the bar.  

For starters, I had some great oysters from Massachusetts.  That was followed by a delicious lamb dish and I finished with 3 hard cheeses.  

Along the way, a glass of Macallan 12 and some nice wine rounded off a wonderful evening.  

Do yourself a favour: go and enjoy it.

Just another happy customer. My sister and I ate here about two weeks ago. The wait staff were friendly, happy to be there (even at the end of their shift), and accommodating. Every time I left my seat, my napkin was folded upon my return. The bread was a delicious cheesy focaccia. We had the burrata, the kale salad and the ceviche. The kale salad features cauliflower two ways, one of which I initially thought was cheese. Very tasty. Burrata and ceviche were not earth-shattering but were tasty. The seabass dish was manna from heaven. It was so good that I literally do not even remember what my sister had as a main course because I was on an unparalleled personal flavor journey. Dessert was the perfect size for people who want to treat themselves without gorging. Would return in a heartbeat.

Aside from the food that I ate here, which was excellent, our service was impeccable.  The staff was friendly, efficient, and accommodating.  It was probably one of the best service experiences I have ever received while dining out in New York City.  It was one of my friend's birthdays, and our server brought out a personalized dessert plate for him, which I did not even have to request, he simply did it of his own accord.  I will absolutely be coming here again, and I would undoubtedly recommend Gramercy Tavern to everyone who asks for restaurant recommendations.

Gramercy was hands down superb. We made reservations via open table and came during lunch on a weekday. The restaurant was not very packed and was very spacious. We ordered the ruby red shrimp and the beef tartare as the first course and the lamb (rare) and chicken and maitake mushrooms as the second course. Everything was superb! The chicken may have been the most perfectly executed chicken I've had in awhile. It was perfectly prepared, cooked through, but extremely tender. The juicy maitake mushrooms complimented well with the rest of the dish and the wine sauce that was drizzled over the entire dish was superb. We'll definitely be back for the chef tasting!

If you are on a budget, I recommend choosing individual dishes from the menu. The lunch seasonal tasting was $98, but doing a two course meal from the menu was about the $60 per person. I love, love the fact that service is included in the price. There is no surprises at the end of the meal when we get the bill. The only thing you would have to account for is tax.

Work team dinner at Gramercy and one of the best experiences one can have in NYC. Huge shout out to our server Kerry (or Carrie?) who, through her detailed descriptions of each menu item, created such excitement as we awaited the arrival of our courses.

Every course was one culinary experience after the other with a few explosions of flavor mixed in. What I like the most is the restaurant's ability to tailor courses for almost every allergy imaginable. When my new boss shared her cinnamon allergy with Kerry, she returned with menu selection confirmations and steered her towards desserts that were cinnamon free. And, even a complimentary box of miniature sweets that were cinnamon free to take home.

Top notch experience and I highly recommend. Try everything!

No Complaints, this place is perfect. I visited the dining room on a Saturday evening with reservations. I did the tasting menu which was very diverse, tons of creative flavours and colours. The wine list is great, service amazing, ambience awesome, flowers EVERYWHERE (which I love) and most importantly delicious. Portions were not laughably small so I was actually stuffed by the end. I will say the dessert was the largest portion which was weird. The tavern is walk-in only so the wait can be quite long (2 hours +) but if you want the certainty, try and get reservations in the dining room for a less stressful experience.

I don't know what's left to be said about Gramercy Tavern except "wow...omg, and everything in between".  What a magnificent experience in a stunningly beautiful room with intelligent and impeccable service and food that is nothing short of spectacular in every sense of the word. GT seamlessly blends leading edge culinary foresight and innovation in a comfortable and approachable manner. 

Words don't do justice to how beautiful the food is and photos don't do justice to how delicious the food tastes. I encourage you to scroll through some of Yelp the photos to see for yourself. 

Gramercy Tavern in NYC dining at its best, friendly, welcoming and oozing NY style and sophistication.  Can't wait to return.

Looking for a casual lunch in Gramercy Park. Stopped by around 1:30pm and immediately were seated in the Tavern. We ordered the Duck Mousse appetizer, which was just melt-in-your-mouth perfection. For the entree we went with their off the menu special - a charred ramp broth and steak sandwich. The soup was good, but the sandwich was AWESOME!!

Overall....great service and food!

Went back for the 1st time in several years, and everything was actually better.  The ambiance felt less stuffy.  The staff is still very professional, but it felt this time friendlier and overall 'happier.'  Am a fan of Danny Meyer and his concept of "tip included in the price" policy, and I think this, like other DM's restaurants, is working for them.  

But as it should be, the food was what impressed us more this time.  We had the 3-course meal, and it was great.  Especially, the smoked trout was the most amazing cooked fish I've had in a long time.  They smoke it for only a couple of minutes, and the fish tastes fresh with just a hint of smokiness, which was absolutely divine. 
The room was still the same and beautiful and elegant, yet it felt more comfortable and inviting.  The service is high quality, friendly, courteous, but without being stuffy.

I expected this place to be overrated but it was really quite good, especially at the price range. I enjoyed the beef tartare which was actually quite delicate. I also had the black bass which was very flavorful. I only wish that it came with slightly more fish, but I was still full when I left. For the wine I had a Loire valley sparkling white which was a good compromise for champagne. 

The service was expert. Even with the device included in the price, our waitstaff was attentive and professional. 

I hope to return soon.

Gramercy is a gem for many occasions, truly any. We wrapped up a birthday dinner here, one of many visits, with custom cake and single malt. Good bless, and hope corporate entities won't plan to take away what makes this place unique and supreme.

This restaurant is NOT inside the Gramercy Park Hotel as some other reviewers have pointed out. It is on 20th between Park and Broadway - a one star Michelin restaurant.

Having said that this is a "fancy" white table cloth restaurant, suitable to bring your parents, bosses or even as a date if you were sit in the area where the bar is vs. the inside dining area. The quality of the food here is TOP NOTCH, you are paying for what you are getting.
Interior is fab, especially now with the spring there are so many flowers inside, it was quite lovely and perfect for a Sunday lunch.

We ordered two app, a main each and two desserts with a bottle of prosecco which got us to a $300 bill.  The lobster salad and shrimp medley for app were very much decadent and delicious. The porktenderloin, arctic char and the chicken were all presented in a very sophisticated and thought-out way. The Matcha dessert full of fresh fruit and matcha moose was the best way to wrap up an already delicious lunch.

Highly recommend it for a special occasion dining!

I really loved Gramercy Tavern and I think it has been my favorite Michelin star meal to date. Would highly recommend going with the tasting menu as that gives a fantastic sampling into the best dishes. Otherwise:

Food favorites: 
- Duck Breast & Sausage - duck cooked so perfectly; sauce phenomenal; I was sad to think that soon the dish would be over
- Artic Char - cooked so wonderfully; so moist
- Lobster Campanelle - really delicious sauce, so hearty 

Atmosphere: The atmosphere doesn't particularly stand out to me, but that's pretty inconsequential compared to the quality of the food.

Service: Wonderful.
Excellent food and service. Highly recommend the tasting menu, great value and variety.

Definitely not a Tavern. Or what we think of as a Tavern. We booked a reservation. Didn't realize it was flat rate per plate dinning with reservations. So when we got there we changed to seating in the bar'ish area and a ala cart style menu instead. Really great! No question. Good food, wait staff was great. Not raving about it but it was great. If you are in the neighborhood, worth checking out.

Gramercy Tavern is a New York institution for a reason. The service here is impeccable and the food is consistently fantastic. I recently brought my mother to celebrate her birthday, and we had zero complaints. We both ordered the regular tasting menu as well as a few cocktails -- which will run you a couple hundred dollars -- but quite worth it for special days. Everything we had was delicious from the Spritz to the roasted chicken. If you ever need a spot to celebrate something special come here. I do also want to note that the front part of the Tavern is also delicious with their a la carte menu and a fantastic place for afterwork drinks.

So annoyed. Have been going to Danny Meyer restaurants for 10 years, at least 20 times a year, so figure at least 200x.  I made a reservation by on Monday May 15th at 6:45 and realized today that it should have been for Tuesday, May 16th. I called today April 29th to ask to move the reservation to the 16th and they gave me the 5:30/9:30 bs.  It is a Tuesday in May and you can't give a good customer a 6pm reservation (btw I asked for anything between 6-7:30).  It is really annoying.  I am done with Union Square Hospitality Group restaurants.  Have a reservation at Mailalino and can not wait to cancel day of the reservation.

***********

Update this week, a very nice woman from Union Square Hospitality team reached out to see how she could help me secure a better reservation.  She was really courteous and did not hold my bad review against me.  I appreciate her reaching out and I hope her managers recognize WS as a great rep for the company.  Thank you!

GT has been one of my favorite dining experiences to date. Their Michelin star was well deserved as exemplified by the creative tasting menu. Gordon Ramsay would have a hard time chewing this place out as each dish is impeccably crafted; the fish was smoked to perfection and the caviar was on point. I shall be back soon.

Wow! 18 dollars for a 4month old can of Other Half that BS!  You people are out of your mind!
To sell old beer from a great Brewery and charge that much you  suck for that!

I'm not sure what to say that's already been said multiple times.
1. Service-impeccable - we didn't have reservations at the restaurant portion, just the tavern-but asked if there was a cancellation to fit us in if possible---we got In!! 
2. Service was beyond amazing and the staff was extremely knowledgeable.
3. We tried the tasting menu. Typically my group always adds salt or need hot sauce but we experienced the good without adding any ingredients which tells you the level of sophistication and each dish.

Hands-down one of my favorite experiences in New York

Review for the off-menu burger only. Will update when I return for a full meal!

Overall (5 stars): The off-menu burger is a gift bestowed upon us. The meat falls apart in your mouth and the smoky flavor of the cheese and bacon complement the thick patty marvelously. The bun is somehow perfectly studded with sesame seeds throughout and toasted so that the outside is crispy but the bun itself still maintains chewiness. The chipotle aioli adds even more spice and smoky flavor to the burger. 

General: Upon stepping inside of Gramercy Tavern, one can feel that this is a world-renowned establishment. We arrived early before the restaurant opened on a Saturday afternoon, though I feel that we still would've gotten a seat if we arrived a little later. Service here is impeccable, from the time it takes to order drinks, order food, receive food, have all your plates cleared away at once, etc. You really receive top-notch treatment here. 

Food: I'm unsure if this is still true but I heard Gramercy Tavern only produces a limited number of these burgers each day. The restaurant grinds ribeye, filet, and other trims of the cow freshly each day. The wood-fire grill they use to smoke and grill the patty and bacon imparts that amazingly smoky flavor to the burger. The meat itself is so incredibly juicy and melts/falls apart in your mouth. The chipotle aioli and pickled fresno chiles are wonderful toppings to the burger for that extra kick of spice. Everything works together to deliver you one amazing burger experience. I can't wait to come back to the restaurant to try some of the items they have on their regular menu.

Overall summary back up top!

Excellent service and a strong range of wines. Food quality was good and its presentation great.

Worth at least one visit by all whom have a passion for food.

Deliciously cooked oysters and clams, as well as fish with lobster & mashed potato main course. Would not recommend the duck main course, it turned out to be a mediocre sausage. Chocolate mousse dessert has a bit too much white cream, makes it a bit greasy but portion is large enough for 2 people. Great house made soda. Overall, awesome experience.

Fabulous dinner celebrating an early Mother's Day tonight! The food is beautiful, thoughtful, and delicious! We (4 of us) did the 3 course dinner - the soft shell crab is truly spectacular! Really, don't miss it! The favorite entree at our table was the pork, but we also loved the tile fish, the Arctic char, and the chicken (the sauce and crispy skin are great)!  The chocolate dessert was the table favorite, and the pear and pineapple desserts both stand out as winners.  I also can't say enough good things about the service.  Our server, Ayisha, was truly excellent!  She described all the dishes beautifully, helped us make selections, and sent out an extra entree and an extra dessert for the table since we were torn by what to order.  This service is hard to find anywhere, and in a gratuity free restaurant, is really unbelievable.  All the "extras" were fabulous- from the rice chip amuse, to the seriously amazing bread, to the chocolates (O-M-G), and granola bars for tomorrow, we were in heaven! Also, we got to share the dining room with Jimmy Fallon, so there's that. We had a great and special dinner in a lovely, flower filled restaurant with unbeatable service - we will be back!

Went to celebrate my bf's birthday on Sunday night and couldn't have asked for a better experience.

We had dinner at the front tavern (a-la-carte) and shared appetizer, two mains and dessert.
- Oysters ($4 each): they have raw and roasted. I recommend you try the roasted, they were delectable
- Grilled Shrimp & Carrot Stew, Cumin, Mint and Sesame Flatbread ($30): deliciousness. The stew was like a cream soup, with hints of ginger. Very well finished flavors and super smooth texture.
- Monkfish, Lobster, Celery Root and Mushrooms ($32): loved it, the sauces on it are light but flavorful. Lobster pieces are small, but I expected given it is not priced as a large lobster dish.
- Caramelized Cheesecake, Tarragon Cookie, Pistachio Halva and Blood Orange Sorbet ($16)

Service was great. Our server explained to us in detail the dishes we were interested in. She also brought a delicious birthday cake after I asked her in secret at the back to bring something with a candle. I knew it was a no-tipping restaurant, so it was a pleasant surprise to be treated so nicely.

Wine selection is really good, organized by type of wine and then region. The somm was also great.

instagram.com/danapgreco

Amazing place. Came here for my friend's birthday; what a treat it was especially on a very rainy Saturday afternoon.

We decided to go with the Seasonal Menu. The service by the way was very warm and the decor--quite classy. I absolutely love the flowers all over.

We started with two freshly, flaky baked buns with butter that had sumac and thyme. Then the Marinated Fluke which was refreshing with the blood orange, fennel and pumpkin seeds. The next course was the smokey Cod in a sauce, asparagus,and yogurt. Perfectly seasoned. Next was the Squash Tortellini paired with Arugula, with Bone Marrow and Crispy Gremolata. Very flavorful. Finally, the Duck Breast & Sausage (I told them no pork--) served with Leeks, Charred Onion and Trumpet Mushrooms. The duck breast was perfectly cooked with the crispiest skin.  We finished it with desserts, a cream puff filled with clementine sorbet and an earl grey creme, Strawberries & Cream with Whipped Vanilla Cheesecake, Crispy Angel Food Cake and Sorrel Ice. They also brought out a coconut mini cake with a candle, two beautiful chocolates and jelly candy. 

Wow, talk about feeling glam and my palate was surprised every time :)

I try to come to GT when I am in town and it never has disappointed me over the years. Servers go out of their way to make you have a warm and memorable experience. Being a fan of the tavern area, I enjoy the energy of the bar and the front area of the restaurant. My grilled lamb with green garlic butter was done to perfection. The cabernet sauvignon wine pairing was such a great complement.

Don't change please. I like the civility (!)

AMAZING. 
I planned a surprise engagement lunch here with my family and my fiance's family for right after I proposed. I spent weeks emailing back and forth with Alessandra M. and Roberta D. about every detail - including the menu, the message, the flowers, the decor - just everything. It was better than I could have ever hoped. 

The flowers were absolutely stunning, Roberta did such a great job! The candles were a beautiful touch too. 

Alessandra handled all of my emails (some of them a bit panicky when I thought I had to change my engagement plans) with total grace and civility. She answered all of my questions quickly, kindly, and efficiently. 

My whole family loved this restaurant. The food was incredible, as was the service, and that should go without saying. Gramercy Tavern private room was gorgeous, the food was memorable, and every detail was perfect. But really, what stands out here was the staff. We had an amazing waitress Cari (unclear of spelling). Roberta and Alessandra are absolute gems, and if you are planning ANY event, it should be with them, at Gramercy Tavern! I recommend without reservation. Thank you GT for an amazing lunch to celebrate such a special occasion!

Very nice atmosphere. Busy but not noisy and friendly and efficient staff. The food is refined and delicious and I highly recommend the cheeses instead of dessert. Service is already included which is a nice touch, I think.

What strikes me every time I've dined here is that almost everyone is smiling. This is fine dining at high prices, but it's not stuffy or serious. People come here to celebrate and have a good time. The conviviality is especially evident in the tavern. The service is so friendly and professional, which certainly helps. Our dinner wasn't the best we've had here -- the cavatelli, pea shoots and cheese plate were all great but the sour of the sour cream dominagted the sundae -- but it was still a very happy occasion.

Owned by Danny Meyer and often considered by various publications to be among the best restaurants in the city, Gramercy Tavern is legendary in the NYC dining world. It's where Tom Colicchio made his name, and although I'm a hair less attracted to him than I am to Padma Lakshmi, I'm a big fan of that Top Chef. The kitchen is now run by Tom's successor, Michael Anthony (remarkable consistency in only having two chefs during a lengthy run in such a transient city and industry). 

I've been hearing about this restaurant my entire life, and combining that with many stars from many critics, I must say I probably came in with almost unreasonably high expectations for my first visit. These expectations were met in various ways, and unfortunately not in others. 

Things That Made Me Believe The Hype:

The squash tortellini with arugula, bone marrow, and crispy gremolata. This was one of the best things I've ever put in my mouth. It was head and shoulders above the rest of the tasting menu (and obviously better than everything on the vegetarian tasting menu that my wife opted for). 

The service. It was relaxed, but impeccable. I'm pretty sure the hordes of fine people scurrying around the dining room in uniform would've brought us anything we asked for. "You want a toe? Hell, I can get you a toe by 3 o'clock this afternoon. WITH nail polish." 

(I also appreciate that this excellent service is included in your meal. It really makes a massive difference when you spring for a meal like this, because 25% of a million dollars is...a lot of money. I'm not good at math.)

The lagniappe. From the perfect bread and goat cheese butter you start with to the coffee and caramel petit fours at the end of the meal, not to mention the chocolate granola bar you are sent on your way with, and the beautiful dessert with a chocolate inscription they sent out for my wife's birthday...this is a restaurant that knows the vast majority of us can only afford to do this on a special occasion. And they treat you accordingly.

Things That Made Me Flavor Flav:*

The marinated sea scallops with blood orange, fennel, and pumpkin seeds. Although it was gorgeous to look at, the scallops were under-seasoned and dare I say it, downright slimy. This was also the first dish of the tasting menu, and such a disappointment. It wasn't the only flaw in the food, but luckily nothing else was as off. That said, it was a sad way to start a meal I had been looking forward to for years. If they were just trying to temper my expectations, it worked. 

Everything else we ate fell much closer to the squash tortellini than the scallops, but the meal overall wasn't quite the perfection I had envisioned. I realize that my expectations were probably unfairly lofty, but that's what prices and a reputation like this get you.

Conclusion:

Please believe me when I tell you that this is still an incredible restaurant. It is impossible to have a bad time here. Between the majority of the food, the service, and the people-watching, you have to hate deliciousness and fun and having your every whim catered to if you walk out of this restaurant in a bad mood. 

But I think I'm going to eat in the Tavern next time, because I can't afford to drop this much money on those scallops.
