Possibly the most awesome place in NYC. Year after Year this place gets more fabulous. The same but better. I ate at the bar with my date, the drinks was perfected to taste, the atmosphere never a disappointment.

Get the burger. Get the burger. Get the burger. It was honestly delicious. I don't know how I feel about the chips (not much creativity or flavor) so if you can switch it up for something, I would do that. But otherwise the burger is awesome !

The lamb dish was VERY chewy and I wouldn't order it again. 

The sea bass was flavorful and light. So if you are looking for a healthier lighter option, I would go for this. 

Service was impeccable and I would definitely come back for that burger.

My favorite restaurant in nyc!

I've been here twice: 
The first time I came about 15min before opening without a reservation and was seated in the exterior room. Ordered a few appetizers for the table and each person ordered a main dish. Everything was delicious!
The second time I made a reservation (also lunch time) and was seated in the interior room (prettier). Did the set lunch menu, it was also amazing. All the flavors balance so well, perfect portions, and great service. 

the interior of this place is beautiful as it's decorated with fresh flowers, even the restroom is full of fresh plants :) 

Definitely pricey (charge ~$6-7 for each glass of soda and coffee that does not include refills) but a perfect restaurant for any celebration!

Within the top 5 meals for me. This special elegant experience exceeded on every level . Our meal was an experience of course some of that was our table, some the location. Some the decor, some the wine, meal and desert. 

This is a place where you'll walk away with more than a great meal. 

Hats off !
This place is an apotheosis of culinary achievement.  SUPERB.
Great food. Great service. Order cheesecake for dessert. Warm lobster salad for appetizer.

Went at lunch on a Saturday at 11:45am . We went after reading this review on the hamburger: https://ny.eater.com/2015/6/17/8704211/gramercy-tavern-hamburger

Expected the burger not to live up to the hype, but we were wrong - it blew our minds.  That with a Venetian Royale Gramercy Tavern specialty cocktail made it the best lunch, and possibly the most memorable activity we did on our New York Baby Moon. Seriously, the burger is that good.

The staff was excellent as well - very jovial and helpful. Dined next to the 18mo old of the hostess and her husband.  The staff kept coming and seeing how he was enjoying his lunch as well. 

Just lovely. Will definitely return one day for the burger, though I agree with the eater review, fries would be an improvement as a side dish.

This was our first Michelin Star restaurant experience and it was a pretty great one! We were a bit indecisive as to which day we were going to go to Gramercy Tavern so we actually walked in without a reservation. The wait time at the bar was about 30-45 minutes and for a table was about 90 minutes. We opted to wait for a table because of all the rave reviews!

They have their restaurant divided into the Tavern & the Dining room. At the Tavern (bar & some table space), patrons can order from the a la carte menu while there is a full multiple course menu in the Dining room.

We started off with a couple of their Specialty Sodas (Strawberry & Basil / Vanilla & Passionfruit) & were offered some bread. All were enjoyable as we browsed through the menu. Per recommendation from our waiter, we decided on getting two appetizers & two main entrees. Everything was ordered at the beginning and the meal was paced by the kitchen.

The appetizers we got were the Asparagus Salad & Cavetelli with Pesto. The Asparagus Salad was light & fresh, I was surprised by how good it tasted with the tarter sauce. The Cavatelli was as expected; the pesto was tasty & the pasta was cooked very well.

For the entrees, I got the Grilled Shrimp & Carrot Stew and my husband got the Lasagna. The stew had a different kind of flavor & the broth was the most enjoyable part. I didn't realize there was going to be any fish in it along with the shrimp so that was a nice surprise! My husband enjoyed the lasagna and it was pretty flavorful but it was a bit on the heavy side.

Overall, a very pleasant meal & the service was spot on! The kitchen paced the meal well and our server helped us by making good recommendations. We'd definitely suggest checking out Gramercy Tavern for a fancy dinner night out.

Definitely one of the best restaurants I've been to in NYC!  My girlfriend and I went there for dinner on my birthday.  I had the lamb and she had the black bass.  Both were delicious!  Plus,  the room is great, classy but cozy - especially in fall / winter.  Also, if you are a chocolate lover, don't miss the chocolate vanilla mousse with fudge sauce!

Tavern/Bar is fun and lively.  It's a la carte ordering and great for the under 45-ish crowd.  Dining room is more conservative and less modern (i.e. a little stuffy) - more classic and more for the "mature" diner.  But food in both spots is outstanding and will provide a great dining experience.

Lunch at Gramercy Tavern - Amazing!!!
What a special place!
Tripoline pasta with spinach 
Chicken with roasted mushrooms and white truffles 
Lamb shoulder braised with white bean purée.
I would highly recommend this as a special romantic amazing restaurant!!!

My favourite restaurant in NYC, same as Eleven Madsion Park in my heart! I came here before for dinner, dinner was perfect. This time came here for dessert! We got 5 dessert and EVERY one is prefect! OMG I can't describe the feeling so you must go and try their dessert!

Best restaurant, food, service hands down anywhere in NYC. The Foie Gras to die for! Everything is just perfect. Presentation, taste & service is on point. The wine pairings with prefix meals not worth it. Better off buying a bottle of buttery Chardonnay or a bottle of Pinot Noir with under notes of cherries, tobacco & the field the grapes were grown in. You will be so thrilled you came! Also try Besso while in NYC it's excellent too!
Irresistible. Always special. Meals are exquisite & oozes ambiance. Always a good time. One must try the oysters (raw or cooked), red snapper & goat cheesecake

Four stars because the lamb was not as good as we expected. However, the flatbread was VERY GOOD, must try. Also, the burger was amazing too. The drinks were over priced. Overall, it was good place to dine. Good customer service and food was good.
As good as it gets. This is my favorite American cuisine restaurant of all time. Kudos to the chef!

Enjoyed a fantastic 3 course meal. Fantastic service and the door was spot on. I loved every course and was especially impressed by the strawberry churro. I'd highly recommend this place and will definitely visit again.

One of the best American style restaurants in NYC. Great place for dates, girls night outs, to get drinks at the bar. Gramercy Tavern is a no tipping restaurant. 

You like nice restaurants, but are turned off by the bougie-ness, then Gramercy Tavern is for you. Unassuming staff, memorable food, and beautiful interior design with super pretty flowers all around the restaurant. Check, check and check. 

Two areas to dine: tavern and main dining room. Tavern is more casual and has more bar-type food. I heard the burger is great. 

We got a la carte lunch at the main dining room. We were debating between a la carte vs. tasting menu but we opted to get individual dishes because we wanted to try the pork loin dish. 

*Pork loin and deckle: omg this was beyond great. The pork was super tender and flavorful. Usually, pork dishes can be very salty and the meat is firm. But Gramercy executed this dish perfectly. The rhubarb definitely upgrades this dish to the next level. Recommend this. 

*Black bass: pretty good, but our hearts were distracted by the pork loin. Fish was cooked perfectly, I wish the flavor was a bit stronger. A bit bland, but still very tasty. 

If you want to impress your lady friend, make reservations and she will love it, I promise!
10 year anniversary dinner here.  Classy joint, pre set menu but they work will allergies.

One of the best, if not the best, dining experiences my husband and I have ever had in NYC or anywhere. Unbelievable. The food coma was intense. We did both prix fix menus and shared and everything was outstanding. The bread was so good we couldn't stop eating it. The service was absolutely perfect. Highly recommend. It's pricy but it did not feel like a waste of money to us. And of course, one of the best wine programs in the city.

Gramercy Tavern used to be my favorite restaurant in NYC. It has served as my go to restaurant for special occasions and business dinners. Every year my best friend and I come here to celebrate our birthdays, this Friday was no different. My friend called ahead and gave notes for the meal- no salt on the food and we are celebrating a birthday. 

When we sat down at the table, we told the waitress of our dietary restrictions on salt. She understood and noted it. We ordered our food. Made it clear NO SALT. 

Service: very poor. We had to ask for refills on water and drinks twice times. Our waitress never came to check on us during the meal. Which was a problem given we did not eat some of the food because it was ice cold and salty. Also, waitresses should not call middle age women "girls". I am a customer and should not be called " you girls". Sorry no. We got the sense that the waitress was disinterested in even talking to us. She stood behind a curtain most of the time. 

Food: thumbs down. Extremely disappointing and very poor quality. My food came out ice cold on both dishes. Not only was the fish ice cold for both dishes but also full of salt. Salt which we requested prior to sitting down be eliminated from our food. My friend has a piece of fish that was less then two ounces and swimming in a red sauce. When we asked what the sauce was agin, the food runner did not know or understand the question. Usually in high end restaurants with tasting menus, food is placed on the table and then described as to what you are eating. Not here. Also, we ordered steak as a third meal, could not eat it as it was salty and sitting in some type of soy sauce. 

The plus was the desserts which are very good. The pastry chef never fails to disappoint. The blueberry dessert was delicious as was the birthday cake. However I did not pay money to eat dessert. Overall the meal was horrible and the service to match.

Back to service: when we did not eat our meals, the gentlemen clearing the plates asked us if all was ok, we said no. He did not even tell our waitress (or if he did) she did not come to check on the meal. You would think someone would have mentioned that the table did not eat their food and looked unhappy.  Nope. After we paid, I completed the comment card and wrote negative comments. We told the manager about our experience and she was sorry. She said she was happy to get the feedback and will discuss it with the waitress. She then said, I would refund you the money but it is too late to do so. HUH? So instead next time (she suggested) that next time we come to eat, she will give us a good seat and overseas us. I told her thank you however there will not be a next time. So clearly she missed the point when I handed her back her business card and said no thank you that would not be needed. 

Do not waste your time here. I did give two stars for the pastry chef.

The lunch we enjoyed at this restaurant deserves all five stars. From the delicious food, impeccable service and friendly attractive ambiance, this was a great dining experience. And the desserts are to die for. 
Reservations ard a must and business casual is the appropriate dress. But definitely come hungry. Don't miss eating at Gramercy Tavern.

As amazing as the food was (and the food was stunning) it's the service that really stands out in my mind. Not only was service at our table just incredible, but every staff member made a point of making sure they moved out of the way of guests, and in fact insisted on it. When I had an idiot moment and ordered the wrong dish, I was happy to eat my mistake, and wasn't going to make a fuss, but they insisted on bringing me what I wanted instead of what I actually ordered. Everyone at our table was blown away by the quality of the service, in every way.
The food, though, was also incredible. My brother had lamb four different ways in one dish, which he loved. My wife had the most incredible chicken, which I think was actually the highlight of the meal. I had pork belly which was simply delicious. The desserts were also very good, though perhaps not quite as amazing as the rest of the food. The cookies though, were raved about by my brother. Overall everyone's favorite food of the trip, and definitely the best experience.

Finally tried Gramercy Tavern this weekend and while it was a great experience, it was nowhere near as mind-blowingly amazing as I expected. All around, a very good meal, but nothing to write home about. First off, the dining room ambiance is rather underwhelming. We were unfortunately seated in the back room facing the wall which was a little disappointing. The bar area and bathrooms however, are gorgeous with fresh flowers everywhere. Service and pacing was great. We were able to enjoy a relaxed pace without feeling rushed which I appreciated.

Food - to start, we were served warm biscuits with goat cheese butter. Great way to start the meal. For my starter, I ordered the beef tartar. It was delicious and a hefty portion topped with mini potato chips. For my main, I ordered the chicken. Served with some peas and mushrooms, it was extremely moist and delicious, with good flavor, but unfortunately not anywhere close to the best chicken I've ever had. Which for a Michelin starred restaurant in NYC, equals underwhelming. For dessert, I tried both the "Chocolate" and "Cherry" and both were fantastic. Probably the strongest part of the meal. 

Overall, a great experience but I don't think I'd rush to come back, especially considering the prices.

Gramercy nails it every time. Appetizers, entrees, and desserts are all perfect. The little bread rolls and goat cheese butter were to die for. The price and portions are fair for what you are getting (for a "fancy" restaurant, I never leave hungry and the prices are reasonably affordable). The menu is seasonal and changes regularly. Service is always spot on. This is hands down my favorite all around restaurant in NYC.

What a lovely place! My boyfriend and I had a great time here. It was our anniversary. When we had arrived, we were seated right away. The staff was very attentive and took in consideration that it was a special occasion. We were given a good spot. I ordered lamb. Honestly, I'm a bit picky when it comes to lamb but I was pleasantly surprised cause the meat turned out to be very tender. My boyfriend had bass, and he enjoyed his food very much. Oh, and they gave us a coconut meringue cake as a treat. It was so good! All in all, I can't think of a better place to celebrate our anniversary. We'll definitely come back to try the tasting menu. By the way, it is pretty spacious inside so the noise level is on the lower side

Came on a weekend night. Given the difficulty of getting a reservation and the price tag I had high expectations. The place was absurdly noisy to the point where you couldn't carry a conversation. For the appetizer we had the chilled celery soup with almonds and yogurt and beef tartare, entree was an artic char and lamb Loin with sausage, the dessert was a sorbet and chocolate custard with black berry ice cream. Nothing particularly stood out for the price the dishes commanded. Personally the best part of the meal was the bread and butter. Left hungry and the they seem to know that since they give you a trail mix bar after you pay for the check.

A new meaning to 5 stars. This place has over 90 employees in the dining room and more than that behind the scenes! They have their own bakery and a manager that's all over it.

Extreme excellent service, courses came and went with the expertise of a team of servers. Each course was plated to perfection and dreamy in flavor.

Our head server acted as the director of an evening performance, guiding us through the menu.

No more to say here, this is a must next time you are in New York!

A restaurant in LA needs to learn how to make a burger like this venue here. Not even joking. I'm so happy my friend told me about this spot as I visited new york because I LOVE BURGERS. It's been a couple weeks since I had it, but man i still dream about this burger and want to experience the flavors of it again. Like how can you hate on a burger so simple, yet delivers flavors beyond ones imagination. Of course I'm over exaggerating, just a bit. But got damn, I want to eat this burger again ! Please to-go me one to LA lol.

Anyhow, burger is about 30 bucks. I say it's worth every bite. Seriously, if you're thinking about what to eat and you're reading this. Don't hesitate and get your ass moving to this location and grab a burger. You could thank me later.

Would I come back? I am back at heart  and i will eat here when I come back in the future.

Absolutely one of our quintessential favorites in NYC.  Gramercy Tavern masters making elegant, fine dining exceedingly comfortable and effortless.  We always love the fresh, seasonal menu and the wine list has improved even further.  Excellent service is a cornerstone of Gramercy Tavern, and has never failed us; all staff are pleasant and professional.  It is incredible that Gramercy Tavern still feels so special and has maintained such momentum for over 23 years.

Atmosphere
- Relaxed and serene, it's all about comfortable elegance.
- Upscale rustic feel with exposed wood beams and amber tones.
- Unpretentious and welcoming to all guests.

Food
We opted for the three course prix fix menu ($125).  Began with the Lamb Ravioli (English Peas, Green Garlic and Pecorino) which was delicate and filled with deliciously succulent lamb.  My wife enjoyed the Smoked Trout (Scallion, Kohlrabi and Roe) - it had a supple buttery texture with deep, yet balanced, smoke flavor.  For mains, both the Pork Loin and Belly (Sweet Onions, Lentils and Rhubarb) and Lamb Loin and Shoulder (Swiss Chard, Heirloom Beans and Raisins) were excellent.  Proteins were executed masterfully, moist and tender, and the flavors were so balanced and enticing.  For dessert, we had the Raspberry (Shortbread, Goat Cheesecake, Puffed Rye Berries, Honey and Wild Rose) and Cherry (Maple Butter, Caramel Pecans, Oatmeal Crisp and Horchata Ice Cream).  Both essentially felt like 'deconstructed' classics, but honestly neither left us yearning for more and they were not very substantial.  Not that the flavors were bad, but more that they paled in comparison to the savory dishes.  Perhaps they were a tad over-conceptualized versus the simple elegance of the preceding courses.

Beverage
Began with the Château de Brézé, Brut, Crémant de Loire, France ($14) which was crisp and refreshing, though not overly acidic - an excellent way to start.  With dinner, we enjoyed the 2013 Jamsheed Pyren Vineyard Syrah from Victoria, Australia ($144), a very elegant and expressive wine, beautifully aromatic.  We love wines from this producer, but they are a bit hard to find, so enjoy where you can!  Had very pleasant interactions with Justin Timsit, recently appointed wine director, who was very engaging and personable.  To conclude, it's hard to go wrong with the 1982 Château Suduiraut Sauternes ($28), just the right amount of sweet, it pairs oh so well with dessert.

Service
- Very hospitable and professional, a hallmark of Gramercy Tavern.
- Wine Director Justin Timsit has not only done a great job tweaking the wine selections, but is also fun to interact with and completely unpretentious.
- No tipping; hospitality is included in all prices on the menu.

We exited this famed establishment wondering what happened to the service?  Now, to be fair, we have had wonderful meals there.  Perhaps it was just a fluke, but here is the story.  

Just wanted an early dinner, so decided to try the bar area.  We were promptly seated and that is when things just didn't seem right.  Our server arrived promptly to provide menus and specials (the 'burger'),  and then disappeared for quite some time.  So, we sat there for about 20 minutes, until we asked one of the hosts to send over our server, who quickly appeared.  He went right to the meal order, but alas, we requested drinks first.  We did order the burger special, though.  Were we not supposed to order the burger, because it took about another 15 minutes for the drinks to arrive.  And what?  The food came on its heals.  Now I will say, that we couldn't help but notice most of the other servers, who were quite attentive to their tables, even stopping and chatting.

So, we ate our meal, was presented with a dessert menu (passed), paid the bill and left.  Pretty disappointing, all in all.

Ran in as last minute dinner decision and luckily there were two spots at the bar. Had the last Cab on the menu by glass, from Wash state and it was so so good. Ordered the seafood tower to share and loved every bite
Amazing food like always, this place does not disappoint. The bass and the salad were spot on. Great cocktails and very attentive service. This place deserves 5 stars on everything.

We had dinner last night and decided to do the seasonal tasting menu. The fluke and lobster salad were very flavorful and original. The bread with the goat cheese was mind-blowing- served warm and just fluffy enough. We had seconds and thirds of that biscuit, it was that unreal. My biggest grip was with the waiter. He had a thick accent and was pretty hard to understand and did not seem to understand all of our questions. There was an obvious communication barrier.  This is turn, also effected the presentation of the food (we did not get what he was saying) and what the dish consisted of.  A restaurant on this caliber should take communication skills more seriously when hiring staff. The biggest issue was  that although they were able to give substitutes for the duck - after I told them I do not eat meat , there was certainly a  surprise when the hake came out wrapped in pork. I am not sure if this happened due to the communication barrier mentioned (it was made clear I do not eat meat). And although they quickly replaced our plates, my spirits were a little dampened and I did not enjoy that plate. 

All in all, an OK experience but we expected more for a $420 dinner for two.

Have been here twice, once on my own dime and once paid by the company. I did not do the tasting menu either time so I cannot comment on that.

Pros: beautiful dining area and beautifully prepared and flavorful dishes

Cons: even at this price point I am accustomed to getting more for my money (even if Im not technically paying). In fact, first time I went here I had to grab another bite to eat afterwards since I was left so hungry. If you have unlimited funds, it isn't much of an issue I suppose but for me there are better high end options that won't leave me quite so hungry

What a horrible fucking value this place is today. I've been here many times in the past dozen or so years and just had the tasting menu with wine pairing. I never complain about portions but this was just fucking ridiculous. Never coming back here again which is a shame since the service is quite good.

Shaquille for the win ! Amazing dining experience. Incredible food. But the man that really stole the show was rookie staff member Shaquille ! He was always there for any request you had, not to mention your water glass never fell below the bottom third of the cup. Attention to detail is key in fine dining and Shaquille exemplified that! Thanks !
Ate here for my 40th birthday in 2013. Everything was amazing. The cauliflower soup stands out.

Does Gramercy Tavern need another five star review? Probably not, but I'm adding mine anyway, because I spent a perfect three and a half hours here and think anyone perusing yelp, still weighing it, should just do it. Go, get the tasting menu, have a cocktail, spend the money & the time, love yourself.

One of the best dinners I've ever had. Their seasonal tasting menu was extremely well prepared and made with the freshest ingredients of summer. Service was impeccable and the wine was outstanding. As a birthday treat, they brought out an additional cake on top of the desserts that already came with the tasting menu. It was a very delicious coconut cake topped with meringue. Then after that they gave us after dinner chocolates - so much sugar! But so worth every bite. 

Budget at least 2 hours if you get the tasting menu, and that's if you're a moderately fast eater.

Delicious 40th birthday dinner.  Main reason for 4 instead of 5 stars is that we had a 10 pm reservation which is late as it is, and our table wasn't ready for us when we got there. We waited outside for at least 15 minutes (no place at the bar to wait) and when we were seated there were at least 10 empty tables inside.  Besides that food was delicious for each course (I had lamb ravioli and striped bass). My friend had the beef tartare which was ok (we have had better) and another fish main. Wish they had a beef/steak dish as part of their entree choices. Otherwise really nice start to finish and servers were attentive throughout. Recommended but not 5 stars on Yelp unfortunately.

Hard to imagine what I can say about Gramercy Tavern that hasn't been said before, but I will throw my lot in with everyone else's to say: yes, this restaurant is worth it. We came for my rehearsal dinner - which was really a dinner with me, my fiance, and our parents (so, kind of a high stake dinner...). The service was outstanding. The sommelier was extremely knowledgeable. The gastronomic adventure we went on was amazing. In particular, there was a  poached lobster dish and a strawberry dessert (with fluffy green ice?) that I still remember fondly, and this dinner occurred over 2 months ago. I've lived in New York for five years, and I hope I'll be back at this restaurant before another five years go by.

First Michelin star restaurant I have ever been !!

5 * (Star service + Food) = 5 Star review from me. 

Being a vegetarian was not at all difficult, in fact, my wife, who is a non-vegetarian was impressed with their vegetarian options .

Special thanks for Aisha, who was super nice. 

Thanks for the coconut cake, that still melts in my mouth when ever I think about it.

The decor, food, and servers was beyond exceptional. Had dinner here with two friends and everything was phenomenal. They only offer their original pre-fix or seasonal pre-fix menu; no a la carte here, unless you're at the tavern section. Our cocktails and champagne was spectacular(they have an extended wine/champagne list). 

All of us thought that the service was impeccable and super attentive without interrupting our conversations. We had two servers handling our table.

Definitely an experience and highly recommend to anyone if you're looking for a classy night out to dress up and have an intimate friend gathering or a romantic dinner date.

*4.2
- Taste 4.2
- Cost Performance 4.0
- Service 4.5
- Cleanness 4.0
- Vibe 4.3

Great service and food. We went there as an anniversary and the waiter gave us a welcome drink and dessert for free which I thought was great service. The food itself was awesome, with a seasonal course, and there were wine to match the meal. No tip here since it is the Union Square Hospitality Group. (https://www.ushgnyc.com/hospitalityincluded/)

Came here today to celebrate my birthdays with my parents and husband in the dining room. I had a pleasant overall experience. The service was great. I was just a bit underwhelmed by the food (not sure if I just had too high expectations because of the stellar reviews). Overall I would give Gramercy Tavern 4.5 stars for service and 3 stars for food.

The four of us ordered the seasonal tasting menu. We had the marinated fluke, lobster salad, hake, spinach tortellini, pasture raised beef, and blueberry. Honestly, the meal was quite unmemorable. All the dishes were cooked well but nothing really stuck out. I think my favorite dish of the night was the hake (which was slightly over salted). My favorite bites were the maitake mushrooms which was served with the spinach tortellini and the complimentary black sesame chocolate truffle (so good)!! The beef was tender but not very flavorful. The spinach tortellini was good but not memorable. Overall, I did have a pleasant experience. The servers were very attentive and service overall was great. We received a complimentary cake for my birthday with a personalized Happy Birthday message. I'm not sure if I'll return though since there are many other options out there at this price range. Maybe if I see an interesting menu in the future I'll give their food another chance.

This place has excellent food and décor! 

Rick (one of the bartenders) was extremely knowledgeable and kind. Because of him, we are coming back.

I loved the decor, the atmosphere, and the food at this institution, though the prices were quite high and the portions quite small. Nonetheless, the taste and flavor of the Sea Bass was pretty incredible, striking a fine balance between uniqueness, flavorful,  yet subtle. The service was also a bit slow, which may be attributed to the popularity of the establishment, though the waiter himself was amiable enough. Overall, I had a great time here with my friends.

This was just perfect in every way. You walk in to a welcoming room and are warmly greeted. They gently escort you through this flower and art filled space and to your table. The surroundings are exquisite. Add to this perfectly fresh ingredients cooked to perfection. Beautiful presentation. Service almost anticipated my needs before I realized them. A classic.

I had an excellent experience at Gramercy Tavern. 
Space:The restaurant was much larger than I expected with high cavernous ceilings and soft light. Given the nature of the space the volume can get a little louder than I prefer but by no means was it overly distracting. 
Service: My waitress was friendly, professional, and knowledgeable. She was easily able to help my fellow diner select/alter dishes given their extensive allergies. While I already knew the wine I wanted, the connoisseur also had great service.
Food: You are given the choice of a pre-set 6 course meal or you can select your own dishes from their menu to create your own 3 course meal. Be aware they request everyone selects the same number of courses for timing concerns. The rolls they bring to your table are hot and fresh but what really makes them shine is the delicious goat cheese butter that accompanies them, everyone at my table had two servings. For my first course I selected the beef tartare as it is a personal favorite of mine at any establishment I visit. The beef was fresh and had some thinly sliced zucchini on top for color and great texture. For my main course I opted for the pork loin and belly. The pork belly was without a doubt the best I have ever had, perfect crispy yet it melted in my mouth. The loin was juicy and tender, well accompanied by the scallions and sauce it rested on top of. Unfortunately I had to leave early and take my third course to go. I opted for the cookie plate as it was one of the only dished that did not have ice cream that would melt. The cookies were good but would not have been my first choice if the situation were different. 
Overall I would definitely recommend Gramercy Tavern and am I looking forward to visiting again soon.
When I have a bad day, I come here and always leave a better off.  Great food, wonderful staff and nice, warm atmosphere. Love their burger!

The sea bass was pretty underwhelming,  It wasn't very flavorful or rich, and the beans in the dish were kind of an odd pairing.  The focaccia bread was pretty tasty I must admit.  Had a drink that was standard.  Pretty expensive for food of this quality.  Overall wouldn't really recommend based on this experience, but maybe the rest of the menu is better.  High ceilings and fairly dense, so probably best for something like a class family birthday dinner.

It's great when a restaurant truly lives up to its reputation. Had the seasonal tasting menu and each course was better than the last. The staff was friendly and ready to answer any questions about the menu.

We reserved the private room to have our weeding celebration after family members insisted something had to be done that day. We were 10 people and after our city hall commitment we headed to the restaurant. We were greeted and told we were early but that the room was being set up for us and in a matter of a few minutes we were directed to our reserved spot and seated. It had been a bit of a last minute thing, so there were mishaps as of what was being served we ended up paying a bit extra for food because of this but stressed because of the whole ordeal of my wedding and on top of that pregnant I let it go. I was very impressed with the waiters, very knowledgeable, patient and efficient our plates were removed and brought on a timely manner with great attention to details. The family was very pleased and so was I. We ordered a wedding cake for dessert which is not included in the food package, and I honestly did not like it, it was very buttery and not tasty, it looked pretty in the photos so I guess that's something to point out. 
When all was said and done and we were all ready to leave the waiter, Jason who had been delightful the whole evening came to say his last farewell, I had read that gratuity was not something this restaurant encouraged or did so I proceeded to thank him for his service and tell him (which was the entire truth) how happy I was with the service. He offered to pack the cake for us to take home and well after paying 450$ for it I thought it was the fair thing to do. We went to the lobby to wait for our cars and ubers and no one came with the cake. over half an hour chatting, saying good bye to parents and grandparents and no one, absolutely no one came with the cake we paid for and were promised to get packed for home. Husband and I of course forgot ourselves and off we went. After this the whole thing got ridiculous, it was a Friday and we were going away for a few days, no one called about the cake, and when we called no one knew what we were talking about until finally someone offered to keep it there for us until Monday and still on Monday tell us it was frozen and ready for pick up.
I wrote the people who took care of our reservation an email about the incident and they offered to give me a new cake top free of charge and that's how this story ends.
The restaurant is beautiful, the food was really good and we are happy we were able to make things happen on a short notice.

Delicious!  House made lemonade was perfect for a hot night. Cucumber salad was tastefully dressed. The grilled lamb was cooked just right and served with a sauce the complemented the meat without overpowering it. The cherry cheesecake was the best way to end a scrumptious meal. Service was attentive and the decor is classic. I went with a friend to splurge on ourselves after work and it was so worth it.

Came here last night for a birthday dinner. 

We had a super friendly waiter, and all the surrounding tables loved him! The food was impeccable and artistic. I got the lamb ravioli for the first course and the pork loin and belly for the second. 

Lamb ravioli was so soft and tender and worked well with the sauce it came with, while the pork loin and belly was embellished with fresh in-season peaches and herbs. Do make sure you get the zucchini bread because it is divine!

For dessert I got the cherry which is maple ice cream on a bed of ice and actual cherries. They also gave a free granola bar that was made in-house as a complementary take away. Overall the food is on par with 11 Madison and Daniel, without the stuffiness.

Thoroughly enjoyed everything about this place. The food was five fire emoji and service was knowledgeable and friendly. There's not much I can add to all of the well-deserved praise GT gets, but I'd like to highlight the beef tartare. I'm not usually a fan of beef tartare, so ordering it was a bit of a reach for me. GT's was absolutely incredible. The inclusion of cashews and cherries elevated this dish far beyond any other I've had. On our way out, we talked to the chef who was extra nice and really passionate about his food. Highly recommended.

Went for lunch with a friend who is visiting from out of town (who is also a chef). The service was impeccable, the decor elegant and earthy and the food was exceptional. We say at the bar and ordered their burger (which is not on the menu but can be made upon request) and the tomato salad with curry ricotta cheese. By far the best burger I've ever had in my life and the salad was unexpectedly delicious!

We sat in the tavern, or at area. First, the service was really top notch. Second, the food was excellent, except for one dish. I'll get to that in a minute. We started with the flatbread which sounded and looked unassuming and then when we ate it it was an explosion of flavor. All agreed it was really very good. I ordered the sea bass which was good, and had a nice sauce and crunchy tasty veggies. My colleague had the swordfish and liked it, and my other colleague had the pasta dish (as one of the few vegetarian options). He said it was good, but said it was kind of like out-of-the-box or can good. We saw the burger and it looked amazing. I think that will be what I order next time!

Think of the Tavern as two different restaurants with the same kitchen -. the Tavern and the Dining Room. The Tavern serves an à la carte menu in a casual, walk-in setting. The Dining Room offers fixed-price and tasting menus with an à la carte option at lunch.

And if you're eating in the dining room do try the tasting menu. There's a reason this is consistently one of the best restaurants in New York.

The three of us went for dinner and had their fixed price menu 3-course tasting menu, one vegetarian, two regular. Just the right amount of food.  And as the other 3000 reviews can attest it was wonderful.  Impeccable service. Somewhat unique is that it's a no-tip restaurant. That doesnt mean you don't tip, it just means they add the tip (20% I think to your bill.)

Someone just said "Insane food. Immpecable service. This place is an institution and for good reason. " and I cant say it any better!!!!
I think you can say you've seen who someone really is when things go wrong.  One time my meal came out very salty...the server cleared my plate immediately with apologies and replaced my wine with another choice to match my new meal. The manager also came over to make sure all was okay and also comped our desserts.  I really didn't expect my wine to be replaced or a dessert but it was really very nice of them to take what they do seriously and so professionally.  Mistakes happen, but its how you handle them so that's not what Im thinking about when I hear the name of the restaurant. Also, I wasn't sure if I would complain but the server was paying such close attention she came over to make sure! You guys are the best ever. Its nice to see such an institution still working for its reputation.
A chef friend recommended GT twenty years ago. I always try to eat there when in NYC. The food and service are always great. Nice relaxing ambience for NYC.
The seasonal tasting menu was phenomenal! Greatly enjoyed the food, the wine, and the service. The service definitely ranks among the best in New York City.
Fantastic service, food, and ambiance. Oysters and Sea Bass were out of this world- definitely worth a return visit

This restaurant was recommended by the concierge at our hotel. Very expensive but very good. Service was impeccable.  Not the traditional menu, pairings and full course style. Portions not large. All ingredients fresh, pure, and tasteful.  The deserts were fabulous.

Went for a pre-theater dinner and it was an absolutely perfect experience! Definitely deserves its Michelin star!

-beautiful classic space, very open and bright
-gorgeous bar with the beautiful hand painted mural above it
-exciting and bustling bar scene
-we ate in main dining room which was more quiet and subdued
-lots of room between tables in the dining room (unusual in New York)
-fantastic waiter who made sure to get us out in time for our show, but not make us feel rushed
-we were given great food, wine and cocktail recommendations 
-food was delicious--expertly prepared and flawless presentation 
-old school feeling of a classic New York restaurant 

Can't wait to go again!

Where do I begin? I've had a ton of experience with Michelin star restaurants all over the city, and somehow their simply not worth the accolades they receive. Gramercy Tavern is a game changer. We did a lunch tasting menu with the wine pairing, and what an incredible experience we had! The food was incredibly intricate, each ingredient showcased with impeccable culinary craft. And the wine was absolutely delicious, each pairing offering a different flavor. I can't recommend it more if you're going for a date, I would go again!

Can I give this place 10 stars?!?
One of the best dining experience I've ever had. The staff is great and the tasting options were simply exquisite. This place impresses! Each dish provides an absolutely indulgent bite. I can't imagine anyone would be anything other than delighted with the tasting menu. The most memorable dishes were the duck breast, tender with a delicious glaze, and the shaved ice with strawberries and cream. It was so light and airy and delicious. Gramercy Tavern is top notch!

After our horrible dinner last year, the guest relations manager graciously offered us a chance to come back to try the Tavern again. My boyfriend hasn't wanted to go, given the prior poor experience (and general lack of time), so I hadn't taken the opportunity to return until yesterday, when my sister agreed to go with me as a sister-sister date on a day off. Oddly enough, this was also around my birthday.
-
Food: The food from start to finish was phenomenal. I don't believe I've eaten at a place that treats vegetables as respectfully as Gramercy Tavern does. To be fair, it is summer, and summer produce is delicious on its own. Even so, the chefs here take these vegetables and really put them on display, figuratively speaking. I started with the summer greens with sesame yogurt dressing and dill. It was fresh, light, and had the perfect amount of dill--never overpowering but flavorful enough to meld with the yogurt in harmony. Every leaf was perfect. My sister started with the cucumber salad with bacon, which tasted both refreshing and savory. Strange but true. She sopped up the remaining dressing with her cheddar bread, signaling a 10/10 salad experience. For her entree, she opted for the cavatelli with pesto. It's one of the heavier dishes but scrumptious. My sea bass with corn and smoked ham was equally if not more scrummy. The fish was soft and juicy and grouped well with the corn, ham, celery, and crispy onions around it. If I had to nitpick, I would say they could've done with half of the amount of celery they used with this dish, as I would've like the corn to come through more. Celery can be aggressive, you know? It was good celery though. Finally, we couldn't leave without dessert, so we ordered the blueberry cheesecake and apricot and saffron sundae. And what a delicious cheesecake it was! The blueberries used for the compote on top were so plump, I could've sworn they won some sort of county fair. Whoever made it should get a gold star for not making it too sweet and just letting them be the beautiful blueberries that they are. My only regret for the day was that I was too full to eat it all. We should have split one dessert, so we wouldn't have wasted such yummy food. My sister loved her sundae but was also too full to finish.

Service: I must make a disclaimer that the time my sister and I were available was an odd 2:30 PM. So we came during the not-quite-lunch-and-definitely-not-dinner time and were seated immediately. This eliminated the main problem that my boyfriend and I encountered during our last visit. Already, it was a good start to the meal. With that said, service was impeccable. Ah, I should amend my previous statement about my one regret. I have a second regret: not remembering our server's name. He was professional and affable all at once. Never pushy but also informative. I would give him a shout out if I could. In fact, all the support staff encountered during this meal were wonderful and attentive to just the right amount. They serve and take from the table with great care. They really are a step above.
-
TL;DR: Take two of Gramercy Tavern was a complete win. I'm thankful to the guest relations manager for giving me the opportunity to try it again, as I would not have done so otherwise. If you love your meals full of heart and love for every ingredient on any given dish (particularly the produce), eat here. Perhaps going during an off-peak time is key?  But the food is delectable regardless.  With this, I might be able to convince my boyfriend to try the Dining Room with me in the future.

Wow - hands down one of the best dining experiences of my life. Gramercy Tavern is fancy, but not pretentious, and nails it when it comes to both food and service. Reservations were difficult, but not impossible, to get... though you should definitely plan in advance. 

In the main dining room, you only have the option of a three course prix-fixe or the tasting menu. If you are looking for more flexibility, go for a table in the Tavern portion of the restaurant. As we wanted to have the full experience, my fiance and I opted for the tasting menu, which is 5 savory courses followed by a dessert course. At $179pp including tip, I think this is a steal. The portions are the perfect size to leave you satisfied but not overly stuffed at the end. I won't go into the details of each course as the menus are seasonal, but they were all incredibly thoughtful and unique. My fiance is not a fan of "complicated" or overly "artsy" food and he genuinely loved every course for both creativity and flavor. None of the courses seemed like it was trying too hard or sacrificing quality for presentation. It should be noted that our meal lasted approximately 2 hours... so if you are trying to catch a show after or have limited time, something to keep in mind for planning purposes. 

The service was fantastic. Our waiter was very pleasant and friendly, and all of the other staff were attentive without being over-bearing. Everything at Gramercy Tavern seems to move like a well-oiled machine. The ambiance is beyond beautiful - it felt like we were whisked away to an intimate spot in the middle of France or Tuscany surrounded by gorgeous decor and fresh florals/greenery. 

Highly recommended for a special occasion as our meal here was truly unforgettable. Hope to be back soon to try out the Tavern!

Celebrated my aunt's 85th b'day in the Dining Room on Sunday and it was sensational.  Refined food but friendly, unsnobby service from Hannah who even got me a handwritten recipe for the Hemingway Daiquiri when I raved about it.

This is first class dining in a relaxed atmosphere and the service was great from greeting at the door to good-byes.

The seasonal vegetable chef tasting menu is the best meal I've ever had. Hands down. Pricey but worth it! Incredible service and a non pretentious atmosphere makes this restaurant a great choice for a special occasion. 
Tip - go easy on the bread with goat cheese butter. It will be hard to resist but in the end worth it because you'll be able to enjoy the rest of your meal.

Gramercy Tavern never disappoints. Between the amazing atmosphere, truly wonderful staff and exciting menu, you literally cannot go wrong here. Every time I come, including my most recent visit last night, I'm reminded what it feels like to experience exceptional dining. Down to the smallest details and surprises, they just get it! Pricey? Yes. But well worth every penny and then some!

Excellent place! I was in town for work, and dining solo so decided to eat at the bar, and the experience could not have been better. The bar tenders provided top notch service with not even an ounce of pretentiousness. The food was fantastic, I went with the burger on the recommendation of the bar tender, and it was one of the best burgers I have ever had. I started with the cucumber salad which was equally amazing and finished with the chocolate pudding cake, again amazing.

As a special treat, my partner and I came here for dinner after attending the US Open tennis. We knew about the long wait for a table and reservation which required to be made far ahead so we decided to turn up anyway to try our luck. We have watched Youtube videos and read many reviews about this place and as we are fans of Tom Colicchio of Top Chef, and knowing his successor, Michael Anthony has taken this place to new heights, we knew we would not go wrong coming here.

First impression - this place is beautiful, has an old style interior decor - leather & wood, fresh flowers everywhere but a little noisy as the seating is intimate. Put our name down for both the bar and a table and stood at the bar waiting for whichever became available first. Bar staff were friendly and attentive even though they had their hands full serving seated customers. We got our drinks about five minutes of being there. 

About 20 mins into our wait, we were approached by a sharply dressed gentleman to head to our table. What a pleasant surprise as we were told that it would be 45 min to an hour's wait. 

Immediately, we were given water and our wait staff Elizabeth came over to introduce herself and gave us the menu. While we were mulling over what to order, the Head Chef came over and offered his recommendations. What a treat! Michael Anthony was a super nice guy as we never would have expected someone this important and busy to wait on us. We even had a little conversation about food, tennis and Massachusetts oysters!

We had the app of seafood tower, entrees of duck sausage and pork fried rice and dessert of berries and cream with Panna Cotta.  Drank Syrah from Vallin Santa Barbara and cocktail of sour whiskey. 

We had a great meal that night! The seafood tower was amazingly memorable - it consisted of Island Creek oysters, grilled shrimps, poke of some white fish, apple kimchi (the best!), lobster salad and several pickled dishes mushroom and veggies. The entire night was a delight and I would definitely return to have a meal here if I visit NYC again. I don't remember getting such great service in any high end restaurants anywhere in the world. They seemed to enjoy what they do and do it with great commitment to excellence.

Perhaps my expectations were too high, but I was very disappointed with my dining experience here. Our reservation was for 8:30pm in the dining room  and from the moment we arrived we felt rushed. E.g. the wait staff kept refilling our wine glasses so quickly I thought they must be trying to get us out quick so they could fit 3 services into a night. 

However,the food was good. I had tomato salad (which was the best part of the meal), lamb loin and chocolate dessert. 
All very yummy but nothing blew me away. Perhaps I ordered wrong? My husband loved the ravioli starter and his Raspberry dessert. The main (pork loin & belly) was good but not great. 

The ambiance is typical of a fast paced bistro. Nothing special. Perhaps because Montréal has such great bistros I expected more. If you are ever in Montréal check out Montreal Plaza, L'express or Lemeac for great ambiance for this style of restaurant.

Overall the dining experience was over shadowed by the rushed service and average atmosphere.  Our bill was more than $450 USD for 2 prix fixe with cocktail and a bottle of wine. This is a no tipping restaurant.

Arrived for 8:30 reservation in dining room. Our table wasn't ready so we went to the bar. We were ignored by the bartenders. It took 15 minutes to get our drinks. Finally sipped my Cosmo and it was horrible...very sour. Just then we are told our table is ready. They MADE us carry our full drinks through the entire restaurant to our table.  Maitred had tray, but told us to carry them. Selected prefix menu...food was good..not as spectacular as we expected. Sausage in the lamb loin entre was tasteless. We told the waiter and no one addressed it. No one ever asked if we needed anything or if it was good. We had coffee with dessert course.  No one asked if we wanted anything else but we're just presented with check. For a restaurant of this caliber,the service and the food should be better....they did keep our water glasses full...

My first time was 12/2013 and I gave them a 3. Unfortunately I wasn't detailed as to why. Just said I was underwhelmed. This time, 9/8/17 I had a totally different experience at the bar. Service was perfect.  Ordered the grilled calamari sofrito which was super tasty. The Cavatelli pasta was insanely yummy, the sauce could go with anything! The grilled lamb with sausage and greens was great too. A far better flavor profile experience than four years ago. I'll be back!

Great food, love the seasonal combinations. You can totally taste the amount of effort the chef puts in each dish it tasted divine. The customer service was fantastic. We chose the lamb ravioli and the pork loin and belly. The pork belly was perfectly crisp and the lamb ravioli was complimented well with the sauce and leafy greens. We left the restaurant completely satisfied. Definitely will go again, we definitely had an experience to remember.

Summary: I've had my expectations set way too high for this place. 

We had a reservation and ended up there about 30 minutes earlier and asked if we can wait at the bar. It was crowded, the couple paid their bill and got up. When my wife took one of the seats, bartender asked her to get up because he had somebody waiting for those seats. These things happen and there are nice and polite ways to handle it, but he was way too rude. This set dark mood for the evening, neither food or wine were able to improve. 

Food is ok, nothing worth mentioning, except lamb ravioli that was great. Pastries were surprisingly good.

Service is there, but sometimes it's hard to get waiters attention. Everything is done by the book, nobody's putting extra effort to make the experience great.
Delicious!! My wife and I celebrated our anniversary with some fine dining. The service was excellent. Each course was a treat and as always this amazing restaurant exceeded expectations.

One of my fav restaurants I have ever dined at. 
Atmosphere: bar area is poppin as you walk through to get to the dining area. The blooms and seasonal decor is out of this world pretty-you can tell they put a lot of effort into their arrangements. We went during 9/11 weekend and they had orange blooms, peppers, flowers, twigs that made the whole environment so romantic.
Service: Our waiter seemed like he had a keen interest in who we were and what we were celebrating, why we were traveling, etc regardless of if he actually cared or not, which I really appreciated.  It made us feel much more welcome as opposed to feeling like we were just another table to quickly turn. We explained that we wanted to try to the beef tartar but we really wanted the seasonal chefs menu too.  He said "don't worry about it, I have an idea and I've got it covered". He showed up and served the beef tartar as an amouse bouche! So Thoughful!
Food: Amazing. Every dish I loved. Ate a pasta dish that immediately became the best pasta dish I've ever had in MY LIFE. The portions were perfect; we walked out feeling satisfied and not uncomfortably full in anyway. The Honey Angel bun breadrolls...just TRY to restrain yourself from devouring them with that goat cheese butter, I dare you.  SO amazing and the perfect way to sop up any leftover sauces from the dishes.
I can't wait to come back here. Amazing experience.

Came here for lunch and got the 5-course tasking menu with wine pairings. Excellent food, beautiful space, and impeccable service. Totally deserving of 1 Michelin star (and frankly better than most of the 1-stars). The menu changes all the time by the season, but every dish was a win. Thoughtful, well-prepared, beautifully plated. As a parting gift, diners receive an assortment of baked cookies (most of which are very good). Highly recommend for lunch or dinner but may skip wine pairing next time.

Came here last week for lunch. We were seated in the dinning area, which is more intimate and refined area of the establishment. 

We ordered a bottle of wine with lunch, which was nice. I ordered the roasted chicken. All the food was excellent. 

Note: The menu in the tavern area (not dinning) serves a completely different menu, more like a tavern menu as opposed to the dinning menu they serve in the back area and private dinning area. I did not know this.

We came here for our 1 year wedding anniversary. We ordered the seasonal prefix and the vegetarian prefix as well. Both were surprisingly scrumptious and delicious. Super Fresh ingredients that are cooked very well to perfection. Very impressed about the vegetarian prefix the flavors were superb and complex at the same time.

My son insist on us going gramercy as this is his favorite in New York City. We visited him recently and boy was he right. We loved the experience and the generous portions. Wait staff was most helpful and friendly. The seven courses tasting turned out to be 10 or more as we lost count. The unique pricing with gratuity included in the price is so clever and generous. I am a fan of Danny Meyer and his establishments. No wonder gramercy is such an icon in New York City. Definitely a must if you are in the big Apple. I'll be back.

Spangetini app was primo as was the tomato and mozzarella. My lamb / sausage.. hummmm good but, Not crazy over it as lamb & Italian sausage guy.. my guest did not finish swordfish nor did my other guest go crazy over the chicken dish. We did enjoy a 120.00 bottle of wine but still not feeling the value after 320.00 lunch. PS.. loved the cookies at the end overall I give it a 2.9-3 rating... The tavern menu looks better .. I saw a great pannini walking into dining room , should have gotten that but that's not served in dining room at lunch. Not going back.. I am a new Yorker.
My first real foray into fine dining 15 years ago and still one of the absolute best restaurants going. Never disappoints, and I always look forward to returning.

Oh Gramercy Tavern...I went there for a celebration with high expectations. Service was attentive and great. I liked the drinks, but the food was a big disappointment. Everything was dull. Some of the dishes didn't taste like much but the portions we adequate. Even the dessert  was a bit of a let down but frankly I was so disappointed by the savory courses that by dessert time I just wanted to be over with this place.

Seriously such a great place to eat. We walked in and we're worried we wouldn't be able to eat here since we had a show to catch and the wait was an hour. But in less than 5 minutes the gentleman came over and sat us down right away. We were so appreciative of that.    The food is to die for & especially the chefs selection cheese plate. It was delicious!! We got an order of the olives and the cheese plate for our appetizers and two drinks. The fiancé ordered sea bass which was to die for and I ordered the special burger which literally melted in my mouth. Everything was great and couldn't have been happier. Service was on point and so glad we came here to eat. Highly recommended
The service and decor are top notch. I'm afraid though that the food is not really friendly to folks with a poor persons taste. This place is upscale and has a lot of weird foods.

I have to say this was a really great place. The food, the service, everything was on point. However, they get 1 star because Sister Town. These two girls just really ruin everything, everywhere, every time. You should probably check out their band.

Ate here for dinner two weeks ago. Ambiance was great, service was very good besides the fact they didn't bring us our second round of delicious bread for 30 min. after asking if we wanted more. Other than that the meal was good not great.  We did the seasonal tasting menu and had a bit of everything. It was all three of our birthdays, so they comp'd us with bubbly to start our meal and ended up giving us a coconut cake at the end in addition to our dessert.  Overall, for the price, I would have rather done the 3 course.  The $179 price for the seasonal didn't really seem worth it compared to other M star rated establishments I've been to...perhaps it was the menu itself that seemed a little underwhelming.  Would like to try for lunch or a different fall or winter menu!

Would assume that people who leave favorable reviews are paid to do so, or they're so far up their own asses they don't know the difference between literal shit and goat cheese butter. Do not come here unless you're into solid but aloof  service that serves you ok food. Holy wow, every dish was mediocre at best. For the amount of money people pay to eat here, this was embarrassing. Even more so when they brought out GRANOLA BARS and bonbons to try and appease our table. Waitress had a great fake smile though!

Fabulous restaurant, flawless service and incredible food/drink! That alone is worth 5 stars, however, Yelp needs a 6th star for those rare occasions when someone elevates hospitality to a level above all expectations. Last night our party of 6 arrived at 8:30 WITHOUT a reservation and decided to have some drinks and just wait for a table.  Chef Michael Anthony noticed we'd been waiting almost 2 hours and stopped by to express appreciation for our patience and treated us to several appetizers courtesy of his kitchen. Each time, personally describing every ingredient and making us feel as if we were special guests in his home.  Our servers were pros, Mary Lee at the host station is so sweet, all causing us to have the best feeling about this restaurant as we walked out the door at midnight.
One star for the server, one star for my company. The food was disappointing. We went for the seasonal tasting menu. The fish was bland, the duck was hard to chew..

Gramercy Tavern deserves 5 stars, but I had to knock a star off because the host experience was a rough start for what was meant to be a special evening. We were celebrating an anniversary and very much looked forward to dining here. Upon arrival, we waited to check in with the host. There were four hosts crowding around a computer screen, busily sorting out tables, but not one person raised their head to greet us. We waited patiently and after a few minutes, one finally looked up and welcomed the older white couple behind us and invited them in. It was like we didn't even exist! Granted we're young, but we had a reservation too. We finally interrupted the hosts to ask if we could please be served. They did not apologize.

The rest of the evening was uneventful and wonderful. Thea, our waitress, was incredible. Some of the best service I've ever had. So genuine, so happy, and so eager to help. She made our night. And of course the food was exceptional. Classically American, unpretentious, and of very highly quality. We'll definitely be back.

Service is excellent, the waiter that served us and the receptionist lady was great! Food is not as good as I thought. It's a bit loud for a high class restaurant. It's a very popular restaurant. Our reservation was at 5:15pm, finished tasting menu at 8ish. We got a free cake because that was my friend's birthday. I'd recommend people to go try still.

I made my third visit to Gramercy Tavern for lunch with my parents and it was a remarkable meal.  Both my mother and father left stunned by the nuanced, thoughtful recipes that Michael Anthony adds to classic American recipes. This restaurant is really one of best in the Country.

For lunch, my father and I had one of the specials, which was a roasted corn soup with a waygo beef, roast beef sandwich. The soup was delicate with olive oil floating on the surface. Each spoonful was full of roasted, smoked corn. It was a lovely soup. The roast beef sandwich was on a crusty bun with cartelized onions and layers of rare Waygo beef. It was beautiful.

My mother ordered the Cavatelli with squash and smoked mushrooms. It was topped with shaved pecorino cheese. I had one bite and it was beautiful dish of fresh pasta with Fall vegetables. 

We were too full for the dessert menu, but it look very good.

Again, Gramercy Tavern delivered one of the most impressive meals I have had. I cannot wait for my fourth visit.

My husband and I went to Gramercy Tavern for our anniversary last month. Not only was the food exceptional, but so was the service. Jason, our waiter, couldn't have been nicer or more attentive. The wine selection was also super amazing. We even got a complimentary dessert to celebrate the occasion! We can't wait to go back!
This place is so Amazing!!! My best friend and I dined here last week and it is our new favorite place to go. Can be a little on the pricey side but so worth it! Exquisite! Highly recommend!!!

There was nothing inherently bad about my lunch, I just expected...more (especially when factoring price into the equation). When the dining staff dresses better than I can, I expect that every facet of the meal with live up to that same standard. The food was: good, the service was: good, overall: just good. This restaurant has the potential to be amazing, the type of place you would go to for a milestone celebration, but everything was just a smidge off.

When I arrived, there were two hosts, one on the phone who completely did not acknowledge us (which is fine, she's on the phone), and a second one who just happened to be in the process of seating someone else. He returned after a couple of minutes, I provided him with the reservation information, and shortly after we were seated in the dining area.  

I started with the mocktail "N/A-GRONI" which was comprised of San Bitters, Grapefruit & Club Soda, if you enjoy San Pellegrino flavored sodas, you'll definitely enjoy this.

We started off with the complimentary "Angel Bread" with goat cheese butter.  The roll was delightful, warm, fluffy, sweet - a perfect foil for the earthiness of the goat cheese butter.

First lunch course was Ruby Red Shrimp, Romano Beans, Almonds, Harissa - I enjoyed the crunchiness of the beans with the almonds and the spiciness of the harissa, but sadly, the shrimp, which should have been the highlight of the dish underwhelmed me, it was just a little more well done than I prefer my shrimp to be.

Second course was pork loin, belly and sausage - nothing wrong with meat in this dish, I just wasn't inspired by this, each bite was again, just good.  The squash under the meat was a little over-ripe so the rind was a tad chewy.

After the first course, there was an inordinately long wait for the second course, so long that while we had originally planned to order dessert, we had to pass in order to make it to our next function on time (we were seated for a little over two hours). When we had finished our first course, one server hovered while waiting for other servers to become available so that our empty plates could be removed at the same time. During the attempted synchronization, one server accidentally bumped my elbow while removing a dish, he apologized, and took my empty course plate, but left my bread dish, while some of the other guests' had their bread dishes removed. Nothing to be upset about, but these tiny inconsistencies almost make this feel like a new restaurant still working on their rhythm, rather than an established experience.

Gramercy Tavern reminds me of a ballet, beautiful planned coordination and costumes, but the orchestra is just a few seconds off, rendering the entire experience palatable, but lackluster.

now THIS IS A RESTAURANT!!! I live in LA and came here to have dinner in late March when I was in NY for some theater productions. 

The place is amazing, cozy, the attention was great, the waiters were extremely nice and helpful. Now the food, the FOOD!!!!! oh my God that was as close to perfection as it gets. 

I've eaten here in LA in all sorts of places, from taco and food trucks to sketchy but well respected low key places with great food, to Michelin star awarded restaurants with pre established meals and wine pairings. But I never had an experience like I had at Gramercy Tavern.

Their food is delish, no matter what you have it'll be amazing. 

Kudos to the owners and management. Keep it up! You guys are awesome

If you have 2 hours to spare, skip the a la carte lunch in dining room and do the tasting menu.   Ever aspect of their service was impeccable; prompt, courteous, knowledgeable, and professional.  You can really tell they taking staff training extremely seriously.

Food was fantastic too.   The way they cook fish and duck meat was quite something.  They don't just cook meat; they cook it in a way that would draw out flavor.  Focus is on freshness and natural taste of ingredients and their harmony.

The price isn't cheap by any means, but lunch tasting menu is a great value for the quality of food.  I look forward to doing tasting menu for next season.

Being the first Michelin star restaurant I have been able to enjoy in my lifetime I'd say Gramercy Tavern perfectly met my expectations in terms of the dining experience. Coming from a very large family the atmosphere at Gramercy Tavern reflects just that; a cozy and inviting home setting. The restaurant's wonderful usage of warm but dim lighting gives you a sense of that cliche yet enjoyable fireplace feel. The kitchen unlike most of the restaurants I have been too sat quite open and viewable from most sections of the restaurant. The noise level is low but not ultimately quiet and it very much invokes a sense of happiness in one to hear the chit-chat and laughter of other guests around you. 

Beginning with the appetizer of smoked trout my tastebuds were delighted to not encounter the fishy taste of most restaurant-served seafood. It gracefully melts in your mouth along with the garnish of delicious scallions, kohlrabi, and roe that contrast with the smooth flavors of the fish. Stopping a second to note the amazing beverage recommendation from the waitress was a dry yet absolutely flavorful selection of Dupont, Brut de Normandie, France. Now onto the main course, the black bass, again I was met with melt-in-your-mouth quality and it was truly astounding. The rich and fresh ingredients that Gramercy Tavern uses will leave anyone astonished at how flavourful going the extra mile can be. 

Finally, the only bump in the road was the final dessert course which left me and my companion underwhelmed. We ordered the cookie plate but were disappointed to find very common-like pastries and an apple pie that did not live up to a Michelin star restaurant. 

Nonetheless, my experience with the staff and cuisine of Gramercy Tavern has put it at one of my top recommendations for anyone visiting New York that is looking for an upscale dining experience. I will without a doubt be returning to Gramercy Tavern in the future... hungry for more.

We had a lovely dinner here for our 15th anniversary. Made the reservations online. As the time got closer, they emailed me to confirm and also asked how long we had been married, any food allergies, etc. The hosts up front we're very friendly. We had to wait about 10 minutes for our table. Our server was so friendly and engaging. All the other servers who helped clear the table and bring new plates were also efficient and welcoming. They have their service well-choreographed! They started us with complimentary glasses of champagne. The amuse-bouche was awesome - we wanted more! We opted for the three course dinner which was just perfect in size after the complimentary rolls, amuse-bouche and complimentary after dinner truffles. The coconut cake and homemade granola bars were also welcome extras that topped off a lovely meal.

What a delightful place. Every member of the staff are so enthusiastic and motivated that they make the dining in experience a treasure. Food is fantastic, brilliant craft cocktails, excellent wine and beer selection. Can't beat a Danny Meyer restuarant.

Excellent food and service.  My only complaint was the broccoli salad, which at about $18, was minuscule, albeit delicious.  On the other hand, the apricot dessert was gigantic.  My swordfish was yummy, and I enjoyed the large portion of beans that came with it.  Lovely ambiance, but prices are a little high.

I don't often write reviews so I will keep this short and sweet.we had a stellar anniversary lunch here.the staff was great,we were waited in by Jason who deserves much praise.ordered 4 first course selections which were fantastic and well paced.on top of the complimentary dessert and beverage we received...they also went above and beyond to give us a sample of the lamb tartare we were asking about.being HUGE tartare fans we ordered the beef but inquired about the ingredients about the lamb and *boom* a sample was there for us.thank you for a memorable day.we will be back again

My wife has been eyeing this restaurant and since we were in the city, figured we would give Gramercy Tavern a try.  Our party was a group of 4 and we elected the tasting menu.  The food was not bad; however, nothing stood out or was remembered a day after visiting this restaurant.  

For the cost, this restaurant leaves much to be desired.

I have lived in NY for  10 years and hadn't been to Gramercy Tavern until last night. We had plans to have an appetizer in the bar area and then go elsewhere but everyone was so welcoming and accommodating from the moment we walked in we decided to stay for dinner. Alvaro and the rest of the gramercy staff gave us the best service we have ever had in an establishment. It was truly a wonderful and special experience. From the food to the wine-everything was so lovely. Thank you to the staff at gramercy tavern for such a wonderful dinner.

My husband and I have been to several Michelin Star restaurants and this definitely ranks in the top 5. I have been here twice in the last two years and tried their tasting menu both times. The service is impeccable. Totally worth the visit!

I dropped by to grab a drink here. Roger Fritz Spritz was really cool, refreshing yet not too strong. I was impressed by the great service. I could say the lighting and decor inside the place were terrific, facilitating photo shooting :)

What I ate: Three course prix fixe
Visit date: October 16, 2017
First time? Yes.
 
Gramery Tavern was definitely a highlight from my NY trip. The service was impeccable (you know you're at a legit classy restaurant when they fold your napkins if you leave your table for a minute), but also not stuffy. There is a coat check if you need it, and any leftover 'ok-to-package' desserts will be waiting for you wrapped up upon your exit from the restaurant. There is a three-course option and a seven course meal with optional wine pairings. Their only ask is that everyone at your table order either the three- or the seven- course meal because of the timing of the dishes. On this visit we enjoyed the three course prix fixe meal and the restaurant kept us on track so we would have plenty of time to head over to see a show.
 
Our meal started with an amuse bouche of biscuits with goat milk butter and cabbage salad. I started with the ricotta cavatelli which had creamy noodles with a beef bolognese, black olives, and pickled peppers. It was a bit on the salty side, but I ate the whole thing because, mmm, salt. Also, I love beef bolognese! My main course was the arctic char served medium well with celery root, quince, and delicately-placed Brussels sprouts leaves. They give you a hearty portion of salmon; I would have liked more of the accompanying items on my plate. The star of the dish: the salmon skin. It was perfectly crisp and salty. For dessert I had a trio of sorbets - raspberry, strawberry, and concord grape. They were served on a bed of cookies. Each flavor was vibrant and refreshing, but also very sweet. I also had a ginger swizzle and hot mint tea to wash down all the good food. To finish, our meal came with petit fours - two kinds of chocolatey bon bons. One was reminiscent of a PB&J and the other had fantastic crisps inside. We also were given a special Gramercy Tavern granola bar for later.
 
My friend had the butternut squash soup, pork loin & belly, and cookie plate. She loved everything and even got to take home the leftover cookies. 
 
This is a great place to celebrate a milestone occasion or for a just-because night out. Let them know if you're celebrating a birthday, too - they give you a mini cake!

Solid spot in NYC.
Sure you've heard of this place and wondered is it worth it? The answer is simply yes.

I came in after some work to have lunch on a weekday. No line, no wait so I thought closed but I had checked and the hours said open.  Come around closer to 2pm and the place is yours (well, sort of there's people but you can get a seat).

I chose to sit at the bar which was filled with a great variety of people from all over - locals and travellers.

The bartender was awesome. She knew her drinks and was very helpful. Really wish I remembered her name but she was professional and seemed to know the regulars.

House made bread to start. I can't remember the cocktail I had but delicious! I went with the broccoli soup and lamb sandwich she recommended. It was tender and flavourful. The soup was amazing!

I sat there thoroughly food satisfied.

So far one of my favourite lunch spots!
The food may not be the best, but the staff is extra attentive and that makes up for it.

This is a favorite stop of mine every time I come to NYC.  Extremely welcoming staff, great food, great service and a warm and welcoming decor.  We didn't have a reservation the fine dining area (need to reserve about a month in advance), so we had a cocktail and waited for a table in the bar area. Didn't take too long.  Excellent cocktail, nice vibe, delicious food.  Note: there is not tipping here (included in the price of the food/drink), the result is a staff that goes out of their way to make you happy and feel welcome.  Great place.

This is a 4.5. It's one of my favorite places to sit, have a beautiful glass of wine and a bit to eat. I need to have my adult pants on as it's not somewhere I would go if I were in sneakers and ripped jeans ( running errands dress code) it gets busy after 5p so snagging a crucial seat is all about timing. The bar menu is very good. More men than women but not the type trying to " buy you a drink."

Absolute quality and excellence in everything, from the location to the venue to the service to the drinks to the food and so on and so forth.
