We doubled up on the chicken, and while I know you're not supposed to get chicken when it costs the same as the sea bass, this was a good decision. The chicken was phenomenal--I'm not sure how the breast was cooked, but the thigh was fried like karaage, and both were super juicy and flavorful. It came with tarragon, carrots, and snappy summer beans.

We ordered four desserts, and Aimee threw in a fifth just for good measure. My favorite was the sweet corn cake, a moist, crumbly cake golden with corn and butter, served with corn ice cream, goat cheese whipped cream, blackberries, blueberry basil jam, and toffee popped sorghum. The Bakewell tart was a close second, the pastry crust dense and buttery, loaded with strawberries, white chocolate, and almonds. It came with a quenelle of strawberry sorbet. I also enjoyed the pavlova, an impressive igloo of meringue filled with mahleb ice cream, finished with sesame and sour cherry. The chocolate hazelnut custard was nice, too, with vanilla cream and apricot jam. The milk and cookie plate was on the house, and it was cute and deeply satisfying. There were two fresh, fat cookies, white almond fudge and chocolate hazelnut, and a tiny mason jar of sweet milk.

We were sent off with luscious cherry basil bon bons and almond caramels, and house granola bars for breakfast. This was a grand meal, with top notch service and wonderful food. I get why Gramercy Tavern is so iconic. It has staying power--it was old when I went in 2009, and I expect it'll still be there nine years from now.

I have always wanted to try Gramercy Tavern to see if they really live up to their high ratings, and they do! Thanks to Alessandra, our private event was organized well within the short period of time we had given her. The service was spectacular, and I honestly think that makes a huge difference. The portion sizes of our three course menu was large enough to make us all quite full. The bread was delicious and served warm. Each dish was presented very well and the timing of the dishes was spaced out perfectly, so that we didn't feel rushed whatsoever. And the flavors in each dish paired so well with each other - duck breast with strawberries and beets. I would say the appetizers and entrees tasted better than the desserts overall, but the chocolate custard dessert was very good.

One of NYC best - full stop. Great food, great service, great ambiance, great location. Finally got around to having the burger - as good as promised. Kicked things off with a greenmarket Tomato and Stone Fruit Salad- peak season goodness. Go. Just go.

I made a reservation here for lunch. My boyfriend and I decided on both getting the daily special. It was one of the most delicious meals that we've had in quite some time. We moved to NYC a few months ago and this was our favorite meal so far. Trying to check out as many Michelin Star restaurants as we can before we move. The flounder was cooked perfectly, a melt in your mouth dish. The sorbet was refreshing despite not being a fan of blackberries but they were perfectly ripe. We ended up with two extra desserts, the baklava and chocolate torte/mousse. They were perfection. We both couldn't stop commenting on how much we loved the experience. The manager stopped at our table and see how we liked the meal. I would definitely go back and take my family. Absolutely deserving of its one Michelin Star.

Fantastic. Each time that I have dined at (Gramercy Tavern it has been amazing. Best restaurant in NY and the World. I have been all over the world and have tasted excellent food but nothing tops the food and service at Gramercy Tavern!!!!!

Delicious food, great service, nice ambiance.

We arrived on a Friday evening for an early dinner, and we had several different dishes throughout the meal, all of which were excellent. The meat was prepared excellently and was very tasty, while the sea bream and the tagliatelle dishes were also very flavorful. The service was very helpful throughout the meal, and it's a nice place to enjoy a fancy meal.

I walked out of GT with a huge grin on my face and a full stomach. Great hospitality, great food, great ambiance...it's a great restaurant! The menu items are seasonal so there's something different to try when you visit. I can't wait to come back again!

The Tasting Menu is overpriced. Service, appetizers, and desserts were spectacular but the entree was seriously underwhelming. For $129, I expected more than a flavorless slice of a chicken breast. I cannot recommend this place.

Great service. The mix of flavors was well thought out and everything was delicious. 
They sure pay attention to the details. 
Tried the seasonal tasting menus and loved every bite. All the courses were well thought out, and the flavors complemented each other.

Pretty place and with bar & table seating. Food was very good but wish they mentioned more what they had drizzle on my zucchini flatbread. ( had maybe a kick to it I wasn't expecting ..) Burgers and chips 
were very good as well as the other apps/ entrees we all had.

Gramercy Tavern sure lived up to the hype! There were four in our party and we opted to go with the prix-fixe menu on the dining room. The selections were interesting and each member of our party raved about their food. First course - tomato salad (2) and buccatini (2). Though the tomatoes were fabulous, the buccatini was the clear winner. Second course - lamb (2), halibut, striped bass. This was a tougher race. The halibut and striped bass were out of this world, but I think I'd call the bass the winner. I can't stop thinking about it!! Dessert was so delicious. We had the vanilla rice pudding (2), cookie plate, and chocolate hazelnut mousse. I cannot pick a winner. All were outstanding. We ordered seven drinks total and they were all fabulous (wine, bourbon, cocktail). Overall the service was good. We only had to wait a few minutes to be seated and we did have a bit of a lag between the entree and dessert courses. Our waitress was knowledgeable and friendly. Ambiance was spot-on. Overall, a truly fabulous dining experience. It was crazy expensive ($734) but worth it.

We came for our anniversary and loved the experience! We sat in the main dining room with the white tablecloths and a serene atmosphere (quite different from the tavern near the street). The space had an aire of a moody napa winery, a nice change from the NYC scene-y restaurants.

We were greeted at our table with a complimentary glass of bubbly (can't remember if it was champagne or prosecco). We each got the seasonal tasting menu with the wine pairings: I think the most inventive dish was first one: the cucumber soup served cold with shrimp was a taste I wasn't expecting and one I'll never forget...sooo good! Everything else was tasty and fresh but not boundary-breaking.

The service was what you'd expect from a Michelin starred restaurant but without too many frills. We'd definitely come here again and would recommend it to anyone looking for an elevated food experience.

Food: 3 stars
Service: 1 star

This review is mainly about their service and my experience ordering the restaurant's vegan options.

The service is very friendly, but so, so, so slow. Yes, I ordered a tasting menu, which is expected to take a while. But we were at the restaurant for over 2.5 hours by the time I asked for the check. Between servings there was an incredible amount of downtime and by the end of the meal no one was coming to the table to check on us. I believe we were the last seating for lunch (2 PM) though we were actually seated by 1:45 PM, so it's possible they were tied up preparing for dinner service, but my service as a patron shouldn't suffer because of that. I'd be more forgiving of a non-Michelin starred restaurant. 

My boyfriend and I came here for the lunch service on a Saturday. I am vegan; he is not. I asked the waiter what on the menu can be made vegan and was directed to the vegetarian tasting menu with modifications; the only other choice was the tomato salad appetizer without cheese. It took a very long time for the waiter to get back to me to let me know what my substitutions would be. Well, one of the more filling dishes (a pasta dish with cheese) would be substituted with a melon salad, and the cheesecake substituted with sorbet (which is available on the regular menu). Seemed like a big tradeoff not worthy of an $80 pricetag but whatever, I went for it. Well, I was lucky that they were able to bring us unlimited bread.

None of my food "wowed" me. Again, I'd be more forgiving of a non-Michelin star restaurant. I was particularly disappointed with my melon salad substitution (literally just chunks of cantaloupe with a sprinkle of mint and peppers) and the roasted eggplant. The eggplant was so salty that it made my mouth hurt, and I enjoy salty food. The sorbet was also very bland, and the cherry flavor was so sour it was practically inedible but maybe it just wasn't my particular cup of tea; I'm more upset about the blandness of the strawberry and blackberry flavors. Nothing was bad or gross, just overall uninteresting. 

For what it's worth, my boyfriend absolutely loved the burger he ordered and said it was probably the best burger he's ever had.

Had a wonderful lunch there earlier in the week. Food was exceptional, including the bread on the table and the complementary sparkling water. Everything was extremely fresh and nothing was over seasoned, they really let the food do the talking. I will be in that area again next month and will certainly have lunch there again.

I realize that I mostly use Yelp to send bad reviews so I wanted to add a positive one.  This place is great - expensive but worth it.  The bar is pleasant, the dining room is large, and noisy (like most Manhattan restaurants) but not so noisy you can't hear your dinner companions.  It seems warm and welcoming.  They have a no-tipping philosophy, which is interesting, and they must reward the staff because all staff was friendly and helpful.  
Our waiters were there when we needed something but not hovering.  Delightful.   The evening starts with a small amuse-Bouche.  Ours was a watermelon gazpacho, refreshing and delicious.  The rolls that came were light, fluffy and warm, served with goat cheese butter.  Yummy. 

We had the tagliatelle, it came bathed in a creamy sauce with just a hint of warm spices and small bits of bacon and summer squash.  The main course of flounder was cooked to flaky perfection with a crispy golden coat.   The fish was accompanied by fresh corn and tiny tomatoes, a delicious end-of-summer combination.  Dessert was a huge serving of fruit - tiny strawberrries, fresh peaches, a scoop of sorbet and a bit of rice pudding.  

All was delicious.  The wine list seems expensive, but then we remember the no tipping, and it lines up with other fine dining restaurants in NYC.

So - save up and go, it is worth the tab.. .

The service was absolutely impeccable - One of the best restaurant services I have ever had. 
We had the three course pre-fixed. Smoked Arctic char is delicious and well presented. Pork chop is great, but not as tender as I would like. Dessert was also great (great portion).
Overall a very positive experience. Way to go for an American restaurant to go non-tipping!

Darling restaurant and impeccable service! Love the bar area. The main dining area is very intimate and cozy. The six course seasonal menu was tasty and beautifully presented. But portions were very small. Even after a couple delicious brioche between the courses, my wife and I were still hungry at the end of the six courses meal.  Good place for a date, as long as you don't come in starving...
Great food as always!  Service was wonderful. Price drinks are still way high. Especially for a local can of Brooklyn Brewery beer.

If I could give infinite stars, I would! I decided to pick Gramercy Tavern for a very special 1 yr anniversary dinner. I contemplated on picking through the many NYC restaurants! I thought the menu, atmosphere, and attention to detail was everything I could imagine. 

To start, the restaurant called a few days ahead of time to ask whether about the  special occasion and any questions/clarifications about the menu . As we were seated, we were given complimentary and delicious champagne. We ordered the vegetarian tasting menu. Everything in this menu was delicious - even the palette cleansing tomato sorbet. We had a great salad with tomato broth with the perfect flavor, amazing tortellini tenderly cooked, and ending with the strawberry creme brûlée cheesecake (yum). We were completely stuffed, but they also provided us a coconut cake. Overall, Gramercy Tavern created an unforgettable meal and night! I will be back to celebrate the best occasions.

Had dinner here last night with two other couples.  In a business capacity.  In other words someone else was picking up the bill.  Thank goodness because this place is not cheap.  It's lovely inside - a bit quirky- not modern or trendy- lots of dried flowers and flowery country themed decor- but a nice feel.  Like you are in France 
The food was yummy.  Had a raw fish appetizer and then a roasted fish as a main. Both super delicious but definitely NOT big portions. The menu is a bit limiting in the sense that you either do the price fixed or the "left page"from which you choose three things.  Does not seem to be an ala cart.  Starter, main, dessert. 
The service is a bit old fashioned and frankly I found it a bit aggressive in one way yet slow in another way  plus... service is always included apparently ...no incentive for them to be fab?
Everyone else seemed to really enjoy their food. My husband had the lamb which I tried and loved .
Decent wine selection by glass and bottle. 
I would race back if someone else was paying but would be hard pressed to go on my own dime. Just too many other great choices.
I took mom here for lunch. Food was very refresh. Service was beyond amazing. Mom loved it! Thanks
This place is a must do in NYC for dinner. Make reservations and sit in the dining room. Great service and food. Loved the rice pudding dessert!

Seriously LOVED this restaurant... my boyfriend and I decided to visit after it was mentioned on Gossip Girl  It ended up being wonderful and one of my favorite restaurants in NY! The vibes are so cozy and warm. We came 45 minutes early to enjoy the bar setting (try the little bird, seriously) and then we were seated at EXACTLY our reservation time. I loved our waitress, she was so informative regarding the menu. There were SO many courses, we left the restaurant feeling very full and satisfied !! Definitely same room for the cookie platter dessert. Only downside? It's pricey. Go for a special occasion and you won't regret breaking the bank.

It is not surprising that the Gramercy Tavern is consistently voted the most popular restaurant in NYC. I had to deploy all my charm to book a table ;-) The neo-colonial decor is perfect, warm and welcoming; the service is attentive without being invasive. The food is close to divine: a wonderfully original beetroot, blackberries, hazelnuts and pancetta salad for starters, and a lamb loin cooked to perfection, accompanied by a fine merguez sausage, broccoli rabe and ricotta on grilled sourdough as the main course. The cheese platter did not disappoint. The wine list is good; my only small complaint is that it could be a little more extensive in the choices offered, but this is just me being pedantic! This delightful restaurant is now definitely in my New York trifeca!
Best meal we have had.  The bar waitstaff was amazing, each dish better than the previous and the dessert put everything over the top.  Eat here, at the bar, well worth the wait!

We went for dinner with son and fiancee. Wonderful food, beautifully presented. Excellent service and atmosphere. Rob, our waiter was one of the best, most helpful and entertaining waiters I've ever had anywhere.

We have been dining at Gramercy Tavern for about seven years. We always celebrate birthdays and anniversaries here because of the stellar service and Michelin-1star quality experience for the price tag. We have never been disappointed. Every dish is expertly crafted. Service is thoughtful and deliberate. Truly a pleasure to spend an evening here.

There are essentially two parts of the restaurant - the front is a more casual dining hall and the back a more formal experience. We sat in the back and had the set 6 course non-vegetarian menu. The menu is seafood heavy. 

Our first two courses were fantastic - the scallops were well balanced by the acidity of the tomatoes and cherries. The shrimp and grits were amazing (the shrimp was cooked to perfection). Though the halibut was cooked perfectly tender, I was underwhelmed by the visual aspect and seasoning, both of which were one-toned. The lobster and squid ink lumache is decent - slightly lack luster for this category of restaurant. The duck was well seasoned but very tough. The dessert (vanilla yogurt mousse) was creamy and decadent. 

I was initially put off by the service, as there were several quirky comments made by our waitstaff. The food overall was satisfactory. I would recommend trying this in spite of the service, although given some deficiencies I would probably recommend ordering the a la carte rather than this specific seasonal menu.
Unmemorable food, slow service, and outrageous wine prices. Nice atmosphere.  NYC is loaded with wonderful restaurants that charge half as much and have better food.

Everytime I'm here Iam constantly reminded why I love this place so much. The seafood and array of wines are the main selling point. I enjoy sitting at the bar if it is just two people. Make sure to reserve a spot because they are always busy.

Historical restaurant with a good locals vibe.  The front of the restaurant has a bar food menu while the back has an old New York feel and a  more formal menu.  The wait staff was fantastic and fun and the food was well executed and delicious.  The amuse bouche and the sweets at the end of dessert were touches of elegance that were impressive and very much appreciated.  The wine that was recommended to go with all the different meals ordered at our table: the 2 different fish dishes, as well as the lamb and my pork dish, was fabulous and delicious-- who knew Patagonia, Argentina made an excellent Pinot noir??
Overall, a fun, fulfilling evening with excellent ambience, well executed dishes, and a great new wine discovery!

What a great place and what a wonderful experience. 

Your staff is well-trained and so helpful and friendly. The pre-meal soup taste was an exquisite touch. The food was perfect, the portions perfect, the ambiance was excellent. You deserve more than five stars.

My birthday cake was cute and delicious.

Just one wow after another. Keep up the great work.

Last night I was a guest at a table for 6 and came away very disappointed as I was from two prior visits. I can't help but compare it to a wonderful meal I had recently at the Union Square Cafe. The highlight last night was  the Sommelier who  was very helpful. We had a wonderful rose champagne and then a super tuscan that was delicious.The good news ends there.
 I find the staff abrupt and condescending from the waiter warning us that we all had to select the three  course or seven course menu in the most unfriendly way to the coat check person who refused my help with six umbrellas but then couldn't find them.
 The kale salad was too salty as was the lobster broth surrounding the fish entree.
 My smoked trout was flavorless. I think it was intended to be a presentation of subtle flavors but it didn't work as there was nothing to distinguish it. The papardelle ragu was tasty but too watery. The other dishes were fine and the desserts very well done. For $1500 I expected to be impressed

Beautiful and cozy bar/restaurant with amazing floral arrangements. The menu is concise and informative. I chose the seasonal squash salad which was breathtaking. My sausage entree was like no other. The Sazarac Rye whisky was perfectly mixed. Love this place

Excellent experience dining in the Tavern (less formal) area while traveling for business.  Very attentive service...and superb food.  Bread was very tasty to start...monkfish entree was a generous portion and was very favorable with creative presentation.  Inventive cocktail.  I would return if back in New York.
All in all five star experience! Danny Meyer was there with friends when we were there and was very nice to chat with!

They canceled my Dining Room reservation made through open table without my knowledge.  They said they called to confirm buy I never received call or vm. 
I called to confirm on the day of our dinner and was told they canceled my birthday dinner...thanks
I'd suggest Call these turds to confirm or they will cancel you. 
"They take the reservation, but they can't keep the reservation"....Seinfeld

Checking this off my bucket list. 3 coarse prefix dinner in the dining room. I was expecting to be blown away by the food and flavor profiles and presentation but I wasn't. First coarse smoked trout. The prettiest of the dishes, delicate tasty. Second coarse pork loin and belly, bland and sad presentation. Third coarse cookies and milk, 2 thick cookies with more of a cake consistency.. these did not work for me. This place is so hyped up as one of the top fine dining restaurants in nyc. I wasn't impressed.

Beautiful, cozy brunch place. Amazing service and food was top notch. Not a bad seat in the house and waitstaff is attentive and doesn't rush you out despite being a popular place. Love the decor. Can't wait to come back!
Duck meatballs were some of the best things I've ever tasted. Definitely dress up a little when you are here or else you will feel frumpy because everyone is very put together. Very attentive staff.

Given that Gramercy Tavern was pretty packed and we did not have a reservation, we appreciated the option they provided to call us when our table was ready. We didn't wait for long at a nearby Starbucks before getting the call.

The bread was okay here, but the food and cocktails were solid. The fried rice was rich and crispy, the duck was done two ways - as a sausage and a breast with mixed greens, the fish was tasty and served with fried shallots over a bed of dressed vegetables, and the donuts were as you would hope them to be - light and fluffy. The chocolate pudding dessert, however, was out of this world. They didn't blow my mind enough to come back, but this struck me as one of those classic NYC restaurants that simply does good food well.

Lunch at this long established Manhattan favorite was delicious. The atmosphere in this great restaurant is fabulous whether dining at a table or at the bar. Well staffed with a terrific bartender and amazing drinks, we had a lovely time!

This place is hands down one of the best restaurants in NYC.  Despite all of the amazing food options in the city, I just keep finding myself coming back here.  Whether you are in the bar or the main dinning room, the food and cocktails never disappoint.  The staff is always delightful and does their best to accommodate you even if you don't have a reservation.  It's not inexpensive by any means, but definitely worth every dollar!

Gramercy Tavern was a pleasurable experience, I had the vegetarian tasting menu, the service was good and i had no complains, they had no fresh juices on the menu but they gave me an orange juice

Bread - 4/5
First course - clary root - 1/5
Second course - cauliflower soup - 4/5
Third course - campanella pasta was delicious - 4/5
Fourth course - carrots were good but the other thing was just not fully cooked 3/5
Fifth course - wild hazelnut desert was average 3/5

The apple sorbet was 1/5 and the pumpkin chocolate was 4/5

Overall - 3.5/5 but rounding up

I had high expectations for Gramercy Tavern after reading all the great reviews online. My lunch here, however, turned out to be just an average experience. Scallops were fresh and seasoned well, but then the sea bass was simply boring. The fish itself was pretty bland and the sauce a bit too salty. Would not recommend. Service was attentive though.
Service was excellent. Burger was divine. Beware--it is rare.

Crowded.  A bit loud.  Had the seasonal pice fixed menu with the wine pairings.  Food was really, really good.  Portions are small. Service was decent but spotty at times. Wine pairings were ok, pours were anemic and poorly timed with the meal. Yikes!!! The sommelier was less than engaged and appeared over taxed.  For $700 for two people you could do much better. All in all solid but for the money not worth it for sure.

Stellar as always. Celebrating a special friend's birthday who has a busy schedule. They worked with me to plan a very special evening even though they were fully booked. Victor is a lovely person who is so respectful of your requests ... he is divine. And of course the food is impeccable and delicious. The house made kombucha is swoon-worthy. It is the meal of dreams ... with a candle that makes your every wish come true.

Sat at the bar.  Ordered the burger, was so so.  Not worth the price and hype.  Better burger  at a traditional pub.  The desert we ordered had caramel popcorn, awful.  Being creative is important, but the flavors have to come together. Service was good, the bar is a frenzy for seats. Not relaxing.  It's more of a pub with overpriced food and decor

Such an amazing and memorable meal. The service rivals any I have ever had, and the food was incredible. The fall cocktail was also delicious, as was the bread and butter (could literally melt away in that), and the complimentary extras (truffles, appetizer). I had the pappardelle, lamb loin, and red wine pears for dessert (with Stilton ice cream that was to die for). Overall incredible impressed with my experience - this will definitely be my go-to fancy / celebration restaurant from now on.

The problem with this review is I can only award 5 stars. Quite simply the best meal I've ever had and that is by no means an easy task given meals I've had at the French Laundry, Restaurant Gordon Ramsay, Le Manoir, Marcus Waring Petrus and The Square in London.

I opted for the tasting menu with wine flight, not one single course could have had anything added to make it any better. The balance of flavours, portion size, weight of each course was perfect.

Each course got better and better and a standing joke with my server, Lara,  was that there was no way the next course could beat the last, it did, for eight courses! The standout being the Agnolotti pasta, I'd eat that every day given the chance. Innovative ideas such as strawberry jam with goats cheese work yet you would never imagine it. A pre dessert of apple sorbet with olive oil and fennel sounded so wrong yet tasted so right and left me wondering how the hell they came up with such a brilliant creation.

The wine flight was on point, interesting, exceptional well matched, perfect temperature and delicious. The sommelier is off the scale, his description of wines and reasoning why make this man worth his weight in gold

The world is a big place, with tens of thousands of restaurants, if there is one that is better I'll challenge you to try Gramercy Tavern and then give me your opinion, simply sensational.

Point to note that the food was equally matched by the service, the delectable Lara was so hospitable, so many restaurants fail when the food is so good but Lara was the perfect host, well done Lara, you were outstanding and made the meal experience even better.

What a horrific experience.  I brought my dearest friends to my "favorite restaurant in NYC."  I've eaten at GT for 15 years.  We left hungry and I paid a $1,000 bill.  Not one 'oooh or aaah' about the food.  The food was mediocre and the server was both snarky and inattentive.  We had 6 people delivering the food to the table at once, but no one that cared about our dining experience.  

It's tragic to say it, but I think the Gramercy era has ended.  I won't be returning.  

Folks, a $50 appetizer and an $85 entree do NOT cut it.   No way, no how.

You can either enjoy an a la cart menu in the tavern or a tasting menu in the main dining room. I recommend coming in for lunch and sitting in the tavern at the bar and getting the delicious burger! One of my favorite burgers in NYC! If you are celebrating or want to treat yourself then sit in the dining room and experience the full tasting menu! The service is amazing! Also hospitality is included!

I'm not sure if I can really add to the reviews here and make a difference in anyone's viewpoint, but I'll try...

We were visiting for a very short trip and I had reservations at a few spots for Friday night dinner and couldn't decide which one to use.  I hadn't eaten at Gramercy Tavern before, and was worried it wouldn't live up to the hype.  I should not have been worried - Gramercy was a stand out!

We were late to our reservation, so considering they give away your table if you haven't confirmed by noon day of, I was concerned.  I called and let them know, and they could not have been nicer.  Thankfully our very lost uber managed to regain his sense of direction and we were only 20 minutes late (an eternity in restaurant reservation times....).

We quickly had our coats taken care of and were off to our table.  We had a perfect spot in a little corner, near the liveliness of the tavern area, but in a slightly more quiet and cozy spot.

Warmly greeted, we spent forever contemplating the menu options...it was between the 3-course and the seasonal tasting menu.  We were debating if it was better to get the 3-course and get totally different items (to try more...) vs the larger menu.  In the end, the descriptions of the items not the seasonal menu sounded too good to pass up.  I also elected for the wine pairings.

We started with marinated scallops.  Oh wow.  Fresh and lively...I wanted to eat it with a giant spoon and ask for 4 more servings...On to himachi and more scallops and lobster and steak...and a number of perfect things in between...Everything was wonderful.  You know how sometimes on tasting menus, there are a few flops?  Well, there weren't any flops here.  I wanted to order another round to get more tastes.  Each course was more delicious than the next!  Even the palate cleanser was amazing!

For dessert, our server nicely chose two different desserts so we could try both.  The hazelnut one and the fruit vanilla mousse thing (I clearly remembered the descriptions well..haha) were wonderful.  

The wine pairings were unique and different and complemented the food well.  I enjoyed the descriptions of each of them and I thought that the amount of wine and variety was perfect.  While I wouldn't mind more tastes of each, this was perfect to accompany the food and not be sooo much wine.  

The atmosphere was both cozy and remarkable in that it was so approachable and fun, but also clearly fine dining.  Sometimes you lose the cozy with the fine dining, but Gramercy is able to do both well.  Also, the flower arrangement on the bar was a standout - wow!

Service was impeccable and everyone there seemed so happy to be there!  There's nothing that puts a damper on dinner like crabby waitstaff...and this is a spot where everyone was pleasant and seemed happy.  Either they are or they are really good actors, but in any case, they made it a warm and pleasurable spot to eat.

Everything was perfect!  It's expensive, but quality and taste are outstanding.  I can't say enough good things - we had an amazing time!

In the words of Phil Collins, "I've been waiting for this moment, for all my life, oh Lord."

Gramercy Tavern has been on my foodie bucket list for nearly 20 years. Finally, I can check this one off my list.

My friend and I had reservations in the main dining room for lunch. They offered an al a carte menu, but my server convinced me to go for the Vegetarian Tasting Menu. It actually didn't take that much convincing because 5 courses for $79 is a real bargain. (By the way, I count dessert as a course). My friend ordered The Daily for $48 which included 3 courses.

Here's how I graded each dish:
Angel biscuits A
Jalapeño corn biscuit A+
Tomato soup C-

Corn tortellini A
Roasted eggplant B-
Sea bass A-
Caramel cheesecake B

This is a non-tipping establishment, but that did not impact their service. Our server was unpretentious and very attentive. The restaurant itself had a very cozy feel to it. I was not expecting that at all! There's not even an official dress code, although business casual is preferred during lunch. 

I'm looking forward to my next visit, where I'm definitely getting their famous $38 burger.

Have been here several times. Always the most lovely service. 
I don't do meat but every once in a while I'll eat fish. This is the pace to do it. 
Wine list here is killer and the desserts.....do not skip the desserts!!!

This was another bucket list place on the NYC trip.  I've been a big Danny Meyer fan since I read his book years ago.

We stopped in for lunch.  It's a warm, inviting décor.  We were seated in the dining room.  We decided on the burger and a pappardelle.  
The pasta was actually an appetizer, but it was sufficient for a light lunch course.  The pasta was cooked perfectly.  The burger was juicy and tasty - a bit greasy though.  You can tell they add a lot of butter to the buns and patty.  

Regardless, the service was absolutely impressive.  From the host, to the waiter, to all the other staff.  I've been to several Three Michelin Star restaurants, but Gramercy Tavern might top them all.  This place is worth going to for the service experience alone. 

The best way to describe it is: you leave the restaurant smiling.

I would definitely come back.

They deserve 5 stars strictly for the dessert alone, but overall definitely a 5 star experience! We came after dinner from another place just to have the famous dessert- and it did not disappoint! The restaurant is beautifully decorated, very warm and inviting. We got seated at the bar quickly and we're waited on immediately by the nicest bartender. Their dessert menu changes seasonally but they have some staples that are always there too. 

We got something that blew my mind! Coconut, chocolates, custard, creme- there were so many components, flavors and textures- it was unreal. 

I haven't tried the food here, but if it's anything like the dessert, I would trust that it'll satisfy.
Wish I could eat here everyday! Their food and service are so amazing and its worth every penny, I mean, every hundreads...

Exceptional service!  Fare is palate pleasing.  Staff is very friendly and attentive!!  
Highly recommended!!!!

Excellent staff, service, and ambience. The bar staff is on their game, with great recommendations, efficient and professional/courteous service, even when very busy. Great wine and cider list, and amazing food. Definitely recommended! Alissa and Rick at the bar are above and beyond and totally worth going back for.
Lunch, Nov 2018. Perfectly good. Wood-fired grill is lovely. But not transporting. Just very good.

The service was great and the food was Stellar..My boyfriend and I went for brunch and we loved it. 
Thanks Monica

Upscale tavern. Food was good, but not worth the $$$$. The angel bread with goat cheese flavored butter was amazing, the beet salad and shrimp appetizer were delicious. I had the lamb for dinner and it was a very small portion and totally flavorless. I was disappointed with the main course. Desert was sold as more appetizing than in real life.
I tried the baklava ice cream, caramelized cheese cake, and apple upside down cake as well as poached pair. My favorite was the cheesecake.

The decor of the restaurant was very nice. I especially appreciated the flowers and ceiling decorations. 

Service was great as the servers always filled your water but we're not in your face too much.

We came here for our anniversary dinner- since it's quite the splurge and we've considered coming here for a while. We did the tasting menu and the accompanying wine flight.

The atmosphere was beautiful and decorated very nicely. We were seated off to the side near the service area which didn't have as nice of an ambience but was still comfortable. I would recommend requesting a table in the main central room.

The service was very good, as is expected at a fine dining establishment. The food was delicious and so was the wine although we were not blown away at the value for the money. We have had several other meals at other nice restaurants for a much lower price point. We likely won't be returning with all of the options for dining in NYC but it was definitely good to try it out.

Gramercy Tavern missed the mark on our recent visit, which I found particularly disappointing because I loved Union Square Cafe.  

We dined in the dining room, and opted for the 3-course prix-fixe menu.  While the service was very good, the food was unremarkable and in my opinion below-average for a restaurant of this caliber.  

My wife and I both agreed that the first course was the best of the meal.  The shrimp were perfectly cooked and served with creamy polenta, and my wife thoroughly enjoyed her tartare.  For the second course, the lamb was disappointing: the flavors were bland and the loin was borderline tough.  My wife's sea bass was just okay.  For dessert, while I enjoyed my cheesecake, I have had much better ones at other restaurants.  My wife had similar feelings about her custard - good but not exceptional.   

Although the food could have been better, the cocktails were very good and the wine recommendations were excellent.  The dining room  decor is beautiful, and the restaurant was already tastefully decorated for the holidays when we visited.

I've been to few restaurants that I would classify as life changing. Gramercy Tavern blew my expectations away. It made me feel like I had flew into an alternative universe where everything was remarkable and sprinkled with a little magic. 

The dining room is beautiful. The service is top notch. The food is so elaborate and well executed that it will have your brain feel like it will explode due to over satisfaction. 

Order things you wouldn't ordinarily eat. Trying new things here will enhance your life. I drank wine from Greece, and ate all sorts of things I would never ordinarily try and it opened me up as a person. It showed me that levels of food bliss exist that I could have never dreamed of.

Thank you GT for such a beautiful experience.

Ok, so Gramercy Tavern might be my favorite restaurant in the city. I remember coming here for the first time while visiting NYC and being beyond words at the food, service, and atmosphere. I love everything Danny Meyer (Shake Shack!!!) and this is no exception. While I haven't tried his other restaurants (apart from Shake Shack obviously)... yet... I'm excited to over the next few months to see how they compare to my original Danny Meyer restaurant, Gramercy Tavern.

Ok, so first the food. Not much to say here except it is just excellent. I highly recommend the tasting menu in the dining room, but have also done ale carte which was great, too (tried the chicken sandwich a few weeks ago and YUM).

What really sets Gramercy Tavern apart is the service and, as Danny Meyer would say, hospitality. It's all of the unexpected and likely noticed by many of their guests, that place Gramercy Tavern on a different level from most other restaurants. From the way the staff queues their colleagues to gracefully remove plates from your table in an orchestrated sweeping almost single movement (it's something!) to always being aware of every guest's needs... it's so impressive. Small things like walking to the bathroom and a server immediately recognizing what you're looking for and showing you the way... or calling to confirm a reservation and giving you a heads up of the tasting menu price... little things that make such a great experience.

I'm always excited to bring visitors from out of town to Gramercy Tavern... just excellent!

We had a great time for drinks and snacks at the bar on a Sunday night.  Our timing was perfect to secure three seats in the very busy bar area.   Our cocktails were very inventive and tasty.  The bar snacks and the entire bar menu was interesting and delicious.   We had smashed potatoes, corned beef flatbread and smoked fish dip.  All were great bargains and really great.  We come here often and are never disappointed.

Had a "treat yoself" lunch here and loved it. I had done some research on restaurants known for their holiday decorations, and I saw a lot of recommendations for Gramercy Tavern. I came on December 1, and the decor did not disappoint. It's not as over the top as Rolf's, but it's got the cozy holiday vibe that makes you feel as if you're in someone's grand living room for Christmas. I believe the trees and wreaths are all real (according to our server). 

We arrived about 5 min after our reservation, and after coat check, we were led to our seats right away in the Dining Room (a la carte lunch menu). Our server was lovely and recommended the Blackfish, which I ordered (also ordered the Fall Classic cocktail and the scallops to start). 

The Fall Classic cocktail was delicious. A little sweet and deceivingly strong! It paired well with lunch. If you're a fan of seafood, you have to order the scallops and Blackfish. The scallops literally melted so easily in my mouth--so sad that there was only three pieces! The Blackfish was also great--didn't necessarily "melt" in the same way as the scallops, but it was light and cooked perfectly. We ordered the caramelized cheesecake for dessert, which we devoured pretty quickly because it was that good.

Excellent, delicious fine dining experience at Michelin star Gramercy Tavern. My bf brought me here for my birthday recently. The space is gigantic and classy, filled to the brim with people. There were groups of friends, large families, dates. Several servers will be running around constantly. Oddly, we were able to retain conversation and forgot how incredibly busy the rest of the place was. If Gramercy Tavern isn't doing something right, I have no clue what that is. 

The dinner experience in the main dining room, which constitutes most of the space, offers a pre fixe menu. It consists of seasonal, vegetable or standard three course. I of course opted for seasonal ($184 pp). Everything off the menu sounded incredible. Menu items as listed: 

Marinated Hamachi
Roasted Scallops
Smoked Char
Sweet Potato Agnolotti
Duck Breast
Vanilla Yogurt Mousse
(some amuse bouche and complimentary desserts included)

The seafood here is excellent, and if you're a seafood lover like me, you can't go wrong with their fall seasonal menu. The meaty duck breast that followed is tender and juicy. For dessert, my bf had the mousse while I substituted mine with three cheeses that vary from funky to creamy - Casatica/water buffalo, Comté/raw cow, and Willoughby/washed rind cow. I must note the cocktails are also great, and it so happened to be the last day of cider week. I chose a wonderful cider flight to complement my seafood in the beginning. While portions seem small in appearance, don't be fooled. I was stuffed by the end. Just when I thought dinner was over though, I was brought out a coconut meringue surprise cake, birthday candle included. The words, Happy Birthday Sara, was beautifully written on the plate. If you want to impress anyone for their birthday with good food, service, and ambience, need I tell you more about Gramercy Tavern.

I had a wonderful time here. I would absolutely return, but I see it as the place for special occasions; it's very classy and upscale yet not pretentious and stuffy. As for service, while servers are bustling non stop, it's in ninja style. I hardly noticed them add water to my cup or clear out the dinner tables next to us. Our server was friendly and explained things off the menu. The food was excellent. I loved the seafood dishes in particular. If you prefer something more casual, the 'tavern' (bar) offers afternoon and evening à la carte. Thank you Gramercy Tavern for making this birthday incredibly memorable.

Great service and ambience. However, food was mediocre. I ordered a fish entree(don't remember its exact name) and it tasted like the grilled fish you can get at any other restaurant offering American cuisine, probably even worse. For what I pay, this is not good value.

Came here on my lunch break with a colleague. Beautiful place with impeccable service. My colleague ordered the burger and I ordered their lunch special - soup and a wagyu beef sandwich. Both were delicious - will definitely be back again. Two mains cost me $68 in total, tax and service included. Got there on a Monday at just 12pm with no reservation and it was fine.
Absolutely love this place. Delicious food and great ambiance. Good crowd and service. Hard to beat this place. I had n idea it was on the Michelin star restaurant. Thumbs up!

Everything was perfect. Especially the service. Benjamin is a pro and helped us to navigate the menu and make great selections. The wagyu meatballs were a favorite for us. The flatbread was awesome and the liver mousse was silky delicious. Drinks were excellent and the bartenders very friendly when we stopped for after dinner drinks.

Amazing restaurant & amazing service by Victoria & Michael Anthony was absolutely amazing!  This place is absolutely fantastic & the service was out of this world I give this place 6 stars.   Absolutely amazing!  A must eat !! 
A must try!! A fantastic restaurant! Staff out of this world!

This is a nice restaurant if you are looking for a tavern style meal with a full bar.  The bar area is small and can be quite full at early dinner time, so plan on an early arrival if you want a seat.  The tavern does not accept reservations which is not ideal.  The wait time was only about 15-20 minutes at 3:30pm.  Food was good, but menu options were small.  The menu has seasonal options.  There were some vegetarian options.  Cocktails were a bit pricey.  There were high end alcohol options for those seeking a nice wine or spirit.  The service was good.  Atmosphere was a bit noisy but tasteful decorated.  Gratuity was included on the bill which was nice.  This is not a family friendly restaurant.  Restaurant is not handicapped accessible.

Culinary orgasm! So great. Also, thanks Mike and Carol for serving us so well! 
Our favorite on the seasonal dinner menu were the scallops. This is excellence in practice, would love to get back here again!

Gramercy Tavern is always a delight -- the food, service, and ambiance are wonderful. I was reminded today, however, that the staff makes it special. Kierstan at the front reception was extraordinarily attentive to me and my pals after some confusion about a telephone number. We are three guys of no particular importance, but Kierstan was apologetic and sympathetic and, most importantly, helpful. What a wonderful professional!

We had such an incredible experience. Service on every level was impeccable. I had a delicious pork schnitzel and for dessert I had the most memorable and delightful poached pears and stilton ice cream...I will never forget those incredible flavors.  It was a real treat to experience Gramercy Tavern during the holidays. Everything about our experience was TOP NOTCH!

Was fairly excited to try Gramercy Tavern. The lobster tortellini and dessert were quite good, but the food was disappointing for $200+ / head. There are many excellent restaurants in NY and you should be able to do better for the price.
Leo at the bar was knowledgeable and personable without being oversolicitous...and he made a mean old-fashioned! Plus -- Best whitefish I've  ever had. Lovely place. Great time!

Oldie and still a goodie.  One of the farm to table pioneers that has the formula down pat.  Duck liver mousse with toast is a good start and the clam flat bread is very tasty.  Grilled lamb entree is fine but overall, even though the meal is good but not great, this spot is still worth a visit because the Tavern Burger holds its own with some of the best burgers in the city.
This place is popular for a reason - amazing food, great ambiance and exceptional service. Definitely a must try place if one is in the mood for an intimate setting.

I had lunch here last week and was seated right next to the line cook working the grill. It was one of the worse experiences I've had. I ordered the tavern burger medium. It was delivered to the table bloody in the middle. The waiter asked how everything was and I mentioned it was under cooked. He said they would fix it. 
As he told the line cook she proceeded to tell him it was cooked perfectly and I didn't know what I was talking about. The worse part is I was within ear shot of her. The waiter then tells the head chef who comes out from the kitchen and tells the line cook the customer is wrong and it's medium. Again I'm sitting right there. No apologies 
My sons a chef and I eat out a lot. Not to mention it's an over priced $32.00 burger. I always thought the customer was always right. I guess it makes sense this is a no tip restaurant they forgot all about customer serv

What a wonderful experience. My boyfriend and I spent a spectacular night tasting delicious foods and enjoy great service. We had high expectations for this restaurant and it exceeded everything we thought. If you are looking for a romantic night out with the best bread and food, then this is the place to go.

We had an amazing dinner at GT for our 10 year anniversary. It was our third time dinning there and it will hopefully not be our last. We ended up meeting executive chef Michael Anthony in the Tavern area and he was incredibly hospitable and actually made us feel like we were dining in his home! Our service was top notch, as it has been every other time we've been there. Thank you so much for a memorable evening!

I ate here for the first time and my expectations were exceeded. I would recommend the restaurant without a doubt. Definitely worth the money. 

We ate in the dining room. I had the lunch vegetarian tasting menu and my sister had the meat option. The food is savory and flavorful. So delicious. 

For lunch you can wear mostly anything. There were people wearing anything from sneakers, to boots and fur. 

You can check your luggage at the coat check

Easily the best restaurant in Manhattan. Been here three times now over the course of 6 years and it continuously holds to high standards. Every dish I've ever had has been exceptional. You can't go wrong here. Might be a little expensive, but it's an amazing place to spend a special night out together and eat and drink phenomenal food and cocktails.

In my opinion they lived up to my expectations. Extensive wine list and well thought out although the American Cabs were not as prevalent as I would think on the menu. 
We went with the tasting menu which was very well done. Great service and dishes that were creative yet within the realm of comfort and not too challenging. The smoked arctic char really stood out and the well known duck was delicious. On point with the desserts and overall deserving of a 5 start experience.

This review is for the bar, which my wife and I have made a point of stopping in every time we're in NYC. Their burger is the best burger I've ever had. We like to get a few glasses of wine and split a burger for an incredible lunch as we did yesterday. Service is always kind and attentive. What an amazing place to have lunch at a beautiful bar for a relatively reasonable price!

This is my favorite restaurant in all of NYC.  I've been to a number of other Michelin starred joints in NYC and elsewhere and I think Gramercy really stands out, both in terms of service and food.  Gramercy is all about consistent excellent execution.  I really enjoy both the tavern area and the back room.  I think you can't go wrong at this place.  It's obviously not an everyday (or every month) restaurant as the quality is reflected in the prices, but do yourself a favor when you're ready to drop a few bucks on a really nice dinner and check this place out.

Was not impressed with the food or the service - I went in knowing I'd pay a steep ticket, but had the expectation the food would be well worth it. The hype failed to hold water in my book - my hopes were far from met. Server was curt and acted put out. Never opposed to give a place a second chance, but it feels like this place has seen its best days. New York offers far better food and service for the money.

This is my favorite restaurant in nyc.  Food is impeccable.  Service is amazing.  This is the kind of place you take your loved ones.  I hadn't been here in a while but visited today for lunch.

I had some sea bass, the chicken sandwich and some schnitzel.  The desserts are delicious.  More broadly I would say pound for pound this is one of the best restaurants in nyc.  

The ambience is just perfect.  The people who run this place should be proud.

The best dining experience I've had the pleasure to enjoy. The food was amazing. The service was above and beyond in the most genuine and authentic way possible. I cannot recommend Gramercy Tavern enough.
I came here in May 2016 with my family to celebrate my graduation. Now in 2019, I can still remember what a wonderful time I had here. Will definitely come back.

party of 1 sat at the bar.....after waiting about 45 minutes on a thursday at 530. great burger. sheet of bacon + the cheese was perfect. high quality meat, and a sesame seed bun that didn't fall apart. also had the chicory salad. loved the crispy bits of pork, almost like cooked chicharron. just know that it will be crowded and expensive.

Just went here for my birthday and was treated like a queen. Are the most excellent fare - the kale apple cheddar salad was to die for! I want to go back immediately and probably will the next time I am in NYC. What I particularly loved was their selection of non-alcoholic drinks! What a classy joint. I will tell everyone to come here if they get a chance.

Love this place.
The ambiance, service and food are top notch and reliable.

Had the three course menu and it was a ton  of food presently beautifully. Have to book table in advance.

Noise level is totally manageable so that my friends and I could speak freely without raising our voices or straining ourselves.

Would love to return and highly recommend for a perfect evening.

I've been here for drinks with my Austrian friend visiting from Las Vegas. The decor is very nice and the bathrooms look so cute, it feels like you're in the country, lol. Will definitely come back for the food.

Incredible experience at Gramercy Tarvern! We went for my parents' anniversary and they greeted us with a glass of champagne to celebrate. We decided to have the seasonal tasting menu with wine pairing and every dish tasted great. My mother was hesitant about the tasting menu as she did not want a duck dish, but they were extremely accommodating and let her choose another dish to replace that with. The complexity of flavors, textures and presentation and the impeccable service is why I give Gramercy 5+ stars. In addition, the culinary team presents surprise dishes throughout the meal-- we received a parsnip puree, apple sorbet, homemade chocolate/gummies and a to-go granola bar. These surprises go above and beyond and that is what you are paying for. My family and I will definitely be coming back to this restaurant on our next trip to NYC!

You won't be disappointed. Worth the price and worth the hype. Fresh and delicious. High end dining. Decor is simple and modern and their changing menu keeps us coming back... That's for damn sure. Wait staff is friendly and knowledgeable which makes our experiences there even better.

If you have the money to splurge then come here for the tasting menu. On my visit the place was packed so that tells you something. The food is really good. As with all high end restaurants the service is over the top. They take good care of you. They also have a seperate dining room which is less pricey and just as busy.

Classic NYC. Naomi was our server and she did NOT steer us wrong on any suggestions. This was a "BALL OUT" lunch with me an my girls and GT didn't disappoint. Fab wine list to boot. Will, or course, be back for a special occasion soon... P.S. do NOT miss the burger!

There is nothing I can say here that hasn't already been said by the other 2500 plus reviews. Our meal was wonderful, and beautifully prepared. Seasonal tasting menu was a bit fish heavy, and none of us is too crazy about fish, so we ordered from the three course menu. It's difficult to get reservations here but when you eat the food, you know why that is.

Had dinner there last week and had the best fish I have ever eaten!  The fish was so tender and mouth watering and the dill sauce truly remarkable.  I had to tell one of the chefs this exact compliment when I was there.  This restaurant is so welcoming with it's staff, decor, ambiance and food.  I can't wait to return next time in NYC!

The worst food I think I've ever had. I have never felt so guilty about spending $180+ dollars on food for ONE person before. I don't mind spending a lot of money on food when it's good, but this was extremely disappointing! The place was really nice & the mood was set nice. We were seated and got water brought to us & then we waited for what felt like forever to get our server. Finally we got drinks & I had the MOST awful drink off of their menu. I don't know why anyone would create such a drink. After one sip I told the server I hated it & asked if I could exchange it for a different drink. He looked at me kind of weird and said sure. He brought me my different drink which tasted SO off but was drinkable. Their homemade bread was very very good ! That was the best part sadly. The 3 courses were absolutely awful. One of the dishes I had was pasta with ground beef & honestly hamburger helper tastes better ! Such a lack of flavor ! My main course the meat was so tough & chewy I couldn't even get it down ! Their baklava IS NOT BAKLAVA ! Not one thing about it resembles a baklava !!! That wasn't even a fancy version of it , it straight up was something else and they put the name on it. Whoever added that to the menu has never seen a baklava in their life ! I don't know how this place had anything more than 1 star and how people actually like this food. I think it's so "high end" that people just agree to say it's good. This place is terrible please DO NOT waste your money on it !!!! Me + 3 other girls all agree that was awful overly priced food & cannot express how disappointed we were ! Awful awful awful !!!!!!

Service: service is somewhat slow, took us 20min to get the first water and some service. By the time we ordered we are at 35min sitting. After that service was ok but started really slow. This is a non tip restaurant perhaps is related to that. Our main waiter was great after the 35min lag 

Food: food was from ok, to really good, however never reached "omg amazing". Nothing was bad or meh. We ordered the tasting menu. Wine selections, interesting and good more non amazing picks.

Price: really good price for what you get. Two tasting menues, plus pairing under 250$. I am not a cheap guy however must say is a a good price for the level.

A wonderful experience! 
My wife and I had dinner there this past Saturday, Feb 9, 2019.
The food was fresh and imaginative with a sophisticated melding of flavors.  The service was attentive without being rushed. A special thank you to our wonderful head waitress Ayisha K. in making the night so special and memorable.

Gramercy Tavern does not need another 5 star review on here but the amazing service and food truly deserves another honorable mention.
We came a few days before New Year for my husbands birthday and ALL items we exceptional:
Beef tartare-rivaled any top restaurant in Paris
Beef bolognese-really flavorful and tender pasta where all components tasted great together. It is very hard to make beef taste good in any kind of pasta and Gramercy Tavern simply perfected this.
lamb loin-perfectly prepared, not chewy and not overly fatty
Chicken breast-yes something as simple as chicken breast was the best I ever had in any restaurant. It was so tender and flavorful, that it tasted more like something from a stew rather than grilled.

I wont even mention amazing drinks and desert but this is just an exceptional restaurant. Worth the $ and the Michelin star.

I was in love with the cocktails here and not to mention their menu.. I loved the roasted oysters! The food was presented nicely with the kale and everything. I also tried the duck meatballs which were crispy and delicious! The vibe in the tavern was great. The bar staff was very attentive and socials as well. I enjoyed the dishes and will be back to try more on the menu.

Never been here before but this quickly is now on my favorite places in NYC. The ambience with the tree branches and the table in the back are absolutely beautiful! Didn't try any food - but the drinks and the service at the bar were fabulous! My boyfriend wasn't feeling well, and the bartender made him his own drink with bitters and ginger ale. It definitely made him feel better! I cannot wait to come back to the city and visit this place! 5 stars for sure.
Nice for special occasions. Price fixed menu. Nice ambiance and very attentive wait staff. Bread would be better a bit less dense. Dessert was excellent
What a dining experience. The food and the ambience are quite elegant t without being too pretentious. I am very much looking forward to going back.

Gramercy Tavern has been around for years and somehow continues to be at the top of their game. We came here for dinner and they had a four course pre-fix dinner where you get a few options for each course. Of course being gluten free always makes this challenging since there are less options for each course. However the staff was ready for us, guided us through the menu, made great recommendation and accommodated our restrictions with missing a beat. 

The gluten-free bread with goat milk butter was better than regular bread. Made glad to be gluten free. The wine recommendation was perfect and complemented our meal well. My wife had beef and I had chicken so that was amazing. 

The desert was crazy good. My wife had a fantastic cheese plate and I had a flourless chocolate cake with coconut pistachio ice cream that was simply way too good. 

But the best part was the next morning. Sometimes due to cross contamination or general carelessness with service and ingredients, I feel bloated or worse. But not this time. I woke up feeling great. 

Gramercy is not cheap, but if you want clean food done right, this is the place.

We came here for a night of celebration and tried their seasonal tasting menu which features 6 courses. Food was solid, but nothing too special, I'd give it a 7/10, portions were pretty large in our opinion, we started feeling full after the 3rd course. service was really good considering this is a no-tipping restaurant. Our server was very tentative, and caring, and it's just nice to know that he wasn't doing it for the $$. Overall a decent experience, I would say $200 for a one star tasting menu was a tiny bit overpriced, considering it didn't really wow us, but I would still recommend, very decent experience.

Had a wonderful experience here for lunch. Right in the Gramercy area, The restaurant is beautiful, the service is attentive and quick but not intrusive. The wine was great, as was my salad and the delicious bread and butter (seriously never tasted butter that delicious in my life). Make a reservation, dress well, and enjoy!

We celebrated our 9 year anniversary here and it was a great choice! All the staff, from the host to the waiters, were so friendly and welcoming. The food was excellent - we had the 3 course meal with poached shrimp and hamachi for appetizers and hake and lamb for mains. Every course was exceptional! We usually swap half way but this time every dish was a winner. Then came the desserts and they were explosions of flavor with every bite! We had the cheese and chocolate tart, the cheese selection was very well put together and the chocolate tart was terrific. 
Special thanks to the sommelier who picked an outstanding wine within our budget and preferred flavor profile. 
Top notch service, relaxed atmosphere and world class food!
Best restaurant in NYC.  The service in the cafe area is excellent.  Creative and rotating menu.  Best time to go is on off hours, rather than dinner time.

This burger was delectable.

We walked in without reservation for a quick bite after a Broadway show and were seated within 10 minutes by the lovely host Kiersten. 

The decor of the restaurant is gorgeous, with flowers and beautiful murals all over the restaurant.

We kept our order simple with burgers and a cheese plate, but both were great and service was fast and efficient. Would definitely recommend a visit here!

The lunch tasting menu for $89 (gratuity included!) is really solid. Each of the five courses (with a palate cleanser and a bread to start) was tasty with no fault. Sure, nothing was amazing and outstanding like a tasting menu 2-3x its price would be, but everything was dependably yummy. My only gripe with the meal was that the our lunch took 2 hours, when I didn't really think it needed to be. The menu we were served was slightly different from what was on the website, though.

The bread was a fluffy whole wheat bun with a crisp exterior, almost like a fried mantou. It had a bit of salt on it, which added just a touch of oomph. The first starter was a fluke with apples and kohlrabi - the fish was in sizeable chunks with a smooth meaty texture, and the acidic dressing complemented it very well.

Next came another seafood course - I forgot what it was - something that felt like scallops, but it also had a tasty sauce around it. The pasta dish was a squid ink pasta with an incredibly savory and umami lobster sauce, this was delicious. The meat dish was a wedge of duck that again was cooked to the right doneness. At this point, I didn't feel like there was quite enough food, and was almost prepared to get sushi after until the dessert came.

Our palate cleanser was an apple sorbet with vanilla oil (tasted like adult applesauce!), followed by a dessert of a vanilla yogurt mousse with a molasses-y pomegranate sauce. I really liked how light the dessert was - it wasn't necessarily calorically light, but the fact that it was yogurt and fruit instead of, I don't know, something baked and chocolate, made it really easy to wash down, and I felt satisfied at the end of the meal instead of sluggish and tired.

Me and my husband checked this place out on our trip to NY.
-Service 4/5: It took quite long, about 20 mins between dishes for us
-Food probably 3/5 because the seafood is fresh, everything is cooked on point. The marinated fluke, smoked arctic and the sea bass were good. The compliment apple sorbet was really good. The other dishes were not really good, they were not bad but just not good to our taste especially the Squid Ink Spaccatelle and the mousse 
In general, we don't think we will come back again.

Let me start with our flight was delayed. We literally came straight from the LaGuardia bags in tow. We were a bit frazzled and on edge. As soon as we walked through the front door we were put at ease. Our bags and coats were checked, immediately we felt better. We were led to our table and just were able to decompress a little. We were in the city for my wife's birthday and everyone we encountered wished her a happy birthday. We had the tasting menu and wine pairing. The meal was fantastic. The atmosphere was great. Very casual, but high end. A great experience.

My bf and I came here on a Friday night. We booked almost a month in advance for the main dining room. Pre-fixed menu is $134 including tips. 

The atmosphere was nice. I got Hamachi for appetizer, striped bass for entree, and cheese plate for dessert. Striped Bass was so delicious with the thick sauce. The pre-dinner bread was amazing. My bf got lamb, he thinks that's just so so.

Service was great, but they were kinda busy so I couldn't find anyone to get out check at the end. But overall it wad good.

This was my fiancé's and my second time to Gramercy Tavern (Dining Room) and we were really excited to be back.  Our first experience was incredible - a memorable meal and certain dishes that we still remember several years later.  Our second experience however was one to forget.  The service was excellent but the food was lackluster.  We live in New York so we lamented wasting a special evening here.

Why two stars and not one? I'll give some credit for our previous five-star experience but the variability in experiences is not acceptable given the cost.
 
We each had the tasting menu (March 2019) and believe it was one of the most pedestrian (and at times disheartening) dining experiences that we've had in a long while.

- Marinated Fluke.  Was a one-dimensional ceviche.
- Scallops with Mussel.  Cooked well but felt the accompaniments (potato medallions, crisped salsify, didn't enhance but detracted)
- Smoked Sturgeon.  At first I was so excited to try the sturgeon because it was unique, but after trying it I realized why I don't see it on menus.  It was rubbery, the sauce didn't enhance the fish and frankly I can't think of a fish that I have liked less in New York City and I love fish! 
- Squid Ink Spaccatelle with Lobster.  Will give credit here, it was excellent.  The chorizo really added a nice depth and it was the best sauce of the night.  Ample amounts of lobster and great flavor.
- Roasted Duck Breast & Confit with Rutabega.  The duck was cooked well and very nice but the confit lacked depth and the rutabega was rock hard with no flavor. 
- Vanilla Yogurt Mousse.  At this point I lost interest but this fell super flat.  I think it was meant to be clean but they went a bit too clean.

We let our waiter (who was great) and the manager know how we felt about our experience and they were very gracious - improvement definitely need in the kitchen though.

O-M-G!!! What an experience... I'd give 10 stars if I could. Put aside any thoughts you had of not liking certain foods because nothing disappoints here. We did the 3 course meal, starting with a watermelon gazpacho shot that had basil oil which was absurdly delicious! Then they gave us the "angel bread" with a goat cheese butter... again, absurdly delicious! Neither of those things were on the 3 course meal listing but so happy we got them with our meal. I ordered the pasta with chunks of bacon as my 1st course. It was cheesy a little spicy but not at all over whelming... it was just plain delicious. Then for the 2nd course I ordered the pork tenderloin, And my husband ordered the duck... both were absolutely amazing! Then we added a cheese board which our waitress was kind enough to select 3 amazing selections of cheeses. And finally for dessert I got the chocolate hazelnut moose and my husband got the pavlova. Can I just tell you, the desserts were out of control! Flavor profiles were amazing, everything was spectaculat.
This is the BEST!! Amazing food, service and atmosphere. Allison was wonderful!! I wish we had this in Tampa Bay!!!
Granmercy is a beautiful establishment. Can be great to gather with friends or go on a romantic outing with your loved one. Great food and even better service.

This is one of the places my boyfriend took me to when I visited New York for the first time. This is, hands down, one of the best restaurants I have ever been to. It's a beautifully decorated place, and it reminded a lot of restaurants in London. There are two sections: one that is more affordable and all the way to the back is the other more fancy section. We did the pre-fixed menu in the latter (I ordered the sampler).  It's quite pricey - I think our dinner was almost $400.00, including tips. Pretty cool they give you complimentary dessert and homemade bars to take home afterwards! My only complaint is the customer service - most of the servers were great, but others were not as friendly (but maybe it's just New York).

Lives up to the hype!

So down to earth while also upscale, with highly attentive yet not suffocating service. Nicest wait, somm, and bar staff I've ever had the pleasure of encountering! Everyone had such great personality, and seemed to really love their job and want to be there. They knew the menu items through and through - we were particularly impressed with the (young and hip and lady!) sommelier, who has a crazy encyclopedic knowledge of wines and wine regions.

The food was delicious, from the pickled veg at the bar, to the shrimp toast appetizers, to the chiang mai sausage and duck meatball entrees, to the enormous sundae dessert - most everything hit a high note!

The fisherman's stew was pretty salty, and the calamari toast was a bit lacking in calamari. We were very impressed with the rest of the meal, so we'd give those another shot in the future in the hopes that it was an off night.

Thanks again for a top notch dining experience!

We snagged a last minute reservation via opentable and had an incredible experience.  from our arrival to our departure - such hospitality.  Our main server Yasin and our sommelier Steven were very helpful and accommodating.  Additional servers unobtrusively changed out the wares accordingly, the food coming out at a very enjoyable pace - it all felt comfortable and relaxed. 

As for the food - it was fantastic.  We got the seasonal tasting menu + wine pairing and a 3 course pre-fixe.  Clean, familiar flavors alongside the new and exciting.  Perfectly prepared and plated and the pairings always interesting and fun.   And while at $550 it cost twice as much as a typical nice dinner out for us, it was a far more exceptional and memorable peak-dining experience.  

My only complaint and it's minor:  Our 11 year anniversary is Tuesday and both our birthdays are next week, so I mentioned this in the reservation - they greeted us at our table w/ a prosecco toast (and closed with a chocolate dessert).  While it's true the prosecco was better than your usual suspects, it was still underwhelming and a missed opportunity to really set the mood of a luxury experience.  Better to start w a proper Champagne toast - I'd be happy to have paid a little more.  We both enjoy bubbles but didn't feel inclined to finish.  That said, they did present the bottle and I suppose a suaver guy would have taken that opportunity to ask for as much.  The other particular detail, though of far less consequence than a prosecco-toast, was upon our departure, one of the servers handed us a wrapped to-go crumb cake, declaring it the best part of the whole dinner.   It was a fine little loaf, but after trying it neither of us could imagine how anyone could possibly say that!   

Looking forward to returning sooner than later.  

tip:  the cocktail menu looks fantastic, but after getting the mescal cocktail, we immediately realized it was going to clash w/ the more delicate flavors of the food.  so something to consider.  glad we went the wine route.
Awesome experience yesterday at the bar. Andrew and Richard are rock stars. Had their 'special' drinks - fantastic!  Great service, great drinks, good snacks, incredibly comfortable and professional.
Good food loved everything nice place we will be back soon this is our 2nd visit and it was good as first time
This is one of my favorite restaurants. The service is amazing. The staff is knowledgeable and attentive. You can come for formal dining or a casual meal between NYC sightseeing.
Wagyu beef sandwich was pretty decent. Came here for a weekend lunch, sat in the main dining room. Good service!

I had been wanted to come here, but it's ALWAYS packed. So I decided to make a reservation and got the first one I could find on a Saturday about 3 weeks out. 

When I showed up it was crowded as usual. I had to wait about 5 min to get to the host stand. 

The vibe here is casual. Both in the tavern and the dining room. Despite the white table cloths, many of the patrons around me were in jeans. I am not sure what I was expecting, but I thought it was going to be slightly more fancy than this. 

The service was great. Always someone around and people checked in with me frequently to see if I liked my food. I ordered the vegetarian tasting menu. 

First bite from the kitchen - these are always good no matter what they are. I enjoyed mine, though I couldn't tell you what was in it other than I think it contained kohlrabi.

Hakurei Turnip
Trumpet Mushrooms, Ponzu. The mushroom was meaty, in a good way. It was bright and tangy from the ponzu. 

Cauliflower
Burrata, Almonds, croutons. Oh my goodness was this good. It was creamy, crunchy. I liked the different textures from the different cauliflower (cooked vs shaved raw). The burrata and the green sauce on the bottom! Oh my! So good. 

Winter citrus with quinoa. I wasn't a huge fan of this dish. I think it was missing something, but I'm not sure what. The quinoa was cooked well and flavorful. I think perhaps it was missing something with a bit more of a crunchy texture. 

Ricotta Cavatelli
Butternut Squash, Kale, Pumpkin Seeds - I really enjoyed this dish. It was small, but heavy. The pasta was thick but had a nice almost gummy texture, which went nicely with the sauce. The sauces in there were creamy and rich, and the pumpkin seeds added a nice crunch.  I really enjoyed this! 

Next was the roasted mushrooms. Following the earlier mushroom dish which I enjoyed, I didn't care for this one as much.  A variety of mushrooms, but I didn't finish. 

Next was the apple sorbet pallet cleanser. Light and fresh. 

Finally was the caramelized cheesecake. This was like a cross between creme brûlée and a cheesecake. I enjoyed the flavors and texture. 

I appreciate that Danny Meyer restaurants are no tipping facilities. I like knowing when I go in how much I'm going to spend, and appreciate even more that the service is still impeccable.

Overall, a few standout dishes and a few that were just okay. Great service. Casual ambiance. 

I'll try the raven next time (if I can ever get a table) to try out that burger!

We had a fantastic tasting menu lunch at Gramercy Tavern on a Saturday. As expected, the food and service were simply exquisite. We started with a fresh and nicely marinated crudo, and followed with a halibut course, squid ink pasta with lobster, roasted duck breast, and a sorbet with meringue. While the restaurant was fairly empty when we arrived, it quickly filled up. When paying the check, we were pleasantly surprised with a few bonbons as a parting treat. Overall a lovely lunch experience. In addition to the lunch tasting menu, Gramercy Tavern offers a $32 "The Daily" set menu of three courses, as well as a la carte options.
Grilled Sea Bass was good, not the best though. Friendly staff and great service at the bar. Wait time was around 20 mins for bar seating on a weekday.

Gramercy Tavern has been on my bucket list for quite some time so its tough taking two stars off.
