Service 5/5 hands down. They were kind, prompt and synchronized when serving dishes which was wonderful. We chose the 3 course menu as all needs to partake in the table. As a vegetarian I went with the following First Course - Brussels Sprouts & Parsnip Salad, Celery, Pecorino& Walnuts 
Second Course - Ricotta Cavatelli Butternut Squash, Kale, Pumpkin Seeds 
Third Course - Chocolate Cream Tart, Rye Crumble, Black Currant Jam, Vanilla Ice Cream. 

The reason I knocked off the star was because the appetizer was extremely underwhelming. The salad was thrown together with not much presentation and  and lacked flavor.  The main dish was definitely filling and flavorful and as a chocolate lover I was in love the dessert. I loved the amuse bouche (incredibly creamy and flavorful) and the chocolate truffles that ended the entire meal. They even presented us with a banana chocolate chip muffin to take home and eat for breakfast the next day (OMG AMAZING)

The experience was wonderful and loved the atmosphere. I would definitely recommend the restaurant maybe just pick a different first course :)

Came here with my girlfriend as it was on our New York "restaurant bucket list" to try the famous burger for lunch on its Tavern Side. Its a beautiful venue with a wonderful wait staff who will accommodate any variety of different requests. There are two different sides to the restaurant, the Tavern and Dining Room. The Dining Room offers a little more of an upscale menu, but both are absolutely delicious. 

The burger is certainly one of the best in New York and comes with a side of chips that are to die for. It isn't cheap, but you get what you pay for. Since it is a little more upscale, dress the part. This is a place that everyone should try when visiting New York!

Gramercy Tavern has the best service ever. They are attentive, friendly, and cheerful.

We had the lunch tasting menu and it was delicious. My favorite dish was the squid ink pasta! I was not a fan of the halibut - it was lukewarm and a bit bland. The pomegranate mousse was rich, creamy, but still refreshing.

This place is amazing! I've never gone to their dining room for lunch/dinner, but I did go to their tavern area for lunch. Such a good value for the price. It's also a non-tipping restaurant and service is fantastic. 

I came here for lunch and I got the Citrus Salad which was essentially an artisan salad. It had candied walnuts, salsa verde and kohlrabi. For my main dish I got the grilled sea bass which had potatoes and bacon and garnished with dill. Very well cooked and refreshing. 

This place lives up to its hype and is honestly a true gem.

Extremely disappointed by this place... 

We had a reservation but still waited 15min at the entrance before being seated.

Service was very average. We didn't understand the presentation for the different dishes. We got the bill slammed on the table with a "here you goooo". 

And for the food... we did the tasting menu for lunch. 
Each dish had at least one of flaw, lack of taste, lack of seasoning, undercooked fish... the only good dish was the black squid ink lobster pasta.

Definite more tavern than high-end...

What a fabulous restaurant! We had a terrific meal and service here. Chef Michael Anthony made our granddaughter a Congratulations Dessert for her getting into Harvard. He was just so nice and has written two cookbooks, as far as I know. We bought "V Is For Vegetables", and we are looking forward to using it!!

Five star service, two star food with wildly overpriced wine. Menu hijacked by strange palate grasping for originality.

Oily  interpretation of bouillabaisse, fish overwhelmed by chorizo, salty, greasy one note. Maybe just make the classic and do it really well? Chiangmai mai sausage was just weird. Over ambitious mix of Asian flavors failed to disguise unpleasant pork sausage, kielbasa with lemon grass. 

Desperately needs overhaul. Resting on very tired laurels.

Nice ambiance. TERRIBLE DRINKS.  My boyfriend and I went for a cocktail after dinner. I've heard rave reviews about this place being a must. I will never be back $70 for 3 drinks that tasted like a dirty glass. I wanted to puke. Very disappointed. Save you money for literally any other bar.
Great restaurant, nice specials & portion sizes. The best part is that it's a no gratuity restaurant & the service is impeccable!

Really great staff, service and food. We had ordered the fluke, the shrimp, the sea bass, and the steak tartare. (really good) Their angel bread was delicious and comes with a goat cheese spread. I could have eaten that as the meal itself, it was probably my favorite thing about the entire dinn

On a side note for those who drive by car to get here: when we had arrived we had asked the Gramercy staff where we could park. They had said that there was an "icon" parking and if they stamp the receipt we'd get a discount. This was not honored by icon, and we were disappointed that we were told otherwise by the restaurant staff.
Over rated and overpriced. Service was horrible and rushed although I did the tasting menu. Never going back!

Beautiful restaurant. Great staff, very knowledgeable of the menu. The food was unreal, I still can't get the goat cheese butter off my mind. The bolognese was so good I scraped the plate clean. 

Fabulous restaurant, I will definitely recommend to any of my friend who visit New York City.

I was here on Friday night and everything I ate was a hit.   HIT!  We ordered a ton of things and all tried each other's food and we weren't disappointed by Anything.  It was all very good.  The service was ok.

Have you ever been speechless while writing a review about food? Almost every bite took my breath away. I can not rave about this place enough. I LOVE, LOVE, LOVE you! If I could I'd give you more than a 5 star rating! That is just how amazing this place is! GO! It's a must!

Came to celebrate my moms birthday. Great food and ambience. Service was just the right amount - very attentive but not overwhelming. Us three all got the seasonal tasting menu and mom added wine pairing. There were a couple highlights among the 6 courses and overall the food was very fresh. The only accident was that There was some thread thingy in my beef dish. They apologized and admitted this shouldn't have happened whatsoever and took it off from the check. Oh, they also nicely accommodated our 9 months old, so if you have babies/kids and don't want to deal with the potential embarrassment at other high end restaurants, this is the place to be.

Went there for dinner tonight. From the moment we walked in, we had great service, great wine, apps, main entree and dessert. We were there for 3 hours and no one rushed us.  Highly recommend to add to your Gramercy list of restaurants.

Went their for our 6 month anniversary on a Tuesday early dinner mission . It is hard to get on weekends. 

Spectacular! The bread to die for...the goat butter uuuufffff

The red ruby shrimp....the pork belly...lamb shoulder ...the service.....the dessert!!!!! One of our best meals in NY to date!

For such a highly rated restaurant, maybe my expectations were too high, but I was slightly disappointed in the food. The ambiance is worth 5 stars- beautiful, fancy yet quaint, upscale yet comfortable. I came with two girlfriends for lunch and while overall it was a pleasant and good dining experience, with all the AMAZING food in New York, it just was not my favorite. Maybe it was because we didn't order the tasting menu? 


The seasonal Arctic char was my favorite. Great textures, tender and cooked to perfection. A little saltier than I prefer but overall good flavor. 

The Brussels sprouts salad was also delicious. A little sweet with a nice crunch. 

The squid ink tagliatelle was just a little off. It was very salty and had a weird, licorice aftertaste. Maybe its an acquired taste but I would probably try something else next time.

Overall fantastic experience. My fiancee and I went for dinner to celebrate the one year countdown to our wedding, and they made us feel so special from the moment we sat down. Every single person that came by the table (to clear plates, fill water, etc) was aware of our occasion and acknowledged it sincerely. Our server Ayisha was WONDERFUL. She was extremely knowledgable and took the time to explain specific dishes in elaborate detail to help us decide what to order. Every course was fantastic from the complimentary biscuits with goat cheese butter (oh. my. god.) all the way through to dessert. Highly highly recommend, especially for a special occasion. We will definitely be back!
Really great service and food. Hands down THE BEST COOKIE I've ever had in my life on the dessert menu

This is an experience! Instagram upperfeast. The space is beautiful and the ambiance rules. They have a huge staff and they're all very friendly. It's fancy but not stuffy or pretentious. PRO TIP order the tasting menu and vegetarian menu and share. It's worth it and kind of a hack to try way more things. I love Gramercy Tavern.

Dinner at Gramercy Tavern was spectacular, and truly lived up to its reputation. The crab salad, artic char and rhubarb-berry dessert were really memorable, all fresh, bright, bold. Service was impeccable and the decor is so lovely. A must do at least once in NY.

Honestly I can tell you that I am not hip to eating raw fish, but this Tuna Tartare has completely my perspective. As soon as this meal reached my tastebuds, there was no stopping me. Absolutely EVERYTHING in and about this dish was superb.
One of the best restaurants in NYC. Burger was outstanding and service was great. I will definitely comeback.

Go for the lunch tasting menu as you'll be able to try many different items without breaking the bank. For me and my lunch guests personally, the food was a little on the salty side. Service was accommodating and having gratuity included was a nice bonus. 

Solid spot, but just missing that last little oomph to make it outstanding.
Great spot . Great environment overall . Sat at bar.   Only complaint is that the lead bartender is pretentious and works to hard to make it feel like an elite joint

Excellent, excellent, excellent!

Food is great, service is top notch, atmosphere is warm and welcoming.

Went there for lunch of party of four. We all had a la carte instead of lunch tasting menu due to time restraints. 

I ordered:
1. Drink: glass of sauvignon blanc
2. Appetizer: Roasted Sea Scallops, Salsify, Potatoes, Mussels - just right, sea scallops don't have the fishy taste or baking soda taste 
3. Entree: Arctic Char, Fingerling Potatoes, Leeks, Green Garlic - out of the world. Highly recommended if you like fish. Crispy fish skin on top, but not burned. Cooked fish meat just about medium. It has some sort of pesto green sauce, flavorful and not salty. 
4. Dessert: Coconut Milk Cake, Passion Fruit, Pineapple Mint Sorbet - so refreshing and has different layers of taste. Smooth and not too sweet, highly recommended
5. Cappuccino - good
Another few pieces of pastries on the house

Even though this is a non-tipping restaurant, staff is friendly and the service is top notch.

Reservation is recommended.

I love this place been multiple times, I've dinned in the main dining room and the tavern. In the Main dinning room, I had the tasting food was great service best I've ever had!! I do enjoy the tavern, different experiences and both amazing. Must have is the seafood tower. Cocktail list is bomb!

Excellent value, service, food quality, menu choices. 
Well presented food with nicely developed flavors and top quality ingredients
Recommend whole heartedly. .

The service was fantastic. From our waitress to the wine steward. The ambience and the decor were fantastic. Overall the food was good but the fact that I'm not a foodie makes it hard to appreciate $130 prefix menus for three courses. Nothing we had was mind blowing but everything was good.

It doesn't get much better than this! In many ways Gramercy Tavern is New York's quintessential fine dining restaurant. The ambiance is only exceeded by the service and the service is only exceeded by the food. Every element of the experience is perfect. We were a large party with an infant, but they never missed a beat. Gramercy Tavern is fine dining at its very best. We have been coming to Gramercy Tavern since it opened and we will be back again and again. Bravo Danny!

One of the classics that still delivers! Had a wonderful dinner - the strawberries & cream, the pork pasta & the crudo were the highlights. They were so accommodating to my friend who is celiac, egg & dairy free. Wine pairings were perfect! Wish there was one more red wine and that dishes were a little hotter. Looking forward to visiting the tavern one day soon!
We tried the tasting menu and each course was delicious. I find the cuisine to be quite simple but very flavorful. The wine paring was amazing!

Ambiance: I loved all the flower decor! Average to low noise level, perfect for a lovely date or just friends get together!
Food: my friend and I both had the tasting menu with wine pairing. Portion size was small. My favorite was fried tilefish and pork with asparagus. Roasted duck breast and strawberry dessert was okay. Scallop appetizer didn't really suit my taste, celery was way too overpowering. Wine was just average. Oh did I mention that the bread here is one of the best breads I've ever had in NYC? So soft and amazing texture! 
Service: our server Ben was very warm and attentive. This is, mind you, a non tipping restaurant. Yet the service surpassed many tipping ones. Will definitely be back to try more a la carte items!

I love this place and always enjoy sitting at the bar with a glass of wine, however, food has been a bit of a disappointment. I tried Gramercy burger last time I was there and it was nothing special, definitely had better. Today I tried duck liver mousse which was very creamy with no taste and the toast was very salty. Great place for drinks and probably for sit down dinner but food served at the bar is not the best one.

Its nice to be able to get top notch food and drinks in the city without having to get all dressed up. We got the tasting menu and the food and service were both great. Every course was spot on. The staff is great at explaining what everything is and were very accommodating with requested substitutions.

I am so sad that I have to give my all time favorite restaurant 3 stars.  I really do not understand why when you have a great thing you change it.   I absolutely loved this place!  I have been here at least 20x & every time I thoroughly enjoyed it.   This time was different.  It just wasn't that great & certainly not the same as it once was.  The prices were astronomical and the meal was average.  The tasting menu was superb & now it's hardly memorable.  The only saving grace of the night was the waiter was friendly and the waitstaff was nice.  Surprising as they don't work on tips.

We ate here tonight to celebrate our 20th Anniversary.  From the moment we walked in, the service and attention to detail was exceptional.  We ordered the 3 course menu and everything we ordered was delicious!  The extra touches, like champagne and a special cake to celebrate our anniversary, just made the experience all the more memorable.  I would highly recommend this place!

Very bad experience with our dinner in this highly rated restaurant. We went to celebrate my son's 21st birthday and what a disappointment. The drinks were horrible and when I asked the waiter about a drink, his description was to compare the drink to penicillin . The food was very salty and absolutely nothing special about anything. Not a place I will go back.

This now my favorite restaurant on the planet! We had an incredible experience last night, the service, food and atmosphere were unbeatable! This is a must for anyone that wants to experience dinning perfection!

The service was the most exceptional part of the experience! Don't think it could be beat even at Buckingham palace.

I was very excited to eat here for my birthday, and unfortunately this restaurant did not nearly meet my expectations. Although our first dishes were great, our second course was overly salty and simply inedible. Even worse than the food was the service (tip included). We asked the waiter about one of the drinks and he said "it tastes like penicillin," and he continued to disrespect my mother, who has a slight accent, by telling her "in a place like this you get the food you get." After we told him we didn't like the dish, he asked us if we wanted to take it home. The food and the service was just unacceptable for a restaurant of this standard.

(Really 3.5 stars) Had the 6 course tasting menu. All of the food was at least good, some of it great, and one or two of the dishes were outstanding. All in, though, it was somehow still not a very memorable meal. And while portion sizes are supposed to be on the smaller end for a coursed menu set, some of the dishes were offensively small. The "lobster" was served as three mini--I kid you not--dime-sized medallions, though in a reasonably tasty sauce. And the savory finale was a slice of (while perfectly done) steak that could not have been more than 1.5 oz. Maybe we can chalk my experience up to the psychology of outsized expectations. Perhaps, sometimes, it doesn't pay to have your reputation precede you.

Came for lunch in the tavern section, and my party of 3 was in and out within 50 minutes- there was no weekday lunch rush at 12:20pm. In addition to the celebratory dinners this place seems to be popular for, Gramercy Tavern is also a great place for a fancier but not-too-time-consuming lunch break!

This is one of those classy places with individual, machine washable hand towels in the bathroom and servers who will neatly fold your napkins for you when you leave the table momentarily. My friends and I, in our t-shirts and jeans, didn't fit the bill for their usual clientele, but everybody we encountered was pleasant nonetheless. As a bonus, tip is included in the prices listed on the menu!

You start the meal with complimentary (focaccia?) bread. I loved this bread. It was cheesy, a bit crispy on the outside but fluffy on the inside. I just wish it was still warm and a bit less oily. They normally start you with one generously-sized piece, but I ended up unashamedly asking the server for more and ate four pieces. The server could tell I really liked it and offered to pack some to-go for me. I decided to decline, though I was definitely tempted. For my entree, I got the sea bream. Great choice for a lighter lunch (or if you want to save room for their delicious bread). The fish was tender and vegetables flavorful. It was a bit too salty for my tastes but still very good. My two friends got the tavern burger, and they both said it's one of the best burgers they've ever had (featured on the Buzzfeed Worth It Secret Menu episode). One of them has been here 3 times and has gotten the burger every time.

It is funny to see Gramercy tavern even have just one bad review, LOL

My boy friend took me here twice, and both visit was AWESOME!! :)

This restaurant is his to go restaurant and now it is my most favorite!!

If anyone says the food is salty, oh that is because this person only had water, lol. If u had a lot of wine and other alcoholic drink, you will need to food to be a little saltier :)) don't ask me why^^

Everything is just awesome!!! 

Awesome!!!

This place is glorious. The cocktails, the bread they hand out, everything. I went there for lunch and thought it was a bit pricy but then when the bill came I was informed it was a non-tipping restaurant. Absolutely fantastic surprise for me!

We popped into Gramercy Tavern on a weekday in the early afternoon, not wildly hungry but seeking a nosh. After ordering drinks - Portside Spritz for me, Gramercy Garden for him - we ordered the three vegetable sides as the strength of the accompaniments show the authentic character of the restaurant. Leeks with a smoky flavor and delicate cheese grated atop, butter beans braised in a number of herbs, and cucumbers with a yoghurt sauce (akin to a deconstructed tzatziki) all shined.

We ate at the Tavern and ordered the calamari flatbread, and for entrees, the Fisherman's Stew and the Tavern Burger. Everything was delicious. I had never had anything quite like the stew, with chorizo and "gold" rice. Even the prelude to the meal, the focaccia bread, was a soft, buttery, carefully seasoned delicacy. The carefully designed decor with rustic accents and a quaint wood burning stove at one end was a nice backdrop to the wholesome food and excellent service (no tipping restaurant!).

When it comes to fine dining, Gramercy Tavern sets the standard for class, flavors, and service. It's become somewhat hackneyed to read about a new restaurant opening where the chef is touted as a "Gramercy Tavern alum" but having finally dined here I understand why it's a badge of honor. I had the great pleasure of being treated to a meal here for a job promotion by a very dear friend. To me, it's a special occasion kind of restaurant, but I could see it being a regular spot for those dealt a fancier lot in life. 

The menu changes frequently (perhaps weekly?) but I enjoyed a halibut entree that came in a savory almost soup-like base. It was topped with watercress and fiddlehead ferns. This dish was well made, but less exciting than the side of polenta my friend ordered. I found the polenta outstanding. It tasted like it was whipped in a cream. It was made with a savory chili oil that gave it a nice kick that built over time. I think spice makes everything taste better. Maybe my halibut could've used some spice.

We paired our entrees with some very well made cocktails and followed it with a brownie dessert highly recommended by our server. While it wasn't the most photogenic dessert, the warm brownie paired with freshly made whipped cream and sliced almonds was a most satisfying sweet end to our meal. Sometimes I forget that not all food is made to post about on the internet.

I had a lovely lunch here recently.  I had a special which was monk fish and it was perfectly cooked.
Also a tasty salad and a sorbet for dessert.  My friend had a vegetarian dish that was good.   We had a bottle of Viennese wine - strange request but my friend is going to Vienna and wanted to try it. It was great.  The service was excellent.  We were seated in the far corner of the restaurant by ourselves but by the time we left the entire restaurant was full.   Very pretty place.  Noise level was low (my friend always notices if a place  is noisy so now I'm aware of those things).  All in all a lovely lunch.

Mocktails alone make it a trip worth coming. A well deserved ONE Michelin Star- no more no less for sure . 

That combined with the excellent service, ambience and Decour it makes for a stellar dining experience.

Now the food:

The complimentary amuse bouche poached eggs with caviar being too solid in the yolk - not perfectly poached -  is the reason I docked a star . But with that awkwardness out-of-the-way I can go on to say that it was truly one of the best dinners I've had in New York City. The strawberry elderflower mock tail left me with an aftertaste that was gently and pleasantly as surprising as a cool breeze in dead of a humid summer day. All the mocktails were fresh And we had the mango lime, strawberry elderflower, raspberry and honey. They were all amazing in their own right. 
In apps: 
The oysters really stole the show-they actually came with their own seasoning and no additional sauces. 

They also had a salad on the menu with beets ricotta and strawberries - the summer triad straight to my heart. 

The tuna appetizer was still solid but nothing to write home about. Gazpacho look interesting on the menu but I avoided it since I have become a snob since moving to New York City in this regard and living next to Jose Andres mercato - little Spain  for a few days where they have an actual authentic gazpacho stall. 

We had two main entrées which both wowed and a chef special spaghettini with crab. One Andre was to sea beam in what appeared to be a lemony refreshing garlic sauce. Chef Michael Antony really outdid himself with that. 

The vegetarian entrée of mushrooms and asparagus also retained a lot of flavor and was very hearty while still keeping it light and healthy. 

Also going into the docking of the one star the spaghetti ratio of crab was a little low, And while the pasta was perfectly hand cut I have had better in New York. You can imagine that I had to request an extra bowl of flakes of Parmesan in order to truly bring out the flavor in this dish. 

The dessert was solidly good-a blueberry tart with rosemary butter composing the crust and a necessary dolop of creme Anglais. They call it a blueberry pie but that is a misnomer. It was clearly American Thanksgiving inspired dessert and perhaps I am a little bit biased there with my leaning towards French desserts so take it with a grain of salt but the rosemary did not complement the rest of the tart as well as I would've liked. Still props for the creative thinking.


I've heard the cheeseboard is amazing. Would definitely go back just for that next since it is right here in the neighborhood!

This is a NY institution for good reason.  We were able to get in without any trouble on a weekday before noon for a table of 2, as the place was just opening for lunch.  The tavern area with about 15 tables up front is quite warm and inviting and casual, much less stuffy than the formal white tablecloth covered tables towards the back of the restaurant.  The wine selection's solid, and I was quite happy with my heirloom tomato soup-sandwich combo, which was delicious, yet light enough for a lunch meal.  The soup was similar to an Andalucian gazpacho, so blended together fresh heirloom tomatoes and olive oil with light salt and spices, with chunks of cucumber.  The sandwich was on a lovely focaccia, with a spicy remoulade of sorts generously slathered on, along with slices of green tomato, bacon, and lettuce.  The complimentary cheddar jalapeno focaccia was also a real treat.  I'll definitely be back.

Had the 3 course meal. What astounded me was the balanced portions to make you full while delivering optimum flavor, awesome service from all staff (greeted every time you walk by), and magnificent take on dessert. I had cookies and ice cream for dessert which turned out to be the most magnificent 5 start quality cookie I've ever had. Great place for a fancy date night or celebration with trust that your food will be the best from appetizer to dessert

Did the tasting menu for lunch. Food was a bit disappointing but not bad. Out of about 5 courses 2 or 3 were really enjoyable with the rest just moving the session along. Ambience was simple yet elegant.
Terrific food and fabulous service glad that they are open late for after theater meal.

We had dinner here for our 8 year anniversary back in February. The food was great, but the service was truly exceptional. The attention to detail was beyond and they made it a very special dinner for us.

Super expensive food.   We made reservations and because of that we had to either eat the three course or six course meal.  Kid just wanted the hamburger that was on the website but apparently you can only get that in the bar.   I guess the customer is always wrong at this place.   Food wasn't anything special, but especially for the $600 price tag.  Waitress had the gall to tell us to come back tomorrow to get a burger 10 ft from where we were sitting.   Ridiculous.

BOTTOM LINE: worth...every...coin. It's rates 4.5 stars on Yelp for good reason
TIP/S: ask for Kevin to experience first class dining. Tip is included in your bill.
...WHO: party of 1
WHY: Restaurant Week (i later found out they don't participate in RW)
WHAT: (Deets) From the moment I entered, i was excited to be here. I sat near the window in a lounge chair dining at a table garnished with a personal garden of small blooms and rosemary. Can't have cheese for the week so Kevin made sure I had the salted wheat biscuit, YUM! I had a perfectly-salted fish bite on a wafer to begin. Water was served in branded glass bottles and left (and refilled) at the table upon request. I enjoyed the char salad, light, bright & delish, similar in appearance and mouth feel to salmon. I enjoyed my beet salad the most. It was a feast for the eyes of magenta and grassy greens with a touch of mint to punch up the flavor bouquet. The duck Andouille sausage with grits & peaches, expected but unexpected. Kevin shared that the establishment uses locally-sourced food, shopping at the farmer's market several blocks away, and their own butchery team (I believe). I completed the experience with the Lavender custard with berries (very creme brûlée, which, is my FAVE non-chocolate dessert). In short, the flavor-texture combo made my mouth happy. Treat yourself if you're in the area!
WHEN: lunchtime 7/22/19
WHERE: take away
HOW: bike/ public transportation 4/5/6 L Q/N/R trains
BATHROOM: Did not use
WIFI: did not use
DRESS CODE: smart casual
SERVICE: Kevin was DIVINE. I can't say enough about the elevated dining experience that Kevin facilitated. WHEN, you go, because, you'll go, ask for Kevin. Thank me later.

We celebrated my birthday party there. From the moment we entered the restaurant, the service and attention to detail was exceptional. I really liked the Roberta Bendavid's flower arrangements. We ordered 2 seasonal tasting menus with wine pairings. The food was fresh and delicious. It's a wonderful place to celebrate your special event.

Always perfect, the redefinition of five stars. Yelp should have a five stars plus reserved for fine dining. 

Stopped into the dining room for lunch today. Had four fantastic entrees. I would have been just as happy in the tavern.  We were initially a two top, but picked up two more this morning. Rez change was accommodated, we just had to arrive 15 minutes earlier. All done through OpenTable. 

We had monkfish, the crispy chicken, and snuck in a stir fry for our vegetarian friend from the tavern menu. 

Amazing to appreciate the flavor profiles, knife skills, and team of servers. 

I haven't been to GT in a while, I like they went to the "gratuity included" model. Take the work out of the guests and just tell us what things cost. 

Bread service and rugelach at check presentation time were a really nice touch. Rugelach was incredible. 

We had to be out speedy given it was a business lunch, and they made it happen!  We forwent apps and dessert, which might be a sin, and there is always next time. We ended up having cold brew lattes and "dough" donuts back at the office with the rest of the team.

So good!! Went here for a nice dinner with my dad without a reservation and ate on the tavern side. That being said, was not disappointed at all. It was amazing with 100% the same quality service and food as the dining room.

Not for the faint of heart, I love to visit this restaurant and feel like Chef Anthony is always updating the menu. Lots of options, great wine selection, and lots of bustle. If you find yourself in the vicinity of Park and 23rd. Check it out.

Absolutely my go-to spot whenever I'm in NYC! Friendly staff and amazing food, consistent perfection just as I remembered since first visit . Can't really describe all the details in one short review, but those little details they put into customer service and food is worth a million.

Unpretentiously delicious. Came here with colleagues for lunch today and had a delicious meal off of the a-la carte menu. 

You can expect top notch service and delicious food that isn't trying to be what it's not. The food is unfussy, delicious, and beautifully presented. Come for good food in an upscale place where you can still be yourself.

Ordered the lobster to start - this was stellar. A good amount of fresh lobster paired with a light base. The perfect way to start. 

My main, the GT burger, was quite possibly the best burger I've had. Perfect ratio of meat to bun, and the beef was tender and flavorful. 

Would highly recommend a meal here!

It is a nice place to come to celebrate a special occasion. 
I've made a reservation for a dinner do two and we were sat on time. They have a prefixed menu and you do not need to tip, cause it already included. 
I tried beef tartar, it was lacking some seasoning, but overall the I'm at was cash with a nice presentation. My husband got calamari I would say they were better seasoned. For the second course, I got a lamb dish, highly recommend, soft medium rear piece, seasoned beautifully, garnished with grilled veggies. My husband got tuna, which they overcooked and instead of medium-rare, he got medium to well- done piece. Disappointing for such should be the perfect place. 
After dinner, they offer some cheese selection to try. 
The desserts were outstanding, even though our waiter almost forgot about our tea/coffee, we still had a good time.
I doubt that I will come back to this place, New York has so much to offer and even better places. For the price you pay, you will get solid service with good ( but not great) food.
I really enjoyed sitting at the bar and having a few drinks. The bartenders are excellent and the service is phenomenal. I highly recommend this place.

Just amazing. Every. Single. Time. As good as it was over 20 years ago, when I first walked in. The food is amazing-- but what really makes this place special is the service. It feels like you are the only one in the room. Family. Home.

There is a LIVE BUG found in my food!!!!!! And I am half way done of that dishes. Vomit right away! Only took that dish off my bill. There is a potential health issue which is more that that 25 dollars!!! Photo for evidence! I will also report to health department!! Unforgivable for restaurant like this.
Phenomenal as always.  Can't say enough good things about this restaurant.   Went for lunch and did the tasting menu w wine pairing.  Perfectly paired.

This place was excellent. I sat at the bar for some wine and got the best service I would have asked for. The bartender Ben allowed me to try as many types of wine as I wanted until I found the right one. The place is really pretty and had also a great selection of cocktails. It does get busy and even to sit at the bar you will have to wait in line for a few minutes!

Wow! A meal at Gramercy Tavern feels like a staycation. The restaurant's interior is tastefully decorated with greenery and flowers, and the staff is so friendly and accommodating. I dined at the bar, and they were very attentive - constantly filling my water and making sure I didn't need anything. I started with rose and a complimentary bread (blueberry cheddar in this case), both of which were fantastic. For my meal, I had the burger. It was delectably juicy, and the chips were well-seasoned and crisp. Don't be too scared of the prices - gratuity is included! Whether it's date night or you're catching up with a friend, GT provides a luxurious dining experience with a seasonally appropriate menu and great wine selection!

As usual. Chef does not disappoint. 
Summer tasting menu and wine pairing i
Was spot on. We came in for a bite and was
Lured to the tasting menu. 
Toni was amazing as our server. And of course Shioban was the most amazing host. She is such an amazing manager. 
Thank you to all. We will see you soon  
Lots of love to the entire staff not mentioned by name. It's the little things you do. There's nothing bigger.

Came here for my birthday lunch. First of all, service is 5/5. The waiters are so observant and welcoming, they ensured that the entire meal went smoothly and were attentive, refilling waters and asking us if we wanted more bread without us even asking. 

The bread, as raves about in many previous reviews, is delicious!!! I think it is whole grain or some kind of grain, and it is perfectly buttery without being over buttery and it just comes off in sheets. The outside is firm but not crunchy and the inside and so fluffy. It is paired with a goat cheese spread which is so light and just delicious!!!

My friend and I got the tasting menu for lunch, which is an affordable option to get a sense of the wide variety of seasonal foods they can provide. The scallops were so fresh and light. The tilefish was just okay to me, didn't really stand out. Neither did the tagliarini, which seemed quite salty to me. The duck breast was delicious!!! After the four courses, I wasn't overstuffed, as the portions were actually quite light, so I was excited for dessert. 

They so kindly allowed me to switch out the strawberries dessert for the cookies and milk so my friend and I could share. Also for dessert they brought out complimentary chocolate and gummy candies as well as a birthday coconut cake for me. There were so many desserts on the table, it was an entire meal in it of itself. Everything was so delicious. I loved my friends strawberries dessert with whipped cheesecake, and the cookies all were so fun to taste. Their milk also is so refreshing has a hint of another flavor (vanilla?). We couldn't finish everything and I wish I could eat more of the coconut cake because that was also so good but also quite sweet. 

I gave it 4/5 stars because two of the tasting menu dishes didn't quite impress me. I wish I could have tried their burger, but I guess I'll have to come back again to do so!!! Can't wait to see them again :)
Went there with my wife and daughter on a Friday night. It was crowded but service was incredible.  I had the meatball dish which was so tender and flavorful!

Finally, I came here to dine with family on a Friday summer evening in The Tavern (walk-ins only). At 6 pm, it was pretty busy and service was very good. The starter bread was phenomenal that I had to ask for just one more piece. We split the dishes and got the grilled tuna, duck, and wagyu meatballs. In the beginning, I thought the portions looked small but I ended up being very full. We were so stuffed that by the time dessert rolled around, we shared the ricotta donuts with jam -- they were simply divine. Totally recommend a visit at least once.

One of the hardest yelp reviews for me, is at Gramercy Tavern. Let me tell you my pros first...
We LOVE this place. Normally we sit at the bar, which we love the process of getting seated. Say goodbye to the stalking of bar seats. When you arrive, tell the bartender you want to sit at the bar and they will put you on the list to be seated. So just order a drink, and hang out! You will get called over when your seat is open. 
Also the pros- the drinks, food and service! Martinis and wine selection are amazing. The char grilled oyster recipe changes frequently, but whatever it is - GET IT. You will send me a message thanking me later. The bartenders are hospitable, attentive and all around great people! 
Now, I hate eating this anything less than a 5. We have always had amazing experiences here, but this needs to be noted. 
For my birthday, I wanted to come to Gramercy for drinks since it is one of my favorites. We go with a few friends, order drinks and some apps including the seafood tower. My husband is allergic to nuts, so naturally I look and make sure that nothing includes nuts as well as alert the person taking the order. When the tower arrives, there was an arctic char seafood that had some questionable toppings. I tasted and immediately asked again to the bartender - are you sure this isn't nuts?? He said no, it's mustard seeds. Another friend of ours did the same thing and also questioned. My husband then had a bite, and at that point the bartender went back to the kitchen to double check (after we said something 3 times now) they were mustard seeds....he comes back a few minutes later and it turns out the kitchen changed the recipe and instead of mustard seeds, they are now PINE NUTS.  
I'll let this sink in, and for anyone that has a loved one that is allergic to nuts im sure you are saying - WTF. I am really sad I need to give negative comments here, but allergies are incredibly important! I have no idea how the kitchen changed a recipe to include nuts but didn't inform the bartenders?! Or the bartenders didn't pay attention!? But honestly - Doesn't anyone realize that nut allergies are life threatening???
Needless to say, my birthday was ruined. Not happy given I normally love this restaurant, but not sure if I can get around the fact that they were so careless with nuts

I have never in my life been to a restaurant that paid so much attention to detail. It opens at noon for lunch, and we were able to get a spot at the bar because we were in line outside at 11:45. We did not need a reservation to sit at the bar, however I believe one would have been necessary to have lunch in the restaurant. My boyfriend pointed out to me that this is one of the few restaurants in the country that has earned a Michelin star. I had a pumpkin soup and it was incredible! I had mint hot tea that was completely prepared behind the bar and all I had to do is pour it into my cup. My boyfriend had an incredible, grass fed beef burger which was prepared perfectly. He was even offered simple syrup as well as other accoutrements to go with his iced tea. It's also kind of cool that this is a non-tipping restaurant, as the Bartender explained to us that the employees split the profits of the restaurant.

I was very disappointed about our experience at Gramercy Tavern. While ambiance and service are nearly impeccable, the cost of our dinner was completely unjustified, some might say morally questionable. 

The unsophisticated 3-course menu was a far cry from what anyone who's experienced the New York city's scene would call fine dining. Yet it was priced more highly than many (excellent) fine dining restaurants in town. 

More disturbingly, my appetizer (a plain tomato salad) and desert (a berry cake & frozen yogurt) were prized at what I would estimate $40 and $30, respectively. A beef tartare or a seafood appetizer were prized the same, as the menu was prix fixe.

I invite the management team at Gramercy Tavern to rethink their policy, use some humility, and be more responsible.
I do love this place. Good food and great service. Food is always fresh and special. Great cocktails too.

Gramercy is truly an institution that lives up to all hype.  Tavern takes reservations but also has about 20 seats at the bar which are first come and full menu.  Food isn't too expensive given the tip is included, so a $32 burger really sits at about $27 which isn't absurd given how good it is.  Cooked perfectly medium rare and a thick cut of bacon/ham and some of the best cheese I've ever had.  Had that french onion cheese feel that gave each bite a full texture.  Juices flow and the bun was so pillowy that you could peel it layer by layer.  Sesame seed of course is way to go and meat itself was great quality.  I asked for a different side to chips and I got some pickled veggies which are on the bar menu, but I think compliment the burger well with a little sourness to the burgers savory.  Cocktails are fire and really can't go wrong with anything.  Their rendition will be one of the best of whatever you order.  I personally had a house manhattan, up, that apparently used to be on the house menu, and I know why because it was boozy, no sugar, and easy to swallow.  Great drink and great food.  Servers are busy but keep you in mind. They remember your name from the onset and monitor you like a good waiter should.  Super polite and just friendly.  I would definitely recommend the bar to anyone trying to get a New York meal.  Could easily stay here for hours drinking and eating, and though it won't be cheap, will be better off here than trying to snag a $30 cocktail or $60 steak elsewhere.

I had really high expectations for this place but it was very underwhelming. The pre-fix menu of $120 comes with one appetizer, one main (same size as appetizer), and a dessert. I can't eat much but i was definitely hungry after the meal. Not to mention that the food was extremely salty....

Sat dining room on a Wednesday night visiting NYC. 9pm res but not seated until 930. Bought us a drink so not a problem.  Generally Good food. Everything was fine. The frequency of service makes it feel like it is well executed but after our tasting we were disappointed to not receive the items listed on the menu. Promise of scallops and halibut answered with fluke and tile fish. It's ok to sub but maybe let us know that you're out? Bad form. 

Everything else was ok. Service was attentive. Wine pairing was adequate though not incredible. The scallop pairing was terrible (sau blanc) but that might have been because we got fluke and not scallops. :/

Wanted this to be an excellent meal but was pretty underwhelmed. Food in the tavern side looked good while I was waiting. Perhaps we try that next time instead.

Oyster raw and cooked to perfect.. peppers were average but the accompanying sauce was dangerously good... the burger was cooked to perfection and the chocolate pudding is what I want to be incorporated into my last meal!

One of the most refined dining experiences in New York, where the staff is passionate about the food, wine list and providing the best service. This is a non tipping restaurant, meaning the place actually cares about their employees. Now for the food: Go for the dining room, as the menu and ambience is so much better there, The best courses were the starters and fish dishes, the pork loin had a bit too much seasoning for my taste. I did not go for wine pairing because I am very particular about my wine, but they do have a very great wine list where you can find almost anything you are looking for. I say almost because they didn't have Billecart Salmon Rosé Brut. 
I will definitely come back to try more dishes.
Love the no tipping concept and the staffs attitude about it.  The food very good, not necessarily cutting edge, but very good.

It's hard to get a five star rating - as most people don't think any place can live up to the 'hype'.  This place is it.  Expensive - and worth every penny.  Service, ambiance and dining experience are incredible.  Wish there was a little more room to wait for your table in the bar - but who cares when your meal is that good?  Attention to detail was amazing - as was our three course meal.  Make main dining room reservation 28 days in advance - and then anxiously wait for this experience!

Gramercy Tavern was absolutely unreal. Went for a business lunch with a client and did the seasonal tasting menu. 

First off the bread they serve you is incredible. I don't know what kind of crack they're putting in it but the dough is the perfect consistency and taste and they too it off with a goat cheese spread instead of butter. I almost cried from happiness. 

First course was fluke with Apple and radish. It was SO good as a cold dish with a good sweet and savory flavor. 

Second was halibut with cannelini beans and kale - the sauce was so good I literally spooned it into my mouth when I was out of solid food. 

Third was my favorite dish, the squid ink pasta with Brussel sprouts and some crunchy breaded thing. (??) It was SOOOO tasty that I again spooned the remaining sauce into my mouth sans pasta or sprout or crunchy breaded thing. 

The final savory dish was roasted duck with confit. I can be picky with duck and this was probably my favorite duck dish to date. 

Lastly we got three desserts - an Apple cidery sorbet that was like cold icy applesauce and so good. We also had these delicious passion fruit chocolate bonbons that looked to be beautifully hand painted and coconut lime jellies. The main dessert was strawberries and cream and was absolutely delectable. 

All in all it was a fantastic meal. Drinks and tasting came to almost $600 for 5 people. Service was great (although a little slow at the ordering but we were indecisive the first time they came around so understandable). Highly recommend!
Had a very sub par dinner at Gramercy tavern. Did the fixed expensive menu.  Total disappointment.  Food ok, service terrible. For the price, will not return!!!!!

Came for celebrate my birthday last night. The service is 5 stars!! Very attentive and friendly kind. Also the room decoration was beautiful,  dry classic. I love it. 

The food is just ok for me. Some of the dishes taste salty. Most I liked was vegetables dishes. Soon, I will try lunch to see how the food taste look like. Little bit disappointed from last night dishes because most of reviews says the food is incredible in here.

I had a lovely dinner experience with friends at Gramercy Tavern. The food is fresh and delicious, quite reminiscent of the food-to-table restaurants of Greece and France. 

Our table went for the three course meal and it was as if the food was prepared for the gods! The tomatoes were just right and the chicken spoke to my soul with its flavor and tenderness. 

The service provided by our waitress and our sommelier was charming and kind. They made us feel as if they were old friends and I recommend you dine here for this reason alone!

Ate in the tavern. Please note that not everything in the dining room menu is available in the tavern.

The service in the tavern was AMAZING! At least 8 people worked our table. This may be due to the no-tip policy. It made for a magnificent experience.

If you look at the prices on their web-site, this is worth keeping in mind.

Surprisingly I've never been to Gramercy Tavern after all my years of working in and visiting NYC and Wow!  What a fabulous experience!  There for our anniversary, we ordered the tasting menu which was amazing - each dish was better than the next and our server, Amanda was awesome.  Gramercy Tavern - my new most fave restaurant in NYC!  Amazing food, top notch hospitality....Gramercy Tavern is a very special place...

Recently had a business dinner in a private room at the Gramercy Tavern.  We started with hors d'oeuvres which were varied and good (especially the tomato tartelette.)  Whoever had selected the wine did an excellent job.  I stuck to white wine and first enjoyed a very good white Bordeaux and then a white Burgundy (Meursault.)  The dinner itself was very good.  I selected a tomato salad with burrata cheese as starter, then followed with an excellent bar; and finished with fresh fruit.  I will return here.

over rated, over priced, they just dont care,
your just another customer 
im tired of these corporate chains 

du urself a favor, seek out one offs, owner operated

I did the following night for dinner

MUCH better experience

Formerly a gem. When visiting NYC, have frequently visited Gramercy with my spouse, friends and clients, with visits dating back at least twenty years. So even though our last visit was not the best experience, I thought I'd take the my kids there on their first visit to NYC. So do the ridiculous wait to make a reservation one month in advance, call exactly when the restaurant opens, get put on hold for five minutes ... and then told there was no availability for our date. The woman answering the phone was downright rude. I was going to go one star, but decided to respect  when this place used to be a great dining destination.
This place was recommended by several co workers, however for the price was a major disappointment. The service was all over the place, which

Just amazing! I can't say enough good things about my experience here. I can't wait to go back. The entire staff from the front to the back of the house were incredibly friendly and welcoming. The decor was beautiful and seasonally decorated with lots of autumn things. I opted for the seasonal tasting menu with the wine pairing. Worth every penny.

Tasting menu for 14/10/2019:

1. Marinated Scallops: pretty nice, served with bits of fruit mixed into it. the scallops don't taste that strong or anything, so this was good for an appetizer.

2. Poached Lobster: this came with a little bit of sauce, which I thought gave it a distinct secondary flavor. still, not super strong tasting, and good for an appetizer.

3. Fish: I actually have forgotten what kind of fish they served. it wasn't sea bass, but it was really nice, very soft and creamy, yet cooked with just the right amount of sear. probably my favorite dish of the evening.

4. Tagliarini: probably the most underwhelming dish. it tasted fine, but the noodles and the rest of the dish reminded me quite a bit of tomato flavored instant noodles.

5. Duck Breast & Smoked Thigh: the smoked thigh is really where most of the flavor is at, so i recommend you eat the breast together with it, instead of eating these things separately. very nice overall.

6. Caramel Pears: way better than what I was expecting. the pears were great, the ice cream was surprisingly even better. where did they get it?

There are also a number of non featured items that we got to eat, such as the bread, the fruit candy thing, the chocolate, some sort of pomagranite juice... overall, I was pretty satisfied with the food. 

The one down side I think is they don't give you a ton of food here, which I think is standard fare for michelin places such as this. I wouldn't say I left hungry or anything, but I don't think I felt full, and that I would say is largely due to the two pieces of bread I ate. For roughly $200, I would have liked to have left a little more full than I was. Service here, of course, is excellent. Our waitress was very knowledgable about all the dishes, and gave a very good recommendation for a wine pairing. The no tip feature is also SUPER WELCOME, THANK YOU FOR THIS. Oh, and in case you're curious, you should budget about 2.5 hours for your tasting menu experience. I'd love to come again sometime, though I think I also have interest in trying a three course meal, or visiting the tavern as well.

This is in the running for the, if not the single, best overall dining experience I've ever had. From the waiters polite, but not intrusive attentiveness, to the food, to the wine pairings, to the way they timed things for us to see our show, it was spectacularly well-done.

My wife and I came here for our 10th wedding anniversary before going to see a 7p show of Hadestown. Only the dining room takes reservations and only at 5p or later. I gave them a call and asked if that would work and they suggested that we do the three-course prix fixe menu rather than the six-course tasting menu just because they felt like it would lead to a nicer and better-paced dining experience.

They were totally right. Between the courses pacing and the wine pairings, the 90-minute meal with 3 courses was just about right for a fun, yummy leisurely, celebratory meal. Beyond that, the were more than happy to let us swap out anything from the tasting menu into the three-course prix fixe menu and were more than happy to do wine pairings for us on the three-course menu. The wine pairings were well-thought-out, somewhat surprising at times, but ally good and they were more than happy to take something back and try again if it really didn't work.

As we sat down, they poured us champagne to toast to our anniversary and left us to that for a few minutes before coming back to get the meal started. That was sort of emblematic of the attention to detail for the whole meal.

The first thing to come out was an on-the-house appetizer of grilled romano beans with eggplant purée. While not the hit of the night, it was certainly delicious and impressive with how something this simple could be this good. Periodically, they would bring out their dinner buns with whipped goat cheese butter starting with this course. The whipped goat cheese butter was very, very good, but not quite the ambrosia I had hoped for given what it was made with. Still the little bit of tartness from the goat cheese really ups the buttered bread in a way that I'd love to have more of.

For our first course I had the beef tartare with pine nuts, rye toast, and pickled mushrooms. My wife had the ruby red shrimp with cauliflower, shell beans, and bacon. While both were good, the beef tartare was pretty spectacular, while I thought the shrimp were merely good. That being said, my wife just didn't want to do raw beef, which I get. So, to each their own.

For mains, I had the monkfish with sungold tomatoes, summer squash, and mussels. It was stunning. The fish was perfectly cooked and just a hint of being firm, while still being buttery and moist. My wife got the beef with mashed potatoes, which was also great although I tend to have an easier time finding a good steak than good seafood. Still, I'm super-picky about my beef and this was more than up for the challenge.

For desert, we got the cookie plate with milk, the chocolate tart with raspberries, raspberry jam and bourbon ice cream, and if that wasn't enough they brought us a coconut cake covered with coconut meringue on the house for our anniversary. Beyond all that, they sent us home with two small gummies and  two chocolate truffles, which I think they give to everyone who comes regardless.

We couldn't finish desert and ended up bringing the gummies, truffles and most of the cookie plate with us for later, but man were they good later. The truffles were almost as good as a Teuscher champagne truffle, which is kind of insane and all the cookies were different and great to try.

The winner of the deserts was really the coconut cake, which they should put on the menu. It was dense, moist and spectacular with the meringue offering some interesting texture as well as some appropriate airiness to the complete coconut package.

The chocolate tart was also good, and bourbon ice cream is great, but a chocolate tart with raspberries is something I've had done well elsewhere.

The desert wine pairings were especially well-done with my wife getting a very interesting sweet mead that was unexpected and incredibly well-paired.

Just has to has to be my 50th meal at Gramercy tavern this very afternoon - always delightful except for the first time I felt the wine steward was not knowledgeable. She was also not very interested in her job. Oh well hope the next time is better
Best overall experience and its an institution for a reason. They are consistently great in all respects.

10/27/19 Tasting Menu

1. Squash Mousse/Pudding Amuse Bouche - this was delicious and I wish I had more of it! 5/5

2. Marinated Fluke - I enjoyed this dish. The fluke was fresh and the marinade was not overpowering. It was like a ceviche so I feel like you can never go wrong and lacked some creativity. 4/5

3. Scallops with Mushroom - my first bite was a bit salty because of the soy sauce so I was a bit thrown off. My fiance enjoyed it. I think the soy sauce overpowered the scallop and was a bit salty for my taste. 3/5

4. Arctic Char w/ Cabbage - MY FAVE! The arctic char was cooked perfectly -- there was so many complex levels of flavor here and it wasn't because of the sauce or anything -- simply because the fish was fresh and really good. Cooked perfectly. 5/5

5. Tagliarini - disappointed. It was overly salted ramen. The soup base was too watery and salty. I wish the sauce was thicker (and less salty) so that the sauce can coat the tiny thin noodles... It was a huge miss. 1/5.

6. Duck Breast w/ Bacon and Grapes - again, super salty... especially with the Bacon. I needed more grapes and cabbage to cut the saltiness with some acidity. We didn't need the bacon on the dish. The duck breast was cooked fine but nothing creative here. 1/5.

7. Caramel Pears w/ Brie Ice Cream - heard GT's dessert is one of the best in town and this dish did not disappoint. The homemade toffee was not too sweet and had this buttery velvety texture. This paired well with the poached pairs and Brie ice cream. 5/5.

Overall, the experience was underwhelming-- from the food to the service. The service wasn't terrible but it didn't feel personal. Only 2 of the whole meal really left a lasting impression -- not worth the price we paid. I expected more dishes to blow my mind but it just fell flat to me.

Funny postscript to this review. Management has arranged 4 calls with me. Never once have they called and actually listened to my complaints.  They simply don't care.  It's a name and reputation and am embarrassing testament to everything wrong in the hospitality and restaurant industry.  $200-400 for horrible service, ridiculously bad attitude and a staff that doesn't care.  The steak was served ice cold too!

Lunch in the Tavern is always a wonderful experience.  The menu is usually more innovative and interesting than the main dining room.
Our only complaint, and this includes our experiences at other Union Square Hospitality Restaurants,  is that the espresso is awful!  It is con sistently sour and bitter.   How about trying  another coffee purveyor....
Please....

Have you ever had a love interest you pined so long for only to find out, when you finally had a chance to go out with her, that there wasn't really anything that special about her? That's what I felt about Gramercy Tavern.

I've been wanting to go here for 20 years. I finally got the chance. And it was nothing special.

The food was fine but I was looking for wow. The service was fine but I was looking for wow. The atmosphere was fine but I was looking for wow. 

"Had a nice time" and peck on the cheek. No need for a second date! 

Slightly upturned face.

Excellent. As always. Sat at the bar twice during a recent NYC trip, the absolute highlight of the trip. Had the seafood stew and the monkfish (although could have sworn it was swordfish on the menu, didn't matter, it was great) both wonderful. Came for dinner after having lunch at the "best"restaurant in NYC, and the overall experience here was MUCH better here. Warm, inviting, bartenders and staff are always so friendly.  Perfect restaurant experience, the kind of place you plan a trip around

Wait staff most unfriendly of any restaurant I have been in recently. Acted liked they could not wait for the evening to end.

Would not have hired any of the bunch.

Cuisine was a C+ and not worth the ridiculous over priced pre fixe price of big $$$$$. 

Tip is automatically included. Explains why the staff is not customer service motivated. i.e. They get a nice paycheck regardless of their performance.

Went there on a Saturday evening. NYC has to many great restaurants to revisit this tourist trap.

Lived up to its high rating.  Beet salad was excellent, lamb was one of the best cuts I've ever had, and the sauce was unique and delicious. Service was outstanding - listened carefully to my dietary restrictions and found great combos.

We flew from SF to NYC for one night only, and I really wanted my husband to try the Tavern. It was Saturday night, and we were told the wait would be 2 1/2 hours. We chose to wait and spent the time shopping nearby on 5th Ave. We ended up getting seated an hour and 45 min later. It was soooo worth the wait. 

We LOVED everything about our experience - From the service, the ambiance, decor, and oh the FOOD!

We started out with the seafood platter - everything was super fresh. The Lobster salad was the standout. 

For our main course, my husband chose the Waygu meatballs. I was on the fence between the chicken under the brick and the seafood stew and opted for the chicken When we got our dishes, the super nice gentleman Rojales (Sp?)  brought us a sample of the seafood stew to try. Who does that?? 

Everything we had were so delicious, and the entire experience was memorable and made it worth our trip! 

This will remain my favorite restaurant in NYC.

Don't get me wrong. I love this place after coming here for the second time for their tasting menu. I just don't think it's worth the price tag anymore. There are just so many other innovative and creative restaurants in the area and Brooklyn. 

Service is still as always top notch. If you are not use to being always attended to, you might feel a little awkward during dinner. I felt like I have to dine on my best manner. It's not a big deal overall. You can always dine in the walk in section of course or the bar. They don't have fries but so kindly serve up potatoes chip to my young nephew and that keep him pretty calm during the dining. 

Most of the dishes are amazing and well crafted. I enjoy every dish but not as memorable anymore. Love the fish and lamb thou. They are delicious but I remembered Gramercy used to be memorable. My first time here was for my anniversary and I remember every bite from them servicing is a champagne to celebrate with us. And the duck I had. 

Overall this is decent on my book but as a newer generation of diner, there are just so many other places.

It was amazing experience for me and my boyfriend. Was beyond my expectations.. our server tony was very friendly and attentive as well as our busser / runner Tyler who was super friendly and professional. I am super impressed by our sommelier Alvaro , who was very informative and had a excellent knowledge about wine and very  comforting hospitality. food was delicious and favourful with wonderful plating

My boyfriend and I came for a late lunch to try the tasting menu.  GT is a NY standby and I was curious to check it out.  TLDR Overrated, and had some MAJOR service issues and also fruit flies, though the food was quite good.  Fruit flies and mediocre service were not really what we were paying $300 for lunch for.

The place is certainly bustling and we had to wait for a bit to be seated despite having reservations.  The vibe is tavern-y and lively, and I would probably come back to go to the Tavern part in the front.

We sat in the back dining room and the service issues began pretty quickly.  Our waiter was very slow to take our order or bring us water, and we felt ignored/had to catch his attention.  Also, when he first walked over, he tripped and dropped the menu on the table, knocking over the glasses (which were empty at the time).  Which I wasn't really troubled by at first since whatever were all human and people trip sometimes.  The issue is more what came next.

Then, when I asked what the vegetarian tasting menu included, he just listed a bunch of ingredients "eggplant, broccoli, sweet potato..." but had literally no description of what the dishes were.

Side note, he said the entree was eggplant and there was NO eggplant at any point during the meal.  Also another waiter later brought by the vegetarian menu because we asked to keep a list of the wines, and I was annoyed our first waiter hadn't mentioned or offered to bring the menu (I thought maybe there wasn't a printed menu for the vegetarian tasting menu).  

We got the tasting menus plus wine pairing, and again, the service for our first course was out of step.  The wine came out a full 10 minutes before the dish, and we finished them before the dish came (and cider and white wine would not be good warm either as time passed).

Last note is that there were fruit flies specifically around our table for some reason.  But we saw them flying around our drinks and then landing on the curtains by us, so maybe the curtains hadn't been cleaned or something, not really sure.  I mentioned this to our first bus woman and she blew it off, by saying "oh, they're probably just attracted to the wine" and walked off.  Which was a pretty egregious thing to say in a "fine dining" establishment.  This response was very annoying, and I feel irritated just remembering it.

Note that I raised it again with our waiter and they moved us to a different table (with a slight apology that it was because of the fresh flowers they bring in sometimes bring in fruit flies) and our service was much better and smoother after that point (with a different set of wait staff).  Truly, our initial waiter and bus woman should NOT have been at a nice restaurant since they had kind of sour attitudes and also were not helpful in describing dishes or resolving issues.

Ok, final note on the food--it was really beautiful presentation and tasty dishes.  And even more than that, the wine pairings were impressive in that I got exclusively white wine and each one was different and delicious, and I typically am not a white wine drinker!

Other side note, in the restroom, I also heard two women complaining that the service has really declined over time, so it seems this sentiment is shared. 

Had a good time because of the company and the story, but there are better places out there for a nice meal in NYC.  

*end rant* :)

Five star experience by far! I would totally recommend! The food blew our expectations away! We came here for our honeymoon, and Gramercy Tavern treated us so well! Check out our pictures! Will D, one of the chefs there  was amazing to us! Thank you!

This is one of the best places I have been to and eaten at. It is more of an experience than a dinner. And Aiysha was our waitress - and her knowledge and service was not just A+, but was the best I have ever seen!

Delicious unique dining experience in NYC. Introduced to Gramercy Tavern from watching a segment on CBS Sunday Morning about the owner and his restaurants. They also incorporate a non tipping policy. Both the service and food was excellent. We had the three course appetizer, entree and desert for $134.

One of the best meals my wife and I have had in quite some time. The staff is very warm and professional and the decor would be what I would call a combination of sophisticated with a few rustic tones. We were celebrating our first wedding anniversary and were greeted with a glass of champagne and also added a complimentary dessert.  You can dine ala carte but we opted for the seasonal tasting menu.  The five courses consisted of fluke, smoked arctic char (which was our star of the night), squid ink and lobster pasta, duck, and a caramelized pear dessert.  We could not find a single thing to complain about and will certainly be returning.

My husband and I went here to celebrate him passing the NY Bar and it was perfect. First off, make sure to mention if you are celebrating something because they really went above and beyond! We were greeted with complimentary champagne as well as several "Congratulations" through out our meal from different staff members. They also brought out a complimentary dessert as well that said Congratulations on it.

We sat in the main dining room. There are 2 different choices. You can do the tasting menu where you get a small portion of 6 different dishes or you can do the 3 course option (bigger portions but only 3 different dishes). The 3 course option is cheaper by about $50ish a person (I don't remember the exact price difference). We opted to do the 3 course option and it was delicious. We were really pleased with our experience here. The service was amazing in my opinion, which just added to the whole evening. There is a seafood dish that has pork dumplings on the bottom and it was amazing! My favorite dish of the night. 

I would definitely recommend giving this restaurant a try at least once!

One of the places that was on my list for quite some time.

We came here and did something rather unconventional for us, we ordered the normal tasting menu and a vegetarian tasting menu. Since we wanted to try as many dishes as possible, this seemed like the best option.

What I remembered about the tasting menu here was that the vegetarian one was superior in taste. Some of this could be that I haven't had a vegetarian tasting menu at such a fancy place before, so relatively this should be a lot better than other vegetarian dishes I've had.

My favorite dish of the night was the first vegetarian course, the gazpacho. It was such a refreshing dish with so many different textures and flavors all perfectly mixed together to not overwhelm your taste buds.

Some of the meat dishes, I just didn't think the ingredients were integrated well. It was like, this squid ink pasta is good and this lobster is good, so let's combine them. Then the pasta was just a bit too firm for the delicate lobster and you could not eat the two together.

What I appreciated from this place was that vegetarian tasting menus can indeed be tasty.

This is a gem and a classic of NYC. There is no way you can fail here. They will always be outstanding on service, food and taking care of everything. For my spouse and I this is our favorite restaurant for special occasions. Expensive but worth it!

I suck at remembering movie lines...but I do remember in 'Elf' when Will Farrell ducked his head into a diner and said something like "World's best cup of coffee? Congratulations!"

That was going thru my head as we approached GT as part of an ongoing search for the world's best burger. 

(Quick side-story. We lived in Nederland. A colleague heard of my search and recommended Frankenburger in Utrecht. I called my wife, she grabbed the kids and we drove over separately. Couldn't find the blue boxes for parking passes, so we parked together in an apparently free zone. Ate two yucky burgers in 15 minutes, came back to find 500 euro in parking tickets...250 on each car. 0 stars for Utrecht's predatory parking!)

Back to GT...confidence increased as we crossed the threshold and sensed the real-deal ambiance & hustle/bustle. Then the hostess who assured we had arrived at burger heaven. Then the menu, whose price for the burger literally check-raised the hostess' bet. 

My skepticism began to turn as we Hoovered the bread basket. Super moist focaccia with thyme. Then the burger. Not gonna slather superlatives. Best $37 I ever spent. The search is over. 

Go, enjoy (and get the pumpkin beignets for dessert), you're welcome.

As you can probably guess, the food here is pretty wonderful. You can tell everything is designed with such care. I also appreciate that they have a vegetarian tasting menu. It's also beautifully decorated. Just be prepared for a very long meal if you are choosing the tasting menu - it's worth it, but you need to allot three hours or more.

I had the pleasure of attending Zagat's 40th anniversary celebration at Gramercy Tavern--to say this was one of the best restaurant experiences of my life would be an understatement.

Everything from the passed appetizers, to the drinks, to the 5-course tasting menu, to the service--was superb. You can easily tell why this place has been around for 25 years and continues to be such a landmark in the NYC dining scene.

As I mentioned before, everything here was absolutely delicious and plated in such a beautiful way. Some of the standouts for me were the oysters, the arctic char, the duck, and the dessert--I know I just named about half of what I ate, but it was all really that fantastic.

In addition, the service was top notch and the ambiance of the dining room/bar were ideal.

Though this isn't the kind of place many of us can really afford to go to regularly, it should definitely be on your list of places to check out at least once for a nice dinner out in the city--you won't be disappointed.

The best in NYC!
This is my third time coming here and the food just gets better and better!
Their food is creative and flavorful, but most of all it is consistent and delicious.
I will say that those with big eyes should go else where. The portions are perfectly appropriate and might underwhelm those that like seeing "a lot" of food.

Ok, ok...the food.
We both ordered black sea-bass in a white wine, garlic, mussel broth. It also had spinach and small white radish that took on the flavor of that heavenly broth and fluffy croutons. The fluffy croutons created such a rich touch to an already delicious dish. His had bacon, mine did not. He was drinking the brother with a spoon, ha! Wow! I love fish and eat a lot of fish and this dish was perfect.

The sides were sesame glazed carrots in a tahini sauce, and Roasted Beets with Ricotta, Hazelnuts, Maple. Yea!

The wine, despite being $29 for a cabernet, was delicious.
This was my only major gripe, the wine pricing. I understand the space is magnificent and the beautiful. They have to pay the rent.

Overall I loved it. 
Thank you for an amazing time! I can't wait to do it again :)
Benny behind the bar is pure class.  He was attentive and accommodating and made us feel welcome on a busy Saturday evening.

Great hospitality, great ambiance, lackluster food.

Overall, we were very disappointed with our burgers at Gramercy Tavern. We have heard amazing things about the famous Tavern Burger and wanted to give it a go. 

We started things off with a few cocktails which were very well prepared and served. Next we enjoyed the mushroom flatbread and baked oysters which were phenomenal. We thought to ourselves "here we go - this is going to be an unbelievable culinary experience". 

That's where it went downhill. We ordered 2 Tavern Burgers and my friend ordered the Lumache pasta. After hearing so much about the burger from friends, colleagues, and social media, we were very excited. The burgers were very dry, flavorless, and overcooked. There were absolutely no juices coming of the the meat patty when you pressed down. The bun was dry as a bone and had some hard parts as if you microwaved your TGI Friday leftovers in your auntie's microwave. 

We all tried my friends pasta and it was outstanding. The two people at the table that ordered the burger were extremely disappointed and joked about how chain restaurants and fast food would even top this. We regret not getting the pasta like my friend did, who enjoyed his entire meal. We had to fight through a terribly cooked burger that tasted like it was sitting under a heat lamp for hours. 

The dessert was unbelievable (pumpkin beignets + macchiato). The burger is a huge miss and we were all very disappointed.
Amazing food, amazing service. The chicken entree is to die for. Cant believe Ive lived in nyc for 12 years and I hadnt been here before. Would come back in a heartbeat!

I live and work in the area so am frequently at Gramercy Tavern for both work and fun. Usually 5 stars but not for Thanksgiving today. We booked a $200 prix fixe lunch and I was surprised (and disappointed) to see that we were seated in the bar area rather than the dining area. My mother has hearing problems so I was concerned about being seated so close to the bar. Luckily it was quiet for the first part until a very loud family showed up and started visiting with their friends at the neighboring table. Suddenly we were surrounded by about 8 people hovering over our table. I was knocked in the head three times and conversation became impossible. It took 20 minutes and 2 requests to the wait staff for anyone on staff to intervene. If I had stood beside their table in the dining room and yelled for 20 minutes, I'm pretty sure I would have been asked to leave!! Totally put a damper on the meal, especially given that we were paying for the same prix fixe as those in the dining room.

We had a wonderful experience here! The food, ambience and the hospitality were all amazing. 
We started with the Brussels sprout salad, it was delightful and all ingredients were matched perfectly. It was plenty for three people.
We ordered the Burger, Bricked Pressed Chicken and Duck Andouille Sausage over grits. I had the andouille, I was initially hesitant at first ordering this dish however; I'm very glad I did. It was truly tasteful and filling without being too heavy.
