The customer service was second to none, it started immediately when you walked in, the hostess was so friendly and cheerful it was very refreshing. I wish I could remember her name to give her the credit she deserves (tall with dark hair) we visited on 11/24/19.
Thank you for an amazing dinner in the Tavern area.

We had a great dinner here during Thanksgiving weekend. Wait was two hours for bar at 4:30 pm but they squeezed us in to dining room much sooner. Burger, Wagy Meatballs, a wonderful salad and Chocolate Pudding Cake- a perfect meal and perfect service.

Thank you to the staff at Gramercy Tavern for an amazing meal! I took my little brother here for a late night birthday dinner since we've been wanting to try out this place for quite some time. I have absolutely no regrets because the experience was amazing from beginning to end.

The service was impeccable. Food was on point. It was an amazing way to end the night. Cheers!

HORRIBLE BAR EXPERIENCE!! However the food was amazing. When we arrived without reservations the host was incredibly kind to put us on a waiting list. (Very tall gorgeous blonde) she took my number and said "30-45minutes but I'll try to get you in sooner". We went next store to have a drink while we waited. Within 10 minutes I got a text our table was ready. We walked in and she said "welcome back Lauren your table is almost ready" big smile and friendly personality. 

Once we were seated it took 15 minutes for the restaurant manager to come over and serve us water. Then another 5 to meet our server. (Medium height with longish brown hair parted in the middle) we ordered our cocktails and food. 20 minutes later our first drinks arrived and as he poured them it was clearly not a martini dry but their house favorite martini. 15 minutes later we had been served our food then finally our correct martinis. 

Checked on us once and then asked are you ready to order dinner. We weren't happy with the service enough to eat more there. When we got the check he Over charged us on a martini fee on top of not offering take the drinks off for us for the mistake and wait. 

The food was incredible but bar service horrible. If I come back it would be to the dining room and request a different server.
Amazing food and great service. Course dinner can take a fairly long time to complete the cycle so make sure you planned for extra time. Hands down that the food is amazing.

At first the wait was intimidating, but a spot at the bar opened up sooner than expected or else I might have left. It's a good thing I didn't! I'm a sucker for grilled oysters and the ones here were no exception! The cheese and garlic flavor went excellently with the oysters, and I used the house bread to get every bit of residue off the shells.

The burger was great, if not very messy. All of the ingredients were of the highest quality, which was evident in every bite. It was messy because it was dripping juice - this is not something you can eat elegantly - leaving the bun pretty soaked, but the still juicy and flavorful burger, and the structurally impressive bun held their own. 

The dessert was the only dish that didn't leave me completely dazzled. Which is not to say it was very bad, though it was a little puzzling. It was a sort of blueberry pie with corn ice cream. There was almost no sweetness, between the tart blueberries, the thick crust, the creme fraiche, corn cracker, and the ice cream which I don't really know how to describe. Overall I thought there was a lot going on. I rarely meet a dessert I don't love, but unfortunately this was one of them.

Overall, I would highly recommend this New York landmark. I once saw it mentioned in a GQ list of classic restaurants worth revisiting often, and I understand why. The ambiance is classy, but not stuffy, while exuding an old-world charm. It's one of the few restaurants that people want to dress up well for, but not in a stuck up way. The one thing I didn't expect, but was pleasantly surprised by, was that the dining room was loud and full of chatter and laughter, the signs of people truly enjoying their meals. The servers did their part in creating  a welcoming and enjoyable atmosphere too, and the fact that this is a non tipping restaurant should be appreciated.

Absolutely amazing restaurant in every aspect. My goal is to visit every Michelin Star restaurant, and this has been at the top of my list for quite a while. 

From the moment we stepped in, we were welcomed warmly and were able to five our bags and coats to coat check. We were walked back to our corner table, and I got to see the restaurant in full. It's a beautiful space, every table angled and painting hung just right. I got a peek at tons of dishes and everything looked absolutely delicious!

We went in for lunch, and while the tasting menu looked absolutely amazing, we decided our stomachs weren't ready for a ton of food just yet. Our server was amazing and knowledgeable, and the service was incredible. Our waters were constantly refilled, something I truly appreciated, having come from a nearby workout. 

We ordered the soup and scallops to start, which were both absolutely delicious. For entrees, my brother ordered the schnitzel while I went for the steak. They actually gave the wrong dish to my brother, which was completely fine as it still looked delicious. They were so apologetic and even offered to let us keep the dish and bring out the one he ordered. The service was amazing throughout and everything was brought out and cleared in a timely fashion. 

Everything was absolutely amazing, and I definitely want to come back for their dinner tasting menu someday!

We had dinner again at Gramercy Tavern last night. This continues to be one of our favorite restaurants in the world. We treat ourselves to dinner there about twice a year, and we have really never had anything less than perfect experience. The maître d' Vanessa always welcomes us warmly and makes us feel right at home. Ask for Lara to be your server; she has the most delightful talent for describing the food you are about to eat. In a rare turn for a Manhattan restaurant, the seats are spaced far enough apart that you truly get to have an intimate dining experience without ever having to raise your voice at the person across the table at you. The chef at Gramercy Tavern is supremely talented at pairing flavors in a way that is innovative and always completely satisfying. We generally get the five course prefix menu with the wine pairing. Often when I order a wine pairing at other restaurants I feel like I am getting whatever wine was left over from prior nights, or wines by the glass that were listed on the menu but did not sell. At Gramercy Tavern the wine pairings are always extremely thoughtful and carefully chosen, served by knowledgeable sommeliers who give you just enough of the story of the wine to make the experience fun. I look forward to many more years of exquisite dining at Gramercy Tavern.

A New York must!   We never miss a chance for lunch. Service is ALWAYS impeccable, and the food is fresh & yummy.  Love the Bloody Mary, and the veggie tasting menu.  Tip is included in bill (they take care of their own),  it extra stars to Stephen, attentive, sweet, professional, ... & cute as Christmas!

We went to Gramercy Park tavern as a work group and our national sales director took us there as a reward for a year well done. It is a very historic and highly rated place to eat and fairly expensive. We had the three-course meal which consisted of a appetizer style choice followed by main course followed by dessert. I chose the lemon and chicken soup followed by the tilefish followed by the cheese platter. The food was fantastic however being a big eater I thought that the portion amounts we were given did not warrant the meal cost of $200 per person. We did not try the tasting-menu although it had some things that looked very good. The staff was incredible. That is the reason for the four star rating and had there been a larger food quantity I definitely would have given them five stars. The bathrooms were small but clean and they did give us some chocolate truffles for dessert which I failed to get pictures of and some banana bread as a parting gift.

If you don't mind paying for the meal this is a great place to eat but reservations are definitely required since it is full of all the time.

My rating system consists of a 3-star being exactly what you expected and neither good nor bad. A 4 means something was extra special and a 5 means you were blown away.  A 2 star rating was disappointing and a 1-star rating is terrible

This review is for a two-person dinner reservation with the 3-course menus. 

Having arrived early, my boyfriend and I checked our coats and sat in their cozy waiting area. They were able to seat us around 15 minutes early and brought us to a corner table.

After snuggling in at our table, our courteous waiter Jason came by to offer us still or complimentary sparkling. He also introduced both of their dinner menus for us: the 3-course meal or the tasting menu with the option of a wine pairing. The restaurant politely asks that there is one menu choice per a table, so we decided to go with the flexibility of the 3-course menu over the specifically curated tasting menu.

As we glanced around the dining room and appreciated the high ceilings, our table was given complimentary cups of soup and fantastic cubes of angel bread. (The seasoned butter was the highlight but I can't remember which herb was involved.) If you're here for ambience, I'd say the pictures do not do it justice. It's a little dim inside after all, and the lighting doesn't capture the full height or the warmth of the atmosphere. 

For our first course, my boyfriend had the octopus salad while I opted for something warmer and had the chicken lemon soup. Both were warm and savory, perfectly balanced in flavor.

We were given a minute for the food to settle before our second course arrived. Our table chose the pork loin and lamb loin, both recommended at medium rare, both tender and tasty. I think lamb and pork can both be tricky as their strong flavors can be improperly accented by the wrong spice, but both our dishes were again, well balanced. 

By the time dessert came around, I was starting to feel full. But the chocolate custard and its raspberry sorbet was divine. The richness of the chocolate was balanced by the sweet sourness of the ice cream and made further complex with the salted hazelnuts sprinkled on the side. My boyfriend's cheese plate had individual pairings that ranged from apricot to regional almonds. Each was well chosen and well taken. 

While the portions here aren't large, they are appropriate and will leave you feeling full at the end due to the number of courses you experience and the pacing of the meal. However, if you're used to large size American portions (ie you triple deck your burger or super size your soft drink), this place isn't for you in terms of size or salt content. 

Overall, our meals were wonderful; the flavors were clean and well balanced. Servers were kind and attentive without being intrusive, well deserving of the meal-inclusive tip. Though we were well fed at the end of the meal, we were further offered complimentary breakfast muffins for the road and chocolates. My boyfriend said he'd love to come back again and I'd love to with him. Gramercy Tavern upholds the standards of a New York classic.

This place never ceases to blow me away every time I find myself in Manhattan. It's nearly become a personal requirement to swing by for a visit while I'm in town, if only for one of the expertly crafted cocktails at the bar. Gramercy Tavern prides itself on being a non-tipping establishment, but you would never guess based on the inviting, friendly & attentive staff at this Manhattan staple. Dining solo at the bar? Your bartender will graciously add you to a list for an open seat (if full) and notify you when available, always on a first name basis. Enjoying a meal with a companion in the dining room? You'll never be wanting of anything with the multi-person crew attending your table throughout the night.

While the stellar service will make your experience memorable in and of itself, the phenomenal cuisine will have you coming back for more. At the Tavern, the burger has to be one of the best in town and the cookie plate (two big cookies & spiked egg nog) is a must to end your meal. In the Dining Room, the Lamb Loin & Shoulder is perfectly tender & delicious. For libations, the Fall Classic is perfection in a glass and the wine offerings are top notch.

I would recommend Gramercy Tavern to anyone & everyone visiting Manhattan. The Tavern offers a casual & comfortable experience with the quality of fine dining while the Dining Room offers an intimate environment for special occasions. The cost can add up, but the no-tipping policy makes the overall experience affordable & comfortable. It's a model I hope other big city restaurants follow, though it's hard to imagine any others as satisfying as Gramercy Tavern.

Gramercy Tavern has been my go to spot for the past 9 years. I've always had my SO take me here even as much as once a month to celebrate as we live in the area. This year my sister treated me to a birthday lunch so it was the first time I saw the receipt (she left it on her counter by mistake) and I was appalled that they don't give free refills on a $5.50 Diet Coke. I am fine paying $40 for a great burger and and overall fine paying $140 for a great lunch but DO NOT NICKLE AND DIME ME!! A $5.50 Diet Coke should come with refills I don't care what type of restaurant it is. I'm not sure I'll be back- just so annoyed by this!

This was  a birthday dinner and it was very disappointing.  We had eaten here many years ago and I remembered it as a fine dining experience with attentive service.

Now, it seemed  more like a  mill, with lackluster food and haphazarded service.  None of the food warranted the high cost.     My daughter's fish was awful but she chose not to complain.   We heard another table near us later complain and wish we had as they were comped.

   I cannot understand how it has a Michelin star.  
 Some of the craft cocktails were ok. The bartender was pleasant.  

I remember years ago a manager came by to ask how the meal was and introduce himself.  Nothing like that happened this time.  

I felt worse for my daughter as when they brought out a piece of  cake for her with a candle  instead of her name on  it  had  a gentleman's name and  clearly for someone else.    The waiter apologized but the manager should have come over.


I do  not recommend.

"top-class" dining with "no gimmicks" at Danny Meyer's enduring Flatiron New American, where chef Michael Anthony's "outstanding" set menus are presented by "eminently suave" staffers in an "upscale-country" dining room arrayed with "gorgeous" flower displays; it's "not cheap by any means", though the front tavern offers a "reasonable" à la carte menu in a "colorful" walk-in setting; P.S. gratuity is now built into menu prices.

This place has two sections.  The front, in the bar area, seems more casual.  The back, table clothed, is about fine dining.  As far as i can tell, they have the same menu.

Secondly, this place accept no tips: server or coat check.  Everything is just "included."  Whoever will just politely refuse.  There is no place in the check to add tips.

That said, it is not a cheap eat.  Everything was delicious and they are more than happy to accommodate whatever you ask.  We had Onion soup that fully ground the onion to smooth and added croutons for texture.  The octopus was superbly made.  The beef tartar was a pleasant surprise of Mexican flare and a good kick!

Then we had the kale salad, fried fish sandwich, and tile fish.  All were excellent and not really stuffingly big.

The desserts were less impressive, particularly the cassis sorbet that was just too tart as a dessert.  The black-pepper ice cream and quince was also on the duh side.

I got barley wine and did not disappoint.  Companion got the Grenache blanc and said it was tasty.

I completely don't mind trying this place again for dinner.

We had a lovely meal to celebrate our anniversary. A few very small service hiccups, but overall the service was fantastic and the food delicious.

We were seated at a middle table along a booth, but the corner table had been cleared (but not yet set) so I asked to be moved, which we were. I'm not sure why they wouldn't have just sat us there from the onset instead of in very close proximity to the neighboring table. We were given complimentary glasses of Prosecco to start the celebration. 

We opted for the seasonal, 6-course tasting menu and ordered drinks (3 glasses of wine between us) off the menu. Warm cabbage broth came out first and it was amazing. We were blown away by the depth of flavor. Fluke crudo was the first course. Flavors were delicious but a few pieces were a tad stringy. We ordered glasses of wine after the first course. The seared scallops were placed in front of us and then our waiter came over to give us wine tastes and chat about the wines. Thought that timing to be a bit odd - he should have come over before the food came so the food wasn't sitting in front of us while he was speaking to us. The scallops were amazing. 

Next came Arctic char that alone was unimpressive but together as a complete dish was wonderful and packed with flavor.  Squid ink pasta with lobster was next but they also offered a pasta with comte cheese and white truffles for an additional charge. We ordered 1 and were able to enjoy both pasta dishes. Both were perfection. A perfectly seared beef dish brought the savory dishes to an end. It was perfectly cooked and perfectly seasoned. A palate cleanser of apple and pomegranate did just that. 

Poached pears with ice cream was surprisingly good. I thought the texture of the pear a bit odd - more of a crunch than I expected but my husband really enjoyed it. A surprise coconut cake with a whipped merengue for our anniversary was delicious but he doesn't like coconut so I ate (most of) it. 2 Chocolate truffles and take home mini chocolate chip banana bread loaves (for the morning) rounded out our meals.

Service was wonderful - on top of everything without being obtrusive.

I can't say one bad thing about this place. It's my favorite Sunday Brunch in the city. Come early, get in line and be prepared to be wine'd and dine'd.

Gramercy has always been a staple in NYC, and I can say that I've never had a bad meal here. The service is very good and the food is executed tremendously. My only beef is that the bar area is a little cramped. 

The cocktails and wine are well manicured. I'm a fan of just about everything on the menu. Pick anything, it won't disappoint.
Definitely one of the must go places in ny!! The burger is amazing! It's a bit expensive but it will be worth it! In the tavern they don't accept reservation, it's only walk in.

Ate at the tavern side! Seafood stew was delicious, as was the chorizo/bolognese pasta shells (although this bordered on being too salty). Service was excellent. Will have to come back and try their tasting menu soon!

People always talk about the bar burger here, so I went and ordered the bar burger. And it is now one of my top 5 burgers in NYC.

It's simple, but perfect. Melted cheddar, topped with bacon, on a toasted bun. Side of duck fat crisps. In terms of "basic" burgers, it's a damn good one. At $32, it's definitely "treat yourself" territory, but it's bucket list worthy.

A quick note - the bar menu is different from the restaurant menu. They have a different burger at the restaurant. Grab a seat at the bar (they maintain their own list so you don't need to check in with the hostesses) and bonus points if it's happy hour (4 to 6). Can't beat $8 beers and $12 wines/cocktails! The Portside spritz I had was delightful.

The bar staff was also incredibly pleasant and friendly. They took the time to explain the menu items (and to commend my choices). Plus, they got me started with the best foccacia I've ever had (basil, sun-dried tomatoes, and Concord raisins). I was tempted to say yes when they offered me a second one, but didn't want to fill up on bread ahead of the burger.

Was also served a tiny, tiny amuse bouche - Romano salad with eggplant puree. What a wonderful and delicious surprise. They really take care of you here!

All in all, I'm a big fan of Danny Meyer restaurants, and was glad to tick another one off the list. And since it's USHG, tips are included. So that $32 burger is more like... $29.

Worth it.

This is our favorite New York restaurant. Outstanding service in a beautiful space. We ate in the Tavern and enjoyed every moment. The drinks were perfect and the attention to detail is unmatched. Perfect for any occasion. At the end of our meal our waiter handed us off to another waitress. We were then forgotten for about 15 - 20 min. She was busy and we understood but it was still a disappointment to an otherwise great meal.

Meat platter with bread and pickled vegetables - YUM! Perfect.

Lumache - Perfectly cooked pasta with seafood and chorizo. Very tasty.

Grilled Black Bass - Unbelievable! This was the best dish of the night. The fish was perfect but the sauce was drinkable.

Heirloom Carrots with Hot Honey and Sesame - We loved this. Smoky, sweet with just the tiniest bit of heat. These carrots could be on my table any time. Scrumptious.

Pear Cobbler - Perfectly subtly sweet. Just a bit too much topping for my taste.

Went here for lunch since bf wanted to try them for the longest time. Both of us agree on giving them 5 stars for service, food and ambiance. Everything we had was delicious and perfectly executed. They start you with a free focaccia bread that has cheese, thyme and peach on it which was savory. We got the roasted oysters, sea bass, duck sausage, sides of braised greens and squash. For desserts, we got the peach cobbler and pumpkin beignets which size is good for 2 people. I'm glad it's not your typical american meal. It has it's uniqueness and all the ingredients tasted fresh. Planning to come back soon to try their famous burger and the dinner menu. Definitely worth the price tag since the tip is included already.

A true five star experience. I booked a noon table in the dining room for my girlfriend's birthday (and mentioned this in my reservation). Gramercy gave us a free glass of prosecco each (and topped them off!) as well as additional desserts to celebrate.

The tasting menu with wine pairings isn't cheap for Maine standards at $165, but is a steal for NYC, and includes tip. After heavenly bread and an amuse bouche, five perfect courses arrived accompanied by flavorful french wines. The pasta course was the best, with the fish a close second. At the end, we were quite tipsy and highly satisfied with our meal.

There are many reasons that Gramercy Tavern has been listed as one of the top 100 restaurants in the United States for 25 consecutive years.

In short, it's because of the incredible and consistent focus on service and the guest experience.  They know your dietary restrictions when you arrive.  The waitstaff is incredibly attentive and focused and understand every dish, the ingredients and how they are prepared.

It's because of the food is innovative, locally sourced, fresh and no expense is spared with respect to the ingredients (Thank you Executive Chef Michael Anthony).  

There are a broad swath of wine choices and the cocktails are fantastic, and the decor is beautiful.

If you dine in New York City, you have a seemingly infinite number of dining choices.  To remain at the top of the heap for so many years is a tribute to the persistence and insistence of always improving the guest experience.

Thank you Danny Meyer!

The GM reached out to me and we had a nice phone conversation. She offered to send me a gift card and gave me her direct info for future reservations. I went again about a month ago.
Admittedly, my bf and I still weren't a fan of the food. I guess perhaps we just don't like the specific cuisine? But the amazing customer service by the GM and staff was noticeable. When we paid, we were given an additional discount. Despite us not being fans of the cuisine, customer service is good. Worth a try.
Our meal was delicious and the service top notch. Wonderful experience. The pork loin was absolutely amazing!

I'm a fan, but not as big of a fan as I was hoping to be.

We did the seasonal tasting menu with the wine pairing and I remember enjoying the fish, the duck, and the palette cleanser they give you. The bread at the beginning was good too. I don't remember what else came on the tasting menu, so I'll just say those didn't standout for me. 

Service was executed fine, but I thought a little judgey after they found out I don't like goat cheese which is in the butter they give in the beginning with the good bread and on the dessert.

Probably wouldn't do that whole thing again but maybe I'll go there for a burger some day!

Came for a friend's birthday on a Friday afternoon to the Tavern. Pretty good crowd at the bar and in the tavern made for an enjoyable atmosphere. Good attentive service as expected. Their house made bread is amazing- focaccia with apple and cheddar. 
Ordered: Seafood Tower for 2 - comes with 6 oysters, clams, scallops with yuzu, lobster salad with aioli, and calamari. Everything was fresh with great flavor. You can also add on a half bottle of champagne to this. 
Smoked Duck Andouille - comes with cheesy grits and poached pears. The grits were on the saltier side and didn't really complement the Duck Andouille. 
Lumache - chorizo with broccoli rabe and pasta. Great flavor and perfect al dente pasta. 
Beef Wagyu meatballs - my friend described it as "IKEA meatballs on steroids" also comes with kale and broccolini 
Pear Cobbler - nice and crispy on the outside with a scoop of ice cream on top
Coconut Pandan Pie - heavy with cream, but has a good flavor. You can really taste both coconut and pandan flavors. The pie crust was also on point. 
My friend also received a mini birthday cake, which we think was a coconut tres leches. 
Overall, a good experience at the Tavern, although when I walked in, I noticed the hostess gave me a quick up and down look over, which was a little unsettling.

My family and I ate dinner at Gramercy Tavern two weeks ago for my wife's birthday.  It was definitely one of the best meals I've ever eaten.  The service is impeccable; efficient, warm and knowledgeable.  I can honestly say the octopus appetizer I had was the best I've ever eaten.  The fish I had was also delicious, but the baklava ice cream was possibly the best ice cream I've every had.  So unexpectedly tasty.  Who would have thought baklava ice cream would work, but it was fantastic.  

For special occasions, this was truly a NYC treasure.

You just can't go wrong with lunch/ brunch at the bar. Always delicious and superb service. The duck liver is sublime!
Also the Lumache pasta special with fish and chorizo was excellent. 
We love that service is included.

There are 2 main reasons why I am only giving 2 stars to this establishment.  I felt deathly ill 2 hours after dinner and the service was strange.  I would have only given 1 star but I cannot ignore the fact that the food was top notch in terms of taste and presentation.  My wife and I both had the seasonal tasting menu.  

1.  About an hour after dinner while on the train I noticed I was getting intermittent abdominal cramps and by the time we got home it was unbearable.  I had to run to the bathroom and I kid you not, it was the worse number 2 that I have ever experienced in my life.  I had to take a break and drink some water while in the bathroom, I literally thought that this was how my life was going to end.  I was diaphoretic and my hands were going numb which was the strangest thing.  My wife thought I was being a baby drama queen until she saw how pale and sweaty I was.  She actually wanted to take me to ER but thankfully I was okay after about 2 hours laying on the couch and drinking water.  It reminded me of the time 20 years ago when I returned from a trip from Mexico and experienced firsthand what "Montezuma's Revenge was all about.  That Mexico experience was worse because it lasted for days and I had to go to the ER for IV fluids.  Seriously I have no idea what the heck happened my wife and I had the same items except for the desserts, she had the cheese cake and I had the Baklava ice cream.

2.  Now for the service this was the strangest thing of the night.  Originally our main waitress was very nice and attentive but everything changed when she tried to take our drink orders.  I explained that we do not drink alcohol and that we were fine with the water at the table.  We both order the tasting menu and were allowed to substitute the fixed dessert which was great.  After she took our order that was last time she made any effort to communicate with us or even check how our meals were going.  We watched her pamper other tables around us and chat with other guest while we were ignored.  I don't know, it just really bothered me, I actually had to yell out "excuse me" can you refill our table water when she was passing our table to tend to other people.  The random waiters/bus boys that bought out our food did a sufficient job of dropping off our food but it was very impersonal.  I do not get it, I know we did not order any drinks but we did pay about $400 for the tasting menu for the both of us.  The next and final time we had any communication with our waitress was when the bill came and she thanked us for coming.  It started to make sense when I noticed the bill stated no tipping is accepted.  Maybe the waiters get a salary or they get paid more depending on how much the customer orders?  

3.  Food: Seasonal Tasting Menu
Smoked Sturgeon - This was perfectly cooked and the caviar on top really enhanced the dish.

Poached Lobster - It was neatly presented and cooked to the perfect texture.  It's lobster and it tasted great.

Ricotta Ravioli - Not much to look but it was good.  

Duck Confit - The presentation of the dish reminded me of an egg roll but with a duck filling.  Crispy on the outside but not too greasy.  One of my favorite dishes of the night.

Roasted Wagyu Ribeye and Braised Short Rib - This was my least favorite item on the tasting menu.  Ribeye was dry and tough and the short rib was just okay.

Baklava ice cream - WOW.  If you are a big fan of ice cream and you like Baklava, this is a do not miss item.  Just perfect.

Complimentary bread - Amazing and it was served with this delicious goat cheese spread.


Overall the ambiance in the dining area was elegant while the bar area was rustic and hip.  I remember telling my wife we should come back and eat at the front bar area to try that menu.  This was before I got sick from the food.  I probably will not be returning for a 2nd helping since I felt ignored by the waitress and got sick from the food.

So happy we snagged a Saturday night res here. I went with a group of 4 and one bummer is the table has to all opt for the same "meal." So we all went with their 3 course dinner menu and got to choose from a variety of VERY fancy apps, entrees, and desserts. 

I'm not experienced in fine dining but the beef tartare was EXCELLENT! It was really spicy and had dried sweet potato in it. The chicken entree was just ok for me. The chicken itself was super juicy and cooked perfectly but the sauce was just meh. And the show stopper was dessert. I was worried about ordering something as simple as "cookies" but man. USHG doesn't do anything simple or mediocre! The cookies were the largest, warmest, chocolatiest cookies I've ever had the pleasure of eating. They even came with a mini milk infused with vanilla or something. It was, again, FANTASTIC. 

On the way out they give you a mini banana bread in case you're feelin' like a little snacky later. I ate it the next morning and that too was just delightful. What an excellent experience! I wish I my entree was more show stopping but they really treat you right and go the extra mile here.
This place has great service. Food is amazing and always great energy throughout the venue.

For our 27th anniversary we dined at Gramercy Tavern last night. From reservation confirmation through departing at the end everything was perfect.  We had the vegetable and special menus with parings, started with great cocktails and wine.  The only thing better than the perfectly balanced bites and surprising combinations was the service.  What a great dining room and staff including the sommelier.  This is our new go to every time we return.  Thank you for an amazing night and wonderful experience.

Second time there and the food was amazing. Got a table in bar area. Every course was better then the last! The service from the maître d' to our waiter and everyone in between was beyond perfect. We didn't feel pressure leave or hurry through any course. Cant wait to go back!

Sooo delicious! Benny was absolutely amazing and made the best drinks! The staff was super friendly. We had the Brussels sprout salad and fluke and it was so delicious! We finished the night off with another round and some dessert which was so tasty! Will definitely return!

We went to the historic Gramercy Park Tavern this past Wednesday with admittedly high expectations. A party of two, myself and a friend who just moved to the city.  This was a dinner that we hoped would become a yearly tradition to celebrate, as I we were escorted to our table, I couldn't help but notice all the smiles on folks faces. As dinner was over and I walked out, I had a face of disappointment, something that I didn't expect in my wildest dreams after reading the other reviews about GPT.

The Review:
--------------------------

I'd been wanting to try out Gramercy Park Tavern out for a while, and we both sat down excited.  We ordered the Seasonal tasting menu which on that night started off well getting a free butternut squash based shooter which was delicious. The pastry chef is unbelievable as proven by both the complimentary bread and banana chocolate take away gift. 

The first course was an underwhelming scallop dish with hints of citrus and ginger maybe? The scallop was bland, and slimy. 

Next up was the poached lobster with sun chokes, rice and ginger. It was a creative recipe in theory, but to both of us lacked any standout flavor and begin to have us questioning our choice in both tasting menu selection and restaurant.

This was followed by the a fish that was unmemorable, a pasta that was once again bland. 

The last dish a wagyu ribeye, carmelized, mushrooms, potato: The best part of this was the shiitake mushrooms. The meat was dry to the point where the plate noticeably lacked a juice from the meat, and the shallot was over carmelized. Not to mention a distinct chewiness, which was very much unappealing. 

The chocolate pudding was once again just ok. 

We also had three glasses of wine each. 

Here is the bottom line, we went into the dinner wanting to not only enjoy the tasting menu and ambiance tonight, but find a place we can come to again and again. We left feeling vastly underwhelmed, and feeling like the food quality that was served was not a $550 meal out the door. Unfortunately we will have to keep looking for our consistent Gramercy Park Haunt.

Lastly the service was amazing, both waiters, and bussers were friendly, engaging and attentive! I don't want to take away from them in the slightest - Mike and Carolyn were awesome!

We love the Gramercy Tavern. It's like an old friend. Consistent good service a great food. 

We often meet friends there because everyone is familiar with the Gramercy Tavern it's a no brainer because while everyone has their favorite nobody has a problem with the Gramercy Tavern

In short is our old familiar go to top shelf choice
The truffle burger is worth the trip. A consistent restaurant with really attentive service and solid food

Gramercy Tavern encapsulates everything that's right in the restaurant industry. 

I went here for lunch with my former professor and had such a phenomenal experience. Our waiter Kevin was very engaging, on point, attentive and eager to answer any questions we had about the menu. Definitely try the roasted oysters and/or wagyu beef meatballs as they were both extremely delectable. 

Undeniably one of the best restaurants in NYC and I can't wait to return.
Went to Gramercy tavern for celebrating our anniversary on 29th Feb... Great food and service... Everything was top notch.

We had very high expectations before going so probably that is why we felt it was just okay. nothing impressive or extraordinary. so if you're just going for regular lunch or dinner and don't mind the price, it's a fine place to go. otherwise there are better choices.
Great place with many options to choose from, and casual ambiance, fun and excellent food

Perhaps I had an atypical experience as this place has near-perfect reviews, however, I ate at the bar and ordered the burger which arrived after an extremely long wait (the people next to me ordered a burger a solid 15 minutes after I did and they got both of their burgers before I did). I can overlook the long wait but what I absolutely cannot accept is a poorly executed burger as mine was cooked medium-well instead of medium-rare. For $32 I expect the burger to be cooked properly and to arrive in a timely manner. I did not bother having them cook another as I didn't have time.

Very pleasant surprise being taken here by a friend! I loved the entire dining experience and glad that we had a formal dinner reservation for the three whole courses.

Interior - GT has lots of modern and traditional art elements going into its decor. There's a front bar/dining area for casual dining, which can get a bit crowded on Fridays, and a large back dining area for formal dinners. I love that idea of having both! Ambience was amazing, formal yet not uptight.

Service - there's coatcheck. Our servers were the best couple in town! They were so friendly and cute, and worked really well together. They settled us in, regularly checked up on us to make sure everything tasted right. My napkin was replaced when I left my seat for the bathroom, bread crumbs were swept away in between courses, and silverware was placed the right directions. They did the whole nine. Way to go :)

Food - I am not gonna go into too much detail about the food cuz everything tasted amazing anyways. Just check out the pics. I think this place deserves to be called an NYC landmark and I can't wait to be back!

We reserved the dining seating to celebrate one of friends' b'day. I chose the 6 course tasting menu and everything was perfect.y favourite was the poached lobster with sunchokes, golden rice and ginger but even the scallops and bass were awesome. The desserts were really good too. 

The service from start to end was outstanding. Thanks a bunch for making our visit so special. 

Next time I plan to grab some drinks at the Tavern, cheers!

Alvaro (their sommelier) the rest of the team truly understand hospitality and how to make your night an unforgettable one.

We chose this restaurant to celebrate our anniversary (and because we knew they'd be so clean and trustworthy during a time where everyone is afraid of corona virus) and did the tasting menu with wine.

Everything was amazing and I would ALWAYS recommend doing the wine pies as they're truly unique wines that pair extremely well and watching Alvaro explain each of the wines was so special. He truly cares and is so passionate and knowledgeable. It's was an amazing dinner and we'll be back for sure. Thank you for making our anniversary special.

after so many years this place still runs as if it just opened and is trying to make a name for it self , great service and carefully prepared food ,the food needs a little more kick, but still special after 25 years

Had such a great experience and met with so many prominent people at gramercy which was unexpected. The best part was when the executive sous chef John karis poured me a glass of water when our server was too busy to check on our table. It was definitely a busy Friday night so it was awesome to get the kind of service we got from the higher ups of the restaurant.

5 Star experience for sure! 

We dined here Valentine's Day weekend for my hubby's birthday. Reservations were easy to make in advance via Resy, but were limited due to the popularity (and holiday weekend) of the restaurant. Everything is top notch-- from the decor, to the food, to the outstanding service. 

There are a few set menus to choose from, including a vegetarian option. If needed, they can accommodate a swap from one menu to another (just ask). 

The highlights of the night were the Brussel Sprout salad (not on the menu, complimentary with the progression), absolutely delicious rolls with goat cheese whipped butter (to die for!) and the Baklava ice cream dessert. Honestly, everything was really good, but these are the dishes that left me wanting more! 

I added in the Resy notes that we were celebrating my hubby's bday and they brought out a delicious coconut meringue cake with candle and birthday message-- definitely made our night and the cake was amazing! They even sent us with a to-go treat of banana chocolate chip coffee cake for the next day. 

I would definitely return if in the city again!
I really miss Spring time in NY topped with a great meal from the Tavern. I love their lunches the most. They pair beautifully traditional and new presentations and update their offerings often.
Great place for dinner or lunch and has a great historical feel. Great food and service plus location is great.

Always good food, nice wine selection and guaranteed being packed )) so get in line early or make a reservation in advance.
Definitely on a high end note, this place will rock you world (in a good way tho)).
Enjoy!

Best restaurant!  Great service, atmosphere, clean and amazing food!  I miss their burgers and their chocolate pudding pie!!! Can't wait until the quarantine is over and they reopen.  I miss you GT and especially my favorite waiter Kevin XO

A Foodies delight.  I have eaten here several times. I wouldn't do the tasting menu if you have to be somewhere as it takes a while.  But the regular menu is so good you will be more than satisfied if you eat there.  what is really fantastic is they used to be part of restaurant week so you can get to try it out for a discounted price.  But be warned you will probably have to eat at the bar those weeks as it books up super fast.  If fact always get a reservation even for lunch.

Decent upscale-ish modern American food.

Service is exceptional here, and for my first-time experience, the kitchen gave me some complimentary dishes.

Gramercy Tavern covers so many different tastes, and use a wide variety of ingredients -- a true display of their culinary skills. During my meal, I ate raw fish, duck liver mousse, seafood, and chicken! A wide variety is sure to please anyone who comes here.

Overall, the food is good and leans more on the comfort food side. Although there is a variety of food, I feel like the flavors are a bit inconsistent, and you feel like you're eating fusion at times. Still, definitely a great place to come if you want to have a taste of NYC's palette.
The food is just top-notch. I'll tell you what, it's been a long time since I've felt such hearty hospitality and tasty food.
I don't understand why Gramercy Tavern is so popular. Food was just okay and nothing special but expensive. I don't recommend this place!

Overheard: "My name isn't as effective as it was before 2016 so I was not able to procure a table last time I was in NYC. Danny Meyer, just like your establishment did to my plans to spend a night with my Choate chums talking nonstop about my initiatives for women's empowerment in D.C., I give you a rating of 'Ah. Okay.'" - Ivanka Trump

First time back since quarantine. Was great to be back. That said, they have kept prices on the menu relatively the same as pre-quarantine but was told they are not including tip in the menu price anymore at the end of the meal. would have appreciated that communicated upfront. Please understand was well worth the price regardless, but felt a bit icky to find out (as a long time client) at the end.

I've been there many times 
and always have a wonderful selection of appetizers and entree s and wines. I highly recommend this restaurant!

Brought my boyfriend here for his birthday. He had never been, we sat in the main dining room and did the tasting menu. 
From the moment of arrival the hostess was so friendly and they were aware of my allergies. They checked my coat and brought us right over to the table. We had. A great table. 
The food was stellar and the wine was fantastic. This was pre Covid but we plan to go back this weekend for a tavern burger ... one of the best burgers in the city. They are now taking reservations for outside seating!!

Other restaurants take note, this is how you serve people especially during a pandemic. It's actually better service than normal lol the new staff is great very attentive and friendly the only thing is the menu does not have as many options as before, but still tasty and great  wine list.

Fantastic place.  Staff + Service are amazing, every  produce is sourced carefully making the food as delightful as can be. The bar area has seating and its own menu so you don't have to spend $300/person each visit (but if you are celebrating something, do have the experience at their main dining room, it's exquisite) this may be the best kept secret burger in town & the wine selection is fabulous... can't go wrong with going here.
Nice staff and great food. Come here after work just to kick back and even with outdoor seating, it's got a great atmosphere.

Was able to make a 5:30pm Wednesday reservation on Sunday night through resy. 

They adhere to the 90 minute limit so I recommend knowing your order before sitting down. Time flies and feeling rushed at the end is not ideal. 

Ordered the summer salad (just ok, small), artic char (amazing), burger (no regrets), pasta (bomb, tastes way better than it looks) and halibut (left a lot to be desired). Not enough time for dessert. 

Staff are super respectful. They took my temp before I went inside to use the bathroom. It's nice that it's on a cross street so much less foot traffic than on the avenue. Also fully covered due to scaffolding / tents. Recommend :)

If I could only eat at one restaurant for the rest of my life, this would be it.  Going to Gramercy Tavern is one of the best parts of big occasions in my life lol. I've been here for quite a few birthdays and anniversaries at this point, and everything is always top notch. Gramercy Tavern completely embodies Danny Meyer's approach to fine dining: excellent service, casual ambiance and world class food made with seasonal ingredients. I've been to a lot of Michelin restaurants in NYC, including 2 and 3 star ones but Gramercy is my favorite because it's casual but the food and service are as good as they can get.

Their lunch prixe fixe is very reasonable for the experience you get. It's a 5 course meal, and they usually throw in additional desserts if it's a special occasion for you. They change the prixe fixe slightly every month or so, and it's been excellent everytime I've been there (probably close to 10 times). I think the free bread is one of the measures of a fine dining restaurant, and Gramercy knocks it out of the park with this. They have freshly baked biscuits and goat cheese at the start of the meal, and it is GODDAMN AMAZING! Over my multiple visits I've had a bunch of interesting things, the Smoked Arctic Char and a Poached Hake are particularly memorable - both were the softest and tastiest pieces of fish I've ever had.

I'd definitely go for the dining room experience, and not the bar seating. I've done that once and it was nowhere close to the full experience you get in the dining room. They're doing outside seating now and I plan on checking out, but really hoping USHG and Gramercy make it out of this pandemic fine. I know where I'll be going to celebrate once all this is over!
While I have yet to try the public seating area, our experience in the private room was fantastic pre covid. The lamb and duck were superb! Highly recommend for your next fancy get together.

I was disappointed. Especially in their burgers. They can't make a burger to the temperature you request as they are already pre made?
Anyway, it is somewhat reasonable but I wouldn't go back for the food.
Maybe a drink?
Amazing place that knows how to take care of regulars! Love everything from food to cocktails to vibe!

Unfortunately, while every other restaurant in the city is bending over backwards to welcome diners and do whatever it takes, Gramercy Tavern, a long-time favorite for special events, doesn't know how to address Covid-era dining. They really want to still justify Michelin-starred prices, even if the menu only has three options, but forget any semblance of the service you once expected from this fine NY institution. We're all in this together (aka I'm thrilled to be eating in the street with sirens and garbage and panhandlers, sounds great! No problem!), and I can even ignore that I'm paying $30 for pasta or a $25 cheeseburger right next to four other restaurants that charge much less to eat a cheeseburger in the street... because THIS cheeseburger is a Gramercy Tavern cheeseburger and this service is going to make me feel like I still live in the city I used to love, right? I wish we'd just gone to L'Express--they are actually happy to have diners during covid. Now is really not the time to be rude to your customers. (You might think, 'oh this is a fallout from the Danny Meyers no tipping policy' but no, they are actually rude in spite of now working for tips again.) In short, they have no idea how to actually balance "you're eating in the bike lane" with "but we're still Gramercy Tavern."

Gramercy Tavern is definitely my favorite restaurant in the city. I've been to the formal dining room a few times and always walk away loving pretty much everything I ordered. The complementary bread rolls are amazing and they are happy to give you extra rolls. This was my first time eating the tavern food and it was also outdoor dining for COVID. I ordered the cheeseburger which was one of the best burgers I've had. The chilled corn soup was so fresh and seasonal as was the peach daiquiri which given how much I love peaches is probably one of the best drinks I've had at a restaurant. The peaches tasted like they were just picked. I hope they do outdoor dining again next year because the street was closed off from cars and it was really quiet and pretty.

A New York institution, Gramercy Tavern is in my top five places to eat. I recently visited for the new outdoor dining situation - Gramercy Tavern in the Streets. The menu is a smaller selection for obvious reasons, but still classic. The "must-orders" are the oysters, chicken liver mousse (light and whipped texture), and the bolognese. Tables were spaced well enough apart, sanitizer on each table, and it was a pleasant dining experience in true Gramercy Tavern fashion. Can't wait to return.

Gramercy Tavern hasn't missed a beat even on The Street!  We found The Street menu excellent.  The Chicken Liver Mousse was very light and did not have a strong liver pate taste.  It went perfectly with the Grilled Pepper Chicken--really big pieces of chicken--and Cioppino.  Ending with the Caffe Panna Gelato--that was so good we ordered an extra Gelato!   The Servers were wonderful in making us feel relaxed and "they got this down."   We appreciate GT's efforts in making the experience of eating outside fun and romantic.  And, goes without saying--EXCELLENT food and service as always!!

I was incredibly excited to dine at Gramercy Tavern after five months of quarantining. I made a reservation for lunch today, their Lunch in the Street menu looked decent. We were seated almost immediately and they very nicely accommodated my 2 year old toddler. The drinks came, a grapefruit gin and tonic, they didn't hold back on the alcohol and we loved it. 

The Arctic char tartare appetizer was bland and tiny in portion. My husband got the burger, which he really liked and I got the grilled pepper chicken from the mains. I should have gotten the lobster roll but decided to give the chicken a shot. The chicken was so tough and stringy, it kept getting stuck in my teeth. It tasted good, a good kick of spice but the texture was horrendous. I powered through it but I should have sent it back. I was offered a steak knife but it still didn't work. I'm hoping i don't get sick from it. 

My daughters child size pasta was drenched in butter, a literal pool of butter in the pasta. 

Will I come back here for a meal? Probably not. For the drinks, maybe. I understand the pandemic has been difficult on everyone. In order to support struggling restaurants make it through these difficult times, we need to be able to justify the money spent on the meals we eat. GT just didn't cut it. Pretty disappointed.

I was excited to eat here after reading the reviews and because I have some friends who swear by this place special occasions. I work for a nonprofit, so eating at Michelin-rated restaurants isn't exactly a hobby (yet, lol). However, I decided to go with 3 friends for dinner and treat myself for once. 

Food: We split the chicken liver mousse appetizer, which was quite good, if small (only 4 pieces of bread, but you can ask for more...yay?). Those of us who got the grilled pepper chicken main dish found it really juicy, delicious, and just the right size, but my friend who got the cioppino was disappointed (it did look like a very small dish...). We did split a bottle of their riesling, which was AMAZING...and only $56 for a bottle. Service - quick, attentive, and following all the COVID regulations. Temperature check needed to use the restroom. Outdoor seating is especially nice since they closed off the street, so you don't get any of that fun Manhattan car noise. 

Did I end up having a nice time and good food? Yes! Was it worth the price I paid ($76)...maybe? I think I was expecting more "wow," but it was a sufficiently fancy Friday! :)

So happy it finally opened up for outdoor seating!

Everything was phenomenal, the food, the service, one of my favourites in the the city for sure.

4 Star experience for sure! My highest rating, always room for improvement. 

We dined here Valentine's Day weekend for my hubby's birthday. Reservations were easy to make in advance via Resy, but were limited due to the popularity (and holiday weekend) of the restaurant. Everything is top notch-- from the decor, to the food, to the outstanding service. 

There are a few set menus to choose from, including a vegetarian option. If needed, they can accommodate a swap from one menu to another (just ask). 

The highlights of the night were the Brussel Sprout salad (not on the menu, complimentary with the progression), absolutely delicious rolls with goat cheese whipped butter (to die for!) and the Baklava ice cream dessert. Honestly, everything was really good, but these are the dishes that left me wanting more! 

I added in the Resy notes that we were celebrating my hubby's bday and they brought out a delicious coconut meringue cake with candle and birthday message-- definitely made our night and the cake was amazing! They even sent us with a to-go treat of banana chocolate chip coffee cake for the next day. 

I would definitely return if in the city again!

My parents and I came here for dinner on my birthday. We were seated at one of their tables in the street and the lights and flowers set up were very nice. When we sat, my dad noticed his fork was dirty so we had to get a new one. We ordered three appetizers to share-the tomato carpaccio, the salad, and the chicken liver mousse. The carpaccio was very good, the dressing on it worked very well with the flavors. I also enjoyed the liver a lot, it was not too salty. For dinner, my mom and I shared the Campanelle Bolegnese and the pepper chicken and they were both great. The chicken was just a bit tough and under seasoned in my opinion but the flavors that came across were still very good and it was enjoyable. The pasta was probably my favorite, the sauce was not too heavy and I enjoyed it a lot. For dessert we got the gelato and the chocolate chunk cookie. The cookie was ok, nothing special so I would definitely recommend the gelato instead if you have to pick one. The gelato was great, so creamy and the flavors worked so well together so it wasn't too sweet. Our waiter was very attentive, our food all came out very quick and he also brought us some warm water when we were cold outside. Overall a pretty good birthday dinner.

First time here made extra special celebrating my birthday! Amazing food and service!
We ate outdoors, which apparently meant a limited (COVID related) menu.
Don't know what I may have missed, but can't have been much as the food and experience was such a treat!

I got takeout here, and the high expectations I had for food from such a vaunted name were frankly not met. At all. 
I started with the Everything Under the Sun salad, which consisted of seemingly undercooked barley, a few pieces of an orange squash, zuchini, and eggplant, and three leaves of lettuce. I opened the box to see these ingredients just tossed in part by part, and topped with the lettuce. Really? This seems more like a cheap ofterthought of a salad, and I'm inclined to think a more apt name might be All the Leftovers Under the Sun salad. 
The campagnelle pasta wasn't bad, but was overly greasy and a tad overdone. After eating the bottom of the box was entirely layered in hardened grease. The dish was topped with parmesan, but not the freshly grated kind either. It's the type of cheese you'd expect to see in an unrefrigerated plastic bottle at Costco or Trader Joe's, or perhaps even at your local dollar slice. Again, really?
The three date rugelachs that concluded the meal weren't any better. They had the consistency identical to that of a soggy two day old croissant left in a sealed plastic bag. The granulated sugar that topped them had dissolved into the pastry, and I honestly wouldn't be surprised if they were indeed leftovers from the day before. For the third time in three dishes, really?
To top it all off, the hostess had an underlying haughty tone that shown through when I was picking up my food. Maybe it's because I was in a t-shirt and a cap, but when your stand is on the sidewalk and I'm getting takeout, the chances I dress up for your restaurant are nil. Other staff seemed more friendly. 
Would I get takeout here again? Absolutely not. Would I give them a second shot in person when the full menu comes back around? Perhaps if some money was burning a hole in my pocket.

This classic NYC venue is fantastic. I went with my 83 yr old parents and the staff was so kind and patient. One of the staff walked my dad to the bathroom. When my dad wasn't too happy with his steak tartar being spiced up, the same woman took it back and the chef sent him another no spiced portion. This place is the episode of class. Worth every penny!

I am very sympathetic about the impact of Covid on restaurants and have spent the entire last 6 months in my GV apartment.  That said, the pricing at GT is out of touch with reality.  The food tasted great and the service was very attentive but the prices!!
$24 for a well rye Manhattan
$36 for a "pork chop" which was slices of pork.  There was so little meat they must have made 2 servings out of 1 chop.
$28 for a glass of Pommerol where the BOTTLE RETAiLS for $40.

You are a NY institution but the prices are crazy and I won't be back.

Delivery was really interesting. I really love this restaurant. My sister even had her engagement party here years ago. But the takeout was really bad! Am posting what it looked like on food app versus real life. The fish croquette was so hard, couldn't even bite into it. Seemed like it was microwaved. Can't really justify $38 for this!! I hope this was just a one off bad experience.
Worth the wait! The food was extraordinary and each plate was distinct with complicated flavors. I remember especially the tomato and watermelon salad that was salted exactly right.

Wow - literally wow!  Best meal and dining experience I've had to date, this group really stepped it up and delivered for our anniversary dinner.  All food lovers should dine here at least once in their lives.  Great job GT team, and thank you for the experience!

Only stand out dish was the Crudo and peaches were good but it was just cut peaches!
Artic char was bland and pork loin was just ok. We weren't able to get any service when trying to ask for water or the bill, possibly in a blind spot isolated in corner. Overall food was ok with the Crudo being a stand out but a bit too much sauce

As part of our Tavern Burger Competition, my friends and I ordered the "Tavern Bacon & Cheddar Burger" from Gramercy Tavern compared this to Minetta Tavern's "Black Label Burger". All of us thought that the latter won by a landslide.

We thought that Gramercy Tavern's version, although solid, was simply not worth the $32 price point. It tasted like a really good burger but was pretty ordinary otherwise. If I'm paying that much for a burger, it better knock my socks off.

I would give this 3.5 stars. Food was decent, however I was expecting to be blown away so I left somewhat disappointed. The best dish of the night was the chilled cucumber soup (not pictured). It was super light and refreshing yet still slightly creamy. It was the perfect summertime soup, extremely mellow and cool. For our entrees we ordered the bolognese and cioppino. The bolognese was very good (4/5). It was very meaty and satisfying and the pasta was cooked perfectly. However, the cioppino was disappointing. For a $39 dish, the portion was extremely small. I'm used to small portions in fine dining restaurants but this was slightly absurd. It came with one scallop, one shrimp, a few pieces of squid and some lackluster vegetables. Furthermore, When I order a cioppino, I'm expecting a very impressive and flavorful broth. This broth was quite bland and had none of the umami I'm used to. The wine and cocktails we ordered were very good and the service was exceptional. However, the cioppino really put a damper on dinner. Perhaps we should have just stuck with the burger.
Always a good experience when I dine here! Alvaro is fantastic! The service and attention to detail are excellent! Thank you!
The food is good.service is nice. But the chair is really uncomfortable. The dessert and the pork dish (main dish) is delicious.

Very nice relaxing atmosphere, good food and amazing service but maybe too strict on the  their covid regulations. They pretty much make you eat in your mask  
Pretty on the overall, unexpectedly dirty bathroom ‍

No doubt a top New Yorker restaurant, with impecable service, superb wine list and lavish and comfortable interior( copper pans and flames in  the open part of the kitchen wine ) .
Food was ok. Just expected more from my main course, eggplant parmigiana. Looked more like a lazy Sunday  dish with roughly cut peppers (with skin!) , the last eggplant in the fridge, some cheese on the top. 
(Not a Michelin star dish, in my humble opinion.
The Brussels sprout salad with pears was superb, though.

Still my vote for the best special occasion dinner in NYC. What to expect: wonderful service - always warm, knowledgeable, and attentive - and consistently excellent food and drink, even with a more abbreviated menu than usual during these pandemic times.

We reserved an early table in order to guarantee that we could eat outdoors to celebrate a dear friend's birthday. A warm greeting from the host was followed by COVID precautionary instructions en route to the table (a small bottle of hand sanitizer was on every table as well). We started things off with a sparkling wine from Sonoma and a half dozen oysters on the half shell. I'm a Mainer, but will show Duxbury, MA some love, these were fairly high in salinity and tasted like the ocean. True love on a plate.

Appetizers were quite good, if unremarkable: a butternut squash soup with broccoli rabe and a brussels sprouts and pear salad. I would have preferred more pear as a balance to the brussels sprouts' natural bitterness, but all was still good and healthy.

Entrees were: a terrific and light - if you can believe it - house-made campanelle pasta with bolognese - and a well prepared grilled sea bass with sweet potatoes, bacon, and napa cabbage. I liked the sea bass and loved the bolognese, which included shiitake mushrooms, the ever present brussels sprouts, and pecorino. We ordered a side of fries, too, just because, and they also hit the spot.

An excellent, fruity and buttery brown sugar apple crumble with a birthday candle completed the meal, along with amaro to sip. Our server, Mackenzie (the name on the receipt, I hope I'm not mistakened), gave excellent guidance on which amaro to sample, matching each of us at the table with a taste most to our liking.

Mackenzie shared that she had recently begun working at Gramercy Tavern - although it seemed like she'd been there forever, offering excellent advice and exuding warmth from start to finish. She made the meal special and other servers and runners showed a similarly thoughtful energy. Each exuded a caring vibe making our presence feel truly welcomed. The restaurant business is a hard one, especially in these days of COVID. As we head into the winter, it is warm feelings like these that make Gramercy Tavern a place to return to often. If you have a special occasion, you can't go wrong here.

We were extremely patient and sympathetic due to the circumstances of this pandemic we are all living through but tonight's dinner was a disaster. We dined here in August when the first reopened, that experience was not great but we figured we'd give it another chance and to support our neighborhood restaurant which we've frequented a dozen times or so in the past several years. 

This time, we had no service, dishes piling up on our table without anyone attending to us. Food was just okay with very limited selections. Our waiter was just awful. I wonder if this is some alternate staff GT employed since their re opening. Both he and the manager was useless. The manager, she was unable to handle the situation. Were they ever trained? We were charged a bill that exceeded our  actual bill by over $100 and no apology for it either. No one was paying attention. That was what GT was all about when it was a great restaurant. Given COVID, we expected less as we know nyc restaurants are just trying to survive, but this was pathetic. Not going back to what was my favorite restaurant. Sorry, GT, I have no sympathy now.
Lobster Salad was such a delicious starter. We had the Grilled & Braised Pork which was a perfect fall dish and the Campanelle Bolognese which was also delicious.
Beautiful dining room and delicious food. The cocktail was excellent as well (En Maison - whisky and fortified wine).

I have to admit, Gramercy Tavern was really phenomenal. The atmosphere is a delight. My friend got Amuse Bouche Rock Shrimp, which I tried and also liked. It was so flavorful. And employees were extremely polite and courteous. Gramercy Tavern I'm telling all my friends to check you out.

Ordered delivery and had a good experience. The Tavern Bacon & Cheddar Burger and grilled sea bass were excellent, and though it got kind of mushed in transit, the apple crumble was incredible. Obviously it's not the same as dining in, but I'll take it!

Like many people said, Gramercy Tavern is truly phenomenal. It has been on our wishlist, and finally tried it through Restaurant Week 2021. This place far exceeded our sky-high expectation. Everything was perfect. I mean everything- the dish, restaurant ambiance, and customer service. I would like to add more stars if I can.

* Restaurant Week 2021 menu : mushroom lasagna, minestrone soup and a triple chocolate chunk cookie.

The menu doesn't sound special. But Gramercy Tavern elevated the dish up to the level of art. I expected mushroom lasagna might be creamy and a little bit oily, but it was not a usual lasagna dish. There was nothing like pouring sauces/ingredients. Rather it was dry that I could taste layer by layer. It was crispy, flavorful, and tasted healthy. The soup also had mind-blowing depth of flavor. The cookie was delicious, too - I could sense bittersweet dark chocolate taste. Every food had such deep flavors that it was like savoring the taste of harmony. I'd say the experience was similar to that when we drink a good wine.

The restaurant had a classically beautiful interior setting and cozy ambiance. The staffs looked cheerful. We will definitely visit again for dining. It is a must dine restaurant.

COVID delivery review. 

I ordered the burger, the mushroom lasagna, and a cocktail. The burger patty was thick and flavorful but the bun unfortunately was soggy when it arrived. The mushroom lasagna I popped into the microwave and then it was delicious. But it was also quite lukewarm upon arrival. The cocktail was listed on the menu as for two but when it arrived it was only one serving which was pretty disappointing. 

I didn't get the full experience that eating in would provide so I look forward to trying it post-covid and hopefully upping the rating to 5 stars.

My wife and I came here during restaurant week since we had been wanting to try this place for a while. Restaurant week menu is fixed. It includes minestrone soup as an appetizer, mushroom lasagna as the entree and dark chocolate chunk cookie for dessert. The minestrone soup was very hearty. The mushroom lasagna was a perfect combination of creamy yet crispy and very filling (perfect option for vegetarians) and did not fall apart. The chocolate chunk cookie was huge! It was soft on the inside and crunchy on the outside. A perfect end to a delicious meal! We will definitely come back again post covid to dine in (the inside space is beautiful).

We ordered their Restaurant Week special of Minestrone Soup,  Mushroom Lasagna and a chocolate chunk cookie.  Based on their reputation we were excited  to experience their food.  The soup tasted as if it came directly from a can.  The lasagna had absolutely no flavor whatsoever.  The cookie was good but nothing out of the ordinary.  Very disappointing and even at the restaurant week value it was not acceptable.

Restaurant Week 

Mushroom lasagna, minestrone soup, triple chocolate chunk cookie 

I've always wanted to try Gramercy Tavern but not gone around to. Perfect timing/such a coincidence I found other restaurant week spots on the same street so Gramercy Tavern here I come. 

I read some reviews that the mushroom lasagna is the dry type and some people call it flavorless. I agree to both. It was surprisingly bland. I would expect pesto or something to go with it. 
Mushrooms on the side (or it just felt out oops) tasted more tart than eating the lasagna as a whole. 
The size seemed a bit small for a main course but it works out they give a soup and cookie too. 

Minestrone soup 
This is less tomatoy than other minestrones I've had. It's nice in its own way being very homey and warm (flavorwise). The abundance of beans and chickpeas make this very filling. 
Overall not a personal fave

Triple chocolate chunk cookie 
Omg this. First of all it's huge, size of my hand. It has a crunchy outside and border with the insides more chewy!!! The outside is slightly too hard for my liking but still good. I feel like they used brown butter with since it's so rich and has some caramel depth. As for the triple chunk, I wonder how they count that. I think there was just one chocolate piece in my cookie. It was a nice dark chocolate though. It seems like there were small white chocolate bits (not whole chunks) scattered across the bottom. I came across three ish pieces. They were surprise finds. 

But yes as you can tell the cookie sold me. I'm open to trying Gramercy Tavern again for other items.

Excellent restaurant - a perennial favorite; can't wait to go back to NYC and Gramercy.

One question: we were served an excellent non alcoholic cider a couple of years ago -- any way I can find out the name? Presumably it's one of a small number that they stock? Would greatly appreciate it!
Never was a fan of this place.  Overpriced and tasteless food.  I guess being a famous chef gives you the right to charge more and give less!!

Came here with my wife and was so incredibly impressed! Have been wanting to try this place for a while and I can tell you it really didn't disappoint. The Wood Fired Tilefish, Lamb Tripoline, and Caramelized Cheesecake absolutely floored us. The Double Chicken Broth, was also a bit a  hidden gem on the menu. The service was excellent and we felt right at home. We'll definitely plan on returning.

Our new favorite restaurant. Just superb. Ordered the Chilled Oysters, Tile Fish, Ginger Dumplings, and roasted chicken. Overall, excellent!  The service  was outstanding. Tile fish is highly recommended. The chicken was super juicy. Oh my this was good. 
.
Served with potato buns and soft butter. Extensive wine menu. Dumplings were good but a tad salty. We will return!

Made reservations for Gramercy a few days in advance for a weekday dinner. It was a great experience! We were running late and also had dietary restrictions and the hosts were super accommodating and understanding. The ambiance is great (a little dark inside but it's fine). I got the only veggie entree option, the grilled eggplant parmigiana, and it was (a) very tasty and (b) a massive portion. It comes in a HOT cast iron skillet. There are layers of grilled eggplant, a delicious tomato sauce, and cheese. The cheese is bubbling on the sides when it arrives and the bits on the side got all crispy and burnt...so good! The tomato sauce was rich, flavorful, and very unique! I feel like a lot of marinara sauces, especially for eggplant parm ALWAYS taste the same and this one was certainly unique in a good way. It almost had some Indian flavors to it (perhaps the spices?). Eggplant was also well cooked and flavored! We also got the cheesecake for dessert. I really enjoyed the cheesecake, it has a great crust and was the perfect level of sweetness. Did NOT enjoy the sorbet at all though, had a funky citrus taste almost like fake candy citrus vibes. My friends really loved it so it was probably just a personal preference. Overall an amazing experience.

I was SO disappointed by my experience on Friday, my 30th birthday. It is already a huge deal to have to go out to dinner during a pandemic and we did thorough research before choosing a place. We chose Gramercy Tavern because we thought we wouldnt be disappointed. But we were wrong. We understand things are different now but this was not ok.

Our server, Cory I believe was his name, was cold, impersonal and somewhat rude. I did notice that this was only the case with our table and not with the tables in our proximity. Maybe it is a gay issue? I was dining with my husband. And finally, my birthday celebration. He did not acknowledge it. Once reminded about the reason for our dinner by my husband he said "right!". That was it. And then the story you know about dessert. We ordered a dessert, it arrived without a candle, dropped off by a manager... This is a HUGE oversight. 

In short, my birthday dinner was ruined by all of this. By the fact I had to remind your manager it was my birthday. By the awkward interruptions and pushiness from your server, by his decision to even when reminded, not acknowledge my celebration.

If you're not dressed to their liking they will make you eat outside in the rain. Hostess stated they were fully booked at 4:30 in the afternoon. Not one person was in that restaurant. Extremely rude.

Came here for dinner tonight and we had a great experience. Our reservation was for 8pm inside and we were seated a few minutes early. All of the staff was super friendly and on point with everything they did. 
The tables were very spaced out and you can tell they were really taking all precautions for covid. The outdoor dining set up was really nice and comfortable looking, especially with all of the heaters. 
Big shout out to our waitress Kristy, she was amazing!! Made great recs and was kind enough to split a few of the dishes for us since we were sharing everything and just a great overall presence. 
We got...
- espresso martini and the Shadow Box cocktail 
- Double Chicken Broth Scallion Ginger Dumplings
- Brioche Shrimp Toast
- Citrus And Chicory Salad
- Roasted Island Creek Oysters
- Wood Fired Tilefish
- the Tavern Burger 
- Caramelized Cheesecake
- GT Signature Cookies

Everything was great and were bigger portions than what I thought they'd be. 
Our favorite was probably the tilefish... it was cooked perfectly and melted in your mouth like butter!! And the snap peas that came with it were so good too. 
Burger hit the spot too (as it should for a $32 burger!) 
The cheesecake was delish and the sorbet it came with was nice and refreshing. 
The cookies are... wow!! So good and decadent. 
People were coming in at 930pm just to sit and order dessert and honestly not a bad idea. 

We ate in the tavern and it was perfect, would love to come back and try the tasting menu in the dining room one day!

This review is for their Tavern lunch menu / outdoor seating.

Great outdoor dining experience for our first dining-out date of 2021! Would definitely recommend to others who want a special yet casual meal.

First off, the outdoor setting at Gramercy Tavern is so cute. It's on a quiet-ish street off Park, so you don't have the fear of trucks barreling through. The super airy structure only had 3 partial walls with plastic covering windows/roof, so we were able to enjoy all the sun while still being kept safe from the elements. There was plenty of air ventilation, while also maintaining a charming aesthetic with the planters. There was a giant heater for each table (each partitioned with screens), but luckily it was warm enough without.

We were celebrating our 6 year anniversary, which we noted on Resy, and we were greeted with a "Happy Anniversary" by almost everyone we met (hostess upon check-in, serving staff, also a card left on the table). The only person who forgot it was our anniversary that meal was my husband, haha. In general, the service was super warm and friendly - although I wouldn't expect anything less from a Danny Meyer Michelin-starred restaurant.

We ordered two apps (roasted oysters, beef tartare), two entrees (burger, hanger steak), and caramelized cheesecake to share. All the food was delicious and perfectly cooked. The roasted oysters were some of my favorite cooked oysters, because they were chilled and still tasted like raw oysters - just slightly more delicate (although I would've loved either). The beef tartare was well-seasoned although very beet forward (in case that's not your favorite vegetable). The hanger steak was well cooked, but if I were to go again, I would just order two of their burgers.
