It was SO juicy and had a deliciously *dank* flavor (couldn't tell whether it was from the meat or the cheese). I know $32 is quite the splurge for a burger, but if burgers are your love language and you were in the mood for a fancy ish meal anyway - why not???

Having experienced the casual vibe of the Tavern/outdoor seating, I definitely still need to make it back sometime to try out the full prix fixe menu inside!

TOTALLY OVERRATED. So many wonderful reviews, so I thought that gramercy tavern was going to be a hit. Sadly, it was a giant miss. My son had the double broth and dumpling soup. The broth was decent but there were only four teeny tiny dumplings. For an appetizer, I had the asparagus and scallion pancake. It was very "herby". It was like the chef had put scallion cream cheese on top of a pancake and then topped it all with sliced asparagus. After the apps, I thought, this has to get better. It did not. For our main meals, my son got the lamb Tripoline (this was a pasta dish). He was so disappointed. It was not tasty at all and had a slightly burnt flavor. For my main dish, I got the eggplant. It was AWFUL. Mushy. The flavor was so smoky that there was nothing else to taste. Sigh. Did I mention that the meal was super expensive, too? We each at three or four bites of our main dishes and gave up. There are SO MANY AMAZING RESTAURANTS in NYC and this restaurant is definitely NOT one of them.

Our experience here can be summed up in one word: amazing! From the cocktails to the entrees and dessert everything exceeded expectations. The service staff, especially Josh, made us feel welcomed and were so so so nice! Josh is an expert when it comes to the wine and the entire menu! We will definitely be returning soon!

The restaurant is split into 2, the front part where they serve the ala carte menu and the dining hall at the back for tasting menu.

We went for the tasting menu. It was okay but it did felt a bit underwhelming after all the great reviews we've heard. Comparatively to the other tasting menu I've had, this seems to be less value for the price.

I would however say, the ala carte does looks much more impressive. Managed to eye the plates from the ala cart menu whilst walking to the restroom and every plate I saw looks real good. And the price is very reasonable given the setting, location and service.

This is definitely unpopular opinion but the burger here is way overhyped. I stopped in with my friend last week. We made reservations which I for sure recommend. Our waitress was nice and quick to take our orders. We started with cocktails. They were light and summery and delicious! They brought out bread which is very unlike NYC restaurants these days and I always appreciate that (especially when you pay these prices...). We both got the burger. They said it would take 20 minutes to come out but it really only took less than 10. They don't ask what temperature you want it at. It comes out at a medium rare which I don't like that much. It's comes with bacon, cheese and lettuce on it. The side is chips which in my opinion is very disappointing. I want fries! Anyway. The burger was alright. Nothing to rave about. The service was good and the drinks were good. The ambience is fun. But the prices are kind of insane. Good place to try once.

Never disappointing. Pricey but worth every penny. Great service, amazing sommelier, i would go a la carte, the tasting menu is great but small portions. Go for The Tavern menu. My last meal could be the carmelized cheesecake!!

This was one of our fav restaurants pre- COVID. We used to love the food there, both in the main dining room as well as in the tavern. 

In the last two months we have tried this place twice and both times have been disappointed. First time I ordered shrimp brioche toast and hanger steak. Brioche toast was soggy and oily and hanger steak was meh with just a bad side. Second time I ordered chicken dumpling soup and roasted chicken. Frankly our neighborhood Quality eats does better food. 

Hoping this place comes back to its old glory.

I had the privilege of enjoying another excellent lunch at the acclaimed Gramercy Tavern. We started with a special citrus salad and the beef tartare. The beef was seasoned with sesame seeds and served with beets. It was excellent. The citrus salad was perfectly balanced with the right amount of acidity. It was light and bold without being overpowering. 

I went for the duck pasta dish. The confit duck was tender and moist, and the freshly made pasta was tender and lovey. Better than I've had in Venetian Michelin restaurants. For dessert I went for the classic chocolate pudding and a double espresso. 

Service was polished and professional. I'm already planning my next meal.

My favorite 1star restaurant

All things are so perfect

Revisit here again and again and again

My favorite menu is the Fall2020

Gorgeous spot in the city. Note that they don't have the fix dinner menu during Monday to Wednesday. 
The fish was so soft and nice! Highly recommend. Dessert is a must! Service was top notch!
My favorite restaurant in all of NYC! They are always so great and accommodate my food allergies.

We came for our May date night on a humid day for outdoor dining. We usually share many items, so here we go -

We had the Speedy Reyes and the Man About Town for cocktails. Both great - the first is very similar to a traditional margarita. The second was complex and interesting. (We made these over the weekend, enjoying it so much.) 

Starters were the oysters, tartare, and flatbread. All fantastic, but the asparagus and ramp flatbread was the surprise for me. Really interesting and fresh - and filling! The tartare and oysters were very tasty. Love the spice in the oysters, and the crisp from sesame seeds in the tartare. 

Next we shared the burger. Very good - no complaints! Sauce and chips were very nice. Best burger I've ever had? Probably not, but solid for sure. 

Finished with the cookies and rhubarb crisp. Chocolate chip cook was outstanding. I didn't love the hazelnut cookie consistency. Crisp was very good. Tart and delicious. We were only able to take a couple bites of the dessert - pretty full by that time. 

Service was top-notch. No complaints! Looking forward to our next visit.

Came here last night to celebrate a graduation with my friend. We did the 5 course dinner tasting menu for $148 per person. I think the highlight of the dinner was the service. We had the nicest waitress and all the wait staff were super attentive and knew we were there for a special occasion. 
When we arrived we were seated right away. There was a hand written note from the staff. Out of the 5 courses, only the duck really blew us away. The mushroom sauce was delicious with the duck. The other 4 courses were good but weren't very special. I also think two of the courses the asparagus and halibut were too similar. Esp since the halibut had an asparagus sauce... I wish they had change one of those dishes to something different. 
It was a nice touch and very kind that they offered us a complimentary chocolate dessert and dessert wine/mocktail (for me) at the end. Overall it was a great atmosphere and service!

Third time around. Still worthy of the Michelin Star. Still satisfying portions. Still great services. Still delicious. Still not expensive compared to other Michelin Starred restaurants. This is becoming one of my favorite go-to places for a great meal.

The service was fantastic! All the servers were friendly and kind and very accommodating. Everything we ordered was delicious! So glad to be able to squeeze in a reservation this place is always busy! Highly recommend.

My fiance and I came to Gramercy Tavern while we were in New York for the weekend. We had gotten engaged earlier that day and had reservations for the pre-fix menu at night. From the time we got there, the staff at Gramercy Tavern made sure that we felt special and taken care of. Our server offered to take photos of us, brought out complimentary wine, and even a chocolate cake at the end! Not to mention she was personable, knowledgeable about the menu, and repeatedly checked in with us to make sure that we were enjoying our meal. Each course that was brought out was more delicious than the last. While this restaurant is expensive, it is worth it. The staff at Gramercy Tavern went above and beyond to make the night of our engagement perfect!

The most endearing of our 1-Michelin star experiences in NYC, this spot has been my goto since 2015 or so when I visit NYC for business and pleasure.

Tasting menu has consistently been spectacular, and the wine pairing constantly broadens my wine repertoire (a Mt. Etna cab was remarkably inky due to the volcanic terroir, and it introduced me to the delightful world of pet nats as a genre).

Personal anecdote (and THE reason I will visit this place every single NYC trip): I was attempting to cobble a business trip alongside a backpacking travel plan and ended up wandering the streets with my then-gf-now-wife lunchless on Thanksgiving 2018 like two travel-hobos.  They took us in despite being fully booked for Thanksgiving-only meals and cobbled us together an amazing multi-course lunch at a mere pittance of $60 (we insisted the bartender keep the benjamin despite the no-tip policy).  And I wish I remembered the wonderful bartender lady's name, but that just made such a connection that they've earned a customer for life.  Anyhoos, there's my well-earned bias toward Grammercy.
Not mind blowing or anything but I had a great time. We had 5 course tasting menu. Service was great. It's been a while but if I remember correctly, they gave us some breakfast to take home.

Words can't describe how wonderful our dining experience was. The food and drinks were outstanding, the service was second to none and the atmosphere was beautiful and welcoming. We finished our meal hours ago and have not stopped talking about how special our night dining at Gramercy Tavern was. It is easily in our top 2 favorite meals of all time. We will recommend this to everyone we know when asked about a must dine spot in NYC.

My husband and I came here for dinner on a Friday night. We'd both been here on separate occasions for the degustation menu. On this occasion, we were dining outdoors, so only the a la carte menu was available to us. Our experience here recently reminded us why Gramercy Tavern is the cornerstone of fine New York dining, and a must-visit. 
We shared the oysters and the asparagus flatbread for appetizers. You can't really go wrong with oysters, and the ones here were roasted, large and fresh. The flatbread was recommended to us by the waiter and was very tasty - it was like a mini pizza with asparagus paste. 
Gramercy Tavern's burger is well-regarded as one of the best in NYC. I was skeptical of this until I actually tried the burger this time. The burger is only available on the a la carte menu (tavern menu), which is only being served for outdoor dining at this time. The burger tied with Emily's burger which I would rate as the two best burgers in New York. My husband and I couldn't get enough of it. 
For my own main dish, I had the summer squash, which was their only vegetarian main. It consisted of thinly sliced pieces of grilled zucchini over butter beans in a rich sauce. 
We shared the cheesecake for our dessert. The cheesecake was good, but it was the weakest part of what was a phenomenal meal. 
Service was top-notch and ambience managed to feel elegant despite street dining in New York. 
This is a place that you should make it a point to eat at at least once while in New York, and more than that if you get the chance.

(The Tavern): Definitely a Michelin-star worthy meal. Staff are all super professional and decor is both classy and welcoming. Presentation for all the dishes was beautiful. Started off with the chilled carrot soup, which had a really unique blend of flavors. It was a bit of an acquired taste for me; I don't regret ordering it but it probably isn't something I'd order again. For my main course I had the tilefish and I have to mention the seasoning here because the flavor was phenomenal. Finished off my meal with a cappuccino and the passion fruit soufflé. Cappuccino was wonderful, had that rich smoothness that comes with really good espresso, and I didn't feel the need to add any sugar at all. The passion fruit soufflé was probably my favorite part of the meal. Honestly the best soufflé I've had in my life-- super airy, delicate, and it just dissolved in your mouth. Paired very well with the roasted pineapple too. Portion sizes were such that I left feeling very comfortably full after 3 courses.
4 stars for the food, 5 stars for service.  The burger was average, the apps were good.  We'll try it again but it didn't live up to the hype

Came here for the tasting menu + wine pairing. Every dish was solidly executed. The service was excellent. The waiter was knowledgeable about the wine and dishes. The wine pours were generous. Overall, highly recommend.

How this isn't a 3-star Michelin restaurant is beyond me. The service is impeccable. Friendly, knowledgeable, accommodating and unobtrusive. The food is incredible. The 5-course pre-fixe we had last night was as good as any meal I've ever had. Been here several times. It never disappoints.

I would guess the motto of Gramercy Tavern is, 
Our guests know they can get a decent meal cheaper. 
But our customers know they are spending just a bit more for a truly great meal, with respectful service and honest quality.  No angles.  No tricks.  No fake smiles with gimmicky meals.  The best!   
I know my meal might run more than many.  But it's predictably the F'n best anywhere.  
I challenge anyone to make even a better hamburger.  The wines are first class with no high margin private label tricks.  Always the best.

The food was a 4-5 star experience; the service, however, was more of a 2 star. But I feel bad giving them less than a four because it wasn't our waitress's fault. They were just extremely understaffed. We sat down at 6:45 pm and we couldn't leave until almost 10pm because of how slow the service was. Meanwhile most of us had early AM obligations. Aside from the extremely slow service with extreme waits between ordering drinks, food, desserts and getting the check, it was an otherwise pleasant experience. The executive chef greeted each table and we always had water.

We split some amazing things. 
#Apps
1) shrimp toast - very fresh on a brioche toast. I was expecting it to have more of a crisp to it, but overall it had a very soft texture.
2) beef tartare - simple and fresh.

#Mains
1) cheeseburger - not sure what they use to make the burger, but it had this deliciously greasy taste that was very different from other burgers I've had. 
2) chicken - I would get this again next time! I don't know how they make the chicken soooo juicy. 
3) fish - the taste and the texture was there! 
4) steak - very simple and very good. 

#Dessert
1) peach melba sundae - MUST GET. It tastes like the best of summer in your mouth. I'm hoping to come back for dessert only; just to have my other friends try this sundae 
2) cheesecake - hard to really assess given how much I loved the peach melba sundae. It was good but not nearly as good. 
3) chocolate pudding - this was complimentary given how slow the service was! We appreciated it. I actually tried this first of the three desserts and thought it tasted amazing. But after having that peach melba sundae, I had another spoonful of the pudding and it also paled in comparison.

In summary, you must come and try this peach melba sundae. Seems like it's a seasonal addition. The time is now. And I hope and pray that you have better service.

I have never spent so much money at a restaurant - $790 - for three people,
and on ordering an after-dinner drink for a guest, been told we could not order second rounds and had to vacate the table.  AN ULTIMATELY TACKY EXPERIENCE and a total disgrace!!!

We got there at 5 pm (weird hour) and were told to leave at 8:30.  I'm well past the age of disturbing the peace.  Had I been told there was a meter on the table, I would have chosen more selectively.

I think it must have been the grandson who told us, a Howdy Doody look-alike with the grace of Baby Face Nelson.

An embarrassing hosting moment - and a pox on the establishment.  Shame on them.

My first review of any kind on the web.  HORRIBLE!
SLV
I got Gramercy for lunch and wasn't too impressed. I probably had higher than normal expectations though since it has a Michelin star and ranks as one of the best restaurants in NYC.

Gramercy is my favorite New American restaurant in New York; we ate at the Tavern, not the tasting menu, but it is still a Michelin starred establishment. 
Our server Hailey was very professional, and the servers felt practically invisible for most of the service. It's a particular style of service which the tavern does very well.
For apps we started with the flatbread, brioche, and oysters. The flatbread was an absolute standout: nice and light, flavorful, and really made me hungry for what was to come. Others have recommended the oysters, I personally don't think they were worth it.
For mains we got the burger and duck pasta. Both were amazing, and the best iteration of the dish I have ever tasted.
We got the peach melbae sundae and the cookies for dessert. Both were very good, the chocolate cookie in particular was the best cookie I've had in a restaurant.
If I come back I'll be getting the flatbread, burger, duck pasta, and cookies.

Really great brunch and mimosas, and perfect location near Gramercy Park! I also love the jam they bring out with the cornbread in the fall - such a nice touch. The takeout was not as good as sitting in restaurant and I was disappointed in the cauliflower (pretty bland for the price) but in-person dining is great and I'll definitely be back.

This review is for the tasting menu in the dining room. 

Overall, solid for the price which is about 150 per person and 100 to 200 more for optional wine pairings.

The tasting menu was five courses, 3 with seafood (fluke, lobster, arctic char), roasted duck and one desert. Wine pairings were 1 sparkling, 2 white or rose, 1 red and 1 desert. 

Nothing that absolutely wowed except one of the wine pairings, unsurprisingly the only red in the reserve pairing list, but everything had strong execution both food and service. Out of all the food pairings I would say the Arctic char was one of the best I've had in recent memory. The taste profile was very similar to salmon.

If you're into seafood tasting menus with a strong preference for white and rose wine pairings, this may be your jam.

Gramercy Tavern used to offer some of the best tasting menus in the city. While I'm so glad that they've been able to survive the pandemic, its unfortunately come with a cost of a different (less impressive) dining experience. 

What you see on the menu is what you get. There was a time when you would be offered exciting surprises like an amuse bouche, palate cleansers and house made chocolates after dessert. Those times are gone. 

With that said, the food, service and wine are still excellent. Our menu included the marinated fluke, poached lobster, smoked arctic char, roasted duck breast and a play on strawberry shortcake. The Arctic char and the duck were delicious and memorable.

Where to start! I was inspired to have my first *Michelin starred* dining experience based on previous Instagram posts from my favorite chef/restaurant owners here in Rochester. They love and are inspired by this place? Say less! Whether you care about the value of the Michelin system or not, there is a certain "we are awesome" swagger and energy that comes with dining in a restaurant that has something (but also nothing?) to prove. Giving off real Anton Ego* from Ratatouille vibes (LOL), I put my phone away, sat down at my reserved Tavern table by myself, and really soaked in the entire experience.

My server was kind, polite, helpful, not in the least bit overbearing, and answered all of my questions. With no fridge in my hotel, I was determined to conquer every delicious bite of this meal and leave leftover-less. I went with a chianti, flatbread appetizer, and steak. The entire menu is a wealth of riches - so choosing was pretty tough. This goes without saying, but everything really was fantastic. Unique flavors, flavorful sauces, and a perfect balance of light veggies to rich meat and tangy punch. Each bite (minus one) was pure perfection.

The minus one comes from a piece of green plastic in my steak dish that looked a lot like a piece of parsley, but was in fact plastic. I really thought about not writing this review at all, but I DID want a way to remember the experience in all of its perfect imperfection. The staff was obviously apologetic and amazing about the whole situation, and I finished my steak in it's entirety without apology. 

I was laughing and smiling about the entire situation for the remainder of my evening in New York, and having this happen made the experience even more unforgettable than it already was. That piece of green plastic was a beautiful reminder that, no matter how high our expectations are and no matter how much pressure of perfection we put on ourselves, shit just happens. In classic Megan-is-the-main-character form, I felt CHOSEN by this plastic!!! How often do you think someone gets plastic in their food at this establishment? My guess is like...never ever?? It was my destiny.

If you're looking for a perfect meal and human experience, get yourself to Gramercy Tavern. I look forward to going back with my partner for their full tasting and wine menu someday in the near future. Amazing location in an under-explored-by-me neighborhood. Get yourself there and treat yourself!

*Disclaimer: I am in NO WAY comparing this review/my status as a reviewer that of the brilliant and incomparable Anton Ego. He is singular.

While it has declined a bit compared to pre-pandemic, the food is still delicious and the experience is generally still good. If prices start to go up, I would say it wouldn't be worth it. But as it stands, for the current prices, I'd definitely recommend. 

(review for a la carte, not tasting menu)

Went on a dinner date with two of my girl friends and decided to sit Outside and enjoy some fine dining. We had boozy suzeys for drinks which was strong, but all the cocktails were about $18 just to give you an idea of pricing. We ordered the shrimp toast and the chilled island creek oysters with leek mignonette. It was my first time eating oysters surprisingly with a little convincing from my friend and it wasn't bad. I have texture issues so I thought I was going to freak out, but not too bad especially with the leek mignonette on top. The shrimp toast forget about it to die for literally. I will be Back just for that. My friends got the tile fish and the hanger steak. The fish was good but not a huge fan of the fregola mix underneath. The hanger steak was absolutely delicious. I got the brick pressed chicken and the grilled flavor was so good. I added a pinch of salt could be my palette but otherwise it was absolutely delicious and I loved the potatoes and pickled garlic scapes underneath,
This place is great.  Great food, pricey, but worth it.  The interior is beautiful and the service is always spot on.

Eh. Went to the bar portion and despite the excellent service I was underwhelmed. The broccoli salad was the best thing we had but the oysters, tartare, steak, and duck pasta dish were pretty average. Food was a 3/5 for me and I bumped it up for the service.

Not what it was. Food was very good but a tad skimpy (had 5 course tasting menu for $175). No bread, no palate cleanser, no petit fours. Bathroom grout was nasty and walls have seen better days. Staff was competent (although a bit scruffy/casual) but I've have equally competent service at mid-range restaurants. Need to up their attention to details.

My husband booked a prefixed dinner for our anniversary a month in advance and talked to them about my shellfish allergy and no raw meat diet restriction due to my pregnancy. They said no problem and will accommodate. When we arrived, the waiter literally told me I can't have the first course as it is a semi raw fish and  they are not going to cook it well done, so I should just have a cold carrot soup instead. Then the second course is a lobster!!! They will just simply remove it from the menu for me, but I can have some really nice garbanzo beans (the garnish) instead. Are you kidding me??? Do you think I'm just some stupid rich dumb face who would just pay whatever for whatever bullshit you are selling? I said oh well it's not going to work out for me and the waiter kept pushing it on me, "I think it's very nice, it has a nice flow, first have some cold soup, then eat some nice beans (then pay 500 dollars and get out here). You guys ruined my anniversary.

Gramercy Tavern is as relevant a restaurant as it has ever been. Excellent was the base line for each of the five courses on the tasting menu in the dining room. Service was flawless. The attention to detail for the non-alcoholic beverage offerings is unparalleled.
Impressive restaurant overall. The elegant yet non-pretentious environment, the knowledgeable staff, the food presentation, everything was on point.

Only knocking it down one star because the service was a bit spotty. Our table wasn't ready in time and although the host was nice and offered to grab us drinks during the wait, no one actually followed through. We were then seated in the tavern area at a table for 4 (there were 2 of us) so we asked if we could move to a more intimate one next to us. No prob, adjusted. But it took a lot of time for our server to come over and place orders/etc. She did notice our body language and certainly picked it up thereafter but the food: omg, so good! And drinks were great. We'll give them a pass on the slip ups and would likely visit again.

My brother recently had a milestone birthday, and he wanted to go out to a really nice restaurant to celebrate. You didn't have to tell my family twice, because we always mark special occasions with restaurant celebrations - and if there's a chance to try someplace new I jump on it. That being said, we were able to snag a reservation for a Sunday lunch and headed on down to Manhattan. 

I quickly learned that there are two different options to choose when dining at Gramercy Tavern. The first option is the dining room, which has a set price and fixed menu. The other option is the Tavern, where you can order a la carte. We chose the latter, since we preferred ordering off a menu and the dining room can be really pricey (not something we were looking for as a family meal). We were seated outside which was great since it was a beautiful day and the restaurant did an awesome job making their outdoor tables as comfortable and possible. 

The menu contains mostly New American fare, plus updated takes on more classic dishes. I started with a garden salad, it was pretty good and contained pieces of prosciutto which was a nice touch. It was light and fresh which made it a great starter. I had heard great things about the Tavern Burger, so I decided to get that as my main. The burger was great - really juicy, and topped with a tasty aioli. The burger came with duck fat potato chips which were super crispy and the perfect complement to the burger. 

Since it was a special occasion, we opted for dessert. We shared the ricotta blintz and the cookie plate with milk. The blintz was good - my grandma loved blintzes so whenever I see them on a menu I always order them. The ricotta was ricotta was just enough and the apricot that came with was a nice complement. The cookies were great - they were thick and warm and perfect for sharing. We got one chocolate chip and one oatmeal raisin and they were some of the best I've had of each. 

Service was excellent - we were consistently tended to and it really augmented the whole experience. Overall, I had an excellent time at Gramercy Tavern. The food was delicious, the service was a highlight, and I would have no hesitations about returning. This is definitely a great place to go both for a more casual lunch or a special occasion.

If I could give more stars I would. My dining party and I had the best time here and recommend it to anyone. 
The bread for the table was some of the best- even the butter was delightful. 

The service was impeccable as well. I dropped my fork and right away they came running with a new one. 

For drinks, we got the Sichuan slushy and sherry cola. Small for the price but tasty. $18 for each. 

One of the dishes we ordered was the brick pressed chicken. It was juicy and so good. The portion size was pretty big and would definitely order it again. 

We also got the tile fish. It seemed like a small portion but it was enough. If you're extremely hungry it's probably not enough but the taste was out of this world. It was fresh and savory. Every bit was eaten and thoroughly enjoyed. The clams that came with it added an extra level of flavor and depth. 

For dessert, we got the GT Signature cookies. They were huge, moist, and perfect. Soft and chewy with a perfect amount of toppings. The triple chocolate chunk was the best but the blueberry oatmeal was fantastic too. 

Although pricey, we Would definitely come back!

An absolutely delightful restaurant that really do try their best to make your dining experience as lovely as possible. Their dining room is exclusively their tasting menu. The cocktails listed on their menu are a touch on the sweet side for my tastes but were overall quite refreshing for a summer evening meal. The pre-course appetizer was in effect a cheesy biscuit with some cured meat, quite nice although a bit boring in flavor. Definitely recommend having something bright to drink with this as it is quite salty. You also have some warm bread with softened butter which I will always take. Bread is of a different fare than what you would most commonly see, the crumb is quite soft and fluffy. 

The first real course is their marinated fluke which had a really nice pop of different textures. The shishito peppers are by no means spicy but were just enough to give a pleasant tingle. The grilled beans and lobster was really tasty and the lobster tasted really juicy and sweet. The smoked artic char was ridiculously smooth and creamy in texture and the summer tomatoes were exploding in sweetness and flavor. The duck breast was probably the best I've had, extremely tender and perfectly seasoned. The dessert course was a berry cheesecake which thankfully wasn't too sweet or heavy after the duck dish. 

I'd overall highly recommend coming to their tasting menu although I would make sure you can eat everything on the menu before coming by.

Unfortunately, a less than stellar experience here. Gramercy Tavern used to be one of my favorite restaurants. I hadn't been here since pre-covid and frankly, I was disappointed. They used to have a wide selection of breads that you could choose from, but now they just give a cold, not so tasty brioche.  Shrimp toast was a tiny portion for $18. Entrees were oversalted. We had the hanger steak, the duck pasta, and the tilefish. Tilefish was probably the best of the three. And dessert was $16 for a chocolate pudding cake that was literally three spoonfuls...I was quite shocked by the portion size. I don't remember leaving Gramercy Tavern hungry, but did so this time.

Decided to check out this place out, finally! Made a reservation during restaurant week. 

I was pleasantly surprised to see that the dining area had a more casual bar/tavern like section and a more formal dining room at the back. 

The seafood was good - lobster and artic char. The fish was on the salty side, just a bit, for me. 

 The dessert was my favourite. The cheesecake was almost like a creme brulee texture with the best tart sorbet and berries. 

The duck was excellent. So succulent. 

They have an extensive wine list. But we ended up ordering cocktails and wine by the glass. The Nero d'avola was a new addition to the wine menu. Definitely glad we tried it. 

The service was excellent. Can't complain. Would return to try the burger.

Had a great dinner here last night.  Restaurant is beautiful.  We were greeted immediately and were sat at a very nice table.  We had brought in a bottle of wine so the som came to our table and decanted the wine, very nice touch.  Our server was the only low point to our experience.  Was not overly friendly and really didn't explain the menu, nor did he make any recommendations when asked.  He also did not talk to us about the drink menu.  Dinner was wonderful, with get flavor profiles that complimented each other.  We stated with the corn flat bread, very well done and just the right amount of heat.  For entree went with the flat iron - they didn't ask how I wanted it prepared but came out perfectly MR.  When making the reservation we informed them it was a birthday celebration.  I do have to say one of the best birthday desserts I have ever seen.  Delicate coconut cream cake on a little pedestal, was delicious!

Had dinner here w friends last week.  Excellent!   Service 5 .   Yummmmy 
Reservations a must .

WOW SO GOOD! 

I had the tasting menu with the wine pairing. I'd say only about two of the wines were spot on pairings but I wasn't a fan as it went on. The wine choices got sweeter and sweeter and just wasn't my cup of tea. 

The food however, was superb! There wasn't a single thing I'd add or omit from any of the dishes. My favorite being the lobster dish. Nothing beats perfectly cooked lobster, nothing! 

The duck was also the best I've ever had. Just melt in your mouth, juicy, flavorful and the skin was crisp and easy to eat. Mushrooms were sprinkled about the plate and wow were they good. ( I'm never a huge fan of mushrooms ). Very good dish. 

Nothing but raving reviews for every single dish I ate, down to the complimentary bread and butter. 

The service was also very good. Our server seemed to be very knowledgeable of the menu and attentive to our needs. My water glass was never empty and the food kept showing up in a timely manner. 

5 stars !  ( s/b this is my third time visiting GT but, by far the best experience. I'm so happy to know that some restaurants haven't lost their charm, possibly even improved through the pandemic).

Oh how I have loved this restaurant.  Oh how happy I was to see them on Goldbelly.  And still happy when I ordered the the burgers for a picnic today.

Less happy when tracking showed it had not left the restaurant at 6pm when delivery was supposed to be by 7(yesterday) and still less happy when it arrived  today at  five pm completely melted so much so the meat was bloody.  Satisfaction from Goldbelly - Nil.

And my opinion of the Gramercy Tavern is destroyed.

We went to New York for a weekend to see the U.S. Open, some thing we love to do. Our friends have an apartment in the city who are complete foodies so they took us around for the weekend to the best restaurants. We had lunch here, we sat outside in the street. The only thing I would change about our visit, I probably would've rather sat inside in the nice atmosphere and air-conditioning... Not outside in the street. I had salad and fish as the main, everything was so incredibly good... It was amazing. Even with the restricted menu because of Covid, they nailed it! We even shared a dessert and we all felt satisfied and not stuffed, the food was just incredible. The fish was cooked perfectly, my husband had the beef... The sauce on each one of them was just as good, can't say enough. The starters were around $20 and the main dishes were 30-50$. Even though it's a little pricey, I would definitely go back!
Love this place! The food was excellent and the service was top-knotch. The poached lobster was incredible and tasted just like the lobster I've had in Maine.

Our meal was so good my son & fiancée are choosing to have their wedding dinner here!

My son and his fiancée have been going on tastings and they're finding the food at reception halls bland. 

I'm asked by them: Dad, what restaurant would you choose to have a elegant party with amazing food? I said without question, Gramercy Tavern. Let's go for dinner so you can decide for yourself?

If you've never been to Gramercy Tavern, its one of the most beautiful restaurants in NYC. Granted, It doesn't have a view but the interior of the restaurant is decorated warmly with wood tones and flowers. The room we were shown (I posted a picture) made our eyeballs pop out of our head. Very elegant and the tasting menu along with the Tier Two Package works for our guests.

Once we had our viewing, we sat down for Sunday dinner. We ordered drinks, I ordered a Viva la Vita which had reposado tequila and freshly squeezed lime juice. The cocktail was so good I had two!

I'm going to New Orleans soon so the roasted oysters were calling me. Topped with Habanero Butter and Swiss Chard, this was a delicious starter. 

When I told the waiter Strozzapreti means strangled priest, he busted out laughing! This was a perfect dish with a little heat on the finish. Always my goto when I see it on the menu. My wife ordered the Arctic Char and my son ordered the classic burger. My future daughter in law also ordered the Strozzapreti, nice! My son was raving about the burger, from the meat blend to the chips fried in duck fat. We had a terrific meal at the tavern. 

Now it comes time for dessert. I zeroed in on the Chocolate pudding cake (As well as my daughter in law) my son went for the blintz and my wife left her comfort zone and had the cookie plate.

The Chocolate Pudding Cake?? Ta die for! Made with Mascarpone Cream, Pecans and topped with a large dollop of Coconut Ice Cream. Sinfully good.

My wife had the GT Cookie Plate. It came with a small glass of milk and two cookies, one was Triple Chocolate Chunk and the other was Oatmeal. Very good and she enjoyed it.

Gramercy Tavern is a beautiful restaurant, one of my favorites in NYC. My son is going to book the dining room next year based on our experience.

Decided to come to the tavern part of gramercy tavern for my birthday dinner and was so happy I did. Everything was delicious and perfect from start to finish.

We sat outside and it was a really nice set up. Our drinks arrived promptly and all of the staff was so efficient and made sure your glasses were always refilled and you were satisfied. We split the brioche shrimp toast and beef tartare as starters and the shrimp toast is a MUST. It was one of the best things I have ever tasted, make sure to ask for it even if you don't see it on the menu.

For entrees I got the chicken and my fiancé got the burger. Both were amazing too. The other highlight was the dessert. We split the chocolate pudding cake and it one of the best desserts I've ever had. It is like a chocolate lava cake on steroids with homemade ice cream and candies pecans and coconut flakes.

Such a good meal, I had a great birthday dinner!

I have said it before that Michelin's standards for restaurants in US vary quite drastically from that for those in Europe. Have never been disappointed by one Michelin stars restaurants in Europe. Well, this was the second time I was disappointed in New York. I had been meaning to try this NYC landmark for some time , finally did last weekend. The burger seemed promising. I asked for a medium should have perhaps gone for the medium rare as suggested by the friendly waitress. Nevertheless the burger was decent but the bacon was burnt black. I pointed it out to one of the waiting staff and he said it was supposed to be charred!!! I have had better burgers elsewhere in NYC, so not really exceptional for a special trip.

Lovely meal, I wish the portion sizes were triple because it was that good, I wanted more and more. At the end of the meal I was quite full. My least favorite was the sorbet paired with the cheesecake, it was way too tart and a lil bitter to my liking. I would definitely like to come back for the bistro section. Service was excellent and I absolutely loved the coconut cake that they gave my mother in Law for her birthday, it was the best coconut cake I ever had, so fresh and coco-nutty.

I like the new protocols on Covid19. The stricter the rules, the safer I feel. 
The food was delicious and the service was perfect. I love when the waiters come in unison to drop off the food at the same exact timing!

We've been here 20 years ago & nothing has changed. Still great!!!

Over hyped. Had a reservation and ordered our entrees the minute we sat down.  90
Minutes later we are still waiting for our food. Actually had to ask tor coffee to stay awake while we waited for our food there are 10,000 other places in the city to eat. Do them a favor and eat there.

My Husband and I decided to book a reservation at the Gramercy Tavern, and let me tell you we were blown away by the duck meatloaf!!! The service at this place was on point we were never without water, drinks, and smiles. From the moment you walk in, and from the time the bill comes. You are catered to and checked on to see if you are well fed, and saved room for dessert. We ate the milk and cookies and we were tilted! Our time at the Gramercy was memorable and we cant wait to return! That duck meatloaf!!! Why is it not on goldbelly already?!!

Two friends and I came here for lunch -- I got the duck strozzapreti, they got some fish entree (forgot the name), and we had island creek oysters to share as an appetizer. Oysters were good, pretty standard. The duck strozzapreti was for sure better than their fish entree which didn't have that much flavor honestly, but the strozzapreti was too salty IMO. In general, I feel like for how expensive this place is I expected much tastier food.

Just like Blair Waldorf, this is my absolute favorite restaurant in New York.

Not only is the interior classic New York with tons of florals and greenery, but the entire vibe is so cool and elegant. 

We came at lunch on a Saturday and sat at the bar since  we didn't have a reservation. I would say we won't make that mistake again next time as the place does fill up, but we had such a wonderful experience at the bar I exclusively want to sit there! The bartenders were friendly and charming and even comped us a round of cocktails. Amazing!

We each had two cocktails and split the corn flatbread, shrimp toast, and tavern burger. Every. Item. Was. Exquisite. There was not a single crumb left on our plates. And the kitchen even cut our burger in half for us and delivered them on separate plates. Small gestures like that really show how much a restaurant cares for its patrons.

I can't wait to come back and try even more off this menu. 10/10 would recommend!

Ok so I don't usually write reviews, but I think this is my all time favorite dining experience I've EVER had in New York. If you want to talk about service above and beyond, with equally incredible food, this is the place for you. Shout out to Haley! Everything was to die for and the staff was truly the nicest. Can't wait to come back!

Sublime! Came with my family for the tasting menu and loved every minute of it. The service and food were absolutely beautiful, and best of all, there was no music playing in the background, so we could focus on the food and each other.

We went to Gramercy Tavern this past weekend for my husband's birthday. 

The good: our food was delicious - especially the gluten free bread. It was by far the best GF bread I've ever had in my life. All of the dishes on the tasting menu were really well made, and we especially loved the dessert. All three desserts they brought out were delicious, especially the "chocolate pudding". Cocktails were really nice as well - we really loved the yes yes yuzu. 

The bad: we were brought out the wrong thing 4 different times during our experience (which is a little scary when you have celiac/can't eat gluten. For example, I told the restaurant in advance of my gluten situation and again once we were seated, but at one point they brought me regular bread with gluten that I almost accidentally ate.). It was also a little too much food. We do a lot of tasting menus, but have never felt that full before after a meal, so I would defiantly recommend taking it slow on the bread. Service was also not great, and we were a little underwhelmed. 

Overall, food and drinks were great, service could be better. Would definitely consider coming back just for the gluten free bread - it was the best!

Gramercy Tavern is a place I require myself to visit everytime I'm in the city. It has yet to let me down, and I'm happy to report that once again it has satisfied a craving. They understandably now recommend reservations for their indoor and outdoor seating. They do however have reserved a select number of tables for walk-in diners.

The service here has always been good, however this time the cadence was a little slow, which was surprising because of how empty the dining room was at 11:30am on a Sunday. Not a big deal, but something that was noticed.

Brioche Shrimp Toast - How they get the toast to be this shrimpy is beyond me. If you like shrimp, give this a shot. Delicious.

Grilled Hanger Steak - In terms of preparation and accoutrement, I'm not sure how much better it can get. Tender, flavorful steak with the right amount of sweetness and umami in each bite.

The Tavern Burger - Since having tried this burger 6+ years ago I haven't experienced one that was better for the money. While the doneness was a little off for my taste, it didn't stop it from being juicy and craveable.

I forget the name of the apple dessert (Apple Sundae?) that we ordered but it incredible. If you're a fan of apple pie, this is up your alley. Layers of cooked, creamy apples, flaky pastry, luscious vanilla ice cream, and a super smooth frozen apple treat that reminded me of applesauce. If I hadn't eaten so much earlier I would have been happy to just sit and savor this. This seemed to be new on the menu and my god it was impressive. A textural marvel to say the least.

Outstanding tasting menu, flawless service and a lovely acknowledgment of my anniversary. Despite that this is definitely not just a special occasion destination. Lots of business meetings and date nights, family dinners and friends get togethers  but still special. Really worth the cost to get such high quality food and service in a lovely airy space.

An institution that I personally find highly overrated. I had the burger and it was good, but not the best burger of my life or anything extraordinary. I also had the pasta dish and found myself wishing for more flavor. The cookies are good but a little bit too sweet. All in all this place doesn't feel worth the hassle it takes to get reservations, and the food doesn't warrant the price point. I will say the service here is exceptional and always 10/10.
Always has amazing food from a large menu. Can eat there any time of the day! Quick service too

This review is solely for the Tavern portion of Gramercy Tavern. Restaurant Week is a fun event that I eagerly look forward to every year. Our experience at Tavern at Gramercy was mixed. We asked to be seated at one of the empty tables adjacent to the building after we rejected a table in the street close to a noisy Verizon truck. They left us standing in front of the empty row of tables for about fifteen minutes while the waiter cleared the issue with the manager. We felt like unwanted patrons.

After setting the table and taking our orders, we waited quite a while for the butter to smear on the tender rolls. For a restaurant of this caliber with several Michelin stars it seemed rather odd that there wasn't enough whipped butter on hand. Helga's appetizer of Brioche Shrimp Toast was like a sponge soaked in oil with little shrimp taste. Her main course of Grilled Hanger Steak with mushrooms, leeks and carrot salsa was minuscule and not only looked but tasted dry. Helga chose a Pale Ale to drink with her meal and this also took a while to be served. I began with the Grilled Corn Flatbread flecked with shisito peppers, Parmesan and pickled Fresno. Both crisp and chewy, the tangy flavors made me sing with joy. Duck Strozzapreti followed. Shredded duck with golden cherry tomatoes and the pasta married flavorfully. I am fond of ice cream so chose the Peach Melba Sundae which had raspberry sauce, peaches and almond cookies. Too many of the cookies in the sundae marred what could have been a stellar chilled dessert. I would have preferred more fruit and ice cream. Before we left the manager apologized for the table snafu but what we paid left Helga with a slightly bitter taste and she won't be returning. For me, the duck beckons.

I've been to the Gramercy Tavern before in their Dining Room and decided to go to the other section (the Tavern) to throw my friend a birthday dinner.  I told Gramercy Tavern we were celebrating his birthday in advance and they wrote a cute note and a dessert which was much appreciated.  The Tavern is substantially more affordable than the Dining Room but I would definitely not call it cheap- and to be honest it shouldn't be.  The food quality and atmosphere are great.  My only qualm about the meal hence four vs. five stars is that, honestly speaking, I wasn't a huge fan of the burger.  It was super salty to me and albeit I do consume a lot of salt (don't do this kids! lol) it was a bit too much for me.  I had a piece of my friend's sea bass which was delicious.  I do have a soft spot for Gramercy Tavern though and will definitely return- they just need to bring back that absolutely fantastic goat cheese and bread!

Gramercy Tavern strikes again!!!  We came back for dinner to celebrate another special occasion.  Today, there was a 5-course tasting menu, offered with or without wine pairing.  The food was extraordinary, as usual.  We were served a marinated fluke tartare with concord grapes, poached lobster with a basil butter sauce, smoked arctic char, roasted duck with squash, and a honey goat cheesecake.  Friendly and very attentive service.

Food was good (on the saltier side the night we went) but for the price would probably would not come again. Especially knowing that I could get similar quality and experience for a lower price. Shout out to the waiters, they were very sweet

Great Michelin representation. The dishes are stunning. The skills are displayed. The menu was built great (cold crudo to seared duck).

We ordered the wine pairing as well and loved the accompaniment. We only got one and we shared it, which was perfect for us!

Consistently delicious food, including for those vegetables-focused like me. Amazingly professional and warm staff. Cozy setting with food themed murals by local artist and fire grill. Everything is always perfectly executed.

I booked the dinner reservation a month ahead of my visit to celebrate my birthday. It was for Saturday and I was excited as the only available time was for 9pm. The menu was somewhat limited. Service was attentive and during pandemic, they did a good job in checking vaccine proof and verified against ID. Pro tip: do not be seated close to the open kitchen. The air ventilation was extremely poor in the dining room. After dinner our clothes, hair.... smelled like a chimney, which totally negated the whole dining experience. I didn't expect that from a restaurant in this caliber or price range. I phoned the restaurant the next day and left a message with a receptionist and never hear back again. There are many fine dining restaurants in the city to choose from. I would not return again.

I finally got to try Gramercy Tavern, even if was only for their lunch menu. But, boy, what a treat it was. I went in with a group of people from work. We ordered everything from the appetizer list. 

The ones that stood out the most was definitely the Steak Tartare. I believe there was hummus inside as it was served with a pita chip. The only downside was I wish they gave more than 1 chip to scoop out the tartare. Since for some it maybe a bit much to just eat the raw meat alone.

Also we had a salad which was very good, but I forgot what it was called. I think there was prosciutto on top and the dressing had a bit of a kick to it.

For the main course I got the Tavern Burger, let me just say this was probably one of the best burgers I've ever had. The sauce in the burger had a smoky taste which was really good. The chips were good, but at the end of the day they were just chips. The buns and pickles definitely were homemade, which I think is unique about this burger. 

Some of my coworkers were able to try other entrees such as the steak, chicken and duck meatloaf. I was able to taste a little bit of the duck meatloaf. It was really good, I thought it would have a gamey taste to it, but not at all and I couldn't even tell if I was eating duck.

As for desserts we had the Sticky Toffee Pudding, Chocolate Pudding Cake and the Apple Sundae.

The Sticky pudding was probably the best dessert, but with that being said the Apple Sundae was also very good. If you had to pick a dessert that you think everyone would enjoy I would say the safest bet is the Apple Sundae. The Apple Sundae has a layer of Apple Sorbet on the bottom which was to die for and you could tell that the sorbet was freshly made in house.

Overall great experience accompanied by great food and service!

Thank you!!i
Loved the atmosphere, the staff, the wine selections, and the food! What we especially loved was the beet salad and the cookie desert! The duck meatloaf was okay, but the swordfish was fantastic!

This review is for the dining room tasting menu. 

Ambiance: the restaurant is decorated beautifully for the holidays - not sure what it looks like normally, but it felt super cozy and festive. 

Service: all in all the service is great. Our main server was very friendly and knowledgeable. There were just some minor qualms, but I think my expectations are super high when it comes to fine dining. One of two of the diners is allergic to shrimp (which they were aware of) and the server (not our main server) gave the shrimp pasta to him instead of me - that could've been quite disastrous. We were also asked if we wanted more bread, which we said yes to, but it never came. 

Food: I will preface this with saying the food was cooked to perfection and seasoned beautifully. I'm glad I got to experience this institution, but the dishes didn't feel super unique and not sure if it's worth the steep price. Surprised by people saying they left stuffed because I definitely did not. Also, go in knowing this is more of a traditional tasting menu versus something with experimental dishes. 

-Seasonal Cranberry Mocktail: this was delicious. Not on the menu, but created by the bartender for me which was really nice. 

-Marinated Fluke: I feel like I've had this flavor profile in a lot of hamachi crudo dishes before, but it was very fresh and light. 

-Smoked Arctic Char: this dish totally reminds me of Le Bernadin. It was delicious. The fish basically melts in your mouth and the sauce was really good. 

-Poached Lobster Lumache: really good. Just me being knit picky, but I wish the sauce was thicker - it was a bit watery. I also feel like they really skimped on the lobster. For the price tag, there should be more (there's literally three small pieces). Also, they didn't give more lobster for the person who couldn't eat shrimp, so that felt like a rip off. 

-Roasted Duck Breast: cooked perfectly. 

-Caramelized Goat Cheesecake: this was good, but a lot. I don't love goat cheese and it's quite a big portion of cheese so I didn't finish this.

We went for Thanksgiving! Always wanted to go and finally had the chance since we weren't having guests for the holidays and we were too lazy to do a big meal that day! First of all, the place is beautiful, the atmosphere was amazing, the service and staff was attentive and nice (and funny). Now for the food... though it was a lot, it was SOOO good! Met my expectations! The best part was we had lots of leftovers that we enjoyed it again at home the following evening!

GT is normally my favorite; go to restaurants anywhere in the world.  Unfortunately, the last couple of experiences have been tarnished immensely by one of the bartenders.  If you are served at the bar, beware of potential rude and boorish service from this particular "professional".

You can choose between the dinning room which is a price per person course meal with chefs choices. Or you can choose the tavern which is just like a normal restaurant and that's what this review is based on for your information. 

This restaurant was sensational. Right in the heart of Manhattan, the location was perfect. The menu was small so I assumed the few dishes would be quality and they sure were. The duck was outstanding. I'm not going to sit here and describe all the menu items I liked because they switch the menu often. Hopefully the duck is available as your reading this. This place hits all the right spots and is a model restaurant. Also I saw a Ferrari 458, Lamborghini Urus, and a Mclaren 570s here so that pushed it to 5 stars. Just kidding it would of gotten 5 stars even without the cars.

We made our reservations back in November. Last night out of the blue we receive an email stating they are canceling our reservation so their employees can rest. I am all for letting employees rest, but this should have been thought through a bit more. Getting reservations in NY during the holiday season is very difficult. This was poorly handled by Gramercy.

This review is for the tavern room not main dining room. Excellent experience from start to finish. Service is top notch. Drinks are excellent- I tried a seasonal cocktail, spicy margarita, non alcoholic sparkling pear drink and tea. My review is 4 stars because I thought the food was very good but not excellent. There wasn't anything wrong with it but it just didn't wow me. We had to start flatbread and seafood sampler. Then to follow cheeseburger and brick chicken. For dessert chocolate pudding cake and the sticky toffee pudding. We also opted for a special lobster with caviar tart- this was my favorite thing we ate. Everything was very good but not wowing. Overall I would return and update my review after trying the tasting menu in the main dining room.

Overhyped and overpriced. The food was nice but simply not worth the price (or hype). The service was also very average. I had to remind our server 3 times that it was my wife's birthday. Ultimately the server ruined the surprise by offering us a desert menu (instead of bringing one of the deserts with a candle as a requested).

OK, Gramercy Tavern has been my favorite restaurant in NYC, since the first time I visited the place in 2002. That's 20 YEARS folks. Quite the run for someone who has lived in NYC now for 14 years. It's the food and the impeccable service which continuously keep me coming back combined with the fact that while this establishment is fine dining, they aren't stuffy and keep it authentic and natural. My last visit was 1/1 for a tasting menu with wine pairing in the dining room. Like I said, I have been there many times but apparently never left a review. My favorite dish was the lobster lumache with rock Shrimp, cubanelle peppers, tarragon. Revelatory! My least favorite was the smoked arctic char but to be fair, I don't generally like smoked fish. Also, whoever is doing the chocolate piping in the back for the birthday dessert has some work to do; Happy Birthday was a mess. You can't come at a baker with that, friend. We had two separate waitresses who were both stellar, though I have sadly forgotten their names. That said, every service member who stopped by our table with water or what not was lovely, absolutely embodied the brand of the place; pros. Thank you GT for always never letting me down. Signed - one of your biggest fans.

This has long been on my food bucket list.  I opted to not do the tasting menu and sit at the bar and order ala carte and I was not disappointed! The bartenders gave great recommendations and service was fantastic. I started with the seasonal bread which was delicious! First course was beef tartare with an aioli and it did not disappoint. Easily the best beef tartare I've ever had. Dinner was swordfish, which I was hesitant to order after a previous had experience elsewhere. The bartender recommended it and I gave it a whirl- it was delicious!!! Topped the meal off with a hot chocolate martini and chocolate cake. Will definitely be back to dine at the bar and will definitely give the tasting a try
This might be dramatic but it also happens to be the truth: The chocolate pudding cake dessert here not only was the best thing I've had in my life, it also fixed my relationship with my father.

Visited the dining room last night for our 20th wedding anniversary. It also happens to be the case that we got engaged at Gramercy. We've celebrated many anniversaries here, so it seemed natural to celebrate a milestone anniversary here as well. The details:

When you arrive, there is someone in the vestibule to check your vaccination card and your ID. 

We were immediately seated for our 7 PM reservation in the dining room. We haven't visited since before Covid, but the restaurant generally looks the same. Tables were always pretty social distanced. 

The General Manager, William, came over to offer us his congratulations on our anniversary and a glass of sparkling wine. Super nice guy and gesture. 

Our server, Morgan, knew that it was our anniversary as well as our history with the restaurant. So great when a place takes the time to know its customers with history (Gramercy always does). 

We had the tasting menu, which is currently the only thing they are offering in the dining room. Morgan did tell us that they will hopefully bring back the vegetarian tasting menu in the future. We hope they so as, even for non-vegetarians like us, that tasting menu in the past was amazing. 

Literally every course was perfect. 

The smoked hamachi had a slight citrus acidity, which paired perfectly with the smokiness of the dish. 

The arctic char was super tender and the sauce so good that we used the delicious dinner rolls to sop up every drop. 

The lobster lumache with rock shrimp didn't disappoint; flavors worked perfectly together. 

The woodfired sirloin was soooo good. In particular, the celery root purée was a perfect pair to the rare cooked steak. 

For dessert they brought us 3 to share! The first was the dark chocolate mousse from the tasting menu. It was awesome. Loved the hazelnut shell over the mousse and how it worked so well with the huckleberries. The second was the chocolate pudding cake from the Tavern menu. It was perfection. The sour cream ice cream it came with on the side was out of this world. Finally, as an addition for our anniversary, they brought us a small coconut meringue cake with "happy 20th anniversary" written on the plate in chocolate. My wife loves coconut, so this one was especially great for her. 

If I could pick on anything, it would be that there was no amuse bouche course (I don't ever remember going to Gramercy and there not being one) and there were no petit fours at the end (also a staple in every visit we've had). They also used to give guests a "gift" to bring home for breakfast; usually a freshly baked muffin or jar of granola. We always loved that, so hopefully they bring it back in the future. 

Overall, it was (as usual) a phenomenal experience. We appreciate everything that William, Morgan, Halle, Amy, and the rest of the guest relations group did to make it a truly memorable experience for us!

During my dinner here last night, this place was on point.   Our server was top notch: attentive, personable, but not overbearing.   The food, oh the food.  We started with the beef tartare and the seafood platter.   The tartare was an interesting take on tartare and one that really worked.   Instead of having the meat mixed with Worcester and egg and other seasonings all mixed together, at Gramercy Tavern they served the meat next to a whipped mixture of seasoning and it worked so so well.   The seafood platter was raw oysters, Arctic Char tartare, and a hamachi crudo.   Each component was very balanced and well seasoned.   But enough of all of this raw food.  Let's talked about the cooked dishes.   The monkfish was great, but I want to talk about this "bucket list" burger, as our sever called it.  I really really love when a burger is stripped down and focuses on the main elements.  Bun, patty, cheese, bacon, spread.   That's it.   That's all this burger is.   While I am partial to a smash patty burger, this thicker beefy patty was utter perfection cooked at an exact medium rare.    We also tried the chocolate pudding cake and the sticky toffee pudding.  Both were really good but that sticky toffee pudding was really something special.   Oh, we also had an adornment of cocktails that were expertly crafted.  All in all, this was a meal conceived, prepared, and served perfectly.   I will definitely be back.
Once a great restaurant this place has been shot for years. Food is over salted overpriced and forgettable  skip it

We did the tasting menu with wine pairings. For the price, the food was mediocre. Nothing really stood out as being very good nor was there anything particularly creative on the menu. The service was good as was the wine, but I would not come back for those alone.

Dinner in the dining room with the tasting menu. It was not delicious. I felt like I was eating food because I had to, not because I wanted to. Felt like it was a mishmash of old ingredients they threw together to try to get rid of. I've been to the Tavern, which was at least tasty. Would not go back here again - completely overrated.

The first dish was hamachi marinated in a creamy sauce. It was fine but nothing special, did not have a bright taste, and the pieces of fish felt a little fatty. Not something I'd want to eat again.

The second course was a smoked arctic char that did not taste good. I did not want to eat it. The sauce was weird, the taste and texture were weird, and the cauliflower pieces around it felt like the same cauliflower pieces that had been served alongside the bread. 

The third course was a pasta with lobster and shrimp; this was the best dish, and it was good because the lobster was delicious, but  it wasn't something that I'd want to eat again.  

The fourth course was roasted duck; the flavor was gross, it was served with mushrooms, roasted apples, and this squash/mustard puree. A weird combination that did not work PLUS the duck was chewy and FATTY. 

The fifth course was dark chocolate mousse with hazelnut, icecream, and huckleberries. Again, not delicious. I didn't even bother finishing. The icecream was a weird texture with no flavor. The huckleberries did not taste good. And the chocolate mousse with hazelnut felt like something CVS would sell on valentine's day. 

The only delicious thing I had was the bread and butter. For the price and given the reputation - completely overrated and overpriced. Would not go here again.

Also, I would add that the table next to us looked like they got something different that I did not see on the menu. Didn't realize there were extras/specials.

Finally, the service was kind of annoying. When we wanted more drinks, no one was around. But the waitress talked to us as if she should have pulled up a chair and sat with us.
Had the tasting manu here for a birthday dinner and it was the best meal i've had in NYC! Definitely a splurge but worth it

Excellent ambiance, good table spacing, duck meatloaf was delicious.

Average service, underwhelming portions for appetizer and main course, mediocre value.  

Union Square Cafe is a better choice.

My first time to this place was for the lunch tasting menu in summer 2016 and it was amazing! Fast forward to moving to NYC, this is one of our favorite lunch spots!

The burger with the duck fat fries are amazing and one of the best burgers in the city. It is super juicy and flavorful and cooked perfectly. How could fries fried in duck fat be bad?? Highly recommend the roasted oysters, it is perfection. You can still taste the oysters, it's cooked but slightly raw and it has an amazing haberno butter on it. You will not want to share this!! 

Hot tip, go during restaurant week. They offer a lunch special only on weekdays for $39, you get an appetizer and an entree. Most entrees are $30-$35 so this is a super good deal! I may have done this 3 times in one year and no regrets.

This is a tough one. I would say overall this was more of a 3.5. I went to the Tavern for lunch. I ordered the famous Tavern Burger and was unfortunately quite underwhelmed. It was just so OVERwhelmingly average that I didn't know what to make of it. Same with the famous cookie and milk dessert. The only thing that was a little bit more interesting was the oyster starter. However, even that I felt was a little heavy on the cream. Perhaps there are better a la carte items to try, but I certainly didn't walk away feeling like I had tasted Michelin level food. Maybe the lesson is to go back for the tasting menu? 

I do have to commend the service here. It's a great combination of attentive but not overbearing.

this review is for the tavern!
we had a 9:15 res on a friday night and we're seated immediately when we got there and they offered to take our coats for us! the place was very crowded - not even an empty seat at the bar! such a fun atmosphere. every worker we dealt with was so kind and helpful! our server was named Ian and he was INCREDIBLE! he was helpful when we had questions regarding the menu, described things perfectly, and was very attentive! one of the best servers i've had in a while. 

i got the multipass cocktail and LOVED it. it was smoky, spicy, and fruity all at the same time. such an interesting and amazing flavor! highly recommend. 

before the meal they bring out focaccia bread which was so delicious!
we started with the flat bread - it was leeks, ricotta, and shallot jam. i was hesitant but it ended up being amazing. it's a little on the smaller side and it's pretty thin so it was a perfect appetizer to split. 
i got the brick pressed jerk chicken and ate literally every bite. the chicken was so tender it just melted in your mouth! the flavor was so good and had a slight kick which i loved. it comes with a little bit of rice which was a great touch!
my boyfriend got the burger and he really enjoyed it! it's super cheesy with a piece of bacon on it which he said completed the burger. the meat was tender and cooked perfectly (medium rare). the potato chips on the side were also incredible! so thin and crunchy and salty - so so good!!! 
we finished off with the milk and chocolate chip cookie. i was so full but couldn't resist this! the cookie was warm, thick, and soft and was so good when dipped in the milk!
overall, it definitely lived up to our very high expectations!

Always fun to drop in
Casually at the bar or having dinner or lunch- I get to feel like I'm at a fabulous country Inn- thank you Danny Meier and team- great food abs atmosphere and service

I have come to Gramercy Tavern for 20 years and have always loved it. I came tonight for my wedding anniversary, and I was rushed and treated tonight like it was a factory like Shake Shack from the moment we sat down. When we explained our dietary restrictions, they said fine but then disregarded them during the meal. It was sad as was always one of NYC's finest that we enjoyed on special occasions and no longer feel they care about anything except filling the room during covid.

Great restaurant! The dining room is great but wish it wasn't limited to the tasting menu. The atmosphere in the dining room is great and service is amazing. I have to admit that it did feel a bit weird seeing people wearing polo shirts and jeans even though some would consider it business casual, I think it seems inappropriate based on the vibe.
Good drinks. Had the tavern burger and the monk fish. The burger was very good but the food selection was a bit limited. Would like to try their tasting menu.

What a fantastic evening! 
The amazing thing about this restaurant is its lack of pretentiousness. You arrive here knowing it's rated Michelin and you would expect stuffiness and almost invisible service along with glamorous people and tiny food in big plates.  
Uh uh.  It's all the opposite. Service is friendly, people wear jeans, the food is so freakin good and original (but not weird) and the decor nice but not like most 3 star Michelin in Europe. 
At first I didn't like it because of it, but I now live it for it. I came here half a dozen time and hands down I prefer maialino, but I'll come back for sure. 
The pastry chef is creating amazing desserts.
The tasting menu was delicious, everything was great and I loved the Arctic char and lobster lumache in particular. Excited to return and try the tavern!

Not sure how it took us over 5 years to finally come eat here but it did and despite the delay we really loved it. We celebrated our dear friend's birthday and dined in the dining room. Reservations were surprisingly easy to make which is always such a treat and once we got to the restaurant I understood why -- it is an expansive space! (Also probably helped that it was an early spot in a weekday night)

Sue, the AGM greeted us and brought us to the table. Funny enough we had actually met her a couple weeks prior so it was such a fun little run-in. 

Some of the highlights - The starter fish dishes - outstanding, fresh, crisp, wonderful textures and flavors. There was an amazingly semi-salty, umami packed Arctic char first bite sitting on cool lettuce as the opener of our meal. I loved the opener. Then we transitioned into a diced bowl of yellowtail, asian pear and sesame. The soft, semi-buttery flavor of the fish and the hints if richness of the sesame paired so nicely with the refreshing bites of the asian pear. I really loved this too. 

The majority consensus was that the lobster pasta dish was the star of the night. My husband and our friend were shamelessly licking their bowls to savor the flavors once they had finished their dish. Generous portions of lobster, chewy perfectly al dente pieces of pasta bathed in some sort of creamy magic sauce that i can best describes as mouthwateringly delicious. 

The duck was also perfect. My husband and I are not huge fans of duck. We have tried it several times in various preparations and it has always been a meh in our books but the duck the chef prepared that night was honestly the best duck we ever had. The fat was nicely rendered and the meat was soft and not gamey. We were a little weirded out that we were enjoying it. Enjoyed the apples and the radicchio - the sweet and the bitter got along so well with the duck. 

Coming into the dinner, my sweet tooth husband was disappointed that mouse was listed dessert. He was expecting a sad bowl of chocolate mousse but was mind-blowingly surprised by a giant ball of a chocolate ball resembling a ferrero rochet and could not be more thrilled once he dug in. We agreed that the dessert was so massive and decadent that we renamed the dish Ferrari Rochet which may not make sense to you but it hilariously did to us. 

Oh! The wine! The wine was awesome! The sommelier was down to earth and so helpful. We enjoyed a couple light french reds that night, both perfect and loved his expertise. 

We had such a wonderful celebration dinner and are curious to visit the tavern next.

Gramercy Tavern never disappoints. I have been going there since the month it opened way back when and each time I go I am amazed at how well run this place is. The food is always excellent and varied. The seasonal cocktails are imaginative altho I do wish they would repeat some favorites of mine like the Ginger Tonic. And the service is impeccable. The decor in the Tavern is timeless and the seasonal branch and flower arrangements are beautiful.

We came on a Saturday night for dinner. Reservations were fairly difficult to get; we were refreshing the reservations page minutes before the reservations for our desired day became available, and in less than a minute almost all the time slots were taken. The tavern part of the restaurant is more laid back with an a la carte menu similar to what you'd see in any American style restaurant in Manhattan. The quality of the ingredients was definitely there, but price-wise I'd say it's a little overpriced for what it is; $40 for a hamburger after tax is pretty steep even for New York. Tables were pretty squished together as well. The entire night we were somewhat forced to listen in to a conversation between two men in the finance industry about their investment strategies...not exactly what we wanted for a weekend dinner. Overall though the service was good and food/drinks were good. Next time I think I'd prefer the tasting menu to get the best perspective of bang-for-buck at gramercy.
Service was EXCELLENT! Food was good but could've been better. Bread, chocolate cake, and coffee were basic. The lobster dish and vegetables of the day were very good.

Always a favorite, whether the tavern or the dining room. The food is excellent, the atmosphere, while busy, is never too claustrophobic. The cocktails and service are a dream. We've even dropped by for lunch (on a weekday) with a toddler in the dining room, and the staff could not have been nicer - though I would not recommend trying this during peak hours, just because of how crowded it can get and how hungry little ones are! That said, I love how accommodating they are and the consistency of excellence - we've never been disappointed by a meal here!

Finally snagged a reservation for the Tavern.  Beautiful room, excellent people watching, stellar service.  Biscuits and soft salted butter were dreamy. 
 We shared a bottle of wine, seafood platter for two and the duck meatloaf.  The food is faultless, if not a little soulless. I would never say, "We must go to Gramercy Tavern - I am craving the duck meatloaf."  But I have found that to be the case at all of Danny Meyer's restaurants (except Shake Shake, ironically - the ShackBurger is definitely soulful).  A great restaurant for when you need to impress someone.

My wife and I dined at Gramnercy Tavern on Saturday, Feb. 26.  We are from DC and we go to NYC several times a year for fun.  We always try new (to us) restaurants mixed with our consistent favorites.  This trip we went to Cosme (new to us, uneven, a shadow of its Mexico City parent restaurant, but good) and Grammercy Tavern.  We had been to GT before.  The food is consistently good.  The atmosphere is great. The service is impeccable.  This time a single dish pushed the meal into the realm of the extraordinary.  
We started with the complimentary focaccia.  Delicious.  Not exceptional but really good.  My wife got the burger.  Again, really good.  It is no Minetta Tavern Black Label burger, but nothing is.  The GT offfering is very good.  And I got the grilled bass.  Another good but not necessarily divinely inspired dish.  All solid.  A good meal.  
But then it came time for dessert.  My wife asked our server about two options:  the purple sweet potato pie and something else.  Our server (unfortunately I can't remember her name--damn wine and age!) told us that the pie was her recipe.
