She explained that they had held a contest among the staff to submit the best dessert and hers won.  She went on to explain that she is from Trinidad and Tobago and the original recipe was her grandmother's.  She also explained that the potatoes come from the local Union Square Farmers Market.  Needless to say we got the pie.
Am I ever glad we did!  It was one of the best dishes (not just desserts) I have ever had.  I told my wife that it tasted like everything you want pumpkin pie to be.  My wife said it tasted like Christmas.  We were both right.  The crust tasted like the best Speculaas cookie you can imagine.  And the potato filling was otherworldly good.  It was somehow dense and light at the same time.  It bordered on savory but packed enough sweetness and spice to let you know it was dessert.  It was perfect--and I don't use that word lightly.
Go to Gramnercy Tavern for the good food, great vibes and fantastic service.  Be sure to stay for dessert and get the Purple Sweet Potato Pie.  Thank me later--or order a second slice to go.  I wish I had.

I was really excited to come here but the experience was lackluster. So many good reviews... we walked out feeling confused? What did we miss? The ambiance, food, entire experience was average at best. For the prices here, we expected to be wowed. I had the ravioli starter (had maybe 8 small raviolis for $30) and then the burger. Both were okay. If they had tasted incredible, that'd be one thing. But for the price, I would have rather gone to one of the many high end restaurants in NYC which go above and beyond. This city is full of impeccable restaurants, this just did not match up.
Dumb.. just dumb!  Best meal I've ever had and a memorable experience!!  Well done guys!!!

This is a one of a kind place. Can't say enough good things about it! Everything is delicious and they easily accommodated gluten free options for me. This is going to be our special dinner we do every year (would love to do it more often but we don't live in NYC and the dinner menu with wine tasting is definitely pricey). Thanks for an unforgettable dining experience!

Very well deserved with all the awards and Michelin star! Made a quite last minute reservation on 12/31 at 5pm, came right on time, checked in my coat, was asked about diet restrictions etc, the whole process everyone I encountered was super polite, kind and professional. I love the decorations of the restaurant, lots of flower elements, with red and green theme which felt super festive yet high class. With low volume music playing, the tables are not set far apart so you could hear people talking but not loud, very suitable place for special occasion or romantic dates.

It was New Years Eve and there's a special menu for that, and went with the wine pairing as well.

Starter - Lobster Tartlette: A
Very nice presentation, looked exactly like an egg tart full of lobster on it, it smelled like scallion and a hint of black truffle. The flavor though was entirely different, it was a mouth full of well-prepared lobster meat, and the tart was very fluffy.

First course - Marinated Scallops: A+
With caviar, sesame and some scallion on top, the visual was not much but wow it tasted very good. The scallop was tasty with hint of sea water saline flavor, with some apple crumbs offering nice balance. One of the best seafood appetizer dish I have ever had.

1st wine pairing - Loire Valley Muscadet, not much on the nose as expected, the saline flavor went extremely well with the scallop.

Second course - Poached Lobster: A+
Again very nicely decorated dish, got some citrus and quinoa aroma along with some pepper spice. There were 3 pieces of lobster and tasted delicious, the juice from the lobster combined very nicely with the quinoa, very delicate. There was some grapefruit added too and the bitterness of it went well with the slightly sour/salty lobster meat. The spiced carrot was well made.

2nd wine pairing - White Blend with Riesling/SB/Pinot Grigio, smelled like white and purple flowers and green fruit, a bit similar to an unoaked Chardonnay, yet with a bit nut and oak on the finish. But I actually would have preferred something with a bit more sugar to go with the lobster dish because the sauce got a tad of spiciness to it.

Third course - Winter Squash Tagliatelle: A+
The Tagliatelle was sooooooo good! Very soft and spongy, very flavorful with sauce from carrot, cheese and truffle. 

3rd wine pairing - Rossese, I was given the choice between a red Rossese or a white and picked red because I have never tried that grape, it tasted a bit like strawberry/banana/bubble gum and reminded me of Gamay. And I was provided a bit of the white too, very generous of them!

Fourth course - Wood Fired Sirloin and Braised Shoulder: A
It got a heavy wood-grilled aroma and some cauliflower notes. I requested medium rare but it came slightly towards to medium side. The texture of both pieces of meat were tender and soft. I also really liked the mushroom and crispy potato came with it. Nothing too surprising about this dish, met the standard of meat dish from a high end restaurant.

4th wine pairing - 2016 Merlot and Cab Franc, aroma of black fruits and some green pepper notes from cab franc, although it would have been better if there was more decanting time to allow it opening it up.

Fifth course - Dark Chocolate Mousse: A
I usually don't like chocolate flavored dessert but this one tasted on the very bitter side (which I love) and along with the cherries and hazelnuts, the overall combination was very delicious.

5th wine pairing - Solero from Southern Australia, I love fortified wine, and it was nicely paired with the cherry-filled dessert dish.

Overall, very delicious food, all the waiters/waitresses that served the table were very nice, explained the dishes and wine in detail, and it was an excellent meal to conclude the year of 2021. I would not hesitate to recommend this place to any of my friends and I can't wait to go back again to try their regular/seasonal menu too!
Nice decor. The table was a little small and tight but the service was very good. The food is really nice.

Highly recommend this gem while in NYC!! The decor and food spoke elegance. This restaurant truly accommodated my dairy free and nut free allergies.

We ordered the flatbread and beef tartare for appetizers. The beef tartare was delightful to munch on. Very juicy and flavorful. The combination of the salt and meat was divine! For the complimentary bread, I asked for 2 more dishes of my bread. It was dairy free and nut free. The moist texture of the breading was exquisite and I craved for more!

For the entrees, we ordered the grilled black bass, brick pressed jerk chicken, the tavern burger, and the braised beef stew. The braised beef was so tender that it melted on my tongue and it was so easy to cut!! The potatoes and parsnips were sweet too. My family had no complaints on the other dishes as well.

I usually can't eat any desserts due to my dairy and nut allergies, but the chef made me a selection of sorbets. The sorbet was delicious and the strawberries were very savory. If you have any food restrictions, this restaurant will surely cater to you and make you feel like a queen! The wait staff was excellent too.

Overall, my experience at this Michelin star restaurant was amazing and I would definitely come back for that beef brisket stew!!
Really enjoyed the place. It was packed with Ben on Sunday night. Cocktails were great. I highly recommend the Multipass cocktail.

One of my favorite restaurants in NYC and a true classic. Beautiful New York grandeur but relaxed enough to enjoy. My favorite experience is actually sitting at the bar on the tavern side for a weekend lunch. But you can't really go wrong here.
Great food nice ambiance; went for brunch; service was also good; the golden beet salad and the brick pressed jerk chicken were both very good

Host didn't feel welcoming maybe because of our skin normally we let theat slide but when she walked us to our table not a word was said. Didn't feel warm.

Waiter showed us the pairing menu on the bottom "Wine pairing" we asked what's the difference of pairing and reserve paring. He stated he will get the Master's of wine. He came to our table and showed us a piece of card board that stated what the wine list on reserve pairing. Left it on the table and walked away. This is what you called RUDE behavoir. We both felt insulted, no explaination, we just have to compare what the wines are. Excused me don't go to work with this attitude, or you can't handle seeing an Asian couple. California still rocks!!

Even worst comes to our table describing the wine without enthusiasm. By the 2nd to the end OMG FREAKEN "A" no smile, no descriptive expect what the wine is and walked away. We looked at each other and both said WTF is this guys problem.

This time we are furious! Really sad part the rest of the crew are kind, helpful and very positive attitude.
With his attitude, feels as if he hated Asian "Races B". Not happy with your job then change. From lady Host to this guy. Such disappointed with note. 
And food is really good.  If I can rate this 1.5 so sad nothing else. After all we paid $$$$ and get treated this way. I wasn't going to yelp, although just so disgusted such behavoir!
Delicious meal with a great bottomless brunch deal! Waitstaff was attentive despite a packed house.

Gramercy Tavern is a true gem in NYC. When we knew we were finally going to be able to go to New York for a post poned birthday celebration from last year, I made a reservation for this Michelin starred restaurant. Gramercy Tavern is divided into two areas for dining: The Tavern and the dining room. As you may imagine, The Tavern is a little less stuffy, but it's still refined. You won't find flip flopped /tank top wearing people sauntering in. Initially I had a reservation for 530p on RESY and was on a waitlist to dine at 700p. The host on the phone was very accommodating in that. We arrived about 10 minutes early for our reservation. Gramercy Tavern hosts make sure that you are taken care of, but not before checking your vaccination status alongside your ID. After that, your coat is checked and you are offered a water while you wait for your table. We were reserved in the Tavern , as I didn't want to have price fixed menu that I had seen as the only thing available in the dining room. Our host told us at 715p that the occupants at our table had not left and we could dine in the dining room on the ala carte menu, as well, if we wanted. We wanted to wait. At 745p we were finally seated. Yes, it was a bit annoying for such a stuffy restaurant as we could see empty tables that never had occupants at them, BUT we also didn't know if this had to do with a Covid rule or something, despite the fact that we are in March 2022. The hostess bought us our first round of drinks and that was kind of her, although she could have saved the quip about it being my husband's birthday as she checked his ID.. (it was last SEPT that I booked this NYC getaway for us as his Broadway bday gift and due to the pandemic it postponed repeatedly) ..so yes, it actually WAS a birthday celebration. Our waiter was amazing. He apologized for the delay in seating profusely. He brought me another champagne and who could be angry when in a Michelin starred restaurant in NYC? The ambience here is beyond charming; it's pretty and rustic but also very up tick. My husband ordered the best burger he's tasted and at $32 it better be :) I had the Duck Meatloaf and again it was amazing!  Our server never missed a beat despite our rough 45 minute late start to the night. The menu here is great.. IF you're wondering how and why in a Michelin starred place my husband would order a burger.. well,, because, why would you not try a Michelin starred burger and duck fat fries!? I'll be the one to go out and order a Duck Meatloaf because well, IT"s different! The waiter brought my husband a Vanilla Coconut Cupcake and candle (even tho we told him of the delayed bday trip!) and it was one of those cup cakes you don't forget. We tried to order something more to split but I have a myriad of allergies to nuts and apparently pea and nut flours are used in most of the desserts. That is perfectly okay for me .. maybe not for someone else wanting that full on experience! BUT for us this was amazing ! If you get the chance, make the reservation and get to Gramercy ... it's a legend in New York City and there's a reason why .. It's nearly perfect !
Excellent service.  Had Chris as our main waiter assisted by Jason.  We had the duck tasting menu with wine pairings.  Interesting and well prepared.

Make reservations days in advance otherwise it'll be a wait to get a table at this fancy place. The inside was beautiful, walls filled with art. The staff was inviting and efficient in their pace of service. I tried a torpedo cocktail and had the duck meatloaf togo. I was worried, strictly by the appearance of my entree, that it wouldn't be as tasty as I surprisingly found it to be. The meatloaf was extremely savory and not gamey at all, you wouldn't know it was duck unless someone told you. The flavors resembled a salisbury steak, oddly, which I truly enjoyed. Especially the grilled char marks, they brought everything together. Id without a doubt get this dish again which means i'd visit Gramercy Tavern again.

I love this restaurant - the seasonal menu makes it so you can go back multiple times and have a new and fantastic experience every time. It's one of my favorite tasting menus in the city - it's not exorbitantly priced, but the food and service are great.

5/5 stars on the ambiance of this restaurant- most beautifully decorated restaurant I've ever seen!!!! Gorgeous artwork, rustic decor, and real flowers are scattered throughout, and there is an open kitchen concept (where you can see all the food being made right in front of you).

I had a lunch reservation, so the tasting menu was not an option; I ordered the Tavern burger after seeing that was a fan favorite. The burger came with bacon and a smoked onion aioli, and duck fat potato chips. It was cooked to a perfect medium rare (as requested), was very juicy, and the flavors went together well. I also tried the roasted oysters and the grilled black bass, both of which were very fresh. Service here was impeccable, our waiter was both friendly and welcoming. Couldn't get over the physical beauty of the restaurant! However, would say I was more impressed with that than the actual food.

Wish I had the names of all the beautiful and tasty dishes we were served but we went in November and I'm posting the review late :( 
The service was amazing, the food was incredible and there is not a single thing I can complain about this place. The drinks, food and service were great, we spent like 3-4 hrs here nobody rushed us out and the waiter was really nice

Our most expensive meal in NYC so far, and I'm not impressed at all. First off, aside from the busser who did an amazing job of always keeping our water glasses full (and they were emptied a lot), it was by far the worst service we've had at a Michelin starred restaurant. Maybe it's because we had kids with us? It took forever for our waiter to take our order. When he brought over the drinks menu, we told him we didn't need it but were ready to order. He walked away with the drinks menu, but then didn't take our order. We waited some more. Then, it was an even longer wait for every single one of our courses. My husband thought our waiter might've forgotten to put our order into the system? Who knows, but there was a lot of waiting.

Then, the food. I didn't love their potato soup. The soup was light, a bit tangy, and reminded me of Thai flavors (maybe it was the coconut?). Not the thick and creamy potato soup I was expecting. Liked their beef tartare though. Wish it was served with another slice or two of toasted bread. I had their grilled black bass for my main. Nothing memorable. My favorite dish of the night was actually their chocolate pudding cake with all of its contrasting flavors, textures, and temperatures. Loved the warm chocolate that oozed out of the slightly baked cake paired with the cool coconut ice cream and crispy pecan pieces.
One of the best dinner tasting menu I ever had, amazing service, great choices of wine/ drinks. We really enjoy our food, friendly staff and knowledgeable. We will see you soon!!

One of my favorite restaurants in NYC and a true classic. Beautiful New York grandeur but relaxed enough to enjoy. My favorite experience is actually sitting at the bar on the tavern side for a weekend lunch. My all time favorite is their cassoulet.. exquisite..  This place is truly one of a kind!

First off this place is beautifully decorated, the ambiance is amazing. You've got art and florals all over giving it such a nice cozy feel. Service was amazing and attentive from the beginning to the end. From the host to the waiter/waitress. We started off with a few apps. The roasted oysters were delicious. I wasn't sure how I would feel about warm oysters but they were surprisingly pleasant the sauce on top gave it a nice herbal, buttery and slight acidic taste. I would not share this plate, get one for yourself because you will not want to share either ! The shrimp brioche was fantastic. It was nice and crunchy on the outside and the savory rich flavor of the shrimp was all the way there ! The flatbread was also good I loved the cheese corn mix and topping gave it a nice kick. The beef tartare was deliciously seasoned, so rich and the hummus paired perfectly with it. I had the swordfish with lentils. It was a very elegant and simple dish. The lemon and herb flavors were very light and nice the lentils cooked perfectly. Others had the steak and they seemed pleased with it. Now for my most memorable portion THE DESSERTS are amazing. I dined here maybe two months back and I can still remember the tastes and fell of them in my mouth ! The beignets so fresh and warm with the delicious tartness from the purée underneath. The apple sundae oh lord where do I begin. So many different layers unraveling it tasted so fresh and the apple crisp was the perfect crunch to it! The cookies omg who would have thought a simple cookie could be so amazing !!!! The crispy outside with the moist inside and hot melted chocolate with the cutest little jar of milk was heaven. My favorite dessert (however I don't remember the name) but I remember it had a taffy sauce with a chocolate cake and the ice cream !!!! That sauce really brought the two components together so well I cannot wait to go back for the oysters, the shrimp brioche and the taffy sauced dessert !!! On another note the service was outstanding. Our waitress was knowledgeable on the menu drinks were served then appetizers were brought out together. They clear the entire table together and had everyone's main come out together. Very attentive and exceptional!
If you were looking to impress someone over dinner this would be the place to go !
The service was really phenomenal and all of the food was exquisite, and displayed such a wide variety of flavors.

Amazinggg tasting menu, great service, left feeling more than full but still wanting more. 

Those biscuits are to die for (am I being sarcastic? Maybe...but man were they good). Topped with a little bit of salt, they are heavenly with butter. When you cut it open you see steam coming out so yes it was "straight out of the oven".

The tasting menu was designed very well with all the flavors coming through perfectly, cooked perfectly and paired well. Service was 10/10. The pasta was perfectly cooked, best pasta I've had in over a year. The lobster and fish was sous vided and the rice on the bottom was a nice touch. The scallops were sweet, and with the touch of celery it was a perfect crunch/bite. 

Dessert was a good end to the meal, not overly sweet but just enough to leave you biting your lip. 

Highly recommend! Reserve in advance!!

We had a party of 4.  Ate outdoors on Monday, May 9th.  Very comfortable. 
Food and drinks were delicious.  Serving staff is professional.  We were even greeted by the Chefs.  Gramercy Tavern is an excellent restaurant.
The food was very good. Creative, well executed. Service was attentive and friendly. The reserve wine pairing was the best I have ever had. Incredible and elevated the meal.

I love this place! Gramercy Tavern is committed to making every diner comfortable - the service was friendly, approachable and helpful (providing recommendations, suggesting wine pairings).

My friend and I were there for lunch - and the ambience and sound levels were great.

The house focaccia was a pleasant surprise, but nothing spectacular. However, the campellini (braised lamb) and brick pressed chicken were delicious! While the campellini was slightly salty, the lamb and cream pairing made it a hearty, but not heavy meal. The brick pressed chicken was cooked just right - very juicy and flavorful! 

We had the lemon meringue pie for dessert, and the lemon filling was absolutely delightful - feather light on the tongue with a refreshing tang. Thank you!

Yes it's pricey, but yes it's worth it!!!! We went for lunch and the interior is gorgeous. They have the perfect menu of items that are familiar enough that you can know what you're getting and that it's excellent, but unique enough to be worth the trip. Their table bread was different and delicious, we would up order ANOTHER round of their oyster sampler because it was just so damn good. The cocktails are delicious. the meatloaf was amazing. Everything. So. Good. Well worth the trip.

Tasting menu dinner review:

Came for the tasting menu for a weekend dinner as a birthday dinner. The restaurant front is deceiving because the back rooms are huge! There's two separate dining areas and we were seated in the back room. The tasting menu is 5 courses, seasonal dishes that change periodically.

The food here is great, the bread was phenomenal and drinks were creative yet strong. Definitely an expensive culinary experience (for 2 people cost all in about $500) but the chefs here executed that quite well.

Drinks:
We started with drinks, which were super interesting and definitely strong. I really liked the multipass. Pomegranate, tangy without it being too sweet (not such a sweet-tooth here).

The food:
We started the meal with a bread service - this was THE BEST BREAD I HAVE EVER HAD. The bread was flaky on the outside and on the inside but also had these natural layers and when you bite into it, you get a slightly chewy and soft texture, like biting into a pillow. The butter was also AMAZING. We liked the bread so much we got refills 3 times - no joke, amazing bread.

Everything was delicious and food came at a good pace. The two highlights of the meal for me: smoked arctic char and the sirloin. The smoked arctic char must've been cooked sous vide because the meat was a pearly translucent color but was fully cooked and very soft to cut into. The sirloin was phenomenal - so soft and flavorful, amazing color marbling pink-ness. 

For dessert, since it was a birthday dinner, they gave us an extra birthday cake - which was a coconut layer cake with a soft meringue texture outside. There was a candle on it too! It was a nice surprise for us. Then, we got the actual desserts of the tasting menu too - the chocolate mousse was really good but to me it was a little bit on the sweet side. The birthday cake though was great.

Summary:
Overall, we had a really good experience here and the price tag will definitely cost you a pretty penny but the courses are large portions and of high caliber. Very well done to the chef here. 

The pro-tip I have is that we didn't notice you can ask for accommodations and since we both aren't huge fans of sweet chocolate desserts if we re-do the tasting menu experience we would request for lighter desserts.

One slight suggestion to make the experience even better is that I wish we had gotten more verbal explanation on how the dishes were prepared / what we were eating but the service was attentive as is.

Came back to Gramercy Tavern for the dinner tasting menu! Always a solid experience; the food was as delectable as ever. However, I will say that my second time here, my experience was not quite as amazing as the first time around. While the service was of course Michelin-star worthy, it wasn't what I remembered it to be the last time I was here for brunch. Not as much thought was made in explaining each course, for example. The service was also not quite as enthusiastic or attentive as last time - the staff almost forgot to bring us our boxed leftovers after we signed our checks and were getting ready to leave. Not a big deal overall, but just a small thing I noticed in contrast to my prior experience here. 

I also noticed they got rid of their brunch tasting menu (which included both a regular and a vegetarian version for $10 less)! Kind of sad, as that menu was a more affordable way of sampling Gramercy Tavern without committing to the dinner prices. I was also caught by surprise when it came time to pay for the bill, and I discovered that gratuity is no longer included; however, the prices are around the same (inflation included).

Came with a friend from Seattle wanting her to experience NYC and picked GT as I expected us to be treated to a wonderful meal with all the trimmings and wasn't at all disappointed! Every course, food and wine pairing, was presented to us with a description of each. Great service, food and wine-- couldn't have been happier!!

Just happened to be in the neighborhood and came across the Gramercy Tavern, I have always wanted to try it and I am so glad I did. I sat at the bar on a Monday and it was relatively quiet which was nice. The bartender Jerry was very nice and a pleasure to talk with.  I had the mixed green salad with the house dressing and it was delightful. The focaccia which was brought out was so flavorful it reminded me of a focaccia I once had in Cinque Terra, it was almost that good .  I then had the duck meatloaf and it was amazing,  the sauce had a perfect amount of flavor to accompany the meatloaf which had so much flavor it was making me smile while I ate it! 

If you're a duck fan please try it!

Had their famous burger along with roasted oyster. 
N very much thankful to their additional birthday cake.

OMG we stopped in for lunch. Had the lamb, burger, chicken and the mushroom quiche. So good we made them all into share dishes! Focaccia was warm and delicious. Like biting into a piece of yummy! It dipped really well into the lamb sauce. Love it and will fav this place.

Haven't been here since 2019. Been here twice before and loved the experience both times. Maybe inflation, but things changed and I am not sure if it's worth the price :(
The food was overall great, we had a wine pairing which was excellent. The bread is still amazing. My favorite was asparagus risotto. There are lots of servers to make sure everyone on the table gets the dish at the same time which is nice.
However - the menu had no options to choose from, just one single tasting menu for all courses for all patrons including dessert. Even for the meat dish we were not asked how it should be cooked and it came out medium which was not what we prefer so I didnt finish it. And they charge that amount.. probably for the servers but not being given any choices for that price was a bit disappointing. I dont think I has that impression last time I was here (but maybe my memory is a blur). I'll come back if they provide at least meat cooking preferences

Went for lunch, it was fine - but $35 for a burger is ridiculous, absolutely not worth it. Also, while eating at the bar, I noticed there were no floor mats behind the bar for the BTs; they work on a stone floor. I asked if GT supplied mats, and they do not. I complained to the general manager: you all should know better. Working on a stone floor all day, every day does a number on feet, legs, knees, and back. You are charging $35 for a hamburger - I'm sure you can splurge on floor mats for your staff.

My friends and I have been looking forward to our dinner here since we made the reservation. Everything on the 5 course tasting menu was delicious beyond words - the flavor combinations, the diversity of each course, and the servers were so attentive and asked a bunch of questions to make sure each course would come out to our liking. The complimentary bread was also fantastic and I agreed to a second serving of them so fast even as we were getting full from the rest of the meal. It's so hard to pick a favorite but it might be the asparagus risotto (and this is coming from someone who doesn't even really like asparagus usually!). The strawberries and cream was also so good I cleaned my plate entirely even though I was stuffed at that point. The different flavors and the difference of texture brought from the ice and the almost crouton-like cake crumble was really the icing on the cake. We'd also mentioned it was our friend's birthday a day ago at the start of the meal and had forgotten that we had until they brought out a little coconut cake at the end that was equally as lovely as the rest of the meal. Kept thinking through the meal how much I'd want to come back and maybe take my parents out for a nice meal here :)

Review for The Tavern.

I was really excited to try Gramercy Tavern. I feel sad for my experience there tonight. Ordered chicken liver mousse, burger, duck meatloaf, lemon meringue pie, and chocolate pudding. 

The meatloaf was super bland and dry. I think the best part of the dish were the peas. I just took one bite of the meatloaf and left the rest. Told the person who took it away that I didn't like it, and they just ignored the comment.

The burger was so salty and I love salt. Wasn't sure if it was the cheese or the bacon. One thing I was looking forward to most. Really disappointed here. 

Another thing, I took a sip of my water glass and immediate spit it back out. Ended up being sparkling water instead. I was so thrown off. 

I will say the When Love Begins cocktail was really good! 

My experience tonight was subpar. I really wanted to love it to go back to try the dining room's tasting menu. I do like the vibes and the decor. Wish the food met expectations to the 4.5 average rating.

Always wonderful! We went for brunch recently after not going for the last few years. Thankfully, they have been able to maintain excellent service & food and the prices have not gone through the roof! The food was excellent as was the service. Only one gripe- my wife order the potato soup which she loved except for the drizzle of Chile oil which was not described on the menu. Otherwise, a perfect experience!!

The food and the service are impeccable in the tavern who's their way of saying, eat at the bar. 

The main dining room is where they serve the tasting menu.

There is a disconnect between thee quality and price of the menu and service and the whole ambiance of the bar. Your reservation is merely a guesstimate of when a table may become available and there is often a long wait, although the white people seem to live along at a brisker pace.
The room is entirely too loud and crowded for it to be a genuine dining experience. The food is fantastic but it takes a long time to arrive, and the portions are small so  it a place to go when hungry.
I guess it's best suited for a leisurely lunch on an off day when it's not crowded

This is one of our favorite restaurants in NYC. We go here almost every single time we are in town. 

I came to town for a friend's wedding but because of circumstances I wasn't able to make a reservation ahead of time. I got there at 11:30 when they opened and there was plenty of bar and outside walk in seating even though it was a gorgeous day. 

I really wanted the beef tartare and the cheeseburger which are two of my favorites here but decided to branch out. The duck liver mousse was amazing. Incredible flavor and combination of flavors. I also had the beef stew because I'm a down home country guy and had to try it and it was good but not great. I am really partial to my wife's beef stew so this wasn't really fair. The strawberry cheesecake for dessert was outstanding! Overall I still give Gramercy 5 stars despite the beef stew because it is almost always epic! Try the beef tartare and burger when you are in. Best of both you've ever had!

Returning to NYC after several years' break, came here on the spur of the moment on the Sat. before Father's Day with my two teen boys. Took a short walk from the hotel, called out to Ryan, the bar mgr., for three to eat at the bar. 20 minutes later, we are seated. We are treated well and served first-rate fare for a truly memorable, special meal. Even teens know when a burger, for example, is elevated to greatness. The starters - oysters, duck liver mousse - are phenonmenal. Interesting people at the bar, attentive service, a perfect experience for visitors to NY. The tab was pretty serious, true, but worth every penny. Eat here.

Grammercy has been our go-to for special occasions for many years now. Last night was a special milestone birthday.  The meal and service as always were exquisite.  We had the tasting menu with reserve wine pairings. The duck breast course along with the scallop dish were the best we have ever had. Completely beyond compare.

Unfortunately, towards the end of our meal a group of three guys who were sauced to the gills and at the point of incoherence were sat immediately next to us. They began making comments about being seated next to the couple having "romantic dinner" and began to drunkenly pull on the curtains separating our tables in an attempt to close them.  Eventually, they were successful and carried on but left what was a beautiful evening soured for us.

Hopefully this won't be an issue in the future and there could be some discretion around the seating location of people who are clearly over-served.

I loved the burger and chips with dip here. So good. I also liked the bread. I did not love the blood orange flan with popcorn. The chocolate pudding cake was ok but not amazing. Really nice decor, friendly service. I would definitely return.

Very disappointed. We had the tasting menu in the dining room. Three of us had it as is and one had vegetarian. At 165 pp food should have been more inventive and exciting. It was ... good. The vegetarian version was basically what the rest of the table had but they left off the animal protein, except for a strange course of grains, mushrooms and strawberries. It went uneaten. I don't usually write reviews but there are better places to break the bank in nyc. :(

I was really excited to try the Gramercy Tavern. Yes, the Michelin Starred Burger is as good as they say. The duck fat fries it comes with are the perfect compliment. The service is exactly as you would expect in an elevated dining experience. I can't wait to come back and try more of the menu.

Two special days in NYC and decided to try Gramercy Tavern for the first time. After all the hype about what a wonderful restaurant this is, we were very disappointed. It was a very boring and unimaginative tasting menu with flavors that definitely did not sing nor did they even hum. Everything from the drinks, to 5 course menu, to dessert where so very meh. Not worth the money or time spent. Makes me question most of these recent reviews!?!
One of the finest restaurants in NYC.  Never fades.

Tried the tasting menu with the wine pairings and it was divine! At first was a little disappointed that it was steak and not duck as it had said on the website, but the steak was done so well i can't really complain
Great food and good vibe.  The pork chop special I had was fantastic.   I've dined there with my wife and then did a group business dinner about a month later. I recommend.
Really had no weakness. Rounding up from 4.5 star rating. Duck meatloaf was memorable.

Highly recommended for discerning taste. The bar keep is well knowledgeable and to put it bluntly "OCD". They know what they are doing down to the details. Friendly atmosphere and nice decor. An absolute must for top shelf enthusiasts.
Had a lovely lunch. Arctic char was wonderfully done with fresh vegetable (cherry tomatoes were sweet and tasty) and whole grain. Staff was very attentive.

Yesterday evening my husband and I had dinner at the Tavern. The location is very cute, a bit loudly of course. I already knew what I wanted to eat, so we ordered the burger. Because I'm pregnant I asked it well done and it was amazing. Usually when it's well done, the meat could be dry but it was the opposite. It was very tender and juicy. I liked also the cheese and I didn't have the bacon because I don't eat pork. The only think was that it was salty (I don't know if it was the type of cheese or they use extra salt). Overall, the burger was delicious. I expected more from the chips. For me was just normal, while my husband found them super good. 
The burger is pricey (35$), but it was very good. We saw couple that split it, so you can do the same if you want just have few bites. 
Before your food they serve you a sort of focaccia that was a good appetizer. We waited a lot for our burger, but the restaurant was very packed.
Cutest interior and outdoor seating! Loved the pork shoulder and peach dish for lunch. Also their complimentary focaccia is amazing!

really good food and appropriate portion sizes. it did seem to move fairly quickly - once we sat down dinner just started rolling through literally until the check came. also it was incredibly loud but that is what happens when there are a lot of people talking loudly over each other all at once so kind of expected.

This place is a gem! I can't believe I hadn't gone before trying it. It was delicious and such a great place to meet up with a friend. We sat and ate at the bar but the tables look quaint and charming. The vibe is so pleasant.
I only had oysters and a burger at the bar with some cocktails and they were amazing. The burger was perfectly cooked! Loved the vibe there too.
A must for foodies looking for classic restaurants while in NYC. The food was excellent as was the service . A great place to have a meal that's very nice but not stuffy!

Chris Henderson, Miguel, and the beverage director absolutely made our night! Incredibly attentive and kind, made our friend reunion something so special! 
Cannot praise them all enough!

We sat in the Tavern. Best birthday ever. Made us feel welcome, excellent burger, great menu recs for desert. $70 per head including one cocktail, burger, and dessert. Sit at the bar for date night. Just a fantastic experience all around. We came here for the best burger in NY and were happily fulfilled.

It had been a hot minute since I had a meal in the Tavern. The last few visits were with guests and we splurged for the dining room. This time around I had a plan. Get there early (I'm old and go to sleep early now so it's easy), cozy up to the bar and go big with the Tavern menu. My hope was their ability to put together a solid dining room menu would translate to a simpler more pared down menu in the Tavern. It was a really good decision. Instead of getting mains we stuck to cocktails and did an appetizers flight.  It was hot out and we didn't want to be weighed down by a heavy meal. We got oysters, salad, corn cake bread, steak tartare, and dessert (+port).  For our appetite level, the choices we made were absolutely perfect to split. The oysters and cocktails were commendable. The ambiance there is world class and the service attentive but not obnoxious.Everything else had incredible polish and freshness (stone fruit/tomato salad) and chocolate cake. There's a reason why this place is one of my favorite restaurants in NYC and they demonstrate it every single time I come here without fail. It's rather remarkable in that way. Special shout out to the tavern burger I didn't get. My neighbor at the bar ordered it and it looks absolutely awesome. I will be ordering that next time I eat at the Tavern.

Great food, art work and environment. It was an interesting summer menu for a Saturday lunch. Expected more light fare and salad options. Ordered a strange combo but it worked!!! Had the oysters (delicious)! Then a burger which was highly recommended. My daughter had the artic char. Overall , really, really great.

This review is loooong overdue. Been a staple for me when I lived in NY & still visit often when in the area. Vibe is always great, service on point & just a relaxing place to catch up with old friends now. Oh yah, food is great too!

This is a very difficult one for me. There are so many things to love about Gramercy Tavern, and all the stellar ratings given by Google and Yelp reviewers, a 1 michelin star awards and all other accolades are well deserved. The ambient is casual but classy. The service was great. The wine was awesome. The only reason why I give this a 4 stars is that although it was a very good cooking, the flavor profile is a bit one dimensional, and I put so much weight on food in my rating.

The meal started off with complementary bread. The spring onion focaccia. The bread was nice and soft. A bit salty to my liking but flavor was good

Next we shared two appetizer: duck liver moose and beef tartare. I found the duck liver moose well seasoned and has pronounce duck flavor with I like. It was served with fig jam, toasted bread, and pickle. I guess the toast was sour dough and was toasted very well. The beef tartare was served with fried leek on top which I think it is a great combination. The flavor of the beef is slightly muted, but overall a good dish.

We ordered the main course to share: arctic char, duck meatloaf, and pork shoulder. The best dish was clearly the Arctic char. The fish was grilled perfectly. I was very surprised how pronounce the charcoal aroma was in a very good way. The seasoning on the fish is was perfect as well.

The other two dishes were good but nothing exceptional about them. Pork shoulder was tender and juicy, and the duck meat loaf was well seasoned and nicely charred.

I ordered a Pinot noir from Williamatte valley to accompany with the food and it was excellent. They waiter was very knowledgeable about the wine as well. 

Overall though, I love this restaurant and it was a very hard for me to rate it especially that I put so much weight on food. I'll definitely come back again in the future.

4 stars* - highly recommended
*Very very close to 5 stars.

Are you kidding, only five stars? Let's say six stars!
The food is served from heaven. Had an incredible lunch there this weekend, what a pleasure.  Roy was a treat as well, very professional.   Looking forward to going back.

Highly recommend! Get yourself a reservation for the tavern for lunch or walk in for dinner at the bar. Must have a cocktail, the tavern burger (best burger ever) and cookies with milk. Amazing service and insanely delicious food!

I had very high expectations for Gramercy Tavern considering the Michelin star however I ended up leaving disappointed. 

TLDR: service 2/5, food 3/5, ambiance 4/5 

The service was terrible and I'm not sure if it's because my friends and I were the youngest ones there but Chris and the staff were inattentive, crass, and put us in a corner and barely talked to us again. 

We did the chefs tasting menu. The first dish they brought out was a 'welcome bite' Similar to a little cracker and it was delish. 

The second dish was scallop served cold. I believe this dish would have been improved by preparing the scallop warm. The dish was nothing impressive. 

The green soup was next. This was my least favorite dish of the tasting menu. 

For the main protein we were served the striped bass with carrots, cannellini beans, and chorizo. Again, this was good but nothing notable. 

The final protein was the roasted duck breast with bacon that was cooked to perfection served with tomatoes, poke beans, and basil . This was my favorite savory dish of the night. 

We ended with the grand finale dessert  which was the strawberries and cream with lime ice. This dish was innovated, beautiful on the plate, and the flavor combination was unique and mind blowing. My ultimate favorite dessert I've had in a WHILE! 

All in all service was 2/5, the food started off average and got better with each course while ending with an incredible dessert. 

Would I come back for the July tasting  menu? No since the only two dishes I really enjoyed were the duck and dessert. I noticed the duck is still on the menu even after seasonal changes so I'd come back and try the new menu. 

Don't waste your money or calories on the cold salmon, green soup, and fish.

What a wonderful time we had here. My bestie and I both got cocktails to start . We had the tasting menu  in the Dining Room. Tiny bites, bread with butter, then fluke add the first dish. The lobster as the second (which was my favorite). Then tile fish, and the steak, which was my second favorite. A bottle of the 2012 Chianti for the whole dinner rather than the wine pairing, it was bright and tasty. Marybeth was our server- who we really liked, as she had such a sunny and cool personality. Dessert was strawberries and creams, of which I opted for the sorbet. Definitely five stars! Will come back again.

Loved our lunch at Gramercy Tavern! We dined at the Tavern but will have to come back for the Dining Room tasting menu. 

Service was attentive and food was top notch. The beef tartare is something I would travel to NY to taste it again

WoWzA!!! Spectacular meal last night.  4 of us had just a wonderful time. Allow me to tell you about the top notch service.  They were all over it. Team effort and point on. I never felt smothered but a waitress or waiter was always close and attentive.  Great help with a French white wine (not my strength). First course was marinated fluke. So light and delicate, that melted in your mouth.
Corn Agnolotti was the 2nd course. The small purse pasta were filled with deliciosa. Cut one in half and grab some lobster on your fork for a mouth watering experience.
Golden Tilefish was next up!! One of my favorite fishes (being from Florida). It was so fresh and worked well with chorizo and cannelloni beans. WoW! who knew to put those together! Fantastic.
Perfectly grilled NY strip steak with strawberries, beets and black garlic. First time experience for me with black garlic. The foodies with love the flavors playing off each other on your tongue! So good.
The desert! Let me try to describe the wonder that you will experience with this. The different textures in your mouth at one time! Your taste buds will sign with delight. Strawberries and Cream. Ha! That's a sorely short description. It has Cream cheese mousse, green sorrel ice and angel food cake.  Your mouth will water waiting for the next bite. 
The best thing is that I left the table very very happy and satisfied with a Fantastic Meal. But was not stuffed to the gills and looking for a couch to lay on.
The night continued at a jazz club.
Expensive and well worth the price. I will
Be returning for sure.

Finally got here after hearing so much about it. 

We did the tavern menu. It did not disappoint. Service was impeccable, food was fantastic, and the drinks were spot on. 

I'm still dreaming about those oysters, and that burger. The latter of which I appreciate as it does nothing fancy to distract from its quality. 

Next time, I will try the tasting menu.

Didn't think I would get into this old staple of a spot in the middle of a bustling weekend evening. As luck would have it, my party of two arrived within an opening at the bar. 

There are many compliments to express. Simply put the folks who work there were as delightful as the fare. The well appointed staff have a right to be as pretentious as their clientele. Yet, they treated us warmly and made us feel like we were as extraordinary as the regulars.

All the cocktails are worth trying at least once. I've only tried three. We had tomato and plum and basil and ricotta as an app. Followed by the pork chop with peaches among other things. Couldn't resist blueberry pie although the corn ice cream was a bit too woo-woo for me. Try it nonetheless. 

Thanks Gramercy Tavern

Best restaurant I've ever been to!!! It checks off all the boxes of phenomenal food, beautiful decor, and excellent service.

I came here for my birthday and they treated us so well. My fiancé requested a romantic table sitting next to each other and they delivered. 

We did the 5 course tasting menu and everything was AMAZING!!! My favorite was the risotto asparagus. It was so creamy and full of flavor.
An absolute favorite in NYC. I love to dine on the casual side of the restaurant, or at the bar...love this place. And I love all the fresh flowers. The best food, in my opinion.

There are not enough words to describe the excellence of Gramercy Tavern. I have been to places with tasting menus with wine pairings before and they were excellent. Gramercy Tavern went above and beyond. The atmosphere is intimate and the waiters attentive without being intrusive which is a tricky with a meal with multiple courses.  The food is delicious and the portions were perfect, not a dab of food with a swirl of fancy sauces nor a pile of food that you have to ignore if you want to make it to the end of dinner. The pairing were right on the money and made the food taste better and vice versa.  The time here enjoying the fare is well spent.

I really enjoyed this entire experience. 
We went for lunch at an odd hour (2:30pm) on a Saturday and was able to get seated at a table right away with no reservations.

They started us off with a blueberry tomato foccacia. I loveee warm bread. It was an interesting (and surprisingly delicious) flavor combo. The blueberry/tomato was actually very subtle.

We got the beef tartare appetizer. It was not the traditional steak tartare, but this version was very well made & flavors are balanced. 

I came here because I heard amazing reviews about their tavern burger - and yes it's good. One of the best burgers I've had. Besides the fact that it is well cooked, I appreciate all the fine details to this burger. They crisped up the bottom bun so it didn't get too soggy to hold from all the delicious juices that seeped out of your medium-rare patty. The potato chips are also suuuper thin. Came with a smokey relish-type sauce... I wasn't sure if it was meant to dip my chips in or if I was supposed to put it on my burger, but it tasted great on both lol. I'm pretty sure they smoked the sauce too.

We ended dessert with vanilla beignets. I had gotten it because it was different than the traditional NYC dessert. I will say that this was 10/10 delicious, but idk I feel like it's an overpriced dessert lol. 

Waiting staff was wonderful.
Ambiance 10/10.
Amazing one Michelin star restaurant. So thankful we got to dine here!

Top choice for excellent food in a charming space served by friendly and accomplished servers who go above & beyond to make you feel welcome. I recommend the Dining Room's Chef Tasting menu--a delicious assortment of 5 seasonal dishes to delight and satisfy. You can add wine pairings if you wish.
Can't wait to return!!
Outstanding food and service! Excellent vegetarian choice, too. Can't wait to return. We are happy the restaurant is now open for lunch.

The culmination of my first NYC food adventure is right here. 

Beef Tartare and The Tavern Burger.

Oh. My. God. 

The beef tartare was incredibly delicious. The little roasted or fried onion rings were crazy good. How did you do that???? Insane!!! Every aspect blew me away, I licked that bowl clean.

That burger is the best burger I've ever had in my life. I was on the verge of tears, but I didn't cry. Incredibly well seasoned, juicy, delicious. I wish I ate that burger more slowly but it was too good. And the chips on the side! I am a huge fan of keeping the original flavor of the potato as much as possible and those soft chips were so good. 

Bathroom has the fanciest paper towels. Props to whoever's idea that was.

For it price point , The Gramercy Tavern's food, ambiance, and service were exceptional and far exceeded my expectations. Easily the best restaurant experience of my life. 

A must try.
Very nice ！The food is good and the service is excellent? The coolest thing is that they have both a "party" like front house and a formal dining area. Recommend for everyone for a try!

Nice lunch set menu though a bit on the expensive side.  Good quality good and friendly service.  I haven't been back to Gramercy Tavern in many years.  Restaurant still retains its old character and good service.  Overall we had a great lunch but there are many other choices at a lower price point.  
The restaurant started with a complimentary small bit and ended with a few bites of fruit.  Our appetizer lobster corn dish was very tasty.  This was followed by our main dish which I chose the grilled chicken - good char and grill.  For dessert, I chose the chocolate pudding (sorry forgot to take a picture).  The only thing I wish they provided in addition was some bread.  
Overall, a pleasant and good meal but probably not a place I'd go for lunch but would return for dinner.

This place was on my list for a long, long time. 

Happy to report the service was pretty solid, attentive and professional. 

We ordered the tartare which is worth one star in and of itself, the burger, which was ok (holy cow the chips were over salted), the duck meatloaf, which was underwhelming, and the cherry sundae, which was a-ok. 

Happy to cross this off the list, had a decent experience but can't imagine wanting to come back for any particular reason.  May be a good place to bring some business colleagues.

We had such a special night here thanks to the wonderful staff and delicious food. Loved the black bass and the banana bread as a departing gift was a nice touch. It was an excellent place to celebrate an engagement and we will definitely be back! Thank you, Stephen, for the fabulous service!

Hubby surprised me with a birthday dinner here last year and it was a spectacular date night. Despite having reservations, we still had to wait a bit which was somewhat of an annoyance but the hosts were really nice. They took our coats and checked them. It annoyed me more that the other guests waiting for tables were not considerate of others. There are very few chairs on which you might be able to sit while waiting for your table and some of these people were literally on top of us, with their bags and bodies far too close for my comfort. If you're near strangers, the least you could do is to respect their personal space and quite preferably, not touch them.

When our table was ready, we were lead to the dining room. They have so much space and they utilize it well. I loved our table. It was in a quiet corner where we could have some conversation and enjoy our meal while socially distant.

Our server and all of the staff that assisted us were extremely pleasant. They made us feel very comfortable and welcomed. We enjoyed a tasting menu and I had a wine pairing. All of the food was exceptional. The complimentary bread puffs were to die for. I loved all of it. We had a wonderful night and I would to go back. This is definitely a splurge worth every penny.

Mediocre food and even worst service. Went to celebrate a special day but ended up having a bad experience. We had a reservation for the main dinning room (tasting menu) but when we arrived we were seated outside until we complained. Food is not something to rave about either. Not going back.

Frenetic environment, hit and miss food, uneven service, $1,000 for two

Front desk was a madhouse at 8:45pm when we arrive for our table in the dining room. Line backed up and out the second door to the street. Five staff looking at each other clearly in the weeds. I was greeted finally and handed a cocktail menu. I was told my table wasn't ready and it would be 'a while'. When I asked, ' some time, your table just got their entrees'.  When my husband and I told them that was unacceptable to us, miraculously there was a table available. I was directed around the side and back of the host stand, stepping over the cords plugged into the wall to get into the hallway that leads past the tavern and into the dining room. 

Okay we are in. We did think about fleeing back uptown to Jean Georges as they had a table open at 9. Our server approached us and took our cocktail order, we also ordered the reserve pairing along with our dinner. 
An amuse of pickled vegetables on a crouton was tasty and then we were excited. 
The fluke crudo was average. Fine, but pedestrian. 
The agnolotti with corn and lobster was very good, especially with the pairing. 
The swordfish was dry, like cutting wet cardboard, but the herb pistou and beans were delicious. The runner didn't know what it was so we tried to determine all of the ingredients ourselves. 
I had the duck which was tasty and my husband had the sirloin that was served with so many other things it was confusing. 
Chocolate pudding and a Madeira for me, husband's was better, he had the cheesecake with fig. 
Staff were crazy running, a couple of smashed glasses, one rolling under a nearby table and the woman next to us on the bench seating was vaping in between courses.  Somm's super friendly and knowledgeable. 

One cocktail, dinner with reserve wine pairing and tip $1,000 is fine for us when it's great. Not great. 
Two stars for Somm's and two good courses.

A truly great dining experience. Food was incredible and delicious. The burger was to
Die for , very juicy and flavorful, hands down the 
Best burger I had for a long time. My sister had skirt steak it was very tender cooked very well . The cheese cake was caramelized with mandarin sorbet so amazing. Servers very friendly and attentive so phenomenal. It is a great place for date night and business dinner . Highly recommend this lovely restaurant.
We thought it was fine. But fine shouldn't cut it for a $200 lunch for two. The desserts were outright bad. Oh well, we can say we went.
Great food. Excellent service and a very pleasant ambience. A consistently excellent restaurant.

I wanted to thank a colleague with a special lunch and decided the GT would be a treat..... the experience was.....mixed.

I had some questions, so tried calling. I got an interminable recorded paean to the chef....and it took four tries to reach a human voice (and yes, I did call during the hours that the restaurant was open.)

I asked for 1230  in the garden on a Tuesday, was told there was nothing available - how about the tavern? No, but you can have 12:45 in the tavern. OK....

I arrived at at 1245 to find my colleague happily seated in the garden, .where there was only one (1) other table with a guest, a situation that did not change the same entire time we were there. No reservations at 12:30? Nothing in the garden?

The staff was perfection; the food was tasty but nothing really special -.....and the cost ridiculous (which I had anticipated that, so no surprise.)

Thanks, but no thanks.

Made reservations for the Tavern on a Sunday night. The Tavern serves a la carte, more casual menu. The place was packed and we saw the host turn away walk-ins. 

What we loved: 
Cocktails - seasonal fall apple cocktail and a martini
Appetizer: Duck liver mousse- GREAT! (Skip the cucumber soup. Thought it was ok, very simple/cleansing, couldn't taste shishito notes)
Main: jerk chicken (super tender, nice char, on bed of shredded cabbage with a light vinegrette)
Duck meatloaf (I almost skipped this because I judged it as just  "meatloaf". It was tender, juicy, amazingly flavorful, rich)
Dessert: pumpkin spice sundae with marshmallow puff and pumpkin pie crust (seasonal) 

My two favorite restaurants in SF/napa are Rich Table, Auberge. I felt Gramercy is right up there in terms of my palette, and all around strong dishes/drinks from start to finish!

Excellent and innovative, seasonal dishes. beautiful ambiance too- we came on the first week of fall and the decor, flowers, paintings were autumn themed.

Excellent experience!   I don't look snooty places and this was a great experience.  Very welcoming and great server with Mitch.   Food was creative and delicious but not pretentious or overpriced.   It is a great date night spot.    Thank you.

My favourite restaurant in NYC! I've eaten in both the dining room and the tavern. Both are great but have really different vibes. Go to the tavern if you want a more laid back, easy dinner; and go to the dining room if you want something more formal. The steak tartare was really yummy and the desserts are to die for. Definitely worth at least one visit while you're in the city!

The food was very good, but the service is what set it apart. Our waiter Mike was incredible, knew the menu inside and out, was very friendly and really cared that we enjoyed the experience.

We did the tasting menu which consisted of 5 courses. We started with an amuse bouche from the chef (a small cracker with a green leaf on top), then had the fluke crudo (1rst course), their homemade biscuits, lobster and corn agnolotti (2nd), swordfish (3rd), duck and steak (4th, we each picked one) and a chocolate pudding and fig cheesecake (5th, again we each picked one). Everything was very tasty but the best bite was the agnolotti. We both loved that dish, super flavorful and extremely satisfying. 

The crudo was very fresh and light, the swordfish was nicely prepared and came on top of a green sauce, and the duck and beef were both delicious, though the duck was better (the steak was a little too chewy, we ordered it medium rare). The desserts were a bit underwhelming, but I am not a big dessert person. The biscuits were very good (not like a southern biscuit, but still flaky with many layers you can break apart). The portions got larger with each course and we left feeling satiated. I would repeat the agnolotti and duck, but otherwise think we would try the tavern over the dining room next time. 

The restaurant itself is huge and nicely decorated. They have an outdoor space they call the garden which is on the sidewalk outside the restaurant.

How can you find fault in a local institution that defines and anchors the neighborhood name.  The food follows suit to its name.  It's your offsite home cooking with a "bar-ish/ale-like" feel that says...."I'm home!"

I never go back to restaurants and order the same dish.  Some establishments fail beyond their signature dish.  Not "the Tavern" as my friends and I refer to it; they make sure every dish in the menu stands on its own merit.

Stop by and taste a piece of history and home.

Cheers

So disappointing. Came for our Anniversary. I am at a loss to understand why a restaurant asks you if you're celebrating a special occasion and then does absolutely nothing to acknowledge it.
That being said, of all the Michelin starred restaurants with tasting menus that we have been to, this was at the bottom of the pack.
We were seated in one of the worst tables in the place. My fault. I should have spoken up.
Of the five courses, one was spectacular, two were very good and two were just okay. Service was professional but impersonal and perfunctory.
We will not be back.

Food is amazing, but service is hit or miss. The first time I came, I had an incredible experience that made me want to come back. The food was delicious and the service was really top tier, and our bubbly waitress was icing on the cake. It made me want to keep this restaurant on our rotation for weekly date nights. 

However, when I returned to Gramercy Tavern (within a month or so) it was not the same wholesome experience, the waitress we had was confused and unaware of how the restaurant functioned. We had to essentially debate her on how we could eat tavern menu and Prix Fixe because the waitress didn't believe you could order more food. She even had to bring the Manager for him just to say, yes they are allowed to eat from the tavern menu (because hello don't you want more money for your business) this whole debacle  soured the experience enough where we won't be coming back. Considering my husband and I dropped about $700 dollars per meal, you would think the service and the food would justify the price. The second visit really just wasn't worth justifying a third. Giving 4 stars because the food is really good and the place is worth trying when you luck out with a good waitress.

Such a great spot!! We came in for some drinks and dessert and we were so impressed!! The bartenders were so friendly and nice and made exactly what I asked for!!  I'd definitely be back here again!! Thanks Gramercy Tavern

This review is for the dining room and pre fixe dinner menu. I think if we were to ever go back (unlikely) it seems like their favorable reviews are for the a la carte tavern menu over the dining room.

The positive: they seated us for our reservation on time and the ambiance is perfect- warm and inviting. Our server was also wonderful and engaging. 

The negative- the food was lackluster. The portions for most dishes were quite small (even for pre fixe) and the temperature of the food on all courses was lukewarm at best. 

The food itself: starting course was a bland, cold almond soup (why are you serving a cold soup in October?): 1/5. Second course was a lobster pasta in a buttery ginger sauce that was sweet without being overpowering but nothing outstanding: 3/5. Third course was a swordfish with beans and peppers- cooked well but boring flavors and the fish was not the freshest (had a slight fishy odor): 1/5. Fourth course was sirloin steak with crunchy onions and peppers (our favorite course but only one TINY slice of sirloin- it was almost laughable): 3/5. Last course was dessert- we tried each the cheesecake and the chocolate pudding- both were okay but nothing spectacular: 3/5.

Overall I expected a lot more out of the food and experience provided the very high tab we paid at the end of this meal. We left very disappointed. I won't be back anytime soon.

This was quite an interesting situation.  We arrived from taxi.  My husband gave address and well we were at the wrong restaurant.

This was the restaurant we wanted to go to, but they were all booked up.  So I don't realize it and telling the hostess we have reservations at 5 etc.. We were there at 5, Gramercy doesn't open til 5:30.  It was a mess. Taxi is gone. I'm grumpy at my husband. The two hostesses saved the night.  Put us at a table in the bar.  We weren't going to drink, but did I mention I was grumpy?  Margaritas were clean, beautiful, yes plural!  My husband was so happy to see their wide selection of whiskeys and bourbons.  He had two different fancy kinds, neat.  Perfect. 
I had the pork chops, delicious!  He had the duck burger, loved it!  Then they knew it was (almost) my birthday.  And brought out an array of desserts to celebrate.  Probably because we spent so much on fancy whiskeys :)

Anyway, thank you to the entire staff for turning our night around.  Thank you to the chef(s) for preparing our delicious dinners before 5:30. Thank you Gramercy Tavern for it all!  Epic!

The best I've had in the last two months is the only one that has a lot of pain and it's not really like making me sick but brown has been really good with me too and I'm not really sick and tired lol I love it all the time and I'm always so glad to be there for me and I hope I don't feel good about that lol I just got home from my work lol I just need a shower lol I love it lol I just need a lot more lol I just got home lol I just need to know what about to you get off work now I just got hit by the house I need a shower lol I love it

A mixed evening for a special birthday included positives and negatives.  Positives - a cheerful and helpful server, which the manager substituted once the initial server was replaced.  excellent bread and butter, nice wine,  a generally pleasant atmosphere, the desserts were nice but not special

negatives - food was vastly overrated and uneven, inedible amuse bouche, too many overly sweet sauces distracted from poorly seasoned food,  bland and tasteless almond soup, followed by oily pasta, swordfish looked pretty but not an interesting taste, sirloin was dry and and overdone, orders confused

We had a good time since fortunately the companionship more than compensated.

Chicory salad was delicious. Burger was solid, albeit bacon slightly overpowered quality of meat. Still super enjoyable with homemade chips and perfect aioli. Chocolate cookie was expertly prepared. Service was spectacular. Great to see this place still going strong, even midweek, after all these years.

Lovely atmosphere and absolutely perfect service. My sidecar was on point. My husband's burger was delicious as were the accompanying chips, and my lumache was good. I liked the apple pie well enough but my husband was a disappointed with his pumpkin spice sundae, saying the pumpkin ice cream was flavorless. He left most of it. It is highly unusual for him to leave a dessert unfinished.  I would say my favorite part of the meal was our wonderful server.

I came here with a party of 5 on a Friday evening for dinner. This has a been a restaurant of interest for many of us. We made the reservation earlier in the week. Since this has been on most of our lists, expectations were high! 

The decor is elegant and the ambience is quaint. It is a rather larger restaurant than other Michelin star establishments. We noticed each room has it's own vibes and music. Our server and sommelier were very knowledgeable and were able to give us good wine recommendations. We ended up getting a bottle of orange wine.

The Tasting Menu is a seasonal 5 course meal. We had the fall menu at the time of our visit. There are a few courses where you're able to choose between two entrees.

For my 5 courses I had:
- Citrus Cured Arctic Char
- Squash Agnolotti
- Swordfish
- Roasted Sirloin
- Caramelized Cheese Cake

To start off the review; I would like to say that my table also ordered the other entrees that I didn't get, so we had a good variety of dishes at our table! 
The citrus cured arctic char is definitely a good starter dish but don't sleep on  the alternative option that is white almond soup. Both starters were equally very good! The soup is cold and very refreshing. 
The Squash Agnolotti was refreshing and flavorful. The alternative, Hay Smoke Gnocchi was good too. Both selections, you can't go wrong with. 
The swordfish entree was probably one of the best swordfish entrees i've had. It's not a very common dish for me, but most of the time swordfish has been very lean and too chewy for my likings; however the swordfish here was cooked perfectly where it wasn't too chewy and just the right texture. The veggie puree and the accompanying vegetables created a great flavor profile that works synergistically with each other.
The roasted sirloin was cooked medium rare, and it was a delicious dish, but the roasted duck breast is truly the better alternative of the two! If you love duck, I would highly recommend going for that. 
As for the desserts: The caramelized cheesecake came with figs, fig sorbet, and fig leaf oil. A very interesting but unique take on cheesecake. I liked it!

In summary; Great food, great presentation and execution. Staff were all courteous. I would come back again during another seasonal menu!

Service, 5 stars: The  staff was amazing. 5 star service!! I couldn't say enough good things about our waiter. The hostesses ' were great too. 

Atmosphere, 5 stars: it was decorated beautifully and it was very busy and buzzing. We went on Halloween and our waiter dressed up. It made our experience definitely festive and fun. They also offered us candy when we left. 

Food, 3 stars: I've been wanting to try this place for 5 years and I finally got a chance to go.... I hate to say it but the food was just alright. We got Beef Tartare, Roasted Oysters, Kale & Cabbage and the burger. All nothing to write home about. The burger was the best thing but I could've probably went somewhere a little cheaper and have gotten one just as good. 

Definitely a great spot. You'll be happy with your whole dining experience but I don't think it will be the best meal you will ever have. At least not in the tavern section.
Great restaurant in New York! Ate there on a business trip and while I thought it was a tad overpriced, the food was enjoyable. I enjoyed the fall decorations as well.

Fantastic dining Tuesday evening.  It started with being escorted to my table by none other than Chef Michael Anthony!  It just kept getting better.  Amazing service, INCREDIBLE sommelier, and the food!  It lived up to my hopes as this has been in my list for years.  I cannot wait to return!

Made a lunch reservation and arrived 30 min early. They seated us immediately. The ambiance was cozy and beautiful. It was decorated with autumn vibes. Their menu also entailed an autumn theme. The service overall was excellent. 

My date and I ordered the Return of the concord and morning glory cocktails. I would say the return of the concord is delicious, tastes like fruit punch. Morning glory is more on the sour end. We were served warm Angel breads with butter on the side. It was delicious! 

We ordered the pre-fix lunch menu. As appetizers, we ordered corn agnolotti and autumn green salad. Both were amazing! The autumn green salad had burrata cheese under and apple slices on top. Can't go wrong with it! it was delicious. 

For the entrees: swordfish and snowdance farm chicken. They were decent, but not comparable to the appetizers. We also ordered bacon and cheeseburger off the menu as an added entree. The burger and the sauce were good, but nothing special. The beef patty and the burger sauce were good. 

Desserts: chocolate pudding and caramelized cheesecake. I loved the chocolate pudding. The popcorn inside wasn't necessary in my opinion. The caramelized cheesecake came with a fig sorbet and a fig itself. Enjoyed it very much! Lastly, we ordered the pumpkin martini which was good too. 

I would like to come back and sit in the Garden for lunch or dinner next time.

Michelin revisited the NY restaurants in 2020-2021and Gramercy Tavern retained its star. After an evening in the dining room I can see why. Gracious service, tasting menu items that were consistently great, and an elegant but low key space. Not sure if the naysayers reflect inconsistency in the execution, or the need for some to be contrarian, but we had a wonderful evening. Spying that burger walking through the casual tavern area, I confess I was a bit jealous. Maybe next time.

Absolutely worst experience ever. My husband and I had reservations. We arrived on time and were told that the wait was still about 20 min. Not off to a good start. When we were seated, we were greeted by this absolute frazzled mess of a child Dan or Dean or whatever. He hurriedly took our drink orders which he struggled to get right when he tried to repeat them back to us. I'm not sure if he was drunk or just on no sleep but this poor thing was struggling hard with basic information. The drinks came and mine was wrong, but given the absolute look of panic in his eyes, I decided to keep quiet when he eventually came back to place a food order. This wasn't any better. After managing to stumble through both of our orders, we waited for nearly an hour for our food, watching him run around seemingly in a panic without so much as an update, or an offer to refresh our drinks. Unsurprisingly our food came out cold. I was tempted to speak up, but my husband insisted that we just deal with it instead of having to rely on this pitiful young man to correct it. Needless to say we won't be back.

I wouldn't necessary go back. I have heard so many great things about Gramercy Tavern that I was expecting a lot. The dishes were were a bit of a mix...some were good, some not very inspired. The main issue was the service, we had to run after our server. We also had to wait over 40 minutes past the time of our reservation to be seated.

Such an amazing experience. Been wanting to go here for a very long time and I was definitely not disappointed.

I made reservations for 2 at the Dinning Room section of the restaurant, which had their tasting menu (5 course menu). Each courses had a choice of 2 plates so we were able to eat all 10 dishes since I ordered 1 plate and my partner got the other. Ask the server about each dish and they'll be more than willing to help you choose. 

The staff was extremely helpful and attentive. The ambiance of the place was amazing. Needless to say, I'll be coming back each season to try their tasting menu. Highly recommended.

Snagged a resy here to celebrate a NYC anniversary. I had heard alot about the burger and was very excited to try it. 

We ordered the beef tartare, their flatbread and their chocolate chunk cookie. I will say, the burger was quite delicious. It's not my top burger in NYC, but it is definitely up there. The chips were also quite good, especially when dipped in the onion aioli dip. You can tell they were made with duck fat, they were very rich. 

The flatbread that we had ordered felt a bit too oily for my taste but it did have some nice flavors on it. The beef tartare was good but I don't dream about it. 

We all loved our drinks, we got Old Fashions. 

The standout to me, however, was the milk and cookies. I'm telling you, these are some of the best cookies I've ever had. I encourage you to order these, even if you aren't the biggest dessert person. 

Overall, a good meal but it's not at the top of my list to come back to. It's a good fancy date night spot or a place to celebrate and worth it to come and try at least once. 

4/5

I hate hate that I am giving them only 3 stars. Gramercy Tavern has been our favorite NYC restaurant and we made a point to come back once a year even living across the continent. This time it was disappointing! We ate dinner in the dining room as per usual. Portion sizes were smaller and the service was ok. The artic char used to come plated beautifully on a regular size plate, this time it was on a teacup size plate. The steak was a teeny tiny piece and slightly chewy. The cheesecake was a circle maybe 1.5-2 inches across. Our waiter- nothing wrong persay but it was not the Gramercy Tavern I had known and remembered. I think it was just him. But I don't think I'll make a point to be back. For the money I don't feel it's worth it anymore.

I've wanted to come here for years and was finally able to check it out last night with my sister. I started with a glass of Ridge Zinfandel which was amazing. I then had the Arctic char, the gnochi, the sirloin and the cheesecake. My favorite dish by far was the sirloin. The service was incredible, my sister eats incredibly slow and they didn't rush us. Really cool environment, feels like you are in a ski cabin. Can't wait to come back.

I have always wanted to eat here. Several years ago I stopped by for a glass of wine but could not get a table. This time I made reservations 30 days in advance which is the earliest you can make them. All I can say is I was not disappointing at all. The ambience of the place itself is spectacular. It looks feels and smells like an English tavern. The wood fire on a cold day is very comforting. My wife and I both loved what we ordered as well.
