My wife ordered the steak tartare and I ordered the grilled pork shoulder. Both were fantastic. We also split the potato and clam flatbread. It was delicious as well. All in all I was very happy I went to the trouble of marking my calendar for 30 days ahead of when I was visiting New York so I could make reservations. I totally recommend this place. The service also is extremely warm and friendly.

Meeting a friend out of town and we decided to walk in here to eat at the bar. We anticipated pricey but wanted to give this well-known spot a try. The daytime bartender took great care of us and we really liked her! She said she was new but we couldn't tell. We enjoyed the cocktails and the dishes albeit not plentiful were delicious. The menu seems designed for couples to order several things to fill up. The service was quite wonderful and we didn't feel out of place dressed business casual.
Classic nyc spot. Very nice ambiance,Relaxed but high end. All the items were great. The almond soup was amazing, really enjoyed the flavor profile

Amazing !!! 

Went to Gramercy Tavern the service was amazing. We had some apps and the Tavern burger & Duck Meatloaf. Every dish was amazing and I'll definitely be back soon.

We went to Gramercy Tavern couple times, but this time is the worst one. We spend more than3 hours just for 5 courses, we wait over 30 minutes for bread and cocktail (cocktail still good, specially the fig one).

Most if the dishes still good, however the dessert completely taste like from whole food.....

Great service.
Great oysters.
Burgers were overcooked and oversalted.  Had to send back to the kitchen but error was corrected promptly.

I would not recommend coming here! It's honestly a pretty basic place with okayy food. I came from CA and had a full schedule of eating, however, this place definitely falls on the lower side. The service was quick, but I just felt like the chicken dish I ordered was not amazing or memorable. The duck liver mousse was very good, but the bread that came with it did not compliment it very well.

My friend really recommended the burger here, so I tried it. It was a bit underwhelming but everything else we ordered was delicious! The atmosphere of this place was also very nice. Really wanna come here with my family one day. The menu items seems to change a lot to. Very looking forward to the next time.
AMAZING spot!! Love how they switch up their seasonal menu. Such good burgers, oysters, soups, etc

5 Course Tasting menu review coming up ahead. 

We were served:
Bread & Butter- the butter was a cross between a biscuit and a 
First Course: Arctic Char & Almond Soup- love seafood so both were on par in terms of taste. I liked the former more while my bf liked the latter more in comparison. Stand alone, they were both great.
Second Course: Lobster Squash Agnolotti and Polenta. The Lobster Squash Agnolotti is not one you want to skip. Absolutely amazing!
Third Course: Duck & Steak- of all the courses, I rank this one #4. However, the Duck was better than the Steak. 
Fourth Course: Fig Cheesecake & Chocolate Pudding- Good dessert but maybe I was expecting to be blown by these further.

This was my first 5-course dining experience in the city and there were some big hits and only teeny tiny misses. The biggest hits, surprising to my preference, were the vegetarian items served. This makes sense since the head chef specializes in this domain; and personally the star of the night for me was the Squash Lobster Agnolotti. A month later, and I'm still thinking about the agnolotti served there.

Expensive meal but you get the best bang for your buck if you go with a +1 and order one of each item on the menu. 

Our service was great, and the restaurant was crowded which is testament to the popularity of the place.

Absolutely amazing service
Catered to our 2 year old
I need the menu changes but
Oysters-phenomenal
Calamari corn salad 10/10
Fish options 10/10
Burger-9/10

Went for the tasting menu and had a great time. Took a little over two hours but was definitely worth the price and experience. All of the dishes were wonderfully prepared and I left surprisingly full.

Excellent dinner spot with a lot of eclectic cuisine but the portions were wanting and we ended up going to Joe's Pizza for a second meal. The best part was catching Manhattanhenge right after we exited.
Great experience at this Michelin starred restaurant! Service was great, and we felt informed and educated with every course.

Our family of 5 was seated in the "dining room" of the tavern. We were told the only availability was the 5 course tasting
menu.  This was not my first rodeo with a tasting menu, as it is a higher priced option. However, Gramercy Tavern is not a 5 star restaurant. The tasting menu was $165 for GARBAGE! If my 95 year old aunt was not with us, we would have left the premises before the first course. Although, the team members were very polite and welcoming, the service staff was reaching over and across us to refill beverages. That's a no-no! 
My 4th course was sirloin steak, a lower priced meat ($10 per pound in Whole Foods) was not medium rare, as requested. All 3 bites (ss it was a tasting) were cooked to a medium temperature. The overall experience was not worth the price, at all!

I can't believe it took me 20 years of living in NYC to get to Gramercy Tavern.  Not only that, but have now been twice in a span of a few weeks!

Have tried both the pre-fix menu and the A La Carte .... You will not go wrong with either.  It all depends on what you're in the mood for and how much you want to spend on a meal.

For the pre-fix I had the Squash Lumache, Grilled Skate, and Cheesecake.  For the A La Carte I had to try the burger.  Everything was just absolutely amazing!!!  The whole food experience is enhanced with the absolutely gorgeous holiday decorations and the impeccable service they provide.  I can only back up every person that has ever recommended this restaurant as a NYC staple.  Definitely make a reservation as it's not an easy feat to get in here!

Súper place! Came here for a quick cocktail with my man. We didn't have reservations but there was an open spot at the bar, the place was packed. I love my man and we are both fans of Tom Colicchio. My man had the pear Japanese  whisky cocktail and said it was the best cocktail ever, I tried it and also loved it. I got the tomato martini which was pricy at $25 but it was really amazing! The flavor really surprised me, just a subtle hint of tomato. The people eating at the bar next to us all had food that looked delicious. This one man was eating creamy soup with the most delectable soft cheese bread of some sort. I really wanted a bite! Chill, trendy servers and really beautiful decor. I will definitely be back for dinner.

UPDATE, came back again and got the tomato martini and celery root soup to spit with my man! Martini was even better than the last.
Soup was silky and delicious. I will try to make it at home.

Their burger is cooked to perfection. One of the best I have had in the city. Soup was served cold, but the staff took care of it seeing my partner's reaction to the first spoonful of cold soup. It's a good Michelin star restaurant and tipped over 30% of the bill.  Service was a little slow and cold soup was served, so going with a four as they were not on their Michelin star game this Sunday. Staff was friendly. Was almost a five. Expect a Michelin star level experience at a Michelin star restaurant is all.  Maybe they were just a little off their Michelin star game this Sunday.

Not a fan of Danny Meyer with his prior COVID booster vaccine fascism at his high end restaurants while not enforcing it for Shake Shack(bleh)... One of his weird inconsistencies that made him look like a hypocrite who only cared about his high end restaurant employees. Did not plan on ever visiting his restaurants again over his COVID vaccine booster stance, but wandered in to Gramercy Tavern. Didn't know it was one of his restaurants until a customer next to us said he was excited to try a Danny Meyer restaurant... If you don't mind giving your money to a guy who was an outspoken pro COVID vaccine booster fascist, it's a good destination with quality food. Four stars is based on the experience we had and not for my disapproval of Danny Meyer. Sticking to my principals and don't plan on going back to a Danny Meyer restaurant, but not knocking the food except for the cold soup. Would have gone with a 5 if it wasn't for the slow service and cold soup. Order taken quickly, but slow delivery.

My review is purely of the dining room. The food was delicious, we did the 5 course tasting menu. My wife and I essentially got one of each so we could try everything on the menu. The pasta dishes (gnocchi and agnolotti) stood out the most to me. The duck entree was also delightful. The steak entree was surprisingly tough. Overall the meal was good but to be honest very surprised that it is Michelin starred. 

My biggest issue was the service. Before even being seated the host took our names and we just waited even though we had a reservation. He told us that it would just be a moment before we were seated. He then proceeded to seat 5 parties  before us and then looked at us and asked if we had a reservation...

During the course of the meal we probably had 6 or 7 different servers but not in an organized dual service plating kind of way. The first server who took our order disappeared the entire meal until the end where he gave us the bill and put in his own tip. There was another server who had given our first course to the table next to us who had arrived and placed their order 15-20 min after us. When the server came out he was confused that they had their course, I told him it was probably ours but he had walked away. Between the second and third course we waited 25 min! There was one server who was very attentive but he seemed to be covering all the tables. The uniform is a blue button down shirt and it looked like pure chaos in a sea of blue with servers just walking around dodging each other. I will say the wine list is impeccable, I had a lovely Turley Cinsault. A gentleman who I assume was the Somm was excellent and knowledgeable and had a great conversation. 

I will try the tavern but do not think the dining room tasting menu is worth the cost based on the service. Perhaps it was an off day and I should give them another chance but it won't be soon.

Sat at the bar this time and it was wonderful. The bartender knows hospitality and keeps service smooth while welcoming and unhurried. Smoked oysters were delicious and duck meatloaf was good. The only drawback was there were three children under the age of 11 seated at the bar. It took away from feeling adult. Very strange to seat children at the bar.

I had just arrived in NYC on a Tuesday evening and we needed a place to eat and unwind.  (We being 2 friends and I) Walked right past it in search of another place that I found on Yelp that looked good but after getting our bearings and finding other place, decided it was too crowded and loud. Went back to Gramercy and while it was kinda loud too, not as bad.  Food was pretty good and it was close to our lodging. Our born/bred NY friend found it acceptable. Service was fine.
Love the ambiance, great food and service.  A gem in the neighborhood.  Definitely get the burger and a glass of Grillo!!
Always a must visit for us when we are in the City. The decor , service and food is too notch.

Here for a luncheon to celebrate an engagement -- and what on earth could be better? Beautiful room, amazing cocktails, and every dish was better that the one before. Even the bread was special. The gracious helpful staff was the cherry on top!

I'm sure I can't add anything that hasn't always been said. If I could give this restaurant more than five stars, I would. The food and the service was exceptional. I chose a Chianti, but was chuffed to see a local (to me) excellent finger lakes wine on the menu. My partner and I split the burger and pasta. The apple and cheddar focaccia that came beforehand was amazing. I could eat it every day. Dessert was beignets and coffee.  

Our server was outstanding. Always there when we needed him but not intrusive. Super friendly and engaging. So looking forward to returning soon. I was too busy eating to take more than one photo. Oops!

The review is for the Dining Room, which offers a 3 course seasonal prix fixe menu for $72. Although fairly limited, the selection is well executed which is apparent in flavors. We had the celery root purée soup and pasta with roasted butternut squash and lobster to start. Pasta was excellent with just the right al dente toothsomeness.  Next came mains roast chicken and vegg as well as skate wing over broccolini. Both were tasty although chicken skin could have been crispier. The skate wing was exceptionally well prepared. Lastly, we had chocolate mousse and cheesecake to finish . Again, well executed and with flavorful detail touches.  Staff was attentive and attentive to small requests like bar potato chips with drinks. We opted for Bloody Mary and soft drinks to the $144 base. Total tab with tax and tip was $243.  Albeit a bit pricey for lunch, as an early dinner which this was, this NY classic is well worth a visit .

As much as we would've liked to say "we loved it, it was amazing!" I'd have to say this was probably not worth the price point. We did the dining room tasting menu. My husband ordered the top five and i the bottom five as did our friends who were a couple.
The only thing that was mind blowing was the squash agnolotti and the tender roasted duck breast they called Peking duck. With two other dishes being under salted or over salted we wished each servings had better consistency (we were able to compare because there were two of the same dishes each course). All in all, wasn't super impressed with the food but the service was great.

Obvs this restaurant is very notable, famous and prestigious... 
Came for lunch, got the $60 prix fix! 
You need to make a reservation, we made ours for the dining room. 
The app of cabbage and kale was the best thing in the whole meal, I wish I could get a bucket of it. The roasted chicken and the skate were also great, would definitely get again. My husband noted his fav thing of the day was also his app which was pasta with lobster. 

I had the cheese plate for dessert and while I love cheese, didn't know what to expect. I am by no means an expert, but our server explained to me her favorites, how to eat it, what everything was, and never once made me feel dumb. 

About our server Hannah... she was incredible, super knowledgeable, answered all our questions, never made us feel rushed and was overall just kept smiling and made us want to stay and now, come back. 

We were there at 12 pm so we didn't do the wine pairing, we had plans after, but next time I def will!

Amazing food. Highly recommend. We are at the tavern. 

Started with oysters which were very good. 

Husband had the burger which was 5/5 fresh bread, and the burger was perfectly cooked and flavor was great. Highly recommend

I ordered the black bass, and it was delicious. I cleaned the plate. 

Definitely make this place a stop on your trip.
one of the best in the city, Always worth it. But if you are doing the tasting menu (not eve sure if they still have it) be prepared for a long evening.

I went to the dining room for a birthday dinner with friends and that experience was a solid 4/5 (one of my fave tasting menus) - excellent food, good variety of dishes, great atmosphere, and reasonably priced. 

I recently went back with a friend because we wanted to try their famous burger. The burger itself was delicious, but what I truly struggled with was eating the burger without fries. It came with duck fat chips instead, which were adequate at best given it tasted very similar to lays original. It was overall still a pleasant dining experience as we also enjoyed the roasted oysters and the duck liver mousse. However, I would very much recommend reserving a meal in the dining room over the tavern if you're looking to do one or the other.

Restaurant Week Lunch $60 These days I would rather splash out then dine mediocre and when the resy appeared after many years of trying to snag one I grabbed it. I dine out a lot during restaurant week and this experience was stellar in every way. $60 -3 course market lunch is a bargain for the level of food & was so appreciative of the bread service too after other dining experiences.
Ate and drank;
Chianti $16
Amuse bouche
Angel biscuits 
Celery root soup & Asian pear
Skate
Chocolate mouse with coconut ice cream 
Muscat grapes 
It has to be years since I had an amuse bouche- defo pre pandemic. The soup was insane- savory and sweet with crunchy Asian pears. 
Skate in chili oil with perfect little cauliflowers.
Of course the mousse was flawless and the charming surprise of muscat grapes to finish.
Wow what a meal!

We had a great dinner in the Tavern. It's what you've come to expect from a Union Square Hospitality place -- a delightful, well run restaurant with well executed food. Everything we ate was good, and while nothing truly wowed, that is not really the point of eating here. The point of eating here is enjoying one of New York's great dining rooms. It's buzzy and alive and is the kind of place where you can be sandwiched between folks celebrating an anniversary and a solo diner having a burger and a beer.

Good but nothing spectacular.  Have a nice dinner, a good drink, a warm dessert, and enjoying watching wealthy 20-somethings spend their money freely.  

The kitchen gave me a dish for free, which was a nice surprise.

Eh. Not much more to say.  I've heard and read so many great things about this place, but it was honestly eh..... Two weeks ago we went and had a multi course tasting menu but I don't remember anything about it.  I literally don't remember what any of the courses were because they were all mediocre, not bad but not great. The service was inconsistent at best which may have resulted from them constantly juggling servers and sommeliers.  It was weird.  They messed up our first drink order which imo is perhaps the worst thing a waiter can do.

Small margins. They are what distinguish good from great, especially in hospitality. They are much of what owner Danny Meyer talks about in his book, "Setting the Table".

They were also, for many years, what drew us back to Gramercy Tavern. We wanted an evening done right, a feeling of being in the hands of professionals, with no distractions from our enjoyment. And we always got it - until this time.

To be sure, things started promisingly as usual. On the day of our dinner, we were able to move our reservation half an hour earlier thanks to the accommodating maître d'. When we arrived, we were welcomed with a smile (though not with a "Welcome back"). We were shown to the table in the dining room nearest to the tavern. After asking for a quieter table, we immediately received a much more intimate two-top.

After a few beats, our server gave us drink menus. We wanted wine with dinner; without knowing what we'd be eating, the drink menus alone were initially useless to us. But the food menus came a couple of minutes later, and our server asked us about food allergies.

Each course offered two choices, excepting three for the main. It took us seconds to choose and a couple of minutes more with the wine list. Yet our server left us, menus closed on the table, for what seemed like an age. In between, the sommelier stopped by. I told him what kind of wine we planned to order with our food options, and he said it was a great choice. Finally we flagged down our server with the help of another diner who saw us haplessly waving. He asked us again about food allergies. And then we ordered.

The wine came first. It was a Beaujolais... and it was full of brett. In case you don't know, brettanomyces is a fungus that infects wine and creates an aroma frequently described as "barnyard" but perhaps more precisely called horse sweat. Brett isn't necessarily a flaw; some winemakers add it deliberately. Still, it is polarizing and can be off-putting. So I was surprised that the sommelier hadn't noted it. When I mentioned it later to the sommelier, he simply said, "Yes, it's part of the style." Hmm.

The bread finally came, and then the food. The first courses went to the wrong diners, but after that everything was correct. Here's what we thought:

Hiramasa: delicate fish, but the only salt was in the sauce; unless the fish and vegetables were drenched, they were completely unseasoned.
Beets: tasty except for the raw beet slices, which probably should have been fried until crispy instead.
Agnolotti: my wife liked it more than I did; I had a piece of crab that didn't taste fresh.
Gnocchi: pillowy, slightly smoky, good comfort food, somewhat overseasoned but satisfying.
Skate: the most interesting dish, a fusion creation with some Thai basil and citrus zing in a creamy sauce.
Polenta: nothing special, merely correct; a vegetarian placeholder.
Duck: tender meat that was salty and smoky enough not to need any bacon alongside; some of the cooked vegetables arrived cold.
Chocolate: thick for a mousse but tasty, nice combination with the coconut and passionfruit.
Cheesecake: black sesame powder was a decent complement, but the sorbet didn't work at all; tangy cheesecake doesn't need tangy fruit.

We made it to the end, though we couldn't finish the bottle. We paid: $528 for two set menus, an $80 wine, tax and a 20% tip. This was a lot of money for a meal where the small margins weren't always there.

One side note - whatever the dress code was at Gramercy, it doesn't exist anymore. On this Saturday night, the dining room was dotted by people in their 20s and 30s wearing hoodies and t-shirts. I understand that things may have changed through the pandemic. But when you're dressed to the nines for a special occasion, being surrounded by folks who look like they've just been on their laptops in their bedrooms does tend to devalue the effort.

We can't call ourselves regulars at Gramercy, but we are repeat customers. In fact, because we can't come so often, each visit is rather meaningful to us. This was a Valentine's Day weekend celebration, our first date night without the kids in months. It wasn't a car crash by any means. It just wasn't quite what we had hoped, expected, and remembered.
Delicious tacos and reasonably price Mexican food at Chelsea Market. Yummy! Highly recommend.

The prefix menu was accommodating to both carnivores and vegetarians, which worked well for our group of eight.

As for beverages, they have well made cocktails, wine pairing and nonalcoholic options. 

Overall a positive experience with exceptional service. Some dishes were better than others. For example, second course of hay smoked gnocchi was much more flavorful than the squash Agnoletti. So don't just assume the meat version will be tastier. In fact, the vegetarian options were more flavor forward.

I've always considered Gramercy Tavern to be one of the best restaurants in New York City. The last time I was there, though,  the food was a little too salty, and the atmosphere felt a bit tense, more of an institution than a cozy place to eat like it used used to be. I hope they can bring back some of that nuance that we used to come there for.
Had an amazing dinner, service is top notch. Pre-fixe menu was a ton of food unlike a lot of places in the city.

We celebrated my wife's 30th Birthday at Gramercy Tavern. It was our first time spending any amount of time in NYC other than business travel. New York hasn't disappointed and The Gramercy Tavern brought our experience to a different level.

We've eaten at several Michelin star restaurants across the world and our dining experience at Gramercy was on par, or better than some of the best restaurants we've ever eaten at. The service was impeccable. The wine pairing with the 5 course meal was perfect and brought our experience to the next level!

Well done! We will be back!

One of the best burgers in nyc!
Great Whiskey sour.
Still wanna try the full tasting menu
Short wait to sit at the bar. Enjoyed sipping on crafted cocktails while enjoying delicious dinner fare. Fun and engaging wait staff. Highly recommend a stop here!
Always good service and elevated atmosphere. Highly recommend for special occasions and just because.

Just came in for a quick meet-up but overall the service is excellent and the vibe is perfect. Have been here in the past and the food was excellent (I mean, it's a 1-star Michelin spot) but the combination of the location, service, food and environment make it amazing.

I loved the ambiance of the Tavern. Great date spot. Service was great and the food was solid (just a bit pricey for what it was, but okay for nicer occasions.) They gave me a complimentary meringue for my birthday (we ordered the other two desserts)

Izakaya cocktail was amazing. Bass was cooked perfectly and the mushrooms were amazing. The dish overall was good. Burger was also good - wish it had more vegetables but it was very hearty (good for meat lovers).

The tasting menu with the wine pairing was incredible! It was definitely really busy but the service did not lack at all. I came here for a work dinner with my team and would definitely recommend coming here for a work related or group dinner. The vibes were great. I would definitely recommend trying Gramercy Tavern!
Delicious! trust the chef! Needs reservations. My third time here. Good for celebrations !

I don't remember what drink I got but get it! Lol. It has milk in it, it was light refreshing and so fab I had 3! 
We sat in the bar area and it was lovely. Skip the duck meatloaf, while delish it's just a tad greasy but that burger was DIVINE. 

And everyone is right- the citrus and beet salad is a must
One of my favorite restaurants in the city. Always come here for bdays, celebrations, etc. Chocolate chip cookie for dessert is excellent!!

Definitely recommend getting a bar seat, especially if you're going solo or with 1 other person. Definitely came here for the burger and the cookie (both worth the hype) 

Steak tartare 5/5
Such a well balanced app. It had little mushrooms which I loved!! It tasted super fresh and they split it onto two plates for the two of us which I thought was a nice touch. Comes with the perfect amount of bread 

Burger 4.8/5
Honestly a really good burger especially when dipped in the aioli. I think my only request would be having a little more veggies in there but the burger itself is super solid. Definitely worth trying 

Duck meatloaf 2/5
I really am not a big duck fan but I found it underwhelming. I didn't love the texture and thought it was a little bland. I wish I tried a different entree 

Cookie 5/5
Super gooey and delicious. Especially paired with the milk it's a perfect ending to a great meal 

Ricotta donuts 3/5
I thought it was good but I may have been stuffed at that point. I probably wouldn't order it again since I wasn't a big fan of the donut itself. The ricotta was good though

If I could put a zero star I would, but this is not an option...and to know this establishment has a one star in the Michelin Guide makes me wonder can you buy your stars cause it certainly seems to be the case here.
The saying "don't meet your hero's" certainly applies at the Tavern, we ended the night by having the finger flashed at us by one of their bar tendres... after having a dreadful experience not just food wise but the lack of passion of most of the team, the lack of attention into the details ( wobbly foldable table,  very dirty bathrooms, sommelier who tries to push expensive wines, and the salt to cover up the bad produce which prevented us to actually eat it was that distasteful) a very big disappointment for such a New York staple. Never experienced such thing in my 11years here, not sure they thought we were tourists none the less go spend your money elsewhere please!
Yes they waived the charge of the diner menu ( we did not eat a thing) we still had to pay for the wine and nothing really was done in a meaningful way to better the experience or try to understand what went wrong. I guess they are far beyond laying on their laurels and taking everything for granted, such a shame! not sure they even know who Danny Meyer is or if they ever heard of Setting the table... honestly go to the shack if you would like a descent meal for it's buck...

I chose to  visit on a solo date while visiting NYC. Because I was alone, I made a reservation for the more casual tavern area, and opted out of the area offering the tasting menu. The cocktail list is straightforward and approachable. Being an Indiana native, I was pleased to see the only non NY beer offered was Three Floyds Gumballhead, which is a classic hoppy IPA. The atmosphere is warm and cozy. It makes you feel welcome while still being elevated. Service was great, as I would expect from a restaurant of this caliber. Not being super hungry, I went staight for an entree and chose the Grilled Black Bass over parsnips and a smoked oyster chowder. The first bite was pure bliss. Flavors expertly balanced and it had just the right touch of salt. I do wish the skin on the fish was slightly more crisp, but it didn't take away from the overall dish. This was a lovely experience and I would definitely come back again solo or with a group.

As a general rule of thumb, I usually hold any place that's on the pricier side to a higher standard. I think it's something about the principle of the thing...if I'm going to drop $$$ on a dinner, I want it to be amazing. Luckily, after my boyfriend and I visited Gramercy Tavern, I'm happy to say this restaurant is a fairly solid choice.

What we ordered:
 
- Beef tartare: I really liked the flavor of this! It came atop a puree (mushroom?) and sprinkled with sesame seeds, which I've decided is the only way I'm eating my tartare from now on. Amazing crunch and absolutely delicious - plus, it comes with a side of bread (yes, I asked for a second helping). 

- Tavern burger: Don't get me wrong, this is a good burger. It's just that this has been so hyped up that I expected it to blow my mind. I wanted something special - an egg maybe, or a special kind of ingredient - something to take it the extra mile. Still, the bacon is *chef's kiss* and the aioli was great. The potato chips were also a nice touch!

- Grilled striped bass: I didn't love the parsnips that it came on (I thought they were a little bland), but the fish was perfectly cooked. My boyfriend had no complaints and I'm pretty sure he licked the plate clean, so that tells you all you need to know.

All in all, I really do like Gramercy Tavern! Is it the best Michelin place I've tried? No. Is it a restaurant with great service and good food? Yes. 

TLDR: come for the atmosphere, stay for the duck fat potato chips. Don't expect anything earth-shattering, but you'll walk away with a great meal.
Nice place to stop and eat with some friends. Too noisy for a date. Good food. Can get really crowded.
I've ordered in many times and food is delicious & high quality. My order always comes correct and well packaged.
Fantastic! Great location, beautiful restaurant. Amazing food. The burgers are juicy and big... every dessert is delicious! Great birthday brunch with my people.

The food and service here is always so amazing. Like, whenever I come here I'm amazed at how delicious food can be. 

The last couple times I've eaten at Gramercy Tavern I've sat in the tavern which is much more laidback than the dining room, but still has great food. The dining room is good for a very special occasion, like an anniversary or something like that. The tavern is better suited for a night out with friends of a casual date night.

Anyway, the food! The espresso martini was fantastic. So was the potato and clam flatbread. It was creamy, but not too rich. For my main I got the Campanelle and WOW. Seriously one of the best dishes I've ever had. The mix of flavors and textures was phenomenal. For dessert we had the cookie and donuts. I didn't eat the donuts but the people I was with loved them.

All in all, an amazing spot for food. Great service, great eats, great plating, it's all there! 

(Included pics from a visit last summer that I didn't review)

Wow, just wow.  From 2008 to 2019 my favorite Burger in the world was at the spotted Pig (first time I visited to last time I visited).  Now that they are closed I have a new front runner.  The Tavern Burger at Gramercy Tavern is a revelation.  A perfect size, perfect proportions, perfect toppings, seasoned perfectly.  Just all around delicious!  
I'm in town for work and walked up around 9pm, there was one spot at the bar available, cozied up to the bar and ordered a local Draft IPA and had my eye on the Burger.  
Cooked over a wood grill, perfectly cooked Bacon, expertly melted aged Cheddar, some sort of magical umami dust they must put on it. It was truly an experience.  
$35 is pretty steep for "Just a burger" but this is hardly that, this is a burger experience.
It's just too loud. The food is fine, I guess. I found it impossible to enjoy myself with so much noise.
I try to make it here at least once a month.Tonight was exceptional.The food,ambience,service and cleanliness of this restaurant is beyond 5 stars !

Amazing! Exceptional service and food. We were a little worried based on what the tasting menu had in it and we each ordered something different and we loved every item! Best meal of our NYC trip, and the staff were attentive to every need and detail. One of the best restaurants I've ever been to. I can't say enough about this restaurant.

Gramercy Tavern, one Michelin star new American style
The decor is very cozy, modern American rustic style of a restaurant, very suitable for family and friends to gather, while very good photo.
I chose the $148 tasting menu and loved the asparagus dish, very fragrant. I love their bread, fragrant and soft, with butter is very good, ate three  main dish without merit, very American style. Dessert unexpectedly crisp, not as sweet as other American-style restaurants. His menu is based on the seasonal ingredients, every time you go will be different. Overall it's still a restaurant worth going to, a very cozy experience

We are in the neighborhood on a quiet weekday. It was 5pm and we tried to walk in for a table of 2. There were atleast 50 visible empty seats. We were turned away because we did not have a reservation. No thanks next time.

If I could give this restaurant more than five stars, I would. The food and the service are ambiance are exceptional. I loved seeing a local excellent finger lakes wine on the menu which was truly incredible. My mom and I split the burger, pasta, and a few appetizers. The apple and cheddar focaccia that came beforehand was amazing. I could eat it every day. Dessert was beignets and espressos.

Our server Mirabelle was outstanding. Always here when we needed her but but not intrusive. Super friendly and engaging. And extremely knowledgeable. At some point I have to try their seafood, because I hear excellent things.
So looking forward to returning soon.

If you're craving a great burger and a chill atmosphere, look no further than the tavern. Excellent service, great vibes, and one of the best burgers you can find in NYC. Duck meatloaf was also unique and satiated our meat craving. We indulged ourselves with the chocolate chunk cookie to top our meal off. Definitely can see why the tavern is so iconic.

In my years of cooking it was a pleasure to work with this team over a decade ago and Chef Michael Anthony and team have not disappointed. Not only was the bar service immaculate but the food was beyond excellent from start to finish.

I was only in NYC for a few days and was hoping to make a trip here and am so glad I did. I have to say thank you to Alyssa (bartender) for procuring an amazing food and beverage experience and converse about the restaurant world post Covid. New York will never be the same again but there are still places like GT that embody the dining experience. 

I dare you to order anything off the menu and not fully enjoy the presentation, flavor and overall service they offer.

Well done to the BOH and FOH team!
Fantastic meal. Every course is the ideal version of that dish.

This place is super cute. We sat on the tavern side. Our server was great with suggestions and we ended up getting the oyster appetizer. It was amazing. The ambiance is a little loud when there is a good size crowd and everyone is talking. Everything tasted like it was homemade. I would definitely go back.

I've been going to Gramercy Tavern for years...both the tavern and dining room. I'm not sure if something has changed in the past year, but I have to say, tonight's meal is one of the worst I've ever had at a restaurant of this caliber. Seated at 7:15pm, we didn't get our bread until 8:15pm, only to be followed by a cold, slow, inattentive meal that dragged on for an additional 2.5 hours (a total of 3.5 hours for 4 tiny plates of food). The food was mediocre at best tonight, lukewarm, and the server barely acknowledged the poor service. A seat of 5, this check came out to be over $1k, and I'm utterly shocked that not even an "I'm sorry" was muttered. Disappointed is the best word to describe tonight's experience and after years of great memories, I will never come back here again.
You won't be disappointed here. Classic neighborhood staple. Recommend if you're in mid town, Gramercy, the  East village or Murray Hill

I've had 5 course meals in the past that I could not finish (nor cared for) however we enjoyed and left nothing behind during this recent visit. Gramercy Tavern is special (Danny Meyer restaurants are ALL special). Our server, Stephanie, was tops - she knew everything about every detail of our meal. Celebrated our 25th wedding anniversary here and we'll never forget the evening.

Went during restaurant week, and the food was amazing. I especially loved the grilled vegetables and the sesame chicken although portion sizes do run a bit small (but you're not coming here to get full, right?). Waiter was really kind and was able to get us a second helping of bread. Definitely recommend going during lunch time to avoid any rush.

it has been a while since I've been there. But the times that I was there I enjoyed what I ate and had nice times with the people I was with. It's very quaint and it's a nice place to go if you dare go in any restaurants these days.It's also historical I believe one of the earliest restaurants in the city I have heard. Yes royal jones has eaten there I saw him
Family favorite! Coming forever. Incredible meal, service and layout! Will be back for sure!. Made us feel special. Well done.
Pricey but you get what you pay or in quality food, atmosphere and service.  This is a great special occasion place.

There is a reason you can barely get into this place. The service, the drinks, the food, the ambience is all just amazing! I can't wait to return when I get back to NYC! Try everything! I promise you it's all delicious!

Walked in at the bar right at 5pm on a Saturday. We were able to get seated for a party of 2 at bar in about 10 minutes. The bartenders were all friendly and knowledgeable. We didn't drink that night, but the draft cocktails looked impressive.

We ordered the Beef Tartare, burger, black striped bass and chocolate cake for dessert. The burger and bass were excellent, but the beef tartare really stood it out. It combined raw beef with beets for sweetness and furikake for an umami twist. The chocolate pudding cake was also amazing - it was basically a chocolate lava cake served with vanilla ice cream, pecans and coconut cream

If we were to come again, I would want to try the Citrus & Beets salad and the steak.

Holy foodie dreams come true. I love Tom Colicchio, and this was my first time trying one of his restaurants. Ya'll he is the real deal! My husband and I snagged a spot at the bar for lunch on a Saturday. Every single detail in the space is well thought out, the staff is incredible, and the food is well deserving of its Michelin star. I truly think this is the best burger I've ever had in my life. The meat is so high quality and cooked to juicy perfection. My husband loved the lobster roll special. We're both die hard Connecticut style lobster roll fans, but this one might have converted us. The drinks were also great! I can't wait to come back the next time we're in NYC.

The burger at the Tavern does not disappoint. For years, Minetta Tavern has had my favorite burger in the city. I now have a new favorite.  Also recommended... the beef tartar and the chocolate pudding cake desert.  The service was also impeccable.

Hey Food, what is impeccable. Classic bistro fare in a casual west  village setting.  
Union Square, Café was equally as good and a very similar menu and ambience   I remember going with my friend Don many years ago and it is still in business.  Every dish was flawless and we each had for dishes.
One of my gotos while in NY. Great for sitting at the bar and having a cocktail or for a 7 course tasting. Service is always great, as well as is the decor and neighborhood.

During my team trip to Manhattan I setup our team dinner at Gramercy Tavern and it was an epic feast, with the same all out feel for the events I setup in Vegas. For appetizers we had ROASTED OYSTERS [Celery Root, Horseradish, Lemon], MARKET GREENS SALAD [Snap Peas, Green Garlic, Brown Butter Croutons], GOLDEN BEET SALAD [Pistachios, Sesame, Yogurt], POTATO SOUP [Coconut, Rock Shrimp, Shiitake Mushrooms], and the BEEF TARTARE [Spring Onion, Fried Leeks, Almonds]. I was stoked to finally try the THE TAVERN BURGER [Duck Fat Potato Chips and Smoked Onion Aioli] for my main course, and we sampled all the desserts. I could have eaten a dozen of the BEIGNETS [Rhubarb Compote, Mango Cream] too. Topping this experience off was when the famous Chef Michael Anthony came out to say hello to us! Before he walked away I had to act like my mother and ask him to snap a pic with us. As a foodie, these are the celebrities I dream of meeting. So grateful.
One of my favorites when I get to the city!!!  Don't miss it!  The crispy tuna rise sushi- so many things!!  So many fantastic things on the menu it is hard to choose.

Arguably one of the best dining experiences I've ever had. The food was unbelievably great, the level of hospitality and service from the staff was stellar and the whole atmosphere was perfect. Yes, it was a little pricey, but I'd do it again in a heartbeat. A core memory that I will cherish forever was created after the experience I had here.
All around great New York meal. Drinks perfect and food was perfectly portioned, it didn't look like it was a lot but it was exactly the right amount of food.

Incredible food
Amazing service
Perfect Ambiance

Every time I come to NYC Gramercy is on the list for lunch. Casual and comfortable it is just a classic Tavern. Grill brick chicken is the winner!

the gramercy tavern has been my go-to upscale place for the past couple of years, especially to take out of towners - have always loved their rotating seasonal menus, their desserts and the complimentary bread. the last meal i had here was a bit disappointing though - lukewarm service and the fish was overcooked. the desserts are always on point though, would maybe come back just for those.

Still the king of all burgers, as well as pretty much everything else they do. This past visit, we got the grilled flatbread with three incredible dips (spring onion, garlic with crab, golden beet), the citrus and beets salad, two burgers, and finished with the meyer lemon cake and chocolate chunk cookie. We'd probably skip the lemon cake next time (I liked it but it's not my wife's thing), but the rest was just perfect.
the food was the most over priced crap I have ever had. The staff was very nice. I would never recommend this restaurant to anyone asking for a recommendation in NYC.
Highly recommend! Great atmosphere and food. Get the burger, and don't skip out on dessert!
Not a good place to eat. Over priced sandwiches and salads. This is a 2-3 star restaurant for the gods sake not a 5 star neighborhood gig.

We split a burger, and a salad. I know it's a sin, but we ordered our burger medium. The burger came
out medium rare...I hate sending things back but I was not going to pay $35 for a burger I wasn't going to eat. We did send it back and a medium burger replaced the rarer one. The burger was very good!  They don't have fries but they do have house made chips that were pretty good. Service was great!

Incredibly average and unremarkable, especially at this price point. For $36, the burger could have been from any generic pub. Not much flavor. The $34 cavatelli was also VERY plain, along with being a very small portion. IDK if the kitchen was having a bad night, if the restaurant has gotten complacent, or what. But this food was certainly not up to par. 

We waited ~25 minutes for the bottle of wine we ordered to be delivered to the table. The appetizer (steak tartare) we ordered came and was finished before the wine arrived. 

The cookie for dessert was the best part of the meal. Which is sad for a place with this kind of ranking, hype, and price point.

The Tavern at Gramercy Tavern is better than the Dining Room.  The burger, salad, oysters, cavatelli, chicken, and especially the deserts (lemon cake, chocolate pudding and chocolate chunk cookie) were all wonderful. Striped bass a little tough, probably due to the grilling.  Service was very good. The cocktails were all good - Morning Glory, Pimms at (Gramercy Park) and The Rose were all good as was the nicely priced Kerner white Italian wine.  The Hanabi Lager was good but not worth $72. Service was fine.
Best meal of my life. Not overselling it. Creative menu, fantastic wine list, perfect service. Cannot recommended highly enough.

Michelin star restaurant, we had a great fine dining experience last time we were in NYC before Pandemic, I made a point to come back again to try  some more food. 

Simple but elegant menu, limited selection, superb food but inconsistent service.  Lots of waitstaff without specific assignments, so some confusion and disorganized service. 

Complimentary Lavender citrus drinks were served: tasted like lemonade, fresh and invigorating. 

Fresh and warm bread were served with carrot aioli and butter: probably whole-wheat bread, very good. 

4*MARKET GREENS SALAD
-Cucumbers, Olives, Turnips: fresh and good 

4*ROASTED CAULIFLOWER-Lentils, Pecans, Apples: like cauliflower steak, different and good 

4*SEAFOOD PLATTER: combination of half raw and half cooked seafood. 
3.5*Topneck Clams &- Meyer Lemon*: okay, nothing specical. 
4*Island Creek Oysters &- Caviar*: raw, smooth and very fresh. 
4*Grilled Shrimp &- Kohlrabi: fine and delicious sauce.
4.2*Striped Bass &- Radish*: good combination of texture.  The sauce was a bit salty to me.

4*COFFEE & COOKIES- Chocolate Chip, Palmier, Macaron: unfortunately coffee was not brought out together with cookies. We waited for 10 minutes, and in the end we had to remind waitress. 

4*BROWN BUTTER PISTACHIO CAKE- Cherries, Rose Ice Cream: good but not special. 

Overall, we had better food, service and dining experience last time.
The food, the atmosphere and the service are consistently great. And they have been so for all the years I've gone to and loved this restaurant.
A stable NYC Michelin restaurant. The service, ambience, and food are all incredible. You can order a La cart and skip the tasting menu for a cheaper meal and it is still so lovely

I was super excited to come to Gramercy Tavern (the tavern side), but I have to say I was disappointed.  Our first drink did not arrive until 45 minutes after we were seated.  I ordered a glass if wine to go with my chosen entree and the wine arrived after I finished the entree.  The servers did not seem to notice or care and certainly didn't apologize.  The food was good enough, but the desultory service really marred what I expected to be a terrific evening.  The flowers were really fabulous though.  I would not bother to go back.

Our lunch at the Gramercy Tavern Dining  Room was fabulous from start to finish. Service was exceptional and food and drink are worthy of their Michelin star. Standouts include the seafood platter, seared halibut, pistachio cake and the cheese platter.
A bit noisy but restaurant is very pleasant to view.  Food is diverse but quite tasty.

The food is always excellent at Gamercy Tavern. Enormous wine list by the bottle to select from-$60 to thousands$. Bar staff is great as we always choose to dine at the bar. The persons at the host station are always difficult-we've been many times and they are very uncooperative every time. Once you get beyond them you're golden.
Best nyc dining experience I enjoyed sitting at bar! Enjoy but hard to get reservation

I have had more impressive food and experience at other fine dining and higher-star Michelin restaurants, but this iconic restaurant still stood for expectation. We did a la carte at Tavern area. The ingredients particularly the vegetables and fruits in all dishes were so fresh including the sour cherries in the sundae (not your usual canned cherries) which goes perfectly with any digestivo. I think that's what separates a restaurant like this from usual fine dining. I'm sure their pre-fix are more outstanding.

We came here for our anniversary.  It's been on top 10 restaurant lists forever so we thought to give it a try.  For it's price you are only offered the pri fixe menu.  Service is amazing and of course you feel like dining here is a real treat due to the attention from the servers.  Unfortunately, from the bread to the courses I just wasn't wowed.  We've been to le bernadin and that food is on a different caliber.  They were nice enough to give us a coconut cake for our anniversary which was pretty yummy.  But for the cost to taste ratio, skip this michelin spot
I think this is the best restaurant in the city. Amazing food, wonderful service, great atmosphere. It's a treat to eat here for special occasions.

We sat indoors in the Tavern portion of the restaurant for lunch. Don't let the fact that it's not the formal dining room sway you from visiting. The food here is absolutely phenomenal (and so is the service! Sarah was lovely) It's also very pretty, with quite a bit of real and faux greenery that is a combination from a traditional American pub and a greenhouse. It can be a little loud with everyone talking around you, but the atmosphere music is very low, so it's fairly quiet if you get here early. 

They started us off with a small chilled pea soup and a focaccia. The pea soup was so good, and we were hopeful it was a representation of what was to come. 

I ordered the Grilled Pork Shoulder and my husband ordered the Sea Bass. My meal almost made me cry. It was perfectly cooked, tender and just the right amount of fat. The flavors of the sauces were phenomenal. The sea bass was also perfectly cooked... I completely cleaned my plate, the broccoli was even delicious beyond reason. 

For dessert, we ordered the Farmstead Cheese platter, with various crackers, cheeses, dried fruit, honey, and Marcona almonds. All the components were absolutely superb, with cheeses ranging from very mild to pungent. 

I had entered on my reservation that we were here for our anniversary, and we received a delightful little coconut cake to round out our meal. It was divine, and you could taste the shredded coconut inside. The icing was torched to perfection. 

Definitely make a point to come here. Just ensure you make a reservation first, as it's very popular at all times of the day.

Had lunch over there. I ordered a two-course set lunch. I had a marinated fluke and snowdance farm chicken with lentils, rhubarb, snow peas. Both dishes were amazingly prepared, especially the chicken. The fluke was very fresh though I wish there were a tiny bit more seasoning with some salt/pepper/citrus to bring out the flavor more, and the chicken was one of the most delicious chicken I've had in my life -- perfectly cooked, very flavorful with crispy skin on the outside, and tender, juicy and perfectly seasoned meat on the inside. Staff was very friendly and nice. The wait was a bit long between the courses but I guess it was worth the wait. Wait go back again.

The duck fat chips and Tavern burger would be my death row meal. The only thing better was the service. Go eat there and thank me later. Actually, you know what - just thank me now - you won't regret it.

Bravo! Everything was perfection. I took folks here for a business lunch, and it was superb.  I look forward to returning!  The raw fluke appetizer, seafood sampler plate and chocolate mousse dessert were divine!

It's been a while since we were last here and decided to come back for our 10 year anniversary. Enjoyed the meal but it wasn't the same mind blowing experience as last time. The prices went up, which is to be expected given inflation and such. But the experience was not the same, almost everything was good but nothing really blew me away. And there was one dish - the halibut that was seriously over cooked. In the past they always had something that really was amazing like a lobster salad or scallop, this time I didn't really get that feeling. So we had the following from the 5 course tasting menu (sharing some dishes so we could try more than just 5 items - one benefit of being married) :
1st course: marinated fluke and sugar snap peas
2nd: pork tortellini and gnocchi
3rd: halibut 
4th : duck breast and sea bass 
5: pistachio cake and chocolate mousse 

So we tried 9 out of the 11 course options (sea bass wasnt on the menu but replaced lamb since wife doesn't eat red meat). For $168 per person, I would have expected to be blown away at least once or twice out of 9 dishes, which last time I was blown away by multiple dishes... It just didn't feel the same. Even the bread at the beginning was just plain wheat rolls. Something is missing, but for a meal that easily costs over $400 for a couple (with tax and tip and drinks, actually almost $500) it should have been more memorable. There was nothing interesting or special, the duck was great but was small (but I was stuffed after the meal so maybe a moot point)

Gramercy Tavern is legendary & there's no doubt why.
I specifically tried their vegetarian menu to see if they work up the same magic as their inventive meat dishes. 
From the delightfully addictive butter rolls, followed by Sugar snap peas, Hay smoked Gnocchi, Norwich meadows Freekeh, Brown butter pistachio cake & Dark chocolate mousse- everything was impeccable and tasted delicious! 
Particularly I loved the Gnocchi that was pillowy soft and sat on a bed of pesto like puree along with that charred Broccolini, Mushrooms & beautifully contrasted flavors of the Chilli oil. 
The balance of flavors, the choice of fresh seasonal ingredients, and elegance of presentation made it a remarkable 5 course experience. 
Service is on point as expected at a high end restaurant. The ambiance though is rather relaxed, no dress code per se but you'd usually wanna look neat. 
GT again proves what great food can make you feel. I happily signed off that cheque :)

Came back and ordered the burger. It was fantastic - highly recommend. Unfortunately, the chips it came with were soggy but the burger more than made up for it. Also enjoyed the Pinot. Will definitely be back again!

Stellar perfect classic NY lunch spot.
Service matches delicious epicurean choices.
Highly recommend

Gramercy Tavern is legendary for a reason.  The full service restaurant is one of the best experiences you can have in NYC; the servers are attentive and willing to modify menu items easily to fit your desires.  This is by far one of the coolest spaces in NYC and a place I go back to frequently for the tavern menu.

Sometimes I think that I write too many five star reviews, but then I remember that I research the sh*t out of restaurants before I decide to make a reservation, so I like the believe that my process of deliberation is a great one. In any case, I finally made it to Gramercy Tavern after being on Yelp for something like eight years at this point. It's always been on my radar but I never prioritized it. However, we got a Union Square Hospitality gift card last year for a solid amount, so we decided to apply it to a meal at Gramercy Tavern. It didn't cover the whole meal, but it made a dent. In any case, we decided to go the Dining Room portion of the restaurant to get the full experience, and we were not disappointed. The service was on point, the beverages were well curated and the food was as good as it gets. A beautiful variety of proteins, ingredients, preparations, etc., and it was the perfect amount of food. They have the details down to a T. I'd expect nothing less from a Michelin-starred restaurant that's been open for two decades. 

Came here at 8:15 on a Saturday night. As I'm sure everyone knows already, Gramercy Tavern is split into the more casual (and a la carte) Tavern half (at the front of the space), and the Dining Room half, which is more upscale and is pre fixe. I was torn between the options, but ultimately I wanted the full Gramercy Tavern experience so I opted for the more luxe version. Though the Tavern is a relatively more down to earth vibe, I didn't find the Dining Room stuffy in the slightest. Sometimes these storied restaurants are too buttoned up for me, but Gramercy Tavern manages not to be pretentious at all despite the price tag of the menu. 

There is a wine pairing option, but for drinks we each went with one cocktail and one glass of wine. Despite my general distaste for vodka, I ended up starting with the Rose martini because I get classic gin martinis all the time. It's not currently on the online menu but I remember it had rose vodka, Lillet rose and Velvet Falernum. Floral and subtly sweet. A great drink, even for the vodka-cautious among us. My husband got their twist on a French 75 which was solid. For wine, my husband got a Nebbiolo and I got an incredibly delicious, Riesling-style (but not a Riesling) white wine. I'm considering calling the restaurant to get the label information because I must have a bottle.

Food-wise, it's a pre fixe menu with two options per category. If you're an adventurous party of two, I highly recommend just ordering one of each of everything and splitting it all. That's always the benefiting of pre fixe versus tasting. The only thing we got two of was the halibut, because I didn't want freekeh after pasta. While the food isn't necessarily super creative and adventurous, it is pristine and perfectly executed. Eats, below:

Marinated Fluke w/ Cucumbers, Daikon, Kombu: A-
The only somewhat boring dish of the night but it was still solid. The fish was super fresh and paired nicely with all of the delicate flavors of the other ingredients. 

Sugar Snap Peas w/ Radish, Pistachio, Burrata: A
How could this tiny little plate of veggies be so great?! Remarkable, really. 

Hay Smoked Gnocchi w/ Broccolini, Mushrooms, Chili: A+
Somehow I missed photographing the pasta course but I can vouch for its beauty and flavor profile. This was rich, earthy, and delicious.

Pork Tortellini w/ Bok Choy, Celery, Lemon Thyme: A+
I loved how different this dish was from the gnocchi, lots of variety here. More of an Asian-inspired dish, with an earthy, vegetal broth and yummy, dumpling-esque tortellini.

Pan Seared Halibut w/ Fava Beans, Turnips, Lemon: A
Just a simple and delicious, silky piece of fish.

Roasted Duck Breast and Confit w/ Lentils, Rhubarb, Snow Peas: A+
We agreed that this was one of the most perfectly executed duck dishes we've ever had. That's saying a lot, because duck happens to be our shared favorite protein of choice. Juicy and rich, seasonal accompaniments, and I loved the little bits of confit to complement the breast. 

Lamb w/ Sweet Potatoes, Walnuts, Chicory: A+
I've never been too into lamb, something about the flavor of the meat, but this dish was just more expert execution and it was gorgeously presented. 

Brown Butter Pistachio Cake w/ Cherries, Rose Ice Cream: A+
Despite being partial to chocolate desserts, this was easily the better sweet treat of the night. The cake was just decadent thanks to the brown butter, and the ice cream was light and floral, a perfect accompaniment. 

Dark Chocolate Mousse w/ Passion Fruit, Coconut Ice Cream: A
My husband doesn't like coconut so that was a disappointment for him, but the mousse itself was rich and delicious, and it paired beautifully with the passionfruit puree.
Classic. Classy. A true New York staple! Don't miss the chance to check it out. From decor to ambiance to food and cocktails. Amazing place.

This is s tough one, first of all this review is based on one visit with my mother, so I didn't exactly try everything on the menu. But everything taken into account both my mother and I felt it wildly overrated. Portions (except for desserts) were extremely small, everything seemed stingy in fact, the bread parceled out in precious plates of two buns at a time, not exactly Christmas. The seafood plate was unglamorous in the extreme, it's presentation mediocre. My mother's main course was similarly spartan. Meanwhile prices were extremely high, cocktails and wine about twenty dollars for instance. The food wasn't that memorable. The restaurant isn't that comfortable either, noisy and cramped due to the spacing of the tables. More of a tourist destination than a comfortable place to hang. We were even seated late for our reservation, and from the seating and the fact that our reservation was made weeks in advance, that they are cramming as many covers in as they can as fast as they can, was clear. 

Now, balanced against all these criticisms was warm and unpretentious service, from the host to our waitress. They asked us how we liked things and I noted everything was stingy and they wanted to comp us anything on the menu. We refused but they still brought an extra dessert. And it wasn't served with a bit of attitude either they meant it as an apology.

I am probably being a little harsh because of this restaurant's inflated reputation. But a similar restaurant back in Philly avoids all these missteps with generous portions, and a general feel of largesse, with the same warm service (Parc). So your call.

My husband and I celebrated our wedding anniversary at Gramercy Tavern and it is absolutely something that I wouldn't mind doing year after year. 

First off, the service. From the moment we walked in to the moment we left, the whole staff new we were celebrating and continued to congratulate us. They absolutely knew how to make us feel special. My face hurt I was smiling so much! All of the staff was so attentive and just on it. I just loved all of them so much!!! Our server was charming and you could tell that he enjoyed his job! We just loved him! 

The food-WOW!!! From the warm bread to the gnocchi to the chocolate cake, my husband planned out tasting menus so we tried almost everything!! It was all divine. It all made us want to come back again and again!!! 

I want to call out special attention to the special coconut cake that the restaurant prepared foe us. It was too special and just too perfect. We were blown away and loved every single bite!!!

Lastly, the ambiance. What a spectacular warm and gorgeous space! My seat looked into the tavern and I just loved being a part of the fine dining room and getting to observe the on goings of the bar and the Tavern! 

Gramercy Tavern, thank you for making our anniversary absolutely an evening to remember. We are grateful :)

Great food, good service and amazing atmosphere!
Located in one of the best city locations
amazing atmosphere, menu, and service. i always take visitors here because they don't miss!! inside, outside, and bar are all worth going for.

This is for the dining room- Ambiance is outdated. Food is surprisingly bland. And the wait time between each dish was about 20 minutes. The meat dishes that came out weren't hot, but rather lukewarm like they had been sitting out waiting for a while. The 5 course meal for two people + 2 drinks with tax and tip was a little over $400. We went for my birthday dinner and we were overall very disappointed. Even the desserts were bad. This is absolutely an overhyped experience. Save yourself the time and money! Giving two stars for the kind and friendly staff and the dish presentation.

A classic New York institution, Gramercy Tavern offers a warm and inviting dining experience. The restaurant, led by Chef Michael Anthony, is renowned for its New American cuisine that draws heavily from seasonal, local produce.

The menu is an ode to New York's agricultural bounty. The Duck Breast with Brussels Sprouts and Concord Grapes, for instance, is a perfect example of Chef Anthony's approach - seasonal, flavorful, and executed with finesse.

The restaurant's décor is timeless. With its rustic tavern setting, floral arrangements, and murals, Gramercy Tavern exudes a warm and cozy ambiance that's welcoming and unpretentious.

The service is professional yet friendly, with staff who are attentive, personable, and genuinely passionate about providing an exceptional dining experience. From dish explanations to wine recommendations, the service team adds a personal touch to every aspect of the dining experience.

Absolutely lives up to its reputation!!
Best meal we had in NYC. Perfect place for lunch.

We had the tasting menu with the wine pairing. Our entire party enjoyed every bite.  The halibut really stood out but it would be hard to commit to a favorite. 

Our server Caroline was first rate. She was very quick and entertaining.

We ate in the dining which provided a very nice ambiance. Very quite. We could speak to each other easily. Everything was very comfortable and spotless clean.

To put it simply - Gramercy Tavern delivers on everything that you would expect while dining at a Michelin starred restaurant.

The service was attentive, it had a comfortable ambiance, and of course the food was ridiculously good. 

We ordered one of each on the menu to try as many dishes as possible (besides we both ordered the halibut). 

Also, great after-work bar.
Has been amazing for a long time. Excellent food and atmosphere. Perfect date place! The menu will excite you.

Honestly, the best food I have ever eaten. Their mushroom ravioli is to die for. My husband and I visited for a weekend getaway and were very well pleased. If we didn't leave a good 3 hours away, we'd be eating there regularly.
Neat little place, little dark inside but fairly cozy.  UK pub type of vibe for sure.

NYC RESTAURANT WEEK HAS ARRIVED!! We're starting off strong with a delicious lunch at the well-known Gramercy Tavern Dining Room. It was a 3-course, $60 lunch menu. I would recommend going with the market salad as your appetizer, the chicken as your main, and the cheese platter as your dessert (trust me it just works). FYI: the bread they give u at the start is just phenomenal. 

The staff was nice and all the dishes were good in their own way. I'd love to go back and explore the tavern portion of the restaurant!

Pictured: bread, cucumber carrot salad, seared halibut, chicken, cheese platter, chocolate cream pie

Great food and cocktails. Pricey but delicious

Always wonderful when I'm in the neighborhood

Highly recommend!!! The food is delicious. Some highlights include: the seafood tower, the steak tartare, and the burger. The service was wonderful and attentive, and I was given free cavier on my seafood tower.

Shoutout restaurant week for the great deals - especially for this gem. My friends and I had the pleasure of dining at Gramercy Tavern for lunch. They were doing a 3 course fixed menu with great options and I am super excited. We started with the Beef tartar and fluke - let me just say this is the best beef tartar ive ever had - absolutely delicious!!! for the main i ordered the chicken which i typically dont go for but the chicken lentil rhubarb combo was excellent - the chicken was so juicy and the lentils were very savory. the dessert i chose was cookies which i was expecting something different but the 3 different cookie combos were great especially the coconut. 10/10 recommend!!

This burger may have been $35 but sometimes you really do get what you pay for! It was perfectly cooked and full of flavor. The side of smoked onion aioli and duck fat potato chips were the perfect complements. Service was great and drinks were good too!

I've had Gramercy Tavern on the top of my to try list for a long time, and we were finally able to try it! I got reservations for lunch at the Tavern side, we lucked out on the weather and sat outside. 

The staff is unbelievably classy and professional. We were seated immediately and given menus. The outside table is shaded and really nice. Even though we were outside, they have 2 wait staff out there at all time, making sure we have everything. Our water glasses were never empty. And we were chugging water, so it was really impressive and appreciated. 

We ordered the roasted oysters, the seabass, the Tavern burger (medium), and the duck meatloaf. The food came out pretty quickly, and it was beyond what we expected. The sauce the seabass came with was incredibly flavorful. I switched to using a spoon instead so I could scoop up as much sauce as possible with each bite of fish. The burger was delicious, a little rarer then medium, but still so so good. The duck fat chips it came with dipped into the aioli was *chefs kiss*. Our favorite dish was the duck meatloaf. So much flavor. The peaches and bread (somewhat of a panzanella salad?) Worked so well with the duck meatloaf too. I would order that again in a heart beat. 

We had a fill day of food so skipped out on dessert. But I have a good indication it would be very very good. I would definitely come back next time I'm in the city. And aim to do the tasting menu on the dining room side.

Ok so this is a five star place but I would say when you take into account the price tag, the value is not really up to par with some other Michelin spots in nyc. We sat in the dining room and did the full tasting menu.


I liked the...
Burrata salad
Gnocchi 
Chocolate cake desert
Freshly made bread 
Halibut 

I was slightly disappointed by...
The steak
The very small wine pours :)

What an incredible dining experience at the Gramercy Tavern! Here is a breakdown of what we ordered:

- Gramercy Tavern Burger: we had to try the famed Gramercy tavern burger and it didn't disappoint! The burger came with white cheddar, bacon, and a side of smoked onion aioli. The burger was so flavorful and you could immediately tell the quality of the beef. I have never had a burger like that, and I'd rank it at the top of the burgers I've tried! The burger is served with duck fat potato chips which were insanely good!

-Matcha Panna Cotta: for dessert we got the matcha Panna cotta. The dish was delicious, and not overly sweet. The dish is served with a blueberries and an almond biscotti

-Sagamore Hill cocktail: this cocktail was so good! This cocktail had clarified milk, which was very unique and interesting to me. This cocktail really shined. 

Overall, there is no doubt why Gramercy tavern has a Michelin star. The service was impeccable and our waiter had incredible recommendations. Highly recommend this restaurant

Went for our anniversary, which was mentioned in our reservation but nothing was done to acknowledge it.
Had the five course tasting menu. One item was outstanding, two were very good and two were unremarkable.
Service was professional but perfunctory and impersonal.
There are many other choices for special occasions so we will never be back.

First time visiting NYC and had the measure of meeting Ryan behind the bar! Ordered the Golden Hour Specialty cocktail along with the Tavern burger and absolutely loved it! Very special evening and much appreciated cheers to Gramercy as well as Ryan! Don't overlook this devious gem and impeccable service!

This was such a great lunch! For our first stop in NYC my boyfriend and I came here and got their prix fixe green market menu. Each item was made perfectly and the ingredients all tasted so fresh. My favorite dish was the hiramasa with jalapeños, it had such unique and refreshing flavors. We also loved the bread service, it had a carrot sauce that we couldn't get enough of. 
Our waitress was so nice and she put pretty flowers on my birthday dessert which was a coconut meringue cake, it was so pretty and tasted delicious.
Excellent good. We tried the duck meatloaf.. who would think? Everything we tried was excellent and so was the service

I have been to the Gramercy Tavern a handful of times during the years. It was the first place my family decided to go after the height of the pandemic ended. It is truly a gem. The food is creative, some of the best I have had the pleasure of eating. They are very accommodating regarding food preferences and have many vegetarian options. The atmosphere is lively without being loud. And the service is I think where they truly standout out. The wait staff is outstanding,  extremely attentive without intrusive.  They do it all. One of the guests at at my table last night broke the heal of her sandal. One of the staff actually fixed it! Thank you all for hanging in there through many challenges in the restaurant industry over the years! Truly special!

Green salad was not fresh with stale corn chips and very spicy dressing
When ask to replace it they brought green leaves with drops of olive oil - called it salad
Wine by glass choice is very poor -one bottle of sauvignon blanc and that's it
This restaurant takes the cake when it comes to food presentation. Excellent options and a great fine dining location. I will be back soon!
So spot on for so many years that it doesn't need another review. Just go but be prepared to pay a high price for the highest quality. A special place for a special date.

Great ambiance! I booked 30 days in advance to get a prime dinner time for a small group for my friend's birthday. We had a fabulous time here, drinking bubbles throughout. Note that they take the bottle away between pours, something that my friend was not a fan of, but were very attentive and made sure our glasses were never empty. We shared the flatbread and dips to start  and I had the famous tavern burger. While it was a delicious, high quality burger and very good, I actually don't rank it as one of the best in the city. To be honest I wasn't blown away by the food here in general (don't get me wrong, it was very good, but perhaps my expectations were just too high) but I did love the ambiance and vibe.

Food, service, and ambiance deserve only an average rating at best.   My first time in NY.  Price is high for the food!   Not worth coming to..
My room service from DoorDash is more worthwhile.   I won't recommend or coming here again.

I absolutely love Gramercy Tavern and come whenever I am in NYC, by far my favorite "foodie"
Restaurant!! 

Our server, Amanda, was so helpful with suggestions on food and wine, she is the ultimate professional and top notch customer service, just felt she made our dinner the Best Experience Ever!! We were celebrating my daughter's birthday and her official move to her first apartment in NYC and Amanda made sure our night was perfect!! 

We had the cucumber soup, hard to describe how amazing a chilled soup could be- you MUST order it!! Then we had beef tartare-quite spectacular! Then  mains were sea bass and cavatelli, both excellent!!

Each item was beautifully plated, with layers of flavors that just all melded into an absolute pleasure on the palate. The ingredients felt Like they were fresh picked from a garden a minute before preparing, everything just bursting with flavor!!

Thank you Amanda for giving us an amazing evening and as always, we will return!!!!

Of note, we Loved the friendly kind professional Hostess and in the past had a fabulous bartender that was top notch- saw him working last night but not sure of his name- a great mixologist who has been there for many years and is excellent at his craft!

Lovely food and amazing service. Yes the prices are extremely high, but the food is great quality. Minus 1 star for the sheer amount of salt they added to the food. The cucumber soup I had to send back because the salt level made me gag. The bread was over salted too, and even my chicken was salty and the skin had fat on it and was soggy.
Excellent food.  Great services.  Good wine. Great atmosphere.   Their Bordeaux is one of the best I ever had.

So I tried this restaurant based on the recommendations of a local New Yorker. The ambiance gives the essence of a tavern with the rustic decor, rudimentary lighting, and shades of tan apparel but feels much like a commercialized quasi-tavern built for Disney World verses the aged home grown feel of a true English tavern. The service was spectacular and the delivery of the food perfectly timed. Several of the dishes were bursting with micro flavors while one of the meat dishes left more to be desired. Overall, I would recommend but certainly not my favorite.
Best kept secret in NY. We've been going here for many years. Excellent food and as important friendly, personal service. We're headed here again next week.
Just splendid. I've been here for lunch and for a private party. It's just elegant to the max. Fabulous !
It's been awhile since I went to Gramercy Tavern but I remember enjoying their chicken consomme, the managers are very nice and accommodating. A good spot for a little splurge!
Had the seasonal dinner menu here and ate the best gnocchi I've ever had! The rest of the dishes were good.

I have a confession to make - with small kids, I am always on the lookout for fancy restaurants that are kid friendly.  How I assess if a given fancy restaurant is kid friendly is not by looking for the "good for kids" tag (because very, very few fancy restaurants will have this tag) but rather by manually searching the yelp reviews for certain keywords such as "kid" and "toddler" and "baby".  By doing this, I have realized that a lot of people use the words, "I kid you not" in their reviews.  But I have also stumbled upon gems like Gramercy Tavern.

Anyways.  The Tavern at Gramercy Tavern is kid friendly.  Toddler friendly.  Baby friendly!  The Restaurant is not so kid friendly.  We brought a 20 month old and a 3 year old.  We sat in the tavern, by the bar.  The atmosphere in the tavern is loud and casual with music playing and nobody gave us any looks.  

The food was amazing, but be careful ordering the cavatelli pasta for the kids (order the plain butter pasta on the secret kids menu instead).  The cavatelli pasta, while delicious, is green.  We also had the duck burger and the grilled pork shoulder.  Both were very flavorful.  Our 20 month old loved the pork shoulder.  We had the donuts for dessert, which paired well with the sweet raspberry sauce.

The service was impeccable as you would expect from a michelin-starred restaurant.  Our toddler nearly knocked over the table at one point and the waitstaff was there in a blink of an eye to clean up fallen silverware and towels (no food, luckily).
