I came to Gramercy Tavern for lunch with a group of 5 after making a reservation. We got a 3-course tasting with drink pairings. I had a ceviche-like appetizer and halibut for my main course, with the cookies and cappuccino at the end of the meal. The wine pairings were excellent as were my appetizer and entre. The appetizer was probably my favorite course, so light and refreshing. The cookie dessert came with two other pastries, but the cookie was the best one (but not as up to par as the appetizer and halibut). The service was great and attentive. 

This was the first time I went to a location with one Michelin star where I wasn't still thinking about the meal after I had left. Maybe I ordered the wrong things or maybe I should be back to try again for dinner. The only dish I really was still thinking about when I had left was that delish appetizer.

We had a great time at Gramercy Tavern! Great service, wonderful interior and delicious food! We had reservations and were seated promptly, and enjoyed cocktails (delicious and not lacking of alcohol) and focaccia while waiting for our food. The Grilled Zucchini was substantial and tasted great. Sea Bass, Brick Pressed Chicken, and the Tavern Burger did not disappoint. We all shared 3 desserts: the Cinnamon Sugar Doughnuts (tough and disappointing), Peach Tart Tatin (wonderful) and the Lemon Poppy Shortcake (the best one we ordered - I could've eaten more shortcake if I had it).
Great spot in the city and we ate in the Tavern, buzzing and lively location.  Very happy to return on our next trip.
A great place with a good atmosphere and delicious food. I recommend it for visiting with friends or family.

Went here for lunch -- maybe that was the mistake? Everything except for delicious was just alright .. tasty but nothing to write home about. That being said the dessert tart was absolutely pretty and delicuous

Gramercy Tavern
As long time fans of The Bar Room at The Modern and USC, friends and I met for impromptu drinks and bites after work. On a Wednesday evening, Gramercy Tavern  was JAMMED.  The host was utterly accommodating, as were the polished servers. Such lovely service despite the very lively bar crowd. Soon after, we returned for a delightful 3 course Market Lunch on a Saturday. The green salad and gazpacho appetizers were fresh and tasty. The halibut and polenta entrees were perfectly prepared and delicious.   The elevated chocolate cream pie was decadently scrumptious.  The cheese course  was very well curated and plated.  Special gluten free muffins and crackers were yummy and thoughtfully served.  Both the Tavern and dining room are so civilized and inviting.  In addition to the lovely ambiance and deliciously well executed food, the service is warm, polite, attentive and IMPECCABLY experienced and polished.  Both the hosts and our utterly knowledgeable and outstanding server (Cameron) added to the truly wonderful experience.  Whether you're in the mood for a casual bite and drink in The Tavern, or a lovely meal in The Dining Room, Gramercy Tavern is a NYC restaurant essential!

I went here for New Year's last year and let me tell you it was an awful experience. Waiters were clearly too busy for us. I would not go back even if they paid me. I tried to talk to them about this and they did try to explain which I appreciate.

Visited for a special occasion dinner. The food was fantastic - it's a 5-course prix fixe, but there is some optionality and they were accommodating to allergies etc. All very strong, but the desserts were stand-out. I ordered the wine pairing as well. I do not know much about wine, but the sommelier seemed like he knew his stuff. Our server, Carolyn, and the rest of the staff were really attentive and friendly as well.

I always go out of my way to dine at the Gramercy Tavern whenever I visit NYC. The ambiance, food, and service are top shelf. It's fancy without being pretentious. Always delightful and worth every penny.

Had always wanted to try the Gramercy Tavern. Finally had my chance on this trip to New York City. Sat in the bar side on a Sunday prior to the theater. Most of us ordered burgers and one ordered another entrée. Good starters brought to the table along with drinks. Trouble was with the entrées.

We were seated near the grill that was putting out all of the burgers and other grilled foods. About 10 minutes  after our appetizers were cleared, I saw the sous chef, cut and plate two of the three burgers. He put them up on the service counter (no heat lamps), where they waited for what seemed like 7 to 10 minutes before they were joined by the third burger and the final entrée before being brought to the table. My burger was warm. I should've said something, but not wanting to raise a ruckus I didn't.

A real disappointment, after years of waiting.

The four of us went here for dinner last minute. Couldn't get a reservation in the Dining Room so we opted to dine in their Tavern. No white table cloth, more of a casual dining experience compared to their Dining Room. You can literally see their dining room from the tavern side as there are no barriers. At 6:30pm when we got there the place was bustling and high energy. We were apologetic as we were coming from moving my son into his dorm and we were dressed very casually. My husband was wearing his golf shorts (gasp!) and feeling really underdressed before getting there but unfortunately we had no time to stop by our hotel to change! :( I apologized for our attire when we got there and the hostess was so gracious and said we looked fabulous as we are! We were seated promptly at a nice table by the open kitchen and that smaller open kitchen were in charge of making all the appetizers. 

What we ate:
*Beef Tartare - pine nuts, nasturtium, Dijon. Very fresh, firm, vibrant flavor. Excellent!
*Duck liver mousse - Grapes, pickles, grilled bread. As good as liver mousse can be!
*The Tavern burger - served with duck fat potato chips, smoked onion and aioli. We ordered medium rare and it was as ordered. Shown in picture cut in half. Burger was juicy and succulent. Very good.
*Grilled zucchini - served with barley, tomatoes, and walnuts. Healthy and delicious
*Sea bass - served with caraflex cabbage, tomatoes, Ancho chili. Well executed.
*Pork chop - I didn't taste, but was told that it was a little on a tough side
*Desserts - we ordered three and I forget what they were exactly, but they were all delicious. :D

Gramercy Tavern is one of those classic landmark type of restaurant that you must go and try once. Service overall was very good and vibe was energetic. Lots of people celebrating one thing or another so I'm thinking it's a special place. I have nothing to complain about and if my friend were to invite me to dine here again, I would be happy to return.

I have been here numerous times for their seasonal tasting menu. Really love that this place manages to hit that sweet spot between casual and fine dining. Highly recommend for a casual date night with the significant other.

The Tavern is the first among our favorite New York restaurants. From the moment you arrive at the podium to your way out the door, you are in the hands of a superb team of professionals so good at what they do, they made a special evening out of one begun with some seriously disappointing theatre. It happens sometimes. The Gramercy Tavern never disappoints.
A long lived great eating institution.  Eaten many meals here through the years.  Always consistently solid.  Tradition American.

I always loved coming to Gramercy Tavern. It's a cozy restaurant with a nice crowd thats located in Gramercy. The bar is usually crowded and like sitting at their bar. The bartenders are very professional and friendly and they are very attentive which is nice. Theres not a lot of food options on the menu, and there is no brunch menu, but the options are good to chose from.

We started with the oysters which were good. They had corn and a sauce on top, so I didn't really know what to expect. The corn does take over most of the flavor of the oysters, but its a really different dish and I would recommend trying it.

The burger was recommended as one of the best burgers in the city. I ordered it medium, but unfortunately it came out well done. They immediately put an order in to re-cook the burger and when it came back it was still cooked a little longer than I Liked. The burger was good, but it wasn't as juicy as I had envisioned and even though the bread was fresh, it had a somewhat stale texture which was a little weird. I don't really know how to describe the bun. The burger was good, but to be honest, I've had better. The chips on the side were good.

I was offered a mimosa for the wait between the burger and I will say the mimosa was very good. I would defiantly order a mimosa again.

I've been trying to get a reservation at Gramercy Tavern's Tavern section, and for the better part of a year, there hasn't been anything available except for the super early 5PM table which usually isn't in very high demand. I had to settle for 5:30PM as I knew if I kept waiting I probably wouldn't get that 6:30-7:30PM sweet spot anytime soon.

Our waitress, Kimberly, was extremely friendly and attentive. We received menus immediately, along with a wine book (not menu). I have been dying to try their famous burger everyone raves about, so we opted for two Tavern Burgers cooked at a medium temperature. 

The burger came with some duck fat potato chips, which were actually really good. I finished them before even trying my burger. The burger comes already cut in half, with bacon and cheddar cheese. I took a bite and it was delicious. Juicy, seasoned, flavorful. Is it worth not being able to get a reservation for almost a year? I wouldn't say so. But I'm not mad that I had it. 

For dessert, we ordered the apple cider doughnuts. These were great! They're served warm on a bed of cream and some kind of apple sauce. They're not too sweet, and perfect to share. 

I would definitely return, but I think I might just get a seat at the bar, as it looked like a much more fun place to be.

I was in the mood for a beefy burger for my birthday, so I came to The Gramercy Tavern.  The website says that their Tavern Burger is chopped
there daily and is a 70/30 mixture of chuck and brisket.

It was tender and juicy.  I ordered it medium rare with white cheddar cheese on top and bacon on the side.

For dessert, I had the Fig Upside-Down Cake with fig sorbet and spiced red wine sauce.  The creaminess of the sorbet balanced out the sweetness of the cake.  I devoured the whole dessert.  It was that good.

The food and drink menus are creative and offer plenty of choices.  I highly recommend The Gramercy Tavern.

I went to the formal dining room at the Gramercy Tavern years ago but haven't had the opportunity to go back until this past month. What I originally remembered was solid food and spectacular service in an elegant environment. I am happy to announce that all of this still applies to this classic NYC restaurant.

You walk in and are immediately greeted warmly by the hosts. You are then accompanied through the lively Tavern area (always crowded, in a good way) into the quieter and more formal dining room. Dinner service is a five course seasonal menu. You can pick from two choices per course. They also have some add-ons, which that night was a raw seafood platter that my friends and I indulged in. I enjoyed everything that I tried for dinner that night. The standout for me was probably the corn agnolotti, which was just perfectly cooked and packed with delicious corn-forward flavor. While the menu and food may not be the most exciting in the city, everything is technically prepared well and tastes good. I can't complain. And of course, service is incredible --- friendly and attentive without being overbearing --- as you might expect from a Danny Meyer restaurant.

Overall, I don't think you can go wrong eating at Gramercy Tavern. It's a NYC classic for a reason.

Please note this is a review of the dining room, not the tavern area (which is also very good but a very different experience).

One hundred stars, if I could. The best culinary and service experience of my life. From the minute I got to the bar, Benny took care of me. He constructed the best Big Sur cocktail (fig leaf, almond, tequila and nutmeg). After two of those, I saw they carried a rare gin that I love (Condessa prickly pear). I asked him to surprise me with a Condessa cocktail, and he made the best mojito I've ever had. The roasted oysters with sweet corn were delectable, and the burger was hands down the best burger I've ever tasted. The Gramercy Tavern is a must!

Quick seating at the bar before the workday ended. Cozy atmosphere. Very friendly and attentive bartenders. Got an old fashioned and a seasonal fall cocktail. Delicious! Ended up getting the tavern burger, which comes with fries and aioli. Tasty! Treated myself to some dessert as well. Scrumptious! Absolutely recommend if you don't mind spending some change.

Amazing experience for brunch. Would definitely come back and a reason why it's a Michelin star. They are a seasonal restaurant so they dress up their decor to the season. We went in the fall and they had beautiful foliage, flowers, and artwork to get you in the fall mood along with an evolving fall menu with fall veggies. 

A tip is that the tavern side is more casual whereas the dining room is a prifixe. You will want to make sure you book the right one. The tavern is the Michelin rated one. However, if you don't have a reservation the trick is to go right when they open and grab a bar seat. They probably have about 15-20 seats at the bar. We went about 5-10 mins before they opened and we were the second party to grab a table at the bar. 

My NYC friends told me I had to have the burger and the cookie and they of course were amazing. One of the best burgers and cookies I've had. We also got the squash soup which was incredible and the duck liver mousse, also good but pretty standard as you would get at other restaurants. The guests next to us got the oysters and we had dish envy. 

The service was great, servers were friendly and knowledgeable. The only miss was that we said it was my birthday but they didn't do anything for us, maybe because we sat at the bar although we saw other guests getting a birthday surprise. Oh well! I will still give them a 5 of 5 overall.

Absolutely incredible service - went above and beyond for us. I loved the decor, the food selections were seasonal selections and delicious. They really mean it when they say above and beyond hospitality. I had ordered two course and my partner ordered three courses. They gave us both three courses and gave us a free champagne because it was our anniversary. We had such a delightful experience as out of town guests and can't wait to be back there next time we are in NYC.

This breaks my heart to give this famous establishment only 3 stars. I have their cookbook and when we decided to visit NY, I thought we should absolutely make this restaurant a priority stop. Unfortunately out of the 7 restaurants we visited this was in the bottom 6 or 7. 
Listen the food is not bad. It just feels like you are in a private country club that is catering to a bunch of business people who are there to network or are on a business trip. The decor reflects that as well. It feels outdated.

Finally tried this place after years of wanting to go. The waitstaff was really nice and attentive but not pretentious. Atmosphere is casual and very pretty french cottage style.  Started with some cocktails, I thought they were very just average, I was expecting something fresher and more innovative.  Got the 6 course tasting menu plus a seafood platter special. The seafood platter was one of my favorite things we ordered, my very favorite was the halibut! Everything was very good, some more amazing then others but overall a very delicious meal. We didn't get the wine pairing but after the meal we regretted not getting it. The only big disappointment was the desserts, considering they were like $50 each we were unimpressed with both of them and is why I am giving this place 4 stars instead of 5. The chocolate mouse was very dry and it said with passion fruit but I could barely taste it. The other one, I can hardly remember it, tasted like a granola bar. Next time I go I will ask if I can substitute the dessert for another order of Halibut, hahahahaha!

Enjoy every visit to Gramercy Tavern. Service is as fantastic as the food.

On most recent visit enjoyed the duck liver mousse, oysters, pork shoulder, and duck meatloaf. All were executed well. Duck meatloaf is divine. Really rich with a lot of umami flavor.

Finished with the chocolate pudding cake and a complimentary cake.

Our lunch at the Gramercy Tavern Dining Room was fabulous from start to finish. Service was exceptional and food and drink are worthy of their Michelin star. Standouts include the seafood platter, seared halibut, pistachio cake and the cheese platter.
Food was excellent.   Seven coarse meal delicious.   It was a full evening, no hurry to changeover the table so it was a long meal.  Be prepared to stay awhile.
Fantastic food and service. Everything was superb. We were here for our wedding anniversary and the staff couldn't do enough. The food was really delicious and the wine was also great.

FOOD & DRINKS: Absolutely loved every single dish on the Thanksgiving Menu which included a starter, main, and dessert. The squash lumache and the braised beef were such wholesome dishes. The flavor profile of each dish was perfectly curated and has depth to every bite. The gingerbread was super moist and the pumpkin pie was so fragrant. Overall a fulfilling meal meant to tingle every taste bud. The cocktail list had a great selection and the Sweet Potato Sour was my favorite. This place is truly a gem.

AMBIANCE: The most charming interior decor for fall. From the front of the restaurant all the way to the back, there are festive items intricately placed that warp you from the city streets into a cozy home. 

SERVICE: Attentive staff easy to carry a conversation with.

The Gramery Tavern is beautiful inside and the drinks are great. The food is average and so is the service. Definitely get the burger, but the chips that come with it are fine. The seafood plate is extremely overpriced for the amount of seafood you get. You're basically paying $52 for 4 oysters and 3 very very very small sides. The baked oysters are not good. Do not order them.
Service is great. Food is solid but nothing stands out. We had the seasonal course menu. This place must be awesome 10 years ago. Now it's more for business people and older generations.

This particular dinner experience was absolutely amazing!  The atmosphere is warm, cozy and has a casual elegance about it.  The Christmas decor added to the magic of the already note worthy restaurant!  

The food was excellent and the service, which is one of the many things it is known for, was above reproach. 

There is a reason this fine establishment has been around for almost 30 years.

We had the most delightful anniversary dinner at Gramercy Tavern. Our waitress, Sydney was amazing - so sweet and personable. Gave good recommendations and genuinely cared about our experience and satisfaction. The food was delicious and we love the classy, relaxed atmosphere of the Gramercy.
Fantastic! Delicious! Stupendous! Highly recommend! We be had the best time here! Staff is friendly and accommodating. Vibe is on point.

At least 5 staff members waited on us and it's a place to go with an appetite. It's a very crowded and loud dining experience. A nice place to visit when in NYC but not sure if it's a place I would go to for an intimate dinner. Prefer lunch here. We ordered the truffle cheese platter (which is a must) for a starter and all of us did the prefix menu. The drinks and every bite was delish. I don't like my meat Sous Vide but everyone else at my table did. Just highlighting that if you have a preference.

Our bill was about a grand with one cocktail and a bottle of the cheapest wine they had. The wine was awful, a red cab that was cold. Honestly this place is very underwhelming for the value, from the slow service to the rather mundane dishes and soft roll as bread. The highlight of the meal was sitting next to Jon Hamm.
I wouldn't come back nor recommend it

Gramercy Tavern is a great restaurant. 
Delicious food and drinks. Ambiance is amazing and the staff is so friendly and personable. We had a great meal and experience. I highly recommend it.

Such a cute place and in a great location. Ate here for dinner last night and below is my review. 

Ambiance: was really cozy and decorated so cute for the holidays. 5/5 

Food:  had the flatbread and dips for an appetizer since I don't eat meat. It was really good just small if there more than 2 people in your party. For the entree we had the pork shoulder, sea bass, and the pasta. All the dishes were really good just again they are on the smaller side but a normal portion you should be eating. I only say they are smaller so if you're on the hungrier side, get another appetizer. For dessert we had all shared the apple cider donuts which were probably the best ones I've ever had. With the dessert I ordered the egg nog cocktail which was amazing but for $19 the glass was only half full. I totally get NYC is expensive but the cup was as small as it looks in the picture and it was about 3-4 sips and the rest was whip cream. Just would've been nice if the small glass was full and the $19 would've been 100 percent worth it. Good overall was a 4.3/5

Service: the hostess and waiter were super nice and everyone is very welcoming!

I can easily see why Gramercy Tavern has a Michelin star. This was one of the best dining experiences I've had in NYC! They have a staff of about a million and cater to your every need while you're there. There's the Tavern portion, which is more casual and doesn't have a Michelin star, and then there's the dining room portion, which is awarded and is $168pp pre-fixe.

We were a table of 6 and started with the seafood tower amongst us. The oysters with caviar and that mignonette sauce were WOW. The clams I could t left, but the lobster salad was also delish. It was the perfect size for 6 people to try a little of everything, although there were only 4 clams (but 8 oysters).

They brought the tower with our first of 5 courses, but before then, we had freshly homemade sweet potato bread and a complimentary sun dried artichoke amuse bouche. Both were great.

For the first course, I got the montauk scallops, and they were wonderful. They had apples mixed in which gave it a nice flavor and crunch. Second course led to the lobster lumache, which combined my 3 favorite things: lumache pasta, squid ink, and lobster. To die for!! Third course was the black bass and mashed cauliflower, cooked to perfection. Fourth course I chose the duck, which was honestly the best duck I've ever had in my LIFE.

Lastly, I ordered the hazelnut tart, which was great. Those at the table who ordered the alternative options to me loved them as well. We weren't rushed at all even though it took us probably 30 min to select a bottle of wine, and when we ordered a second but they had run out, they gave us a more expensive wine for the same price as the one we had ordered that was OOS, which was so kind of them. 

A phenomenal spot if you can swallow the price, but worth every penny!

Fantastic staff and service - 5 stars

No hot water in the restroom- incredibly tacky - not cool - 1 star 

'Roasted oysters -  gross -  it was like they ran them under warm water and the put them in the table.  

Vegetarian entree' - good combo and flavors, but grilled zucchini and squash were undercooked and hard.  

My lunch companion thought the chicken was really good. 

I'm happy to fork over $300 for lunch for two people, but it had better be excellent.

We were here for a Friday lunch, reservation was only available on the dining room portion but I believe they serve the same menu as the tavern for lunch. The beef tartare is served with cabbage (or something similar to that) instead of a toast/biscuit, which works surprisingly well with the slightly more refreshing style of tartare they served. The sea bass was cooked just right with a great sauce to complement it. The steak was a bit on the leaner side but might actually be better than a more fatty cut for a casual lunch. The cocktails are quite decent too. The price point is very acceptable for a Michelin starred restaurant with great ambiance and service. Would love to try the dinner some time in the future!

Spectacular setting and personable yet attentive service. Food was great. Highly recommend the Manhattanhenge cocktail to start. Pacing was exactly what we wanted and they even sent us in our way with a little apple crumb loaf that were perfect for breakfast the next morning.
Gorgeous restaurant, delicious food and drinks, and lovely service! My family really enjoyed our experience here and highly recommend it.

Fantastic food and great service. They have a staff of about a million and cater to your every need while you're there. There's the Tavern portion, which is more casual and doesn't have a Michelin star, and then there's the dining room portion, which is awarded...
Came here tonight- love the atmosphere! Had a 5 course meal and thought the portions were small but I was quite full by the end. Amazing service- highly recommend!

While the room is lovely and the service impeccable, I found my dinner mediocre especially considering the price.  I had the beef tartare appetizer and found it slightly, oddly sweet and I totally don't understand the idea of serving it with bitter endive. I would have been much happier in the Tavern which is the (very crowded) front room rather than the overly pretentious dining room.

It's our first night in NYC and we stayed at a condo down the street so we wanted to give it a try. We only came for cocktails but loved the atmosphere. Vibrant, friendly and festive around this time of the year. Just found out it's a one-star Michelin restaurant too so we got it right.  Love!

The wife "wanted to try this place for a long time, and it has a Michelin Star!" so we went.

The place is clearly well-maintained, the bathroom is very clean, they have a coat check.  The staff is welcoming and professional.

They have a rule that either everyone at the table orders the prix fixe, or no one.  OK, no biggie, I'll forego my prix fixe even though I really love duck and the duck dish can only be had as one of the prix fixe courses.  We ordered the seafood platter to share, the wife opted for the striped bass for her entree, and I -- for the sirloin.  I also got a glass of rosé figuring it would pair OK with both the seafood and the sirloin.

The meal started with some butter and pumpkin bread, which was very good.  The seafood platter was a mixed bag.  It would never occur to me to put caviar on top of oysters, even though I like both separately.  Having tried the combination, I can confidently say it will never occur to me in the future, either.  The oysters themselves were kind of mediocre.  The rest of it was pretty tasty.  

Then our main courses arrived.  My wife enjoyed her striped bass.  My dish was delicious!  Unfortunately there were only about 6 ounces of meat on the plate (perhaps I am even a bit generous) and 5-6 tablespoons of the kale puree, plus several mushrooms.

My rosé was not enjoyable, I felt a weird soapy aftertaste throughout.  Not sure if they hadn't rinsed the glass well or the wine just was that way.

The wife didn't want dessert so we skipped.  With tip, it ended up a bit over $210 for a regrettable glass of wine and what felt like 3 appetizers.  I felt hungry and taken advantage of.  

To summarize:
 - the service was good;
 - the interior design and ambiance were pleasant but not particularly memorable;
 - the quality of food was inconsistent and the portions were laughably tiny;
 - the whole thing was forgettable enough that I cannot honestly say to myself "well, I went there for the experience, not to get full" even if I wanted to;
 - why this place has a Michelin Star is a mystery to me.

This is based on the lunch menu -- perhaps the dinner experience is better, but I don't plan to find out.

Came to GT to celebrate our anniversary and we were very impressed with how beautiful and large this place is! We thought it would be stuffy but the staff are actually very sweet and you can tell they like to have a bit of fun too! We chose the seasonal menu, it was 5 courses with 2 options for each course which is perfect because we got to try all of it! When they learned we were celebrating our anniversary they brought extra treats and even sent us home with a little gift bag with coffee cakes. I loved the experience, the atmosphere, the FOOD, and the wonderful staff. Thank you so much for the sweet memory!

Came here during restaurant week. We enjoyed the old fashioned ambiance. The food was good but did not blow me away as a 1 Michelin star restaurant. Maybe it was because it was during restaurant week so maybe we have to go back for the real menu! Service was good but could be better. Overall a nice place.
Best date place. Great bar scene and great food in a great location.  Cannot go wrong here.

We love this place but obviously difficult to land a reservation.  I called Friday afternoon about the Tavern and they told me there are no reservations available but around 7 if 4 of us walk in it may be a short wait but they would definitely accommodate us for a table.  We got there and they said there wqw a wait for the bar but 4 was unlikely and they never would have said a table might be available.  Well thats what they told me on the phone.  Fortunately we were able to find another restaurant and if they had told me originally that a table was not likely it would have been fine.  The fact that they assured me otherwise was annoying.   We love it there but this is as frustrating.

My family and I came here for my brother's birthday after making a reservation weeks in advance. When you make the reservation, make sure you're choosing the right menu because the front of the Tavern serves their more casual fare whereas the back rooms host their tasting menu. We had the tasting menu - a 5 course menu. Each course had 2 dishes you could choose from: one that's meat based and one that's vegetarian. We also opted for the seafood starter tray which had the best shrimp I've ever had. My favorites of the menu were the squid ink pasta with lobster and the sea bass which had an Asian flavor profile that was both delicate and bold in flavor. Delicious!

Shout out to Caroline who was a fantastic server that night and made our experience so fun! The place was clean and had a very casual vibe which I loved because I get annoyed by the pretentious vibe of fine dining restaurants. The staff were all professional and friendly. My only issue is that the place is so large and open that if you're a group of 5 or more and are seated at a large table, the place gets a lot of echo, which makes it hard to have quiet conversations with the whole table. But, it's great for intimate tables for 2 people who are seated close to each other. 

I absolutely plan to come back and try the vegetarian options of their tasting menu.
I had a wonderful experience celebrating my birthday last Thursday. The food was very flavorful and the service was outstanding. I will definitely be back when I return to New York.

We did not have a reservation but took our chances for two bar seats.  We lucked out and were seated in less than 10 minutes. Our server, Aaron, was top notch. His recommendations were spot on. We loved everything we ordered, including the wine recommendations. The Gramercy Tavern is always number one on our list when we are in the city.  The food and atmosphere are sublime!

Best burger I have ever had. Ever. This place rules. I sit at the bar. The Bartenders take pride in working there. They remember you. Those are little things that go along way. Plus Chef Mike Anthony has got a great menu. You might also meet him.
Perfect special occasion spot with amazing service. Great memory maker and great dining experience

Place screams elegant and tradition, but it's expensive AF.  We did the restaurant week tasting menu, and it was good, but not Ahhhhhmazing.

Believe it or not, the hilight of the meal was the bread.  It was fresh cooked and sooooo soft. Slightly pretzelish outside vibe with the Maldon? Salt on it.

Try it for the ambiance and the name, but eat something before, or plan on snacking after.
Fantastic burgers and bacon! It gets cramped but I think it adds to the vibe. It's a cool spot

Inconsistent in quality. I went to Gramercy Tavern a few weeks ago to try the famous hot chocolate. It was a delicious experience -- sipping a thick creamy dark chocolate topped with a torched marshmallow. Fast forward to today, the hot chocolate was watery and lukewarm, with a cold marshmallow. I was shocked by the inconsistency.

Overall (3.5/5): Service was so sweet and attentive! The ambiance was pretty spacious for NYC with lots of seating but would definitely grab a reservation in advance. Lots of business lunches and more elevated than your casual lunch spot. 

Note: aren't a TON of menu options. 

Lunch special (potato soup combo with roast beef sandwich) (3/5): The soup was hot, not too heavy for a creamy potato, and I was surprised how much I liked the flavor. I'm docking them for the main dish because the baguette was tough, not crispy, and ended up being soggy from the excess sauce of the meat. While the beef was juicy, it was way too salty and wouldn't recommend because the flavor wasn't anything special.

Desserts (4/5): We got the apple upside tart and chocolate pudding, but I preferred the chocolate because it wasn't too sweet, had nuts, and the mix of fresh whipped cream / ice cream were perfection! The apple tart was crispy but definitely felt like a much smaller portion incase you're planning to share.

Beware of purse snatchers. Food sucks too. 
Don't leave your belongings out of sight. 
Seems the local precinct is aware of the problem.

Good
Luck with the rest of your journey today and keep us happy always enjoy the food go

As usual, Danny Meyer knocks it out of the park with a beautiful country space and as usual, the service is fantastic. Grant, you is Restaurant week so sometimes the meals are lackluster, which this one certainly was. The potato soup was very good. The shrimp dish was soggy and not that flavorful. The waiter Madison was great and exchanged it for the beet dish, which had beautiful and presentation and good. My Tile fish needed some seasoning just average. The biggest disappointment was the chicken tasteless and rubbery management quickly substituted it for the hanger steak, which was just average again not much flavor. The highlight of the meal was the chocolate cream pie, which was delicious pie was slightly misleading since one would expect some crust. I'm happy it didn't have any and it was absolutely delicious. I was so looking forward to coming here since it's been a long time since I've been back but unfortunately it didn't live up to my expectations
Best restaurant week deal of 2024 in my opinion. Outstanding service, ambiance, and great options!

I've been dying to try Gramercy Tavern to see what the burger hype is all about. I finally snagged a resy in the tavern this afternoon. I loved the complimentary focaccia they gave us and really enjoyed the flatbread with dips (onion, pea/crab, sesame/pepper). The burger was good but comparable to The Smith. Not sure it's worth the high price point. I'd like to go in the main dining room next time to try the tasting menu.

Major bummer. I've been a huge fan of this restaurant for years. But there has recently been a change in the staff. The rude and head honcho "bruiser" behind the bar should find new employment, as a first step toward getting back to their previous standard of professional customer service. There has clearly been some kind of ugly shift with this place. After a decade of enjoyment, I have decided to give Gramercy Tavern a permanent rest.

This was one of my solid go to/favorite restaurants for a long time. Unfortunately, it no longer is. There must have been some major change in staff (wait staff and kitchen staff) since service for both noticeably declined since last time. 

Service was much less attentive and orderly. Everything took a long while to happen and they kept mixing up minor things like who's the birthday person and who's allergic to what etc. Lastly, food was either too salty, too dry, too sweet or too underwhelming. It's no longer the balanced dishes I remember. I was at pavillon shortly before and the difference was noticeable.

Food was great.  Came in with big expectations, this was my first time coming here.  I loved the dining experience.  The service was perfect, we were waited on often.  The vibe and ambiance of the place was a 10.  I think the food was perfect as it came out. Highly recommended.
One of the best restaurants in NYC, great food and service but expensive and worth it

Came by for dinner the other night and it was a decent experience. Gramercy Tavern is a Michelin 1 star restaurant and features a tavern for more casual Millennial/Gen Z dining or the dining room for more senior Boomer 5 course white tablecloth dining. 

Made a reservation for the dining room and my table was ready upon arrival. The tavern showcases an open kitchen which is open to staff only. Staff are wearing a uniform blue dress shirt along with an apron. The Gen Zstaff were wearing ill-fitting dress shirts...

Upon arrival, there is a coat check (bring some small bills for tips). During my visit, it was Restaurant Week where the dining room was participating for lunch. To my surprise, a good portion of the evening tasting menu was also available for Restaurant Week...

The dining room is starting to show its age with some of the cushions at the booth starting to wear out. I counted at least 4 light bulbs in one section of the dining room that were burnt out. The loo was also quite casual, not quite in line with a Michelin 1 star restaurant...

Service by the staff throughout the evening was attentive and cordial. The dining room seems to be a special occasion restaurant where every other table seemed to be celebrating some type of birthday or anniversary...some of the diners were quite green to the fine dining scene.

Despite being marked as a New American/Contemporary restaurant, I felt this restaurant was leaning towards the Traditional American flair with a slight tilt towards the New American. As other Yelpers mentioned, the flavoring on the dishes was uneven, some were on the bland side and other were quite salty and rich...

Started off with the arctic char which was a light and refreshing way to start of the meal.

Moved on to the sweet potato roll which was served with a super fragrant and light butter spread. The sweet potato roll was decent, although I've had lighter versions of rolls.

The marinated beets was added on the house and was one of the highlights of the evening with light and refreshing flavors.

The squid ink lumache pasta featured a generous portion of perfectly al dente pasta along with 3 clams and 3 pieces of perfectly poached pieces of lobster. Excellent pasta course.

The striped bass course was interesting. I felt that the bass was over salted although I did enjoy the contrasting textures of the pan fried bass along with a soft interior. The complementary bok choy was interesting as bok choy tends to be a lower end vegetable...

The lamb course was good although on the bland side. The loin was quite lean and the accoutrements were definitely on the very rich and heavy side...not quite what I had expected. The side of mushrooms were also quite salty...

Meal ended off with the chocolate cream pie which was super sweet and rich...

Post dessert, the waitstaff brought some additional sweets along with some bread for the following day.

~$220/head after tax and gratuity for dinner in the dining room.

Bad experience having a lunch at this restaurant. I got to the restaurant on time but I wasn't seated for 20 minutes pass while other people who came after me got seated. Between appetizer and Main course, my friend and I waited at least 20 minutes while the restaurant is not full. Overall food tastes good, but service is below average.

There are many things to love about Gramercy Tavern. I've only had terrific experiences here over the years. The staff is great and actually paying attention (that is hard nowadays!), the food is always really good, bathrooms always well kept. I think the drinks are a bit overpriced for what they are but that's a matter of opinion. One of my absolute most favorite things about this NYC staple though is that it is never a scene. Just normal people that want to have a nice and normal dinner. Excellent food for adults!

Came for the restaurant week lunch. 
If they join restaurant week next year, I will definitely come back!

The service is great, check in coat, reading chiefs's book while waiting. 

After seated, enjoy the food! Nothing will go wrong on the menu! The shrimp is our favorite, and chief told us the shrimps are from Long Island. 

We were really full! The appetizer portion was really big. Super satisfied!

Great food and service. Was here during restaurant week. Highly recommend getting a reservation, we got lucky by just walking exactly when it opened. They were kind enough to accommodate us. Even though it was a three course meal. They had a complementary drink (pomegranate ginger based I think) which had a really strong flavor and perfect balance. They also had a couple of other complementary tastings which were really unique. 
The service was really organized and smooth.

My landmark birthday (60) deserved an epic experience and Gramercy Tavern did not disappoint. It was a toss up between the prix fixe and the a la carte but I really like the menu of the latter so I chose that option. We ordered the steak tartare, the $35 burger (worth it!), and pressed chicken. Everything was delicious and it was one of those incredible meals that you lingered over. The service was on point (natch) and a big shoutout to the sommelier from Apéritif to Calvados.

Now this place is a fine restaurant with the price tag to match.  One of my all time favorite places in the city.  We went for the Christmas Eve lunch and we were not disappointed.  The restaurant was decorated beautifully and the staff are top notch.  The sommelier was incredibly helpful and friendly, turning us onto a wine neither of us had heard of and it was exquisite.  The food is just delicious and the atmosphere charming.  They have thought of every little detail and it shows.  We did have a laugh over the $36 cocktails they were offering which is a first even for NYC!

The burger (made of ground beef short ribs and brisket) is phenomenal. 2nd only for me to Au Cheval.  The beef tartare is great if you like a more citrus/acidic experience.  For me, I tend to like less of that.  The service was fantastic.  Max C. was our server and did an awesome job.  KUDOS to Max C!

Came for the Dining Room as an engagement celebration and had such a wonderful experience. I have to say the waiter was possibly the best or second best I've seen - he was amazing at making your experience feel truly personalized to you. Food was also amazing and just overall really enjoyed the ambiance.
100% recommended!

Came in on the last week of Restaurant Week for their lunch deal. Unfortunately, I didn't have a reservation and was told that the reservations were booked out. However, I did get there during opening and was told that I could wait 15 minutes to see if there were any no shows. Fortunately for me, there was, and I was seated and give about 75 minutes for the table. 

Butternut squash bite at the beginning was full of flavor. The bread at the start was really good. Definitely a precursor to what would be a very filling meal. The lumache was bigger than I expected. Rather than being an appetizer, I felt that it could've been the main. It came with a huge seafood fragrance, but it wasn't that strong of a seafood taste. The shrimp was really sweet though. I tried my friend's sweet potato agnolotti, and it was really good too but also very rich. 

Roasted duck was great. The duck was perfectly cooked. I loved the vegetables that came with it. It was a simple presentation, and the duck was tender. 

Apple tart tatin was okay. A little bit too sweet for my preference, but it was a nice warming dessert for a very full meal. Should've gotten something lighter like the lemon tart to round off the meal, but it wasn't bad. Gummies were given at the end. I didn't like the spices for the gummy, and the texture was very soft. It didn't remind me of a gummy at all. 

Staff were super friendly and came around to refill water often. We were given good suggestions and recommendations. 

The Restaurant Week meal was such a steal for Michelin starred food. I would definitely consider taking advantage of it when the next Restaurant Week comes again.

Went on a Sunday afternoon for my wife's birthday. Met up with my son and his wife. The service was beyond good - the best term would be elegant. We starred with flatbread and three excellent dips. The standout here was somethinig  that tasted of avocado and honey. My hangar steak with parsnips was stellar. Donna and Bob had the grilled cauliflower main dish. At dessert time everybody ordered goodies except birthday girl, but they brought her out a perfect tiny cake anyway. The word classy does not begin to describe this place. It was a perfect celebration in an iconic city eatery. Bravo!!

I came here for restaurant week lunch. The place was buzzing as everyone was taking advantage of this amazing deal. The restaurant was serving only the restaurant week menu. Service was impeccable yet very timely due to scheduled reservations. I want to say I was there for about 90 minutes. 

The ambiance was pretty showcasing an old-school New York Tavern vibe, so I can't imagine the type of people that come in to dine. 

The restaurant week menu was offering dishes that are seen on their regular tasting menu during dinner service.

To start, the complementary bite and sweet potato roll were amazing. The complementary bite set my palate for the three dishes that I ordered. The sweet potato roll and butter were amazing. I don't usually eat rolls before my meal because it is filling, but I definitely devoured this roll. 

So the restaurant week portions are smaller than what would you get if you were to dine here on a normal night. For the appetizer, I ordered the sweet potato agnolotti, which was amazing from the texture of the freshly made agnolotti to the butter sauce. I made sure that every piece of agnolotti was drowned in the sauce, so the plate would be perfectly cleaned.

For the entree of the roasted duck and it was a perfect portion. The duck was cooked medium, and it was lean. I still enjoyed that agnolotti dish. For dessert, I had the Meyer lemon tart, which was a perfect ending to my amazing lunch experience. 

I'd definitely return to dine in the bar because I want to try their famous Gramercy Tavern Bar and their wine or cocktail.
An NYC staple. Drinks are classy and strong. Foods are great. You can't go wrong with this if you are able to score a table or bar seat.

Love that Gramercy cares enough to make its restaurant feel special. Wonderful floral display. The place has a great sense of place. The food is always delicious and the staff is happy to be there and help you enjoy the experience.

Every staff member we interacted with was polite, courteous, and friendly. The food was sensational. (It wasn't on the menu this time, but their burger is to die for! If you ask for it, we think they'll make it for you. We saw 4 burgers on the open kitchen grill as we left!) Cocktail and wine list- fantastic! Making reservations is simple and easy through their website. The restaurant is very large inside and there's lots of seating. We're from out of town and have now been to Gramercy Tavern twice during our trips. We enjoy it so much that we'll make sure to dine in again on all of our future trips!

My 2nd time at Gramercy Tavern in the dining room.  Not inexpensive - but I think it's worth the $168 prix fixe in the main dining room.  I had
- Citrus cured arctic char
- Squid ink lumache
- Caraflex cabbage
- Duck breast
- Crispy chocolate cake

The char was phenomenal.  Very fresh, well seasoned.  Good presentation.
The squid ink lumache was very good
I tend to avoid vegetable/vegetarian courses.  But, as I had two seafood course 1st, and the alternative was a 3rd seafood course, I chose the "cabbage".  This was the best dish of the meal.  
The duck breast was good, tender, but not nearly as good as the seared magret de canard I get on my frequent visits to France.  
The chocolate cake was also quite good, - the filling was good quality chocolate, but the hard pastry shell did not add much. 

Service was pretty good, properly attentive, but did not always do a good job explaining each dish.

As it turns out, you get what you pay for. 

The 5 course tasting menu was exceptional, from the flavors, to the mix of ingredients, to the freshness of those ingredients, to the plating, to the service and pacing, everything was wonderful. Highlights would include the beets with pistachio and sorrel, squid ink lumache with lobster and muscles (perhaps my favorite bite of the night), the roasted duck breast with carrot puree, and the roast lamb with kale pesto. If there were any weak links, it perhaps would have been the desserts, though to refer to them as such isn't to say they weren't still wonderful, only that they didn't provoke me to stop and catch my breath after the first bite the way the other courses did. 

It's an excellent meal top to bottom if you've got a special occasion or need an excuse to treat yourself.

How does this place have almost 5 stars? Ate in the tavern. Nice interior with a good ambience. Food is decent. As is service. BUT...certainly did not live up to the hype. Nor did the whole experience. It was basically very expensive bar food.
Best Burger I've ever had, hands down 11/10. Worthy of the michelin star. Price is worth. The fish and the beef tartare were good, but get the burger! Come here.

Gramercy Tavern lives up to its name and reputation! I was invited here for a baby shower and was blown away. Firstly, the service was impeccable. Aquila (hope I spelled that right) took such great care of us!! Her and the staff made us feel right at home, everyone was so friendly. They were also very attentive, I noticed that my napkin was folded every time I got up to use the restroom. Onto the food- my favorite was the sweet potato lumache with a duck ragu. Flavortown!!! Pasta was cooked perfectly-al dente. I also loved the dessert which wasn't my typical choice. It was a pear upside down cake. Sooooo good. Not one crumb left. Also got a chocolate chip cookie to go. The restaurant was beautiful inside. Very cozy and had gorgeous arrangements and decor. Would return again in the future!
Always great food. And service. And before or after visit the Teddy Roosevelt home next door.

5 star service!!! 

I think I just prefer other flavors to American so I thought the food was alright but nothing amazing or mind blowing. 

Sweet potato duck pasta - fresh pasta texture was good. Sauce was too salty for me and it made it a heavy meal. Besides the salt the flavors were good but it was too glaring of an issue to overlook. 

Drinks - rlly liked the manhattanhenge drink! Drinks were strong hehe 

The best thing about gramercy tavern was that they were really accommodating for allergies. My friend has a lot of allergies and they were able to modify the dishes for him while preserving the flavor!!! Moreover, it was his birthday and they saw how much he enjoyed the allergy friendly cake that they sent another one with him for the road!!! It was very sweet and the service was excellent!!!

We had a great lunch here for a friend's birthday on a Thursday. Got seated by the window with comfy bench seats and it was a gorgeous sunny day outside. 

The food was excellent (citrus beet salad - fantastic and fresh, arctic char (very flavourful and light and perfectly done), the potato leek soup (creamy and lovely) and brisket sandwich (great), the chicken (nicely done), a chocolate pudding (rich and delish), the pear cake (great), and an extra slice of birthday cake with icing/banana. We were VERY full after. 

However, the service was extremely slow (but friendly and knowledgeable when it was there). We didn't get our bread (fresh and good - but we had to ask for butter/oil) for 10-15 minutes after we had ordered our meal. And we had to flag down a different waiter for dessert after waiting 20 minutes (our table had been cleared already). 

Would definitely come back for the ambience and food!

I made a brunch reservation in the A La Carte Tavern without knowing the menu, the prices, or that it had a Michelin star. The food was good, but portions small and expensive. 

It's not one that I would go back to.

Really solid price fixe menu and a beautiful restaurant. Waitress forgot our cheese plate order and some other technical details, which wasn't ideal. Food review below!

Arctic char appetizer - 4/5, didn't love the sesame topping (tasted stale?)
Squid Ink Seafood Pasta - 5/5, the seafood was insanely yummy
Skate - 5/5, so interesting. Loved the textures
Lamb - 0/5, this was a huge miss. Overcooked and bland. Sauce was too rich and smoky
Lemon Tart - 4/5, good but nothing innovative like the other dishes
Outstanding dinner! Great wine pairing suggestions from outstanding wait staff. Highly recommend the Tavern Burger, brick pressed chicken and Cauliflower.

Beautiful place, great food, nice service. Have dined here several times over the years and never been disappointed in the food. Always fresh and well prepared. Seasonal entrees have been delightful. Wine list is well paired with the food.

Food - 
Appetizers: Grilled bread with dips, beet salad.
Entrées: Duck meatloaf, Burger, Pork shoulder.
In depth notes on the food: Pork is tasty and juicy. Duck meatloaf is very flavorful. The burger is the staple dish and really tasty.
Service - Angel was our server, very knowledgeable and professional. An added benefit to our experience.
Ambiance - Professional crowd, not loud. Beautiful and artistic restaurant with high ceiling. 
Highly recommended

Our group of 6 came in here for lunch while being violently hungover after a bender that consisted of American Bar to the Spaniard to Roscioli to Peculier Pub. Just a rough one. I could do that in college but I really feel it now smh.

All this to say, Gramercy Tavern brought us back to life.

I walked in here and felt like I walked into an Anthropology. I mean that in a compliment of the highest regard... Nobody touching Anthro, idc.

The seemingly hundreds of flower arrangements, the natural light flowing in, the colorful art on the walls... It's just so happy in here. 

I sat out on hair of the dog and ordered a black americano because I'm a warrior, haha.

We started with a dozen oysters and the grilled flatbread platter... I need to go on a side quest here about this flatbread platter. This was one of the best decisions we had made all weekend, honestly probably the best.

This flatbread HAS to be made in house with how it was tasting. God it was so good... It reminded me of making homemade tortillas back in elementary school on Cinco De Mayo. Those were like CRACK.

When we destroyed the flatbread and there were half the dips left, our waitress came by and said "do you guys want some more flatbread?" ... We all just kind of made eye contact with each other around the table like "That's an option!?!?"

We got a re-up on the flatbread and sent that to the shadow realm as well. All this to say, get the flatbread.

I think 4 of the 6 of us got burgers lol, but it was so necessary with being that hungover... One of those hangovers where if you think too hard your thoughts will rattle off of your brain. I was fighting for my life.

I got my burger medium rare, as that's what the recommend and it was a little too rare for me ahahha but nobody to blame but myself, because I asked for this. Still good though don't get it twisted. The chips that came with the burger were perfect as well.

For dessert, we got the Apple Cider donuts and the Chocolate Chunk Cookie. When the apple cider donuts came my internal dialogue was like "Damn, $18 for 3 little donuts" ... but I've never been so happy to be proven wrong. These were the best donuts I've ever had in my life. Granted, I'm not the biggest donut guy ever but I have dabbled, and these are IT!

I also need to highlight the staff, as they are LOCKED in here. Bringing all our plates at the same time and clearing them in unison is such a small attention to detail that makes a HUGE difference. It's not in a try hard way either. They are always smiling and seem genuinely happy to be working here, and it's infectious. I actually just got back from the Locked In Factory, and they knew the entire Gramercy Tavern staff... 

One of the best vibes of any restaurant I have been to in New York City, even while battling a ruthless hangover. I'LL BE BACK FOR THAT FLATBREAD! FLATBREAD ALL STARS!

Tiktok @jnov_reviews

My husband and I enjoyed dinner here to celebrate my birthday and we had an amazing experience. The entire wait staff was very attentive, and explained each course to us when they brought it to the table. My husband has celiacs disease and they did a great job making sure every course they served him was gluten free. Every course was amazing, and our only critique is that we wished the fourth course was bigger so we could have enjoyed more of the lamb and duck. After our last course, our waitress surprised me with a little birthday cake that was gluten free so my husband was able to enjoy it with me. We had such a great experience, and can't wait to come back and enjoy the next seasonal menu.

First night in New York decided to enjoy a nice meal at the Gramercy Tavern which is located in the Flatiron district. 

They serve up some interesting cocktail names and the server did also say they change the names od the drinks from time to time.

It was a fun girls night so we all ordered three drinks to enjoy with our meal. We also decided to share all our food. 

We ordered the citrus & beets, beef tartar, Tavern hamburger, roast duck, and a pasta dish. 

Everything was cooked well and I did enjoy the pasta dish but I forgot what the name was! The roast duck also has enjoyable flavors. 

Our server was fun and we overall just had a wonderful dinner filled with fun memories.

First time dining in the tavern section - very impressed. Busy and buzzy with the easy-going feel of a pub, but with impeccable customer service and attention to detail. Felt very welcomed by the friendly bartenders and all the service was unpretentious and accomplished. Food was excellent: duck liver, roasted oysters, burgers, desserts all first class.

Ambiance - Professional crowd, not loud. Beautiful and artistic restaurant with high ceiling.

Highly recommended
Traditional cuisine in a fun area of NYC, Flat Iron district. You can't go wrong ordering anything here.

Amazing night!!! We took the kids to NY and they got their first taste of a Michelin rated restaurant. It was also our first time at Gramercy Tavern. The service was friendly, impeccable, and made great food suggestions. The cocktails and wine (suggested by somm) were amazing and every dish from our appetizers to the main courses we had were truly amazing! We can't wait to come back and try the dining room .

Samantha was unbelievable and gave us a dining experience that will be difficult to top. She went over and above with recommendations for food and drinks and made our engagement more than we could have hoped for. We will be back for other milestone moments in our life together.
Excellent dishes and service! Enjoyed our visit here in December. We visited for lunch and had a reservation.

I brought my son here from LA and we have been exploring all of the culinary delights of the city. When I left NY in 2006, I still had never been here so I was excited to try it. It is disappointing and not worth the meal. We ordered the duck confit parpadelle, arctic char and a coffee. The olive bread tasted like I took a teaspoon of salt, and the food was over salted as well. I had a stomach ache from all the sodium and my coffee refill was lukewarm. They did bring out a piping hot cup after I asked for one, however.
Amazing and so atmospheric ..I look forward to my next visit ..It's so glad to part in a legend that has maintained its reputation ..

Came here for Valentines Day last year with one of my best friends. First thing that stood out to me was how warm and cozy it feels once you're inside the dining room. Food and service were both outstanding. Would love to return.
Expensive and food is only ok.  Service was fine but nothing to write home about.  I don't think I will be going there again.

I had the lunch Pork Shoulder(36) per the recommendation of the server. It was delicious. Many flavors, so many flavorful flavors. A true example of how something doesn't have to be hot and still be flavorful. It was very fatty. I don't think I'd order it again because of this. But it's true, fat is flavor!

Duck Meatloaf(34) is what my wife ordered. She enjoyed it very much. I felt it was a bit dry, which surprised me with duck. 

Socratic Method(19) is what my wife ordered. A little smoke flavor and a aftertaste that is a pleasantly and subtly bitter. 

I'd return and I'd love to try more menu items.

Welcoming ambiance and staff.  Waiter really tried to get to know us and make our dining experience personal and fun! Really appreciate his kindness. Sommelier was friendly and knowledgeable and the food was excellent! Definately recommend!!

Just keeps getting better and better, if that's possible! Been fans for almost 30 years and still continue to be blown away by the incredible food served in the prettiest, most comfortable dining room by the warmest servers you could hope to find. Not often do you go into this kind of a restaurant without feeling a tiny bit intimidated - I usually have lots of questions about the food and sometimes get icy glares from snooty wait people. Never going to happen here - these people are pros and will go out of their way to make sure you're totally satisfied and completely comfortable. Our number 1 favorite for special occasions!
Bad service.  Ordered a drink and then ignored.  Originally planned to stay for dinner and more drinks, but left. Very  disappointed.

After the highly anticipated reservation we had a lovely evening for a birthday celebration.

5* Flavors 
5* Service
5* Authentic atmosphere 
4* Drinks were great
3* Not the best burger in NYC. Was a bit dry with complex flavors, bun was too big for the amount of meat and cheese
1* They blew off the birthday celebration (really)
5*Oysters were amazing.
Cocktails and food were delicious and the service was impeccable. I highly recommend G Tavern, although it is a bit pricey.

Over priced, over priced, over priced. 
Service was awful, food mediocre. 
I would not be back there!

We had a late lunch reserved in the Tavern. We were looking forward to finally trying their burger. It was too lively and boisterous (loud) for our companion with a hearing aid and even hard for the rest of us to chat across the table. Luckily,  even though they were busy, we were able to move to the restaurant. We'll have to try the burger another time; it's not on the menu in the restaurant. The service was great in both rooms. All our food came out when it should and to the correct person. They easily split the check - no drama. I loved the rolls and amuse buche at the start. We ordered an appetizer to share, our own entrees, and dessert to share. Everything was delicious. We left feeling very full and happy. The cocktails were all smooth and well balanced, too. Another fabulous meal. I'm amazed at how they've been able to maintain such high standards over all the years. Kudos to Chef Mike Anthony and Danny Meyer.

Extremely over rated and decently over priced. Burger was the saltiest thing I've ever had. Rest of the food was meh.
Service was actually really good though. 
I don't understand the hype

This is a place I have heard of for a long time, but have never been able to attend...
on my last trip to NYC, I was invited there. 
I was
Not prepared for the fixed menu of the back restaurant.
It is very interesting restaurant layout; a vibrant bar and bistro in the front; and a more subdued fine dining experience toward the rear.
The diver is very lively in the front, and nice and spacious and understated in the back.
The food was wonderful, and they were very accommodating with my dietary restriction.
While the food was wonderful, honestly the outstanding part of the evening was the stunning service. It was seamless, polite, knowledgeable and engaged.
I have not had such outstanding service in a very long time.
They handled dietary restrictions easily, and did some custome cocktails with precision and fervor.
Bravo
Bravo...
FYI they have an amazing pastry chef who creates amazing vegan delights.
Honestly I am interested in seeking out service leading establishments after that meal.
Highly recommend for the experience...
Cannot speak to parking...
NYC... use public transportation....

Grammercy Tabern is my idea of the ideal restaurant. The setting is bright and modern. The service from the friendly welcome to the impeccable servers all works beautifully. And then, there's the food. We've had many items on the menu. I love their duck liver mousse. One measure of a good restaurant is the quality of their bread. Here the bread is excellent. Every entree on the menu is worth ordering. You can never go wrong choosing Grammercy Tavern.

SERVICE:
Most service in NY seems like they hate their customers. But I think it's just because I'm not from NY? Either way, so many other customers (non-local) said the same thing so I know I'm not alone. Despite that, the food was awesome. 

FOOD:
$21 DUCK LIVER MOUSSE: a hefty portion of delicious liver accompanied by kumquat jam. Put those on top a freshly toasted bread and it's perfection! Comes with some pickled vegetables. LOVED THIS! 

$23 BEEF TARTARE: the Dijon vinegar sauce beneath the beef tartare was the perfect complement of flavors bursting in your mouth. I wish there were more crispy pieces for texture, but it was delicious! The cheese (bayley hazen, blue cheese) was pungent & amazing! LOVED THIS! 

$38 ARCTIC CHAR: this is a fish similar to salmon. It's VERY LIGHT, comes in a light broth that I absolutely loved! Exactly what I wanted. 

OVERALL:
I loved the vibe and food here. Would always come back.

We went to try the tasting menu, but instead, ordered almost all of the entrees. For 4 people we ordered 6-7 entrees and were full, but not stuffed. Portions were a bit small. The duck entree was a chef's seasonal special and was amazing. Shrimp & the sauce + fish entree were very good as well. And the complementary bread- the best bread & butter I've had in a while!

Better and better as the evening progressed. My son and I arrived at 7:50 for our 8:00 reservation in the dining room. 15 minutes passed and a couple walks in and is asked to wait as well. They, however, are given apologies for having to wait. Furthermore, they are brought complimentary bubbly for the inconvenience. It was quite painful to be sitting a foot away as the cork is popped and given nothing (not even an acknowledgment). Even though we arrived before them, they were seated first. This is clearly old-style NYC, high-profile treatment. Catering to their best clientele while overlooking the average. Once we were seated, things improved and the meal was divine. The few extras like small bites, a mini congrats cake for my son, and lemon loaf to go (for the morning) made up for the rough start.

Every point of service from hostess to food runners is set up to make you feel welcome without fussing over you. 

You must, must, must have their Hamachi Crudo. It's a small plate of magic in both presentation and flavor. 

All their dishes use seasonal ingredients sourced from the local farmers' market just blocks away.  I have a new found love of snap peas, rhubarb, lemon, and radishes after lunching here.

Decided to try a la carte (not prix fixe) indoor dining. The food was tasty but the portions were so small. I was definitely not full after eating a full meal with cocktails here. The restaurant itself is cute and the vibe is upscale but casual. Service was rather slow - took about 10-15 minutes before our waiter came back to take our order and we had to ask where he was. Limited bar seating.

An otherwise very good meal was somewhat diminished by the extremely small pour when you order a glass of wine. The server pours the wine from a bottle but it wasn't the fault of the server. I noticed that at the table next to us another couple ordered glasses of wine and the pour was embarrassingly small. Clearly, the policy of the restaurant.

We had the seasonal menu. The marinated beets, skate, duck breast and lemon tart were all quite good. So if you're ordering a bottle of wine you'll not have this problem but if you're only desiring a glass, be prepared for disappointment. One expects more from a high end restaurant.

For my bday dinner, we ended up booking the dining room. Compared to other Michelin start places, I was disappointed in the food and ambiance. It just was all forgettable, nothing was wrong with it, but it didn't leave an impression. 

The service was professional and coordinated, can't say anything bad there. 

It felt like the place was full of tourists and I liked the local scene, so this was another miss for me.  People weren't dressed up either. 

The dishes seemed like things they had been cooking for years rather than doing something new weekly or even daily. 

Maybe the tavern is more fun and local, but I'd skip this one.

Service is impeccable. Drinks were amazing (we also got the GT manhattan and GT old fashioned, as well as the Socratic method --very peaty & leathery, fantastic-- and Sausalito fog--herbal & refreshing). The beef tartare was wonderful, with bites of bleu cheese & cubed pear. The sweet potato pappardelle with braised beef was savory with a hint of spice. The burger was juicy, and well cooked. It wasn't my favorite burger ever, and it's expensive, but I would say it's a flavorful, juicy, hearty option. 
Dessert: they gifted me a lovely hummingbird cake that was sweet and delicious. My husband got the chocolate pudding cake--I have a nut allergy, so they put the nut products on the side so I could try his, which was very kind of them. The pudding cake was rich and delicious. I got the vanilla rhubarb sundae, which was jammy, tart and sweet. I really enjoyed it; it made me feel like a kid again; the rhubarb was a sorbet almost, and tasted like one of those popsicles you'd get as a child from the ice cream man. The creamy vanilla balanced it well; I think it would be even more balanced with crumbled graham cracker. 

It was busy at 5:30, when we had our reservations, and quite loud. I'd recommend reservations! We had a really great time here!

Came here to celebrate a birthday! The staff was kind and friendly and had great recommendations. Plus the burger is one of the best cheeseburgers in the city.

It was lively in the restaurant but not too loud. I also love a restaurant with plenty of room, I didn't feel like I was squeezing past other guests.

We'll be back again and again.

Great food, nice atmosphere, lots of flowers, not too loud, good service, would go back! Right atmosphere and price  balance between fancy and casual - definitely on the fancy side but not like a 3 star and honestly prefer this! And about half the price or less of the 3 stars generally and food is pretty much just as good!
Our server, Amanda was a delight! Her recommendations were spot on. The food and ambience for our lunch in the tavern were exceptional. Very pleased customers.

First time back in 10 years, this time in the more informal Tavern.  There's nothing to dislike about Gramercy Tavern, from delicious food to solid service.  GT is a restaurant that takes pride in doing things right.  Among the dishes we ordered, the roasted oysters and Tavern burger were standouts.  The oysters are lightly cooked, almost raw, and sprinkled with chard and tiny bits of green apple.  The burger has the perfect combination of beef, bacon and cheese on a soft bun and comes with homemade potato chips.  Best burger and chips I've ever had.  We also had the broccolini salad, duck liver mousse and grilled pork shoulder but didn't feel they were as remarkable as the oysters or burgers.

Compared to our last visit 10 years ago, there are now many more restaurants in NYC serving innovative American and Western cuisine.  GT continues to distinguish itself but will have to work hard to remain relevant.

I chose the Gramercy Tavern because it's an NYC institution with a great reputation and excellent reviews. I figured that I couldn't go wrong, until we encountered our server who treated us with incredible disrespect. I have never in my life been spoken to so condescendingly. The food was fine (not incredibly memorable). Being that it was my birthday, we actually would have loved to stay for dessert because the menu looked great but we couldn't wait to leave due to the way we were spoken to. 
Regarding the ambience - we were sat outside...the inside was lovely, the sidewalk was just like any other. 
I wish I could remember "his" name, and my husband will forever regret not confronting him instead of leaving the 20% tip that he did. It was an absolutely horrible experience.

Absolutely amazing. From the atmosphere, the food, the staff. 
All courses were amazing. Tortellini was fantastic. The cabbage was not your mother's cabbage. Pressed into a square and grilled. Fabulous. 
William took care of us and ensured everything was perfect. 
Thank you.
The cauliflower main course I had , was one of the best dishes I had for a long while and I eat well. Kudos to the team. Consistency is what brings me back to Gramercy.
Excellent food, service, and beautiful interior.  The gave us a very delicious cake and champagne for our anniversary.

Went tonight with friends. Four people total; we shared three appetizers and four entrees. The total was nearly $500 which would have been fine had we not left the restaurant starving! The portions are so measly. Yes, the food is fresh and well prepared but we literally walked out and went to get pizza. Will never return.

One of my favorite restaurants in Manhattan.  

Recently went with family to celebrate a birthday and did the $168 prix fixe.

Everything was delicious and just as I remembered from pre-COVID.

This is one of our favorite upscale restaurants in NYC. The food is consistently delicious and enjoyable. There are always a couple dishes with unexpected flavors, which we enjoy, and generally find everything fresh and delicious. The last time we came here we had a nice family dinner with relatives and it was a lovely and tasty meal!

First time visiting Gramercy Tavern during the Summer Fancy Food Show. The restaurant was down the street from my hotel so I went there right before dinner started and sat at the bar which is the only walk in seating available. The restaurant started to fill up shortly afterwards and tavern and bar area were packed. The bartenders were great especially Kimberly who was attentive and on it. I've never seen a Vesper martini on a cocktail menu so I was excited since I make them at home. I ordered the burger and chips in duck fat and it was very good. Overall ambiance is great, Kimberly was great and food was very good. 4.5 stars

I loved the steak.
The staff was also very accommodating.
And it was a very nice place.
It was also very close to my neighborhood which was awesome
Danny does it again! By far the best restaurant for service, hospitality and safe environment.  Seafood platter is great when bring colleagues to join.

Went in to celebrate a birthday and the service couldn't have been better. Our server Miguel was gracious, kind, and knew how to crack a joke, making us feel welcome and allowing us to really savor the experience of the tasting menu. I was excited to come eat, but the experience was even better than expected !

Great atmosphere and so fun for weekend brunch. Coffee was excellent. Service was quick and menu is extensive. Also amazing prices for what you get. Definitely earned its spot as a neighborhood favorite and it's always crowded so come early if you need a table (walkin for 2 was fast and counter seating was available right away).

If you asked ChatGPT for an "elevated dining option in NYC with a seasonal menu and a slightly loud atmosphere and a Michelin star" I'd expect Gramercy Tavern to come up. (Note: I just entered exactly that into ChatGPT and Gramercy Tavern came up. Boom.)

If you're a first-timer, go for the seasonal entrees. The burger will always be there...so tis the season to order the duck meatloaf and brick pressed chicken! From now on, when I'm asked how I like my chicken prepared (because it's obviously a question people receive all the time), I'll gently but firmly request that it be pressed by a brick. It's the only way.

The chocolate chip cookie was fine, but don't go in expecting that it'll blow your mind.
food was very good, service was insanely slow.... 2 hours for three courses.  it's a shame, if the service was better I'd be a regular

I went to Gramercy Tavern last week with a friend for lunch. Lunch reservations aren't so difficult to get during the weekdays, which is great.

The restaurant is large, with a la carte in the Tavern and a prix fixe or tasting in the Dining Room. We had lunch in the Dining Room and opted for the tasting ($95 for three savory courses and one dessert course).

Our tasting consisted of:

Roasted Carrots (green garlic, quinoa, pumpkin seeds) (4.5/5): This was a good dish. The carrots were cooked well and had a snap to them but weren't too hard. The accompaniments paired well with the carrot.

Pan-Seared Arctic Char (asparagus, crab, basil) (4/5): The fish was good, prepared nicely. It came with roe and a nice basil sauce. I did particularly enjoy the bed of crab that the char sat on.

Roasted Duck (arrowhead spinach, turnips, wild rice) (4/5): The duck was well prepared, and I really enjoyed the wild rice with it.

Apricot Shortcake (green tea, honey, Lillet Blanc) (4/5): This was a really nice dessert, but incredibly rich and buttery. It was a heavy end to a very filling lunch.

I enjoyed this experience at Gramercy Tavern. The tasting was really good and a decent price. I would return.

We had a reservation and had been frequent customers over the years including private dining room for parties. For an early dinner during which the main dining room was perhaps 10% occupied we were taken to a table which was next to a service station abutting a post which was perhaps the worst possible seating.
