We asked for another table which was accommodated, but the bad experience had already occurred. Why place us at such an undesirable table when it was virtually empty. We believe there was bias in deciding where they seated us. Shameful.....

We tried the 5 courses tasting menu 

Love the server's service. Really approachable probably the favorite kind for Michelin restaurants 

Two of the appetizers are really good. Entree was not that impressive. 

Overall love the experience!

2/5 good wine pairings but the wheat berry course tasted like prison food and I left hungry. I had to go buy a burger for dinner after dropping all that money on child sized portions of forgettable food. Obviously resting on their laurels and cashing in on the name these days. It's not a tasting menu, it's 5 amuse bouches, one of which Oliver Twist wouldn't have asked for seconds. I would not go again.

This was the second time to Gramercy Tavern for my wife and I but this time, we took our college age daughters to enjoy the delicious meal at the Dining Room. The service was attentive and accommodating. The sauces were plate licking worthy. There was not a bad bite to our lunch.

Food was generally OK.,   but I ordered the Hamachi appetizer, (which is Japanese for the raw yellowtail in sushi) and was instead given a heavy pasta dish with tomato sauce with two or three smallish cooked shrimp on top.  It was not good and I believe the dish is an entree brought to me by mistake and not an appetizer at all.

When I complained and asked where the yellowtail fish was my waitress told me that the pasta pieces were hamachi. I let it go thinking that maybe there is a pasta called hamachi that I  (silly me) never heard of.  I ate the shrimp and left the not good pasta.

This is not the case and I feel cheated.  The Arctic Char was good but maybe a little bland, or maybe just not a good second course after the "Hamachi."  The apricot shortcake was good.

I left a 25%  tip which is what I really regret, since I now feel my server intentionally cheated me.  

And if the restaurant did not have any more Hamachi she should have said so and I would have ordered another cold appetizer such as salad or cold soup.

The ambiance is nice, although they were busy ironing tablecloths around me while  I was eating desert.   (I had a 2:15 lunch reservation and although I was on time I had to wait to be seated.)

Amazing food and great service. 
Everything was exceptional. Would pass on cucumber soup since it's just not our flavor profile preference, but it is nice and refreshing. Tomatoes are a nice addition to it for texture.

I've always enjoyed dining at Gramercy Tavern, but this time they outdid themselves. The restaurant fully accommodated my recently-tested food allergies. They made excellent substitutions or removed ingredients, while preserving the high quality they are known for. The kitchen was particularly prepared for gluten-free requests. This is exactly what I would expect from a master chef. One of the best meals I've had all year.

This place is worth all the hype!! Amazing service and even better menu. Looks limited but everything is so delicious. The lager, the wine selection, the complementary starter...not quite sure what it was but it was bite size and delicious. Burger is legit.

We have been looking forward to dining at the Gramercy Tavern for some time. I was able to snare a reservation for Restaurant Week. Only lunch is available under the Restaurant Week program. 

The menu offers three courses for $60, so a bit of a premium to dine here. 

Lots of live flowers adorn the dining room, and some are huge. 

We were here on a hot muggy summer day. The water glasses were small, requiring refills. I should have asked for ice, in retrospect. 

The dinner rolls came straight from the oven. 

My wife had hamachi, raw fish with snap peas , coconut, lime, appetizer. I had lumache, Shrimp, which was delicately flavored shrimp and al dente  snail shaped pasta. Al dente is a bit chewier than what I am used to, but it was heartier and very good. Nice smooth sauce and the shrimp was buttery smooth. 

The roast duck was delicious, but I only wish there was more of it. 

For dessert, I had apricot shortcake. Now the portion size for this dish was disappointing. I was expecting something in the order of a slice of strawberry shortcake, but this ended up being the size of a very small cookie. 

If you come with a big appetite, you may end up wanting a hot dog afterwards. 

Service and ambiance were nice, but I would not want to come here and pay full price.

I've been here a few times for work and always ate in the dinning room. Booked a table for restaurant week and booked the Tavern, which was a big mistake. There is a huge difference between the Tavern and Dining Room both in terms of space and menu.

The Tavern is far more down-market and basic and with very tight space, the tables are far too close together. Not suitable for business lunches or a romantic dinner. The tavern menu is very different too and more basic than the dining room and not what I expected from GT. The special was soup and half a sandwich for $30! Reminded me of Panara Bread or Lenwich but far more expensive.

Overall, seems that GT is not what it used to be and there are too many other great places in the neighborhood. The Tavern space and menu are nothing special and not the same as the dining room. Not sure I will be back in a hurry. However, the maître d' and staff were extremely polite and courteous.

If every restaurant had service like this the world would be a better place. From the moment we stepped in, everyone was friendly yet unobtrusive. Water and wine glasses were never empty, appetizers and dinner served at a perfect pace. The food was delicious. I understand why it's so popular; this place puts one in a good mood.

Had a great time at dinner with friends here on a Friday night. Service is great. We ate in the a la carte tavern side. For apps we got the biscuits and flatbread. I loved the biscuits. They also brought us some tasty on the house focaccia. I tried both burger and the sweet potato parpadelle and I liked the parpadelle better. The burger gets talked about a lot and it was solid but nothing out of the ordinary. I would definitely opt for a seasonal entree. We got the cookie for dessert and it was rich and delicious.

The service at Gramercy Tavern was exceptional! The restaurant is large and there were multiple people waiting to be seated when I entered, but it moved quickly because there were multiple hosts showing people to their seats. My friend was able to be seated before I got there, which is always appreciated as most of the time people don't arrive at the exact same time. Our server was friendly and knowledgable and checked on us throughout the meal. The server was also kind enough to show me where the bathroom was. The bathroom was large, had multiple individual stalls, and was clean.

We came for Restaurant Week, which they only offer during lunch. The menu was slightly different from the menu on the Restaurant Week website, but it was accurate on the Gramercy Tavern website. The meal was well paced, everything was tasty, presented nicely, and the portion sizes were filling.  I got the hamachi with sungold tomatoes, the smoked wagyu brisket with carolina gold rice and crimson chili, and the peach and plum crisp. Everything tasted fresh, was seasoned well, and incorporated fresh ingredients. They gave us sweet potato rolls to start, which were warm, soft, and fluffy. The hamachi was light and refreshing and the ponzu sauce was not too overpowering. The crimson chili was not my favorite but the brisket was very tender and well prepared. The peach and plum crisp was served warm with vanilla ice cream and it had generous chunks of fruit. Overall a great dining experience and I would defintely go back!

I absolutely love spending birthdays/anniversaries/etc. at Gramercy Tavern. By far one of my favorite restaurants in the city - the decor, service, drinks, and food, are just perfection. The seasonality of the menu makes every visit feel like a new one. The hummingbird cake they give you for your birthday is literally the best - gluten free, dairy free, but so scrumptious! (I literally want this to be my wedding cake that's how good it is...) this was my second birthday celebrated at Gramercy Tavern and I can say that every dish that came out exceeded my expectations. Do yourself a favor and order an espresso martini with mezcal to finish the meal, you will not regret it. Until next time...

Not sure how to start. For sure not the best experience I had in Gramercy tavern or at a Michelin starred restaurant. Restaurant itself is lovely with fresh flowers everywhere, like always. Food this time was overly salted and entree portion was extremely small. Execution was poor that wild rice accompanied the duck was way undercooked, and the turnip puree was too salty to eat with. The size of hanger steak was ridiculous that it probably only weighed 2oz. Service was slow that we waited a good 25 min for entrees. No one ever checked on us whether everything was okay. We never saw our waitress again after placing the order. We walked out not feeling content at all, from food to service.

Very nice seasonal menu with a great wine pairing. Attentive staff who know the offerings well. We had a very nice five course meal to celebrate our anniversary. Each dish was thoughtfully prepared and seasonal. Nothing felt overdone. 

This wasn't quite Michelin Star caliber but certainly worthy of a visit. Prices are high but not as steep as some places with similar food. We spent $1200 for three folks after tip and with wine pairings. The atmosphere is lively and exciting.

It was alright. Walking in with no reservation I was a bit worried, but promptly seated outside. It was a nice evening so no big deal. Service was a tad bit slow and I felt as though the server was not up to par with the knowledge of the food and drink. We tried a variety of things, salad(tasty), beef carpaccio (weird texture), the chicken dish, a burger, and the meatloaf. The burger had no flavor, the chicken was disappointing mainly because the description says sea island red peas and I would have thought it would have had more than 10 peas. Rice was not mentioned to be in the dish, but it was there. The meatloaf was under seasoned and not really our cup of tea. Wine order was messed up and luckily the beer was nice. Overall, would I come back?  If I am in town, maybe, but with all the options around, highly unlikely.

Haven't eaten there in 20 years. Still that same NYC buzzy energy. But it feels like they are coasting. A lot. First, we sat down and my banquette seat had a big tear: very NJ diner vibe. My husband asked for our server to recommend wines in a certain price range--he recommended ones almost double the amount. Pretentious. Our first course was hamachi: it was good but I dunno, not really inventive. The pasta and main meat course were very good. Arctic char starter execution was meh and dessert was not memorable. And the little details: rolls and amuse bouche were just OK. Bathroom had messy water all over the sinks. Our bill for two was $600. This is a Michelin starred restaurant--too many other choices out there...

I nearly say... a delicacy of the East coast. One of my favorite restaurants visited in recent memory. From the jump I was greeted by a a couple savants behind the bar. Easily one of best Old Fashions I've ever had. Bold,flavorful & well balanced. I originally asked the bartender if I should order the pork shoulder or the smoked brisket. The man looked at me with a stern face & said "order the burger". I looked at him kinda funny as I'm usually pretty reluctant to order a burger when dining out but then another bartender said the same to the couple next to me. I then turned around & realized everyone around me had ordered the burger... well let me tell you that happened to be the best burger I've ever had. I ordered the biscuits as well. Phenomenal meal, very happy I found my way in.
Cool and makes a lot of sense taste so yummy I really love the chicken and rice and also chips

Had a late dinner here with family and thought everything was absolutely delicious. From the swordfish special to one of the most fantastic burgers I've had in a while, this place is no joke. Would love to try the dining room for their pre fixe menu soon -- but the tavern is serving up great stuff. Also had a great experience with our server who was so kind and helpful!
Fantastic experience, from the waitstaff to the food and especially the manager Kristen who went above and beyond to make sure that everything was perfect

We went here for restaurant week which was lunch-only. The offering was a $60 3-course prixe fixe, a quite a bargain for a popular Michelin-starred restaurant in NYC.

We split the beef tartare and hamachi appetizers, as well as the roasted duck breast and the smoked wagyu brisket. All the food was delicious, although I couldn't finish the beef tartare appetizer, because it was a large portion for such a rich food. The duck and wagyu were perfectly cooked. I forget what dessert was but it was seasonal and fresh and was also delicious- get whatever they are offering that day.

Cocktails are $19 and up but were also great.

The true difference in eating at this caliber of restaurant is the service which was spectacular. The hosts, management, and our servers were all polite, friendly, and top-tier professional despite us being there for a (relative) bargain meal.

I've been to restaurants that look down on restaurant week diners, but Gramercy Tavern did not!

I highly recommend this restaurant for any special occasion or important dinner.

THE BEST deal from restaurant week. Though $60/per person leans on the pricier side for lunch, it was worth every penny, and my partner and I saved $$$ too! The service was also top notch and they were nice enough to refill our bread - though we were absolutely stuffed at the end of the meal. 

- Lumache, 5/5: creamy, light and flavorful Aldente pasta with a slight spicy kick 
- Broccolini salad, 5/5: not a salad girl but this was sooo flavorful. Nice roasted pine nuts with a deep roasted and creamy sauce 
- Duck, 4.5/5: juicy, crispy skin, delicate flavors
- Hanger Steak, 5/5: medium rare but it was well done ;), crispy veggies underneath and each bite was well seasoned
- Table bread, 5/5: soft softttt and warm potato rolls(?) with rich room temperature butter (we requested this bread twice!)
- Cheese Sampler, 4/5: super funky cheeses (a Brie, blue cheese and Gouda) paired with sour cherries
- Peach Cobbler, 5/5: not too sweet, ice cream melted beautifully on the hot cobbler

This is not an ad :') but we paid for the meal through InKind and our $120 bill ended up for only $20!! We were lucky to get a $100 coupon from the app... so of course this was very worth the splurge

Went to the back room at Gramercy Tavern and it was an unreal experience! The tasting menu was so perfect for the food that I like and every dish was so good! 

I very rarely like every dish that's on a tasting menu and that was the case here. Every dish had a main ingredient that was the star of the show and cooked really well, but I also really liked the unique flavors that the chefs used in the dishes. I really liked the combination of flavors and the different mouthfeel from some ingredients. 

Some highlights were the lamb and the arctic char as well as the pasta with chorizo and corn. I came here for a birthday and the birthday cake was incredible! It was made with coconut and banana and was absolutely divine. I can't wait to come back!
Great service, tasty food, nice decor. Good wines, too!  Came here with family for a celebration, and it was a lovely time!

Angelle was our server she made dining an experience. Friendly, cordial, fast, efficient and at the top of her game. 
The food was excellent. Hot food was hot, cold food cold.

Came here last night with friends. We ordered a nice bottle of wine that was recommended by the sommelier. It was very very good. 
We ordered appetizers to share all of them were delicious. For the main course I ordered the chicken with corn. Amazing!!!! Absolutely amazing. The other three in the group also left not a drop of food. All of us loved every bite of the food. And yes, we got dessert, it was fantastic too.
Our server was professional and attentive and nice to talk with.
This is not our first time having a meal here, and it won't be our last!!

We have eaten in the Dining Room, and now in the Tavern. Both were exceptional experiences in every way. We will return to The Gramercy Tavern every time we are fortunate enough to visit NYC. Thank you for a peak dining experience!!!

Absolutely stellar meal and experience. Had a reservation at 7:30 and got there a bit early (7) to see if we could get a drink at the bar beforehand. Although crowded, we were able to get a drink in a few minutes. Whiskey sour, egg white, straight up was JUST how I like it. We found an area to stand while waiting for our table. 

Exactly at 7:30 on the dot, our table was ready. We sat outside and they turned the heaters on as it was pretty breezy. We all got another cocktail and ordered apps. Beef tartare and oysters are NOT to be missed!! Perfect combo of flavors on both - truly a treat. I got the grilled pork shoulder for my entree. Truly outstanding, tender, & paired perfectly with the veggies. 100% recommend. My dad got the duck meatloaf and my mom the bass. Duck meatloaf was great... I had a taste and it exceeded expectations. Didn't try the bass but my mom loved it. 

Now onto dessert... we were pretty full but didn't want to miss out on the great dessert offerings. I'm a sucker for anything almond, so we had to get the almond cake. Great choice!! Also a chocolate chip cookie I just can't skip on... Ordered that as well and couldn't say better things. 

Cannot finish the review without mentioning the exceptional service. I'll note it was a tad slow, but we were enjoying each other's company so didn't mind. Our waiter was attentive and the entire staff didn't skip a beat.

Had a great experience at the Gramercy Tavern and would totally recommend it to anybody looking for a nice upscale but cozy, comfy meal in New York. We will be back!!

Gramercy Tavern, a one Michelin-starred restaurant, is renowned for its burger, but my experience was a bit mixed. We started with the roasted oysters and duck liver mousse. The oysters were paired with Swiss chard, which added a bitterness I didn't enjoy, and the duck liver was more of a pâté than a mousse--something I could have easily skipped.

For the entrées, the server recommended the duck meatloaf, which turned out to be juicy and flavorful. Naturally, I had to try the tavern burger, but while it was decent, it wasn't the standout I had hoped for--it was a bit dry.

Overall, there's a good chance I won't be returning.
Wonderful meal to celebrate my husband's 50th birthday. We loved everything except the duck meatloaf.

This restaurant was a delight. We had the price fixe multi course dinner with wine pairings. There were options for each course. Everything was perfectly prepared and plated beautifully. The service was impeccable. All in all, our dinner there was a great experience. We're hoping to return the next time we get a chance.

We had a dining room tasting menu reservation. The service was fantastic, the wine was great, the employees were nice, it's just the food itself wasn't that great. I guess that's the risk of a tasting menu, but each plate just left a little to be desired. 

For the price point of the tasting menu I couldn't help but feel disappointed. I would come back to try the tavern but would probably not do the dining room tasting menu again.
Food was amazing I had the pork shoulder. The service was amazing. We sat outside and it was very nice.

We arrived for a late lunch in the tavern without a reservation, so we expected a wait, which was fine. 

It's a weird wait list process. If you are eating in the tavern, the bartender controls the list. Elsewhere is controlled by the host stand. So we felt we need to hang by the bar until space was available versus outside or in the lobby. 

When we were up we wedged (yes - wedged - 1 less chair at the bar would have given everyone an extra inch of breathing room) ourselves into the area and ordered our meals. 

Food was good. Didn't blow us away. Didn't live up to the hype. Wouldn't run back next time we're in nyc.
Wonderful service--- can't wait to try the cocktail at home!!! Always a great experience at Gramercy Tavern, whether you are at the Bar,  Tavern,  or in the Dining Room it's the best!

OMG! This was mine and husbands first time in NY, we left Harry Potter store and found this gem!
Firstly the service from start to finish was impeccable. The staff was very friendly and knowledgeable. 
The atmosphere is definitely sophisticated even during a weekday lunch. 
Secondly the drinks were marvelously flavorful. 
The cheese and bacon biscuits were savory, and the entrees delectable. 
We had a fantastic experience and hope that we can visit again soon!

Had a very delicious meal while visiting NYC. Our server was so friendly and knowledgeable. She helped us feel celebrated as it was a special dinner for our anniversary. I was surprised how much she knew about the wines, too. The courses were the perfect amount of food, also loved the seafood platter addition. The only knock was the sommelier didn't seem overly friendly and any time he did come over to share about the wines, he seemed totally uninterested. Otherwise, the evening was verh enjoyable and I'd definitely recommend a meal at Gramercy Tavern!

We came here for our anniversary dinner and it did not disappoint. I have several food intolerances, including dairy, gluten and corn, and always stayed away from this restaurant thinking that they would not be flexible to accommodating my restrictions. But I was so wrong! Mary Beth, our wonderful server, was very thorough and careful to go above and beyond to ensure that I was able to fully experience each part of the tasting menu. I was extremely surprised by the dessert portion. I was almost certain that the kitchen made a mistake because everything tasted too good. I was assured that it was safe for me to enjoy. I was able to eat carrot cake safely for the first time in nearly a decade!!!
The menu rotates pretty frequently, but every time I have been here, the duck has been awesome. The drinks are strong, and the desserts aren't too sweet. Grammercy tavern is great.

Have to join the rest to say one of the best lunches we had while in town, truly exceptional.  The oven roasted oysters, I was skeptical but they were lightly cooked with such good flavor, bits of apple & greens in the background.  Sounds strange but they were the best we've had.  The Broccoli rabe salad was perfection in both texture & taste.  Must get the recipe!!!!  The focaccia with its charred grape & crusty bits was insanely good along with the famous burger-again-best we've ever had.  The fall flavored cocktail was a bit warm & sweet but certainly didn't keep us from drinking it, great flavor.  We can't wait to get back for one more lunch before we leave, it was THAT good!

I've been meaning to try this place for YEARS but found the tasting menu to be disappointing and dated overall. I just didn't find it very delicious or well done. With that being said, I think it still justifies its existence and I don't hate it or anything. But I'm definitely not going to go back again.

This was our "closer" restaurant for NYC long weekend and did not disappoint! The decor is beautiful and setting classy without being stuffy. The service was impeccable and helped make the experience amazing. We had a minimum of 5 people serving our table at all times, from head waiter to Somm to dish servers to water fillers - precision work.

The food! 5 course meal - each dish was divine in its own way. Beautiful colors, textures, and flavors. I'd probably skip the extra cheese course for $15/pp next time. Highlights were both pasta dishes in course #2 and the Duck Breast for Clurse 3 - divine.

We were celebrating my wife's 50th birthday and they made it awesome with special dessert and Amaros from our waiter's homeland in Italy! 

Only minus was the wine list was crazy expensive - we asked for a bottle ~$100 and ended up being $168. Whoa. The total was $1500 for 4 people () but we were blowing it out for special occasion! If you have the budget, Gramercy will treat you right

We had a lovely dinner at Gramercy Tavern to celebrate my birthday! Beautifully appointed interior decor, excellent service, and definitely a well-established staple for all-knowing patrons, this crowd-favorite was bustling in the main area before we got to the back. To be quite honest, the food itself was forgettable. Our experience was underwhelming and overpriced for what it was. We're glad we got to have a chance to experience GT, but it just wasn't our thing.

A new york staple! came by for a kid week afternoon drink and dessert and sat outside. large selection of wines by the glass and fun seasonal desserts! the apple cider donuts were crispy and coated in sugar, and our waitress recommended the chocolate chip cookie which was dense and chocolaty and balanced perfectly with the glass of chocolate malt served on the side. hope to come back to try the rest of the menu!

In the past I had given Gramercy 5 stars but this time I am struggling to even give it 3.  Ate in the Dining Room and had the fixed menu.  It started with an Amuse Bouche that was a truly just a small tidbit.  The next dishes were nice but there was nothing worthy of a one star Michelin. What further disappointed was that the lamb was a very gamy lamb chop, not a lamb loin from the rack. What further disappointed was the service, while many attended to the table we were left with bread crumbs on the table throughout the meal.  Sorry to post this but not my best experience.
Great place and enjoyed the menu options.  My only complaint is that it's alway crowded..
Food and service was great. Took two nights but finally got seats at the bar. Sitting at the bar is the best.

Amazing lunch with delicious food, impeccable service, and a very comfortable atmosphere. There were maybe 50 guests in the tavern side and about 20 staff who were very aware of our needs and proactively too care of our every need. The woman filling waters was very prompt and refilled after every sip (not quite) but glasses were never less than half full. The dining room side could be a high end formal occasion while the tavern is comfortable and easy for lunch with friends. Highly recommended!!!

It was my first time in Gramercy tavern, although I've heard a lot about this place. For first time I took a tasting menu and it was delicious. 5 courses and nice touch after food as few cookies to go. I loved that there's space between tables and you can talk more privately despite of the full restaurant . The service was 100% as well. Thank you

The ambiance is a solid 5 stars - the service is always good -- Hamburger in the bar area with a seafood tower is my normal order -opted  for a pasta dish too this visit and it was not great - but we still had an amazing meal and evening at GT! Drinks and wine are always reliable here as well - be prepared to wait for a seat and ask the bartenders if you need a seat at the bar - they'll gladly assist and provide an appoximate wait time --

Fantastic on all levels.
Excellent food and ambiance and elegant.
Beautiful flowers.
Consistently great service and a true joyous spot for an exquisite dinner or lunch experience!!

A culinary highlight of my visit to Manhattan. I tried last minute to get a bar seat around 5:30PM on a weekday and waited ~30 minutes. The waitlist for the bar only got longer and longer as the night went on. Reservations are a must! 

The brick-pressed chicken was one of the best-cooked chickens I've had at a restaurant. The freshness from the corn and okra were much appreciated. 

All of their desserts looked good and the corn sundae did not disappoint. 

The atmosphere is lively and I had a great time chatting with the bartenders and other solo diners near me.

The service is courteous, prompt, and knowledgeable, ready to address any and all queries.  Likewise, accommodations made for my anniversary are not soon forgotten.  This is redressed, however, by two niche-- and highly specific-- mishaps incurred my partner.

With that said, the food is in the C+ to lesser B+ tier, execution-wise; and within the B+ to A- range for quality of ingredients.  The well-priced (relatively), diverse and yet meaningfully adjoined menu is pleasantly arranged and may be ordered to one's liking with low probability for incompatibility; partially a testament to the quality of the menu, as well as the limits and seemingly bounded constraints of the menu.  Unlike many Michelin restaurants where everyone at the table must order the prix fixe/chef's menu if even one person orders it, or where a reservation or type of reservation binds one toward a certain type of order, I was pleasantly surprised to find that guests are permitted to break from both conventionalities here.

In optimizing adventure, I would recommend one person order the tasting menu, and having the other order 1 to 3 a la carte items; pending preference and ability to pack away the calories.  Luckily, I have an adventurous albeit much lower capacity partner.  It works out for the both of us.

Creativity while remaining grounded in core elements is likewise something I would make note of here.  Very good job in that respect.

Very beautiful ambiance and table presentation.

It is difficult to pinpoint which dish is my favorite, but I will definitely note the scallops, schnitzel, and chocolate cake as being stars; with the duck breast being among the anchors, conversely.

We were in the area and decided to stop in for drinks during happy hour. There wasn't any space at the bar but they have a wait list. We found a spot at the window where they have a small ledge for drinks. We enjoyed our Sancerre wine. The space was beautifully decorated for Thanksgiving with a harvest vibe. The service was really great -- everyone wanted to find us a spot to enjoy our drinks. I'd love to go back for lunch or dinner.
We went in with high expectations and they were all surpassed. Incredibly warm space and staff and absolutely delicious food!

Never a miss at Gramercy Tavern.  The food is exceptional, and the service is always spot-on.  Little things, like not placing food down if one of the party is not seated at the table.  They'll run it back to keep warm.  Bringing new silverware in a box, not just carried over in their hands.  Attentive without being obsequious.  There is a more "formal" dining room in the back, with the bar and tables up front.  Prices are as expected in NYC, but the salads, sandwiches and main dishes are all worth it.  And make sure to get the warm donuts at the end!
I was so excited to finally try those famous spot. The service was great, the burger was outstanding but the menu wasn't that appetizing. I may have to come back again to try.

1-Michelin star, 5-course tasting menu for 175 is really good value. It's got a proven track record for consistent well-prepared dishes with an upscale presentation. It's understated given the quality and reputation but sometimes you need a more causal vibe but with bougey-er food. It's an interesting combination but a must do if you never been.

Food: 8/10
Service: 7/10
Vibe: 7/10
Value: 9/10

Gramercy Tavern is a NYC institution type of restaurant and for the most part, I think for good reason. The staff is fabulous and the setting is impressive, but not overly formal. The food was mostly great too. Roasted beets and carrots was a great starter, definitely recommend. Brick roast chicken was good, but the burger left a little to be desired. I found it a little dry and not super flavorful (thought the bacon on top was great). The chocolate peanut butter pudding cake was very tasty too! Overall I would definitely recommend coming and I would like to try the tasting menu one day, but also not in a rush to come back. Happy to say I went!
Probably the best dirty martini I've had. Great great cocktails. You must make a reservation! The aesthetics of the restaurant and the service are spectacular.

hadn't been there in a couple years after going there basically every couple of weeks, prefer the bar and it was absolutely the same! the consistency is uncanny! the service was fantastic and the food was just the same, its really nice to have somewhere in the city where you can come back to after years away and it is just the same as you rememeber it, in the best ways!!!! great wine selection as usual also! bravo!

Came for our first wedding anniversary dinner and the service and food were top tier!

We started with oysters and some seafood before our tasting menu began. Each dish was flavorful, beautifully plated and well portioned. We were full by the time the dessert came. 

The waiter was so nice and surprised us with an extra mini cake to wish us a happy anniversary and sent us home with some little banana bread loafs! 

Great for a celebratory dinner or just a date night!

Would very much recommend going to the Tavern if you can snag a reservation! We opted for the Tavern over the dining room since for the most part, we have generally had better meals in the "lower scale" part of a Michelin star restaurant, which we find to have heartier but still delicious food and above average service and a cozier ambiance. The Tavern definitely did not disappoint and hit all the points I listed above. 

For appetizers we got the carpaccio (melt in your mouth), the roasted oysters (not my favorite but still good, I think I prefer them raw) and the bacon cheddar biscuits (my favorite). Would seriously order a basket of those biscuits if I could. 

For entrees we got the burger, the pork shoulder and the brick pressed chicken. I will caution that things seem to lean a bit more on the salty side. The chicken was amazing, I don't normally order chicken but chose it due to some rave reviews and it lived up to the hype. I had some of the burger but it wasn't my favorite, but I prefer thinner patties in general. Pork shoulder was very tender but my husband actually raved about the beans that came with it. 

Dessert we got the almond cake and chocolate pudding cake. These were good, but didn't stand out like some of the other dishes did. 

Overall, great experience and would recommend.

First time I've been in a while and prices seem significantly higher. I felt like it was extremely overpriced, even compared to other comparable options. 

Flat bread was okay. Nothing special. Basically 2 small pieces and 3 regular spreads. Complete crime to charge as much as they are. 

Meat loaf was also small but worse it was extremely salty. Quite disappointing. 

Friend got the burger and he was also disappointed. Mentioned it was quite plain and nothing special about the beef. 

I won't be returning. 

Burger was average

The restaurant was very nicely decorated with Christmas vibe. 
The food was ok. I don't like the pork dumpling dish at all - the dumpling skin was very soft which tastes like it's been soaking in the soup for a long time without any chewiness; the dumpling meat is very dry without juiciness. 
Some of the servers are not very professional in their way of delivering dishes. A few times I was scared they might spill the dish onto me. Actually one server knocked down the water to my fiancé when handing the dish, which made the table and my fiancé's leg wet. At first they just put a napkin on top of the wet table which got wet very quickly. But we didn't want to have dinner served on a wet piece of napkin. So we asked them to replace the table linen. They did it very quickly which is nice. They apologized but in the end they didn't make up for it by any means - in restaurants we've been to if any accidents from their end happens they always show apology by giving some discount or offering free desserts etc,. But nothing from Gramercy Tavern. 
Overall both my fiancé and I don't know how they got one Michelin star. Won't come back or recommend to Others.

I'm often pleased with Union Square Hospitality Group and my recent visit to Gramercy Tavern was in line with my other experiences at other Danny Meyer spots! We dined in the tavern and the main reason for this visit was to order the burger and it surely did not disappoint! 

The Tavern Burger ($35)- at $35 this is one of the more expensive burgers I've had, and the quality of the meat really stood out. I would have enjoyed fries with the burger but I have to say that the duck fat chips were a nice accompaniment. The smoked onion aioli was delicious. It didn't need ketchup, although I do like ketchup on my burgers. 

Brick pressed chicken ($36)- this was tasty but did not stand out in the same way that the burger did. I felt the portion of chicken was small. 

Chocolate pudding cake ($18)- wow, just wow! So tasty! The popcorn was a nice addition. I love chocolate cake. 

I look forward to visiting Gramercy Tavern again!

GET THE HOT CHOCOLATE!! I can't believe it's been 7 years since I've been back to Gramercy! The last time I came I did the prefix menu in their dining room and it was amazing (see my previous review).

This time I walked into their Tavern. If you don't have a rez you can put your name on the waitlist with the bartender. They also have a small foyer where you can order drinks from! 

Now onto the food. Everything here is done with so much care. Highly recommend their seasonal cocktails (Fall Classic was our favorite) as well. 

Hot chocolate 5/5: perfect amount of sweetness and has a touch of cinnamon on top. Very good and similar price for other hot chocolates around the city. 

Burger 5/5: I prefer smash burgers but this was fantastic 

Cookie with malted milk 4/5: really good cookie and a good portion - I was expecting something more with the milk (tasted like bornvita or boost that we had as kids) 

Biscuits - 5/5 very good I'd totally get this again

Flatbread 3/5- the bread was great but the dips were okay

Fall classic 5/5 - fav cocktail of the night 

Coffee corrected 4/5 - this was good but a higher price tag!
What a great dining experience! We attended a small dinner for my wife's birthday and neither the food nor the service disappointed. Spectacular! Our primary server, Sarah, was outstanding.

Cool, easy vibes, very good service combined with outstanding food and drinks. 
It's easy to see why this is a Michelin starred restaurant. From reservations through checkout, this was an amazing experience. I highly recommend this restaurant.

Unlike the multicourse tasting dinners I've had in Gramercy Tavern's more formal back dining room, one can order as much (or as little) as desired in their front tavern area. I prefer that freedom, as well as the tavern's laid back atmosphere and lively bar scene.

Enjoyed my pretty cranberry daiquiri, a perfect blend of tart and sweet. Duck liver mousse appetizer tasted great spread on included rustic toast points. I took my Yelp friend Gail B's advice and ordered the Tavern Burger, my oh my that was one delicious burger! One might think "how special can a simple cheeseburger be"? Well GT's version, made of house ground chopped beef topped with melty cheddar cheese and thick bacon, was a revelation - tender and juicy to the max. Thanks for the tip Gail! Also loved the duck meat loaf, nicely spiced and resting on fresh fingerling potatoes and veggies; a uniquely delicious dish. Apple cider doughnuts for dessert (served warm) were outrageously good, albeit overpriced at $18 for two small ones.

Service by Kiara was friendly and generally prompt, hit a couple of snags but that's to be expected on a crowded Saturday afternoon. Reservations are hard to come by (especially this time of year), but slots do open up online the day of as mercurial diners change their plans last minute. Or try to snag an open bar seat, but the wait can be long.

Everything was perfection at this beautiful cozy well appointed establishment! 
We had the 5 course dinner in the dining room with the wine pairing. It is a bit on the pricey side $175 for the 5 courses, $115 for the wine pairing, but well worth the money. The best meal I have ever had! Highly recommend!
Great festive ambience. Brings out a joyful mood.  Warm atmosphere.  Everyone seems happy.  Accolades so deserved  I was there first night it opened. !!!

Phenomenal food and service that far exceeded our expectations! The duck liver mousse, duck meatloaf, and sea bass were perfect. We also felt that the cocktails were of fantastic quality, especially relative to other restaurants we frequent. The chocolate pudding cake was out of this world decadent. The environment is romantic, welcoming, lively, and cozy. We were in NY celebrating our engagement and first Christmas in NYC, and because of that the staff surprised us with a small dessert cake with "congratulations" beautifully written across the plate. They really went above and beyond to make our dinner special, and we spent the rest of the trip talking about it. It was far and away the best food of our trip and just generally the best meal we've had in a long time. Gramercy will be a staple for us on all future NY visits.

Dined at the Gramercy Tavern to celebrate the holidays. I was excited to try their 5 course seasonal menu. We opted to add on their seafood platter to start the meal. What a disappointment! We found a broken shell in a clam and oyster. The mignonette that accompanied the oysters was tasteless. We pushed forward hoping things would get better. Unfortunately, things went south. First, we informed the waiter that a person in our party had a nut allergy. Yet, the runners still placed the dishes that contained nuts in front of the person in the party with the allergy.  You would think that an establishment with 1 Michelin star would have better communication between the waiter and runners.  Each course was bland, confused in composition, and fell short. The skin on the duck breast was soft and chewy. We ordered the lamb medium and it came out rare. At this point we didn't want to complain, took the meal as a loss and had the last course. The dessert was good, but nothing to write home about. Drinks were crafted well and were the highlight of the meal. I have been to better tasting menus in NYC. Perhaps the tavern is better than the dining room.

Still perfect after all these years.  The alchemy of a very classy "tavern" with premium prices and very good classics still works.

5 star food:  even a burger here is exceptional.  These folks have it down to a science on always giving a consistently good dining experience

5 star service:  like the food, you'll never have bad service here.  Servers tend to stay here a long time and be very very competent 

4 star ambience:  my only minor gripe is the ambience.  It fits with the tavern vibe but for fine dining I prefer a little sleeker and less is more decoration wise

We were on a quick trip to NYC and didn't have time in advance to make reservations, but still wanted to have a nice dinner. Dinner time, Friday night we walked in without a reservation since I'd heard they take walk-ins in the Tavern dining area. We were seated after a short wait. Staff was amazing. Everyone was at the top of their game... friendly, helpful, knowledgeable. The tavern area was busy and lively without being too loud. The wine-by-the-glass list was brief but full of excellent choices. The dishes were outstanding. Best beet & burrata salad I've ever had and that's a staple of ours normally. Duck meatloaf was incredible. Didn't really care for the smoked fish entree, but that was more of a personal preference than a failure in execution. Desert & seasonal cocktails to wrap up the night were fantastic.

Gramercy Tavern is definitely a refined establishment that is a classy destination. 

Over lunch to start, I had the Squash soup which came with Apples, Collard Greens, Shell Beans and the Golden Tilefish as my main dish which came with 
Royal Red Shrimp, Carrots, and Freekeh.

For a mild winter day this was fitting. The portions were decent and the flavors complimented each other. 

The consistency of the Squash soup was smooth and not too heavy. While the Golden Tilefish had a great presentation it felt more like an appetizer than a full entree. 

The staff were very attentive and the Dining room setting was very warm and inviting.

Good food but stodgy atmosphere. New Year's Eve was positively boring! 6 course meal. Who needs it? Very disappointing. Not a single person looked like they were having a good time... not even dressed for NYE. 30 seconds of celebration .

Why has it taken me over 20+ years to write a review? From my first visit during  restaurant week in the 199?s to now, the service at Gramercy Tavern has always been impeccable. We've held private events and dined in the dining room on a number of occasions and service never fails. Even when they make a mistake, they quickly acknowledge the mistake and make compensations.

On top of that, the dining experience is also exceptional. The food, the decor. It's what a NY fine dining establishment is meant to be.

This is likely one of the finest dining experiences in NYC
Spent NYE there with outstanding staff members Dristan and Marybeth to name just a few ... this staff is probably the most professional restaurant group team I've seen in years 
Great hospitality and service, highly knowledgeable about the food and beverage but most of all they all love their work 
The food is nothing less than exceptional and the five course service timed perfectly 
We opted for the wind pairing as well and as wowed by the selections. 

Absolutely nothing needs improvement 
Nice work everyone.. you provided what every diner seeks... a perfect dining experience

I booked a table at Gramercy Tavern to celebrate my birthday and it was definitely a very memorable experience. I had a table for two on a Wednesday at around 9pm and when we arrived the place was still very full (considering it was a weekday this was very surprising!). The "tavern" is separate from the "dining room", offering an a la carte menu and more casual feel as opposed to the prix fixe tasting menu offered in the latter. The space is very beautiful, has high ceilings, rustic decor, and feels classy and cozy-- perfect for a nice, but lowkey celebration. Our waitress came by very quickly and was really likable! She was pleasant and friendly in a genuine way, very attentive of us without being overbearing. We started off ordering some drinks: my fiancé got a glass of wine while I got an espresso martini. The espresso martini was a little too sweet for my taste but the wine was perfect. For food we shared: 

- Beets and Carrots: delicious and bright. Perfect combination of sweetness from the beets and perfectly roasted carrots, nuttiness from the pistachios, and creaminess from the burrata. This is hands down one of the best beet apps I have ever ordered. The execution was perfect and the quality of ingredients was top notch. 

- Broccolini Salad: another very fresh tasting and light dish. The broccolini was perfectly cooked, and the freekeh gave the dish a super nice texture/substance. The thinly sliced almonds added a nice crunch. 

- Wood-fired Sea Bass: Very nicely cooked sea bass! Perfectly flaky and buttery. It was a little too salty for my taste (perhaps the bacon aioli), but well balanced with the tangy potatoes which helped neutralize the flavors. I was particularly impressed by how well the fish was cooked.

- Brick Pressed Chicken: super tender, perfectly cooked and juicy chicken. Tasted like it had some BBQ sauce on top, or at least had a sweet smoky flavor that was reminiscent of BBQ sauce. It came over a bed of very flavorful lentils which made the dish feel really hearty. Overall, pretty good!

- Chocolate Chunk Cookie: I had to order this after hearing so much hype about this cookie online. The cookie came out warm and was surprisingly not as sweet as I thought. The dough itself had s lightly spiced flavor that went very well with the rich chocolate chunks. The cookie was buttery, with a gooey inside and a nice crust. It had coarse bits of sea salt on top which brought out the sweetness. The chocolate milk on the side was perfect to balance it out. Would definitely recommend. 

- Chocolate Pudding Cake: This was a decadent, rich dessert that is perfect for any sweet tooth. It was like a deconstructed lava cake, with a fluffy light chocolate cake paired with thick fudge, topped with creamy vanilla ice cream and topped with caramel popcorn which was honestly just the best addition. This was my favorite dessert of the night. Delicious!

- Hummingbird Cake with coconut frosting: I did not intend on having 3 separate desserts, but the staff knew I was celebrating my birthday and brought out a small cake with a candle which I thought was very kind! The cake was a hummingbird cake with pineapple and banana, with a light coconut frosting-- honestly was very reminiscent of a pina colada! Light, and gluten/dairy free. Very perfect way to end the meal. 

Overall, Gramercy Tavern has a very nice ambiance, with excellent quality food. The mains and apps were all delicious and clearly very well prepared. The seasonal aspect makes it exciting to come here now that you expect to have the freshest ingredients and there is always promise for something new in the next rotation. The desserts were phenomenally executed! There was not a single bad bite... I would really come here exclusively for dessert. The service was top notch, I really did feel cared for during our whole meal. Highly highly recommend this place for a special occasion or if you ever just want to splurge yourself to a nice meal.

Visited Gramercy Tavern just after the lunch rush on a weekday and grabbed a seat at the bar. There were very cozy and welcoming vibes! I already had lunch that day and was left with a hankering for a sweet treat! I've heard great things about all of their desserts, but specifically the cookie. I'm pleased to say that it has earned a spot in my heart for top 5 cookies in nyc! I also ordered their hot chocolate which had a perfect little spike of cinnamon from the marshmallow. Also wanted to note that the bartender working was the loveliest human! He gave me his top three cookies in nyc (one being GT of course) and I can't wait to check them out

Love! 
Ambiance 100% classic NY
Food 100% 
Service 100%
We loved the 3 course lunch in dining 
Fireside Chat is a must 
And OMG the potato chips with smoked onion dip - heavenly

Came for restaurant week at lunch and it was overall a nice experience, but it wasn't a particularly large meal. The squash pasta was probably the most surprising dish with it's deep rich flavor and satisfying texture from the pasta. Everything else was executed well, but not eye opening in any way. For the desserts, I did enjoy the pudding the most out of the desserts since it was very smooth and unique. It came out close to a Panna cotta, but definitely more of a pudding texture. I'd go back for a new menu like this again at some point.

Let's start with the good: service was excellent and kind.  Water glass was empty often, but I didn't have to wait terribly long before someone came.  But why was the water glass empty so often?...the food was extremely salty.  There was great flavor and balance of umami, citrus, etc.  But there was always too much salt.  So much that my lips started getting irritated by the end of the meal.  I had read prior reviews complaining of the salt but I ignored them to my detriment.  It wasn't until the last main entree that I brought it up to the staff because I really couldn't stomach the salt anymore.  And this is where the service was great, they offered to redo the dish twice.  Sadly the second try was worse than the first as the meat was a hockey puck and still overly salted.  Really not the server's fault. He and the manager were super nice.  But really the food is too salty.  If the patron are on the older side and have started to lose their taste buds (yes it happens) and the restaurant is catering to that demographic...ok...maybe...but their second try still failed so sadly I wont be returning to this classic establishment.  The restaurant was decorated beautifully, rustic yet modern appearance.  I will miss Gramercy.

Lived up to its expectations! We went for restaurant week and were not disappointed. Service was incredible, with many folks taking care of us and ensuring we never needed anything. I loved the ambiance with the beautiful flower and nature arrangements. And of course the food was fantastic. My only complaint was in the broccolini salad, I felt that some broccolini was not adequately washed as I felt both silt as well as something hard that almost broke a tooth. Everything else was incredible. Really appreciate our server, Oliver, for switching out one of the wine pairings when I disliked the moscato. It came to $60 for a three course lunch for restaurant week with an additional $55 wine pairing.

Honest review of Gramercy Tavern: 

I was happy to be notified by Michelin starred restaurant Gramercy Tavern! I had heard that the food is a must but an absolute must is the seasonal hot chocolate! Both the exterior and interior are majestic, the hostess at the door was very courteous and took me to my table where I was greeted by my waitress Anastasia. I started my meal with the hot chocolate of course and the Lobster salad with copious amounts of citrusy lobster, fresh broccolini, seasonal Meyer lemon, earthy flavored radish and an avocado dressing that definitely made you excited for the next course! My waitress then brought out a fresh sweet potato bread roll that I enjoyed while waiting for my main course the Hanger steak cooked rare to medium rare with a tender center with cauliflower, radicchio, and pickled Shallots. The hanger steak was acceptable but not exceptional. It had a flavor that I could not put my finger on but I believe it tasted sweet with a mellow citrus taste. It's very rare that the vegetables outshine the meat but they absolutely did here! The cauliflower had amazing flavor, fresh crisp to it, the radicchio and pickled shallots pairs well together! Now the dessert, Im going to tell you right now....It's a crime against humanity that not every soul on this planet will be able to experience that Meyers lemon cake with candied Kumquats and house made Pistachio ice cream! 
That flavor profile took my taste bud on a glorious journey to sweet, savory every bite. The smooth pistachio house made Ice cream was the best I've ever had. My overall experience here was great, the highlight of this meal was the hot chocolate, and that Meyers lemon cake...oh and the exceptional service by all the staff but especially Anastasia! If you are in the Gramercy park area this is a great choice to dine.

It's been about a decade since we've been here, and it's just as good now as it was the first time we came. While we were happy with all of our dishes, the complimentary bread it actually what we'll remember about this meal. It was so fluffy and tasty! I got the dark chocolate cake dessert and my favorite part was the candied chestnut. I could eat a whole bowl of those - so good.
The service was also good - friendly and helpful; but not stuffy.

Such a great experience when we came for restaurant week. It was $60 for 3 courses and everything was delicious. We got the lobster, squash pasta and white bean soup as our appetizers. Everything was a little salty but the flavor was great. I really liked how Al dente the pasta was. For the mains, we got the hanger steak, chicken and fish. I thought the fish was so soft and it also came with two pieces of shrimp. I really liked the squash flavor, the chicken was a little dry but the thigh was super juicy. I don't usually eat steak but my roommates really liked it. For dessert, everything was fantastic as well. The apple tart tasted more like a cake, chocolate cake was super dense and rich, the lemon cake with pistachio ice cream had nice flavor as well. Our favorite was probably the sweet potato roll they gave us in the beginning (and got extra of). It was so warm and the butter paired perfectly. The service was impeccable and they gave us apps on the house then chocolate at the end.

This is a review for the dining room. The experience was entirely disappointing. We went there for my birthday lunch. First, the server was not very kind. Maybe she was having a bad day, so I brushed it off. She told us we needed to rush to get our order in because the kitchen was closing? Which was strange because it was only 1 pm. We ordered quickly but later there were continuous issues throughout. I ordered the chicken but was given the fish. They apologized and said they would make me the chicken right away. It took about 20 minutes and by the time I got the correct dish everyone else's food was cold. The piece of chicken they gave me also was not white meat like they said it would be (I'm suspecting the kitchen was closing and they had to quickly put something together). They also did not bring out a cake for my birthday (even though it seems standard) and they knew it was my birthday. Just strange. Maybe I came on an off day.

Mathew was a marvelous server of a magical meal. Everything was spectacular. The lobster salad, the squash pasta, the lamb, the lemon cake, the bread, OMG!  The chef is a master of amplifying flavor. The depth and intensity are unparalleled. WOW!

Had been many, many years since I last visited Gramercy Tavern.  

The space is more gorgeous than last time, and the service was very good.  

Unfortunately, I wasn't thrilled with my food.  

I started with a broccolini salad.  While I was excited to eat some greens, I found it uninspiring and somewhat bland. 

My main course was the pasta.  How can you mess up pasta?! 

The pasta was served with an unsavory beef sauce that had a gritty texture. 

There's nothing worse than leaving a high-end restaurant hungry, but that's exactly how I felt. 

Maybe it was because it was a Sunday night?  Not sure. 

I won't be back.

It starts and look like a great gastro pub.  Walking into the dining area you get white table clothed Michelin starred elegance.  It all works.  The service is impeccable, from the water to the understated clearing of plates and bringing each plate warmed just right.  Cocktails are amazing.  The red wines nice and paired.  (in fact all the wines, cognac and drink you could ever want offered) Tasting menus give you two options so you and your partner can try each one down the line.  Venison on the bone.  Tender lamb.  Dumplings that rival any dim sum place in the city.  Ruffle chips with a caviar dip a great blend.  Tile fish like soft tofu.  If I could eat like that everyday I'd be going at another way on top.

I've always wanted to try this famous place. We went in on a rainy Saturday night with no reservations but we put our names on the list at the bar and got seated after 15 minutes. We sat at the bar. The cocktails were great! I had a negroni and my husband had a glass of red. Service was impeccable! The atmosphere was wonderful. Very classy and old school. The food was delicious, especially the beef rib. We also ordered the bass. For dessert, we had a chocolate pudding cake. Very pleasant and lovely evening!

Came here for lunch on valentine's day! Sat in the dining room and we ordered a la carte - the beef carpaccio, lobster salad and bacon biscuit were so so good. For the entree, we shared the fish which was just okay - tender, but nothing special. For dessert, we got the chocolate cake which was amazing! They also gave us free valentine's cookies to take home.

Impeccable food and service. Had a special occasion celebration at GT. The tasting menu was outstanding. I especially loved the cabbage that was prepared in a stack like lasagna noodles. Savory and delicious. Who would have ever thought cabbage could be so good. Beautiful setting too!

Gramercy Tavern in NYC is a culinary gem, blending rustic charm with exceptional farm-to-table dishes. The cozy ambiance and impeccable service make it perfect for special occasions. After dining, unwind with a word game at Wordle Today. A must-visit for food lovers!
